articles.title: I found the cheapest portable monitor ever — a $40 display for work and play
articles.text:
I found the cheapest portable monitor ever: Give your laptop a second screen for under $40 this Black Friday — Amazon knocks 20% off the 15.6-inch MNN Full HD display
A budget-friendly upgrade for your mobile workspace
This must be the cheapest portable monitor I've seen this year. The MNN 15.6-inch screen combines a Full HD IPS display with USB-C connectivity and a protective cover that doubles as a stand. And it's down to $40 for Black Friday.
Most portable monitors, even the budget ones, hover around the $50 to $60 mark, so this is a genuine steal if you want a standard second screen for your desk or playing games.
Best For: Remote workers, business travelers, students, and anyone looking for an affordable second screen for their laptop.
The Deal: The MNN 15.6-inch portable monitor is now $40 (was $50) at Amazon for Black Friday.
Today's top portable monitor deal
MNN's 15.6-inch portable monitor features a Full HD IPS display, 300 nits brightness, HDR support, dual USB-C ports, HDMI connectivity, integrated stereo speakers, and a protective smart cover stand.
Why we recommend it
The MNN portable monitor features a 15.6-inch IPS display with a 1920 x 1080 resolution, 300 nits of brightness, a 1000:1 contrast ratio, and 178-degree viewing angles. It also supports HDR and includes low blue light and flicker-free technology.
You can connect it to any compatible laptop using a single USB-C cable for both power and video. There are two full-function USB-C ports, an HDMI connection, integrated stereo speakers, and a 3.5mm headphone jack.
The monitor supports both landscape and portrait orientations, and you can extend or duplicate your existing display, or use the MNN as your primary one.
At just 0.3 inches thick, it's designed to fit into a bag without taking up too much space, and the PU leather smart cover protects the display during travel while also doubling as an adjustable stand.
For more top picks, we've tested all the best portable monitors.
Price context & historical value
Amazon's Black Friday discount brings the MNN 15.6-inch portable monitor down to $39.99, the cheapest we've ever seen it, or any such display. The included protective cover and USB-C and HDMI cables mean you won't need to budget for additional accessories.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the MNN 15.6-inch portable monitor if...
If you frequently work away from your desk or want a second screen without spending much money.
❌ Skip the MNN 15.6-inch portable monitor if...
If you need a higher-resolution display, professional-grade color accuracy, or a brighter screen for working outdoors. Check that your laptop supports video output over USB-C so you can take advantage of single-cable connectivity.

articles.title: HP HyperX Omen RTX 5070 laptop gets $1090 Black Friday price cut
articles.text:
Walmart slashes nearly $1,100 off the HP HyperX Omen laptop for Black Friday, with Ryzen 9 power and RTX 5070 graphics
Plenty of power for video editing and 3D rendering
You don't need to buy a dedicated mobile workstation to tackle demanding creative and professional tasks. The HP HyperX Omen combines a powerful 16-core AMD Ryzen 9 processor with Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 graphics and a high-resolution IPS display, making it suitable for much more than gaming.
Best For: Content creators, video editors, 3D designers, gamers, and professionals who need plenty of processing and graphics power.
The Deal: Walmart has slashed the price of the HP HyperX Omen 15.3-inch laptop from $2,389 to $1,299 for Black Friday, saving you $1,090 (46%).
The HyperX Omen features a 16-core AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX processor, Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 graphics, 16GB DDR5 RAM, 1TB SSD, 15.3-inch WQXGA 180Hz IPS display, and Windows 11.
Why we recommend it
The heart of HP's HyperX Omen laptop is AMD's 16-core Ryzen 9 8940HX processor, based on Zen 4 architecture. It's paired with an Nvidia GeForce RTX 5070 laptop GPU, which uses Nvidia's Blackwell architecture and features fourth-generation ray tracing and fifth-generation Tensor Cores.
It comes with 16GB of DDR5 RAM, a 1TB SSD, and a 15.3-inch WQXGA IPS display with a 2560 x 1600 resolution, a 180Hz refresh rate, and 100% sRGB color coverage.
The Omen Tempest Cooling system uses dual side fans, enlarged vents, and additional bottom ventilation to help keep the temperature low. Omen Fan Cleaner helps reduce dust buildup.
The laptop runs Windows 11 Home and includes a three-month Microsoft 365 Personal subscription and two months of Xbox Game Pass Premium.
Price context & historical value
Walmart's Black Friday discount knocks nearly $1,100 off the HP HyperX Omen, bringing it down to $1,299. That's an impressive price for a laptop combining a 16-core Ryzen 9 processor, RTX 5070 graphics, and a 2.5K display. It's also the cheapest price we've seen this model sell for.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the HP HyperX Omen if...
You need a powerful laptop for video editing, 3D design, GPU-accelerated applications, or gaming.
❌ Skip the HP HyperX Omen if...
Portability and battery life are your priorities, or your work involves little more than office applications and web browsing. At 5.56 pounds, it's not particularly lightweight, and 16GB of RAM isn't really enough for truly demanding projects.

articles.title: Free, AI-free creative studio NIVA now live as designers push back on automation
articles.text:
'It's not template-based like Canva; it has no AI to do it for you': A free browser studio launches without subscriptions or automated shortcuts
Free browser workspace ditches templates and AI tools
- NIVA reportedly attracted nearly 30,000 users within its first 48 hours
- 56% of early users created something within 40 seconds of access
- Browser-based tools combine photo editing, vector graphics, and graphic layout
A new graphic design platform has attracted nearly 30,000 users within 48 hours of becoming publicly accessible, offering creative tools without subscription fees.
Called NIVA, the browser-based software allows users to produce visual projects without relying on AI tools to generate their designs.
Its launch comes amid growing disagreements over automation and the increasing costs associated with established professional design applications.
A browser-based creative studio attracts thousands of users
British conceptual artist Stuart Semple developed NIVA after becoming concerned about AI increasingly entering software used by professional designers.
Within the first two days of its launch, 56% of users created something within 40 seconds of accessing the software.
That early activity suggests considerable interest in tools that allow users to undertake creative work rather than delegate production to automated systems.
NIVA combines several creative capabilities within an accessible browser environment, removing the need for conventional desktop installations.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Its approach also differs from template-driven services, allowing users to exercise their own judgment when developing visual projects.
“It’s not template-based like Canva, it has no AI to do it for you and it doesn’t have a million features you'd never use. It’s a place to really practise your craft. It’s for people who still believe in making stuff,” Semple said.
The software's emphasis on independent creation comes as artificial intelligence becomes increasingly common across applications used by professional designers.
For creators concerned about automation, the availability of software without AI-generated designs offers another way to approach everyday creative work.
NIVA challenges the direction of established design applications
Adobe has continued expanding artificial intelligence capabilities across its creative software, including applications widely used by professional designers and digital artists, and recently revealed additional AI developments that attracted criticism from some creative professionals.
Concerns include the possibility that increasingly automated workflows could reduce opportunities for designers to practise traditional skills and develop technical expertise.
NIVA takes a different approach by leaving the creative process in users' hands rather than offering automated shortcuts for producing finished work.
Its introduction also comes amid continuing dissatisfaction with subscription-based software, particularly among independent creators facing recurring payments.
Earlier in 2026, Adobe agreed to pay $150 million following a settlement with the US government concerning its subscription and cancellation practices, without admitting wrongdoing.
Although the settlement concerned subscription practices rather than artificial intelligence, it adds context to continuing criticism of established creative software companies.
Semple has criticized software companies for repeatedly charging creators while introducing automated capabilities into applications that professionals depend upon daily.
“Good design comes from taste, emotion and understanding,” said Semple, emphasizing the importance of human judgment in creative production.
The circumstances surrounding NIVA's development also involved an interruption that required its creator to abandon the project's original identity.
Semple acknowledged that legal considerations forced him to start again midway through development, although he declined to discuss the details publicly.
NIVA is now accessible through its website, offering creators worldwide an opportunity to explore its tools without subscriptions, downloads, or artificial intelligence.

Efosa has been writing about technology for over 7 years, initially driven by curiosity but now fueled by a strong passion for the field. He holds both a Master's and a PhD in sciences, which provided him with a solid foundation in analytical thinking.

articles.title: Iran-Aligned Volant Manticore Uses IPFS-Based KuboShell Backdoor in Espionage Campaigns
articles.text:
A previously undocumented Iran-aligned cyber espionage group called Volant Manticore has targeted telecommunications companies, airlines, and critical infrastructure in Cyprus.
Central to the group's operations is a backdoor called KuboShell that uses the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS) for command-and-control (C2) and deploys Homa, a post-compromise framework that's a reimplementation of MuddyWater's MuddyC2Go. Evidence indicates that the threat actor has been operational since late August 2025.
Also delivered alongside these tools are Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) programs like MeshCentral and NetLock RMM. In tandem, the group has been observed orchestrating credential harvesting campaigns to harvest email and corporate credentials of some of the impersonated organizations.
The use of legitimate RMM tools for persistent access has been a hallmark of the MuddyWater group, although the adversary has since also increasingly deployed its own malware in attacks. Both MuddyWater and Volant Manticore are assessed to be affiliated with Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS).
"While we identified multiple links to MuddyWater, we assess that Volant Manticore likely consists of former MuddyWater operators who branched off from the group and currently operate as a separate threat cluster," Check Point said in an analysis published today. "Volant Manticore's targeting priorities appear responsive to regional geopolitical developments."
This assessment is based on the use of an older MuddyWater framework and its playbook, while diverging from established modus operandi over time to incorporate its own attack methods like credential-harvesting campaigns. The targeting of Cyprus, a country that does not align with MuddyWater's targeting patterns, and the use of separate infrastructure points to a group that pursues its own strategic objectives.
Attack chains have been found to leverage artificial intelligence (AI)-generated personas in bogus CVs to trick targets into clicking on a link to download the complete resume, resulting in the deployment of KuboShell on the victim's system. The activity is said to have been aimed at a Cyprus-based airline that operates flights between Cyprus and Israel.
This includes a shift toward Saudi Arabian healthcare entities, coinciding with escalating hostilities between Saudi Arabia and the Iranian-backed Houthis.
"This fits the MOIS's track record of targeting hospitals and healthcare providers through cyber operations during military conflicts, in some cases attempting to disrupt their operations," the cybersecurity company said.
As recently as September 2026, the group has been found to launch a phishing campaign against Saudi targets, distributing the backdoor and N-able RMM through two different healthcare-themed ZIP archives named "AI_Healthcare_Seminar.zip" and "Ai_Healthcare_Seminar_Online.zip," respectively. Some of the emails have been sent from a compromised account belonging to a private hospital in Saudi Arabia.
A Windows backdoor, KuboShell, uses IPFS for C2 and relies on Pinata to facilitate file transfer over the peer-to-peer (P2P) file-sharing network.
"On startup, KuboShell checks whether it has administrator privileges. If not, it tries to relaunch itself with higher privileges, which triggers a User Account Control (UAC) prompt," Check Point explained.
"KuboShell retrieves the MAC address of the machine's first network adapter and uses it as a unique identifier for each victim. It then registers the host by uploading a file containing hi, saved to C:\Users\Public\<MAC>.log, using a hard-coded Pinata access token."
Once registered, KuboShell checks Pinata for a command file named <MAC>.txt, and if the file exists, looks up the file’s IPFS identifier and downloads its contents through Pinata's public gateway. The downloaded content is executed via PowerShell in a hidden window. The results of the execution are saved in a file named "C:\Users\Public\<MAC>re.txt" and uploaded back to the server.
It's worth noting that the backdoor is not responsible for capturing the output. Rather, the results are returned only if the received command writes them to the text file. KuboShell then checks for a new command every 60 seconds.
Analysis indicates that KuboShell is primarily used to run basic reconnaissance commands and assess the compromised environment before downloading and executing a more capable backdoor, which includes the modular Homa Framework. This involves a three-stage process -
- PowerShell stager, which contacts a hard-coded IP address ("185.205.187[.]109:8000") to fetch a PowerShell loader and execute it in memory
- PowerShell loader, which decodes and launches a JavaScript backdoor
- JavaScript Backdoor, which implements a continuous C2 loop to receive and execute PowerShell, SSH, and "cmd.exe" commands
It's suspected that the third-stage backdoor is used to execute additional modules, although the precise nature of those components is presently unknown.
"We assess that Homa's client is a JavaScript reimplementation of the older MuddyC2Go client, potentially allowing Volant Manticore to retain the more complex server-side component with minimal modifications, thereby reducing development time and resources," Check Point said.
The post-compromise framework has also been distributed via a macro-enabled Microsoft Word document called "MilitaryHeritageProposal.doc" that's believed to have targeted a Cypriot defense-related government entity. Enabling the content triggers the execution of a VBA backdoor that serves as a conduit for running follow-up payloads or commands using "cmd.exe."
"Volant Manticore shows how Iran's cyber ecosystem continues to reshape itself," Check Point concluded. "What appears to be a group of former MuddyWater operators now operates independently, pairing legacy MuddyWater tooling with new implants of their own while pursuing a regional focus that has until now drawn little attention."
"If MuddyC2Go is the latest MuddyWater framework Volant Manticore's operators had access to, the split may have happened around 2023 as MuddyWater replaced MuddyC2Go with DarkBeatC2 in late 2023.

articles.title: Cientos de videos falsos de Jensen Huang hechos con IA circulan en redes tras el escándalo de Nvidia
articles.text:
Cientos de videos falsos creados con inteligencia artificial muestran a Jensen Huang, el cofundador de Nvidia, bailando en una discoteca, cantando o apareciendo en escenas de películas. Circulan en Instagram, X y otras redes desde que se conocieron sus infidelidades, y varios suman millones de visualizaciones, según The Verge.
Uno de los más vistos, con casi 6 millones de reproducciones en Instagram, lo muestra en una fiesta en Ibiza con su chaqueta de cuero negra. Es una versión de un meme existente, en el que un obrero británico baila de la misma forma. En la copia, Huang aparece junto a Alice Huang, la ejecutiva china sospechosa de espionaje con quien tuvo una relación.
Entre los otros clips virales figuran una escena de la serie The Office y el video musical de “Careless Whisper”, de George Michael. Otro recrea el momento en que la cámara de besos de un concierto de Coldplay captó el año pasado al entonces director ejecutivo de Astronomer con una empleada. El rapero 50 Cent publicó una edición de su video “P.I.M.P.” con la cara de Huang.
Newsweek informó que el ingeniero belga Peter Dedene creó la versión de Coldplay con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial de código abierto mientras leía noticias sobre Nvidia desde la cama, y que el clip sumó millones de vistas, según The New York Times, citado por esa revista.
Herramientas chinas y chips de Nvidia
El creador de los videos de Ibiza, que se identificó ante The Verge como un hombre de 40 años de Melbourne, Australia, y no dio su nombre, dijo que gastó “miles” de dólares en generación de video. Usa modelos como Seedance 2.5, de ByteDance (la empresa china dueña de TikTok), y Wan 3, de Alibaba. Su cuenta acumula cerca de 100 millones de vistas con distintas versiones del meme, y la agencia AFP señaló que muchos clips se generaron en segundos con esa herramienta.
Varios modelos de video funcionan sobre procesadores de Nvidia, algo que un usuario resumió en un comentario citado por The Verge: sin la empresa, estos memes no serían posibles.
Meta, dueña de Instagram, permite estas ediciones siempre que los creadores avisen de que fueron hechas con IA, aunque AFP indicó que muchos clips circulan sin etiqueta. La compañía no respondió a la consulta del medio.
No todo es humor: audios e imágenes falsas con fines políticos
AFP y France 24 documentaron contenido que no era una broma. Cuentas prochinas difundieron un audio atribuido a Lori Huang, esposa del ejecutivo, en el que supuestamente defiende a Alice Huang, y una imagen que vincula a Huang con el Partido Comunista Chino. La organización NewsGuard, que vigila la desinformación, concluyó que el audio era falso, con un 99% de probabilidad de haber sido generado con IA, según France 24. La imagen también es falsa.
Joshua Tucker, codirector del Centro de Redes Sociales, IA y Política de la Universidad de Nueva York, dijo a AFP que la generación de imágenes y video con IA se usará tanto para engañar como para llamar la atención.
Zohaib Ahmed, director de la firma de detección Resemble AI, afirmó que las parodias de Huang son fáciles de reconocer, pero que el riesgo mayor persiste. Voces clonadas de directivos que piden transferencias y candidatos laborales con la cara cambiada siguen estafando a empresas, advirtió.
Hany Farid, profesor de la Universidad de California en Berkeley, dijo a Newsweek que hoy cualquiera con una descripción escrita puede crear videos sofisticados. A su juicio, estos clips son relativamente inofensivos, pero erosionan la confianza en el contenido visual: cuando aparezca un video real de Huang, será más fácil que él afirme que es falso.
El lunes 23 de noviembre, el directorio de Nvidia anunció que Huang volvió como presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del directorio, tras “una serie de conversaciones y reuniones” y “aportes de altos niveles del gobierno de Estados Unidos”. Desde entonces, según The Verge, aparecieron memes que lo muestran victorioso.

articles.title: BYD négocie le rachat de l’ancienne usine Smart en Moselle
articles.text:
BYD est entré en négociations exclusives avec Ineos pour racheter l'usine de Hambach, en Moselle, où Mercedes fabriquait autrefois la Smart. Si la vente aboutit, le géant chinois de la voiture électrique possédera sa première usine automobile en France.
Si vous y étiez, vous vous souvenez comme si c'était hier que Jacques Chirac et Helmut Kohl avaient inauguré l'usine de Hambach en 1997 pour lancer la Smart, la petite citadine de Mercedes. Le constructeur allemand a ensuite transféré la production de la Smart en Chine, avec Geely, et cédé le site au britannique Ineos fin 2020. Depuis 2022, Ineos fabrique à Hambach son 4x4 Grenadier et sa version pick-up, le Quartermaster. Mais Ineos réalise environ 70 % de ses ventes aux États-Unis, et il a annoncé qu'il produirait ces deux modèles sur le sol américain à partir de 2028. Dans la foulée, les deux constructeurs ont confirmé leurs négociations exclusives pour la vente de Hambach. En fabriquant ses voitures en Moselle, BYD échapperait aux taxes imposées par Bruxelles aux modèles importés de Chine.
BYD veut fabriquer en France pour échapper aux taxes européennes
Depuis fin 2024, l'Union européenne surtaxe les voitures électriques importées de Chine. Les marques chinoises ont alors vendu davantage d'hybrides, qui échappaient à ces droits, et Bruxelles a obtenu de Pékin qu'il divise par deux leurs exportations. À partir du 1er décembre, l'UE limitera ainsi à 350 000 par an les importations d'hybrides chinois. Une voiture assemblée à Hambach ne serait soumise ni à ces taxes ni à ce quota. « Notre ambition est d'y produire des véhicules spécifiquement conçus pour les automobilistes européens », assure BYD dans son communiqué.
Pour sa première usine européenne, à Szeged, en Hongrie, le constructeur avait construit un site neuf, et il doit bientôt lancer la production en série. En juillet, Alfredo Altavilla, son conseiller spécial pour l'Europe, avait annoncé le rachat d'une usine existante, en France ou en Espagne. C'est donc la France qui l'emporte. « Notre projet d'investissement à Hambach reflète notre confiance envers la France », se félicite Stella Li, vice-présidente exécutive de BYD. Le constructeur serait seul propriétaire de son usine française, alors que son compatriote Dongfeng doit fabriquer ses voitures dans l'usine Stellantis de Rennes d'ici 2028, en partenariat avec le groupe.
BYD promet de préserver les emplois de Hambach
Environ 900 personnes travaillent à Hambach, et leurs représentants doivent encore être consultés avant toute vente. BYD se dit « déterminé à pérenniser l'activité industrielle du site, à préserver les emplois locaux et à créer de nouvelles opportunités pour les salariés et les fournisseurs de la région ». Mais on ne sait pas encore combien de postes il gardera, ni quelles voitures sortiront de Hambach. Selon Ineos, le Grenadier et le Quartermaster continueraient d'être produits sur le site « à moyen terme ». Les deux constructeurs pourraient donc partager l'usine jusqu'au départ d'Ineos pour les États-Unis.
Emmanuel Macron a salué l'opération avant toute signature. « BYD travaille avec la France à une implantation industrielle en Moselle ! », a écrit le président sur X, qui parle d'« une conséquence directe » de sa politique économique et de son action européenne sur l'automobile. L'État ouvre ainsi à BYD les portes d'une usine française, mais il aurait refusé à deux reprises son entrée au capital de Renault, dont il est actionnaire.
Le président renvoie les annonces détaillées au sommet Choose France du 18 janvier, à quelques mois de la fin de son mandat. Les salariés de Hambach sauront peut-être alors combien d'entre eux BYD gardera.

articles.title: VMware vCenter Hit by Another Critical 9.8-Rated Auth Bypass Flaw After Zero-Day Exploitation
articles.text:
Broadcom has shipped patches to address 23 vulnerabilities impacting VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation, Fusion, and Avi Load Balancer, including one critical bug that could be abused to bypass authentication.
The critical vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-123903, is rated 9.8 out of 10.0 on the CVSS scoring system. It resides in the VMware Directory Service ("vmdir").
"A malicious actor with network access to vCenter may exploit this issue to bypass authentication and gain unauthorized access to the system," Broadcom said in an advisory released today.
The company credited sglab of QiAnXin, Qi Qin (@LeoQ7_) of depthfirst, and VulTeam and XGTP from ThreatBook for independently reporting the flaw.
Also patched in vCenter are four high-severity flaws, including an arbitrary file write vulnerability while processing certain archives that could be exploited to achieve code execution on the appliance (CVE-2026-123904, CVSS score: 7.5).
The remaining three vulnerabilities relate to denial-of-service in the VMware Directory Service (CVE-2026-123905, CVE-2026-123906, and CVE-2026-123907, CVSS scores: 7.5).
The issues have been addressed in the following versions -
- VMware Cloud Foundation and VMware vSphere Foundation 9.1.x.x - Fixed in 9.1.2
- VMware Cloud Foundation and VMware vSphere Foundation 9.0.x.x - Fixed in 9.0.2.0300
- VMware vCenter 8.0 - Fixed in 8.0 U3m
- VMware vCenter 7.0 (Contact Broadcom Support, if on extended support contract)
- VMware Cloud Foundation 5.x - Fixed in 5.2.5
- VMware Telco Cloud Platform - Fixed in vCenter 8.0 U3m (TCI: 3.0, TCP: 3.0, 4.x, 5.0.x, 5.1.x, 5.2)
- VMware Telco Cloud Infrastructure - Fixed in vCenter 8.0 U3m (TCI: 3.0, TCP: 3.0, 4.x, 5.0.x, 5.1.x, 5.2)
The fixes arrive days after Broadcom shipped updates for CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS score: 9.8), another authentication bypass flaw impacting the VMware Directory Service that was exploited as a zero-day by a suspected China-nexus cyber espionage group called Armory Castle. VMware has noted that CVE-2026-123903 is a distinct issue and is not related to CVE-2026-123890.
While Broadcom makes no mention of any of the newly disclosed flaws as being exploited in the wild, it's essential that customers apply the updates for optimal protection.

articles.title: Pasos para reducir el gasto de datos móviles en iPhone
articles.text:
El iPhone permite ver qué aplicaciones consumen datos móviles y limitar su actividad cuando no se usan. Los ajustes están en la app Configuración: el menú Celular muestra el gasto por aplicación, y los modos de datos reducidos y de actualización en segundo plano frenan las descargas automáticas.
Estos pasos se basan en las páginas de soporte de Apple consultadas en noviembre de 2026. Los nombres de los menús pueden variar según la versión de iOS, el modelo y el operador de telefonía.
Muchas aplicaciones siguen trabajando aunque el usuario no las abra: buscan contenido nuevo, sincronizan fotos o descargan actualizaciones. Si el plan de datos es limitado, esa actividad puede agotar los gigas antes de fin de mes.
Primero, descubrir qué app gasta más
Apple indica abrir Configuración y tocar Celular. Más abajo aparece la lista de aplicaciones y servicios, y al tocar Mostrar todo se ve la cantidad de datos móviles que usó cada una debajo de su nombre.
Esa cifra corresponde al período actual y no se reinicia sola: para empezar de cero hay que bajar hasta el final de la pantalla y tocar Restablecer estadísticas. Apple aclara que, para conocer el consumo exacto de un período de facturación, hay que consultar al operador.
En esa misma lista, cada aplicación tiene un interruptor. Al desactivarlo, la app usa solo Wi-Fi; sin esa red, no podrá conectarse. Los servicios del sistema aparecen aparte, y Apple precisa que no se puede apagar su acceso a los datos móviles de forma individual.
Activar el modo de datos reducidos
El ajuste más general está en Configuración > Celular > Opciones de datos móviles. En iPhone con 5G, se toca Modo de datos y se elige Modo de datos reducidos. En conexiones LTE o 4G, el interruptor aparece directamente en esas opciones. Con dos tarjetas SIM, se elige primero la línea.
Según Apple, el modo existe desde iOS 13 y pausa las actualizaciones automáticas y las tareas en segundo plano. También reduce la calidad de la transmisión de video, detiene las descargas y copias de seguridad automáticas y suspende las actualizaciones de Fotos de iCloud.
Las aplicaciones de Apple se adaptan de forma propia: App Store desactiva la reproducción automática de video y las descargas automáticas, y Podcasts solo baja episodios con Wi-Fi. El modo también puede activarse por separado para cada red Wi-Fi, desde el botón de información junto a su nombre.
Limitar la actualización en segundo plano
Para un recorte menos radical, se puede ajustar la actualización en segundo plano: Configuración > General > Actualización en segundo plano. Allí se elige entre Desactivada, Wi-Fi o Wi-Fi y datos móviles. La opción Wi-Fi evita esa actividad en la red celular. Debajo, una lista permite apagarla aplicación por aplicación.
Este ajuste no bloquea todo el consumo: un video que el usuario reproduce o una descarga que inicia siguen usando datos. Tampoco equivale a silenciar notificaciones. Para impedir que una app use la red celular por completo, hay que desactivarla en Celular.
Si la actualización en segundo plano aparece desactivada o no disponible, conviene revisar si están activos el modo de datos reducidos o el modo de bajo consumo, que también la apagan. Un perfil de administración de la empresa o la escuela puede imponer restricciones adicionales.
Para comprobar el efecto, conviene anotar las cifras de la lista de aplicaciones antes de los cambios y compararlas después de un período de uso similar. Apple no publica cuántos datos ahorra cada ajuste, por lo que el resultado depende de las apps instaladas y de los hábitos de uso.

articles.title: The analog photography craze is real, and this Polaroid Now Gen 3 is the right gift to rekindle anyone's love afair with prints
articles.text:
The analog photography craze is real, and this Polaroid Now Gen 3 is the right gift to rekindle anyone's love afair with prints
Point, shoot, and smile
It's not even Black Friday yet, and I've already spotted a pair of great deals on an iconic, analog camera, the Polaroid Now Gen 3. In one case, the price drops from $119 to a very attractive $94.99.
In our increasingly intangible world, there's nothing quite like holding a slowly developing Polaroid photo in your hand. The frame is small, the imagery not quite as sharp as what you can see on a screen, but it oozes warmth and nostalgia. Plus, you can pin it to your wall or fridge, or hand the photos out to New Year's Eve partygoers.
• Browse all today's best Black Friday deals
I know there isn't much logic to the current love affair we're having with analog photography, but for those of us old enough to remember when it was the only kind of photography, the moment is oddly gratifying.
So seeing one of Polaroid's best and easiest-to-use cameras as part of early Black Friday sales seems, if not cause for celebration, then at least worth noting and passing along to anyone ready to take the analog plunge.
This is the classic Polaroid you've been looking for. It's a simple point-and-shoot that spits out real, slow-developing prints. If you were looking for a return to analog photography, there's no better place to start than this. Just remember that film is kind of pricey.
Why this camera
Of all of Polaroid's growing line of point-and-shoot analog cameras, the Now line most resembles their iconic Polaroid 600s of the last century. And with few exceptions, it works just like it.
Boasting a classic look, the Polaroid Now Generation 3 is equipped with zero digital features and works much like the classic 600 line, right down to supporting Polaroid 600 film (it also supports the newer Polaroid i-Type film).
Unlike the original Polaroid cameras, however, the battery no longer comes with the 8-shot instant photo packs. Instead, like the rest of the modern Polaroid line, it's a rechargeable camera.
It does have a built-in flash and even twin lenses, which help with autofocus.
This is the classic Polaroid you've been looking for. It's a simple point-and-shoot that spits out real, slow-developing prints. If you were looking for a return to analog photography, there's no better place to start than this. Even though the film is kind of pricey, this better-than-most deal will leave you with enough bucks to afford at least one film pack.
If you're giving the camera as a gift, it's worth reminding the gift recipient that photos taken with the Polaroid Now Gen 3 will take 10 minutes or more to fully develop. Even then, they should not directly compare them with photos taken with a DSLR or even their best smartphone.
I've seen numerous Black Friday deals for this camera; some bundle a starter set of film, others do not.
The Best Buy Deal, slices $20 off the list price but does not include a starter film pack. Amazon's deal on effectively the same camera (with no film included) drops the price from $119.99 to 94.99! That sounds like a steal.
Just remember, film packs can start at $20, so be sure to include at least a couple with the gift.

articles.title: US DOJ touts "largest-ever" crackdown on scammers across the globe as it seizes 14,000 devices and $17 billion in illicit funds — operation results in 800 defendants and frees 2,200 forced scam laborers
articles.text:
US DOJ touts "largest-ever" crackdown on scammers across the globe as it seizes 14,000 devices and $17 billion in illicit funds — operation results in 800 defendants and frees 2,200 forced laborers
More than 400 criminal cases have been filed across 85 federal districts in the U.S. alone.
The United States Department of Justice announced today that more than 800 defendants have been charged and over $8 billion in intended victim losses have been recovered in what it describes as the "largest ever" crackdown on scammers and fraudsters in its history. The charges have led to over 400 cases, filed across 85 federal districts, with outcomes including extraditions, guilty pleas, and prison sentences for those involved.
"We are not just going after individual scammers," Fox News reports U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche as saying. "We are dismantling the criminal networks that have been stealing from the American people for far too long."
The push follows President Donald Trump's executive order from March, which required a government-wide crackdown on the kinds of fraud and predatory schemes that people fall victim to each and every day across the country.
FBI Director Kash Patel also gave details of Operation Blackout, an interagency project that targets international fraudsters running centralized facilities. Patel said that FBI agents, alongside their international counterparts, have dismantled 29 centralized compounds across Asia, Africa, and the Middle East. The department claims those agents have seized almost $17 billion in funds, that more than 14,000 involved devices have been confiscated, and that 50 "scam actors" have been brought up on U.S. federal charges. The FBI also says its support allowed its foreign partners to arrest or detain more than 320 criminals in foreign jurisdictions.
Perhaps most importantly, these compounds often use human trafficking victims to run online scams. Patel claims that more than 2,200 trafficked workers have been freed as a result of the initiative.
Global scams and hacking are an ongoing problem for the United States and its citizens, not to mention its businesses, big and small. Just last month, more than $5 million in gift cards were stolen from Staples before being used at retailers like Target and Lowes. A Chinese crime ring was behind that attack, which involved more than 15,000 cards.
Earlier this year, a Chinese phishing service was dismantled after it used AI tools to build scam websites linked to almost $2 billion in losses. An October report even detailed a computer, hidden behind a Japanese hotel room fridge, that was responsible for more than 480,000 phishing emails.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The problem is only likely to get worse as the capabilities and availability of AI tools continue to expand. U.S. banks have scrambled to restrict AI agent activity over concerns about what they could do to customer accounts. Some banks raised the alarm after detecting agents accessing customer accounts and even attempting to process transactions. Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan, and Wells Fargo are among those that have blocked the agents while updating their terms of service accordingly.
That growing threat only emphasizes the fact that the department has much work left to do. The $17 billion seized by the FBI is only a portion of the estimated $68 billion Americans lost to scams in 2025, according to Gallup data, so the ongoing game of cat and mouse between the government and criminal enterprises the world over will only continue.

articles.title: Bornes de recharge : toujours plus de vols, toujours moins de nouvelles installations
articles.text:
Pour l'électrification de la flotte automobile française, il va falloir bénéficier d'une infrastructure solide. Mais le déploiement fait face à des problèmes aujourd'hui évidents !
En France, le gouvernement espère pouvoir atteindre les 400 000 bornes de recharge publique pour automobiles électriques à l'horizon 2030. Mais pour cela, il faut pouvoir tenir une forte cadence d'installations de nouvelles bornes de recharge, et faire en sorte que le réseau existant fonctionne bien. Or, nous avons encore des problèmes sur ces deux points.
Le nombre de nouvelles bornes de recharge installées bien plus faible en 2026 que l'année précédente
Le dernier baromètre publié par l'Avere nous montre une claire décélération du nombre de nouvelles bornes de recharge en France. Au mois d'octobre, celles-ci ont été de 1 189 unités.
Ce qui donne, pour les dix premiers mois de l'année, 18 940 nouvelles bornes de recharge publique qui ont vu le jour en France. Un chiffre qui, quand il est comparé à celui des dix premiers mois de l'année 2025, à savoir plus de 26 000, fait clairement pâle figure.
Le volume de bornes de recharge indisponibles plus de 7 jours consécutifs atteint un record
Si l'on regarde l'ensemble du réseau, on peut comptabiliser à la fin du mois d'octobre 2026 un ensemble de 203 993 bornes de recharge électrique - ce qui peut apparaître intéressant, mais aussi encore clairement très loin des fameux 400 000 bornes d'ici 2030.
Et en plus, il faut ajouter que le réseau existant est aujourd'hui malheureusement la victime d'une explosion de vols de câble durant l'année 2026. Plus de 850 sites ont ainsi été touchés depuis le début de l'année. Résultat, la part des points de recharge électrique indisponibles durant plus de 7 jours consécutifs a pour la toute première fois atteint les 10%. Autant dire qu'il y a clairement devant nous un phénomène qui va demander de nouvelles réponses.
Source : BeVolt

articles.title: Okta Links ShinyHunters-Associated Vishing Group to New INCEPTION Data Leak Site
articles.text:
A threat cluster previously assessed to be affiliated with the ShinyHunters extortion crew may have rebranded and continued operations under a new name called INCEPTION, according to Okta's Threat Intelligence team.
The cluster, dubbed O-UNC-053, is characterized by the use of voice phishing (aka vishing) attacks to trick targets into entering credentials in phishing pages and approving multi-factor authentication (MFA). Okta said it's been tracking the group since March 2026.
The identity and access management provider said targets of this cluster previously had stolen data published to the ShinyHunters data leak site (DLS). However, as of November 16, 2026, a new data leak site operating under the name INCEPTION has listed the data siphoned from O-UNC-053 targets.
"While this threat cluster has changed their brand affiliation, the operators remain active in targeting organizations with voice phishing attacks and account takeovers resulting in data theft and extortion," Okta researchers Moussa Diallo and Katie Nickels said in a report shared with The Hacker News.
Social engineering and credential harvesting attacks mounted by O-UNC-053 have targeted a broad range of sectors, including technology, healthcare, biotechnology, financial services, insurance, entertainment, gaming, retail, transportation, hospitality, and legal.
Similar to O-UNC-066 and UNC6671, the newly identified cluster also relies on a phishing kit to intercept authentication flows and capture a user's credentials and MFA codes. However, the kit is not designed to bypass phishing-resistant methods like passkeys and Okta FastPass.
"While interacting with targeted users on the phone, the operators socially engineer them into sharing factors like one-time passcodes and approving push notifications," Okta said. "If successful, the operators gain access to SaaS applications and exfiltrate sensitive data, which is often used to extort targets under the threat of releasing it on a data leak site."
Domains created by the group are registered through NiceNIC, Spaceship, Tucows, and NameSilo, with the domain names using the following patterns -
- legal-<target>[.]com
- legaldept-<target>[.]com
- <target>[.]legal
- <target>-legal[.]com
The use of "legal" themes in these attacks is said to have started in October 2026, and is often registered on or within a day of a campaign starting. Prior campaign waves have employed help desk-, support-, and claims-related themes for the registered domains.
These findings also dovetail with an alert from Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, which has warned of widespread vishing activity using legal-themed domains that either begin with "legal-" or end with "-legal" using the ".com" top-level domain.
More than 70 such domains have been observed since October 2026, it said, adding each domain is specifically created for an intended target operating in different industries, like cryptocurrency, financial services, healthcare, high technology, and hospitality, among others.
"Registered in rapid evening batches and shielded behind Cloudflare, these web-only domains deploy a filtered kit that delivers tailored content to intended victims while routing visitors it is not configured to attack to the targeted organization's legitimate Okta or NetIQ sign-in flow," ReversingLabs researcher Robert Simmons said.
Some of the confirmed domains linked to the activity are listed below -
- legal-pepsico[.]com
- legal-paychex[.]com
- legal-duolingo[.]com
- activisionblizzard-legal[.]com
- legal-westernunion[.]com
- legal-dropbox[.]com
- legal-indeed[.]com
- legal-creditkarma[.]com
- legal-amd[.]com
- legal-grubhub[.]com
- legal-twitch[.]tv
The crux of the campaign is to tailor the landing page to the specific identity provider of the target, while filtering unwanted visitors and forwarding them to the organization's authentication infrastructure, such as Okta.
"Throughout our tracking of O-UNC-053 between March and September 2026, we observed the names of targeted entities appear on the ShinyHunters DLS between 1 and 28 days after the phishing infrastructure was registered," Okta noted.
However, it's unclear at this stage if the published data on the INCEPTION site is authentic and whether they are running the site themselves or are collaborating with another extortion gang. The exact nature of the relationship between ShinyHunters and O-UNC-053 is also unknown.
It's worth noting that the ShinyHunters data leak site went offline in late September 2026 following the arrest of three alleged members of the group, including a Canadian co-conspirator responsible for the breach of the FBIjobs.gov portal.
There is no evidence of data from O-UNC-053 targets being published on any data leak site from early September 2026 through October and early November 2026, until listings for multiple targets appeared on the INCEPTION site last week.
"This gap in publishing on any leak site followed by publishing on a new data leak site with a new brand is consistent with prior shifts from Com-affiliated actors," Okta said. "Regardless of the nature of the relationship with the INCEPTION DLS, O-UNC-053 remains active in conducting vishing attacks against targets in an effort to take over accounts, steal data, and extort targets."
INCEPTION Denies ShinyHunters Link
In a post on their dark web site, INCEPTION has denied any affiliation with ShinyHunters, insisting that it operates independently with its own members and objectives.
"We are not ShinyHunters. We were never ShinyHunters. We are INCEPTION," the group said, adding "certain parties in the threat intelligence industry have been eager to give us a history we never asked for."
"We are also not copying anyone. If our methodology resembles what came before, it is because we took inspiration from operators who, whatever else may be said of them, understood that the weakest component of any secure system is a human being holding a phone. That is not theft of tradecraft. It is acknowledgment of a good idea -- the same way every group after LockBit used a leak site, and nobody called them LockBit."
(The story was updated after publication to include a statement posted by INCEPTION on its dark web site.)

articles.title: Más de 150 organizaciones piden a Amazon y eBay que dejen de vender juguetes con chatbots de IA
articles.text:
Una coalición de más de 155 organizaciones y especialistas en infancia pidió a Amazon y eBay que suspendan la venta de juguetes con chatbots de inteligencia artificial integrados, durante estas fiestas y hasta que pruebas independientes demuestren que son seguros para los niños.
La carta fue enviada a Andy Jassy, presidente de Amazon, y a Jamie Iannone, presidente de eBay. La encabeza Fairplay, una organización estadounidense sin fines de lucro que defiende a la infancia frente a la tecnología, y la firman, entre otros, Zero to Three, Set@16, Alliance 4 Children y el movimiento The Anxious Generation, del psicólogo Jonathan Haidt.
Los firmantes representan a todos los continentes excepto la Antártida. Entre los especialistas figuran la pediatra Jenny Radesky, la profesora de la Universidad de Chicago Dana Suskind y la exministra británica Andrea Leadsom.
Según NBC News, Amazon dijo que había retirado algunos de los juguetes con IA que esa cadena de noticias y un grupo de consumidores habían probado recientemente. Amazon y eBay no habían respondido públicamente al pedido en las fuentes consultadas.
Cuatro exigencias concretas
La coalición pide suspender todos los anuncios de juguetes con chatbots generativos dirigidos a menores de 16 años o que probablemente usen. También reclama que sigan fuera de venta hasta que un análisis independiente evalúe los daños psicológicos, de desarrollo y de privacidad, además de los físicos.
Otra exigencia es eliminar las ofertas que presentan al chatbot como amigo, compañero emocional o herramienta de “crecimiento emocional”, y corregir las que se contradicen sobre la edad. La cuarta es avisar a quienes ya compraron uno sobre los riesgos y ofrecerles reembolso.
Las organizaciones pidieron a ambas empresas que respondan antes de Navidad, para trasladar esa información al Congreso de Estados Unidos, al Parlamento británico y a los padres.
“Los mercados son responsables de la seguridad de lo que venden y ya retiran productos peligrosos”, sostiene la carta. Rachel Franz, directora del programa de infancia de Fairplay, dijo que las tiendas han retirado juguetes uno por uno cuando se los señala, pero que eso “no es suficiente”.
Qué encontraron en los anuncios
Fairplay informó que se hallaron más de 50 juguetes con IA a la venta en Amazon en Estados Unidos y casi 30 en Amazon en el Reino Unido a fines de octubre. Muchos títulos decían “para niños de 3 años o más”, mientras que la ficha del propio producto indicaba edades de 16 a 18 años.
Un conejo de peluche para mayores de 3 años se conectaba a chatbots generales como ChatGPT, cuyas condiciones de uso exigen tener al menos 13 años. Varios anuncios ofrecían clonar la voz de familiares o seguir el “crecimiento emocional” del niño, y la mayoría de los juguetes los vendían comerciantes externos poco conocidos.
La coalición cita casos en los que estos juguetes mantuvieron conversaciones sexuales con niños o indicaron dónde encontrar cuchillos y fósforos. Alliance 4 Children probó el conejo de peluche y, según The Guardian, el juguete sugirió que un niño podía dar su consentimiento para ser tocado con fines de placer.
La coalición advierte también que la inteligencia artificial de un juguete puede cambiarse a distancia, de modo que su comportamiento puede variar de un día para otro.
Presión regulatoria creciente
La carta recuerda que California prohibirá desde enero de 2027 los juguetes con chatbots de compañía para menores de 16 años, y que en el Congreso de Estados Unidos se presentó un proyecto para vetar los chatbots de IA en juguetes infantiles.
En el Reino Unido, parlamentarios pidieron a Amazon y eBay quitar estos productos y propusieron usar la Ley de Protección del Consumidor de 1987 para prohibirlos, según la agencia PA. El Gobierno británico dijo que investiga con urgencia los riesgos, y su Oficina de Seguridad y Estándares de Productos recibió aportes sobre la normativa de juguetes entre julio y octubre.
El plazo que fijó la coalición para que Amazon y eBay contesten vence en Navidad.

articles.title: Vous payez Amazon Prime ? Ce forfait B&YOU 170 Go l’inclut à 14,99€ pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
Prime Video, livraison Premium et forfait mobile sur une seule facture : c’est la formule des Packs B&YOU, dont Bouygues Telecom a écoulé 5 000 exemplaires en une semaine de Black Friday, versions Prime et Deezer confondues. Le B&YOU Pack Amazon Prime 170 Go passe à 14,99 €/mois au lieu de 17,99 €, une baisse de 3 € qui mérite le calcul, surtout si vous payez déjà Prime à part.
Lancé le 5 octobre, le B&YOU Pack Amazon Prime associe un forfait mobile sans engagement de 170 Go en 5G et un abonnement Amazon Prime, compris dans le prix. Pour le Black Friday, Bouygues Telecom l’affiche à 14,99 € par mois au lieu de 17,99 €, soit 3 € de moins chaque mois. L’enveloppe comprend 60 Go utilisables en Europe et dans les DOM, ainsi que les appels, SMS et MMS illimités en France métropolitaine.
L’offre vise d’abord ceux qui regardent Prime Video ou commandent régulièrement sur Amazon, et qui veulent un forfait bien doté en data. Elle est réservée à l’ouverture d’une nouvelle ligne sur le site de l’opérateur.
Le B&YOU Pack Amazon Prime, 170 Go en 5G sans engagement, passe à 14,99 €/mois au lieu de 17,99 € chez Bouygues Telecom pour le Black Friday.
Pourquoi choisir le B&YOU Pack Amazon Prime ?
- Amazon Prime sans abonnement à part : Prime Video, la livraison Premium gratuite sur des millions d’articles, les offres réservées aux membres et l’accès anticipé aux Ventes Flash sont compris dans le forfait. Le tout figure sur une seule facture.
- 170 Go en 5G pour les gros consommateurs : L’enveloppe laisse de la marge pour regarder des séries ou partager la connexion en déplacement. En voyage, 60 Go restent utilisables en Europe et dans les DOM.
- Un forfait qui se quitte facilement : Sans engagement, il se résilie quand vous le souhaitez, pour 5 €. À l’entrée, comptez 1 € pour la carte SIM et 1 € de frais d’activation.
Séries dans le train, colis et data en voyage : à qui sert ce pack
Le premier usage tient dans le nom : Prime Video se regarde sur le téléphone comme sur les autres écrans, et les 170 Go en 5G permettent de lancer un épisode dans le train sans surveiller sa consommation. La livraison Premium gratuite parle aussi à ceux qui commandent souvent sur Amazon. Hors de France, les 60 Go d’Europe et des DOM couvrent un séjour à Madère, en Grèce ou à la Réunion. Une fois l’enveloppe épuisée, l’internet mobile et les MMS hors France métropolitaine sont facturés aux tarifs en vigueur.
Le pack intéresse surtout le lecteur qui paie aujourd’hui Prime à part, à 6,99 € par mois, et un forfait de l’autre côté. Il est moins pertinent si vous êtes déjà client B&YOU, puisqu’il est réservé à une première souscription sur une nouvelle ligne. Les abonnés Prime actuels doivent d’abord résilier leur abonnement en direct, puis se reconnecter avec leurs identifiants pour retrouver leur historique. Et si vous voyagez souvent hors d’Europe, une enveloppe internationale plus large vous servira mieux.
Prime dans le forfait, ou deux abonnements séparés ?
Le calcul se fait en deux temps. Prime coûte 6,99 € par mois à part : à 14,99 €, la partie forfait revient donc à 8 € pour 170 Go en 5G, alors que notre comparatif des meilleurs forfaits mobiles relevait début novembre des offres 5G de 100 Go dès 11,99 € chez RED by SFR et de 13,99 € chez B&YOU. En contrepartie, le service disparaît en cas de résiliation ou au moindre changement d’offre, même vers un autre forfait B&YOU. Le voyageur hors d’Europe regardera plutôt le B&YOU 200 Go Voyage, affiché à 15,99 € au lancement des Packs, avec 40 Go utilisables dans plus de 160 destinations.
✅ Les points forts
- Amazon Prime inclus, d’une valeur de 6,99 €/mois
- 170 Go en 5G, dont 60 Go en Europe et dans les DOM
- Appels, SMS et MMS illimités en France métropolitaine
- 3 € de remise par mois pour le Black Friday
- Sans engagement, sur une seule facture
❌ Les limites
- Réservé à une première souscription sur une nouvelle ligne
- Prime perdu en cas de résiliation ou de changement d’offre
- Abonnés Prime actuels : résiliation préalable obligatoire
- Série spéciale proposée en quantité limitée
Prime déduit, la data revient à 8 € par mois : le B&YOU Pack Amazon Prime reste à 14,99 € chez Bouygues Telecom, en série limitée.

articles.text:
Black Friday business monitor deals: 4 productivity screens from $160 — led by my favorite Dell pick
Stay productive
I've uncovered some great Black Friday business monitor deals if you're looking to boost your productivity.
My top overall pick for most professionals is the Dell 27 Plus QHD, which is down to $160 (was $220) at Amazon. This 27-inch 1440p IPS panel at 144Hz, delivers sharper, smoother monitor for work - we tested out its sister model and absolutely loved it.
But since everyone's workflow is different, I've also selected three more monitor deals from LG, Samsung, and Asus, with 32-inch, 34-inch, and 49-inch picks for total immersion.
Today's top business monitor deals
A 27-inch IPS panel with a 2560 x 1440 resolution, 144Hz refresh rate, 1ms MPRT response time, and 1500:1 contrast ratio. It has HDMI and DisplayPort 1.4 inputs, two built-in 3W speakers, AMD FreeSync, and a 4-star TÜV eye comfort rating for lower blue light. The stand adjusts for height, tilt, swivel, and pivot.
A 34-inch 21:9 curved VA panel with an 1800R curve, 3440 x 1440 resolution, and a 100Hz refresh rate. It supports HDR10 and 99% of the sRGB color gamut, and inputs include HDMI, DisplayPort, and USB-C with 65W power delivery. LG's OnScreen Control software lets you split the screen, and Picture-by-Picture shows two sources at once. The stand adjusts for height and tilt.
A 49-inch QD-OLED panel with a 32:9 aspect ratio, Dual QHD resolution (5120 x 1440), a 144Hz refresh rate, a 0.03ms response time, and an 1800R curve. It's VESA DisplayHDR True Black 400 certified, supports AMD FreeSync Premium Pro and G-Sync Compatible, and includes logo and taskbar detection plus a thermal system to reduce burn-in risk.
A 32-inch WOLED panel at 3840 x 2160 and 240Hz, with a dual mode that drops to 1920 x 1080 at 480Hz. It has a 0.03ms response time, VESA DisplayHDR True Black 400, 99% DCI-P3 coverage, two HDMI 2.1 ports, DisplayPort 1.4, and USB-C with 90W charging. A custom passive heatsink keeps it cool without a fan, and ASUS's warranty runs three years, including burn-in.
Why we recommend them
We haven't reviewed the exact Dell 27 Plus model, but we gave its sibling, the Dell 27 Plus QHD USB-C (S2725DC), an Editor's Choice award in our Dell 27 Plus QHD USB-C review, calling it a perfect budget business monitor for any office. The S2725DSM drops the USB-C port but adds a faster 144Hz refresh rate, which makes it a better fit for scrolling timelines and documents. Built-in speakers are a nice bonus, but you'll still want real speakers or headphones for music and games.
At 34-inches, the LG 34WR55QK-B ultrawide is one of the best productivity upgrades you can make. You get roughly the width of two smaller monitors in one seamless screen, and USB-C lets one cable carry video and charge your laptop up to 65W. It's a work-first monitor, so 100Hz is smooth for everyday use but not for competitive gaming, and it has no built-in speakers.
The Samsung 49-inch ultrawide monitor gives you the screen space of two 27-inch 1440p monitors without a bezel down the middle, which is great for racing and flight games and for keeping several windows open side by side. QD-OLED adds perfect blacks and rich color, and Samsung's burn-in protection features help with the taskbars and static windows that come with desktop use. Amazon buyers rate it 4.3 out of 5. The G91SD tops out at 144Hz, and that's the main trade-off compared with Samsung's pricier 240Hz G9 models.
Our sister site Tom's Hardware gave the Asus ROG Swift OLED PG32UCDP an Editor's Choice award in its review, praising its image quality in both SDR and HDR, its accurate color, and its gaming performance. In testing, it hit 706 nits with a 25% window in HDR, which is very bright for an OLED. The reviewer had nothing negative to say beyond the price. Now at $799, that's now far easier to swallow with this Black Friday deal.
For more top picks, we've tested the best business monitors.
Price Context & Historical Value
We don't have much price history on the Dell 27 Plus, but it's hard to find a fully adjustable 1440p 144Hz IPS monitor from a major brand for less.
For the LG monitor, coming in under $260 is a very good price for a 34-inch ultrawide with USB-C charging from a major brand.
Samsung lists the G91SD at $1,299.99. Amazon has sold it for $799.99 several times this year, so $795.99 is just below that and in line with the best prices we've seen. If you've been waiting for a deal on this monitor, this is it.
The PG32UCDP launched at $1,299.99, and Amazon's best prices earlier this year were $899.99 and $949.99. At $799, this is the lowest price we've seen on it.
Should You Buy It?
✅ Buy the Dell 27 Plus QHD if... you're upgrading from a 1080p screen, you want smooth scrolling, or you need a stand that adjusts to fit your desk.
✅ Buy the LG 34WR55QK-B if... you want to replace a dual-monitor setup with one screen, you use a USB-C laptop and want one-cable charging, or you work in spreadsheets, timelines, or several windows at once.
✅ Buy the Samsung Odyssey OLED G9 (G91SD) if... you want the most immersive screen for racing, flight, and open-world games, you'd like to replace two monitors with one, or you want OLED picture quality on a huge canvas.
✅ Buy the ASUS ROG Swift PG32UCDP if... you have a graphics card that can push 4K at high frame rates, or a monitor that can pull double duty for work and play.

articles.title: Hackers Found a Way Around GitHub SHA Pinning. This Webinar Explains How to Close the Gap
articles.text:
Pinning GitHub Actions to an exact version of their code, known as SHA pinning, has become the go-to defense against software supply chain attacks. Attackers have already found a way around it.
In March 2026, the hackers who hijacked Trivy, a widely used open-source security scanner, planted malicious code that looked like it came from GitHub's official checkout tool. They even labeled it a security fix. Teams pinned to it would have passed every check.
The trick works because GitHub lets copies of a project, called forks, share code with the original. In May, the same technique hit the popular actions-cool/issues-helper tool, stealing credentials from the pipelines that ran it.
The lesson: pinning guarantees the code won't change, but not who wrote it.
That gap is the focus of an upcoming webinar, GitHub Actions Security Beyond SHA Pinning. If your team treats pinning as the finish line, save your seat to learn what it actually protects you from, and what it doesn't.
Immutability Is Not Provenance
Pinning earned its reputation. When the tj-actions/changed-files compromise repointed tags to a malicious commit across more than 23,000 repositories in March 2025, teams that had pinned to SHAs were unaffected.
GitHub now lets administrators enforce pinning as an organization-wide policy, and few security teams argue against it.
📅 Save Your Spot: Learn Why “Best Practice” Won’t Stop the Next GitHub Actions Attack
But a pinned SHA leaves three questions unanswered:
- Authorship: A SHA doesn't tell you who wrote the commit. Any fork commit can be pinned.
- Project membership: Org-level enforcement checks that a reference is a 40-character SHA, not that the commit actually lives in the upstream project.
- Runtime: A Docker-based action pinned to a SHA can still build its image at runtime, pulling in dependencies that were never frozen.
With agentic development pushing more code through CI than ever, each of those gaps gets exercised more often and reviewed less closely.
GitHub's Lockfiles Help. They Don't Finish the Job.
GitHub's 2026 Actions security roadmap, published March 26, put deterministic dependency locking front and center. Workflow lockfiles entered public preview on October 14 and became generally available on October 28, 2026. They tie every run to recorded commits for actions and their transitive dependencies, even if a tag moves later.
That's real progress. Locked commits must exist on a branch of the source repository, which blunts fork-only impostors. But GitHub's own changelog is clear that locking "does not determine whether the dependency itself is safe." Commit authorship and runtime builds remain open; immutable releases only help when maintainers opt in, and lockfiles aren't currently supported on GitHub Enterprise Server.
Not sure where your pipelines fall in that gap? Register for the webinar for a clear-eyed breakdown of what GitHub's roadmap fixes and what it still leaves to you.
What You'll Learn
Led by Erika Heidi, Staff Developer Relations Engineer at Chainguard, the session draws a hard line between immutability and provenance, and covers:
- What org-level pin enforcement actually verifies, and the false confidence it can create
- How impostor commits work, and why GitHub's repository network makes them possible
- What GitHub's Actions roadmap addresses, and what it doesn't
- Other ways to close the trust gap, including a curated catalog of vetted actions
Who Should Attend
Platform and DevOps engineers who own CI/CD, AppSec and DevSecOps teams writing pipeline policy, and security leaders who signed off on SHA pinning as "done." If your workflows pull in third-party actions, this session is for you.
Attackers have already shown they can disguise a malicious commit as a hardening fix. The next one won't announce itself either.
Register now for GitHub Actions Security Beyond SHA Pinning, pick the session time that works for you, and find out what your pins aren't telling you.

articles.title: Black Friday : Amazon réduit de moitié le prix de son nouveau réveil connecté Echo Time
articles.text:
L’Amazon Echo Time est un réveil connecté personnalisable qui intègre l’assistant vocal Alexa. Pour le Black Friday, son prix dégringole de 51 % : il passe de 214,99 € à 104,99 €.
Près de 215 € pour un réveil connecté, vous trouvez ça trop cher ? Il semblerait qu’Amazon soit d’accord avec vous. Durant le Black Friday, le cybermarchand a décidé de diviser par deux le prix de son Echo Time, afin de le proposer à 104,99 € au lieu de 214,99 €. La remise est précisément de 51 %. Facile à installer sur une table de nuit, ce réveil doté d’un écran rond intègre Alexa, et donne même un accès anticipé à Alexa+.
Le réveil connecté Amazon Echo Time est à 104,99 € pour le Black Friday, contre un prix de référence de 214,99 €.
Pourquoi choisir l’Amazon Echo Time ?
- Pour son affichage personnalisable : des centaines de cadrans permettent d’adapter l’horloge à vos goûts, et l'écran réduit sa luminosité la nuit.
- Pour ses fonctions audio : musique, podcasts et sons d’ambiance sont accessibles à la voix, selon les services utilisés.
- Pour ses commandes domotiques : vous pouvez piloter un éclairage ou d’autres appareils compatibles depuis votre lit grâce à Alexa.
Un réveil qui ne fait pas que vous sortir du lit le matin
L’Echo Time dispose d’un écran tactile circulaire de 3,2 pouces et, contrairement à beaucoup d’appareils connectés de ce type, il n’embarque pas de caméra. Outre le fait que l’affichage de son écran soit personnalisable et qu’un vaste choix de sonneries soit proposé pour vous réveiller le matin, vous pouvez utiliser ce réveil connecté de différentes manières. Vous pouvez l’utiliser pour écouter de la musique, des podcasts et même des sons relaxants en faisant une simple demande vocale à Alexa.
Avec Alexa+, une fonction facultative utilise également des ultrasons pour estimer les phases de sommeil léger et adapter le déclenchement de l’alarme avant l’heure programmée, afin de vous réveiller plus en douceur. Son utilisation s’active manuellement et implique de laisser les microphones activés.
Plus complet qu’un réveil classique, moins polyvalent qu’un Echo Show
Si l’Amazon Echo Time est parfaitement adapté à une chambre à coucher, il ne dispose pas de certaines fonctionnalités que l’on trouve dans les appareils Echo Show. Il est impossible, par exemple, de s’en servir pour regarder des vidéos malgré la présence d’un écran.
✅ Les points forts
- Écran personnalisable avec affichage adapté à la nuit.
- Sons d’ambiance et alarmes progressives.
- Absence de caméra et bouton de désactivation des microphones.
❌ Les limites
- Pas de streaming vidéo ni d’appels vidéo.
- Support orientable vendu séparément.
L’Amazon Echo Time est disponible pour 104,99 € durant le Black Friday grâce à une réduction de 110 €.
Si vous disposez déjà d’enceintes connectées Echo Show, alors l’Amazon Echo Time peut représenter un complément de choix pour étoffer votre écosystème connecté. C’est une belle façon d’inviter Alexa et tous ses avantages sur votre table de nuit.
Si vous utilisez déjà votre smartphone pour vous réveiller le matin ou si vous n’avez pas l’habitude d’utiliser Alexa au quotidien, cet investissement est peut-être moins pertinent. Il peut, malgré tout, faire office de porte d’entrée dans l’univers Echo d’Amazon.

articles.title: Cómo saber lo que hacen tus hijos en WhatsApp: aplica para adolescentes
articles.text:
WhatsApp habilitó desde septiembre de 2026 una herramienta de supervisión parental que permite a un adulto vincular su cuenta con la de un adolescente de 13 a 17 años para fijar reglas de privacidad, limitar el acceso a Canales, Estados y Meta AI, y recibir alertas de actividad. Los mensajes y llamadas del joven siguen protegidos por cifrado de extremo a extremo: nadie fuera del chat, ni siquiera la aplicación, puede verlos ni oírlos.
La función es opcional y se despliega de forma gradual, por lo que puede no aparecer todavía en la configuración de algunos teléfonos. WhatsApp la presentó el 30 de septiembre en su blog oficial, donde la describió como herramientas que padres e hijos configuran juntos.
Cómo vincular las dos cuentas
Según la página oficial, el proceso empieza en el teléfono del adolescente: en Ajustes se toca Control parental, se confirma la fecha de nacimiento y se siguen las indicaciones para enlazar la cuenta de un adulto. La interfaz puede variar según el idioma y la versión de la app.
Bitdefender, empresa de seguridad informática, describe el flujo completo. En el teléfono del adolescente aparece un código QR. El adulto lo escanea con la cámara de su teléfono, entra al enlace y completa una verificación de que es mayor de edad.
Después crea un PIN de seis dígitos, que será necesario para cambiar cualquier ajuste protegido. Según Bitdefender, ambos deben aceptar la vinculación y los dos teléfonos necesitan la última versión de WhatsApp. Luego se vuelve al teléfono del adolescente, se escribe el PIN y se revisan las opciones.
Para cambiar la configuración más adelante, se abre en el teléfono del joven Ajustes y Control parental, y se ingresa el PIN. Según Bitdefender, el adulto también puede revisar la actividad desde su propio teléfono, en la misma sección. Los controles pueden ajustarse o apagarse en cualquier momento, según WhatsApp.
Qué puede decidir el adulto
En privacidad, puede elegir ajustes como quién ve la foto de perfil del adolescente o quién puede sumarlo a grupos. Si el joven quiere relajar alguno, necesita la aprobación del adulto mediante el PIN, según el blog de WhatsApp.
En Estados, el adulto define de quién puede ver publicaciones el adolescente y quién puede ver las suyas, con cuatro opciones: sus contactos, sus contactos con excepciones, solo contactos elegidos o nadie. Por defecto, el ajuste es el de sus contactos, según el centro de ayuda de la compañía.
En Canales, hay tres opciones: todos, solo los aprobados por el adulto o ninguno. También puede impedir que el adolescente cree canales. Estos cambios no afectan a los canales que ya seguía o había creado, según la misma página.
Para Meta AI, el asistente de inteligencia artificial de la empresa, hay dos niveles. El estándar permite temas acordes con las clasificaciones de contenido para mayores de 13 años y viene activado por defecto. El limitado restringe más los temas, y con él no están disponibles las funciones que usan Private Processing, según el centro de ayuda.
Alertas y límites de la supervisión
El adulto recibe avisos cuando el adolescente se une a un grupo o lo deja, o cuando un grupo en el que participa crece de forma notable. La página oficial agrega las notificaciones por nuevos contactos. Bitdefender suma los cambios en la foto de perfil y señala que se puede elegir qué avisos recibir.
La empresa advierte que el control no elimina riesgos como estafas, acoso o enlaces maliciosos enviados por alguien que ya está en contacto con el joven. El analista de redes sociales Matt Navarra dijo a la BBC que el carácter opcional es una “debilidad obvia”.
Para menores de 13 años, la página oficial describe otra modalidad: cuentas administradas por los padres, con controles obligatorios donde el adulto revisa las solicitudes de mensajes de desconocidos y decide a qué grupos pueden unirse. Se crean desde la app del niño con la opción de cuenta administrada por un adulto.
WhatsApp no informó un calendario por país e indica que la función puede no estar disponible aún en cada región, y que mantener la app actualizada permite recibirla cuando llegue a la cuenta.

articles.title: Privacy-first cloud rival Proton launches one-click migration tool
articles.text:
Ditching your Big Tech cloud storage just got a whole lot easier — a new encrypted rival now moves years of files in the background without filling up your PC
End-to-end encrypted cloud drive now transfers years of files online
- Proton now transfers Google Drive files directly between cloud platforms
- Users can migrate large archives without filling their computers with temporary downloads
- Easy Switch preserves folders and converts Google documents into Office formats
Leaving Google Drive can involve transferring years of documents, photographs, and records, making the prospect of changing providers difficult for many users.
Proton is attempting to remove that obstacle with a feature that transfers stored material into its encrypted cloud service without routing files through a laptop.
The new tool works online in the background, allowing customers to continue using their accounts while the transfer proceeds without interrupting their work.
Moving years of files without a computer
Proton's new Easy Switch feature connects a Google Drive account to Proton Drive and transfers content between the two services via their respective cloud systems.
Users therefore avoid saving an entire archive locally before uploading it again, a process that can consume substantial time and available disk capacity.
Large archives can take hours or days to move manually, particularly when connections fail or available computer storage becomes insufficient.
Online transfers also spare computers from temporarily holding entire collections before files are uploaded again to another cloud storage service.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The transfer also retains existing folder arrangements, reducing the work required to locate documents after they arrive in the new storage account.
Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides are converted during import into Microsoft Office file types, specifically DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX, respectively.
This conversion allows users to open imported documents through software that supports those widely used formats, rather than relying on Google's original apps.
Proton says customers can monitor the operation through status information in account settings and receive an email when the process finishes.
If an import stops because the available Proton storage allocation is insufficient, it can continue after the customer upgrades their plan.
The company says imported material receives the same end-to-end encryption applied to other files stored in Proton Drive.
Under that arrangement, Proton claims access is limited to account holders and individuals they deliberately authorize to view their files.
Easy Switch is available through Proton Drive's web interface across all subscription plans and its gradual rollout began on November 19, 2026.
Growing European demand for alternatives to Big Tech
The release arrives amid questions in Europe about reliance on digital services supplied by companies operating beyond the region.
A Proton survey conducted in the United Kingdom, Germany, and France found that 8 in 10 respondents considered their countries excessively dependent on American technology - and another study cited by Proton found that 65% of technology enthusiasts use Google Drive, while 90% value privacy and end-to-end encryption most.
Proton research found that 90% of technology natives consider privacy and encryption essential when selecting services for storing personal files.
The European Commission's 2026 Digital Decade Eurobarometer reported that 82% want the bloc to reduce dependence on digital technologies originating elsewhere.
The same survey found 85% favored prioritizing services developed and controlled within Europe, while 58% would consider switching even at a modestly higher price.
Those figures suggest interest in regional providers, although willingness to change services does not necessarily mean consumers will migrate.
“People shouldn’t have to stay with a service simply because moving their files is too difficult. The desire for more private cloud storage is there, but the effort required to switch can be a major barrier,” said Anant Vijay Singh, Proton Drive Lead.
“With Easy Switch, we’re removing that barrier and making it genuinely simple to move your files to an end-to-end encrypted service.”
