articles.title: Google Researcher Shows How a Single Bit Change in .NET Files Bypassed Windows Code Integrity
articles.text:
A quirk in how the .NET Framework loads a program file let a local attacker run untrusted code past two separate protections on Windows built to block it, Google Project Zero researcher James Forshaw showed in a write-up published yesterday.
The same loading behavior bypassed Oracle VirtualBox's process hardening on Windows hosts, tracked as CVE-2026-87268, and Windows code integrity, tracked as CVE-2026-108398.
Oracle fixed the VirtualBox flaw in September, and Microsoft fixed the Windows one on October 13, both before the write-up appeared.
VirtualBox on Windows monitors the system calls that load program files into its virtual machine processes, so a less-trusted user on the same computer cannot push code into them. Forshaw got past that watch through the .NET Framework.
The framework can run a .NET program file from a plain copy in memory when the normal way of loading it, as an executable image, fails. Version 4 of the framework takes that fallback on one specific error, and the memory copy skips the image checks a loaded program would face.
The VirtualBox check returned that error for any .NET file compiled as AnyCPU, a form meant to run on any processor, so an unchanged file loaded through the path the hardening never inspects.
To get the file loaded while a virtual machine was started, he registered a COM object in the current user's settings that a protected VirtualBox process would pull in, a method known as COM hijacking. He set out the mechanism in his technical analysis.
Oracle rates the flaw, CVE-2026-87268, as a local problem that needs low privileges and no user interaction, scores it 7.8, and lists VirtualBox 7.2.16 on Windows hosts as affected. Its security advisory says a successful attack can result in the "takeover of Oracle VM VirtualBox."
The code runs inside the protected VirtualBox process. It is not a break out of a guest virtual machine onto the host, and the attacker begins as an ordinary user on that host.
The same idea worked against Windows' own code-integrity checks, which decide what user-mode code is allowed to run. There is no VirtualBox hook here, only the system call that maps a file as an image.
The researcher found that clearing a single bit in a .NET file's header, the IMAGE_FILE_EXECUTABLE_IMAGE flag, made that call reject the file while .NET still loaded and ran it.
"This single bit change is all you need to load an untrusted .NET assembly," he wrote. He tried it on Windows 11 S Mode, which enables User Mode Code Integrity (UMCI), the policy that limits which user-mode programs can run. A logic error in .NET's own policy check let the file load even with UMCI enforced.
The flaw, CVE-2026-108398, works through the .NET Framework version 4 loading path and needs a program willing to load the assembly. It is not a way to seize any Windows machine over the internet.
Microsoft rates it a local, low-privilege security-feature bypass, scores it 8.8, and fixed it on October 13. The company lists it as publicly disclosed but not used in attacks.
The same file reached a more sensitive target as well. Protected Process Light, or PPL, is a kind of Windows process that ordinary programs, even ones with administrator rights, are not meant to enter. By hijacking a COM object that WerSecureFault.exe loads, he ran his test code inside a PPL process at the highest protection level without administrator rights.
The older Protected Process type resisted the technique because the .NET runtime files lack the page hashes it requires. The October fix corrects the policy check for UMCI but does not change loading for protected processes, so that PPL route should still work, according to the researcher. It carries no separate CVE.
What to patch
On Windows hosts, update VirtualBox to a build that carries the September fixes. The affected versions are 7.2.16 and 7.2.18, and 7.2.18 shipped on September 15 with that set. An upstream code fix is not the same as a released binary, so check the running version rather than assume an older build already has it.
.NET systems need the October 13 update that matches the exact Windows and .NET Framework version in use, not one shared package. The update release notes list the right KB for each. On Windows 11 version 26H2, for example, it is KB5127694.
| Flaw | Affected | Fixed in | 
|---|---|---|
| CVE-2026-87268 (VirtualBox) | VirtualBox 7.2.16, Windows hosts | Oracle's September update, build 7.2.18 | 
| CVE-2026-108398 (.NET Framework) | .NET Framework 4 on Windows, UMCI case tested on Windows 11 S Mode | October 13 update, per-version KB | 
Forshaw first presented the Windows code-integrity bypass at the 44Con conference in September, having judged it fell outside Microsoft's rules for what gets fixed. After .NET developers told him the behavior he had counted on was accidental, he reported it in late September. The fix arrived in October's Patch Tuesday, less than a month later.

articles.title: Frontier AI employees alarmed that unseen Open AI and Anthropic models are too powerful to release, report claims — worry spreads that executives are ‘out of touch’ with severity of risks, will choose profit over safety
articles.text:
Frontier AI employees alarmed that unseen Open AI and Anthropic models are too powerful to release, report claims — worry spreads that executives are ‘out of touch’ with severity of risks, will choose profit over safety
Is this the beginning of Skynet?
Multiple employees from both OpenAI and Anthropic are sounding the alarm on the AI labs’ latest models. According to Axios, researchers are still looking for ways to contain and control unreleased models as they become more powerful, leading to debates about whether these models should be released publicly or if they should remain for internal use only. Some people are also arguing that it’s becoming impossible to keep the latest AI leashed and that companies should stop their development immediately.
“If we continue trying to make models much smarter, such that they’re actually smarter than us... they will in fact be able to trick us successfully,” a researcher told the publication. “And once you get to that point, many of the schemes that we’ve had at work up until now sort of go out the window.” There have previously been various incidents where unreleased models were able to break out of their testing environments and hack their way around the internet.
The report, which claims to have more than two dozen sources, cites "multiple" employees at frontier AI companies who worry their execs will choose profits over safety when it comes to releasing AI models. Furthermore, "they feel executives have become out of touch with the severity of safety risks."
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has even warned about an even more devastating occurrence, saying that an AI-driven botnet “swarm” could take over the internet in less than a year. The company went as far as listing “existential risks to humanity” as one of its risk factors in its IPO prospectus, although it has ironically proposed an AI safety bill that only kicks in if 50 deaths or $1 billion in damages are on the line.
Jensen Huang, the CEO of the company behind some of the hardware that enabled these breakthroughs in AI, said that “we have to shut the labs down” if these AI models prove to be unsafe, and that the civil and criminal liabilities that labs and developers would incur if AI models cause damage would be “incredible.” Still, he said that these fears are nothing but a distraction and not a call for regulation. A former OpenAI safety employee also said that the company’s safety culture is inherently broken and is calling for Silicon Valley to rely on safety experts from nuclear engineering and aviation to help “ensure that no single machine failure or human error would result in tragedy.”
A few months after the news of AI models escaping their testing environments, the White House convened the United States’ top AI tech executives, where they promised to “self-police” AI development and take steps “to build a positive future.” Despite that, a Democrat congresswoman has called for a ban on artificial superintelligence, echoing Sen. Bernie Sanders’ proposal to put a 20-year prison term on anyone caught developing the technology, and calling artificial intelligence an “out-of-control” industry.

articles.title: Apple lanzará dos dispositivos más para crear un hogar inteligente
articles.text:
Apple prepararía el regreso de su línea (PRODUCT)RED con dos productos inéditos antes de que termine el año. Según informó Bloomberg, la compañía alista versiones en rojo de su altavoz de entrada y de sus auriculares de gama alta, en una colaboración que reaparece tras varios años sin novedades.
Mark Gurman adelantó que los lanzamientos llegarían aproximadamente el 1 de diciembre, fecha que coincide con el Día Mundial del Sida. Se trataría del HomePod mini 2 y de una nueva versión de los AirPods Max 2, ambos con detalles en rojo vinculados a la fundación (RED).
Cómo serían los nuevos dispositivos de Apple
- HomePod mini 2
El primero de los dos productos sería una variante del HomePod mini 2 con un exterior de malla de color rojo. El altavoz ya está disponible en rosa, verde, azul, blanco y medianoche, por lo que el rojo se sumaría como una opción adicional dentro del catálogo actual.
De acuerdo con fuentes citadas por Bloomberg que pidieron no ser identificadas porque el anuncio todavía no es público, la empresa se encuentra en fase de preparación para su salida al mercado. No se mencionaron cambios internos ni de funciones respecto al modelo ya existente, sino únicamente la incorporación del nuevo acabado cromático.
- AirPods Max 2
El segundo producto filtrado corresponde a los AirPods Max 2, que llegarían en un acabado plateado combinado con almohadillas de malla blanca y diadema también blanca. El elemento distintivo sería la Digital Crown, el control giratorio ubicado en la parte superior del dispositivo para gestionar la reproducción, que aparecería en color rojo.
Apple no ofrece en la actualidad los AirPods Max en tono plateado, por lo que esta variante representaría una opción de color nueva dentro de la gama. A diferencia del HomePod mini 2, el rojo en este caso quedaría limitado a un detalle puntual y no cubriría la totalidad del producto.
El regreso de la colaboración (PRODUCT)RED
Los productos bajo la etiqueta (PRODUCT)RED forman parte de una licencia benéfica entre Apple y la organización (RED), creada en 2006 para financiar la lucha contra el sida. Una parte del precio de cada artículo vendido bajo esta línea se destina al Fondo Mundial.
Apple mantuvo durante años distintos productos con este distintivo, entre ellos el iPod, varios modelos de iPhone y numerosos accesorios. Sin embargo, la presencia de la colaboración se redujo con el tiempo: el último dispositivo lanzado en rojo fue el Apple Watch Series 9, y en la actualidad solo continúan a la venta dos fundas (PRODUCT)RED, correspondientes al iPhone 14 y al iPhone 14 Plus.
El iPhone 18 Pro, pese a contar con un acabado de tono burdeos, no forma parte de esta colaboración. De hecho, lo único vinculado a (RED) que ofrece actualmente la tienda de Apple son esferas gratuitas para el Apple Watch.
Por qué Apple lanzaría estos dispositivos antes de terminar el año
El regreso de estos productos en rojo llegaría acompañado de un doble significado. Por un lado, el 1 de diciembre se conmemora el Día Mundial del Sida. Por otro, la fecha coincide con el 20 aniversario de la organización (RED), lo que convertiría el lanzamiento en una ocasión simbólica para reactivar la colaboración.
A la vez, la aparición de estos colores llegaría en plena temporada de compras navideñas, lo que le daría a Apple nuevas variantes para vender en uno de los períodos de mayor consumo del año.
Apple declinó hacer comentarios sobre la información, de acuerdo con lo señalado por Bloomberg. La compañía tampoco confirmó oficialmente ninguno de los dos lanzamientos, por lo que los detalles conocidos hasta el momento provienen de fuentes no identificadas y de filtraciones previas a cualquier anuncio formal.

articles.title: 3 motherboards I'd actually buy this Black Friday
articles.text:
Black Friday motherboard deals: 3 Newegg Z890 and B850 boards I’d actually buy — from $140
Save up to $210 on three Black Friday motherboard deals at Newegg from Gigabyte and Asus
Newegg has some great motherboard deals running this Black Friday, and I've picked out three of my favorites for anyone building a high-end Core Ultra PC, an all-white Ryzen PC, or a compact AMD machine.
For Intel Core Ultra builders who want premium features without paying flagship prices, check out the Gigabyte Z890 Aorus Master LGA 1851 ATX motherboard for $290 (was $500).
On the Ryzen side, if you're planning a white-themed PC with Wi-Fi 7, I like the Gigabyte B850 Aorus Elite WiFi7 Ice AM5 ATX motherboard, which is $200 (was $255). And if you're building a well-equipped micro ATX board at a budget price, I'd opt for the ASUS TUF Gaming B850M-E WiFi AM5 micro ATX motherboard at $140 (was $220).
Today's top Black Friday motherboard deals
An ATX motherboard for Intel Core Ultra (Series 2) processors with the LGA 1851 socket and Z890 chipset. It has four DDR5 slots, five M.2 slots, a PCIe 5.0 x16 slot, Wi-Fi 7, Marvell AQtion 10GbE LAN, and Thunderbolt connectivity. Gigabyte's EZ-Latch features make swapping GPUs and SSDs easier.
An ATX motherboard for AMD Ryzen processors with the AM5 socket and B850 chipset. It has four DDR5 slots supporting up to 8200 MT/s overclocked memory, three M.2 slots (with PCIe 5.0 x4 support), Wi-Fi 7, 2.5GbE LAN, USB-C, and Gigabyte's EZ-Latch for tool-free GPU and SSD installs. The board and its heatsinks are white.
A micro ATX motherboard for AMD Ryzen 7000 and 9000 processors with the AM5 socket and B850 chipset. It features an 8+2+1 power stage design with 80A DrMOS, four DDR5 slots supporting 8000+ MT/s overclocked memory, PCIe 5.0, Wi-Fi (802.11ax), and 2.5Gb Ethernet.
Why we recommend them
In its Z890 Aorus Master review, our sister site Tom's Hardware praised its 14 rear USB ports, very fast memory support, 10GbE networking, and efficient operation. Its main complaints were a last-generation audio chip and no high-output 60W USB-C charging. At this price, it costs about what a mid-range Z890 board normally does. I especially like the Wi-Fi 7, 10GbE networking, five M.2 slots, Thunderbolt, 14 rear USB ports, and support for very fast DDR5
The Aorus Elite sits in the middle of Gigabyte's lineup, with enough power delivery for a Ryzen 7 9800X3D and the easy-install features Gigabyte has been adding to its boards. White motherboards usually carry a premium, so getting one with Wi-Fi 7 and a Gen5 M.2 slot for about $200 is a good find. Beyond the white theming, on connectivity I appreciate the 2.5GbE LAN, three M.2 slots including PCIe 5.0, and support for DDR5 up to 8200 MT/s
ASUS's TUF line is built for durability, and this board's 80A power stages can easily handle a Ryzen 7 9800X3D or even a Ryzen 9. B850 adds PCIe 5.0 support over the older B650 chipset, so you get room to grow with faster SSDs. It's a good fit for smaller cases where a full ATX board won't fit. I'm a fan of its 8+2+1 power stage design with 80A DrMOS, PCIe 5.0, Wi-Fi, 2.5Gb LAN, and support for DDR5 overclocked past 8000 MT/s
Price Context & Historical Value
Based on price history, I'd categorise the Aorus Elite as a fair price for a white AM5 board with Wi-Fi 7. The TUF board is a good price for a B850 board with this level of power delivery. The Aorus Master is a wildcard. It launched at $599.99, so $289.99 is less than half its launch price. To be upfront, Gigabyte ran it as low as $200 during a sale in June, so this isn't the lowest it has been, but it's still a strong price for a board this well-equipped.
Should You Buy It?
✅ Buy the Gigabyte Z890 Aorus Master if...
you're building with a Core Ultra 7 or Core Ultra 9, you want 10GbE and Wi-Fi 7 built in, or you need lots of M.2 and USB ports.
✅ Buy the Gigabyte B850 Aorus Elite WiFi7 Ice if...
you're building a white PC, you want Wi-Fi 7 on an AM5 board, or you want a PCIe 5.0 M.2 slot without paying for X870.
✅ Buy the ASUS TUF Gaming B850M-E WiFi if...
you're building a Ryzen 7000 or 9000 PC in a micro ATX case, you want PCIe 5.0 and Wi-Fi without paying for X870, or you want strong power delivery for a Ryzen 9.

articles.title: 2027 SOC Budget Reset: 5 Priorities to Cut Costs and Reduce Cyber Risk
articles.text:
What if your biggest SOC budget problem isn't how much you spend, but how much analyst time you lose?
According to ANY.RUN's estimates, SOC teams could recover 450 analyst hours per 1,000 investigated alerts through faster threat analysis and IOC research. That's a significant opportunity as manual investigations, repeated checks, and unnecessary escalations continue to drain resources.
As 2027 approaches, here are five priorities to reduce SOC costs, recover capacity, and strengthen protection against costly cyberattacks.
Why 2027 SOC Budget Planning Is Getting More Challenging
Cybersecurity spending is facing conflicting pressures. According to IANS and Artico Search, 55% of CISOs reported flat or declining budgets in 2026. Meanwhile, PwC's 2027 Global Digital Trust Insights found that 84% of surveyed security and finance leaders expect cybersecurity budgets to increase.
For SOC leaders, this creates several challenges:
- Growing workloads: More alerts and complex threats demand additional investigation capacity.
- Rising operational costs: Manual processes, staffing needs, and expanding security infrastructure put pressure on budgets.
- Pressure to prove ROI: Every investment must demonstrate measurable improvements in security and operational efficiency.
- Increasing cyber risks: Cost reductions cannot come at the expense of detection coverage or response capabilities.
1. Prioritize AI That Delivers Measurable SOC Value
AI is becoming a major cybersecurity investment priority, but adding AI capabilities won't automatically improve SOC efficiency. For 2027, the focus should be on reducing investigation costs, improving analyst productivity, and avoiding unnecessary escalations.
For example, ANY.RUN's Interactive Sandbox combines automated threat analysis with AI-powered reporting to help teams achieve these goals:
- Cut manual investigation time: Automated Interactivity follows redirects, extracts QR code links, and handles supported CAPTCHAs, exposing malicious activity that would otherwise require additional analyst effort.
| ANY.RUN’s Interactive Sandbox automatically solves CAPTCHA, revealing full attack chain | 
- Reduce investigation and escalation costs: AI-powered Tier 1 reports provide clear summaries of malicious behavior and recommended next steps. This helps analysts make faster decisions and reduces the need for repeated investigations and unnecessary Tier 2 involvement.
| AI-powered Tier 1 report with attack summary and recommendations for faster handoffs | 
These improvements have measurable business value. ANY.RUN reports up to 20% lower Tier 1 workload and 30% fewer Tier 1-to-Tier 2 escalations, helping SOCs handle growing workloads with less pressure to expand their teams.
The 2027 budget priority: Evaluate AI investments based on investigation time, workload reduction, and escalation rates, not the number of AI features included.
Make Your 2027 AI Budget Deliver Measurable Results
Reduce Tier 1 workload by up to 20% and control investigation costs.
2. Recover Analyst Capacity Before Expanding Your Team
As alert volumes grow, hiring additional analysts may seem like the obvious solution. But before expanding headcount, SOCs should calculate how much capacity they could recover by improving investigation efficiency.
ANY.RUN estimates that faster behavioral analysis through its Interactive Sandbox, combined with less manual threat research, can save 450 analyst hours per 1,000 investigated alerts.
Consider a SOC handling 4,000 alerts annually:
| Metric | Estimated Value | 
|---|---|
| Annual investigated alerts | 4,000 | 
| Potential hours saved per 1,000 alerts | 450 | 
| Annual analyst hours recovered | 1,800 | 
| Fully loaded analyst hourly cost | $60 | 
| Annual labor capacity value | $108,000 | 
Illustrative calculation based on ANY.RUN's estimate and an assumed hourly rate. Actual results depend on SOC workloads and investigation processes.
The $108,000 represents recovered analyst capacity, not guaranteed cash savings. However, these hours could help reduce overtime, limit outsourcing, or defer additional hiring.
The budget priority: Compare projected alert volumes, investigation workloads, and staffing requirements before approving additional headcount. Recovering existing capacity can help SOCs handle more threats without proportional increases in personnel costs.
3. Reduce IOC Research Costs with Connected Threat Context
Investigating a suspicious IOC often means searching multiple sources to uncover related infrastructure, previous attacks, and malicious activity. These repeated checks consume analyst time and increase investigation costs.
Used by 700,000+ security professionals across 16,000+ organizations, ANY.RUN helps SOC teams benefit from threat intelligence generated through shared malware and phishing investigations.
Its Interactive Sandbox provides Related Threat Context, connecting discovered IOCs to previously observed threats. Analysts can pivot directly into Threat Intelligence Lookup to explore related IPs, domains, files, and attack infrastructure.
| Related threat context displayed inside TI Lookup for deeper investigations | 
This connected approach helps teams identify broader attack patterns faster, avoid repeated research, and make better-informed investigation decisions.
The budget priority: Reduce time spent on manual IOC enrichment and threat correlation. Faster access to relevant intelligence means lower investigation overhead and more capacity to investigate critical threats.
4. Get More Detection Value from Your Existing Security Stack
Before investing in additional security products, organizations should consider how effectively their existing systems use threat intelligence.
Even advanced SIEM and SOAR platforms can miss emerging threats if they lack fresh indicators. Integrating real-time intelligence into existing workflows can help teams:
- Detect threats earlier: Identify malicious activity using recently discovered IOCs.
- Reduce operational costs: Automate indicator collection and minimize manual detection-rule maintenance.
- Maximize existing investments: Improve detection coverage without purchasing additional security products.
For example, ANY.RUN's Threat Intelligence Feeds deliver malicious IPs, domains, and URLs through STIX/TAXII, APIs, and supported SIEM/SOAR integrations.
| TI Feeds provides actionable IOCs into existing security stack | 
According to ANY.RUN's internal research, up to 30% of unique malicious IOCs found in studied Sandbox analyses were already available in its TI Feeds, providing an opportunity to detect related threats earlier.
The budget priority: Strengthen intelligence coverage within your existing infrastructure before allocating funds to additional security products.
5. Prioritize Investments That Reduce the Financial Impact of Cyberattacks
Cutting SOC expenses means little if slower detection increases the risk of costly incidents. For 2027, investments should be evaluated against their ability to prevent attacks from escalating into serious breaches.
According to IBM's 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report, the average financial-sector data breach costs $6.3 million.
Based on industry breach-cost research, ANY.RUN's internal risk model estimates potential avoided losses starting at $60,000 per qualifying phishing or malware incident in financial organizations through earlier detection and containment.
While this is a modeled estimate rather than guaranteed savings, it highlights why preventing incident escalation matters when allocating security budgets.
The budget priority: Assess investments based on their ability to improve detection, shorten response times, and reduce potential financial exposure.
Make Every SOC Investment Count in 2027
A stronger SOC doesn't necessarily require a larger budget. The real opportunity lies in making smarter investment decisions that improve security while keeping operational costs under control.
These five priorities can help organizations:
- Reduce operational costs by eliminating repetitive investigations and unnecessary manual work.
- Increase SOC capacity without proportional increases in staffing.
- Get more value from existing security investments through connected threat intelligence and stronger detection.
- Reduce financial exposure by improving threat detection and response before attacks escalate.
For 2027, the goal is clear: invest where improvements can be measured, eliminate unnecessary expenses, and build a SOC that delivers stronger protection with greater efficiency.

articles.title: TP-Link's Archer BE770 tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router is $120 off — 10 Gbps LAN ports and blazing fast wireless speeds for $280
articles.text:
TP-Link's Archer BE770 tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router is $120 off — 10 Gbps LAN ports and blazing fast wireless speeds for $280
A big drop from its usual $400 asking price
The TP-Link Archer BE770 is a mainstream tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router that is typically priced at $399. But given that we’re closing in on Black Friday, you can throw that MSRP out the window. Instead, Amazon is currently selling the Archer BE770 for a more palatable $280.19, representing a 24 percent discount.
I reviewed the Archer BE770 earlier this year and came away impressed with its 6 GHz (around 2,500 Mbps in iPerf3) and 5 GHz performance (around 1,500 Mbps), and the inclusion of a 10 Gbps WAN port and a 10 Gbps LAN port. I questioned the four 1 Gbps LAN ports at the $400 price point; however, with a $120 lower price tag, that deficit is easier to ignore.
TP-Link provides a clean web browser interface with dedicated tabs for network mapping, wireless bands, and advanced configurations. Out of the box, the built-in HomeShield security suite includes basic parental controls, Quality of Service (QoS) bandwidth management, and security scans, with optional paid tiers for advanced threat protection.
The TP-Link Archer BE770 is a tri-band Wi-Fi 7 router that offers incredibly fast speeds on the 5 GHz and 6 GHz wireless bands. It also offers a 10 Gbps WAN/LAN port and a 10 Gbps LAN port to handle your faster fiber internet connections and wired devices.
The HomeShield tab provides a subset of its full feature suite for free. Network Check scans your network to identify security risks and areas to improve overall performance. There are limited parental controls you can implement per device, and QoS settings you can enable to limit download and upload bandwidth for individual devices. But for the full breadth of controls, TP-Link offers its Security+ for $35.99/year or its Total Security Package for $69.99/year (for the first year, $129.99 starting with the second year).
If you’re looking for a high-performance standalone Wi-Fi 7 router, the Archer BE770 definitely fits the bill. At $400, it’s definitely a hard sell, but for $280, it’s an easy recommendation.

articles.title: Tuxedo unveils a formidable Linux laptop with up to 128GB RAM — but will it be enough to tempt users away from a Laptop Surface Ultra or MacBook Pro?
articles.text:
Tuxedo unveils a formidable Linux laptop with up to 128GB RAM — but will it be enough to tempt users away from a Laptop Surface Ultra or MacBook Pro?
Tuxedo's new InfinityBook Pro 15 takes up to 128GB of upgradeable RAM and a 300Hz screen
- Tuxedo's InfinityBook Pro 15 Gen11 is a modest refresh, pairing a Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 with up to 128GB of upgradeable DDR5
- The base model costs €1,504.20 before VAT, roughly $1,650, with December 2026 shipping that comes with a disclaimer
- Black Friday pricing has cut the M6 MacBook Pro to $1,849, eradicating much of Tuxedo's entry-level pricing lead
Bavarian Linux specialist Tuxedo Computers has opened pre-orders for the InfinityBook Pro 15 Gen11, a 15.3-inch Ultrabook built around AMD's 12-core Ryzen AI 9 HX 470 with room for up to 128GB of DDR5 memory and up to 8TB of SSD storage.
Tuxedo's configurator currently prices the base model, with 16GB of RAM and a 500GB SSD, at €1,792 including 19% German VAT - meaning US consumers will have to fork over about €1,506 before tax, or roughly $1,650.
On paper, it undercuts both machines this laptop will inevitably be measured against: Microsoft's Nvidia-powered Surface Laptop Ultra and Apple's MacBook Pro, but the harder question is whether the spec sheet holds up once memory speed, graphics, battery life, and software enter the picture.
Same chassis, slightly faster silicon?
The Gen11 is an evolution, not a reinvention; however, Tuxedo's press release, carried by TechPowerUp, says the machine "ships ready to use with full Linux support" in the same 1.75kg, sub-20mm aluminum body, with three power profiles of 35W, 54W, and 90W, the last requiring full fan speed.
VideoCardz also reports the 90W limit, which is ambitious for a chip AMD rates at a 28W default TDP. Whether a chassis this thin can sustain it quietly is a claim only independent testing can settle.
The processor is a small step forward: The HX 470 keeps four Zen 5 and eight Zen 5c cores, and TechRadar's review of the GMKtec EVO-X1 Pro describes it as a refresh of the Strix Point design behind the HX 370.
Graphics remain integrated, however, in the form of a 16-CU Radeon 890M, and that is the first major gap with both rivals. Buyers who need a discrete GPU will find it elsewhere in Tuxedo's own range, in machines such as the InfinityBook Max 16.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
On the memory front, Tuxedo uses two standard DDR5-5600 SO-DIMM slots, so buyers can start small and upgrade later instead of committing at checkout, as Apple's unified memory and the Surface Laptop Ultra's LPDDR5X both require.
Anyone ordering today hits a catch, though: the configurator lists both the 96GB and 128GB kits as sold out. The most memory Tuxedo will currently fit at the factory is 64GB, a €460 upgrade that, oddly, costs only €100 more than the €360 step to 32GB.
The same Tuxedo page pitches the CPU at workloads including "local AI language models (LLMs)," and AMD said at CES that ROCm 7.2 would bring official Ryzen AI 400 support on Linux as well as Windows.
Capacity is not speed, however; The offered dual-channel DDR5-5600 configuration peaks at about 89.6GB/s. Apple quotes up to 307GB/s for the M5 Pro and 614GB/s for the M5 Max, roughly 3.4 and 6.9 times as much. Token generation in local models is usually limited by memory bandwidth, so a large model that fits in 128GB of DDR5 should load, but it will likely run far more slowly than on Apple's top chip.
Reaching 128GB elsewhere is costly, though: Only the 40-core M5 Max can be configured with 128GB, and a 16-inch touchscreen model with that chip and a 2TB SSD costs $7,399. Microsoft's top Surface Laptop Ultra pairs 128GB with 1TB for $5,899. Tuxedo, for now, cannot sell a 128GB build at all, so reaching that figure means sourcing a pair of 64GB SO-DIMMs yourself at today's memory prices.
On the price front, while the Gen11 does a fairly decent job, Black Friday has since shifted the numbers considerably: Amazon has cut the M6 MacBook Pro to $1,849, with the 32GB model at $2,249. Matching the Mac's 1TB adds €50 to the Tuxedo, which still leaves it roughly $150 cheaper before shipping, taxes, and import charges.
The Tuxedo's clearer advantage is memory. A 64GB, 1TB build costs €2,302 with German VAT, or about $2,125 before tax. That is less than the discounted 32GB Mac and well below the 24GB Surface's $2,599.99 starting price.
That will not quiet the familiar complaints that have accompanied its predecessors, however: reviewing last year's InfinityBook Pro 14, TechRadar's Wayne Williams called it "far too expensive compared to the competition," noting that cheaper Windows laptops can dual-boot Linux.
For developers who want a light, upgradeable, Linux-first laptop with headroom for containers, datasets or memory-hungry models, the Gen11 makes a credible case, and nothing Apple or Microsoft sells runs Linux as comfortably. But TechRadar's roundup of Surface reviews put that machine's buying test bluntly: "Grab it if local models above 24GB are your daily work."
One could argue that user needs are decided by compute requirements, not just the ability to host a model. Anyone who needs GPU muscle or memory bandwidth will still find the Surface and the MacBook Pro in a different class, at very different prices, and Tuxedo's InfinityBook Pro 15 Gen11 is just one of many X86-based options, albeit with a larger RAM configuration capacity.

articles.title: “Ese día pasó hace tiempo”: Bill Gates admite que la IA lo superó programando y advierte sobre el futuro del empleo
articles.text:
Bill Gates admitió que la inteligencia artificial superó las habilidades de programación que cultivó desde la adolescencia y lanzó una advertencia sobre el futuro del empleo frente al avance de estas tecnologías. El cofundador de Microsoft reconoció que, hacia fines de 2025, sus conocimientos técnicos quedaron desactualizados frente a los sistemas automatizados.
“Ese día pasó hace tiempo”, sostuvo al referirse a su aspiración juvenil de convertirse en el mejor programador del mundo, una meta que hoy considera inalcanzable para cualquier ser humano.
La declaración surgió en una entrevista con The Observer publicada el 25 de octubre de 2026, en la que el empresario también analizó el impacto de la inteligencia artificial sobre el mercado laboral y las capacidades que las máquinas podrían dominar en los próximos años.
Bill Gates y la obsolescencia de sus habilidades de programación
Gates recordó que empezó a programar a los 13 años, un oficio que lo acompañó durante décadas y que terminó definiendo buena parte de su carrera en Microsoft. Sin embargo, afirmó que hacia fines de 2025 pudo comprobar que esos conocimientos ya no estaban a la altura de los sistemas de inteligencia artificial actuales.
“Pude ver que mis habilidades de programación se volvieron básicamente obsoletas”, afirmó el empresario en la entrevista con The Observer.
El reconocimiento no se limitó a su caso particular. Gates vinculó este cambio con lo que describió como un “evento evolutivo”, en referencia al salto que representa la irrupción de la inteligencia artificial en disciplinas que hasta hace poco dependían de forma exclusiva del conocimiento humano.
En esa línea, sostuvo que las máquinas pasarán a liderar los avances en matemáticas, ciencia e ingeniería. “Las IA son superiores a los humanos en esas cosas. Estamos en un momento bastante dramático de la historia”, señaló.
La inteligencia artificial ya superó las capacidades de programación que Bill Gates desarrolló desde los 13 años, según reconoció el propio cofundador de Microsoft.
Qué tipo de empleos podría reemplazar la inteligencia artificial
El cofundador de Microsoft identificó tres frentes donde la inteligencia artificial puede avanzar sobre capacidades laborales hasta ahora reservadas a las personas. Mencionó las habilidades de invención, las tareas propias del trabajo administrativo o de oficina, y el trabajo físico humano, en este último caso a partir del desarrollo de robots humanoides.
Gates advirtió sobre las consecuencias que esta transformación puede generar en el empleo. Describió un escenario posible en el que las compañías decidan “contratar al robot, despedir al humano y no mirar atrás”, una frase que resume el tipo de disyuntiva que, según planteó, enfrentarán muchas empresas en los próximos años.
El empresario señaló además que este proceso podría reducir los ingresos destinados a financiar las redes de protección social, justo en un momento en que esa asistencia resultaría más necesaria para acompañar la transición tecnológica.
La propuesta de Bill Gates para gravar a la inteligencia artificial
Frente a ese escenario, Gates planteó la posibilidad de analizar un impuesto a la inteligencia artificial como mecanismo para obtener recursos a partir de la productividad que generan estas tecnologías. La idea apunta a sostener los sistemas de protección social en un contexto de menor demanda de trabajo humano.
El cofundador de Microsoft también propuso que determinados empleos podrían reservarse de manera exclusiva para personas, con la posibilidad de que su ejecución quede prohibida para sistemas de IA. Esta medida se enmarca en el conjunto de ideas que planteó para administrar el impacto laboral de la automatización.
Pese a las advertencias, Gates destacó también aplicaciones positivas de la tecnología. Señaló que puede utilizarse para acelerar el descubrimiento de medicamentos y contribuir a reducir las listas de espera dentro de los sistemas de salud.

articles.title: Tesla et SpaceX préparent la plus grande fusion de l'histoire pour la fin 2026
articles.text:
Le projet de fusion entre Tesla et SpaceX avance à grands pas. Un groupe vient ainsi d'être mis en place pour atteindre le plus rapidement possible cet objectif !
C'est une idée dont on entend parler depuis longtemps, et que l'on sait en cours de développement depuis un certain nombre de semaines. Les deux entreprises géantes d'Elon Musk, Tesla et SpaceX, vont fusionner, avec l'approbation de leur patron commun. Et on vient de passer une nouvelle étape, qui pourrait permettre de conclure rapidement les opérations.
Cinq administrateurs vont gérer la fusion de Tesla et SpaceX
On est passé au mode sérieux du côté de Tesla et SpaceX, selon des informations qui nous sont communiquées par le Financial Times. Cinq administrateurs ont ainsi été nommés pour cette opération, deux en provenance de SpaceX et trois de Tesla.
Leurs noms ont été données par le média, il s'agit de : Roelof Botha et Randy Glein (SpaceX) d'un côté, et Robyn Denholm, Jack Hartung et Kathleen Wilson-Thompson (Tesla). Tous ensemble, ils vont devoir gérer la naissance d'un monstre, avec une capitalisation de 3 500 milliards de dollars - ce qui en ferait la quatrième entreprise au monde à l'heure actuelle.
L'objectif est d'achever la fusion avant la fin de l'année
Il faut noter que l'acteur le plus important de tout ça Elon Musk, ne sera pas autour de la table. Il n'a en effet légalement pas le droit d'y participer selon les règles de gouvernances texanes, qui s'appliquent à Tesla - l'entreprise étant enregistrée dans cet État depuis 2024. Pour rappel, Elon Musk détient 20% des votes chez Tesla, et plus de 80% chez SpaceX.
Mais même si l'homme le plus riche du monde ne sera pas là physiquement, les cinq administrateurs qui vont négocier le projet sont tous des proches de longue date du businessman. Et ils vont semble-t-il tous travailler pour ses meilleurs intérêts, puisque les échanges « s'orientent vers une échéance potentielle fixée à la fin de l'année ». Ce qui permettrait ainsi à la nouvelle entité de naître avant que les démocrates ne prennent le pouvoir au Congrès, en janvier 2027.
Source : Financial Times

articles.title: Microsoft Fixes Azure API Management Classic Flaw as Actor Targets Customer Secrets
articles.text:
Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) has disclosed that it became aware of a security vulnerability in Microsoft's Azure API Management (APIM) that has affected multiple businesses in the country, including energy companies Equinor and Skagerak Energi.
"An unknown actor has been actively looking for access tokens, secrets, and named values in APIM," NSM said. "It is still uncertain how extensive the exploitation of the vulnerability is, and has been."
The security agency said it has so far seen no evidence that has had any impact on Norwegian businesses.
According to a non-public advisory issued by Microsoft, the issue is said to affect the APIM classic tier. Instances on v2 tiers are not affected.
"On 18 November 2026, Microsoft identified a security issue affecting Azure API Management Classic tiers that could allow unauthorized access to certain management functionality if the service was not configured according to documented security best practices," Microsoft said in the advisory.
"Microsoft closed the access path on 19 November 2026. Our investigation found that customers were exposed and an unauthorized party could have used the issue to access secrets stored in Azure API Management Classic instances before Microsoft identified the security issue."
As a result, credentials or configuration secrets associated with the API Management resources may have been accessed by an unauthorized third-party if the service has not been configured as per security best practices. The information that may have been accessed could include -
- Secrets stored in Named Values Client secrets associated with identity providers
- Client secrets associated with OpenID Connect providers
- Subscription keys
- Tokens used to call direct management APIs
As of November 21, 2026, the Windows maker has released guidance for customers to help identify and rotate the secrets and credentials configured in their Azure API Management instances. It did not disclose how many customers were affected.
"If someone obtains a credential from that configuration, they may be able to use it directly against the service it protects," security researcher Anders Kristiansen said. "What they can reach depends on the credential's permissions and whether it is still valid."
NSM has also warned that the vulnerability affects several sectors in Norway and other entities outside of the country, adding it's working with national and international partners and businesses about the matter.

Time to get paid

articles.title: WhatsApp en modo Harry Potter: fondos de pantalla exclusivos antes del estreno de la serie
articles.text:
WhatsApp incorporó una nueva función que personaliza el fondo de las conversaciones con diseños inspirados en el universo de Harry Potter. La novedad llega semanas antes del estreno de la nueva adaptación televisiva de la obra de J.K. Rowling, prevista para HBO.
Según reporta Wizarding World Direct, medio de fans dedicado a la saga, la aplicación permite elegir entre cuatro imágenes oficiales que representan a las casas del colegio Hogwarts: Gryffindor, Ravenclaw, Hufflepuff y Slytherin. Cada diseño retoma los colores, símbolos y escudos característicos de cada una.
Qué contenido incluye la actualización
Los cuatro fondos disponibles reproducen la identidad visual de las casas de Hogwarts tal como aparecen en la saga original. Cada opción conserva la paleta cromática y el escudo distintivo de Gryffindor, Ravenclaw, Hufflepuff y Slytherin.
El lanzamiento se produce como antesala del estreno de la nueva serie basada en los libros de Rowling, que lanzará su primer capítulo en HBO el 25 de diciembre de 2026.
Dónde estarían disponibles los fondos de pantalla
El acceso a la actualización se encuentra restringido según el tipo de dispositivo. Hasta el momento, la función solo estaría disponible para teléfonos con sistema iOS, sin registros de su habilitación en terminales con sistema operativo Android.
El despliegue, además, se realiza de forma progresiva. Usuarios de distintas zonas geográficas confirmaron contar con la herramienta activa en sus cuentas, mientras que otros dispositivos compatibles con iOS todavía no reciben la opción.
Para quienes aún no visualizan la novedad, la disponibilidad se habilitaría de forma gradual en las próximas horas o días, según el ritmo habitual de despliegue que aplica la compañía en sus actualizaciones.
Cómo activar los fondos temáticos
Para aplicar alguno de los cuatro diseños en los chats, es necesario cumplir con una secuencia de pasos dentro de la configuración de la aplicación.
El primer requisito consiste en verificar que WhatsApp esté actualizado a su versión más reciente en la tienda oficial correspondiente al sistema operativo del teléfono.
Una vez actualizada la aplicación, el procedimiento continúa de la siguiente manera:
- Ingresar al menú de Ajustes de WhatsApp.
- Seleccionar el apartado denominado Apariencia.
- Pulsar sobre la opción Fondo.
- Desplazarse hacia la parte inferior de la pantalla hasta localizar la categoría Colaboraciones (Collaborations).
- Elegir el diseño de la casa preferida entre las cuatro opciones disponibles.
- Confirmar los cambios para aplicar el fondo en el chat individual o grupal correspondiente.
La nueva categoría Colaboraciones aparece como una sección adicional dentro del menú de personalización de fondos, diferenciada de las opciones estándar que ofrece la aplicación.
Qué se sabe de la nueva serie de Harry Potter en HBO
La producción que motiva el lanzamiento de los fondos en WhatsApp es un reinicio completo de la saga literaria, sin continuidad con las películas ni su reparto original. La historia retoma el punto de partida de Harry con los Dursley, antes de recibir la carta de Hogwarts.
La primera temporada, titulada Harry Potter y la piedra filosofal, debuta el 25 de diciembre de 2026 en HBO Max. Tras el estreno especial, los capítulos restantes se emiten cada domingo hasta el cierre, programado para el 14 de febrero de 2027, con ocho episodios en total.
Warner Bros. y HBO proyectan siete temporadas, una por cada libro de J.K. Rowling, distribuidas a lo largo de diez años. La segunda entrega, basada en La cámara secreta, ya fue renovada y comenzó a rodarse en septiembre de 2026 en los estudios Warner Bros. Leavesden, en Reino Unido.
El elenco principal está integrado por Dominic McLaughlin, Arabella Stanton y Alastair Stout en los papeles de Harry, Hermione y Ron, junto a John Lithgow, Janet McTeer, Paapa Essiedu y Nick Frost como el cuerpo docente de Hogwarts.

articles.title: Batteries solaires et stations Anker SOLIX : les offres du Black Friday
articles.text:
Face au prix de l’électricité et à l’incertitude qui l’entoure, mieux gérer sa consommation devient une préoccupation pour de nombreux foyers. Pour le Black Friday, Anker SOLIX propose jusqu’à 2 300 € de réduction sur ses solutions de stockage d’énergie, avec plusieurs modèles adaptés aux besoins de la maison, comme aux déplacements.
Nous pouvons tous en témoigner, la facture d’électricité reste une source de préoccupation pour les Français. Selon un sondage OpinionWay pour Anker, 74 % des personnes interrogées redoutent une future hausse des prix de l’électricité. Plus révélateur encore, 72 % déclarent avoir déjà modifié leurs habitudes de consommation au cours des deux dernières années, notamment en consommant moins, ou encore en décalant certains usages pendant les heures creuses.
Dans ce contexte, le stockage de l’énergie peut constituer un avantage on ne peut plus intéressant. Lorsqu’un logement dispose de panneaux photovoltaïques, une batterie permet de conserver l’électricité produite en journée pour l’utiliser le soir, lorsque les panneaux ne produisent plus. Selon la solution et le contrat d’électricité, il est tout à fait possible de recharger sa batterie pendant les heures creuses pour utiliser cette énergie précisément lorsque le prix du kilowattheure est plus élevé.
A l’occasion du Black Friday, Anker SOLIX propose justement plusieurs solutions pour répondre à ces différents besoins. Voici cinq équipements à découvrir, en promotion jusqu’au 30 novembre 2026 dans le cadre d’une opération qui offre jusqu’à 2 300 € de réduction.
En complément, Anker SOLIX offre aux lecteurs de Clubic le code promo CLUBIC, qui donne droit à 5 % de réduction sur tous les produits achetés sur son site officiel.
SolarBank Max AC : une solution pour mieux exploiter ses panneaux solaires existants
Vous disposez déjà de panneaux photovoltaïques et souhaitez conserver une plus grande partie de l’électricité qu’ils produisent ? La SolarBank Max AC répond précisément à cette problématique. Contrairement à une batterie solaire classique directement raccordée aux panneaux, elle fonctionne en couplage AC, ce qui lui permet de s’intégrer à une installation photovoltaïque déjà existante, y compris équipée de micro-onduleurs. Pour le Black Friday, la SolarBank Max AC passe à 1 899 € au lieu de 2 499 € chez Anker.
Avec une capacité de stockage de 7 kWh (extensible jusqu’à 42 kWh avec des batteries supplémentaires) et un poids de 73 kg, elle permet de conserver ce précieux surplus produit pendant la journée, pour venir alimenter les équipements de la maison en soirée. Sa gestion intelligente peut également optimiser les cycles de charge et de décharge en fonction des tarifs de l’électricité.
La SolarBank Max AC constitue donc une piste particulièrement intéressante pour les foyers déjà équipés, et qui souhaitent faire évoluer leur installation sans nécessairement repartir de zéro. Enfin, pour le Black Friday, le compteur intelligent Anker SOLIX Gen 2, d’une valeur de 109 €, est offert pour l’achat de la batterie.
Un modèle SolarBank Max, proposé à 2 599 € au lieu de 2 899 € (-10 %), est également disponible, et s’adresse davantage aux installations photovoltaïques utilisant un onduleur de chaîne.
SolarBank 4 E5000 Pro : une batterie domestique évolutive pour toute la maison
Pour les foyers qui souhaitent disposer d’une solution de stockage, la SolarBank 4 E5000 Pro propose une capacité de 5 kWh. Son système accepte jusqu’à 12 panneaux photovoltaïques et une puissance solaire maximale de 5 000 W. Pour le Black Friday, la SolarBank 4 E5000 Pro passe à 1 799 € au lieu de 2 399 € chez Anker.
De quoi couvrir là encore une partie des besoins du logement, tout en conservant une réserve d’énergie pour les heures où la production solaire devient insuffisante.
L’un de ses avantages tient à son évolutivité, puisqu’il est possible d’ajouter facilement des batteries supplémentaires pour atteindre jusqu’à 30 kWh de stockage. Elle dispose également d’une sortie hors réseau de 2 500 W, utile pour alimenter certains appareils en cas de coupure électrique.
Une solution à envisager pour les foyers qui souhaitent construire un véritable système de stockage domestique, capable d’évoluer avec leurs besoins. Là aussi, le compteur intelligent Anker SOLIX Gen 2 est offert pour l’achat de cette SolarBank 4 E5000 Pro.
SolarBank 3 E2700 Pro : un premier pas vers l’autoconsommation solaire
C’est un fait, tous les logements n’ont pas les mêmes besoins énergétiques. Avec sa capacité de 2 688 Wh, la SolarBank 3 E2700 Pro constitue une alternative plus compacte pour les foyers qui souhaitent stocker une partie de leur production photovoltaïque, sans forcément investir immédiatement dans un système de grande capacité. Pour le Black Friday, la SolarBank 3 E2700 Pro passe à 1 199 € au lieu de 1 599 € chez Anker.
Elle accepte jusqu’à 3 600 W de puissance solaire en entrée et peut elle aussi accueillir des batteries additionnelles, pour atteindre jusqu'à 16 kWh de stockage. Son système de gestion intelligent lui permet de piloter les flux d’énergie et d’adapter leur utilisation aux habitudes du foyer.
C’est incontestablement une option à considérer pour une installation solaire résidentielle de taille intermédiaire, avec la possibilité d’augmenter progressivement ses capacités de stockage.
Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 : une station électrique pour la maison et les déplacements
On quitte ici les batteries résidentielles pour s’intéresser à une station électrique portable. La C2000 Gen 2 embarque une batterie LFP de 2 048 Wh (pour un poids de 18,9 kg), associée à une puissance de sortie de 2 400 W. Deux poignées latérales facilitent son transport, avec un poids équivalent à celui d’un micro-ondes selon Anker. Pour le Black Friday, l’Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 passe à 949,99 € au lieu de 1 499,99 € chez Anker.
La C2000 Gen 2 peut ainsi alimenter plusieurs appareils simultanément, que ce soit à la maison ou aussi dans un atelier ou même lors d’un séjour en camping-car.
Elle dispose notamment de cinq prises secteur, de ports USB-C (pouvant délivrer jusqu’à 140 W) et d’une fonction de basculement automatique en alimentation de secours en 10 ms. Elle peut également être rechargée par panneaux solaires ou via un alternateur compatible. Sa capacité peut être portée à 4 kWh avec une batterie additionnelle.
Et pour ceux qui recherchent un format plus compact, la C1000 Gen 2 est également en promotion à 499,99 € au lieu de 999 € (soit une remise de 50 % !). Elle embarque 1 024 Wh de capacité et délivre jusqu’à 2 000 W de puissance (pour un poids de seulement 11,3 kg).
Anker SOLIX S2000 : une réserve d’énergie pour les imprévus
Dernière possibilité avec la S2000, une autre station électrique portable (de 16 kg) qui mise sur une capacité de 2 000 Wh, mais dans un format facile à déplacer par une seule personne. Elle délivre jusqu’à 1 500 W de puissance et peut alimenter différents équipements, du réfrigérateur à l’ordinateur en passant par les appareils électroniques du quotidien. Pour le Black Friday, l’Anker SOLIX S2000 passe à 699,99 € au lieu de 1 199,99 € chez Anker.
Elle dispose également d’une fonction ASI (alimentation sans interruption), avec un basculement en moins de 10 ms en cas de coupure électrique. De quoi maintenir certains équipements essentiels en fonctionnement, sans la moindre intervention manuelle. Sa batterie LFP est annoncée pour 6 000 cycles avant de conserver 80 % de sa capacité.
Une solution qui vise à trouver sa place à la maison pour anticiper les imprévus, mais aussi lors de certains déplacements (la prise voiture promet une recharge de 0 à 80 % en 18 heures) qui peuvent nécessiter une alimentation électrique autonome.
Jusqu’au 30 novembre pour profiter des offres Anker SOLIX
Que l’objectif soit de mieux exploiter une installation photovoltaïque existante, de constituer une réserve d’énergie domestique ou de disposer d’une alimentation autonome à la maison comme en déplacement, la gamme Anker SOLIX couvre plusieurs profils d’utilisation.
Les réductions du Black Friday, qui atteignent jusqu’à 2 300 € sur une sélection de références, permettent d’envisager ces équipements à des tarifs plus accessibles.
Les offres et les différentes configurations sont à retrouver directement sur la boutique officielle Anker SOLIX France, jusqu’au 30 novembre 2026. Le code promo CLUBIC permet en outre de bénéficier de 5 % de réduction sur l’ensemble des produits du site.

articles.title: Cette barre de son Samsung notée 5/5 tombe à 800 € pour le Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : La barre de son Samsung HW-Q990H "5 étoiles" à 800,00 € (-10%)
Actuellement notée 5 étoiles par notre rédaction, la Samsung HW-Q990H délivre une scène sonore spectaculaire grâce à sa formule 11.1.4 canaux et ses effets surround immersifs. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : elle passe à 800,00 € chez Fnac.com, Boulanger.com, Darty.com et Cdiscount Marketplace, soit une baisse d'environ 10 % et 89,27 € d'économie.
La Samsung HW-Q990H est un ensemble home cinema sans-fil conçu pour reproduire une spatialisation sonore complète dans le salon. Ce modèle associe une barre principale, un caisson de basses et deux enceintes arrière satellites afin d'immerger l'auditeur au cœur des bandes-son de films. Cet équipement s'est distingué lors de son passage dans notre labo grâce à un rendu acoustique solide et équilibré.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la barre descend à 800,00 € chez Fnac.com, Boulanger.com, Darty.com et Cdiscount Marketplace, soit environ 10 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours fixé à 889,27 €. Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 89,27 € sur cet ensemble complet.
Une immersion sonore 11.1.4 canaux complète pour les films et la musique
Comme le détaille notre test complet, cet ensemble acoustique utilise une configuration à 11.1.4 canaux qui s'appuie sur un total de 23 haut-parleurs. Cette architecture physique permet de projeter des effets surround précis tout autour de la zone d'écoute, sans dépendre uniquement de réflexions virtuelles. Le caisson de basses sans-fil fournit des impacts nets et vifs qui soutiennent l'action sans écraser les voix, préservant ainsi des dialogues parfaitement intelligibles au centre de la scène sonore.
Pour les joueurs et les cinéphiles équipés d'écrans récents, la connectique HDMI prend en charge les signaux 4K à 120 Hz ainsi que le VRR. Cette compatibilité évite les déchirements d'image et assure une transmission directe des flux vidéo des consoles de jeu vers le téléviseur, tout en décodant les pistes Dolby Atmos et DTS:X sans perte.
Samsung HW-Q990H
Points forts
- Sonorité puissante et équilibrée.
- Effets surround immersifs et précis.
- Caisson de basses compact, puissant et réactif.
- Dialogues clairs et intelligibles.
- Prise en charge des flux 4K/120 Hz et VRR.
- Bonne qualité de construction.
Points faibles
- Effets Atmos qui manquent un poil de hauteur.
- Petit afficheur.
- Nouveautés 2026 anecdotiques.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Des effets de hauteur discrets et un afficheur frontal minimaliste
Si le système enveloppe efficacement la pièce sur le plan horizontal, les canaux orientés vers le plafond manquent légèrement d'élévation sur les pistes Dolby Atmos complexes. L'afficheur intégré en façade reste aussi très étroit pour lire confortablement les modes audio ou les entrées actives depuis le fond d'un canapé. Ces limitations techniques ne gêneront toutefois pas les utilisateurs qui recherchent avant tout une grande dynamique d'ensemble et qui effectuent leurs réglages depuis l'application mobile dédiée.
Sennheiser Ambeo Soundbar Plus : l'autre option face au Samsung HW-Q990H
La Sennheiser Ambeo Soundbar Plus mise sur une conception monobloc compacte, sans enceintes surround arrière indépendantes ni caisson séparé dans sa configuration de base. Elle utilise des traitements numériques avancés pour créer une scène sonore 3D enveloppante, avec un encombrement réduit au sol qui simplifie l'intégration dans les pièces de taille modeste.
Le système Samsung HW-Q990H comprend pour sa part de véritables satellites physiques et un caisson externe pour saturer l'espace sans artifice, tandis que le modèle Sennheiser est vendu 10,00 € moins cher. La Samsung HW-Q990H conserve un net avantage sur la directivité des effets arrière et la puissance des basses, tandis que l'Ambeo Soundbar Plus convient mieux à ceux qui refusent d'encombrer leur pièce avec plusieurs enceintes distinctes.
Sennheiser Ambeo Soundbar Plus
Points forts
- Rendu sonore équilibré, riche et d’une précision admirable.
- Effets Atmos et surround bluffant de réalisme.
- Calibration acoustique efficace.
- Connectique et connectivité complètes.
- Compatible avec de nombreux formats sonores 3D (Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, MPEG-H, 360 Reality Audio…).
- Très bon niveau de finition.
Points faibles
- Latence conséquente en communication Bluetooth.
- Pas de prise en charge des flux 120 Hz et VRR.
- Une interface TV aurait été le nec plus ultra.

articles.title: WHMCS SQL Injection Could Expose Customer Data and Admin Password Hashes without Login
articles.text:
A flaw in WHMCS's shopping cart, the billing and automation platform many web hosting companies use to run their businesses, could allow anyone on the internet to retrieve customer records and administrator password hashes from an installation's database. No login is needed.
The company disclosed the SQL injection yesterday along with two other flaws that need a logged-in client, and released fixed versions. It has not reported attacks using any of the three.
Because no login is needed, the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-82981 (CVSS score: 8.7), is within reach of anyone who can load the shopping cart of a vulnerable installation over the internet.
The records an attacker could pull include clients' personal and support information as well as admin accounts with their hashed passwords, according to the company's advisory. A stolen hash is not a working password, but it gives attackers something to try to crack offline.
The 9.0.10 and 8.13.8 updates shipped yesterday, and the release notes list them as maintenance releases. For the 9.1 series, the security advisory names 9.1.2 as the fix, but that build had not yet appeared on the company's 9.1 release notes page at publication time.
Fixes are available only for supported versions, so installations on the 8.0 to 8.12 series must upgrade to a fixed release.
Installing the updates falls to self-hosted administrators, since WHMCS Cloud installations are updated automatically, according to the company's updating documentation.
The second SQL injection, CVE-2026-82979 (CVSS score: 7.1), sits in the Client Area and needs a logged-in client that holds the View & Manage Contacts permission. That client could read other customers' personal, billing, and support information, as well as the same admin records and password hashes, the second advisory says.
The third flaw, CVE-2026-93700, lies in how email campaigns process client-supplied data. A logged-in client could use it to read sensitive configuration files on the server, including database credentials, and to run code on the server, its advisory says.
It carries the highest score of the three, 9.0, though its CVE record uses the older CVSS 3.1 scale while the other two use CVSS 4.0. That record's vector indicates that some user interaction is required, and the company has not said what else exploitation entails.
All three flaws were reported by a single researcher who uses the handle alakazamspooon.
For the email-campaign flaw, updating is not the whole job. The email-campaign advisory also tells administrators to:
- Delete every planned or ongoing campaign under Utilities > Email Campaigns, using Delete in each campaign's Manage Campaign menu.
- Clear the template cache under Utilities > System > System Cleanup, using Empty Template Cache.
- Update to a fixed release.
The advisory does not explain why existing campaigns must go, leaving open the question of whether updating alone is enough.
This is at least the third round of WHMCS security fixes this year. The company patched an authorization flaw in the Client Area on May 12, described in its May advisory, and an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw on September 3, described in its September advisory.

articles.title: Fallo de Windows 11 permite saltar la pantalla de bloqueo con el Narrador y no tiene parche
articles.text:
Un investigador de seguridad publicó el 19 de noviembre un método para saltar la pantalla de bloqueo de Windows 11 mediante el Narrador, el lector de pantalla del sistema, y ejecutar programas en una computadora bloqueada. Microsoft dijo que trabaja en la corrección. Hasta ahora no existe parche.
El método, llamado FastUnlock, lo difundió en GitHub Abdelhamid Naceri, quien publica fallas de Windows con el alias Nightmare Eclipse. Según su informe, lo probó en Windows 11 versión 26H2 con las actualizaciones de noviembre instaladas y en un equipo con el cifrado BitLocker activado.
Naceri escribió que pasó de hallar la falla a entrar en esa máquina en cinco minutos, y la atribuyó a “total negligencia” de Microsoft. Afirmó que el método funcionó de forma consistente en todas las computadoras que probó. No comprobó si sirve en Windows 10.
Cómo funciona y qué se necesita
El ataque empieza en la pantalla de bloqueo. El atacante elige la opción de recuperar el PIN o la contraseña olvidados y, cuando aparece la ventana de la cuenta de Microsoft, pulsa las teclas Windows y U para encender el Narrador.
El Narrador abre entonces una ventana que no se ve en pantalla. Con la tecla de mayúsculas fijas apretada y las flechas, el atacante llega a un enlace de configuración, abre los Ajustes de Windows y, desde ahí, activa la reproducción automática de unidades externas. Al conectar un USB, se ejecuta el programa que contiene.
Ese programa corre con los permisos de WsiAccount, una cuenta restringida del sistema que usa la pantalla de bloqueo. Según Naceri, el origen del error es el rediseño del Narrador: Microsoft no impidió que la nueva interfaz se ejecute en el contexto de la pantalla de bloqueo.
Hay límites claros: hace falta acceso físico al equipo y que al menos una cuenta esté vinculada a una cuenta de Microsoft en línea. No hay componente remoto. El investigador reconoce que el método rompe la garantía de que una computadora con BitLocker bien configurado no puede abrirse aunque alguien la tenga en las manos.
Reproducción independiente y respuesta de Microsoft
Kenneth Walker, ingeniero de investigación de inteligencia de amenazas de la empresa de seguridad ThreatLocker, reprodujo la técnica en una máquina de pruebas, según Cybernews. Entró como usuario WsiAccount y copió un archivo desde un medio externo. Publicó un video del procedimiento.
Un vocero de Microsoft dijo al medio que la empresa conoce el informe y trabaja para corregir el problema. Subrayó que la compañía defiende la divulgación coordinada, un proceso en el que el investigador avisa antes al fabricante para que repare la falla antes de hacerla pública. El sitio francés Les Numériques informó que Microsoft no había recibido ese aviso previo. Tampoco se asignó un número de vulnerabilidad (CVE), el código con que se catalogan las fallas conocidas.
Qué se puede hacer mientras tanto
ThreatLocker recomienda activar el PIN de BitLocker previo al arranque. Cybernews precisa que esa medida protege a un equipo apagado o hibernado, pero no a uno que ya inició Windows y está en la pantalla de bloqueo.
El valor predeterminado de BitLocker, que se apoya solo en el chip de seguridad TPM, desbloquea la unidad al encender el equipo. Por eso el atacante encuentra los datos accesibles, y por eso un portátil en suspensión es más vulnerable que uno apagado, según Les Numériques.
Entre las medidas recomendadas figuran apagar o hibernar el equipo en lugar de suspenderlo, desactivar la reproducción automática de unidades extraíbles y no dejar sin vigilancia computadoras encendidas. Quienes solo usan cuentas locales, sin cuenta de Microsoft, quedan fuera del método descrito.
Las próximas actualizaciones de seguridad regulares de Microsoft están previstas para el 8 de diciembre, salvo que la empresa publique antes una corrección de emergencia.

articles.title: RTX 5090-equipped Asus ROG Strix SCAR 16 laptop is $350 off — snag a great deal on a ridiculously powerful 2025-model 16-inch gaming laptop with 32GB of RAM and Core Ultra 9 275HX processor for only $4,149
articles.text:

One of the least expensive RTX 5090-equipped laptops we could find in stock
After looking around for laptop deals, we finally found one that’s worth sharing. Newegg has the Asus ROG Strix SCAR 16 (G635LX-XS97) on sale; it's one of the least expensive RTX 5090-equipped gaming laptops we’ve seen so far for Black Friday week. The $350 discount drops the price to $4,149, with others at ~$4,500 or more.
Hardware-wise, the SCAR 16 comes with a 8p/16e (24 threads) Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX processor with peak boost speeds up to 5.4 GHz, along with 13 TOPS from the NPU. It also comes with 32GB (2x16GB) of DDR5-5600 RAM. While this isn’t the fastest RAM available, it’s
still good enough for high-refresh-rate gaming or productivity. The 32GB capacity is the sweet spot for most users in 2026, so you should be set there for a while. On the storage front, it includes a 2TB M.2 PCIe 4.0 x4 NVMe SSD to store your OS, applications, and plenty of games. It also has a second PCIe 4.0 x4 socket for expansion.
Get a great deal on this flagship-class ROG Strix Scar 16 gaming laptop from Amazon. You'll be able to play most games at high frame rates or even run your own local AI.

Otherwise, the clock speed is limited to 1,597MHz. And of course, it comes with the full complement of 24GB GDDR7, easily running today's (and tomorrow’s!) games at WQXGA 2560x1600 (16:10 aspect ratio). It’s also ideal for running large AI models, too. The 240Hz Mini-LED display covers 100% of the DCI-P3 color gamut and has a 3ms response time. So it’s good for productivity and gaming purposes.

articles.title: 'Simple doesn't mean basic' - how this gaming keyboard won my heart
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Glorious has taken its mechanical keyboard game back to school, with a remarkably straightforward 96% keeb that offers a truly excellent experience for typing and gaming. The Glorious GMMK Eternal feels like a high-end, well-constructed product, with triple-layer sound damping under each keycap and per-key RGB lighting, but the pricing is surprisingly reasonable. Of course, this back-to-basics approach and sensible price tag mean that it lacks the unique features that make some other keyboards stand out, but this is still a fantastic choice for any PC gamer.
Reasons to buy
- + Satisfying switches with good sound damping
- + Excellent build quality
- + Compact without feeling cramped
- + Good value for money
Reasons to avoid
- - Wired only
- - No extra features
Why you can trust TechRadar We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Glorious GMMK Eternal: Two-minute review
Sometimes simple really is better. That seems to have been the ethos behind the new Glorious GMMK Eternal, a 96% form factor gaming keyboard that I could immediately tell would be worthy of standing among the best gaming keyboards on the market.
There are no fancy bells and whistles here; no tiny LED display, no multi-device connectivity, no optical key switches with adjustable actuation. Glorious has focused on the basics, delivering a product that simply functions exceptionally well for both typing and gaming.
A big part of this is the build quality. While it might look fairly pedestrian in aesthetic terms as far as gaming keyboards go, the GMMK Eternal feels like a high-end device straight out of the box despite its $99.99 / £89.99 (around AU$150) price tag.
Beyond the per-key RGB lighting (which is practically a given for any decent gaming keyboard these days), the design is not at all ostentatious. The backplate is solid aluminum with a very slim bezel around the edges, and the keycaps are double-shot ABS plastic, both in matte black. There's no in-your-face branding, save for the Glorious logo stamped on the underside.
As I mentioned earlier, the GMMK Eternal uses a 96% key layout; in other words, you get the functionality of a full-size keyboard, but with a much smaller overall footprint. The numpad, arrow keys, and function row are all still in place, but some of the navigation keys are eliminated, and there are no dedicated media controls – one thing I do like to see on gaming keyboards, so it's a shame they weren't included here, even if it does allow for a more svelte overall device.
On the underside, there are double-level feet that allow for three different inclines. Connectivity is wired-only, via an included USB-C to USB-A cable. Anyone looking for multi-device functionality should look elsewhere – as I noted before, Glorious is keeping things as simple as possible here.
Simple doesn't mean basic, though. The linear red Glorious Fox key switches are excellent, providing a solid amount of actuation force (55g, a little beyond the average linear switch) with a pleasingly muted striking sound thanks to the triple-layer sound-damping underneath, which uses a silicone base with two layers of PU foam surrounding each switch.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
As a linear switch enjoyer, I was very enamored with the GMMK Eternal's typing experience. It doesn't quite give the 'thwock' you might expect from a more expensive mechanical keyboard, but nonetheless the sound is very satisfying. If you prefer a different type of switch, like clicky blue or the classic tactile brown, every switch on the Eternal is easily hot-swappable with an included tool.
In terms of actual use, I had a great time with the Glorious GMMK Eternal. It felt reliable and responsive both for everyday typing and for all kinds of games, including competitive shooters like The Finals and Marathon and MMOs like World of Warcraft Forever. I also tested out the Glorious Core utility software, which lets you tweak the (somewhat limited) settings of the keyboard
I did use my own wrist rest for some of my time testing the GMMK Eternal, since it doesn't come with one included in the box (unsurprising, given the stripped-down approach here), but I did actually find that it was perfectly comfortable to use without one on the lowest incline.
Overall, the Glorious GMMK Eternal is an easy recommendation, purely because it's such good value for money.
Glorious GMMK Eternal review: Price & availability
- $99.99 / £89.99 (around AU$150)
- Available now in the US and UK
- Excellent value for money
The Glorious GMMK Eternal will cost you $99.99 / £89.99 (around AU$150), and is available now in the US and UK; shoppers in Australia will have to try their luck with third-party retailers.
There's only one configuration available, which uses the manufacturer's own Fox Red key switches, but these are hot-swappable so you're always free to replace or upgrade them later on.
It's not exactly cheap for a wired mechanical keyboard, but it notably does come in at a lower cost than gaming-oriented competitors like the HyperX Origins 2 1800, and it's a lot cheaper than the (admittedly excellent) Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75%. In terms of bang for your buck, the GMMK Eternal offers a great value proposition.
Glorious GMMK Eternal review: Specs
| Layout | 96% | 
| Switch | Mechanical (Linear Red) | 
| Programmable keys | Yes | 
| Dimensions | 14.6 x 4.8 x 1.7 inches (372 x 122 x 44mm) | 
| RGB or backlighting | Yes (customizable) | 
Should I buy the Glorious GMMK Eternal?
Scorecard
| Attributes | Notes | Rating | 
| Value | Not exactly super-budget, but offers exceptional value for money with a premium-feeling design. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Design and features | A bit feature-light, but delivers top-notch build quality with a straightforward but stylish appearance. | 4 / 5 | 
| Performance | The linear switches feel satisfyingly weighty and responsive, but are surprisingly quiet for a mechanical keyboard. | 4.5 / 5 | 
| Overall | The GMMK Eternal is a fantastic back-to-basics effort from Glorious, easy to recommend for anyone who wants a premium keyboard that won't cost the world. | 4.33 / 5 | 
Buy the Glorious GMMK Eternal if…
You love quiet switches
The GMMK Eternal only comes with Glorious Fox Red switches, but they're so delightfully quiet and thunky that you won't want to swap them out.
You want value for money
For the premium build quality and typing experience it offers, this keyboard is very sensibly priced indeed.
Don't buy it if…
You want lots of features
Without a built-in display or dedicated media controls, the GMMK Eternal is pretty basic as far as gaming keyboard go.
You want something super cheap
Although the GMMK Eternal is very competitively priced, PC gamers with very tight budgets might still want to look elsewhere.
Glorious GMMK Eternal review: Also consider
HyperX Origins 2 1800 
The HyperX Origins 2 1800 is another wired gaming keyboard with mechanical switches and hot-swappable hardware, though it's slightly more expensive than the GMMK Eternal. However, it still boasts premium build quality, and the retro translucent casing will no doubt appeal to some PC gamers.
Read our full HyperX Origins 2 1800 review
MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra
If absolute value for money is your goal, the FUN60 Ultra is even cheaper than the GMMK Eternal and offers a solid build with ultra-responsive analog switches – though the customization software does leave a little to be desired.
Read our full MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra review
How I tested the Glorious GMMK Eternal
- Tested for just under a week
- Used for various tasks as well as gaming
- 8+ years of experience reviewing gaming hardware
I tested the Glorious GMMK Eternal for just under a week, swapping out my regular keeb – the Asus ROG Strix Scope RX – and using it for everyday tasks as well as gaming and creative work.
In terms of the games tested, I played a broad selection, including The Finals, Warframe, Soulframe, Marathon, and World of Warcraft Forever (which, incidentally, rules).
I've been a die-hard PC gamer for more than 20 years, building my first system when I was 16, and I've been working as a professional hardware reviewer for more than eight years – starting my tenure at Maximum PC magazine before making the leap to digital journalism and joining the TechRadar team in 2021. I put every bit of knowledge and experience I've gained over the years into my product reviews, so you can be sure you're getting an informed and unbiased analysis.

He was a regular fixture amongst our freelance review team before making the jump to TechRadar, and can usually be found drooling over the latest high-end graphics card or gaming laptop before looking at his bank account balance and crying.
