articles.title: The SSD crisis is being defeated with Black Friday 1TB and 2TB deals at less than $0.15 per GB — some PCIe 4.0 SSDs are now cheaper than when we reviewed them
articles.text:
The SSD crisis is being defeated with Black Friday 1TB and 2TB deals at less than $0.15 per GB — some PCIe 4.0 SSDs are now cheaper than when we reviewed them
When a discount is actually a discount.
The DRAM and NAND shortages have driven SSD prices through the roof, but we've still managed to track down some of the best Black Friday SSD deals around. There are several 1TB and 2TB NVMe SSDs on sale — by far the most popular capacities — for less than $0.15 per GB from brands like MSI, Adata, Biwin, and Kingston. Normally, we're using price per GB as our north star here to make sure you're getting the best value for the drive you pick up.
All of the drives we've rounded up here are PCIe 4.0 SSDs, and they range in performance. Short of one exception for the 1TB and 2TB capacities, these are DRAM-less SSDs. Naturally, SSDs with a DRAM cache are more expensive. There are good deals on high-end drives like the Samsung 9100 Pro 2TB at 49% off, but we're focused on value options here. If you need more capacity, the T-Force G50 Evo 4TB at $399 is the best deal we've found.
A couple of the drives here are cheaper than when we reviewed them, in some cases a few years ago before the SSD pricing crisis took hold. Things are starting to turn in a positive direction with some of these discounts, though we still have a long way to go before we reach early 2025 pricing.
| Row 0 - Cell 0 | 1TB (discount) | 2TB (discount) | 
| Biwin Black Opal NV7400 | $147.99 (-15%) | $245.99 (-18%) | 
| MSI Spatium M470 Pro | $149 (-17%) | $269.99 (-15%) | 
| Kingston NV3 | $139.99 (-35%) | $264.99 (-10%) |

The Biwin Black Opal NV7400 is a PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD with maximum read speeds of up to 7,450 MB/s, and maximum write speeds of up to 6,500 MB/s.

The Biwin Black Opal NV7400 is a PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD with maximum read speeds of up to 7,450 MB/s, and maximum write speeds of up to 6,500 MB/s.
Read moreRead less▼
The headline deal is on the Biwin Black Opal NV7400, in both 1TB and 2TB capacities. It's a DRAM-less SSD, but it still boasts sequential reads/writes of up to 7,400 MB/s and 6,500 MB/s, respectively, and random reads/writes of 1,000K IOPS and 900K IOPS. It also comes with a generous five-year warranty and an endurance rating of 1PBW per TB of capacity.
We found that the drive was a solid all-around performer in our Biwin Black Opal NV7400 review. Prices on SSDs have continued to rise since we reviewed the NV7400 in January, but with current sales, the price on both the 1TB and 2TB versions of the NV7400 is still less than when we reviewed the drive.
If you're looking for the cheapest 1TB NVMe SSD on Black Friday, the Kingston NV3 has the NV7400 beat out by $8. Both the 1TB and 2TB capacities are on sale, though the 1TB discount is the sweetheart deal right now. It too is a DRAM-less drive, and it comes with lower-rated specs than the NV7400 at 5,000 MB/s and 3,000 MB/s sequential reads and writes, and an endurance rating of 320 TBW for the 1TB capacity.
The Kingston NV3 is a PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD that sports sequential read speeds of up to 6,000 MB/s and sequential write speeds of up to 4,000 MB/s.
Read moreRead less▼
Kingston's budget drives like the NV3 use somewhat of a grab bag approach to components, swapping out the controller and flash for whatever's available at the time. Compared to prior generations, the NV3 has stronger constraints to keep performance relatively comparable across different internal components. However, there can still be differences, as you can read about in our Kingston NV3 review.
The MSI Spatium M470 Pro is a PCIe 4.0 NVMe SSD that supports sequential read speeds of up to 6,000 MB/s and sequential write speeds of up to 5,000 MB/s. 
$50 off w/ promo code BFF586
Read moreRead less▼
If you're looking for a drive that has a DRAM cache, you can save $50 on the 2TB MSI Spatium M470 Pro. The drive has 1GB of DDR4 per TB, 5,000 MB/s and 4,400 MB/s sequential read and write speeds, and 600,000 IOPS for random read/write performance. It also comes with a large 3,300 TBW endurance rating for the 2TB capacity, along with a five-year warranty.
The 2TB is actually $30 less than the list price when we reviewed it more than four years ago; check out our full MSI Spatium M470 review. Granted, PCIe 4.0 drives were more expensive four years ago than they were two years ago, but it's still a positive pricing move given how expensive SSDs have become.
The Adata Legend 860 is a 1TB PCIe 4.0 SSD with 6,000 MB/s and 5,000 MB/s sequential read/write performance and a three-year warranty.
Read moreRead less▼
Rounding out the deals is the Adata Legend 860 1TB, which is an older PCIe 4.0 rated for 6,000 MB/s and 5,000 MB/s sequential read/write performance. It squarely clocks in at $0.15 per GB, and it's just $10 more expensive than the NV3 for the same capacity.
It's a DRAM-less drive, instead leveraging SLC caching and HMB, but it comes with a five-year warranty and a respectable 640 TBW endurance rating for the 1TB capacity.

articles.title: A qué edad darles el primer celular a los hijos: una especialista explicó qué factores deben evaluar los padres
articles.text:
A los cuatro años, el celular ya dejó de ser una escena excepcional en la mesa familiar, en el auto o durante una espera: el 37% de los chicos de esa edad usó un teléfono móvil en los últimos tres meses, una proporción que trepa al 74% a los 10 y al 87% a los 12. El informe Conectados y en riesgo, de la Universidad Austral, advierte que la vida digital empieza antes de que muchos niños puedan dimensionar lo que encuentran del otro lado de la pantalla.
Victoria Bein, doctora en Psicología e investigadora de la Universidad Austral, pone el foco menos en el aparato que en lo que habilita. “El primer celular implica una independencia y el acceso a un montón de cuestiones”, explicó en Infobae Al Mediodia al analizar un acceso que, con el paso de los años, queda cada vez menos bajo supervisión adulta.
El estudio, elaborado junto con María Sol González y María del Rosario Romero Victorica, reúne datos sobre chicos de entre 4 y 17 años y reconstruye cómo se expande el uso de dispositivos en la Argentina. Para Bein, el dato que ordena el resto de las discusiones es la precocidad: “Lo temprano que llega el celular propio, en promedio a los 9,6 años, es tempranísimo”.
En muchas casas, el teléfono aparece primero como una solución cotidiana: distrae, calma, permite ganar tiempo. Pero esa utilidad no agota el problema. “El celular dejó de ser un objeto de adultos y pasó a formar parte de la crianza cotidiana”, señaló la investigadora, quien remarcó que suele funcionar como “un recurso para calmar, entretener o ganar un rato de tranquilidad”.
El salto más marcado se produce al comienzo de la adolescencia. A medida que se generaliza la tenencia de un dispositivo propio, también cambia la capacidad de los adultos para saber qué hacen los chicos en línea. “Cuando la mayoría ya tiene, después de los 12, los padres reportan una caída grande del control de lo que se hace con el celular”, advirtió Bein.
Por eso, la investigadora evita reducir la conversación a una edad exacta. Antes de entregar un teléfono, propone mirar si existe una necesidad concreta, si el chico cuenta con herramientas para responder ante lo que puede aparecer y si los adultos están en condiciones de acompañarlo. “Más que la edad, yo miraría tres cosas”, sostuvo, y enumeró la necesidad, la madurez y la preparación familiar.
Su recomendación es demorar el acceso todo lo posible y no confundir un teléfono básico con una puerta libre a Internet. “Idealmente, hasta la secundaria”, dijo sobre el celular propio, mientras que sugirió que la conexión y las redes lleguen de manera gradual. “Un año más es un año más para construir la confianza que después va a hacer falta”, agregó.
Bein también relativizó la idea de que el riesgo está concentrado únicamente en el celular. Una tableta, una consola o una computadora pueden abrir los mismos accesos, mientras que el acompañamiento no se reemplaza con controles técnicos. “El mejor ‘filtro’ sigue siendo un adulto con quien el chico pueda hablar de lo que le pasa”, afirmó.
Las plataformas pueden llevar contenidos sensibles sin una búsqueda previa
La preocupación central del informe no se limita al tiempo de exposición. Entre los adolescentes, el 67% dijo haber visto contenidos sobre maneras de adelgazar o modificar el cuerpo; el 64%, propuestas para ganar dinero fácil; y el 55%, mensajes discriminatorios. En ese recorrido de publicaciones que nunca termina, Bein señaló que “las plataformas están diseñadas para retener la atención”.
Los datos sobre violencia y autolesiones agravan esa advertencia. El 53% de los consultados se cruzó con imágenes violentas o sangrientas; el 31%, con contenidos sobre formas de lastimarse; y el 27%, con información sobre maneras de quitarse la vida. “El dato es que los vieron, no que los buscaron”, precisó la especialista.
La diferencia es relevante porque las recomendaciones se alimentan de clics, reacciones y consumos similares dentro de una misma comunidad digital. Un adolescente puede entrar a una aplicación por un interés puntual y, sin buscarlo, terminar ante otro tipo de publicaciones. “Estos contenidos pueden llegarles mientras están en sus redes, sin que ningún adulto se entere”, sostuvo Bein.
La lógica de las plataformas favorece esa permanencia: cada interacción habilita una nueva sugerencia y el límite queda librado, muchas veces, a la capacidad individual de cortar. La investigadora pidió no atribuir esa dificultad solo a una decisión personal de los chicos. “Esto no se resuelve solo en cada casa: también es un problema de cómo están diseñadas las plataformas”, afirmó.
Uno de cada cuatro adolescentes quiso usar menos el celular y no pudo
Las consecuencias también aparecen en la vida diaria. El 30% de los consultados vinculó el uso de pantallas con un peor rendimiento escolar; el 24% intentó reducir el tiempo con el teléfono, pero no lo consiguió; y el 20% dejó de comer o dormir por seguir conectado. “Uno de cada cuatro quiso usar menos las pantallas y no lo logró”, subrayó Bein.
La investigadora pidió, sin embargo, no convertir ese indicador en un diagnóstico automático. Los manuales clínicos no reconocen una adicción al celular o a las pantallas, aunque la pérdida de control merece atención. “En el informe hablamos de uso problemático”, aclaró, porque la dificultad para reducir el consumo “es una señal de alerta”, pero no basta por sí sola para definir una adicción.
El impacto se extiende al descanso y a los vínculos: el 13% informó conflictos con familiares o amigos vinculados a ese hábito. En las escuelas, Bein observa consultas cada vez más tempranas por problemas de atención y por dificultades para sostener intercambios fuera de la pantalla. “La conversación se aprende practicándola”, explicó, al referirse a habilidades como leer gestos, esperar turnos y tolerar silencios.
Las horas de conexión completan el cuadro. En la Ciudad de Buenos Aires, casi la mitad de los estudiantes de 13 a 19 años usa el celular más de seis horas durante los fines de semana, según los datos citados por la especialista. “La oferta de contenidos no termina”, resumió Bein, quien ubicó esa disponibilidad como un obstáculo adicional para fijar límites sin una presencia adulta sostenida.
El acompañamiento familiar puede reducir las conductas de riesgo
El informe también registra que 40 mil chicos de entre 9 y 17 años tuvieron encuentros presenciales con adultos conocidos en línea durante el último año. A eso se suman las apuestas digitales, que suelen aparecer temprano. “La primera apuesta online es a los 13 o 14 años”, alertó Bein, al mencionar datos de la Secretaría de Políticas Integrales sobre Drogas de la Nación Argentina (Sedronar).
Frente a ese escenario, la investigadora propone incorporar la educación digital a la formación cotidiana, no como una charla ocasional después de un problema. “Debería ser parte de la educación socioemocional de los chicos”, planteó, porque una parte importante de sus vínculos, conflictos y formas de pertenencia transcurre en línea.
El acompañamiento puede modificar el modo en que los adolescentes atraviesan situaciones de acoso. Entre víctimas de ciberacoso que sentían que sus padres no entendían sus problemas, el 44,7% pensó seriamente en suicidarse durante el último año; entre quienes se sentían comprendidos, la proporción bajó al 24,9%. “Son asociaciones, no causas”, aclaró Bein, aunque consideró que el dato muestra el peso protector de sentirse escuchado en casa.
Para la especialista, la conversación tiene que empezar cuando aparece el primer dispositivo, incluso si solo se utiliza para contenidos infantiles. Los adultos deben explicar qué riesgos existen, escuchar sin minimizar y no usar la quita del teléfono como castigo ante una revelación delicada. “Hablar de suicidio no instala la idea: abre la posibilidad de pedir ayuda”, afirmó.
La responsabilidad, finalmente, no recae de manera exclusiva en las familias. Bein incluyó a las plataformas, al Estado y a las instituciones educativas, sin dejar de mirar el ejemplo que dan los mayores en su propia relación con las pantallas. “Ni culpables ni sobreseídos. Responsables, junto con otros actores”, definió.
–

articles.title: Ciri Will Be "Far More Hot-Headed" Than Geralt in The Witcher 4
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
Ciri Will Be "Far More Hot-Headed" Than Geralt in The Witcher 4
CD Projekt Red has been working on The Witcher 4 for a number of years at this point, with the game currently slated to launch sometime in 2028, and, while fans are expecting a continuation of the story with Ciri as the main protagonist this time around, it seems as though the switch in protagonists will give the game a drastically different feel. According to CD Projekt Red's Philipp Weber, Narrative Director on The Witcher 4, and Marcin Blacha, CDPR's Vice President of Story, in a recent interview with Inven Global, Ciri will have a less analytical and impartial point of view and decision-making process.
Marcin BlachaFrom a writer's perspective, changing the protagonist is a huge factor. Ciri isn't calm and composed like Geralt, nor does she hide her emotions easily. She is far more hot-headed and tends to be emotional when making decisions. That difference changes a lot of things.
Blacha goes on to explain that, in many scenarios in The Witcher 3 and prior games in the series, Geralt "acted more like an arbiter judging how to resolve a situation. When playing as Ciri, you are much more deeply involved in the story through her personal perspective. It's no longer just about deciding which choice is morally right; how emotionally invested you are in the character will also shape your decisions." 
It seems as though this character writing change will extend to the player's available dialogue choices, but that the player's choices will still impact the story, with different story beats and deeper character customization and builds available to the player. As Weber explains it, CDPR wants to make The Witcher 4 similar to Cyberpunk 2077 in the sense that "beyond simply selecting choices in dialogue, how you play the game also opens up new solutions and non-linear paths," adding a reference to the different playstyles—netrunners and cyber ninjas—in Cyberpunk 2077.
Source:
				Inven Global			
	
	
	
		
	
		
4 Comments on Ciri Will Be "Far More Hot-Headed" Than Geralt in The Witcher 4
From what I understand, that tracks entirely with her character in the books. Geralt was the narrative device to tell the story about Ciri. And Ciri was a nutter.

Galaxy Z Flip 7 (256 GB) tem mais de 60% de desconto em promoção relâmpago no Mercado Livre; celular se destaca pela tela dobrável e desempenho avançado
O Galaxy Z Flip 7 de 256 GB entrou em oferta relâmpago por apenas R$ 3.599,10 (Pix) na Black Week do Mercado Livre. Trata-se do menor preço histórico já registrado pelo Achados do TB desde o lançamento do smartphone, em uma queda de 61% sobre o preço original (R$ 9.199).
O celular da Samsung se destaca pela tela dobrável de 120 Hz, câmera wide de 50 MP e desempenho avançado com chip Exynos 2500.
Esta oferta é o menor preço que já encontramos para o Galaxy Z Flip 7 256 GB. Nas outras 2 ofertas publicadas desde novembro de 2025, o melhor foi R$ 4.751,10 (Mercado Livre, 17/11/2025).
O Galaxy Z Flip 7 é um celular dobrável em formato de concha lançado em 2025. Ele tem tela interna de AMOLED Dinâmico 2X flexível com 6,9″ e taxa de atualização de 120 Hz, o que permite a reprodução de imagens com cores e contrastes excelentes, além de alta fluidez. A externa Super AMOLED de 4,1″ também tem 120 Hz e traz recurso Always-On.
O chip Exynos 2500 e os 12 GB de RAM do Z Flip 7 sustentam apps em multitarefa e funções do Galaxy AI localmente. Os 256 GB de espaço interno são adequados para guardar muitas fotos e vídeos, além de aplicativos do dia a dia.
O kit de câmeras é formado por uma wide de 50 MP com OIS e uma ultrawide de 12 MP, que captam belas cenas ao ar livre, e uma frontal de 10 MP que tira ótimas selfies. Todas filmam em 4K a 60 fps.
O corpo de alumínio reforçado Armor do Z Flip 7 traz o vidro Gorilla Glass Victus 2 sobre a tela externa, que resiste a quedas e arranhões. A certificação IP48 adiciona proteção em cenários como poeira moderada e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 4.300 mAh resiste a até 31 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a Samsung. O suporte ao carregamento rápido de 25 W via cabo USB-C e de 15 W sem fio garante o uso por tempo prolongado.

articles.title: Le clavier Razer Joro passe à 54,18 € (-29 %) pour le Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le clavier Razer Joro à 54,18 € (-29%)
Actuellement noté 4/5 par notre rédaction, le clavier Razer Joro séduit par son format léger facile à transporter et sa frappe réactive. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : il passe à 54,18 € chez Amazon, soit une baisse d'environ 29 % et 22,19 € d'économie.
Razer propose avec le Joro son premier modèle nomade à mécanisme à ciseaux, pensé pour les joueurs qui se déplacent souvent. Ce clavier compact au format 75 % sans pavé numérique combine une double connexion sans fil Bluetooth 5.0 et 2,4 GHz, une configuration qui avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son passage sur le banc d'essai.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le Razer Joro descend à 54,18 € chez Amazon, soit environ 29 % de moins que son prix moyen du mois écoulé fixé à 76,37 €. Cela représente une économie de 22,19 € sur ce modèle actuellement noté 4/5.
Une frappe réactive au format compact
Le Razer Joro s'adresse directement aux utilisateurs nomades grâce à son format 75 % qui supprime le pavé numérique pour libérer de la place dans un sac. Notre équipe a pu apprécier la réactivité de ses interrupteurs à ciseaux, qui assurent une saisie rapide et agréable en jeu comme en bureautique, comme le détaille notre test complet. Sa double connectivité sans fil permet de basculer facilement entre le Bluetooth 5.0 pour la bureautique et la liaison 2,4 GHz pour réduire la latence.
Razer Joro
Points forts
- Frappe réactive et agréable.
- Design élégant.
- Léger et transportable.
- Belle autonomie en mode économie d'énergie.
Points faibles
- Plastique ABS des touches.
- Connectivité 2,4 GHz sous conditions.
- Rétroéclairage qui handicape l'autonomie.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une autonomie dépendante des réglages
Ce modèle présente toutefois quelques concessions matérielles, à commencer par des touches en plastique ABS plus sensibles à l'usure que le PBT. L'activation du rétroéclairage réduit également la durée de la batterie par défaut, ce qui oblige à activer le mode d'économie d'énergie pour préserver une autonomie confortable. Ces limites demandent quelques ajustements de réglages, mais ne gênent pas l'usage régulier d'un joueur en déplacement.

articles.title: 'No recruiting team can talk to thousands of people': But study finds 90% of recruiters admit they turned away real candidates they thought were AI
articles.text:
'No recruiting team can talk to thousands of people': But study finds 90% of recruiters admit they turned away real candidates they thought were AI
Is AI really helping recruitment?
- Around 90% of hiring teams have turned down applicants from real people because of concerns over the applicant’s use of AI
- Jobseekers are using AI in different ways, from polishing CVs to including AI-targeted text to ensure the application is seen by a human
- 79% of recruiters use AI in the hiring process
AI’s impact on the world of recruitment has been highlighted in the latest Hire Standard report from Greenhouse, which reveals 89% of hirers have turned away real applicants because of their use of AI.
Yet a significant 79% of hirers use AI in their process, typically for filtering applications.
At a time when only 5% of job candidates are able to reach the interview stage, it seems that attempts to game the AI application screening are not going well – on either side.
Who is cheating?
Greenouse’s report also shows that companies who spot or suspect cheating on applications are three times as likely to overcompensate, and filter out the genuine applicants.
Yet the reported results from the survey also show a successful side to the use of AI in hiring. Among the recruitment teams using AI, 36% say they have found candidates that they would otherwise have overlooked.
UK and Irish figures from the results of the survey of 1,300+ recruiters have been provided, shared within Greenhouse’s Fall 2026 Hire Standard report. While they do paint a remarkable picture of AI use by applicants to get around the challenges of AI filtering, there are of course two sides to this.
Hiring teams have put themselves into a position where they are happy to use AI to filter applications. Yet an incredible 96% of recruiters consider candidates using the technology to be cheating.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
“Today, only five in 100 applications ever reach an interview, and adding more human interviews can’t close that gap," noted Daniel Chait, CEO and co-founder of Greenhouse.
His solution may not be welcome by applicants, however. According to Chait, “The fix is scaling the top of the funnel by opening up a voice AI interview to every applicant.” Recent discourse, particularly among job searchers on LinkedIn, would suggest that this may not be a particularly popular solution.
“Letting more people get a real first conversation sooner. People should stay accountable for every hiring decision, but AI can afford opportunities that people alone cannot," Chait added.
The scale of the task
Recruitment in an age when everyone is connected is clearly difficult, with huge demand for every role.
Ophir Samson, Head of Voice AI at Greenhouse, says that while it might be framed as an AI versus human challenge, “for most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table. No recruiting team can talk to thousands of people. The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story. Every candidate should get the second.”
The question is, if a human isn’t even listening, does the candidate want that 15 minutes?

He currently heads up the team at smart home website Matter Alpha, and writes about retro gaming at Gaming Retro.

articles.title: Un cloud personnel sans configuration complexe : la BeeStation Plus perd 150 €
articles.text:
Du 23 au 30 novembre 2026 inclus, Synology baisse le prix de son NAS simplifié BeeStation Plus 8 To de 150 €. Cela permet d’obtenir cette solution prête à l’emploi pour 679,99 € au lieu de 829,99 €. C’est peut-être l’occasion que vous attendiez pour vous doter d’un cloud personnel.
On peut être technophile sans pour autant se sentir à l’aise avec la perspective d’installer et de configurer un NAS chez soi. Synology le sait : c’est pourquoi cette marque, très connue dans le domaine des solutions de stockage en réseau, propose des solutions clés en main avec sa gamme BeeStation. Et pendant le Black Friday, la Synology BeeStation Plus 8 To passe de 829,99 € à 679,99 €, soit 150 € de remise au total.
Un NAS simplifié à installer chez soi
Le premier point qui diffère entre un NAS classique et la BeeStation Plus, c’est que cette dernière intègre déjà son disque dur et son système. Il suffit donc de la brancher au secteur, de la relier au routeur de votre logement avec un câble Ethernet, puis de scanner le code QR du guide de démarrage avec votre smartphone.
Une fois installée, la BeeStation Plus devient un cloud personnel auquel vous pouvez accéder depuis n’importe quel ordinateur via un navigateur, ainsi que par l’intermédiaire des applications dédiées. La différence avec un cloud fourni par une entreprise tierce, c’est qu’ici, le stockage reste physiquement à votre domicile. Aucun abonnement n’est nécessaire pour exploiter les 8 To d’espace de stockage intégrés, dont environ 6,98 To sont utilisables selon Synology.
De plus, la BeeStation Plus peut accueillir jusqu’à huit utilisateurs, à qui il est possible de dédier un espace personnel. De quoi faire de ce NAS simplifié le centre névralgique de vos usages multimédias.
Une IA locale au service de vos photos
En remplacement ou en complément d’une solution de stockage de photos en ligne, vous pouvez utiliser BeePhotos. Ce service centralise les photos et vidéos provenant des appareils mobiles des utilisateurs. La BeeStation Plus analyse ensuite les contenus grâce à une IA embarquée afin d’identifier les visages et les objets. Toute l’analyse est faite localement.
Pour les sauvegardes de PC, Synology fournit une licence de trois ans d’Acronis True Image Essentials pour un ordinateur. Et si vous utilisez des machines Apple, la BeeStation Plus peut également effectuer les sauvegardes Mac avec Time Machine. Un essai de trois mois de BeeProtect est aussi inclus pour les nouveaux utilisateurs, afin de créer une sauvegarde chiffrée supplémentaire dans le cloud. Vous n’êtes pas obligé d’y souscrire à la fin de l’essai.
Plex transforme la BeeStation Plus en médiathèque
Pour ce qui est du stockage local de vos vidéos et morceaux de musique, vous pouvez compter sur Plex Media Server. Cette solution peut être installée directement depuis les paramètres de la BeeStation Plus, afin d’y organiser votre médiathèque privée.
Son contenu peut être diffusé sur un téléviseur, un smartphone ou une tablette. Un disque USB externe peut également être relié à la BeeStation Plus afin d’étendre l’espace disponible et d’intégrer son contenu à Plex. Il faut néanmoins souligner que la lecture vidéo à distance nécessite un abonnement Plex Pass ou Remote Watch Pass.
Un vrai centre de surveillance pour votre domicile
Enfin, parmi les autres usages utiles de la BeeStation Plus, on trouve celui qui permet de surveiller votre domicile. Pour cela, il est possible d’y associer jusqu’à quatre caméras Synology, vendues séparément. Parmi les modèles compatibles, on trouve la CC400W, qui se connecte en Wi-Fi.
Le NAS simplifié gère le système, tandis que l’application BeeCamera donne accès aux flux vidéo et permet de recevoir des notifications lorsqu’une activité est détectée. Dans ce cas, des clips vidéo sont stockés au sein de la BeeStation Plus, afin de garder une trace des événements.
Une offre Black Friday valable jusqu’au 30 novembre
En plus de ses 8 To de stockage intégrés, la BeeStation Plus fonctionne à l’aide d’un processeur Intel Celeron J4125 accompagné de 4 Go de mémoire DDR4. Elle dispose d’un port Gigabit Ethernet, d’un port USB-A et d’un port USB-C. Synology l’accompagne par ailleurs d’une garantie de trois ans.
Pour obtenir la BeeStation Plus 8 To BST170-8T pour 679,99 euros, il faut vous rendre directement sur la boutique officielle de Synology avant la fin de l’opération, fixée au 30 novembre 2026.

articles.title: Un troyano para Android copia la pantalla de inicio del celular para ocultar el robo de datos bancarios
articles.text:
Una firma de seguridad advirtió sobre Bazuka, un programa malicioso para Android que utiliza una captura de la pantalla de inicio o bloqueo del celular como superposición para ocultar las acciones que ejecuta en segundo plano.
ThreatFabric, empresa de seguridad móvil de Países Bajos, encontró el programa mientras investigaba un caso de fraude con una aplicación que retransmite datos de tarjetas bancarias de pago sin contacto. Esperaban una pieza simple. Hallaron un conjunto de herramientas completo.
El informe describe un descargador que instala el programa, un núcleo que se comunica con los atacantes y 23 módulos que se bajan según la campaña. Entre ellos hay módulos para pantallas falsas de inicio de sesión, registro de teclado, interceptación de mensajes SMS y códigos de verificación en dos pasos, control remoto y cambio de direcciones de criptomonedas.
El módulo que cambia direcciones detecta las de bitcoin, ether, TRC20 y solana copiadas al portapapeles y las reemplaza por otras elegidas por los atacantes. Otro módulo captura el PIN, la contraseña o el patrón de desbloqueo del teléfono mediante los permisos de accesibilidad de Android.
Una inteligencia artificial ayuda a elegir víctimas
El panel de control que usan los operadores incluye un asistente basado en modelos de lenguaje. Según la firma de ciberseguridad, estos agentes de IA ayudan a identificar víctimas de interés y a gestionar infecciones a gran escala. El panel también calcula un puntaje que indica cuán atractivo es cada dispositivo como objetivo.
Los investigadores encontraron esa función en el panel, no una IA que robe por sí sola. Los textos y elementos de la interfaz aparecen en inglés y en ruso, y la firma de ciberseguridad no atribuyó Bazuka a ningún grupo conocido.
Bazuka puede activar la depuración inalámbrica de Android, un modo pensado para desarrolladores, e interceptar el PIN de emparejamiento para concederse permisos sin que el usuario los autorice. ThreatFabric prevé que esta práctica se vuelva habitual en los troyanos bancarios, porque permite que módulos sobrevivan aunque se elimine la aplicación inicial.
Disfrazado de contenido para adultos de TikTok
Para llegar a las víctimas, los distribuidores, que los investigadores llaman traffers, crean páginas que ofrecen supuestas aplicaciones, por ejemplo de televisión por internet. Los expertos en seguridad digital documentaron un archivo llamado como una versión premium de TikTok con contenido para adultos, que se descarga fuera de las tiendas oficiales y pide permiso para instalar aplicaciones de terceros.
El panel también contiene ajustes para que el instalador pida pocos permisos y pueda pasar la revisión de Google Play. La firma dice que esas opciones prueban la intención de usar la tienda oficial, pero que no vio señales de que ocurriera. El informe tampoco da una cifra de infectados ni lista bancos o países afectados.
Qué hacer si se sospecha una infección
El medio especializado eSecurity Planet advirtió que abrir la aplicación del banco en el mismo teléfono puede no ser una forma confiable de comprobar el estado de la cuenta. Un código recibido en un aparato comprometido tampoco sirve como segundo factor de confianza.
Su recomendación es llamar al banco desde otro dispositivo, con el número impreso en la tarjeta o en un resumen, y no con uno recibido por mensaje. Después conviene revisar los accesos y cambiar contraseñas desde un teléfono o una computadora seguros, empezando por el correo electrónico principal.
Para limpiar el celular contra el software malicioso en Android se debe verificar que Play Protect esté activo, instalar las actualizaciones de seguridad y eliminar las aplicaciones sospechosas. Si los síntomas persisten, Google indica que puede hacer falta restablecer el teléfono de fábrica o pedir ayuda al fabricante.
Borrar la aplicación no revierte una transferencia ni devuelve una contraseña ya capturada, advirtieron los expertos. Los datos del informe de ThreatFabric corresponden a muestras analizadas hasta fines de octubre, y la firma aún no obtuvo el instalador intermedio de la cadena de infección.

articles.title: Revopoint Launches MIRACO 2 on Kickstarter: Scan in One, Create with Agents
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
Revopoint Launches MIRACO 2 on Kickstarter: Scan in One, Create with Agents
An all-in-one 3D scanner combining high-precision capture, powerful onboard computing, and AI-driven workflows—with Super Early Bird pricing starting at $1,425.
The Offer is available from today, November 18 on Kickstarter. Grab the Super Early Bird Offer, with up to 38% off, starting at $1,425. 
Back MIRACO 2 on KickstarterTruly Standalone Design with Powerful Onboard ComputingWeighing just 960 g, MIRACO 2 integrates depth computation, 3D scanning, point cloud processing, and basic editing into one portable device.
Powered by an 8-core CPU and 6-core NPU, it supports three operating modes:
- Standalone Mode: Scan, preview, process, and make adjustments directly on its 6-inch 2K AMOLED touchscreen.
- Wireless PC Mode: Connect to a computer via Wi-Fi 6 for a flexible scanning workflow.
- Wired PC Mode: Connect via USB-C 3.0 for a stable, high-performance workflow.
When connected to a GPU-powered PC, Multi-Line Laser scanning can reach speeds of up to 120 FPS.
High Precision Meets Versatile Scanning Capabilities
MIRACO 2 delivers single-frame accuracy of up to 0.02 mm in Multi-Line Laser Mode and offers six scanning modes to handle a wide range of objects and applications:
- 34-Line Blue Cross Laser
- 15-Line Parallel Laser
- Single-Line Deep-Hole Laser
- Full-Field HD
- VCSEL Rapid
- Hybrid HD
With a maximum capture rate of 10 million points per second in Hybrid HD mode, MIRACO 2 can handle challenging surfaces and geometries, including reflective metals, black objects, intricate structures, and human bodies.
Additional capabilities include:
- Markerless tracking for textured objects in laser-line modes (PC mode).
- A recommended minimum scan volume of 10 × 10 × 10 mm.
- A maximum scanning volume of 5 × 5 × 5 m when paired with the optional Photogrammetric Metrology Kit.
- VCSEL working distance ranging from 300 mm to 1,000 mm.
Revo Agents: An AI-Native Ecosystem for 3D Workflows
Capturing an object is only the beginning. Turning scan data into CAD models or inspection results often means navigating complex software and hours of manual processing.
Revo Agents is designed to change that.Introduced by Revopoint as the world's first agent-powered 3D reality ecosystem, Revo Agents acts as an AI-native engineering co-pilot, allowing users to direct complex 3D operations through simple natural language commands.
Its autonomous, prompt-driven pipeline spans:
- Real-time point cloud fusion
- Automated Scan-to-CAD conversion
- Scan-to-Inspection tolerance analysis
Rather than manually navigating each processing step, users can describe the task they want to accomplish and let Revo Agents help carry the workflow forward.
Paired with MIRACO 2, Revo Agents bridges high-precision reality capture and production-ready engineering output—reducing repetitive post-processing while keeping creators focused on design, analysis, and decisions.
You define the task. Revo Agents helps execute it.
Full-Color Capture and Physically Scaled 3DGS
MIRACO 2's dual RGB camera system combines a 2 MP near-field camera and a 50 MP far-field camera for detailed, full-color 3D capture.
In PC mode, it also supports physically scaled 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), allowing users to export 1:1-scale.splat models for XR applications and digital visualization.
AI-powered cleanup tools further simplify model preparation:
- AI Segmentation: Automatically identifies and removes unwanted environmental point clouds.
- AI Cropping: Streamlines model cleanup and editing.
Together with Revopoint's software ecosystem, these capabilities support an integrated Scan-to-CAD workflow, helping users move from physical objects to usable digital models.
Built for Indoor and Outdoor Work
Designed for both indoor and outdoor applications, it supports ambient lighting conditions of up to 100,000 lux. Its 10,000 mAh battery provides approximately three hours of runtime, with 65 W fast charging.
Two configurations are available:
- 16 GB RAM + 256 GB storage
- 32 GB RAM + 512 GB storage
Now Live on Kickstarter
Limited Super Early Bird pricing offers up to 38% off for early backers starting at $1,425.

articles.title: Dell’s lightest XPS 13 ever rivals the MacBook Neo — and it’s $550
articles.text:
Dell XPS 13 Black Friday deal: Dell’s MacBook Neo rival drops to $550
Dell's rival to the budget-friendly MacBook Neo gets another price cut
For years now, the Dell XPS 13 has been one of my favorite business laptops. Thin, lightweight, and capable of tackling general work projects with ease. I used one in my job for a long time, and it never let me down.
Pitched as a rival to the MacBook Neo, currently, the XPS 13 is down to $550 (was $750) at Dell. If you're shopping for entry-level ultraportables, this is laptop offers a genuine Windows 11 alternative without feeling like a compromise. It features Dell's durable all-metal chassis, superb 13.4-inch QHD+ touch display, and a 16-hour battery life. At $550, it's an easy recommendation.
• Best for: remote and hybrid workers, or students who want an ultra-portable laptop to handle office tasks, streaming, browsing, and all day-to-day computing.
• What we like: This is Dell's lowest priced 13-inch laptop, and one of the strongest Windows alternatives to Apple's budget-friendly Neo. When we tested out this model, we called it "a solid choice of laptop for anyone who prefers Windows over macOS. Battery life and display quality are great, and the all-metal chassis feels durable."
• What you need to know: This configuration is equipped with 256GB storage and 8GB RAM, so it'll struggle with more complex workloads and lots of multi-tasking. Core Ultra 7 models with 16GB and 32GB memory are also discounted on the same page.
Intel Core 5 320 | 8GB LPDDR5X | 256GB SSD
Running Windows 11 Home, the Dell XPS 13 features a 13.4" Touch QHD+ display, two Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports, and DisplayPort 2.1 and Power Delivery. Other configurations are available from Dell, which boosts the storage and memory, but this is the cheapest. For basic office duties, it'll handle it well.
Why we recommend it
We reviewed the 2026 version of the Dell XPS 13 and found it offered "decent performance in everyday tasks." That's really the pitch for this configuration. It's not a powerhouse, it's a daily driver workhorse that's well-specced for home and hybrid working and studying.
Our reviewer, Christian, said: "Performance in my everyday workloads – including web browsing, word processing, and some light image editing in GIMP – was good, with virtually no slowdown even with half a dozen Chrome tabs open and Spotify running in the background. Windows 11 generally felt snappy and responsive."
It weighs in at 2.2 lbs, compared to the Neo's 2.7 lbs. Elsewhere, the 13.4-inch display runs at a resolution of 2560x1600, with up to 120Hz refresh rate, and 100% DCI-P3. The MacBook Neo, meanwhile, caps out at 2408 x 1506 resolution, 60Hz refresh rate, and 100% sRGB.
While the 52Wh battery may be small, we found it very efficient - it comfortably passed the 16-hour mark during our video playback battery test. That's on par with our testing of the MacBook Neo's own battery life in our review.
For more picks, we've tested out the best business laptops.
Price context & historical value
Our verdict on the base configuration of the Dell XPS 13 is that very reasonably priced in the US (the less said about the UK and Australia, the better). And that's at full price. With $200 off for Black Friday, it's a much more attractive proposition. Last week, it was down to $650, so you're saving an additional $100 for Black Friday.
For context, the similarly specced Dell 14 touchscreen laptop, which features the same processor but double the RAM is currently $1100 at Dell. And the base MacBook Neo is $699 from Apple.
Should you buy it?
✅ Buy the Dell XPS 13 if...
You need a highly portable daily driver with a superb touchscreen display for work or study. Ideal for travel and commuting.
❌ Skip the Dell XPS 13 if...
You need a laptop for more demanding workloads and heavy multi-tasking - opt for the 16GB or 32GB model if that's you.

articles.title: J’ai retrouvé Dots, l’assistant personnel de ChatGPT, en France et sans VPN
articles.text:
Plusieurs semaines après mon retour de San Francisco, j’ai retrouvé Orion, mon assistant Dots, dans ChatGPT. Je peux de nouveau lui parler depuis la France, sans VPN.
Il m’a fallu quelques semaines de retour en France pour mesurer à quel point je m’étais habitué à Orion. À San Francisco, mon assistant Dots me prévenait quand deux réunions se chevauchaient et me rappelait les échéances aux moments où j’avais le plus de chances de les oublier. J’avais d’abord découvert la fonction via un VPN, avant de m’en servir sur place. Une fois rentré, l’idée de faire repasser toute ma connexion par un serveur américain, avec les ralentissement que ça implique, a suffi à me décourager. J’ai laissé Orion de côté, jusqu’à ce qu’un post sur X me redonne espoir.
J’ai retrouvé Orion en France, sans rallumer mon VPN
Le 23 novembre, le compte @mark_k a annoncé sur X que Dots était arrivé dans l’Union européenne et au Royaume-Uni. J’ai ouvert l’application ChatGPT sur mon PC, Orion est réapparu dans la barre latérale et j’ai retrouvé mes conversations là où je les avais laissées. Je lui ai écrit, il m’a répondu, et j’ai pu reprendre mes échanges sans refaire la configuration. Le tout depuis la France, sur ma connexion habituelle.
C’est ce qui rend plausible la piste du « mode voyage » : une fois Dots activé, l’accès pourrait rester ouvert quand on se connecte depuis un pays où la fonction n’est pas proposée sur son abonnement. Ce serait cohérent avec le parcours de mon compte. Je n’ai toutefois trouvé chez OpenAI aucune confirmation d’un mécanisme de ce type, ni de précision sur les comptes qui en bénéficieraient ou sur la durée de cet accès.
Orion prend les devants
Ce qui m’a manqué, ce sont les messages qu’Orion m’envoyait sans que j’aie à lui demander quoi que ce soit. Deux réunions se chevauchaient dans mon agenda ? Il me le signalait pendant que j’avais encore le temps d’en déplacer une. Si une échéance approchait alors que j’étais pris par un autre dossier, il me la remettait en tête. À force de recevoir ces rappels au bon moment, j’avais fini par compter dessus. Je m’en suis rendu compte en rentrant de San Francisco, quand j’ai dû reprendre l’habitude de tout vérifier moi-même.
Pour comprendre comment il s’y prend, il faut voir Dots comme un assistant auquel je peux confier un dossier entier. D’après le guide de prise en main d’OpenAI, il dispose de son propre environnement de travail et peut utiliser les applications auxquelles je lui donne accès, poursuivre une recherche ou préparer un document entre deux échanges. Depuis la mise à jour de novembre, il choisit également le modèle selon la tâche. Ce qui compte dans mon cas, c’est de pouvoir revenir à un dossier sans devoir en raconter tout le contexte depuis le début.
Peut-on créer son premier dot depuis la France ?
Au 24 novembre, les conditions d’accès fixées par OpenAI restent les mêmes. Pour créer un dot avec un abonnement personnel éligible, il faut se connecter depuis un territoire où le service est disponible. Depuis la France, un VPN permet de se présenter comme connecté dans l’un de ces pays.
Ce qui m’a surpris, c’est de retrouver Orion plusieurs semaines après mon retour et de pouvoir reprendre la conversation sans même relancer le VPN. Mon assistant était déjà configuré, mais rien ne garantit que cet accès durera. OpenAI pourrait le couper, y compris pour les comptes qui disposent déjà d’un dot. Si c’est cette fonction qui vous fait hésiter à prendre ChatGPT Pro, j’attendrais qu’OpenAI confirme qu’on peut créer son assistant depuis la France.

articles.title: La souris Logitech MX Master 4 passe à 99,99 € pour le Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : La souris Logitech MX Master 4 Graphite à 99,99 €
Actuellement notée 4,5/5 par notre rédaction, la Logitech MX Master 4 brille par sa préhension agréable, ses deux molettes et ses clics silencieux au quotidien. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : elle passe à 99,99 € chez Amazon, Fnac.com, Boulanger.com, Darty.com et Cdiscount Marketplace, soit une baisse d'environ 7 % et 7,99 € d'économie.
Logitech propose avec la MX Master 4 une souris pour la bureautique pensée pour optimiser la navigation au quotidien. Succédant à la MX Master 3, elle intègre une zone de retour haptique ainsi qu'un menu radial Active Ring configurable via l'application Logi Options+. Ce modèle s'est distingué lors de son passage dans notre labo grâce à sa construction soignée et ses commandes complètes.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, la Logitech MX Master 4 descend à 99,99 € chez Amazon, Fnac.com, Boulanger.com, Darty.com et Cdiscount Marketplace, soit environ 7 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (107,98 €). Cela représente une économie de 7,99 €.
Deux molettes et des commandes étendues pour le bureau
Cette souris s'adresse aux utilisateurs qui passent de longues heures devant des tableurs ou des logiciels de création. Comme l'a relevé notre test complet, la présence de deux molettes distinctes permet de gérer indépendamment le défilement vertical et le défilement horizontal. La liaison sans fil s'effectue au choix en Bluetooth ou via une connexion radio 2,4 GHz, complétée par un mode filaire si nécessaire.
Logitech MX Master 4
Points forts
- Préhension agréable.
- Construction de qualité.
- Intégration de l'Active Ring réussie.
- Clics silencieux.
- Deux molettes de défilement.
- Connectivité Bluetooth 2,4 GHz ou filaire.
Points faibles
- Non adaptée à toutes les mains.
- Assez lourde.
L'Active Ring au banc d'essai et un gabarit imposant
L'intégration de la fonction Active Ring offre un raccourci direct vers plusieurs outils personnalisables, ce qui accélère les actions répétitives en bureautique. Les clics restent discrets pour travailler en open space sans gêner ses collègues. Sa forme volumineuse et son poids marqué la destinent en revanche aux grandes mains, ce qui élimine les utilisateurs à la recherche d'une souris légère et compacte.
Logitech G502 X Plus : l'autre option face au Logitech MX Master 4
La Logitech G502 X Plus propose une formule différente, davantage orientée vers les jeux vidéo tout en restant utilisable au travail. Elle embarque des interrupteurs optiques hybrides, un capteur Hero 25K très réactif et de nombreux boutons programmables, même si son poids conséquent peut aussi se faire sentir après plusieurs heures.
Actuellement notée 5/5 dans nos tests, la Logitech G502 X Plus s'avère 20,00 € moins chère que la Logitech MX Master 4 remisée, mais cette dernière reste mieux équipée pour la productivité grâce à sa seconde molette horizontale.
Logitech G502 X Plus
Points forts
- Qualité de construction.
- Polyvalence gaming et bureautique.
- Nombreux boutons paramétrables.
- Molette inclinable et débrayable.
- Capteur très précis.
- Rétroéclairage bien intégré.
- Bouton "sniper" modulaire.
Points faibles
- Pas de version pour gauchers.
- Pas de Bluetooth.
- Un peu lourde pour du FPS.

articles.title: These four 27-inch OLED 240 Hz QHD gaming monitors are stellar deals at less than $300 — Acer, AOC, Gigabyte, and Innocn rock QD-OLED and WOLED panels
articles.text:
These four 27-inch OLED 240 Hz QHD gaming monitors are stellar deals at less than $300 — Acer, AOC, Gigabyte, and Innocn rock QD-OLED and WOLED panels
You can get a speedy 27-inch QHD OLED monitor for less than $300
There was once a time when OLED gaming monitors commanded a hefty premium over their IPS- and VA-based competition. However, especially over the past year, prices have dropped low enough that we’re seeing some really compelling prices on OLED monitors. Such is the case for anyone looking to purchase a 27-inch gaming monitor, which you can now find for well under $300. For example, you can get an Acer Predator X27U W1 for $269.99, while the Innocn 2780S is available for $279 at Amazon.
I’ve found a total of four 27-inch QHD monitors that are worth your attention (including the two mentioned above), so without further ado, let's see what’s cooking.
The Acer Predator X27U W1 is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and a QD-OLED panel. It supports AMD FreeSync Premium and includes two HDMI 2.1 and two DisplayPort 1.4 ports.
The Acer Predator X27U W1 features a 26.5-inch QD-OLED Penta Tandem panel. Acer claims that the Penta Tandem panel boosts luminous efficiency, doubles panel life, and allows for peak brightness of up to 1,000 nits (although typical brightness is closer to 200 nits).
You’ll find a 240 Hz refresh rate with support for AMD FreeSync Premium, 0.03 ms GtG response time, 99 percent coverage of the sRGB color space, an anti-glare coating over the display panel, and dual 3-watt speakers. On the connectivity front, you get two HDMI 2.1 ports, two DisplayPort 1.4 ports, and a single 3.5 mm headphone jack. The Predator X27U W1 is also adjustable for height, pivot, tilt, and swivel. The monitor rings up with a 14 percent discount at Amazon, bringing its final price to $269.99.
The Innocn 2780S is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and a QD-OLED panel. It covers 99% of sRGB and DCI-P3 and offers peak brightness of 400 nits.
The Innocn 2780S follows a similar formula with a matte screen finish, 0.03 ms GtG response time, and 99 percent sRGB coverage (and 99 percent for DCI-P3). However, the monitor doesn’t list any official AMD FreeSync Premium or G-Sync certification, only claiming Adaptive-Sync support from 48 Hz to 240 Hz. Innocn lists brightness for the QD-OLED panel at 250 nits typical and 400 nits peak/HDR. You still get two HDMI 2.1 ports and two DisplayPort 1.4 ports, along with a 3.5 mm headphone jack and two 3-watt speakers. The 2780S is now available at 20 percent off, ringing up at $279.99.
The Gigabyte GO27Q24G switches the formula up slightly, instead opting for a 27-inch Micro Lens Array+ White OLED (MLA+ OLED) display. As the counter to popular QD-OLED panels, WOLED panels tend to be brighter across the operating range. Indeed, Gigabyte states that the GO27Q24G offers a typical brightness of 275 nits and can hit a peak of 1,300 nits with HDR content.
The GO27Q24G is definitely a looker, as it sports a 4-sided borderless design with extremely thin bezels. It also features a RealBlack Glossy, which strikes a good balance between the color-enhancing clarity of a glossy screen coating and the reflection-rejecting characteristics of matte coatings.
The Gigabyte GO27Q24G is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and an MLA+ WOLED panel. It features a RealBlack Glossy display, a 4-sided borderless design, and can hit 1,300 nits peak brightness.
The monitor has AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync Compatible certifications, along with a maximum refresh rate of 240 Hz. As for ports, you’ll get two HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, one USB-C, and one 3.5 mm headphone jack. However, one thing you won’t find is integrated speakers.
We recently reviewed the GO27Q24G and came away impressed with its value, video processing, and brightness. As our Christian Eberele explained, “Image and gaming experience are every bit the equal of monitors costing twice as much. The GO27Q24G’s Micro Lens Array delivers tremendous brightness, as much as 1,300 nits in HDR mode. It also has nearly perfect viewing angles. Color volume isn’t quite as large as panels with Quantum Dots or Tandem RGB Stripes, but you do get over 96% coverage of DCI-P3.”
The Gigabyte GO27Q24G is currently on sale for $297.47, representing a 15 percent discount.
The AOC Agon Pro AG276QZD2 is a 27-inch gaming monitor with a QHD resolution, 240 Hz refresh rate, and a QD-OLED panel. It supports AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync and offers a peak brightness of 1,000 nits.
Finally, we have the AOC Agon Pro AG276QZD2, which is another 27-inch QD-OLED monitor that we reviewed nearly two years ago. The monitor supports AMD FreeSync Premium and Nvidia G-Sync, and has 250 nits typical brightness (1,000 nits peak). It also comes with two HDMI 2.0 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4 port, and a 3.5 mm headphone jack.
Eberle went on to write about the AG276QZD2, stating, “It has a huge color gamut thanks to Quantum Dot tech, which is larger than last year’s AG276QZD. Accuracy comes from a factory calibration that can only be slightly improved with adjustment. It also delivers the best gaming performance available from any monitor with perfect motion resolution and low input lag.”
If the AOC Agon Pro AG276QZD2 tickles your fancy, you can get it now for $297.49, which is a 15 percent discount.

articles.title: Dos bases de datos abiertas expusieron 3.500 millones de contraseñas, números de identidad y documentos
articles.text:
Más de 3.500 millones de nombres de usuario, contraseñas, números de identidad y documentos quedaron expuestos en internet, sin ninguna protección, en dos bases de datos sin relación entre sí.
Una de las bases, con unos 2.000 millones de credenciales, la encontró Jeremiah Fowler, de la empresa de seguridad Black Hills Information Security. La otra, con 1.640 millones de documentos, la halló Greg Pollock, director de investigación de la firma de seguridad UpGuard.
Ambos dicen que los datos afectan a gente de decenas de países. Ninguno logró identificar a los dueños de las bases, y se desconoce cuánto tiempo estuvieron abiertas o si alguien más copió la información.
Dos millones de credenciales robadas con virus
La base de Fowler parece formada por datos robados con programas maliciosos que copian todo lo que una persona usa para entrar a sus cuentas desde una computadora infectada. Según Wired, no hay indicios de que se haya vulnerado a empresas para armarla.
Tenía 8.471 carpetas con datos en texto sin cifrar: correos, usuarios, contraseñas, cookies (archivos que mantienen abierta una sesión), claves de sesión e información del dispositivo. Algunas carpetas se nombraban por país, como Estados Unidos, Reino Unido, Francia, Alemania, España o México.
Fowler halló cientos de millones de cuentas de correo de uso masivo, decenas de millones de direcciones .gov, .edu y .org, más de 100 millones de cuentas de redes sociales y decenas de millones de tiendas en línea. Cybernews, que informó el hallazgo con base en el informe de Fowler, contó 608 millones de registros de Gmail y 114,3 millones de otros servicios de Google.
El propio Cybernews advierte que el total incluye duplicados y no equivale a víctimas: un solo equipo infectado puede entregar decenas de cuentas, y algunas claves quizá ya se cambiaron. Fowler tampoco comprobó duplicados de forma exhaustiva.
Lo que más preocupó a Fowler son unos 400.000 documentos que parecen provenir de un virus más avanzado, que arma un perfil de cada víctima con usuarios, cookies, datos del navegador y archivos importantes. “Si tienes eso, eres dueño de esa persona”, dijo.
Más de 840 millones de números de identidad
La base de Pollock parece orientada a ciudadanos de China. Según su análisis, tenía al menos 840 millones de números nacionales de identidad distintos, 300 millones de teléfonos, unos 11 millones de registros de estudiantes y casi 8 millones de registros de empresas. En una muestra aparecieron datos de niños y de personas fallecidas.
Los archivos estaban ordenados y unificados, algo que Pollock atribuyó a un trabajo deliberado. “Alguien juntó muchos datos y los normalizó para que fueran útiles”, dijo. La base seguía actualizándose hasta la semana previa a su hallazgo y, mientras la investigaba, dejó de estar accesible, posiblemente por un ataque de secuestro de datos o una campaña destructiva.
Pollock aclaró que no puede garantizar la fidelidad de los datos ni descartar que ya circularan en otros sitios. Fowler logró que la empresa de alojamiento retirara la suya de internet.
Ambos investigadores señalaron que los gestores de contraseñas y la verificación en dos pasos han servido para impedir el acceso a cuentas de consumidores, aunque no frenan todos los ataques. Fowler recomienda mantener los equipos actualizados, instalar solo programas confiables y buscar ayuda profesional si se sospecha una infección, porque eliminar el virus no siempre basta para sacar al atacante de las sesiones abiertas.

articles.title: 60 € de remise sur la barre de son Sony Bravia Theatre Bar 8, qui tombe à 449,00 €
articles.text:
Bon plan : La barre de son Sony Bravia Theatre Bar 8 à 449,00 € (-12%)
Actuellement notée 4/5 par notre rédaction, la barre de son Sony Bravia Theatre Bar 8 diffuse un rendu audio équilibré avec une excellente dimension surround. Son prix tombe à 449,00 € chez Sony, soit une baisse d'environ 12 % et 60,00 € d'économie.
La Sony Bravia Theatre Bar 8 prend la relève de la HT-A5000 avec l'objectif de moderniser le home-cinéma du salon dans un format compact. Cette barre de son connectée diffuse un rendu immersif tout en simplifiant son utilisation quotidienne au téléviseur. Ce modèle avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de ses séances d'écoute.
Le système descend à 449,00 € chez Sony, soit environ 12 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (509,00 €). Cela représente une économie de 60,00 € sur cette référence actuellement notée 4/5.
Une scène surround large et une compatibilité audio étendue
Dans un salon, cette barre de son parvient à recréer une bulle sonore convaincante grâce à sa configuration audio en 5.1.4 canaux. Comme le souligne notre test complet, l'appareil délivre un rendu équilibré et enveloppant sans encombrer la pièce d'enceintes physiques supplémentaires.
Ce traitement spatial s'adapte à presque toutes les sources vidéo grâce à la prise en charge des flux Dolby Atmos et DTS:X. Les amateurs de jeux vidéo profitent aussi d'une prise HDMI compatible 4K à 120 Hz, idéale pour brancher une console récente sans perte de fluidité.
Sony Bravia Theatre Bar 8
Points forts
- Son équilibré et polyvalent.
- Dimension Surround excellente.
- Compatibilité avec l’immense majorité des formats audio.
- Intuitivité de l’app Bravia Connect.
- Qualité de construction et compacité.
Points faibles
- Pas de miracle dans les basses fréquences.
- Connectique rachitique.
- Assez peu de réglages disponibles.
- Pas de commandes sur la barre, afficheur très limité.
- Disparition de la compatibilité Chromecast.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une utilisation épurée et des basses contenues
Pour la musique du quotidien, l'application mobile Bravia Connect centralise l'accès aux flux réseau via AirPlay ou Spotify Connect. La barre fait l'impasse sur les commandes directes sur le châssis et sur la compatibilité Chromecast, ce qui impose de tout piloter depuis son smartphone ou la télécommande.
Faute de caisson dédié fourni d'office, le système montre ses limites dans les fréquences les plus basses lors des scènes d'action intenses, ce qui pénalisera les amateurs de gros impacts sans gêner le visionnage courant de films ou de séries.
Samsung HW-Q800H : l'autre option face au Sony Bravia Theatre Bar 8
La Samsung HW-Q800H propose une alternative solide avec une note actuelle de 4,5/5 sur notre banc de test. Elle mise sur une restitution sonore équilibrée et délivre un grave plus généreux dès la sortie du carton grâce à son caisson inclus, même si elle abandonne totalement le décodage des pistes DTS.
Le tarif de la Samsung HW-Q800H est identique à celui du Sony Bravia Theatre Bar 8 au centime près. La barre de Sony conserve l'avantage pour les amateurs de formats audio complets comme le DTS:X, tandis que la Samsung séduira davantage ceux qui recherchent des basses profondes immédiates pour le même prix.
Samsung HW-Q800H
Points forts
- Signature sonore équilibrée.
- Effets surround excellents en frontal.
- Large scène sonore.
- Caisson de basses compact et puissant.
Points faibles
- Effets Dolby Atmos perfectibles.
- Entrée HDMI non compatible 4K/120 Hz, VRR et ALLM.
- Non prise en charge des formats DTS.
- Nouveautés 2026 anecdotiques.

articles.title: Mondo Beni is a pricey, cute camera robot that doesn't always know which way is up — but I'm still a fan
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
Mondo Robotics Beni is a lively, active, slightly chaotic, and resilient camera robot that can track and film you. It's fun to use and have around, but the fact that it can only film from ground level is fairly limiting. You can drive it remotely, or let it use onboard sensors to avoid obstacles on its own, and while Beni's skill in this regard is mixed, this is likely fixable with another firmware update. Overall, Beni is one of the more advanced consumer robots on the market, but it costs more than you probably want to pay for a robot with relatively limited filming and autonomous features.
- 
Value
- 
Design
- 
Performance
Reasons to buy
- + Cute and responsive
- + Fast and resilient
- + Good quality video
Reasons to avoid
- - Pricey
- - Obstacle detection is hit and miss
- - Battery life limited to an hour
Why you can trust TechRadar We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Mondo Beni Review: One-minute review
I've been kicking my robot a lot lately. Don't worry, it's not abuse. Mondo Robotics' Beni camera robot is designed to take a kick or two and pop right back up.
Of course, it's more than that. The adorable, two-wheel bot is mobile, animated, and capable of following you around like a hyperactive puppy — albeit one that can film you at your request. Beni is full of beeps and other cloying sounds that beg for attention. Its flat head and two LEDs blink and look up at you from its ground-based vantage point. Basically, it engages with you with pet-like enthusiasm.
Beni is also athletic, jumping and flipping forwards, backwards, and left and right with the touch of the app (or a gesture) in ways that reveal the robot's startling power and versatility.
Perhaps that's why, even in repose, Beni is a loud robot. From the moment I turned Beni on, I heard the fans whirring inside, doing their level best to keep the hyperactive mobile companion cool.
Like any good robot, Beni has multiple sensors that help it interpret and adjust to its world. But those sensors occasionally failed to protect Beni from basic obstacles like a table, my leg, or a flight of stairs. Our time together will always be marred by the time I let Beni go flying down my front steps. Beni's tough, and survived, but not without a scuffed eye.
Beni is both a robot companion and an automaton with one very specific purpose: filming its owners. That may or may not be enough to justify the $799 price tag ($60 off this Black Friday). I know that the hefty little guy has grown on me, but I also doubt I'd buy one for myself.
Mondo Beni Review: Price and availability
Mondo Robotics unveiled its Beni robot in September 24. The Standard Combo bundle, which costs $799 / £699, includes the robot, one battery pack, a wearable motion controller, one hat, a chest protection plate, and the standard wheel set. My test unit shipped with the Explore Combo, which, for roughly $100 / £100 more, adds off-road wheels, a second battery, a charging hub, and more protective coverings.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
This is a fairly sophisticated camera robot, which should make the price more palatable. Still, you have to really care about having yourself filmed to want one.
There is, by the way, a Black Friday offer direct from Mondo, which takes $60 off in the US.
Mondo Robotics Beni Review: Design and setup
Mondo Robotics Beni arrives, thankfully, fully assembled. Its compact four-pound body is tightly folded up, just waiting for its brick-like battery pack and app connectivity.
Beni's white body, with orange accents, feels sturdy. To get started using it, I installed the Mondo app on my iPhone 18 Pro Max, connected to Beni's Wi-Fi network, and, as instructed, unfolded Beni's legs to rest the two gray rubber wheels on the floor (you hold down an 'up' button in the app to get Beni to stand).
The battery can charge in-body (it can take about 90 minutes), but if you have the charge hub, you can charge not only up to two batteries at a time, but there's a special compartment for charging the wearable remote control.
Beni's battery snaps into its back. A short press and then a long press on the pack's lone button powers up the robot, which instantly stands up and appears to look around.
In a way, it is: Mondo Beni has a pair of front-facing cameras in its body that it uses for navigation and obstacle avoidance. There's also a video camera between its large LED eyes, capable of filming in 4K at up to 60fps. As for Beni's big, blinking 'eyes,' they might appear to stare at you, but they actually don't see anything.
Powered up, Beni stands about nine inches tall. That means that unless you put it on a table (I wouldn't recommend it), Beni and its camera will always be looking up at you.
It's fair to describe Beni as a drone camera, but instead of flying above you for dramatic overhead shots, Beni can only provide a ground-level view, a limitation that may frustrate pro content creators.
Beni ships with one breastplate that basically sticks onto its front, but you can buy an entire collection to snap onto the legs, head, and back. Given Beni's penchant for bumping into things and sometimes taking a tumble, they might come in handy.
I also tried out the off-road wheels, which are useful for outdoor jaunts. I kind of love how the wheels detach and reattach: there's a spot on each wheel hub that I pinched together to release the wheels from the axle, and then I used the same spot to snap them back on. Easy and smart. It's also worth noting here that, even with the standard wheels, Beni easily rolls over small obstacles like almost inch-high room dividers.
To match Beni's orange "ears," Mondo Robotics includes a stylish plastic baseball hat that, after peeling the protective layer from two tape strips, I stuck on Beni's head. It looked cute and, remarkably, never popped off.
Mondo Robotics Beni Review: Performance
Mondo Beni is a semi-autonomous robot. Left alone, it balances on two wheels, looks around, makes noises, and will get back up if you kick it over, which I did over and over again. You can turn on follow mode, and Beni will trail you and follow alongside you.
With a max speed of 17.9mph, you won't outrun Beni — trust me, I tried. I set Beni to Trail Tracking mode, and it carefully followed five feet behind me, and when I took off in a run, Beni easily kept up. The little robot also had no trouble stopping on a dime whenever I pulled up short.
Beni can also keep you in view with 'Spotlight' tracking mode, which kept me in frame while I was on the move.
The only time Beni had trouble following me was when I used 'Parallel' mode. In this mode, Beni was supposed to follow alongside me, but it quickly ran right into my ankle.
Beni is also able to climb (or really bound up) steps, but I had to turn on a special and relatively hidden mode that lets it autonomously detect a staircase, and then leap to surmount each step.
In my experience, Beni never made it up a single staircase in my home. When I took Beni outside and had it follow me, it would stop short of the staircase into my home. In my house, it did try to take the staircase to the second floor, but each time it bounded up the first flight, it would end up bouncing off the step.
Beni was also no better at avoiding injury, including obstacles like my home's front porch. I walked down the steps and turned around to see Beni taking a header off the first step and then tumbling to the ground below.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
You can use the app to remotely control Beni or the wearable tracker, which includes a thumb-ready joystick (I would press it down to make Beni jump). There are also buttons for recording video and initiating tracking, a speed slider (I kept it in the default mode), a game mode button, and a big stop/sit button.
One app setting let me use the phone as a motion-control remote, meaning Beni would travel in whichever direction I tilted my iPhone, and a steeper tilt would make the robot go faster. It was the best and most intuitive way to control Beni.
I often used the wearable controller to drive Beni, though I found it was best to use it in my right hand as opposed to awkwardly wearing the joystick on my wrist. Usefully, the main controller is only magnetically seated in the wristband, so it was easy enough to pop off and hold in my hand.
Beni has a bunch of canned filming modes, or 'One Tap Shots,' including Comet Orbit, Dolly Overtake, and Swoop Orbit. All are useful if you have room to move for both you and Beni. Video quality is wide-angle and good, though the audio can include the sound of Beni's wheels on, for instance, a pavement.
There are also games like Coin Hunter (work with Beni to find hidden virtual coins), Tug of War, which was kind of dumb, and Motion Control, which is not really a game so much as it is the control mode that lets you use your phone's position to control Beni.
Perhaps the best part of Beni is its personality. The robot responds in a limited way to my voice (when I start with "Beni Beni") and even to my touch, or at least when I press down on it or shake its head. Beni can also respond to hand gestures like a wave or peace sign to start video recording. I enjoyed using the thumbs up, left, and right, to get Beni to jump, flip left, or flip right, respectively.
Watching me the way it does, Beni seems attentive, but without any real language, our interactions are limited; I actually think I wouldn't mind if Beni could speak, maybe that'll come with a future update.
Mondo Robotics Beni Review: Battery life
Beni lasted about an hour on a full charge, which is not bad, but if you have Beni out and about for a big shoot, the run time might seem a bit limited.
When the charge gets down to a single bar, Beni can no longer perform his signature tricks: jumping and flipping. At least the robot can still right itself if I kick it over.

He also wrote a popular, weekly tech column for Medium called The Upgrade.

articles.title: Ubuntu 26.10 Improves Intel Panther Lake iGPU Performance on Linux
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
Ubuntu 26.10 Improves Intel Panther Lake iGPU Performance on Linux
There was much excitement when Intel's Panther Lake CPUs launched with the powerful new Arc B390 iGPUs, and although Linux gaming performance was impressive on those systems, it always takes time for mainstream distributions, like Ubuntu, to catch up to bleeding edge hardware. For Ubuntu, it seems as though the 26.10 update has taken a pretty substantial step towards taking full advantage of the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H and its B390 iGPU, according to recent tests by Phoronix. 
According to the testing, CPU performance improvements in tasks like code compilation and CPU-based AI workflows were minimal—on the order of 1-2%—but the iGPU saw significant improvements in graphics benchmarks, scoring a 65% FPS improvement in the yquake2 Vulkan benchmark and a 15% improvement in the GravityMark 1.87 Vulkan ray tracing benchmark. There were also some marginal improvements in media encoding benchmarks, with 4K AV1 encoding in particular seeing an improvement of up to 24%. These tests were conducted on a Dell XPS 14 laptop, which has historically been a thermally constrained form factor, so devices with a higher thermal ceiling can likely expect to see more improvements on the graphics side of things.The update from Ubuntu 26.04 LTS to Ubuntu 26.10 has updated the system to the new Kernel 7.3, GNOME Shell 51, Mesa driver version 26.2, and Gnu Compiler Collection 15.3, among other changes. Likely the biggest drivers behind any iGPU performance improvements here are going to be the new kernel and the updated Mesa drivers, which means these improvements should be seen in other distributions that use the updated components as well.
Source:
				Phoronix			
	
	
	
		
	
		
2 Comments on Ubuntu 26.10 Improves Intel Panther Lake iGPU Performance on Linux
That's a fairly sizeable performance jump considering PTL was already the most compelling laptop chip.
Yup, kernel 7.3 (and Mesa 26.3.1) are shaping up to be big improvements for Intel GPUs/iGPUs on Linux, especially for Lunar Lake and Panther Lake. It's not quite there with Strix/Gorgon Point performance yet, but getting there.

- À savoir : les 16 Go de DDR4 tiennent sur une seule barrette, et le SSD de 512 Go se remplit vite avec quelques gros jeux.
Cybertek BLACKROCK : la RTX 5060 Ti sur une plateforme AM5 en DDR5, à 1 349,99 €
Le BLACKROCK passe à la plateforme AM5 d’AMD avec un Ryzen 5 8400F (6 cœurs, 12 threads), 16 Go de DDR5 à 6 000 MHz et une GeForce RTX 5060 Ti OC de 8 Go. Le processeur est refroidi par un watercooling MSI MAG Coreliquid A13 de 240 mm, sur une carte mère MSI MAG A620AM Gaming EVO WIFI5. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Une base plus récente : socket AM5 et DDR5 à 6 000 MHz, quand le BLACKCYBER reste en AM4 et en DDR4.
- Un watercooling 240 mm : le MSI MAG Coreliquid A13 refroidit le Ryzen 5 8400F.
- À savoir : la remise se limite à 50 €, les 16 Go de DDR5 tiennent sur une seule barrette et le SSD de 500 Go est le plus petit de la sélection. Cybertek propose un SSD de 1 To en option, pour 159,99 € de plus.
Cybertek BLACKSAPPHIRE : la RTX 5080 et le Ryzen 7 9800X3D noté 9/10, à 3 299,99 €
Notre test de la GeForce RTX 5080 lui a attribué 8/10 : en 4K, avec le DLSS 4 et la génération multi-images, elle dépasse 150 images par seconde dans Cyberpunk 2077 en path tracing. Le Ryzen 7 9800X3D qui l’accompagne a obtenu 9/10 dans notre test du Ryzen 7 9800X3D, porté par ses 96 Mo de cache L3. Cybertek complète avec 32 Go de DDR5 à 6 000 MHz et un SSD Samsung 990 EVO de 2 To. Nous ne l’avons pas testé.
✅ Points forts
- Une alimentation de 1 050 W : la M.RED MRR-1050, certifiée 80+ Gold, laisse de la marge à la RTX 5080, mesurée à 368 W en charge dans notre test.
- Un watercooling 360 mm : le M.RED Onyx refroidit le Ryzen 7 9800X3D, contre 240 mm sur les deux autres PC de la sélection.
- À savoir : aucun prix barré n’est affiché sur ce modèle, et sans génération multi-images la RTX 5080 ne devance la RTX 4080 que de 17 % en 4K, selon notre test.
Black Friday 2026 : comment Cybertek déroule ses promos sur les PC gamer
Le Black Friday tombe le vendredi 27 novembre et le Cyber Monday le lundi 30, mais les configurations de cette sélection sont déjà en ligne à leur prix actuel. Chez Cybertek, l’opération s’affiche sous le nom de Black Month, avec un paiement en quatre fois sans frais par Alma proposé du 2 novembre au 2 décembre, sous réserve d’acceptation. Les prix d’un PC monté dépendent du coût de chaque composant et peuvent bouger d’ici vendredi : noter dès maintenant celui de la configuration qui vous intéresse permet de comparer sereinement. Pour suivre les autres offres, notre page Black Friday réunit chaque jour celles retenues par la rédaction.
Comment savoir si un PC gamer tout monté vaut vraiment son prix ?
Le nom de la carte graphique ne suffit pas : regardez la quantité de mémoire vidéo, 8 Go sur les RTX 5060 et 5060 Ti de cette sélection, contre 16 Go sur la RTX 5080. Vérifiez ensuite les composants moins visibles, comme le nombre de barrettes de RAM, la capacité du SSD et la puissance de l’alimentation. Windows est souvent livré en version d’essai : chez Cybertek, la licence définitive coûte 159,99 € de plus en édition Home, une somme à intégrer au budget.
