articles.title: Un robot blando impreso en 3D corre a 17 kilómetros por hora sin usar electrónica
articles.text:
Ingenieros de la Universidad de California en San Diego construyeron un robot de seis patas, hecho solo de materiales blandos e impreso en 3D de una sola vez, que alcanza 4,72 metros por segundo (unos 17 kilómetros por hora) sin ningún componente electrónico. El trabajo se publicó el 18 de noviembre en la revista Science Robotics.
Según la universidad, es el robot totalmente blando más rápido construido hasta ahora. Corre sobre arena, mantillo, grava, césped y concreto, baja escaleras, nada y camina bajo el agua. Se fabrica con un solo material y una impresora de escritorio común.
El equipo lo dirigieron el investigador posdoctoral Yichen Zhai y el profesor Michael T. Tolley, del Laboratorio de Robótica e Diseño Bioinspirado de la Facultad de Ingeniería Jacobs. Su primer robot blando impreso en 3D y movido por aire, desarrollado en 2022, avanzaba 4 centímetros por segundo. El nuevo es más de 100 veces más rápido.
Una idea tomada de la máquina de vapor
Dentro del robot hay una serie de cámaras, válvulas y tubos que mueven las patas cuando circula aire a presión. Para ir más rápido había que aumentar la presión, pero eso desperdiciaba aire que aún tenía mucha energía. La solución fue copiar la máquina de vapor de expansión compuesta.
El aire circula dos veces: primero por cámaras pequeñas de alta presión, que accionan las válvulas, y después por cámaras grandes de baja presión, que mueven las patas. Según el artículo científico, con una presión de 408 kilopascales el robot da 29 pasos por segundo, y las patas generan una potencia mecánica estimada de 169 vatios.
Las patas se mueven en dos grupos de tres, alternados, como un trípode. Con una carga de 257 gramos, el robot conserva más de la mitad de su velocidad máxima: 2,69 metros por segundo.
“Nuestro primer robot caminante demostró lo que era posible, pero era demasiado lento. Esperábamos superar esa limitación y tuvimos la suerte de encontrar una solución para hacer el nuevo robot 100 veces más rápido”, dijo Zhai, quien ya no integra el laboratorio.
Terrenos distintos, mismo control
El robot usó siempre la misma lógica de control neumático, sin sensores ni programación, en todos los terrenos. La mayor velocidad fuera del laboratorio la logró en grava: 3,82 metros por segundo. En el resto de superficies, por falta de tracción, avanzó entre 1,6 y 2,2 metros por segundo, y en el agua, tanto en la superficie como sumergido, no superó los 0,5.
Los autores también lo hicieron funcionar con agua de la canilla en lugar de aire. Con ese líquido rindió menos que una versión más simple, porque el agua casi no se comprime y el segundo paso de expansión no aporta trabajo adicional.
El límite: sigue atado a una manguera
Por ahora el robot solo funciona conectado a una fuente de aire comprimido, como un compresor. Consume 254 litros estándar por minuto. En una prueba con un cartucho portátil de 16 gramos de dióxido de carbono líquido, el aire duró unos dos segundos: recorrió 1,2 metros en 4,5 segundos, con una velocidad máxima de 1,2 metros por segundo.
La durabilidad también es limitada. Cinco robots sometidos a pruebas de vida útil fallaron tras entre 330.000 y 380.000 ciclos, es decir, de tres a cuatro horas de funcionamiento continuo, por grietas en las membranas internas.
Los investigadores plantean usos donde la electrónica no funciona o no conviene: zonas con radiación o campos magnéticos intensos, respuesta a desastres y exploración espacial. En el artículo mencionan además el riego y la limpieza con agua. Sus próximos pasos son reducir el consumo de aire para operar sin manguera y lograr movimientos más complejos, como girar y manipular objetos.

articles.title: Bambu Lab shows off H3C tool changer, first laser at Formnext 2026 — Prusa Research, Snapmaker, Creality, Elegoo, Anycubic, and Flashforge also on display
articles.text:
Bambu Lab shows off H3C tool changer, first laser at Formnext 2026 — Prusa Research, Snapmaker, Creality, Elegoo, Anycubic, and Flashforge also on display
The latest in 3D printing tech comes to Frankfurt.
Once a year, all the world’s 3D printing manufacturers gather for Formnext in Frankfurt, Germany, to showcase new technologies, software, and ideas. This year’s show was more compact, with three halls instead of four, but consumer 3D printers had a larger presence. Spread across two halls, we found Bambu Lab, Prusa Research, Snapmaker, Creality, Elegoo, Anycubic, and Flashforge, plus a few newbies like Axiloop.
Startup SnowX was a popular booth, presenting the first consumer-grade desktop metal 3D printer coming soon to Kickstarter.
I counted ten tool-changing 3D printers on the show floor, five of which I’ve already reviewed. Elegoo surprised us all by launching its Centauri X Ultra four-color tool changer at the show, while Axiloop’s MC 8 arrived on my front porch that morning.
Only Anycubic is standing pat with a single-nozzle multicolor machine. Instead, it presented its new partnership with Thingiverse.
Full-color UV printers were on display as well, with Flashforge showing off its CJ270, which was teased last year.
Editor’s Note: Snapmaker provided travel accommodations for this trip. Coverage remains editorially independent.
Bambu Lab H3C: Nine tool heads
Bambu Lab showed off its latest printers, the H3C, a tool changer (starting at $2,499) with nine lightweight tools we reviewed earlier in the month, and its first laser, the R1, reviewed in September, which retails at $2,499.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
More interesting is the launch of “Bambu Circle,” a pilot program that will start in the Netherlands and slowly expand across Europe. The goal is a network of local hubs to assist entrepreneurs with their 3D printing side hustle. Bambu Circle would enlist repair specialists and community ambassadors to provide a helping hand and an in-person retail shop with space for meetups. ,
At the moment, there is no plan to launch a similar program in the United States; however, we have many retailers here who offer official warranty support, parts, and tons of filament. A map on the Bambu Lab lists 31 US resellers, though that number is a bit skewed since there are also 31 MicroCenters in the US.
Prusa Research: Print Anywhere without the Cloud
Prusa Research previewed the Rugged, a CORE One L+ adapted for printing in the harshest environments. The printer has a sealed case that keeps out both humidity and dust while providing extra protection during transport for machines used in the field. The CORE One L+ tucked inside is equipped with a high-temperature, hardened steel nozzle for printing advanced engineering filaments. It also comes with Prusa’s Zero-Trace system, which is an air-gapped machine with no flash drive storage, no USB slot, no Wi-Fi, and no camera. They can only accept files from your own cryptographically paired Prusa Connect server. These extremely secure, extremely tough machines are meant for classified and proprietary work environments.
However, you don’t need to have a security clearance to jump on board Prusa Connect Local, a free-to-use version of Prusa Connect for anyone who wishes to keep their 3D printers off the internet. The server can run on Linux, Windows, Mac, or a Raspberry Pi, and can handle a print farm of two to 400. It’s currently set up for any Prusa Printer, but it is open source, so you are free to tinker around with it and add your own extensions.
Snapmaker: Full Spectrum
Snapmaker showed off what you can do with its four-color U1 tool changer. Ratdoux, the developer behind Full Spectrum, was on hand to chat with us. He devised a system of color-blending filaments that take thin layers of cyan, yellow, and magenta mixed with either gray or white, which can create nearly any other color. He said it was inspired by a conversation on Reddit where users were mixing colors in Blender, and he came up with a simpler way to do it in the slicer. Snapmaker immediately hired him to lead a development team for its fork of OrcaSlicer.
Amazingly, Full Spectrum went from an experimental slicer hack to a must-have for every tool changer in the space of nine months. Snapmaker’s Full Spectrum is tailored for the U1 on open-source OrcaSlicer, while Bambu Lab installed a “Color Mixing” tool in Bambu Studio and Prusa Research developed their own “ColorMix” technology based on hex codes.
Full Spectrum and similar tools can be used on any multimaterial 3D printer. However, because it looks best with super thin layers, tool changers are more efficient and less wasteful.
Snapmaker has since introduced a Full Spectrum filament bundle optimized for four-color machines: a CMYW for lighter, bright colors and a CMYG (gray edition) for darker shades. Ratdoux said the secret is in the filament’s light Transmission Distance (TD), which measures how translucent the material is. Colors that allow more light to pass through them create a better illusion of blending. The parrot and fox pictured above were printed using CMYG and a .08mm layer height. There was no orange, purple, green or black filament used in those prints.
Axiloop MC8 Pro : Eight Color Kickstarter
We also found Axiloop, an eight-color tool changer that’s already raised over $700,000 on Kickstarter. The fully enclosed CoreXY machine has a 300x300mm build plate, 4-second tool swaps, and claims to have “near-zero” wipe-free tool changes. Its price for the MC8 Pro is $1,499 for early backers, while the open frame MC8 is $1,099.
Our review unit arrived while I was at Formnext, so I’m excited to put it to the test soon.
Peopoly: Its a Big Boi
Peopoly’s Giga 800 is a large-scale pellet feeder that’s a bit north of our normal prosumer range at $15,000, but I felt it was worth mentioning because it's from our friends at Siraya Tech, who make superior filaments and resin. I noticed quite a few YouTubers happily climb into the machine to show how big it truly is.
The machine has an extrusion output of three kilos an HOUR, which would be equivalent to three spools of normal filament, and can use a 3mm nozzle for chonky prints. We’ve reviewed a similar-sized open-frame “giga” machine before, so I know that being hampered by a normal .4mm nozzle is not something you want with a print volume this large. The enclosed machine is capable of running everything from PLA and TPU to PET-CF and PPA-GF.
Creality Ender Lasers, Scanners and a Kid Printer
Creality had quite a few machines out, but the most interesting were the Creality Falcon T1 UV Laser we reviewed this summer and the new Falcon A1C portable laser we’ll be reviewing soon. The T1 is able to do inner engraving in glass in just a few minutes, and the team was happy to show me the workflow after I supplied them with a photo. They took my selfie, ran it through Creality’s AI to create a 3D bust, then zapped it into a 2 x 3 inch chunk of glass. It was an impressive demo.
They also showed off several handheld scanners, which Creality feels will enable makers to create more practical prints without needing a ton of CAD skills. My favorite is the Creality Pika we reviewed in October.
I’m also particularly intrigued by the mBox kid printer, with a small 153x153mm build plate but lots of safety features to make it child-friendly. The printer is priced at $329, which isn’t bad for a full-feature printer. However, good luck finding one to buy: this printer is only available on the TikTok Shop in the US until December 10.
Another disappointment was the Creality M1 filament maker with its companion R1 shredder. The unit was on display, but not running, which makes me believe they haven’t quite figured out how to make the dream of home filament making a reality.
Elegoo Centauri X Ultra: Four color tool changer
Elegoo surprised us all with the Centauri X Ultra, a four-color tool changer variation of the wildly successful Centauri Carbon. The Centauri X Ultra is scheduled to release early in 2027. It has a 256x256mm bed, making it the same size as its siblings. The machine is completely enclosed and cleverly contains the side-mounted spools in a Tupperware-like sealed box. The machine has filament drying and a nozzle that can hit 350C, making it a good candidate for high-temperature filaments. It also claims to have 5-second color swaps without waste, but we’ll test that as soon as we get our hands on one.
BIQU: Even more Panda-Verse
BIQU once again impressed us with their line of Panda-Verse accessories for your Bambu Lab machine. The Panda Treat ($159.99), which applies edible ink to cookies, cakes, and cups of frothy coffee, is out and ready for review. The BIQU x FOXLT Infinity Bed ($259) adds a tiny conveyor bed to your P1S or P2S printer for endless printing. But the most ambitious this year is the BIQU Vault, starting at $499. This is a filament storage system like no other, with an RFID tag tracking system that helps you catalog your filament and tell you where it is in your workshop.
FlashForge: CJ270 UV Printing
FlashForge revealed its CJ270 full-color 3D printer, priced at $ 3,999 and now shipping. It is listed as a MultiJet Printer, which uses UV ink to build up models, with a build size of 180 x 120 x 100 mm. Unlike other UV printers, the CJ270 has seven printheads (one for each ink channel), so if one gets clogged, you don’t need to replace the entire printhead. It uses CMYK ink, plus white, clear, and a water-washable support material. The sample models shown were impressive, with lots of detail and strong color.
Anycubic x Thingiverse
Anycubic didn’t have any new machines to show off, but they did have a huge announcement to make: they are collaborating with Thingiverse to bring millions of models into Anycubic’s file-sharing library, MakerOnline. Select designs will be converted into multicolor models for one-click printing from Anycubic’s mobile app.
The company is also looking into adding an AI tool dubbed AnyLab to its website to help users create their own designs.
Download the Tom's Hardware app for up-to-the-minute updates on iOS and Android. Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Denise Bertacchi is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware US, covering 3D printing. Denise has been crafting with PCs since she discovered Print Shop had clip art on her Apple IIe. She loves reviewing 3D printers because she can mix all her passions: printing, photography, and writing.

articles.title: Congress scrutinizes Jensen Huang’s return as Megaspeed restrictions raise questions
articles.text:
Congress scrutinizes Jensen Huang’s return as Megaspeed restrictions raise questions
Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle are criticizing Nvidia Corp.’s decision to rehire Jensen Huang as its chief executive.
The criticism came against the backdrop of a controversial move by the U.S. Commerce Department. The agency applied new export restrictions to Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud operator. The company played a prominent role in the spy controversy that led to Huang’s resignation. According to trade experts, the Commerce Department left out a key clause that is usually included in such restrictions.
Huang resigned on Nov. 12 following revelations that he had an affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive. Early reporting about the relationship indicated that she was found to have passed intelligence to China. The U.S. Justice Department later stated that it has not yet reached a conclusion on whether Alice Huang is a spy. Earlier this week, the New York Times reported that she maintained contact with a Chinese intelligence official.
Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang on Monday after U.S. President Donald Trump and tech industry figures urged directors to bring him back. The move drew widespread criticism from members of Congress.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York), who is set to become House Speaker, called the reinstatement “indefensible, irresponsible and incomprehensible.” Rep. Don Bacon (R-Nebraska), the chair of House Subcommittee on Cyber, Information Technologies and Innovation, said that “it’s inexplicable to me why they want this guy back as CEO.” Former Utah Republican Senator and Massachusetts Governor Mitt Romney tweeted: “Let me get this straight: we rushed AI along without regulating safeguards in order to stay ahead of China and at the same time, we sold China the very chips they’d need to get ahead of us. Smells of profit, corruption and perhaps worse.”
Multiple lawmakers told CNBC that they plan to scrutinize Huang’s conduct closely. The executive is scheduled to testify before multiple Congressional committees next Tuesday. Furthermore, Sen. Ron Wyden (D-Oregon) told the outlet that Democrats plan to scrutinize the Trump administration’s role in the matter.
The Commerce Department today added Megaspeed and several of its regional affiliates to its Entity List. Companies on the list can only purchase sensitive products such as graphics cards if they obtain a license from the U.S. government. According to Gizmodo, the move has drawn scrutiny because the restrictions applied to Megaspeed include a loophole.
All the companies on the Entity List are prohibited from buying Nvidia’s latest chips unless they secure a license. Most of them are also unable to buy lower-end graphics cards, high-bandwidth memory and related hardware. The latter restrictions are specified in a clause called the FDPR provision. The Commerce Department has reportedly not applied the FDPR provision to Megaspeed when it added the company to the Entity List.
Huang returned to Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters on Monday. The news sent the chipmaker’s stock soaring more than 30%, although it parred some of the gains today. Nvidia shares are down 5.8% from Monday.
Wired today published excerpts from Huang’s all-hands meeting with employees. The executive apologized for his affairs and for his management style, which has also come under scrutiny in recent days. He added that he will undergo a “360-degree review” and that Nvidia’s code of conduct is still in effect.

articles.title: ZSA Lauches Wireless Voyager Ergonomic Keyboard with User-Replaceable Batteries and QMK Support
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
ZSA Lauches Wireless Voyager Ergonomic Keyboard with User-Replaceable Batteries and QMK Support
After publicly resisting the demand for wireless ergonomic keyboards, citing concerns about reliability, longevity, performance, and ZSA has seemingly finally given in and designed a wireless update to its Voyager split ergonomic keyboard. The wireless Voyager uses the same base as the existing Voyager keyboard, a 52-key split ergonomic mechanical keyboard with optional modular trackpad and trackball attachments. The new Voyager is also still based on the Choc V1 switch standard. The only major change is that there is now a battery pack and wireless module strapped to the top of each half of the keyboard, providing Bluetooth connectivity to the host and between the two halves of the split keyboard. 
ZSA says that the wireless Voyager is capable of up to 7 days of use on a single charge with RGB backlighting enabled and both the Navigator trackpad and trackball connected and up to 30 days with just the keyboards and with RGB disabled. The wireless Voyager also works with Oryx, the brand's QMK-based configurator software, and the two halves of the keyboard can still be connected via a TRRS cable to make charging easier. The new Wireless Voyager is available on the ZSA online shop for $699 including both the Navigator trackball and trackpad. Just the wireless Voyager keyboard will set you back $429. That price also gets you shine-through, double-shot PBT keycaps, a dedicated carrying case, and plenty of accessories.ZSA has updated the previous FAQ page addressing its prior lack of wireless connectivity, explaining in the update that, with the Wireless Voyager, ZSA has managed to satisfactorily address most of the issues surrounding the use of wireless connectivity in a keyboard. The batteries are user-replaceable, and they use bog-standard 18650 cells, which means that even if ZSA doesn't provide spares, there will be a supply of affordable cells for years to come. ZSA even brags that a "single Phillips screw is all that stands between you and the Wireless Voyager's battery," suggesting the battery replacement procedure is also designed to be simple. Although ZSA doesn't specify battery capacity for the Wireless Voyager, a standard 18650 cell can hold up to 3,600 mAh if procured from a reputable source, meaning the Wireless Voyager could have up to 7,200 mAh of capacity, which lines up with the long battery life.

articles.title: L'action-cam GoPro Mission 1 Pro passe à 529,00 € pour le Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : L'action cam GoPro GoPro Mission 1 Pro - Caméra d'action cinéma 8K 60 à 529,00 € (-13%)
Capablpe de filmer en 8K 60p avec un bruit numérique réduit et une excellente stabilisation, la GoPro GoPro Mission 1 Pro - Caméra d'action cinéma 8K 60 affiche une note actuelle de 4,5/5 dans nos tests. Le Black Friday 2026 est l'occasion de se l'offrir moins cher : elle passe à 529,00 € chez Amazon et Boulanger.com, soit une baisse d'environ 13 % et 81,33 € d'économie.
Avec la GoPro Mission 1 Pro, le fabricant américain opère un virage technique majeur en misant sur un véritable saut qualitatif pour l'image. Cette caméra d'action s'adresse aux créateurs exigeants grâce à une captation très définie, capable de s'intégrer directement dans des flux de tournage avancés. Ce modèle haut de gamme avait convaincu notre laboratoire lors de son évaluation.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, l'action-cam descend à 529,00 € chez Amazon et Boulanger.com, soit environ 13 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (610,33 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 81,33 €.
Une qualité d'image en 8K 60p pensée pour les tournages exigeants
Sur le terrain, la GoPro Mission 1 Pro franchit un cap net par rapport aux générations Hero traditionnelles. Elle autorise un enregistrement vidéo très fin qui grimpe jusqu'à la définition 8K à 60 images par seconde, tout en limitant le bruit numérique sur les séquences d'action. Comme le souligne notre test complet, les vidéastes peuvent également exploiter des fichiers GP-LOG ou ralentir fortement l'action via les modes 4K à 120 images par seconde et 1080p à 960 images par seconde. L'ensemble bénéficie en plus d'une fabrication soignée et d'un écran arrière tactile particulièrement réactif pour faciliter les réglages en direct.
GoPro GoPro Mission 1 Pro - Caméra d'action cinéma 8K 60
Points forts
- Qualité d'image en 8K 60p.
- Moins de bruit numérique que par le passé.
- 4K 120p et ralentis 1080p960.
- Presque un compact expert 28 mm.
- Qualité de fabrication.
- Écran arrière très réactif.
Points faibles
- Plus lourde que la Hero 13.
- Pare-soleil peu fiable.
- Attention à la chauffe en 4K 120 et 8K 60 !
- Progrès qui arrivent un peu tard.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une montée en température à surveiller sur les formats lourds
Cette débauche de puissance réclame toutefois quelques précautions d'emploi lors des sessions prolongées. L'appareil a tendance à chauffer nettement lorsque les cadences les plus exigeantes sont sollicitées, en particulier en 4K à 120 images par seconde ou en 8K à 60 images par seconde. Cette contrainte thermique gênera surtout les utilisateurs qui tournent en continu sous un climat chaud, mais elle reste sans impact sur les prises de vue courtes ou les séquences dynamiques du quotidien.
GoPro Hero11 Black Mini : l'autre option face au GoPro Mission 1 Pro
Pour un usage plus simple ou pour fixer une caméra dans des espaces réduits, la GoPro Hero11 Black Mini adopte une philosophie différente. Ce boîtier compact fait l'impasse sur l'écran de contrôle et impose de passer par un smartphone, mais il conserve une stabilisation de haut vol qui lui vaut la note maximale de 5/5 à ce jour dans nos colonnes.
La Hero11 Black Mini coûte 312,39 € de moins que la Mission 1 Pro à son tarif remisé. Si vous cherchez un boîtier épuré et très économique, la Hero11 Black Mini est tout indiquée, mais la GoPro Mission 1 Pro reste indispensable pour qui exige la précision de la 8K 60p et les réglages vidéo avancés.
GoPro Hero11 Black Mini (Hero 11 Black Mini)
Points forts
- 5,3K à 60 i/s, 4K Ultra HD à 120 i/s, 2,7K à 240 i/s.
- Excellente stabilisation.
- Maintien de l'horizon intégré très performant jusqu'à 360°.
- Résistance aux chocs et étanche jusqu'à 10 mètres sans caisson.
- Doubles fixations directement intégrée au châssis.
- Compacité.
- Différents modes créatifs facilement utilisables.
- Upload et montage automatique (avec abonnement).
Points faibles
- Gestion complexe des angles, des définitions, des cadences et des stabilisations.
- Les meilleurs modes de stabilisation ne sont pas disponibles aux cadences les plus rapides.
- Chauffe rapidement avec les réglages les plus exigeants.
- Pas d'écran de contrôle ou de retour vidéo.
- Diffusion en direct limitée à la définition FHD.
- Qualité d'image qui n'évolue pas.

articles.title: 3,5 milliards de données personnelles en libre accès : des pirates laissent à leur tour fuiter leurs fichiers
articles.text:
Deux chercheurs en cybersécurité ont découvert d'immenses bases de données accessibles sur Internet sans la moindre authentification. Identifiants, mots de passe, données administratives et cookies de session y côtoyaient des dossiers permettant de reconstituer la vie numérique de leurs victimes.
Les cybercriminels ne sont pas à l'abri des erreurs de sécurité qu'ils exploitent chez les autres. Comme le rapporte WIRED, deux chercheurs ont découvert, à peu près au même moment, deux bases de données sans lien apparent entre elles, qui totalisaient plus de 3,5 milliards d'enregistrements. Tout porte à croire qu'elles servaient à centraliser et à exploiter des informations personnelles dérobées au fil des ans.
Des milliards de données volées, collectées et triées
La première base, découverte par Greg Pollock, directeur de la recherche chez UpGuard, regroupait 1,64 milliard de documents concernant en grande majorité la population chinoise. Le chercheur y a recensé au moins 840 millions de numéros d'identité nationale distincts, près de 300 millions de numéros de téléphone associés à des données vraisemblablement collectées auprès d'Alipay, quelque 11 millions de dossiers d'inscription scolaire et près de 8 millions d'enregistrements d'entreprises. Loin d'avoir été stockées en vrac, ces informations, issues de sources distinctes, avaient fait l'objet d'un important travail de recoupement et de structuration.
La seconde base, découverte par Jeremiah Fowler, chercheur chez Black Hills Information Security dont les travaux ont été publiés par ExpressVPN, contenait près de 2 milliards d'identifiants et de données de connexion, répartis dans plus de 8 400 dossiers, dont plusieurs classés par pays, France comprise. Cette fois, les informations semblent en grande partie issues d'infostealers, ces logiciels malveillants capables de siphonner les données stockées sur les appareils infectés. Des centaines de millions de comptes de messagerie, plus de 100 millions de comptes de réseaux sociaux et des dizaines de millions de comptes de commerce en ligne figuraient dans les fichiers, sans que rien ne laisse penser que les plateformes concernées aient elles-mêmes été piratées.
Les deux bases ne sont désormais plus accessibles au public, la première ayant disparu au cours des investigations de Greg Pollock, qui soupçonne une attaque par ransomware ou une opération de destruction de données, et l'accès à la seconde ayant été restreint par son hébergeur après un signalement de Jeremiah Fowler.
Les chercheurs n'ont toutefois pas été en mesure d'en identifier les propriétaires, Jeremiah Fowler n'excluant d'ailleurs pas que la seconde base ait été constituée à des fins de recherche en cybersécurité, ni de vérifier l'intégralité de leur contenu ou d'en éliminer tous les doublons. Impossible, donc, d'établir le nombre exact de victimes, la proportion de données inédites ou encore de savoir si d'autres personnes ont profité de leur exposition.
Quand les pirates en savent assez pour prendre possession de votre vie numérique
Outre le volume d'informations exposées, les chercheurs s'inquiètent de la complémentarité des données collectées. Un numéro de téléphone, une adresse mail ou un numéro d'identité nationale prennent une tout autre valeur aux yeux d'un escroc dès lors qu'il peut les rattacher à un même individu. En accumulant et en croisant les informations issues de vols successifs, les cybercriminels peuvent ainsi affiner leurs campagnes de phishing, usurper votre identité ou se faire passer pour un organisme avec lequel vous entretenez déjà des relations.
Plus préoccupant encore, Jeremiah Fowler a mis la main sur quelque 400 000 documents qui associaient aux identifiants de connexion des informations sur les appareils infectés, des données de navigation, des cookies et des fichiers récupérés sur les machines. Or, lorsqu'ils sont encore valides et réutilisables, les cookies d'authentification peuvent permettre aux pirates de détourner une session déjà ouverte, sans avoir à saisir votre mot de passe ni à franchir l'étape de la double authentification.
On rappellera donc que, si l'utilisation de mots de passe uniques et l'activation de la double authentification vous protègent contre une grande partie des tentatives de piratage de comptes, ces précautions ne vous mettent pas à l'abri d'un détournement de session. En cas d'infection par un infostealer, il vous faudra aussi révoquer vos sessions actives et renouveler vos mots de passe depuis un appareil sain, en prenant soin de désinfecter la machine compromise avant de vous y reconnecter.

articles.title: ChatGPT Health has finally arrived on Android — and it can help you understand what all those numbers on your fitness tracker actually mean
articles.text:
ChatGPT can now make sense of all that health and fitness data on your Android phone — and it could make your smartwatch a lot more useful
Personalized insights with some important AI limitations
Your Android phone can now use ChatGPT to help you make more sense of all your health data. OpenAI has enhanced ChatGPT Health with an expansion to Android and desktop. Crucially for Android users, the expansion includes support for Android Health Connect, Google's system for sharing health and fitness information between compatible apps. It gives ChatGPT access, with your permission, to information about your daily habits that previously would have required some tedious manual input.
The appeal of bringing that information into ChatGPT is fairly obvious to anyone who owns a fitness tracker but rarely looks beyond their daily step count. Most fitness apps are excellent at collecting information, but figuring out what to do with it can be more complicated. Having an AI assistant that can explain those numbers in everyday language could make them considerably more useful.
Android's healthy connections
ChatGPT Health is available to eligible users aged 18 and older in the US on the Free, Go, Plus, and Pro plans. The Android expansion is happening gradually, so you may need to wait a little longer before it appears on your account. Some of the more advanced features, particularly those involving OpenAI's autonomous personal agents called dots, require a Pro subscription.
To get started, update the ChatGPT app on your Android phone and look for Health in the sidebar or under the Explore menu. Once you've opened Health, select the option to connect your information and choose Android Health Connect. You'll then be asked which categories of information you're willing to share before ChatGPT begins syncing your data.
Health Connect acts as an intermediary between ChatGPT and compatible fitness apps. If you use a Garmin smartwatch or an Oura Ring, for instance, you'll need to make sure its companion app is sharing information with Health Connect. Exactly how much ChatGPT can learn about your exercise habits will depend on what your devices record and what their respective apps make available.
Once everything is connected, you can ask questions about your fitness information in an ordinary ChatGPT conversation. You can also add @Health to a prompt to explicitly request that the AI consult your connected information. There's no need to spend every conversation about your daily walks in a dedicated corner of ChatGPT.
The most immediately useful aspect of the update may be the ability to explore relationships between different parts of your daily routine. You could ask ChatGPT to compare your sleeping habits on weekdays with those on weekends, for example. You could then ask it to examine whether the days when you're most physically active coincide with longer nights of sleep.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
That sort of analysis is possible with many existing fitness apps, but it often involves navigating several screens and interpreting graphs yourself. ChatGPT allows you to pursue whatever detail catches your attention without being constrained by the layout of a particular dashboard. It essentially gives your fitness statistics a conversational interface.
There are some mundane but potentially rewarding applications, too. If you've been trying to walk more regularly, you could ask ChatGPT to identify which days of the week you've historically found it easiest to fit in a longer walk. That might be more useful than another notification from your smartwatch informing you that you've spent too much time sitting down.
Oversharing your health
Of course, sharing information about your body with an AI company warrants considerably more thought than connecting a music streaming service. Your fitness data can reveal quite a lot about your life, including when you're usually asleep and how your routine changes over time. Even information that seems relatively innocuous in isolation can become surprisingly intimate when combined with months of other records.
OpenAI says it doesn't sell personal information collected through Health, and users can choose which accounts and categories of data they share. However, its updated privacy notice also explains that conversations involving Health can contribute to ChatGPT's memory if that feature is enabled. The company's current policy gives users control over whether conversations and memories are used for model training, making it worth reviewing your personalization and data settings before connecting anything.
There are practical limitations to consider as well. Consumer fitness devices are imperfect measuring instruments, and ChatGPT can't recover information that your smartwatch failed to collect. An impressive explanation of a sleep pattern is only as reliable as the underlying measurements, and the AI itself can misunderstand those numbers.
I'd be particularly wary of treating an apparent relationship between two measurements as proof that one caused the other. ChatGPT might identify that you tend to sleep less following particularly active days, but there could be plenty of unrelated reasons for that pattern. It's an interesting observation to explore rather than a scientific conclusion about your body.
The same caution applies to the wider medical capabilities of ChatGPT Health. Although the service supports connections to certain medical records, OpenAI describes it as a supplement to professional healthcare and says it isn't intended to diagnose or treat medical conditions. Having more personal information available to an AI doesn't confer a medical degree upon it.
ChatGPT probably won't transform you into an athlete simply because you've granted it access to your step count. Nor should you feel obliged to give an AI company access to every measurement your smartwatch has ever recorded. But this update might make your fitness tracker a little more valuable than just another expensive watch.

articles.title: La IA pone en duda el objetivo de cero emisiones de Meta: la empresa revisa su plan para 2030
articles.text:
Meta está revisando su objetivo de alcanzar cero emisiones netas en toda su cadena de valor para 2030, una meta fijada en 2020. La compañía atribuye la reevaluación al rápido crecimiento de la infraestructura necesaria para desarrollar y operar servicios de inteligencia artificial (IA). En su informe de sostenibilidad de 2026, también señaló que reconsidera los plazos, la secuencia de trabajo y los objetivos intermedios de corto plazo.
El reporte indica que las emisiones netas de gases de efecto invernadero de Meta aumentaron 45 % en 2025, hasta llegar a 11,8 millones de toneladas métricas de dióxido de carbono equivalente. La mayor parte provino de su cadena de suministro, en particular de los bienes y servicios adquiridos y de los bienes de capital, como los equipos y las instalaciones que necesita para expandir sus operaciones.
La empresa no anunció que abandone su compromiso ni precisó qué fecha o metas podrían cambiar. Rachel Peterson, vicepresidenta de centros de datos, y Blair Swedeen, responsable global de cero emisiones netas y sostenibilidad, escribieron que el crecimiento previsto, la reducción de los costos de energía limpia y los cambios en el sistema energético no se han desarrollado como esperaban.
Los centros de datos elevan la demanda de energía
Los centros de datos alojan los servidores que procesan y almacenan información para los servicios digitales. Las aplicaciones de IA requieren una infraestructura de gran escala, y Meta sostiene que la demanda creció más rápido de lo previsto. La compañía advierte que construir esos centros al ritmo y la escala necesarios plantea retos que el sector no había afrontado antes.
El informe también registra un aumento de 35 % en el consumo eléctrico de Meta durante 2025, a medida que entraron en funcionamiento nuevos centros de datos. La empresa afirma que desde 2020 ha igualado todo su consumo anual de electricidad con energía limpia y renovable, principalmente mediante contratos de compra de energía a largo plazo. En 2025 contrató más de 10 gigavatios adicionales y elevó a más de 30 gigavatios su capacidad contratada de energía limpia.
Igualar el consumo con energía limpia mediante contratos no significa que cada centro de datos funcione exclusivamente con electricidad renovable en todo momento. La disponibilidad de energía, las conexiones a la red y los plazos para construir nuevas instalaciones eléctricas también condicionan cómo se abastecen los centros.
Meta contempla otras fuentes para alimentar sus instalaciones
La compañía ha señalado que podría recurrir a gas natural generado “detrás del medidor” si las empresas eléctricas no pueden cumplir los plazos que requiere su negocio. Esto significa producir electricidad cerca del centro de datos y suministrarla directamente a la instalación, en lugar de depender por completo de una conexión a la red. La opción puede acelerar el suministro, pero también plantea desafíos para reducir las emisiones.
En Luisiana, Meta anunció la ampliación de su centro de datos en Richland Parish hasta una capacidad informática de cinco gigavatios y financia siete centrales eléctricas de gas natural para abastecer el proyecto. Otros centros de datos que la empresa construye en Estados Unidos también podrían utilizar gas, al menos en parte.
La presión climática alcanza a otras tecnológicas
Meta no es la única gran compañía tecnológica que enfrenta mayores emisiones durante la expansión de la IA. Según sus propios reportes, las emisiones de Microsoft aumentaron 25 % en 2025, las de Amazon 16 % y las de Google 18 % bajo la metodología basada en sus objetivos. Las cifras no son directamente equivalentes, porque cada empresa puede aplicar distintas metodologías y límites de medición.
La revisión de Meta deja en suspenso el calendario de uno de sus compromisos climáticos más visibles. La compañía mantiene inversiones en energía limpia y otras tecnologías de bajas emisiones, pero todavía no ha detallado cómo compatibilizará esas iniciativas con la construcción acelerada de centros de datos para IA ni cuándo definirá los cambios a sus objetivos de 2030.

articles.title: Poco X8 vs Poco X8 Pro: qual smartphone Xiaomi comprar?
articles.text:
Poco X8 vs Poco X8 Pro: qual smartphone Xiaomi comprar?
Comparamos os testes entre Poco X8 e Poco X8 Pro; descubra o que muda em desempenho, tela, câmeras e bateria
O Poco X8 e o Poco X8 Pro são celulares intermediários da Xiaomi com boa relação custo-benefício. Mas enquanto o modelo Pro foca em desempenho avançado para games, a versão base tem preço mais acessível, se destacando pela bateria gigante e resistência aprimorada contra água e quedas.
O Tecnoblog comparou os testes feitos com cada smartphone para te ajudar a decidir qual é o melhor modelo para você. Conheça as principais diferenças entre o Poco X8 e o Poco X8 Pro neste artigo.
|  | Poco X8 | Poco X8 Pro | 
|---|---|---|
| Lançamento | Setembro de 2026 | Março de 2026 | 
| Preço de lançamento | a partir de R$ 2.098 (em conversão direta) | R$ 6.999 | 
| Tela | 6,83″ AMOLED, resolução de 2772 x 1280 pixels (1.5 K) a 447 ppi | 6,59″ AMOLED, resolução de 2756 x 1268 pixels (1.5K) a 460 ppi | 
| Processador | Qualcomm Snapdragon 6s Gen 4 | MediaTek Dimensity 8500-Ultra | 
| Memória RAM | 6 GB, 8 GB ou 12 GB (LPDDR4X) | 8 GB ou 12 GB (LPDDR5X) | 
| Armazenamento | 128 GB (UFS 2.2) ou 256 GB (UFS 3.1), sem entrada para cartão microSD | 256 GB ou 512 GB (UFS 4.1), sem entrada para cartão microSD | 
| Câmera traseira | Lente grande-angular de 50 MP (f/1.8) e sensor de profundidade de 2 MP (f/2.4) | Lente grande-angular de 50 MP (f/1.5) e ultra-angular de 8 MP (f/2.2) | 
| Câmera frontal | Lente grande-angular de 16 MP (f/2.4) | Lente grande-angular de 20 MP (f/2.2) | 
| Vídeo em até | 1080p @ 30 fps | 4K @ 60 fps | 
| Biometria | Sensor de impressão digital sob a tela | Sensor de impressão digital sob a tela | 
| Bateria | Capacidade de 8.340 mAh | Capacidade de 6.500 mAh | 
| Sistema de fábrica | Xiaomi HyperOS 3, baseado no Android 16 | Xiaomi HyperOS 3, baseado no Android 16 | 
| Conectividade | 5G (SA e NSA), 4G, 3G e 2G, Wi-Fi 5, Bluetooth 5.1, NFC, Dual SIM | 5G (SA e NSA), 4G, 3G e 2G, Wi-fi 6, Bluetooth 6.0, NFC, Dual SIM | 
| Resistência à água | Sim, IP66, IP68, IP69 e IP69K (profundidade máxima de 2 metros por até 72 horas) | Sim, IP68 (profundidade máxima de 1,5 metro por até 30 minutos) | 
| Dimensões | 163,45 mm (A) x 78,27 mm (L) x 8,6 mm (E) | 157,53 mm (A) x 75,19 mm (L) x 8,38 mm (E) | 
| Peso | 223 g | 201 g | 
| Cores | Preto, branco e laranja | Preto, branco e verde menta | 
Contrariando as expectativas, o Poco X8 é maior e mais pesado do que o Poco X8 Pro. Veja as medidas a seguir:
- Poco X8: 163,45 mm x 78,27 mm x 8,6 mm, pesando 223 gramas.
- Poco X8 Pro: 157,53 mm x 75,19 mm x 8,38 mm, pesando 201 gramas.
Também há diferenças no design na traseira: o modelo base do Poco X8 possui um pequeno módulo de câmera que envolve o kit de lentes na carcaça lisa e traz um visual com linhas divididas inspirado em robôs. Esse design está presente nas versões em preto, branco ou laranja.
Já o Poco X8 Pro possui uma traseira lisa nos modelos preto ou verde menta, mas a variante branca inclui um design com linhas divididas similares às do Poco X8. E na versão Pro, as lentes da câmera traseira saltam diretamente da carcaça, sem um módulo dedicado.
O Poco X8 Pro tem construção premium, que inclui fibra de vidro na traseira e bordas de liga de alumínio de grau aeroespacial. Enquanto isso, o Poco X8 adotou uma traseira de plástico reforçado, além de molduras de plástico com fibra de vidro e alumínio fundido.
Apesar disso, no papel, o Poco X8 é mais resistente. Ele chega com proteção total contra água e poeira (IP66, IP68, IP69 e IP69K), suportando submersões de 2 metros por até 72 horas. E ainda oferece proteção contra quedas de até 3 metros. Promete ser ideal para quem pega chuva constantemente ou está mais suscetível a quedas.
O Poco X8 Pro também tem proteção contra água e poeira, mas aguenta submersões de até 1,5 metro de profundidade e por apenas 30 minutos. E a Xiaomi não menciona nenhuma proteção específica contra quedas.
A tela do Poco X8 Pro leva vantagem por trazer suporte a Dolby Vision e HDR10+, conseguindo reproduzir os realces de brilho, cor e contraste em conteúdos compatíveis.
O Poco X8 não traz esse suporte e as imagens reproduzidas tendem a ficar menos fiéis em relação ao conteúdo original. Em compensação, seu display conta com Gorilla Glass Victus 2, mais resistente do que o Gorilla Glass 7i presente na tela do Poco X8 Pro.
No mais, os dois celulares entregam bastante espaço para visualizar conteúdos, brilho satisfatório mesmo em locais bem iluminados, imagens em alta definição e excelente fluidez gráfica. As especificações são:
- Poco X8: 6,83″ AMOLED; resolução 1.5K (2772 x 1280 pixels); 120 Hz; 3.500 nits (pico).
- Poco X8: 6,59″ AMOLED; resolução 1.5K (2756 x 1268 pixels); 120 Hz; 3.500 nits (pico).
O processador Snapdragon do Poco X8 é indicado a tarefas mais básicas, como streaming, navegação na web e redes sociais, além de jogos casuais menos exigentes. Já o chip MediaTek Dimensity 8500-Ultra do Poco X8 Pro garante performance avançada principalmente para jogos e atividades mais exigentes, a exemplo de edições de vídeo e cargas de trabalho de IA.
Os padrões de memória RAM e armazenamento também influenciam nessa conta: o LPDDR5X usado no Poco X8 Pro é mais eficiente e oferece maior largura de banda do que o LPDDR4X do Poco X8, acelerando e otimizando o desempenho em multitarefas.
No quesito armazenamento, o Poco X8 tem versões de 128 GB (UFS 2.2) ou 256 GB (UFS 3.1), enquanto o Poco X8 Pro está disponível em 256 GB ou 512 GB no padrão UFS 4.1, que tem velocidades maiores de leitura e gravação. Isto é, a versão Pro salva arquivos e abre aplicativos armazenados mais rapidamente.
As câmeras não são o foco principal de nenhum dos dois celulares deste comparativo. Mas o Poco X8 Pro se destaca por oferecer um conjunto mais versátil e com melhores resultados do que o Poco X8.
Por mais que as câmeras principais dos dois celulares tenham 50 MP, a do Poco X8 Pro traz um sensor maior e maior abertura de lente, o permite mais entrada de luz e melhora a qualidade das capturas (especialmente à noite).
Fora isso, a lente ultrawide da versão Pro habilita fotos em ângulos mais abertos, e as selfies do Poco X8 Pro capturam mais detalhes.
Já falando sobre vídeos, o Poco X8 Pro consegue gravar em 4K @ 60 fps, com mais margem para recortes e filmagens mais fluidas. E a versão base do Poco X8 é limitada a filmagens em Full HD (1080p) @ 30 fps.
Considerando a capacidade e autonomia bruta, o Poco X8 é o campeão em bateria deste comparativo. Ele tem um componente de silício-carbono com capacidade para 8.340 mAh e aguentou 59 horas longe das tomadas em nossos testes.
Entretanto, o Poco X8 Pro não faz feio: são 6.500 mAh (Si-C) e autonomia para mais de um dia em uso comum. Além disso, a versão Pro tem carregamento mais rápido, de até 100 W, e recarga reversa cabeada de até 27 W. Já o Poco X7 tem carregamento limitado a 67 W e recarga reversa de até 22,5 W.
O Poco X8 Pro se destaca com um sistema de refrigeração avançado de camada dupla, chamado de Poco 3D Ice Loop, que dissipa o calor e pode reduzir a temperatura do SoC em até 3ºC. No Poco X8, a Xiaomi menciona apenas uma proteção térmica que pode desativar recursos para evitar superaquecimentos.
As especificações reforçam como o Poco X8 Pro foi projetado para lidar com processamentos exigentes. Alto desempenho gera mais calor. E temperaturas elevadas demandam um sistema de resfriamento dedicado para que o smartphone mantenha a performance sem superaquecer.
Como a versão base do Poco X8 não apresenta esse sistema avançado de resfriamento, o celular pode interromper algumas tarefas se o aparelho esquentar demais. E isso traz limitações de performance em atividades mais exigentes.
Tanto o Poco X8 quanto o Poco X8 Pro têm 5G, NFC e sensor infravermelho. A diferença é que o X8 usa o protocolo Wi-Fi 5 e Bluetooth no padrão 5.1, enquanto o X8 Pro adota o padrão Wi-Fi 6 e Bluetooth 6.0.
Na prática, o Poco X8 Pro consegue atingir velocidades de transferência de dados mais altas quando conectado ao Wi-Fi, além de oferecer uma conexão mais estável mesmo com vários dispositivos conectados ao roteador.
Já o padrão Bluetooth 6.0 garante ao modelo Pro recursos como medição de distâncias mais precisa e conexão mais eficiente com dispositivos próximos.
Os dois smartphones chegam com o sistema operacional HyperOS 3 (baseado no Android 16), com suporte de atualizações de sistema por quatro anos. A interface é simples e intuitiva, apesar de conter vários apps pré-instalados.
A maioria dos recursos de sistema estão disponíveis para os dois modelos, como temas variados, widgets personalizados e o HyperIsland — funcionalidade similar à Ilha Dinâmica dos iPhones.
No entanto, a versão Pro é compatível com a otimização WildBoost, que aprimora o desempenho geral do dispositivo. E também inclui várias funções de inteligência artificial, a exemplo de transcrições, tradução automática e ajuda de escrita. Nenhum desses recursos está presente no Poco X8.
A versão base até conta com algumas ferramentas de IA, mas restritas à edição de imagens. Com elas, você pode remover objetos, otimizar o efeito bokeh do modo retrato ou expandir a foto, por exemplo.
O Poco X8 é uma boa escolha para quem busca um smartphone resistente e com boa autonomia de bateria, mas não precisa de alto desempenho bruto. Ele é aquele tipo de celular que lida bem com tarefas cotidianas, e que promete durar anos ao seu lado, faça chuva ou faça sol.
Mas fique atento ao preço: muito acima de R$ 2 mil (8 GB + 256 GB), a relação custo-benefício já não é tão interessante.
Já o Poco X8 Pro é um smartphone com altíssimo poder de fogo para para quem não quer pagar o preço de um celular premium. O aparelho entrega maior desempenho para jogos e tarefas gráficas exigentes e tela com suporte a conteúdos HDR.
Na faixa dos R$ 2.700, ele disputa com aparelhos como Galaxy S25 FE (câmeras mais avançadas) e Motorola Edge 70 Pro (12 GB de RAM e câmeras melhores).
O Poco X8 se sobressai em relação ao Poco X8 Pro nos seguintes aspectos:
- Bateria duradoura: a bateria do Poco X8 é relativamente maior do que a do X8 Pro, com autonomia superior a dois dias de uso.
- Resistência aprimorada: o Poco X8 tem proteção contra quedas de até 3 metros e suporta submersões mais profundas e por mais tempo do que o modelo Pro.
- Preço mais baixo: O Poco X8 é encontrado em promoções a partir de R$ 1.800 (6 GB + 128 GB).
O Poco X8 Pro vence a batalha contra o Poco X8 quando o assunto é performance, tela, câmeras e conectividade. As principais vantagens do celular incluem:
- Desempenho superior: o smartphone tem desempenho avançado, com processador, RAM e armazenamento mais rápidos em comparação ao Poco X8.
- Tela com HDR: o display traz suporte a Dolby Vision e HDR10+, oferecendo uma experiência de streaming mais fiel e imersiva.
- Sistema de resfriamento avançado: o Poco 3D Ice Loop reduz superaquecimentos do aparelho diante de processamentos exigentes, o que ajuda a prolongar a durabilidade do smartphone.
- Câmeras melhores: o Poco X8 Pro tem uma ultrawide e conta com câmeras melhores que a do Poco X8. E ainda consegue gravar em 4K @ 60 fps.
- Conectividades mais recentes: os padrões Wi-Fi e Bluetooth mais recentes garantem conexões mais rápidas e estáveis com outros dispositivos.

articles.title: Reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang must still face China congressional and Senate Banking committees — senators and representatives demand answers from Nvidia CEO on national security threats and export controls
articles.text:
Reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang must still face China congressional and Senate Banking committees — senators and representatives demand answers from Nvidia CEO on national security threats and export controls
U.S. senators and representatives want to know how Nvidia is dealing with reports of AI chip smuggling into China.
Even though Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO earlier this week under pressure from President Donald Trump, members of the U.S. House of Representatives and the U.S. Senate say that he must still appear before them and testify as they dive into their respective investigations. The Select Committee on China posted on X that the Nvidia CEO and the company’s general counsel, Tim Teter, are set to face the committee on December 1 and 2, respectively, while Bloomberg reports that Jensen will publicly testify before the powerful U.S. Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs on December 3.
“The NVIDIA board’s brief internal investigation and reinstatement of Jensen Huang do not erase the national security threats and questions that must be addressed,” the Select Committee on China said. “Jensen Huang and Tim Teter have confirmed they will appear for their transcribed interviews on December 1 and December 2 as previously planned. We remain committed to getting answers on the mass smuggling of NVIDIA products, their diversion for Chinese military purposes, and their key role in advancing our foremost adversary’s AI capabilities.”
The chairpersons of the House Committees on China, Foreign Affairs, and Intelligence first called upon the Nvidia CEO on November 7 for a closed-door meeting to discuss the allegations that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, which lawmakers say “raise significant national security concerns.” Just a day later, Jensen admitted to having an affair, although he did not mention the name of the third party. On the same day that the Nvidia board reinstated Mr. Huang, Senate Banking Committee Chairperson Tim Scott said that Jensen will appear before the committee and publicly testify during a hearing about U.S. export controls on advanced AI hardware.
One of the biggest issues that Jensen Huang is facing is the numerous reports of chip diversion involving Nvidia’s products. The U.S. first put export controls on Nvidia H100 chips in 2022 as it feared that China was using it for military purposes. However, there have been rumors that you could easily get these chips in China as long as you know who to ask as early as 2023, even though the Nvidia CEO answered, “There’s no evidence of any chip diversion,” when asked about it one time. Furthermore, Alice Huang, one of the people that he had an affair with, was allegedly instrumental in securing over $7.5 billion worth of illicit Nvidia GPU imports to China. Jensen Huang himself is known to be against export controls and has called them a failure.
The Select Committee on China’s meeting with the Nvidia CEO will be conducted privately. Although there is going to be a transcription of the interview, it’s unclear if and when the data will be released publicly. On the other hand, the Senate Banking Committee hearing is open to the public and will be broadcast live and online, which will also be the first time that Jensen Huang will face a formal congressional hearing.

articles.title: Et si l’informatique quantique révolutionnait le secteur de l’énergie en premier ? Ils y croient
articles.text:
Réseaux électriques, solaire, hydrogène… L'informatique quantique multiplie ses premiers essais dans l'énergie. Et des entreprises y voient déjà le premier grand terrain de jeu de cette technologie.
Car l’informatique quantique possède des propriétés uniques. En s’appuyant sur les règles qui gouvernent l'infiniment petit, là où un ordinateur classique teste les possibilités une par une, une machine quantique peut en explorer un très grand nombre en même temps. Mais il faut encore la dompter, car ses composants sont d'une grande fragilité et les erreurs de calcul sont nombreuses.
Les promesses, elles, sont immenses : découverte de médicaments, cybersécurité, logistique, finance… Pourtant, c'est vers un autre secteur, auquel on pense moins, que de nombreux regards se tournent aujourd'hui : l'énergie.
Un casse-tête permanent
Car faire fonctionner un réseau électrique est un casse-tête permanent. À chaque seconde, la production doit coller à la consommation, alors que le solaire et l'éolien varient au gré de la météo. Il faut aussi choisir quelles centrales allumer ou éteindre, et quand, pour répondre à la demande au moindre coût. Les combinaisons possibles explosent, et c'est précisément le genre de problème où le calcul quantique pourrait faire gagner un temps précieux.
Et ils sont déjà nombreux à s'y atteler. La firme britannique Phasecraft travaille par exemple avec NESO, le gestionnaire du réseau électrique, sur la gestion des échanges d'électricité et l'isolement de portions du réseau en cas d'urgence. Selon l'entreprise, son logiciel accomplirait ces tâches jusqu'à 1 000 fois plus vite qu'un ordinateur classique.
« Les retours commerciaux sont réels : des réseaux plus efficaces, ce sont des coûts d'exploitation plus bas et davantage de valeur tirée des infrastructures existantes », assure Ashley Montanaro, patron de Phasecraft.
Des avancées pour les matériaux
Mais ce n'est pas tout, car la start-up collabore également avec l’entreprise Oxford PV sur de nouvelles cellules solaires. En effet, le calcul quantique offre aussi de nouvelles perspectives dans le domaine des matériaux, les molécules obéissant aux lois de la physique quantique. Sur le papier, ordinateur quantique est donc mieux armé pour les simuler, de quoi imaginer des cellules solaires plus efficaces, de meilleures piles à hydrogène, ou des catalyseurs qui réduiraient l'usage de l'iridium.
D’autres jeunes pousses sont sur le coup, à l’instar de Quantinuum, qui modélise des matériaux pour les piles à hydrogène et le captage du carbone. ORCA Computing, elle, tente de comprendre comment brûlent les biocarburants. Des acteurs bien plus anciens se penchent aussi sur cette technologie. C’est le cas d’Aramco en Arabie saoudite, d’Iberdrola en Espagne et même d’EDF pour optimiser la recharge intelligente.
Si pour l'heure, nous en sommes encore à la phase de recherche et d'expérimentation, ces avancées pourraient marquer un tournant à l'heure où le réseau électrique n'a jamais été autant sous pression.
Source : CNBC
Un problème d’optimisation combinatoire consiste à choisir la meilleure solution parmi un très grand nombre de combinaisons possibles (par exemple quels moyens de production activer, à quel moment, et à quel niveau). Dans un réseau électrique, il faut en permanence équilibrer production et consommation, respecter des contraintes techniques (capacité des lignes, stabilité, maintenance) et minimiser les coûts. Avec des sources variables comme le solaire et l’éolien, l’incertitude augmente et le nombre de scénarios explose. Ces problèmes deviennent vite difficiles à résoudre exactement en temps réel, d’où l’intérêt de méthodes capables de trouver plus vite de bonnes solutions.
La différence vient du fait que des états quantiques (qubits) peuvent représenter et manipuler des superpositions d’états, ce qui permet à certains algorithmes d’explorer plus efficacement l’espace des solutions qu’une approche classique naïve. Cela ne signifie pas que tout devient automatiquement plus rapide : il faut des algorithmes adaptés et des problèmes structurés pour en tirer un gain. Aujourd’hui, la limite majeure est le bruit : les qubits sont fragiles, et les erreurs de calcul s’accumulent vite sans correction d’erreurs à grande échelle. En conséquence, beaucoup d’essais actuels relèvent du “quantique NISQ” (machines bruyantes), où l’on vise surtout des accélérations ponctuelles ou hybrides avec du calcul classique.
La chimie et les matériaux sont gouvernés par la mécanique quantique, et décrire précisément le comportement des électrons dans une molécule ou un solide devient rapidement hors de portée des méthodes exactes sur ordinateurs classiques. Les approches classiques utilisent donc des approximations, suffisantes dans de nombreux cas, mais parfois limitées pour concevoir des matériaux très performants. Un ordinateur quantique peut, en principe, simuler plus naturellement certains systèmes quantiques, ce qui aiderait à prédire des propriétés clés (rendement, stabilité, réactions catalytiques) avant de passer au laboratoire. L’enjeu industriel est de réduire le temps et le coût de R&D, par exemple pour des catalyseurs moins dépendants de métaux rares comme l’iridium ou pour des composants de piles à hydrogène mieux optimisés.

articles.title: Zowie Launches 6 Updated Gaming Mice with 8 kHz Polling and Flagship Internals
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
Zowie Launches 6 Updated Gaming Mice with 8 kHz Polling and Flagship Internals
Zowie has just announced a refresh to a slew of its classic gaming mice, bringing modern mouse tech and a new "dry coating" to some of the brand's fan-favorite designs. The updated Zowie mice feature 8 kHz polling over wired and wireless connections, paired with the included Enhanced Wireless Receiver. The internals have also been updated to feature up to 42,000 DPI sensitivity and dedicated Performance Mode—a latency enhancing firmware mode that was previously shown to reduce click latency to under 0.5 ms—and Motion Sync options. The included enhanced receiver also doubles as a charging dock, status indicator, and base station that can be used to change certain mouse settings, like DPI, polling rate, lift-off distance, and click response time, which is handy if you want to avoid opening the mouse's dedicated configuration utility. 
Zowie has also updated the coating on all of the new mice, with the so-called "Dry-Touch" coating, which provides a claimed smooth, non-sticky matte surface and is optimized to remain consistent and prevent stickiness during long gaming sessions. Of the new mice, there are three asymmetrical shapes, which are largely iterations of the same shape with small, large, and medium size variants and small tweaks to the shape to accommodate the different sizes. Zowie also says that it has optimized the main click buttons for quick rebound, in a system it calls Rhythm Click, and it has added sharper angles on the sidewalls across the board to make lifting the mice and repositioning it easier and quicker.The new Zowie EW-series upgrade lands for six mice in total:
- EC1-EW: asymmetrical shape measuring 129.4 × 69.3 × 42.3 mm and weighing 55 g
- EC2-EW: asymmetrical shape measuring 123 × 65 × 42.1 mm and weighing 52 g
- EC3-EW: asymmetrical shape measuring 118.4 × 65.6 × 41.1 mm and weighing 52 g
- FK2-EW: low-profile symmetrical shape with a mid hump measuring 125.1 × 64.9 × 36.4 mm and weighing 50 g
- ZA13-EW: symmetrical shape with a tall rearward hump measuring 121.7 × 62.8 × 40.2 mm and weighing 50 g
- U2-EW: symmetrical shape optimized for claw grip with a tall front, measuring 123.3 × 64.3 × 38.1 mm and weighing 52 g
The shapes are arranged in order based on the above list:The U2-EW and FK2-EW will be available in the EU in late November, and the rest are expected to land in the EU, US, and the rest of the world sometime between late December and March.

articles.title: Key insights from HPE’s Q4 earnings report
articles.text:
Key insights from HPE’s Q4 earnings report
Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co.delivered a record fiscal fourth quarter this week, roughly doubling its fiscal 2027 growth outlook, but its stock gave back nearly all of the prior day’s rally. The selloff suggests Wall Street still prices HPE as a low-margin server vendor, even though the results describe a networking and artificial intelligence infrastructure company with demand exceeding its ability to ship.
Fourth-quarter revenue rose 50%, to $14.5 billion, orders grew 88%, and adjusted earnings of $1.43 per share topped the high end of guidance. HPE now expects fiscal 2027 revenue to grow 27% to 35%, with adjusted earnings of $5.05 to $5.35 per share, according to its earnings release.
I joined a briefing with Chief Executive Antonio Neri and a small group of independent analysts shortly before the results came out. Here are my four takeaways for investors and information technology leaders:
Demand continues to outrun supply
Neri explained that networking orders grew more than 4.5 times faster than networking revenue in the quarter, up from 3.5 times the quarter before, and HPE exited the year with $10.5 billion in AI backlog.
HPE doubled its networking purchase commitments over the summer and raised them again in the fourth quarter, but those components carry lead times of 28 to 40-plus weeks, so Neri expects networking conversion to pick up starting in the second quarter. Supply constraints are a better problem to have than weak demand, but they mean fiscal 2027 hinges on converting orders rather than winning them.
Networking is becoming the profit engine
The Juniper Networks integration is complete, and the annual cost-synergy target has risen to $800 million, but the bigger story remains the profit mix. Chief Financial Officer Marie Myers said networking will account for more than 40% of HPE’s operating profit by the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, up from less than a quarter of revenue. AI is a major driver, with routing orders growing by triple digits as customers connect AI data centers to one another.
Security was the soft spot, which Neri called “just timing.” When I asked whether the security portfolio is where he wants it as the industry consolidates around big platforms, he argued for a different path.
“Fortinet and we have a different strategy — the convergence of security and networking — and we are taking it all the way down to the silicon level,” he said. The convergence of networking and security is underway but will take time to execute, as a considerable amount of technical debt must go through its depreciation cycle. In a greenfield situation, organizations can easily deploy a converged solution, but in a brownfield environment, it requires much more work. This is the right strategy, but it remains a “prove-it” business for HPE.
HPE won’t bankroll the neoclouds
Many neoclouds rely on vendor financing and chip-backed debt, raising real concerns about who is left exposed if the buildout slows. HPE says it has stayed out, and Neri was quite emphatic about it on the briefing.
“I want to be clear: We have not financed any neocloud through HPFS, our financing arm,” he said. “We have zero exposure to any AI financing for neocloud.” HPE has likely left some revenue on the table, but it drew the line in the right place. It will sell to neoclouds, as its $1.2 billion Vultr order shows, without acting as their bank. Enterprise and sovereign customers account for the majority of its cumulative AI orders, and if the neocloud financing chain breaks, HPE’s financing arm won’t be the one holding the paper.
Inference pulls AI back on-premises
Training built the first phase of AI infrastructure, and Neri believes inference will build the next and will dominate demand for AI infrastructure. “I believe by the end of the decade, 80% will be in AI inferencing,” he said. “Much of that will land on-prem. Much of that will be distributed, for sure. That’s why the server business is structurally well-positioned.”
Once agents are in production, token costs become a recurring bill, and companies will want inference running alongside their own data. Those servers require far more memory and pull in storage and services, which is better business than racking graphics processing units for a hyperscaler.
Evidence of this is the interest in Helios, the Advanced Microdevices Inc. rack that uses HPE’s Ethernet switching rather than Nvidia’s proprietary interconnect. I asked Neri whether Jensen Huang’s brief departure from Nvidia Corp. had opened that door. He said interest was building before then, as customers look to diversify.
Why the stock is down
HPE shares jumped 17% on Monday ahead of the report as part of a broader AI rally, then fell about 13% in early trading on Tuesday, ending near where they started the week. I see three reasons for this.
The first is margins. Cloud & AI operating margin was 18.4% in the quarter, and HPE guided to about 14% for fiscal 2027. Reuters reported that JPMorgan analysts called margin mix the key debate for investors.
The second is pricing. Myers said higher selling prices have been the biggest driver of server growth, and she expects gross margin to moderate in the second half as AI server volumes ramp and costs rise faster than pricing.
The third is timing. HPE expects about 54% of revenue in the second half, with the ramp tied to Helios shipments, the Oracle Corp. deal, customer data center readiness and component supply. Those are fair execution questions, but they miss the shift in where HPE’s profit comes from.
Why investors should look past these numbers
On the topic of margins, the 18.4% came off an unusual stretch of favorable pricing that should not have been modeled as permanent. Neri argued the guide is still “significantly higher than any historical margin we have had in this business,” and he’s right outside the past year. A year ago, the segment’s margin was 9.3%. Margin rate also isn’t margin dollars. At 30% to 40% revenue growth, my math shows Cloud & AI adding well over $1 billion in operating profit at the midpoint.
The bears are right that price-driven server growth doesn’t warrant a premium multiple, which is why the mix matters more. The market is fixated on the segment whose margins are normalizing and ignoring the one whose margins are expanding. Adjusted earnings per share are still guided to grow by 27% to 35%, in line with revenue growth. That’s far from the margin doom-and-gloom narrative on the stock.
The back-half concern is real but manageable. Myers described the pipeline as multiples of the backlog, and Neri said the guide assumes only historical win rates against it.
Then there’s quality. HPE is guiding to about 30% growth and at least $5.5 billion in free cash flow, has no neocloud financing exposure and has already brought leverage below its target. It trades at about eight times the midpoint of its adjusted earnings guidance. “I don’t see us at a multiple that is 8 to 9x; it makes no sense whatsoever,” Neri said on the earnings call.
For old HPE, that’s true, as it’s a server vendor, but HPE is increasingly a network vendor each quarter. In fact, during our pre-call with Neri, he led with networking and spoke at length about the business before pivoting to the server business. Expect networking to continue to drive a larger share of profits.
What this means for IT leaders
- Lock in supply now. HPE expects memory and other critical parts to remain constrained through at least the second half of 2028, so get 2027 delivery commitments in writing.
- Use Helios as leverage. An Ethernet-based rack is a credible alternative in any AI infrastructure negotiation, even if you never buy one.
- Plan for on-premises inference. Track your token spend today, decide which workloads should run alongside your data, and budget for the storage and networking that come with them, not just the servers.
Final thoughts
Fiscal 2027 is an execution year. HPE must convert purchase commitments into shipments, ramp Helios and prove that networking margins can climb even as cloud and AI margins settle. I’ll be watching networking order conversion more closely than server margins. If HPE executes, today’s multiple will prove to be too low.
Zeus Kerravala is a principal analyst at ZK Research, a division of Kerravala Consulting. He wrote this article for SiliconANGLE.

articles.title: Chrome “bebe” até 700 MB de RAM mesmo quando Gemini está fechado
articles.text:
Chrome “bebe” até 700 MB de RAM mesmo quando Gemini está fechado
Usuário relatou consumo de RAM no Windows; configuração controla o acesso ao assistente pela bandeja do sistema e por atalho.
A integração do Gemini pode manter processos do Chrome funcionando mesmo depois de fechar todas as janelas do navegador. Um usuário do Windows relatou consumo entre 300 e 700 MB de RAM nessa situação e afirmou ter resolvido o problema ao desativar o acesso rápido ao assistente.
No relato publicado no Reddit, o autor afirma que encontrava processos chrome.exe no Gerenciador de Tarefas. Desativar extensões e remover aplicativos também não resolveu o comportamento. Em outro teste, um perfil novo e sem login na conta Google permitiu encerrar o navegador normalmente, segundo a postagem.
A documentação oficial do Google já explica que, após a ativação, o Gemini pode ser acessado pela bandeja do Windows, a área de ícones próxima ao relógio, e por atalhos de teclado. Assim, fechar as janelas não significa necessariamente finalizar todos os componentes do navegador.
Vale lembrar que o Gemini integrado ao Chrome permite resumir páginas, comparar informações entre abas e interagir com outros serviços do Google. O acesso pela bandeja do sistema oferece outra forma de chamar o assistente, além do botão exibido durante a navegação.
No caso relatado, foi necessário desligar o controle específico da bandeja e do atalho manualmente para que os processos fossem encerrados.
Confira os passos indicados pelo Google:
- Abra as Configurações do Chrome pelo menu de três pontos;
- Entre em Inovações de IA e selecione Gemini no Chrome. Também é possível acessar a tela acima pelo comando chrome://settings/ai/gemini na barra de endereços;
- Em Preferências, desative a opção que mostra o Gemini na bandeja do sistema e habilita o atalho de teclado no Windows;
- Feche as janelas e confira no Gerenciador de Tarefas se os processos foram encerrados.
Se o menu não aparecer, procure o Gemini primeiro no menu de três pontos e conclua a ativação inicial, caso seja solicitada. A mudança desliga esse acesso rápido, mas outros recursos ou aplicativos também podem manter processos ativos. Para o consumo durante a navegação, a Economia de Memória é outra função que libera recursos de abas inativas, enquanto os alertas de desempenho ajudam a identificar páginas exigentes.

articles.title: À l'occasion du Black Friday 2026, le XGIMI MoGo 4 Laser tombe à 499 € (-23 %)
articles.text:
Black Friday 2026 : Le vidéoprojecteur XGIMI MoGo 4 Laser à 499,00 € (-23%)
Avec sa batterie intégrée, son interface Google TV et sa note actuelle de 3,5/5 par notre rédaction, le vidéoprojecteur XGIMI MoGo 4 Laser permet d'improviser une séance de cinéma facilement n'importe où. Pour le Black Friday 2026, son prix tombe à 499,00 € chez Boulanger.com et Son-Video.com, soit une baisse d'environ 23 % et 150,00 € d'économie.
Le XGIMI MoGo 4 Laser est un vidéoprojecteur compact pensé pour projeter des films facilement en déplacement comme à la maison. Ce modèle fait évoluer la formule de la marque en intégrant une batterie et une source lumineuse laser, tout en corrigeant des défauts de la génération précédente. L'appareil avait convaincu notre laboratoire par sa simplicité de fonctionnement.
À l'occasion du Black Friday, le XGIMI MoGo 4 Laser descend à 499,00 € chez Boulanger.com et Son-Video.com, soit environ 23 % de moins que le prix moyen constaté ces 30 derniers jours (649,00 €). Cette baisse de prix permet d'économiser 150,00 €.
Une utilisation nomade facilitée par Google TV et sa batterie intégrée
Ce projecteur Full HD (1920 x 1080 pixels) mise avant tout sur le confort d'installation au quotidien. Il s'équipe d'une batterie intégrée et d'un pied réglable, ce qui permet de poser le boîtier sur une table sans chercher une prise de courant immédiate. La mise au point et la correction du trapèze s'exécutent de manière automatique pour aligner le cadre sans manipulations manuelles fastidieuses. Comme détaillé dans notre test complet, l'interface repose sur le système Google TV, qui intègre nativement des applications de streaming comme Netflix pour lancer vos vidéos sans brancher de lecteur externe.
XGIMI MoGo 4 Laser
Points forts
- Meilleurs couleurs et contraste que le MoGo 4 Led.
- Interface Google TV complète avec Netflix en natif.
- Pied intégré très pratique.
- Mise au point et correction du trapèze automatiques.
- Un vrai port HDMI.
- Batterie intégrée.
- Silencieux.
- Alimentation USB-C.
Points faibles
- Colorimétrie très imparfaite.
- Luminosité limitée.
- Input lag perfectible.
NB : La baisse de prix rapportée est calculée en comparant le prix le plus bas du jour avec la moyenne des prix les plus bas pratiqués par tous les marchands pour le produit le mois dernier, avec des règles de sécurité pour écarter les prix des boutiques dont la politique en matière de TVA n’est pas claire (dites boutiques “grises”, typiquement en cas d’import de Chine).
Une luminosité modeste qui impose l'obscurité
La source laser apporte un contraste plus marqué et des couleurs plus étendues que sur la déclinaison Led, tout en conservant un fonctionnement silencieux. Il faut néanmoins composer avec une luminosité limitée et une colorimétrie très imparfaite, ce qui destine principalement l'appareil à des séances de visionnage dans une pièce plongée dans le noir. Les joueurs réguliers devront aussi composer avec un retard à l'affichage perfectible.
Epson Lifestudio Pop EF-61 : l'autre option face au XGIMI MoGo 4 Laser
L'Epson Lifestudio Pop EF-61 repose également sur Google TV et propose une note actuelle de 3,5/5. Sa technologie 3LCD élimine tout effet arc-en-ciel et son faible retard à l'affichage autorise les sessions de jeu vidéo, deux éléments qui manquent au modèle de XGIMI. En contrepartie, l'appareil d'Epson fait l'impasse sur la mise au point automatique et ne dispose pas d'un vrai pied réglable.
L'Epson Lifestudio Pop EF-61 coûte 50,01 € de moins que le XGIMI MoGo 4 Laser au tarif remisé, mais le MoGo 4 Laser conserve l'avantage de sa batterie intégrée pour projeter sans fil.
Epson Lifestudio Pop EF-61
Points forts
- Format compact et léger.
- Technologie 3LCD sans effet arc-en-ciel.
- Interface Google TV complète.
- MEMC efficace et réglable.
- CMS complet pour la calibration.
- Bon input lag pour le jeu vidéo.
- Silencieux.
Points faibles
- Pas de mise au point automatique.
- Réglage d'inclinaison très limité.
- HDR assez mauvais.
- Télécommande non rétroéclairée.
