articles.title: Coalizão pressiona UE contra restrições da Apple a navegadores
articles.text:
Coalizão pressiona UE contra restrições da Apple a navegadores
Grupo com Mozilla, Vivaldi, Brave e outras empresas entende que Apple não cumpre lei de concorrência digital da Europa ao restringir navegadores no iOS.
Uma coalizão que reúne organizações como Mozilla, Vivaldi, Brave, Y Combinator, Shopify e várias outras empresas publicou uma carta aberta direcionada a Ursula von der Leyen, presidente da Comissão Europeia. O grupo pede uma fiscalização rigorosa contra a Apple por causa das restrições que dificultam o uso de navegadores de terceiros no iOS.
Não é que não seja possível usar browsers que concorrem com o Safari no iPhone. Chrome, Firefox, Edge e tantos outros estão disponíveis há anos no iOS. O problema é que esses navegadores são obrigados a usar o WebKit como motor de renderização.
Esse motor é o que permite que o navegador leia o código de uma página web e apresente o resultado na forma de um conteúdo visual e interativo para ser acessado pelo usuário. Nos demais sistemas operacionais, navegadores como Chrome, Edge e Opera contam com o Blink como motor, pois são baseados no projeto Chromium. O Firefox tem um motor próprio, o Gecko.
Em 2024, a União Europeia colocou em vigor a Digital Markets Act (DMA), ou Lei dos Mercados Digitais, uma legislação que visa favorecer uma concorrência justa de âmbito digital nos países do bloco.
Graças às várias regras da DMA, a Apple se viu condicionada a permitir que navegadores de terceiros usem seus próprios motores no iOS. Isso na teoria. Na prática, empresas concorrentes acusam a Apple de impor condições que inviabilizam o uso de motores diferentes do WebKit por esses browsers.
Um trecho da carta da Open Web Advocacy, a entidade que está por trás da coalizão, diz:
Mais de dois anos e meio após a entrada em vigor da DMA, em 7 de março de 2024, nenhum fornecedor de navegador conseguiu migrar seus usuários na União Europeia do WebKit da Apple para seu próprio motor. Isso permite que a Apple limite os recursos da web no iOS, prendendo desenvolvedores e consumidores ao seu próprio ecossistema da App Store.
Coincidência ou não, a carta aberta foi publicada quase que ao mesmo tempo em que a Mozilla explicou o porquê de não ter um Firefox “puro” no iOS. Sim, a causa está justamente nas restrições impostas pela Apple.
O grupo pede, principalmente, que a Comissão Europeia inicie o quanto antes um processo de fiscalização contra a Apple para obrigar a companhia a seguir, de fato, o que determina a DMA. Note que a carta aberta não pede a criação ou a alteração da legislação vigente, mas o seu efetivo cumprimento.
Na prática, a coalizão quer que as autoridades europeias atuem para derrubar as barreiras técnicas e jurídicas impostas pela Apple, de modo a beneficiar não somente fornecedores de navegadores, mas também empresas que dependem da web em modelos de negócio variados.
A Comissão Europeia não se manifestou sobre o assunto até o momento. A Apple tampouco. Contudo, em ocasiões anteriores, a companhia argumentou que as suas exigências relacionadas a motores de navegador visam preservar parâmetros de segurança e privacidade para os usuários de iPhone.

articles.title: I tested Sonos, WiiM and Klipsch’s budget-friendly Dolby Atmos soundbars against each other — here’s which one I’d buy on Black Friday
articles.text:
I compared 3 budget-friendly Dolby Atmos soundbars from Sonos, WiiM, and Klipsch — here’s the one I’d recommend for most people
Which soundbar should you buy on Black Friday?
Black Friday is coming up, and there’s no better time of year to upgrade your tech. And one thing I’d highly recommend checking out would be soundbar deals. A good soundbar can totally change the way you enjoy movies and TV, with clearer dialogue, genuinely powerful bass, and far more expansive audio than your set’s built-in speakers could ever dream of providing.
So, if you get a soundbar this Black Friday, which model should you buy? I think it’s always best to go for a soundbar with Dolby Atmos support — this tech is used across multiple streaming platforms, most 4K Blu-rays, and some video games too. Ideally, we don’t want to break the bank, either, so I’ve taken a look at some of the best soundbars I’ve tested with Dolby Atmos support that are still affordable.
The three I settled on were the WiiM Bar, Klipsch Flexus Core 200, and Sonos Beam Gen 2. Each of these is a single bar option, meaning you don’t need to lug a subwoofer into your living room or anything, and all of them have a very similar list price. I compared all of them across areas including features, performance, and design, ranking the soundbars in each category to find an overall winner.
Which model came out on top? You’ll have to read until the end to find out. But first, let’s take a look at the key specs for each of our contestants.
Meet the contestants
| Header Cell - Column 0 | WiiM Bar | Klipsch Flexus Core 200 | Sonos Beam Gen 2 | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Price | $479 / £449 / AU$769 | $575.99 / £449 | $449 / £449 / AU$699 | 
| Dimensions | 41.7 x 4.1 x 3.1 inches / 1060 x 105 x 80mm | 54 x 3 x 5 inches / 1,371.6 x 76.2 x 127mm | 25.6 x 2.7 x 3.9 inches / 651 x 68 x 100mm | 
| Speaker channels | 3.0.2 | 3.1.2 | 5.0 | 
| Connections | HDMI eARC, digital optical, RCA, USB, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 5.3, Ethernet | HDMI eARC, digital optical, USB-C, sub out, Bluetooth 5.2 | HDMI eARC, Ethernet, Wi-Fi | 
| Dolby Atmos / DTS:X | Yes / Yes | Yes / No | Yes / No | 
Features
Let’s take a look at the spatial audio support, connectivity options, and customizability of these soundbars one by one, and determine which offers the most flexibility for users at home.
WiiM Bar
The good: The WiiM Bar has excellent spatial audio capabilities, with support for both Dolby Atmos and DTS:X. It’s a 3.0.2 model with dedicated up-firing drivers, so you’ll get plenty of height to the soundfield when watching movies or listening to music in more expansive formats.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
In terms of connectivity, it’s got you well and truly covered as well, with the usual HDMI eARC, optical, and Bluetooth, but also Wi-Fi for higher-res wireless listening, RCA for connecting a turntable, and an ethernet port too.
If you download the WiiM app you can also access a lot of brilliant features, including sound modes (like Voice or Night), parametric EQ, RoomFit calibration, or channel level adjustments. The app itself is also easy to use and well laid out.
The bad: As you can see, the WiiM Bar has just about everything you could want from a soundbar in this price-range… but ‘just about’ is the key phrase there.
One thing it omits is AirPlay 2 support, which may trouble iOS users — though Bluetooth could be a viable alternative in some cases, and Android users should be covered with Google Cast. Another thing I would’ve liked to have seen is HDMI passthrough. While it’s not commonplace for soundbars in this price-range, you already have to sacrifice and HDMI port for the soundbar itself, so getting an extra port is always nice.
Klipsch Flexus Core 200
The good: The Flexus Core 200 supports Dolby Atmos and has dual 2.25-inch up-firing drivers for convincing height effects. It takes up a 3.1.2 configuration, and can be built out with additional surround speakers if you’d like amazing surround sound.
When it comes to connectivity, the Flexus Core 200 has most of what you need. There’s HDMI eARC, digital optical, Bluetooth, and USB-C as well. What’s more, there’s a sub out port for adding a wired bass unit and a Flexus Transport port for adding a wireless transmitter for compatible subwoofers and surround speakers.
Klipsch’s companion app also has preset and custom EQ options, Night Mode, a dialogue boost option, as well as volume controls.
The bad: The Klipsch Flexus Core 200’s biggest sin is its lack of Wi-Fi streaming support. That means that Spotify and Tidal Connect are off the table and you’ll have to stream music from an app on your TV or over Bluetooth (do note that the latter offers worse overall sound quality).
And unlike the WiiM Bar, it doesn’t support DTS:X, which may be a gripe if you prefer to use that format with some of your favorite 4K Blu-ray discs, say. It also doesn’t have a room calibration tool. You also won’t find HDMI passthrough here.
Sonos Beam Gen 2
The good: Like the aforementioned options, the Sonos Beam Gen 2 has Dolby Atmos support, though it’s worth noting that this is virtual rather than ‘true’ Atmos. It uses a 5.0 driver configuration, enabling it to create solid width for a compact bar.
Something that makes the Beam Gen 2 stand out is its interplay with the Sonos ecosystem, there’s TV Audio Swap, which enables you to transfer media to your Sonos Ace or Sonos Ace Ultra headphones, multi-room connectivity, and the option to pair compatible speakers as a sub or surrounds.
The Sonos app also lets you switch up EQ, make channel level adjustments, or access a voice assistant. TruePlay is also on-board for room calibration.
The bad: While you get HDMI eARC and Wi-Fi connectivity, the Beam Gen 2 doesn’t have much else — there’s no Bluetooth, USB-C, RCA or anything fancy. It also lacks DTS:X, meaning it’s not quite got the versatility of the WiiM Bar. Like the other two models, this bar doesn’t feature an HDMI input slot.
| Features ranking |  | 
|---|---|
| Soundbar | Rank | 
|---|---|
| WiiM Bar | 1st | 
| Sonos Beam Gen 2 | 2nd | 
| Klipsch Flexus Core 200 | 3rd | 
Performance
I mainly focused on movies for my soundbar performance test, using 4K Blu-rays with the UHD Blu-ray player in our TV testing room at Future Labs. I used Top Gun Maverick to assess height effects and dialogue fidelity, The Mask to judge width and dynamism, and The Boy and the Heron to test bass and treble response among other things.
WiiM Bar
The good: I think the best thing about the WiiM Bar, performance-wise, is its expansiveness. In The Mask, there’s a scene where the titular character swirls around the screen, and this was replicated brilliantly — it was as if I could hear him spinning into the corners of our testing room. In Top Gun Maverick, scenes where Tom Cruise flew the jet upwards were also tracked nicely with relatively convincing verticality.
The WiiM Bar can also offer considerably better bass than your basic TV audio, something I noticed in a low-end heavy segment of The Boy and the Heron. Dialogue is generally clear too, and music in movie soundtracks is brilliantly balanced.
The bad: Personally, I think that the WiiM Bar could sound a little more dynamic. When The Mask flung through the glass door, the almighty smash didn’t offer the sudden impact that I experienced from the Klipsch soundbar. More generally, I also felt that the bass on offer from the WiiM Bar was a bit softer than I would’ve liked.
While I found dialogue to be clear on this soundbar, it didn’t quite sound as natural or true-to-life as it did from rivals — there was a slightly artificial quality to voices. The Klipsch also arguably delivers marginally superior width to the WiiM Bar, though I was still very much impressed with its expansive sound overall.
Klipsch Flexus Core 200
The good: I was mightily impressed by the Klipsch Flexus Core 200. Dialogue in Top Gun Maverick sounded spectacular, with the echoey quality of the large open room replicated very well. Said dialogue was also expertly separated from the movie’s dramatic score — something that I realized across all of the movies I tested.
For a single-box solution, the Flexus Core 200 also delivers seriously weighty bass. In Maverick, the roar of jet engines was deep and regimented, offering the most impact out of all three models. Atmos is great here too — the verticality of Cruise’s takeoff was captured to good effect, while the width of The Mask’s titular character felt exceptionally broad and spacious.
The bad: There really isn’t much bad to report here whatsoever. In The Boy and the Heron, the ultra-low frequencies during one scene were perhaps not the most driven or full-sounding I’ve experienced, but they still came through decently. And height effects, while good, aren’t the most life-like when compared to some more premium rivals. Overall, though, the Flexus Core 200 put in a very strong performance.
Sonos Beam Gen 2
The good: For such a small soundbar, the Sonos Beam Gen 2 conjures up astonishingly authoritative and nuanced sound. In Top Gun Maverick, everything from the roar of engines to the accurate tracking of vehicular movements to the crystal clear dialogue instantly stuck out to me. I was even relatively impressed with the height effects on offer, despite the Beam Gen 2’s Atmos being virtualized.
Dialogue between mobsters in The Mask might just’ve been the clearest in this competition, and the dynamism on offer when the glass door smashed was more refined than on the WiiM Bar. The Mask’s spinning movements also had tremendous width, and sounds like gunshots being fired were placed nicely while coming through with plenty of bite and venom.
The bad: While the Sonos Beam Gen 2 performed better than you may expect it to, there are a few limitations here. The most obvious is the lack of up-firing drivers, so sounds like jets flying overhead didn’t seem the most natural or believable (though still impressed me overall).
You also won’t quite get the same bass rumble here that the Flexus Core 200 can provide, which is totally understandable given this soundbar’s dimensions. And in some cases, I found that the WiiM Bar offered slightly better musicality than the Beam Gen 2, though overall, I surprisingly preferred the Sonos model.
| Performance ranking |  | 
|---|---|
| Soundbar | Rank | 
|---|---|
| Klipsch Flexus Core 200 | 1st | 
| Sonos Beam Gen 2 | 2nd | 
| WiiM Bar | 3rd | 
Design
And finally, who will take the crown as the best-looking, and most brilliantly designed soundbar? Let's find out...
WiiM Bar
The good: The WiiM Bar has a central display, which you can customize with an image saved in your phone’s gallery which I found pretty cool. The display can also display the time, album covers when listening to music, volume details, and more.
I also really like the remote that comes with the WiiM Bar. It feels really well made, has individual buttons for each sound mode, and even a built-in mic for voice controls. You can use the app for most of this instead, but given that some soundbars omit a remote control altogether, this is certainly nice to have.
The bad: As fun as the screen is, I think it gives the WiiM Bar a bit of a strange shape, with an awkwardly raised center. The plain black design is OK looking, but it lacks the texture or style of the Klipsch and Sonos bars, and fails to exude the sense of luxury its rivals offer.
Klipsch Flexus Core 200
The good: I quite like the aesthetic of the Klipsch Flexus Core 200. The top of the bar has wooden segments that just ooze class, only accentuated by metallic details. Sure, it’s a plain black model, but the variety in materials gives it a bit of an edge over the formulaic look that a lot of rivals possess.
The bad: The remote that comes in the box doesn’t feel as premium as the WiiM Bar’s, with a plasticky look — though this is a fairly minor complaint. And while I like the materials used on the Flexus Core 200, the large Klipsch logo and fabric grille aren’t the prettiest.
Sonos Beam Gen 2
The good: I love the look of the Sonos Beam Gen 2. It comes in either Black or White to suit the rest of your system or vibe of your space and has a sleek, modern, and minimalist aesthetic which is versatile and understated. Even though the Beam Gen 2 is made from plastic, it’s finished really nicely, and the neat display on the top keeps things looking cohesive and organized.
The bad: The Beam Gen 2 doesn’t come with a remote in the box. For most people, that won’t be an issue — you can adjust volume with your typical TV remote thanks to HDMI-CEC and make other adjustments in the Sonos app. But if you prefer a physical controller, then you may be a little disappointed.
| Design ranking |  | 
|---|---|
| Soundbar | Rank | 
|---|---|
| Sonos Beam Gen 2 | 1st | 
| Klipsch Flexus Core 200 | 2nd | 
| WiiM Bar | 3rd | 
Final ranking
So, the results are in. And our winner is none other than the Sonos Beam Gen 2 — surprised?
Yes, the odds seemed to be stacked against the Beam Gen 2 here: it doesn’t have dedicated up-firing drivers, it’s more compact, and has the same list price as its rivals in markets like the UK. But even still, I think it’s the best all-rounder. It sounds spectacular, with perhaps the cleanest dialogue of all three models, plenty of low-end weight, and great virtual Atmos.
It also looks spectacular, and while it skips on some connectivity options, HDMI eARC and Wi-Fi are realistically going to be all you need in most cases. What’s more, it can often be found at a lower price than both of its rivals during sale periods.
The Klipsch Flexus Core 200 just misses out on top spot, ranking 2nd overall. Look, I’m very comfortable recommending this one too. While the lack of Wi-Fi streaming is a shame, this model performed really well, with excellent width and bass weight on offer. It’s not quite as stylish as the Sonos, but if you’re solely focused on performance for movies, you may want to grab this bar.
In third, we have the WiiM Bar. It’s a good soundbar for sure, with impressive Atmos effects, amazing connectivity options, and neat customization options in the WiiM app. But sound-wise, I think it falls just short of the competition, and as unique as the display is, I still think the overall design is a little awkward. If there’s a good sale on this one for Black Friday, I’d still say it’s an option worth considering, and it will definitely offer a considerable upgrade over plain TV audio, but ultimately, I’d go for Sonos or Klipsch over this.

articles.title: How brewers can protect beers from smoke-tainted hops
articles.text:
The 2020 Oregon wildfires burned over 1 million acres, destroyed thousands of structures, and killed 11 people. Smoke from the fires spread across the entire region; this “smoke taint” adversely affected not only local wine production, but also hops grown for beer brewing. Since the Pacific Northwest produces more than 95 percent of US hops and about 40 percent of the global supply, the potential economic impact is significant.
That’s why Oregon State University (OSU) scientists have been studying how brewers could offset the negative impacts of smoke taint while still incorporating affected hops in their brews. Most recently, they found that it all depends on the quantity of tainted hops that are included and when hops are added during the brewing process, according to a new paper published in the Journal of the American Society of Brewing Chemists.
As previously reported, the chemistry of brewing beer is a very active area of research. For instance, in 2018, OSU chemist Thomas Shellhammer—who also co-authored this latest paper—identified the growing popularity of “dry hopping” (adding hops after fermentation, common for pale ales) among craft brewers as the likely culprit of the exploding beer bottle phenomenon.
All beer contains hops, a key flavoring agent that also imparts useful antimicrobial properties. (Beer spoils quickly without them.) Brewers mash and steep grain in hot water, which converts all that starch into sugars. This is traditionally the stage where hops are added to the liquid extract (wort) and boiled to give the beer that hint of bitterness. During the boiling process, a portion of the resins (alpha acids) in hops isomerize into iso-alpha acids. That chemical rearrangement of the molecules is what produces bitterness. Yeast is then added to trigger fermentation, turning the sugars into alcohol.

articles.title: 4,1 Milliarden EUR für den Tankrabatt: Warum viele Autofahrer:innen kaum Entlastung spüren
articles.text:
Studie zum Tankrabatt: Im Mittel bleiben 13 Euro im Monat – 61 Prozent merken kaum Entlastung
Für Haushalte mit Verbrennerauto brachte der erste Tankrabatt im Mai und Juni im mittleren Wert lediglich 13 EUR Ersparnis pro Monat. Das geht aus einer neuen Studie des Instituts für Makroökonomie und Konjunkturforschung der Hans-Böckler-Stiftung in Düsseldorf hervor.
Bei diesem sogenannten Median spart die eine Hälfte der untersuchten Haushalte weniger Geld, die andere Hälfte liegt darüber. Entsprechend nahmen 61 Prozent der befragten Autofahrer:innen kaum oder gar keine Entlastung wahr, während nur 19 Prozent großen Nutzen sahen.
Hohe Einkommen erhalten fast die Hälfte vom Tankrabatt
Die beiden Studienautoren Jan Behringer und Lukas Endres werteten zwei repräsentative Online-Befragungen unter rund 14.000 Personen in Deutschland aus. Haushalte unter 2.000 EUR Monatsnetto sparten durch die Steuersenkung im Mittel rund 8 EUR, ab 5.000 EUR netto waren es rund 20 EUR.
Gutverdiener:innen ab 5.000 EUR netto stellen knapp 24 Prozent der Verbrennerhaushalte, erhielten wegen höherer Fahrleistungen aber 45 Prozent des gesamten Rabattvolumens. Gemessen am eigenen Monatsbudget lag die Entlastung selbst bei Geringverdiener:innen im Mittel bei höchstens 0,55 Prozent, und Haushalte ohne Auto gingen leer aus.
Nach Haushaltsgröße aufgeschlüsselt blieben Paaren mit Kindern monatlich im Mittel rund 16 EUR, Paaren ohne Kinder 14 EUR und Einpersonenhaushalten 10 EUR. Dennoch stufte selbst unter Familien mehr als die Hälfte der Haushalte den staatlichen Nachlass als gering oder wirkungslos ein.
Der Nachlass habe zwar kurzfristig die Teuerungsrate gebremst und den Zinsdruck auf die Europäische Zentralbank gemildert, erklärt Institutsdirektor Sebastian Dullien in einer Mitteilung. „Er hat allerdings auch eine Reihe von Nachteilen, sodass er für eine langfristige Entlastung bei hohen Energiepreisen nicht ideal ist“, sagt der Ökonom.
Hohe Preise für Benzin und Diesel drücken den privaten Konsum
Trotz der Steuersenkung änderten 82 Prozent der Haushalte mit Verbrennerauto wegen der gestiegenen Kraftstoffpreise in diesem Jahr ihr Verhalten im Alltag. Rund 51 Prozent fuhren spritsparender, 48 Prozent ließen den Wagen öfter stehen und 18 Prozent wählten häufiger öffentliche Verkehrsmittel.
Zugleich kürzten oder verschoben 35 Prozent der Verbrennerhaushalte andere Einkäufe und Dienstleistungen, um die Mehrkosten an der Zapfsäule auszugleichen. Unterhalb von 2.000 EUR Monatsnetto schränkten sich 42 Prozent beim Konsum ein, ab 5.000 EUR netto waren es 24 Prozent.
Für die kommenden zwölf Monate planen 44 Prozent der Verbrennerhaushalte weiteren Konsumverzicht, was 11 Prozentpunkte über vergleichbaren Haushalten ohne Auto liegt. Allein 43 Prozent machen sich große Sorgen um die künftigen Spritpreise, und in dieser Gruppe wollen sogar 63 Prozent weniger ausgeben.
Demgegenüber planen unter unbesorgten Autofahrer:innen lediglich 17 Prozent Abstriche bei Waren und Dienstleistungen. „Die anhaltende Verunsicherung der Menschen aufgrund der hohen Spritpreise dürfte den privaten Konsum somit zusätzlich belasten“, schreiben Behringer und Endres in ihrer Studie.
Mineralölkonzerne, Modellgrenzen und der geplante Spritpreisdeckel
Methodisch markieren die errechneten 13 EUR sogar nur eine rechnerische Obergrenze, da das Institut die Jahresfahrleistung pauschal durch zwölf teilte. Zudem rechneten die Autoren mit festen Durchschnittsverbräuchen von 7,7 Litern für Benziner und 7,0 Litern für Diesel sowie voller Steuerweitergabe.
An den Zapfsäulen sank die Weitergabe gegen Ende Juni jedoch deutlich ab, zeigt eine Auswertung des Deutschen Instituts für Wirtschaftsforschung in Berlin. Nach Berechnungen der Monopolkommission in Bonn verblieben allein beim ersten Tankrabatt mindestens 200 Millionen EUR bei Raffinerien und Mineralölkonzernen.
Trotzdem legten Bund und Länder den Rabatt bis Dezember neu auf, sodass beide Runden zusammen 4,1 Milliarden EUR Steuergeld kosten. Ab Januar 2027 plant die Bundesregierung für drei Monate einen Spritpreisdeckel, den der Monopolkommissionsvorsitzende Tomaso Duso ebenfalls ablehnt.
„Gedeckelt wird der Tankstellenpreis, doch die Margen der Tankstellen sind ohnehin gering“, warnt der Ökonom in einer aktuellen Stellungnahme. Weil die Großhandelspreise der Raffinerien frei bleiben, drohen bei niedrigem Deckel Lieferengpässe und bei hohem Deckel steigende Preise an günstigen Stationen.
Stromsteuer und fehlende Kontodaten bremsen gezielte Hilfen
Unter den befragten Autofahrer:innen sprechen sich 52 Prozent für eine einheitliche Pauschale an betroffene Haushalte und 29 Prozent für Hilfen an Geringverdiener:innen aus. Nur 11 Prozent befürworten einen verbrauchsabhängigen Rabatt für Vielfahrer:innen, während 9 Prozent staatliche Zuschüsse bei hohen Kraftstoffpreisen grundsätzlich ablehnen.
Auch die Düsseldorfer Studienautoren empfehlen Direktzahlungen samt einer Senkung der Stromsteuer, damit das Preissignal für sparsameren Kraftstoffverbrauch erhalten bleibt. In der deutschen Verwaltungspraxis fehlt für einkommensabhängige Überweisungen allerdings bis heute die technische Datenbasis beim Bonner Bundeszentralamt für Steuern.
Laut einer Antwort des Bundesfinanzministeriums lagen dort im Frühsommer erst für 16,1 Millionen Steuer-Identifikationsnummern Kontodaten vor, während fast 70 Millionen Einträge fehlten. Zudem beherrscht das staatliche Auszahlungssystem bislang nur gleiche Pro-Kopf-Beträge, weshalb eine soziale Staffelung erst nachträglich über die Einkommensteuererklärung greifen könnte.
Auch im deutschsprachigen Nachbarraum gehen die Regierungen eigene Wege, nachdem Österreich im Frühjahr eine Preisbremse für Kraftstoffe ohne Autobahntankstellen einführte. In der Schweiz lehnte der Bundesrat Steuernachlässe dagegen ab, was laut dem Sender SRF verstärkten Tanktourismus nach Österreich und Deutschland auslöst.

articles.title: Experimental XNU Linux Project Boots macOS 27 Desktop on Linux
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 24th 2026
Experimental XNU Linux Project Boots macOS 27 Desktop on Linux
Unix software enthusiasts, rejoice! An experimental project called "XNU Linux" has successfully booted a complete macOS 27 desktop on an ARM64 Linux system. This breakthrough offers a new way to run Apple's operating system without relying on traditional virtualization methods. This is significant news for the community, as there is a large group of enthusiasts eager to create custom macOS desktops, also known as Hackintoshes. The project utilizes Apple's open-source XNU kernel, modified to function as a loadable module within Linux, enabling macOS and Linux processes to run on the same hardware.
Instead of translating macOS applications into a format Linux can execute, XNU Linux takes a different approach by integrating Apple's kernel into the Linux environment. It consists of two primary components: xnu.ko, which runs the hosted XNU kernel, and fki.ko, which provides an interface to Linux resources such as memory, networking, timers, and storage. This setup allows macOS processes to run natively on the host CPU without an intervening hypervisor. The setup has been tested on an NVIDIA DGX Spark running Ubuntu, as well as an Apple Silicon Mac running Linux in a virtual machine. The system successfully reached the macOS desktop, including Finder, Dock, WindowServer, and loginwindow, with Safari and Chrome also operational. Applications such as Spotlight and file-system operations remained functional during a brief 30-minute stress test.Graphics support is also part of the project, with a bridge that routes macOS Metal workloads through Vulkan and Mesa to the host GPU. However, this currently requires a compatible Virtio-GPU setup. The NVIDIA DGX Spark demonstration still uses CPU-based rendering. There are also hardware restrictions, as the project currently requires an ARM64 processor with pointer authentication, 4 KB memory pages, and at least 16 GB of RAM. Users must supply their own macOS 27 installation, and conventional x86-based PCs are not supported, largely due to the optimizations done by Apple for its Apple Silicon M-series of chips for macOS.

articles.title: Nvidia engineer who quit over Jensen Huang's exit says he 'may have moved too quickly' — robotics engineer who went viral after post is now open to returning after CEO's reinstatement
articles.text:
Nvidia engineer who quit over Jensen Huang's exit says he 'may have moved too quickly' — robotics engineer who went viral after post is now open to returning after CEO's reinstatement
Darrell Dai says he's "open to exploring the possibility of returning"
Former Nvidia robotics engineer Darrell Dai made a viral post just nine days ago announcing his resignation from Nvidia, which has gathered over 7 million impressions on X alone (Dai also posted to his LinkedIn account). Dai resigned due to what he described as a lack of transparency around CEO Jensen Huang's exit. But now that Huang is back at the helm, Dai has followed up, saying that he "may have moved too quickly," although his resignation has already taken effect.
Dai says that although he's open to the possibility of returning to Nvidia, he wants to approach his next decision with "a clearer mind." Huang resigned 11 days ago following reports of two separate affairs, one of which reportedly involved an alleged Chinese intelligence asset.
Despite reports of belligerent behaviors toward employees, Nvidia retains an exceptional rating on Glassdoor, and many employees rallied around the CEO's return. A petition to reinstate Huang gathered over 150,000 signatures online, including high-profile names like Elon Musk.
Huang publicly admitted to having an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. In his statement, the Nvidia co-founder apologized to his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang, and his two children, Spencer Huang and Madison Huang, both of whom still work at Nvidia.
Days following the admission, a report from The New York Times accused Huang of having another affair with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who reported directly to Huang, citing five anonymous sources within Nvidia. Huang resigned as CEO the following day. Neither Huang nor Powell have commented on the alleged affair.
Dai's last day at Nvidia was November 19, just a few days ago. President Donald Trump said on Monday that he contacted Nvidia's board, and went as far as to claim he "made the deal," according to CNBC. Following the announcement of Huang's return, Nvidia's stock rose more than 30% upon market open.

articles.title: Backing Canada’s Telesat could be central to Quebecor’s Telus bid
articles.text:
Support for Canadian satellite company Telesat could play a role in Quebecor’s bid to purchase Telus.
Sources who spoke to the Financial Post said that while there has been no explicit plan to back Telesat through investment, loans, or other means, such support could emerge as part of discussions to win Ottawa’s blessing for Quebecor’s bid to buy Telus.
To add some context, Quebecor has been trying to purchase Telus since earlier this year, submitting two offers, with the most recent one being on Nov. 9. CEO Pierre Karl Péladeau also said that American satellite competitor Starlink was a big motivator for the purchase, and called a possible Bell-Telus merger bad for consumers (as if a Quebecor-Telus merger wouldn’t be equally as bad for consumers).
The Financial Post also noted that bolstering the Ottawa-based Telesat could help offset concerns about consolidation in the telecom sector by showing what a stronger telecom company, such as the combined Quebecor-Telus, could do to benefit other companies.
Currently, Telesat is developing Lightspeed, a low-earth orbit (LEO) broadband network for telecom, government, maritime, and aeronautical customers. In 2024, the federal government awarded the satellite company a $2.1 billion loan, with a source for the Financial Post noting that Prime Minister Mark Carney’s inner circle saw the company as an important piece in establishing Canada’s telecom sovereignty.
The one caveat is that Lightspeed isn’t expected to deploy commercially until 2028, and the Financial Post notes that the company is struggling to restructure a lot of legacy debt. Last week, the company secured a standstill agreement that ensures creditors will not take any “enforcement action” before Jan. 8, 2027.
Part of Péladeau’s pitch to purchase Telus mentioned that the two companies could save nearly $400 million in operating capital, and that it would go toward advancing digital sovereignty by building stronger domestic platforms. Péladeau said the near-$400 million savings would go toward paying down debt and building what he calls the “network of the future.”
Quebecor reportedly had exploratory discussions with Telesat, but emphasized that the talks focused on the possibilities offered by Lightspeed, and no investment proposal has been made yet.
However, this all seems like a pretty convoluted and expensive way to ward off foreign satellite competitors, especially when Quebecor could just directly back or purchase Telesat instead. The company could skip most of the regulatory hurdles that come with purchasing Telus and walk away with a strong, Canadian satellite partner that it could potentially profit off of (alongside saving billions).

articles.title: 1 000 créneaux en 24h : pourquoi ces voitures électriques chinoises tournent en rond dans les parkings la nuit ?
articles.text:
La vidéo a de quoi surprendre. À 6 heures du matin, deux voitures électriques Avatr 06 et 12 manœuvrent côte à côte en parfaite synchronisation dans le sous-sol désert d’un parking. Capturées par les caméras de surveillance, ces vidéos montrent plusieurs modèles dotés du système intelligent Huawei Qiankun en train de tourner en rond. Loin d’être un phénomène surnaturel, l’explication vient tout simplement d’un concours organisé par Huawei pour récompenser l’usage de son aide au stationnement.
La course aux points qui fait tourner les têtes (et les voitures)
Du 31 octobre au 13 novembre 2026, la deuxième édition du championnat de conduite intelligente Huawei Qiankun a rassemblé plus de 190 000 participants. Dans la catégorie dédiée au stationnement, les cent meilleurs utilisateurs cumulant le plus de créneaux automatiques réussis gagnaient des points utilisables chez la marque. Prêts à tout pour grimper dans le classement, certains propriétaires ont répété les manœuvres à la chaîne, un conducteur affirmant même avoir franchi le cap des 1 000 sessions en 24 heures.
Problème de réglage horaire ou mauvaise lecture du règlement du concours, les vidéos diffusées montrent des véhicules s’activer entre minuit et 6 heures du matin, alors que le comptage s’arrêtait à 22 heures. Ces véhicules qui dansent en pleine nuit n’apportent donc aucun point supplémentaire à leurs conducteurs.
Capteurs capricieux, manœuvres à distance ou bug ?
Trois raisons peuvent expliquer ces rondes nocturnes sans fin. Lancées depuis un smartphone via l’application, les manœuvres de stationnement à distance ont pu être déclenchées volontairement par des conducteurs. Le mauvais éclairage, des marquages au sol effacés ou des espaces étroits peuvent également poser problème à la voiture qui relance alors le créneau encore et encore. La dernière piste est tout simplement celle du bug logiciel, mais cela n’a pour l’instant pas encore été confirmé.
À lire : GTA 6 pousse le réalisme des voitures électriques très loin, mais oublie un détail essentiel
Comme l’indique la réglementation chinoise, les fonctions de stationnement automatique sont bridées à 30 km/h dans le pays et demandent une supervision humaine permanente. Chez Avatr, la documentation technique indique une vitesse d’exécution plafonnée à 5 km/h avec arrêt d’urgence en cas d’obstacle. Quoi qu’il en soit, cet étrange balai des voitures dans les parkings rappelle que les fonctions d’aide au stationnement sont encore loin d’être infaillibles.

articles.title: Google transforme son moteur de recherche en assistant personnel, avec vos données comme carburant
articles.text:
Google étend les connexions entre son Mode IA et vos applications pour enrichir ses réponses avec vos dépenses, vos documents et vos conversations Gemini. Une nouvelle étape vers un moteur de recherche qui connaît vos projets, à condition de lui en ouvrir l’accès.
Pour préparer un voyage, on cherche une destination sur Google, on compare les prix, puis on ouvre sa boîte mail pour retrouver une réservation. Avec son Mode IA, Google veut réunir ces étapes dans la même conversation. Le moteur connaît déjà le Web. Il voudrait maintenant avoir assez de contexte sur vous pour vous aider à organiser la suite, sans vous demander de tout raconter à chaque recherche. Et pour cela, Google va se servir dans l’ensemble de vos données personnelles.
Vos fichiers et vos conversations rejoignent la recherche
Google ajoute ainsi Wallet aux connexions de son Intelligence personnalisée. Drive et l’application Gemini doivent suivre dans les prochaines semaines. Ces services rejoignent Gmail, Agenda et Photos parmi les sources susceptibles d’alimenter les réponses du Mode IA.
Le moteur de recherche avait déjà intégré l’analyse des dépenses de Wallet dans Gemini. Cette fois, ces informations arrivent directement dans le moteur de recherche, pour aider à comprendre son budget ou à repérer des économies. L’accès aux données financières reste limité à la lecture.
Drive apporterait le contenu des documents, tableaux et PDF. Quant au lien avec Gemini, il permettrait de reprendre dans la recherche une idée explorée avec le chatbot, et vice-versa. Google prévoit aussi que le contexte des recherches récentes accompagne davantage les réponses, y compris dans un nouveau fil.
L'idée derrière ces modifications est de vous faire gagner du temps. Plus besoin de réexpliquer le contexte dans une nouvelle conversation. Comme dans un chatbot traditionnel, le mode IA de Google va retenir les informations clés pour vous apporter une réponse rapide, précise et pertinente.
Un assistant personnel auquel il faut donner les clés
Si donner accès à vos informations de paiement ou vos fichiers vous dérange, Google a pensé à vous. Ces connexions demandent une activation volontaire et peuvent être coupées à la demande. Google prévoit une icône sous les réponses personnalisées pour montrer le contexte utilisé. L’utilisateur pourra également corriger une information dans la conversation. Le service peut toujours se tromper sur vos goûts ou vos intentions.
Cette personnalisation a aussi un coût. L’aide de Google précise que des résumés, extraits et déductions issus des contenus consultés peuvent servir à entraîner ses modèles. Dans certains cas, un extrait peut correspondre à l’intégralité d’un message ou d’un document court. Attention donc aux informations que vous partagez.
Pour les utilisateurs français, il faudra encore patienter. La France ne figure pas dans la liste actuelle des pays compatibles avec les connexions de contenus à la recherche. Google réserve par ailleurs l’accès à Drive aux États-Unis, en anglais.
Le moteur de recherche se rapproche ainsi de l’assistant personnel que Google construit autour de Gemini. Pour lui demander conseil, il suffira toujours de quelques mots. Pour qu’il vous connaisse, il faudra décider jusqu’où le laisser entrer.

articles.title: 6 bonnes raisons de donner sa chance à Blade Runner 2099, au même niveau que les films ?
articles.text:
Attendue avec autant de curiosité que de prudence par les fans, la série Blade Runner 2099 possède la lourde tâche de perpétuer l’héritage d’un monument de la pop culture. Libre adaptation du roman « Les androïdes rêvent-ils de moutons électriques ? » (1966) de Philip K. Dick, le film Blade Runner (1982) de l’immense Ridley Scott a contribué à définir l’esthétique des œuvres dystopiques au cinéma. Audacieux mélange entre SF et néo noir, il nous plonge dans l’enquête de Rick Deckard (Harrison Ford), un flic torturé qui appartient à une division spéciale, les « Blade Runner », chargée de traquer les Réplicants jugés déviants.
Dans ce Los Angeles pluvieux et situé en 2019, une entreprise privée, Tyrell Corporation, détient le monopole de création des Réplicants, des androïdes biosynthétiques utilisés comme de la main d’œuvre corvéable à merci. Avec son esthétique cyberpunk, ses looks eighties et ses décors extérieurs époustouflants, Blade Runner demeure un classique du genre, immédiatement reconnaissable. On vous donne 6 bonnes raisons de donner une chance à sa suite en série.
1. Replonger dans le monde hypnotique de Blade Runner
Comme bon nombre de films avant-gardistes, Blade Runner a connu une sortie en salles contrastée : échec aux Etats-Unis, le film devient un succès à l’étranger. Les critiques ont été dures, mais il a remporté des prix prestigieux (Bafta et Prix Hugo). Au fil des années et avec la sortie d’un Director’s Cut, Blade Runner acquiert le statut de film culte.
Trente-cinq ans après sa sortie, Denis Villeneuve réalise une suite fleuve, Blade Runner 2049, portée par Ryan Gosling. Esthétiquement éblouissant et cohérent avec la mythologie installée dans le premier film, il convainc une grande partie de la critique mais son rythme lent et son ambiance froide ne séduisent pas le grand public.
Avec deux films marquants et une série d’animation, Blade Runner : Black Lotus (2021), Blade Runner a acquis un noyau dur de fans, impatients de découvrir la dernière itération d’un univers devenu franchise, la série Blade Runner 2099.
2. Ridley Scott a eu (un peu) son mot à dire
Dans un marché audiovisuel qui se replie sur les IP (Intellectual Property) – des récits déjà connus du public comme des romans, podcasts, films etc. – la création d’une série autour de l’univers de Blade Runner fait sens. La peur numéro une des fans, bien légitime, reste de voir leur film préféré dilué dans une production cheap ou que cette suite vienne contredire la mythologie de l’œuvre originale.
Dans ce genre d’entreprise risquée, la présence des créateurs du matériel d’origine rassure. Créée par Silka Luisa, la série a pu compter sur Ridley Scott, producteur exécutif sur le projet. Le producteur Broderick Johnson a confirmé en interview : « Ridley Scott a participé à cette version depuis le début, en décidant de la temporalité, si cent ans, cinquante ans ou autre s’était passé. Il était impliqué dans tout le projet, jusqu’à donner son avis sur les montages des épisodes et tout le reste. »
L’avis de Ridley Scott est toutefois demeuré consultatif. Un peu plus tôt dans l’année, le réalisateur de The Dog Stars (2026) regrettait d’avoir perdu le contrôle créatif de Blade Runner (moyennant un beau chèque !). « Je ne peux pas blâmer mes avocats et mes agents de l’époque, mais d’une manière ou d’une autre, nous avons laissé filer les droits de Blade Runner. Et quand on n’est pas l’auteur du texte, on ne possède pas l’œuvre. »
Des propos qui reflètent l’amertume du réalisateur de n’avoir pas pu réaliser Blade Runner 2049. À l’époque, il avait laissé sa place à Denis Villeneuve pour réaliser Alien : Covenant. Ridley Scott se console d’ailleurs avec la franchise Alien, dont il est resté propriétaire. Il a notamment produit la série Alien : Earth.
3. La série rebat les cartes de la mythologie
Silka Luisa a imaginé l’histoire de Blade Runner 2099 en continuité avec les deux précédents films. La série prend place un demi-siècle après le long-métrage de Denis Villeneuve. Les Réplicants ont pris le pouvoir dans un Los Angeles en proie au réchauffement climatique. Les oppressés d’hier sont devenus les oppresseurs d’aujourd’hui. Voilà qui offre des possibilités narratives intéressantes.
Ce sont eux les nouveaux « Blade Runner », qui traquent leurs propres anciens modèles présentant un danger pour l’ordre public et traitent les humains comme des citoyens de seconde-zone.
L’histoire débute quand Cora, une humaine en cavale, décide de se faire passer pour une Réplicante dans le but de protéger son frère. Le subterfuge fonctionne et elle enquête bientôt aux côtés d’Olwen, une Réplicante en fin de vie chargée de « mettre à la retraite » son ancien partenaire Réplicant.
Côté mythologie, la showrunneuse s’intéresse également à la généalogie des Réplicants et notamment aux tous premiers modèles Nexus One. Voilà qui devait créer quelques nouveaux fils de discussions sur Reddit ! Si la série fait référence à Deckard, Silka Luisa a fait savoir qu’elle ne trancherait pas la question de la nature de ce personnage culte, humaine ou Réplicant. Un choix fort sage : Harrison Ford et Ridley Scott eux-mêmes sont en désaccord sur la question !
4. Un duo féminin qui déménage
La série Blade Runner 2099 repose sur la dynamique d’un duo de personnages féminins, Olwen et Cora, incarnées par Michelle Yeoh, reine hollywoodienne des films d’action (Tigre et Dragons, Everything Everywhere, All at Once) et la très demandée Hunter Schafer (Euphoria, Hunger Games : La Ballade du serpent et de l’oiseau chanteur). Les deux actrices brillent autant dans les séquences d’action que dans les scènes plus émouvantes.
La relation entre ces deux femmes dures à cuire, qui ont plus en commun qu’elles ne le pensent, constitue le cœur battant de la série. Au fil de leur enquête, elles vont apprendre à s’apprivoiser et à dépasser leurs préjugés respectifs sur les Réplicants et les humains.
C’est une très bonne idée de proposer un buddy movie au féminin, là où les deux précédents films étaient centrés sur des personnages masculins et plaçaient leurs protagonistes féminines dans des rôles très secondaires et sexualisés (les IA nues de Blader Runner 2049, la petite-amie parfaite de K, où la très passive Rachel dans le premier film). Adieu le male gaze : la mini-série prouve que les questions existentielles se conjuguent autant au féminin qu’au masculin.
5. Une fresque ambitieuse
Pour faire revivre le Los Angeles futuriste de Blade Runner, Amazon Prime n’a pas lésiné sur le budget : 160 millions de dollars pour huit épisodes d’une heure. Réalisés par Jonathan Van Tulleken, les deux premiers épisodes mettent en scène un univers qualifié de « Sunshine Noir », ou le genre du polar se marie avec une photographie grillée par le soleil. Esthétiquement ambitieuse, la série alterne diverses ambiances, dont quelques séquences pluvieuses, clin d’oeil à celles du film de 1982.
L’exigence artistique se fait sentir dans le choix des plans, le travail sur la lumière, l’utilisation d’outils rétro-futuristes (n’oublions pas que Blade Runner a anticipé Facetime !) ou encore l’ampleur et la diversité des décors présents. Sans être la claque visuelle des premiers films (elle n’a ni le budget nécessaire, ni la primeur de la nouveauté pour ça), la série s’inscrit dans leur continuité et leur fait honneur.
6. Une SF plus actuelle que jamais
Depuis la sortie du premier Blade Runner, au début des années 80, notre rapport aux œuvres de science-fiction a évolué au fil des innovations technologiques de la vraie vie. Certains aspects du film ont vu si juste que nous vivons déjà dans Blade Runner. Si les voitures volantes ne sont pas à l’ordre du jour (sniff…), l’intelligence artificielle, contrôlée par des entreprises privées, est en train de révolutionner notre monde. Et la question de l’autonomie de l’IA contre les intérêts des humains commence très sérieusement à se poser !
À rebours des séries ultra-rythmées et de nos vies minutées, la série prend son temps pour nous raconter son histoire et nous immerger dans son univers mi-inquiétant, mi-fascinant. Le choix d’une photographie solaire s’appuie aussi sur la réalité du réchauffement climatique en cours.
Sous le bon vieux genre du thriller, les thématiques soulevées par la série – les rapports de domination entre humains et machines, la quête d’immortalité, la puissance des souvenirs et notre tragique propension à l’autodestruction – se révèlent encore plus d’actualité qu’il y a cinquante ans. Sans apporter de grandes réponses définitives, Blade Runner 2099 est une invitation à la réflexion et à la contemplation.
Le verdict
Blade Runner 2099
Voir la fiche
On a aimé
- Un duo féminin convaincant
- Une fresque ambitieuse esthétiquement
- Une série qui prend son temps
- Une SF aux thématiques actuelles
On a moins aimé
- Des personnages badass mais un peu froids
- Elle n’égale pas la claque visuelle des deux premiers films
Avec son esthétique soignée et son univers toujours aussi hypnotique, Blade Runner 2099 réussit à prolonger intelligemment la mythologie imaginée par Ridley Scott. Sans chercher à rivaliser avec la puissance visuelle des deux films, cette mini-série ambitieuse apporte un souffle nouveau à la franchise, notamment grâce à son formidable duo féminin incarné par Michelle Yeoh et Hunter Schafer. Elle renoue avec la dimension contemplative de la saga tout en actualisant ses questionnements sur l’intelligence artificielle, le pouvoir et la condition humaine. Une proposition de science-fiction élégante, immersive et profondément actuelle, qui mérite largement le détour.

articles.title: Le dernier verrou humain saute : Claude peut désormais signer lui-même le code qu'il a écrit
articles.text:
Anthropic permet désormais à Claude de valider son propre code : les développeurs vont-ils devenir inutiles ?
Jusqu'ici, Claude écrivait le code et un humain avait le dernier mot avant la mise en production. Claude Ship, présenté ce lundi 23 novembre, rend ce verrou négociable : trois agents se relaient pour inspecter les modifications, réparer ce qui coince et, si l'équipe le veut bien, donner eux-mêmes le feu vert final. En interne, Anthropic dit avoir doublé le nombre de modifications intégrées tout en réduisant la casse.
Anthropic a lancé le 23 novembre Claude Ship, un service qui permet à Claude de relire du code, de le corriger et désormais de l'approuver lui-même. Jusqu'ici, ce feu vert final revenait à un développeur avant que la moindre modification, ce qu'on appelle une "pull request", rejoigne un projet. Si les règles de l'équipe l'autorisent, Claude peut maintenant s'en charger sans qu'aucun humain ait relu une seule ligne.
Le service est disponible en bêta pour les entreprises abonnées aux offres Team et Enterprise de Claude, sur les projets hébergés par GitHub. Loin des joueurs qui s'amusaient à recréer des jeux avec Claude Code, Anthropic vise ici les équipes de développement professionnelles.
Introducing Claude Ship (beta): Claude can review your pull requests, work on fixes, and approve the ones your team's policy allows.
The goal is to help you ship code as fast as you can write it. pic.twitter.com/b9OBAhEBmr
— ClaudeDevs (@ClaudeDevs) November 23, 2026
L'éditeur part d'un constat simple : Claude écrit déjà environ 90 % du code de Claude Code, son outil de programmation, et les relecteurs humains ne suivent plus. Chez Anthropic, l'homme chargé de sécuriser Claude va jusqu'à annoncer la fin du travail. L'entreprise rappelle que "la plupart des équipes veulent qu'une personne approuve chaque modification, et c'est facile à tenir tant que des humains écrivent chaque ligne". Son objectif tient en une formule : "livrer le code aussi vite que les équipes l'écrivent".
	
La plupart des équipes veulent qu'une personne approuve chaque modification, et c'est facile à tenir tant que des humains écrivent chaque ligne.
Trois agents pour relire, réparer et valider les pull requests
Le premier maillon, Code Review, n'est pas nouveau. Lancé en mars, il est en version finale depuis le 15 octobre. Il passe le code au crible et classe ses remarques par gravité.
La nouveauté s'appelle PR Steward. Cet agent intervient quand des tests automatisés échouent, quand deux modifications se contredisent ou quand un relecteur fait une remarque. Il pousse alors lui-même les correctifs. Après chaque intervention, il laisse un commentaire qui détaille ce qu'il a changé et comment l'annuler. Une simple mention "@claude stop" l'arrête net, et il n'a le droit ni d'approuver ni de fusionner quoi que ce soit.
Claude Approvals rend enfin son verdict. L'équipe rédige ses règles en langage courant dans un fichier placé dans le projet : une coquille dans la documentation peut passer seule, tandis qu'une modification qui touche à des données financières sensibles devra passer sous les yeux d'un humain.
Les développeurs peuvent aussi tout lancer eux-mêmes avec la commande /ship, en cours de déploiement dans Claude Code et dans l'application de bureau. Claude ouvre la demande, relit la modification, puis traite les remarques et les tests en échec. Les droits d'accès et les règles du projet décident toujours de ce qui peut être intégré.
Try it on your next PR: update Claude Code and run /ship. It's rolling out in the CLI and desktop app now.
Claude opens the PR, reviews your change, and works on feedback and failing checks. Your permissions and branch rules still decide what can merge. pic.twitter.com/UNPQqZUZp4
— ClaudeDevs (@ClaudeDevs) November 23, 2026
Des gains spectaculaires chez Anthropic, des garde-fous de rigueur
Entre juin et septembre 2026, l'équipe Claude Code a plus que doublé le nombre de pull requests intégrées. Sur la même période, la part de modifications annulées après coup a baissé de plus de 40 %. Anthropic reconnaît que la part propre de Claude Ship dans ce résultat ne peut pas être isolée du reste de sa méthode. Ces chiffres viennent d'une équipe où l'IA tient déjà la plume, au point qu'Anthropic a activé ses garde-fous les plus stricts face à des IA qui se construisent elles-mêmes. Avec des modèles comme Claude Fable 5.2, qui a codé un système d'exploitation en huit jours, le volume de code à valider ne va pas baisser.
Boris Cherny, le créateur de Claude Code, rappelle qu'il y a un an, Claude Opus 4.5 devenait le premier modèle à écrire 100 % de son code. Il dit utiliser Claude Ship "toute la journée, tous les jours" et ne plus imaginer "livrer du code sans".
A year ago we launched Opus 4.5, the first model to write 100% of my code.
Shipping PRs hasn’t caught up, so today we’re launching Claude Ship in beta for Team and Enterprise. I use it all day every day and can’t imagine shipping without it. https://t.co/IfK0Oua6rZ
— Boris Cherny (@bcherny) November 23, 2026
La documentation officielle admet que les agents peuvent laisser passer des bugs ou des failles de sécurité. L'éditeur conseille donc de commencer par un seul projet, en mode observation : Claude Approvals indique ce qu'il aurait décidé, sans rien bloquer. La fusion automatique de GitHub demande aussi de la vigilance, puisqu'elle peut intégrer un changement sans aucune intervention humaine si les règles n'en exigent pas.
Côté facture, chaque passage consomme des jetons payés en plus de l'abonnement, avec des plafonds de dépenses réglables. Les organisations qui ont activé la non-conservation des données ou certaines options renforcées de conformité et de chiffrement n'y ont pas accès pour l'instant.

articles.title: OpenAI Scales Git for Coding Agents with Pando
articles.text:
OpenAI has detailed Pando, a new backend that scales Git for concurrent coding-agent workloads without replacing familiar Git workflows. The company reports nearly 80% lower median push latency by coordinating branch updates independently and reusing stored packfiles across fetches.
Pando now powers all development in OpenAI's monorepo and is serving nearly a petabyte of Git data per day. OpenAI attributes the increased load to Codex-driven development, and each push can in turn trigger multiple CI jobs that all fetch the same history. Pando went into production in April 2026.
Rather than replace Git's client and protocol, OpenAI has changed how the backend coordinates reference updates and stores and transfers objects. On a push, Pando validates the incoming packfile as it's being streamed to immutable blob storage, without unpacking it into a local repository. A metadata transaction records the reference version (containing the new branch tip, the packfile and its dependencies on earlier reference versions) and atomically updates the reference pointer. Updates to unrelated references can proceed independently of one another; updates to the same reference still need to be coordinated.
OpenAI refers to this as causal consistency with serialisable updates to individual references and read-your-own-write consistency. A reader gets the history needed for the requested revision, but fetching a number of branches won't provide a repository-wide snapshot. Two clients can see different combinations of branch versions during concurrent updates. The trade-off removes a shared coordination point for unrelated pushes.
Pando also changes how Git decides which objects to transfer. By default, when a client pushes a new feature branch, the server will advertise only a designated trunk branch as its base. That constrains the dependencies of the resulting packfile, which in turn allows Pando to reuse it for readers who already have that trunk history. Repeated or stacked branch pushes can resend objects outside trunk, trading some additional bandwidth for the benefit of reusable packs.
Pando’s topic-branch packs depend on advertised trunk history and can repeat objects from earlier pushes (source)
For fetches, Pando maps the client's existing and requested commits to reference versions and picks out the appropriate stored packs to cover the missing history. Git's packfile-uri capability allows the server to return download links rather than generate a bespoke pack for each client. Express, a regional pack-delivery cache, serves those downloads. OpenAI reports cache-hit rates in excess of 99% and tests in which clone and fetch operations saturated 10 Gbps network links.
Background compaction groups packs into larger, geometrically sized covers, resembling compaction in a log-structured merge-tree. The covers provide better compression and act as a skip-list-like index for fetch planning. Pando keeps packs at every level so that clients with different histories can still be served.
Pando groups successive packs into larger covers to improve compression and fetch planning, retaining packs at every level (source)
The design contrasts with Anthropic's Scion, previously covered by InfoQ. Scion replaces Git's underlying model with changesets recording files changed relative to their first parent and content-addressed pointers to compressed file contents; commits, merges, rebases and history queries run server-side. Its clients retrieve missing immutable trees and blobs, rather than negotiate Git packfiles, and use bounded local caches and sparse or virtualised checkouts.
Both systems make use of immutable data and regional caches to reduce repeated computation. The way in which they draw the compatibility line is very different, though. Pando preserves Git's object model and client-side workflows and changes the backend coordination and delivery. Scion, on the other hand, assumes an online client and moves the repository operations into a dedicated service. The improvements they report are not directly comparable. OpenAI reports on push latency, whereas Anthropic reports on checkout speedups and infrastructure reductions compared with its previous Git-based setup.
Git compatibility did not eliminate migration work. OpenAI initially deployed Pando as a read- and write-through proxy, moved clients in phases, and migrated hundreds of integrations using legacy APIs, webhooks and repository downloads. It also distributed its own Git build, which supports parallel downloading and indexing of independent packs. OpenAI says some client improvements are already upstream, with others available in its public repository.
For the architects, it's a case of two separate decisions: which source control operations go on the server and which of the consistency and transfer guarantees do the workloads actually need. Pando retains the Git workflows but dispenses with the repository-wide snapshot across branches and accepts redundant transfers in order to reduce the amount of coordination and per-fetch computation.

Black Week: Huawei Watch GT 7 Pro tem promoção relâmpago em 10x sem juros
Huawei Watch GT 7 Pro com tela de 3.000 nits e suporte a diversos esportes atinge o menor preço que já vimos, com desconto de 53% no prazo com cupom no Mercado Livre
O Watch GT 7 Pro está saindo por R$ 1.281 em até 10x sem juros com cupom DESCONTOSMELI no Mercado Livre. O smartwatch da Huawei, com corpo de titânio e tela AMOLED, atinge o menor preço visto pelo Achados desde o lançamento, com desconto de 53% sobre o original de R$ 2.699 na semana da Black Friday 2026.
Esta oferta é o menor preço que já encontramos para o Huawei Watch GT 7 Pro. Nas outras 4 ofertas publicadas desde outubro de 2026, o melhor foi R$ 1.484 (Mercado Livre, 17/11/2026).
O novo Huawei Watch GT 7 Pro possui uma tela AMOLED de 1,47″ com brilho de até 3.000 nits, que entrega imagens com cores excelentes e visibilidade garantida. O vidro Cristal de Safira protege-a em acidentes diversos.
Este gadget suporta mais de 110 modalidades esportivas, incluindo novas como golfe e esqui, contra pouco mais de 100 do Watch GT 6 Pro. Seus sensores suportam funções de qualidade de vida, como eletrocardiograma (ECG), monitores do sono, da saúde da mulher e da oxigenação no sangue (SpO2).
Este wearable pode fazer a diferença em situações de risco: ele dispara uma contagem regressiva caso detecte uma emergência médica e, se o usuário não se recuperar sozinho, pode ligar para números de emergência como 190 (polícia) e 192 (ambulância), desde que pareado a um celular.
O corpo em liga de titânio de 46 mm do Watch GT 7 Pro conta com a certificação IP69 e resiste a até 50 metros de profundidade (5 ATM), podendo ser usado em esportes aquáticos.
Sua bateria de 867 mAh tem autonomia de até 21 dias de uso no modo de economia, 12 dias em uso moderado e 7 dias com AOD ligado, segundo a fabricante, e suporta carregamento sem fio de 10 W.
O Huawei Watch GT 7 Pro (R$ 1.281 em até 10x sem juros com cupom DESCONTOSMELI) possui conectividade Bluetooth 6.0 e GPS multibanda.

articles.title: Jensen Huang reveló a la junta directiva de Nvidia más relaciones extramatrimoniales antes de su regreso
articles.text:
Jensen Huang, cofundador y director ejecutivo de Nvidia, confirmó ante la junta directiva de la compañía nuevas relaciones extramatrimoniales durante una reunión, según reveló The Wall Street Journal. El encuentro se produjo horas antes de que los directores votaran por unanimidad su reincorporación al cargo, apenas 11 días después de haber renunciado.
El propio Huang ya había admitido semanas atrás una infidelidad vinculada a Alice Huang, una ejecutiva señalada por autoridades estadounidenses por presuntos nexos con inteligencia china. Pero la reunión del domingo sumó un capítulo que, según las fuentes citadas por el diario, va más allá de los dos vínculos que ya habían trascendido públicamente.
Qué reveló Huang ante la junta directiva
Durante el encuentro, los directores interrogaron a Huang durante varias horas sobre su conducta, su transparencia y su franqueza respecto a los episodios. Según el reporte, el ejecutivo mostró arrepentimiento por su comportamiento y reconoció “aventuras adicionales más allá de las dos que habían sido ampliamente reportadas”.
El texto no precisa el número exacto de relaciones adicionales ni la identidad de las personas involucradas, aunque otras coberturas periodísticas sugieren que la cifra total de vínculos alegados podría llegar a por lo menos cuatro.
Pese a la decisión de reincorporarlo, la junta concluyó que Huang había violado el código de conducta de la empresa, tanto por sostener esas relaciones como por no haberlas revelado a tiempo. La compañía indicó que la investigación independiente sobre si el directivo fue blanco de una operación de inteligencia extranjera continuará, con la cooperación plena del ejecutivo.
Según trascendió, Huang también se habría reconciliado con su esposa, Lori Huang, en paralelo a las conversaciones con el directorio.
Cuáles son las relaciones señaladas en los reportes
Antes de la confesión del domingo, Huang ya había sido vinculado con al menos tres relaciones extramatrimoniales. La primera, reconocida públicamente por el propio ejecutivo, involucra a Alice Huang, exejecutiva de la firma de computación en la nube con sede en Singapur Megaspeed, bajo investigación del Departamento de Comercio por posible desvío de chips hacia China.
The New York Times reportó posteriormente una segunda relación, esta vez con Kimberly Powell, vicepresidenta de salud de Nvidia, quien reportaba directamente a Huang. Tras el anuncio de su renuncia, Reuters informó sobre una tercera relación con otra empleada de la compañía cuya identidad no fue revelada.
No está claro si las “aventuras adicionales” que Huang mencionó ante la junta el domingo incluyen a esta tercera empleada sin identificar o corresponden a vínculos completamente nuevos.
Jensen Huang ya regresó a Nvidia
La junta acordó el regreso de Huang, tras el respaldo del presidente Donald Trump, quien publicó en Truth Social que la reincorporación sería la mejor decisión “para la empresa, y también, para Estados Unidos”. El mandatario reconoció ante el Journal que había querido intervenir antes, pero dudaba de poder lograrlo: “El clima se volvió cada vez más propicio a medida que la acción de la compañía comenzó a derrumbarse”.
El fiscal general Todd Blanche le habría transmitido a Trump que Huang no era objeto ni blanco de una investigación del Departamento de Justicia y que no existía evidencia de que representara un riesgo para la seguridad nacional. En una llamada a CNBC, Trump afirmó que el directivo había sido “exonerado”: “Creemos que está bien, está absolutamente bien”, dijo, y lo calificó como un “tesoro nacional”.
En el comunicado oficial de reincorporación, el presidente de la junta, Harvey C. Jones, señaló que los directores “creen que Jensen es la persona indicada para liderar Nvidia” y que su regreso “es lo mejor para los accionistas, empleados, socios y clientes”. El propio Huang expresó sentirse “honrado de regresar a Nvidia” y agradeció el respaldo recibido durante la transición.
El lunes, al volver a la oficina, el ejecutivo recibió una bienvenida con ovaciones de empleados que coreaban “te amamos, Jensen”. La noticia de su reincorporación impulsó la acción de Nvidia más de un 31%, hasta 165,05 dólares, tras la caída registrada la semana anterior.

articles.title: Walmart teams up with Meta to bring Black Friday deals to AI agent Muse
articles.text:
Shopping with AI is becoming less of a futuristic idea and more of something companies expect us to do. Walmart is the latest retailer making that shift, teaming up with Meta to let customers shop its Black Friday deals through Muse, Meta’s AI agent.
The partnership, announced Tuesday, gives shoppers another way to find products, compare prices, and make purchases without browsing Walmart’s website themselves. Instead, customers can simply tell Muse what they are looking for and let the AI do the work.
The announcement highlights how differently Walmart and Amazon are approaching AI shopping. While Amazon has taken steps to stop third-party AI agents from making purchases for customers, Walmart is leaning into the idea.
To get started, users open the Muse app, sign in to their Walmart account, and return to the assistant to begin shopping. They can ask it to find specific products, compare options, or track down deals. Once a customer makes a request in Muse, the assistant sends it to Walmart, which returns relevant products and helps build a shopping cart.
Walmart says it has built privacy protections into the experience. For instance, Muse doesn’t get access to a customer’s Walmart shopping history or other personal information. Shoppers can also set spending limits, require approval before purchases, and review orders placed by the agent.
Plus, the company notes users can always delete their agent’s profile if they want to.
The experience is powered by Walmart’s Agent Gateway, a new system that allows outside AI assistants to connect directly with the retailer’s online store. This launched in October, and the company is planning to open it up to more developers and AI platforms, meaning Muse could eventually be just one of several assistants capable of shopping Walmart’s online store.
Walmart is not the only company teaming up with Meta’s Muse. Instacart also recently joined forces with the AI assistant.
Beyond Muse, Walmart has recently rolled out more AI-powered features to its own shopping assistant, Sparky.
Some of the newer additions include turning handwritten shopping lists into shopping carts, using photos and voice commands to find products, and helping customers get around their local store. Shoppers can search for an item and use a pin on the store map to see exactly which aisle it’s in. There’s also a “Flash Price Tag” button that makes the item’s shelf label light up.

articles.title: Your iPhone's ExpressVPN app has just changed its look
articles.text:
Your iPhone's ExpressVPN app has just changed its look
Version 13 brings new colour themes, a map-focused homepage, rebuilt tools, and passwordless logins to iOS
- ExpressVPN version 13.0.1 landed on the iOS App Store on November 23
- The redesign brings new colour themes, a map-led home screen, and more
- It also introduces passkey sign-in options on both iOS and Android
ExpressVPN has pushed a major visual overhaul to iPhone and iPad users with version 13.0.1 of its app.
Listed on the Apple App Store on Monday, November 23, the release refreshes one of TechRadar's best VPN recommendations just days after rival Proton VPN redesigned its own iPhone app.
In its App Store notes, ExpressVPN promises a "fresh new look" built for "a cleaner, smoother, and more intuitive experience."
ExpressVPN Basic: Save extra with this improved deal
Was: $2.99/month
Now: $2.79/month
ExpressVPN has added a further saving to all its 28-month plans for Black Friday. The best value choice, Basic, includes ExpressAI and ad, tracker, and malware blocking, all for less than NordVPN's lowest-cost option that merely includes the VPN. Try it, risk-free with ExpressVPN's 30-day money-back guarantee.
What ExpressVPN's iOS update is about
Speaking to TechRadar, an ExpressVPN spokesperson confirmed that iOS version 13 is a standalone interface update rather than an expansion of the June visual makeover on Mac, Windows, and Linux.
"Version 13 is a redesign of the ExpressVPN mobile app. It's a full refresh of the look and feel, with new colours, visuals and colour themes," the spokesperson told TechRadar.
The company explains that the update seeks to simplify the navigation and make the app easier to use.
"The homepage now puts more focus on the map, with a more detailed connection status and a new pause feature, and we've rebuilt Speed Test and Secure Device Assistant from scratch," ExpressVPN told us.
Existing ExpressVPN subscribers can download version 13.0.1 from the App Store today to try the new layout.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
New ways to sign in, and what the iPhone app still misses
Version 13 also changes how mobile users access their accounts on both iPhone and Android. According to the spokesperson, the update brings "a one-time code sent by email, a login token, and passkeys."
That login token is gradually replacing ExpressVPN's older activation code. Instead of reusing a static key, subscribers generate a temporary token in their ExpressVPN+ account portal and either type it in or scan a QR code, with each token expiring after a short period.
Does a fresh look and rebuilt menu fix everything iPhone users miss? Not entirely. While ExpressVPN's iOS release notes show steady additions in 2026, like Lightway in Rust and IP-based split tunneling, our ExpressVPN review notes that ExpressVPN's fastest Lightway Turbo protocol remains Windows-only.
The iPhone app still lacks Android's auto-connect rule for untrusted Wi-Fi and full app-by-app split tunneling, too.
Underneath the redesigned interface, the App Store listing confirms ExpressVPN's core privacy tools stay in place. You still get servers across 113 countries, including all 50 U.S. states, RAM-only servers that wipe data on every reboot, an audited no-logs policy, and Threat Manager to block trackers, requiring iOS 15.5 or later and 120 MB of storage.
The mobile redesign arrives during aggressive holiday pricing.
ExpressVPN recently cut its 28-month Basic plan to $2.79 per month, undercutting NordVPN while bundling ExpressAI alongside ad, tracker, and malware blocking, with higher tiers supporting up to 14 simultaneous connections.

articles.title: Gamer hijacks plane in GTA 6 using just mind control and eye tracking — Xbox controller mapped to read brain signals using EEG, maps mental commands to an Xbox controller without surgery
articles.text:
Gamer hijacks plane in GTA 6 using just mind control and eye tracking — Xbox controller mapped to read brain signals using EEG, maps mental commands to an Xbox controller without surgery
She used eye tracking and gyroscopes for thumbstick control.
EEG machines are used to detect and record brain activity, so one enterprising tech enthusiast decided to use them to play GTA VI. Creator Perri Karyal showed her feat on X, where she streamed her gameplay while wearing a wireless electroencephalogram (EEG) designed for research.
Perri could be seen jumping a fence with Jason on a motorbike, before proceeding toward a parked fighter to steal and fly it. Her brain activity is overlaid on the screen while she’s playing, and viewers could also see the creator intensely focused on the game.
She trained the software to recognize specific brain signals and mapped them to an action on her Xbox controller. For example, imagining pushing a cube forward would correspond to a button press, getting angry lets her interact with cars and other vehicles, while picturing a hopping cricket would also make her character jump. The joysticks, on the other hand, are controlled via eye tracking and through gyroscopes on the head unit.
While Perri makes it look effortless, using the EEG device for gaming is way harder than what many people think. “People don’t realize how challenging it is!” Karyal replied to a comment. One viewer also mentioned the huge mass of brainwaves that appeared on the screen when she took off on the jet, to which she responded, “I was so stressed out. DO YOU KNOW HOW MANY TIMES I TRIED TO DO THIS.” Even though using wireless EEG for gaming does not have any apparent side effects, the creator said that she gets headaches after hours of gaming because of how much the headset squeezes her head.
This isn’t the first time that we’ve seen people playing games using just their mind. Neuralink has recently shown off one of its patients shooting at NPCs and even “threading the needle” with a speedboat using a brain-computer interface (BCI) chip. The big difference between Perri’s creation and Neuralink’s BCI, though, is that the latter requires invasive neurosurgery.
It may be surprising to think how a tech creator could beat Neuralink at its own game, but the latter has already applied the technology to multiple trial patients. We’ve seen them playing complicated games like World of Warcraft and Counter-Strike 2, while others used it for productivity and creativity, like editing a YouTube video.
These technologies are still in the development and trial phases or are being experimented on by enterprising creators and tech tubers. However, it also gives hope to individuals with limited mobility, as it gives them hope that they could regain some form of mobility and independence in the future.
