articles.title: Tidal announces ban on AI-generated music; 27 million tracks will be deleted
articles.text:
Most streaming music providers have opted to label AI-generated content on their platforms, and until now, Tidal was one of them. However, the company is about to take a harder stance. Tidal announced that in the coming weeks, it will fully ban AI music because of the harm it does to human artists.
Tidal debuted its initial AI policy in July 2026, which included labeling and demonetizing all songs created entirely with AI. That wasn’t enough to stem the tide of AI slop, though. Over the past 90 days, Tidal reports that 43 percent of new uploads were completely AI-generated. On November 6, new uploads to Tidal hit a whopping 60 percent AI-generated.
As things stand, Tidal hosts 27 million tracks labeled as AI, all of which were obviously added in the past couple of years. That accounts for 6.3 percent of Tidal’s total catalog. On December 9, Tidal will delete all those songs. The streamer notes this will have essentially no negative impact, because 96 percent of AI-labeled tracks got zero plays in the past 90 days. Throughout its announcement, Tidal is careful to stipulate that it’s only talking about music that has been fully created by AI. Artists can still use AI tools as long as the final product contains human elements.
Some people don’t particularly mind AI music, but the team at Tidal has come to believe the harm to artists is too great. AI models can pump out random noises faster than humans can create things of real value, which can mislead listeners and siphon royalty payments away from creators. There’s also an issue with AI uploaders who are actively attempting to steal royalty payments. Tidal says it has already removed about 66,000 tracks from its service for impersonating artists, which was against its AI policy even before this update.

articles.title: All three of Amazon's new Alexa tablets are on sale for Black Friday — here's how to choose between them
articles.text:
Alexa Tablet 12 Pro vs Tablet 11 vs Tablet 8 — here's how to choose between Amazon's new Android tablets
All three of Amazon's new tablets are on sale for Black Friday
Once upon a time, Amazon Fire Tablets were some of the most popular Android tablets to buy over Black Friday. They were the definition of 'cheap and cheerful', and almost always enjoyed massive discounts in November.
That's no longer the case, though; Amazon discontinued the Fire range earlier this year to make room for the Amazon Alexa Tablet range.
These new slates are more advanced than their Fire-branded forebears, and they run Android rather than Amazon's own Fire OS software. They also have more modern builds, with iPad-like flat edges and narrow bezels.
But just because Amazon's Fire Tablets are gone doesn't mean the savings have to stop; in fact, all three of Amazon's new Alexa Tablets are on sale for Black Friday.
So, in this guide, I'm going to run you through the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, Tablet 11, and Tablet 8 to help you decide which to buy. I won't focus on specs as much as the actual characteristics of each slate: what other tablets they'll feel like, and who'd be best suited for each model. Hopefully, before the end of the article, you'll know exactly which device to pick up.
Alexa Tablet 8
A simple screen for entertainment
Of the three new Amazon tablets, the closest to the older Fire devices is arguably the Amazon Alexa Tablet 8. This is a smaller model, measuring just eight inches across, like the popular Fire Tab 8.
With 4GB RAM and a MediaTek chipset, it's not particularly powerful, but its 14-hour battery life means it lasts longer than many alternatives. This all means it's primed for the same kind of use case as the Fire Tab 8: on-the-go entertainment.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Like the older tablet, it's designed as a portable screen, so you can watch TV shows on a flight or play simple games while you're on the bus. This isn't a device for work or creative tasks, just for your videos. As such, it's probably not one to pick up if you're interested in using the Alexa+ smart assistant that much.
You might have assumed that the jump to full Android would open up the functionality of the Alexa Tablet 8, but in fact, it just lets the Tablet 8 do its entertainment tasks better. Now it'll be easier to download the games and access the streaming services you like, without Prime Video and Amazon Music being omnipresent.
Amazon is pitching the Tablet 8 for a second kind of buyer too: Kindle users. Between the size and links to Amazon's ecosystem, it's an alternative to an e-reader for people who want to read, while offering a little bit more too.
This is the cheapest Amazon Alexa Tablet. It starts at $229 / £119 (about AU$240) for the 64GB model, and goes up to $279 / £239 (about AU$480) for 128GB storage.
Alexa Tablet 11
Like an iPad that runs Android
In some ways, the Amazon Alexa Tablet 11 is just a slightly bigger alternative to the Tablet 8. It has the same chipset, same storage options, and same features, so it's not going to feel that different to use.
However, there are a few tweaks that'll make it feel different. For one, not only is its display bigger than the Tablet 8's, but it's higher-res too. And while the chipset is the same, there's double the RAM at 8GB, so this slate will be able to handle more complex tasks as well as multitasking. The battery is said to last an extra hour too.
All of that means you're paying more here. The Amazon Alexa Tablet 11 costs $329.99 / £289.99 (about AU$580) for its 64GB storage model, and $379.99 / £329.99 (around AU$660) for 128GB storage.
Its specs, size, and price put the Amazon Alexa Tablet 11 in the same league as Apple's entry-level iPad. That slate costs $349 / £329 / AU$599 for its 128GB version, so it's cheaper if you're comparing like-for-like storage, but pricier if you're comparing base-level models.
The entry-level iPad is arguably the go-to mid-range tablet, and many tablet makers try to make Android equivalents to sway some buyers; this seems like Amazon's attempt. It has a better battery life and access to Android, but it's a fair amount weaker.
Still, I'd recommend the Amazon Alexa Tablet 11 to the same kind of user who might consider an iPad. It's sufficient for tasks like college coursework or as a portable work machine.
Alexa Tablet 12 Pro
An iPad Pro on a budget
The biggest and most expensive member of the new Amazon tablet lineup is the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro. As its name suggests, it has a 12-inch display, and before you ask: no, there's no non-Pro model.
Specs-wise, it's another modest step up over its predecessors. Its screen has extra pixels to match its size, while its main camera has a few more pixels; it has a bigger battery, and it charges quicker, too. It's also available with more storage: either 128GB or 256GB, and that latter model gets 16GB RAM.
The most important upgrade is the chipset. The 12 Pro doesn't have the same modest MediaTek Kompanio seen in the other devices, but a MediaTek Dimensity 8400, which should make it much better at gaming. But this isn't just a gaming slate.
Amazon's pitching this model quite differently to the others. It's selling it in productivity bundles alongside the Alexa Tablet Pro Pen and Tablet Pro Keyboard, and advertising it as useful for drawing, video editing, and various Alexa+ functions.
This, therefore, is a slate for professionals, and it can also be equipped (for a cost) with a neat Nanomatte display technology, which improves visibility outdoors and makes on-screen text look as if it’s sitting on top of the screen.
The Pro tablet market is quite a big one, with slates like the iPad Pro, Samsung Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra, and Huawei MatePad Pro Max all offering impressive features, power, and convenience at huge price tags. Amazon is offering all of those things, too... except the price tag. The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro sells for $499 / £449 (about AU$900) in its 128GB/8GB starter configuration, and $599 / £549 (about AU$1,100) in its 256GB/16GB variant.
That's a much lower price than other Pro tablets I mentioned, undercutting some by as much as half. The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, therefore, is a great budget-friendly alternative to the big dogs.
Now, it won't exactly match those rivals in terms of power — the iPad Pro, for instance, has more video editing power, while the Samsung slate is better for gaming — but it'll be close enough for most people.
Which should you buy?
Now that you know the difference between each Amazon Alexa Tablet, it's time to decide which one would be best suited to you.
The Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is only worth considering if you've got a fair amount of money ready to spend. Not only is it the priciest of the bunch, but it's the one best suited to the stylus and keyboard peripherals (they're only compatible with this model). It's more of a productivity machine.
The Amazon Alexa Tablet 11 is a jack of all trades, master of none. If you want something that's fine for coursework, watching movies in bed, or playing music out loud while you're doing your chores, it's the best pick. If you have one particular job in mind for a tablet, it might not be suitable.
The Amazon Alexa Tablet 8 is only worth picking up if you're deliberately looking for an affordable option. It's good for on-the-go entertainment, whether that's downloading some TV shows or reading with the Kindle app, but you won't have a great time if you try using it for anything more complex.
Since these are first-gen tablets, we don't know if Amazon will continue to flesh out the range, or if this is it. Will there be an Alexa Tablet 8 Pro? Or a Tablet 14, 15, 16, perhaps? No one knows. For now, these are the three models available, and it's not worth considering any prospective additional models when you're making a buying decision.
As mentioned, all of Amazon's new Alexa Tablets are the subject of big Black Friday discounts as we speak, so if you know which one you want, jump on the deals while they last.

articles.title: Dozens of oil and shipping tankers hacked in recent weeks, per report
articles.text:
U.S. officials suspect Iranian hackers may be behind as many as 50 cyberattacks targeting shipping vessels in recent weeks, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal.
The ships carrying oil, liquefied gas, and other explosive chemicals were hacked as they traveled across Asia and Europe. Several oil tankers headed toward the U.S. coast in August also had their navigation systems breached, prompting cybersecurity teams within the FBI and Coast Guard to board the vessels.
The report said officials are investigating if Iran is expanding its recent wave of hacks against the U.S. by targeting large vessels to sow fear among shippers, disrupt routes, or to cause an explosion at a port. (Ships have backup controls in the event that automated systems are hacked or fail.)
Hackers may have been abusing a bug dubbed FortiBleed, which allows hackers to break into networks by compromising vulnerable Fortinet-made routers. A joint FBI-Coast Guard security alert from September warned that Fortinet routers are used on shipping vessels.
Iran has been firing back on all sides since the start of the U.S./Israel-led war earlier this year, which killed the country’s supreme leader. Many of Iran’s retaliations have been in the form of cyberattacks, with U.S. officials blaming Iran for hacks targeting hundreds of American water providers and U.S. medical tech companies.
A spokesperson for the FBI did not respond to a request for comment about the shipping hacks or whether it had a more accurate figure.

articles.title: How to save big on your phone plan this Black Friday
articles.text:
As the holiday season ramps up and Black Friday deals are popping up left and right, it can be helpful to remember that the best deals save you money on things you were going to buy anyway.

articles.title: KI-Nutzung: Sorge vor nicht abschätzbaren Risiken steigt
articles.text:
Boomer holen bei KI-Nutzung auf: Sorge vor nicht abschätzbaren Risiken steigt
Ende November 2022 gelangte ChatGPT auf Basis von GPT-3.5 erstmals ans Licht der Öffentlichkeit und löste einen bis heute anhaltenden Boom bei generativen KI-Tools aus. Innerhalb weniger Tage verzeichnete der KI-Chatbot eine Million Nutzer:innen. Zwei Monate nach dem Start waren es schon 100 Millionen monatlich aktive Nutzer:innen.
81 Prozent nutzen generative KI
Vier Jahre später nutzen rund 1,2 Milliarden Menschen ChatGPT wöchentlich, darunter knapp 45 Millionen Deutsche. Laut einer aktuellen Tüv-Studie nutzen 81 Prozent der Bundesbürger:innen ab 16 Jahren generative KI-Tools – ein Plus von 16 Prozentpunkten gegenüber dem Vorjahr.
76 Prozent der deutschen Nutzer:innen setzen dabei auf ChatGPT. Das bedeutet allerdings einen Rückgang um neun Prozentpunkte im Vergleich zum Vorjahr. Dahinter steckt, dass die wichtigsten Konkurrenten Google Gemini und Anthropics Claude kräftig aufgeholt haben.
ChatGPT vor Gemini und Claude
Geminis Anteil an der KI-Nutzung in Deutschland ist von 33 auf 60 Prozent gestiegen. Claude kommt nach drei Prozent im Jahr 2025 mittlerweile auf 22 Prozent. In den Top-5 der Anwendungen findet sich mit Deepl immerhin ein Anbieter aus Deutschland.
Derweil ist die KI-Nutzung vor allem bei den älteren Menschen stark angestiegen. Den aktuellen Zahlen der Tüv-Studie zufolge verwenden 61 Prozent der Menschen ab 65 Jahren KI-Anwendungen. 2025 waren es nur 35 Prozent.
Immer mehr ältere nutzen KI-Tools
„KI ist längst kein Thema mehr nur für Technikbegeisterte“, erklärt Joachim Bühler, Geschäftsführer des TÜV-Verbands. „Die Anwendungen sind so einfach zugänglich, dass Menschen aller Altersgruppen sie für sich entdecken.“
Die KI nutzen viele Menschen mittlerweile eher als persönlichen Assistenten, denn nur als Suchmaschine. Die Tools werten etwa Dokumente aus, organisieren Fotos oder geben Rat bei persönlichen Fragen.
Trotz Datenschutzbedenken haben 30 Prozent der KI-Nutzer:innen schon persönliche oder vertrauliche Informationen mit einem Tool geteilt. 61 Prozent verzichten aber aus Sorge um persönliche Daten bewusst auf eine Anwendung oder bestimmte Funktionen.
Sorge vor nicht abschätzbaren Risiken
Die deutschen Nutzer:innen treiben aber noch andere Sorgen um. Immer 90 Prozent stimmen laut Tüv der Aussage zu, dass von KI derzeit „nicht abschätzbare Risiken“ ausgehen. Dabei stehen vor allem mögliche Cyberangriffe durch KI im Fokus. Aber auch die Sorge, dass KI-Anbieter einen zu großen Einfluss auf Wirtschaft und Gesellschaft erhalten könnten.
Die überwiegende Mehrheit der Deutschen erwartet sich daher von der Politik mehr Engagement für die KI-Sicherheit. Dazu gehören für die Befragten eine stärkere Kontrolle europäischer Sicherheitsregeln, das Aufstellen gemeinsamer Standards mit Ländern außerhalb der EU, darunter USA und China, sowie unabhängige Prüfungen.

articles.title: Es oficial: ‘Los Anillos de Poder’ tendrá cuarta temporada en Prime Video
articles.text:
Buenas noticias para los fans de El Señor de los Anillos: Amazon ha renovado oficialmente Los Anillos de Poder para una cuarta temporada. El anuncio se da unas pocas horas antes de que la serie de Prime Video estrene los últimos dos capítulos de su temporada 3, que hasta aquí ha recibido muy buenas críticas.
Los detalles de la cuarta temporada de Los Anillos de Poder son todavía escasos, y con razón. Lo que Amazon sí ha confirmado es que el equipo creativo que lideran J.D. Payne y Patrick McKay continuará al frente del proyecto basado en el trabajo literario de J. R. R. Tolkien.
Por lo pronto, Los Anillos de Poder tiene su cuarta temporada en etapa de preproducción. El rodaje se pondrá en marcha durante la primavera de 2027 en Reino Unido, así que todavía quedan varios meses por delante antes de que las cámaras comiencen a grabar en Shepperton Studios.
Amazon confía en seguir explorando la Segunda Edad de la Tierra Media con una siguiente entrega de Los Anillos de Poder. La compañía no indica si el objetivo es concluir la adaptación con la cuarta temporadas, o si está la puerta abierta a la posibilidad de continuar desarrollando tramas en el futuro.
Los Anillos de Poder, confirmada para una cuarta temporada en Prime Video
Por lo pronto, Los Anillos de Poder no tiene fecha de estreno confirmada para su cuarta temporada. Considerando que el rodaje se realizará a partir de la primavera de 2027 y que las primeras tres entregas tuvieron dos años de diferencia entre sí, no es descabellado pensar que llegará hacia finales de 2028. De todas maneras, todavía no hay confirmación oficial por parte de Prime Video.
La atención de los fanáticos hoy está puesta en los últimos dos episodios de la temporada 3 de Los Anillos de Poder, que llegarán a la plataforma esta misma noche. Los mismos mostrarán el momento más esperado por los fanáticos: la forja del tan codiciado Anillo Único. Los episodios estarán disponibles en Prime Video a partir de las 21:00, hora del Este de Estados Unidos. Esto significa que se podrán ver a partir de las 20:00 en México, las 23:00 en Argentina y las 03:00 del 25 de noviembre en España.
Prueba Amazon Prime Video totalmente gratis durante 30 días y disfruta del catálogo completo de la plataforma sin límites. Solo con darte de alta tendrás acceso instantáneo a las mejores películas y series, además de envíos gratis en Amazon y otras ventajas.
Peter Friedlander, jefe de televisión de Amazon MGM Studios, celebró la renovación de Los Anillos de Poder para una cuarta temporada. "El Señor de los Anillos: Los Anillos de Poder se ha convertido en una serie emblemática para Prime Video. Ahora que la tercera temporada nos ofrece el gran acontecimiento que los fans llevaban tanto tiempo esperando —la forja del Anillo Único—, nos enorgullece confirmar la cuarta temporada con J.D. Payne, Patrick McKay y todo el equipo creativo. Estamos deseando sumergir aún más a los espectadores en el fascinante mundo de la Segunda Edad de Tolkien", remarcó.

articles.title: Ist der Anthropic-Boom schon wieder vorbei? Aktie fällt unter den Ausgabepreis
articles.text:
Ist der Anthropic-Boom schon wieder vorbei? Aktie fällt unter den Ausgabepreis
Die Aktie der KI-Firma Anthropic ist wenige Tage nach ihrem Rekord-Börsengang unter den Ausgabepreis gefallen. Im frühen US-Handel notierte sie nach einem Minus von mehr als acht Prozent an der Marke von 80 US-Dollar.
Den Ausgabepreis hatte Anthropic zum Börsendebüt am 19. November auf 83 Dollar festgesetzt – angesichts einer hohen Nachfrage von Interessenten deutlich über der zuvor festgelegten Spanne von 70 bis 78 Dollar. Zudem bot Anthropic mehr als 150 Millionen Aktien mehr zum Kauf an als ursprünglich geplant. Damit machte die KI-Firma richtig Kasse und legte mit einem Erlös von 107,3 Milliarden Dollar den bisher größten Börsengang hin.
Abwärts nach starkem Start
Am ersten Tag schien der Erfolgslauf zunächst weiterzugehen: Der erste Kurs lag mit 111,50 Dollar um 34 Prozent über dem Ausgabepreis. Danach ging es abwärts. Aus dem regulären US-Handel ging das Papier am ersten Tag mit einem Kurs von 97,17 Dollar. Das war immer noch ein Aufschlag von gut 17 Prozent auf den Ausgabepreis.
Schon am 20. November aber waren Technologie-Aktien auf breiter Front unter Druck. Auch die Hoffnung, dass der Anthropic-Börsengang zu einem Stimmungswandel bei KI-Aktien führen könnte, verpuffte damit. Am Markt waren zuletzt abermals Sorgen größer geworden, ob die gewaltigen Investitionen in Rechenzentren für Künstliche Intelligenz zurückverdient werden können. Allein Anthropic veranschlagte für die kommenden Jahre Ausgaben von fast 900 Milliarden Dollar für Rechenleistung.
Huang-Euphorie für KI-Aktien verpufft?
Am 23. November dann sorgte die von Präsident Donald Trump durchgesetzte Rückkehr von Jensen Huang an die Spitze des Chip-Riesen Nvidia für einen Auftrieb bei Tech-Aktien. Doch schon einen Tag später stand der Markt wieder unter Druck.
Bei Anthropic muss man als Investor daran glauben, dass die Zukunftsversprechen aufgehen – denn bisher gibt es vor allem hohe Verluste, wenn auch das Geschäft schnell wächst. Ab dem Börsendebüt konnten zudem auch viele Anthropic-Mitarbeiter Aktien verkaufen. Es ist allerdings unklar, ob das zu der Talfahrt beigetragen haben könnte.

articles.title: Black Friday : votre prochain PC gaming pourrait commencer avec le Ryzen 7 7800X3D à 283,99 € chez Amazon
articles.text:
Avec une remise de 43 % proposée par Amazon à l’occasion du Black Friday, le processeur AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D revient actuellement à 283,99 €. Un prix intéressant pour ce CPU qui optimise les performances en jeu grâce à sa technologie 3D V-Cache.
Flambée des prix des composants oblige, la période actuelle est assez peu propice à l’assemblage d’un nouveau PC gaming. Mais c’est sans compter sur les remises d’Amazon durant le Black Friday. Jusqu’au 30 novembre, le processeur Ryzen 7 7800X3D est proposé à 283,99 € chez le cybermarchand, contre un prix de référence de 496,99 €. Avec ses huit cœurs et ses seize threads, ce CPU est particulièrement adapté à une configuration gaming. Il est conçu pour être installé sur une carte mère AM5 et fonctionne avec de la mémoire DDR5.
Le processeur AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D est à 283,99 € chez Amazon, avec une remise de 43 %.
Pourquoi choisir le Ryzen 7 7800X3D ?
- Pour son cache dédié aux performances en jeu : les 96 Mo de cache L3 peuvent accélérer les jeux gourmands en accès mémoire.
- Pour ses huit cœurs : cette configuration permet aussi de travailler et d’utiliser plusieurs applications au quotidien.
- Pour son efficacité énergétique : notre test a relevé un bon équilibre entre performances en jeu et consommation.
Un processeur au potentiel évident dans les jeux
Notre test du Ryzen 7 7800X3D met notamment en avant le bénéfice de la technologie 3D V-Cache dans les usages gaming. Cela en fait un processeur particulièrement adapté aux joueurs en quête d’une fréquence d’images élevée, à condition de l’associer à une carte graphique adaptée. Le test souligne également l’efficacité énergétique du processeur, ainsi que sa montée en température modérée au regard de ses performances. Il a reçu la note de 8 sur 10.
Un choix orienté gaming plutôt que création intensive
Même si le 7800X3D d’AMD est sorti il y a quelques années déjà, son intérêt dans une configuration gaming est toujours d’actualité. En revanche, si vous désirez réaliser du rendu 3D ou des encodages intensifs, des processeurs dotés de davantage de cœurs peuvent s’avérer plus pertinents.
✅ Les points forts
- Performances en jeu et apport du 3D V-Cache.
- Huit cœurs et seize threads.
- Bonne efficacité énergétique.
❌ Les limites
- Carte mère AM5 et mémoire DDR5 indispensables.
- Système de refroidissement non fourni.
Disponible pour 283,99 € durant le Black Friday d’Amazon, le Ryzen 7 7800X3D peut se faire une place de choix dans une config’ gaming.
Si vous disposez déjà d’une machine AM5 ou que vous êtes en train d’en construire une pour jouer, alors ce processeur AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D peut la compléter de manière efficace.
Pour une utilisation davantage tournée vers la création 3D, il faudra plutôt opter pour un CPU avec davantage de cœurs. De même, pour les usages essentiellement bureautiques, cette puce est sans doute trop puissante, et donc, trop chère.

articles.title: NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; Sarvam unveils upgraded model amid Token Factory row
articles.text:
NVIDIA reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO; Sarvam unveils upgraded model amid Token Factory row
Nvidia has reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as its president, CEO, and board director, less than two weeks after his resignation from the company. In other news, Sarvam’s new AI model promises better performance at a lower cost.
Dear Reader,
In a quick turn of events, Nvidia has reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as its president, CEO, and board director.
This development comes less than two weeks after Huang’s resignation from the company. It follows discussions between Huang and the board, alongside inputs from senior US government officials, the company said.
In other news, Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu has said AI is transforming coding and intellectual work the way mechanisation impacted farming and weaving.
Backing an observation by AI researcher Subbarao Kambhampati, Vembu said, in a post on X, “What happened to farmers and weavers and carpenters and ironsmiths in the waves of mechanization and automation is now starting to happen to mathematicians and programmers.”
Amid the backlash over hosting Chinese models on its Token Factory platform, Sarvam has clarified its AI strategy.
Co-founder Pratyush Kumar said a model’s country of origin and the location of the infrastructure on which it runs are two different matters. He also emphasised that building inference infrastructure does not diminish Sarvam’s core focus on its own models.
The company has released an upgraded model that it says delivers better performance at a lower cost. More on that below.
Meanwhile, the Ministry of Home Affairs has urged users to log out after using WhatsApp Web to prevent account hijacking. An advisory issued by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre says active WhatsApp Web sessions could be misused to access private messages, impersonate users, and carry out cyber fraud.
In today’s newsletter:
- Sarvam’s new AI model promises better performance at lower cost
- Digital Naaris: A network of women micro-entrepreneurs
Here’s your trivia for today: What does ‘dim sum’ mean in English? (Scroll down for the answer)
Artificial Intelligence
Sarvam’s new AI model promises better performance at lower cost
Sarvam AI has released Sarvam-105B-1711, a model designed for businesses handling large volumes of customer queries, phone calls, and software-based tasks. The company says the updated version of its 105B model follows instructions more reliably, uses digital tools better, and handles Indian languages more effectively, all at a lower cost.
The latest release is part of a broader push by Sarvam to build models for different applications. It follows Sarvam Prism, a model designed to make quick, straightforward decisions; Bulbul V4 Flash, which turns written text into natural-sounding speech; and Saaras V4, which converts spoken language into text across 22 Indian languages.
More for less:
- Sarvam-105B-1711 was trained on Nvidia’s Blackwell B200 chips, powerful processors built for AI calculations. The model’s architecture activates only selected parts to generate each response, reducing computing requirements.
- Potential uses include customer-service chatbots, AI voice assistants that speak with callers, and digital assistants that use software to complete tasks.
- Sarvam is making the model’s learned settings, known as ‘weights’, available for download. Businesses with suitable computers can run the model themselves rather than relying entirely on Sarvam’s online service.

How PayNearby is building a network of women micro-entrepreneurs
PayNearby was founded in 2016 to enable neighbourhood stores to offer digital banking and financial services. As its reach expanded over the years, the company noticed that more men were accessing its services than women.
So, in 2024, the fintech platform launched Digital Naari to train women as financial and digital service providers serving other women in their communities. The company says the initiative now reaches women across more than 15,000 pin codes, helping them earn through transaction-based commissions.
Key takeaways:
- A Digital Naari is a banking touchpoint within a community, operated by a woman agent. After training, agents use a mobile phone to provide services such as banking, insurance, credit, bill payments and telehealth.
- PayNearby says about 80% of the women joining the programme are first-time entrepreneurs. Participants include women from low-income households, single mothers and widows supporting their families.
- Digital Naari not only creates an income opportunity for women, it also makes financial services more accessible to other women within their communities.

articles.title: Engineering Around Non-Determinism: Evals, Grounding, and Release Gates for AI-Drafted Suspicious Reports
articles.text:
Key Takeaways
- A drafting agent should refuse to draft when the evidence is missing. Stopping with an explicit "insufficient context" signal is safer than a fluent narrative built around gaps.
- An LLM judge is itself non-deterministic. Freeze its version and pair it with a deterministic fact-checker for names, dates, and amounts.
- Building agentic systems on probabilistic LLMs requires engineering around them: evals, context engineering, observability, regression runs, and human-in-the-loop controls contain the effects of randomness rather than removing it.
- Grounding the system in authoritative case evidence and a knowledge-augmented graph data system helps ensure that every material claim is supported by traceable data.
- Versioned models, prompts, policies, retrieval configurations, and reviewer actions make the system observable, reversible, and suitable for regulated production environments.
Investigative narrative drafting in a financial institution
Financial institutions must investigate potentially suspicious activity and prepare accurate, complete, and timely reports for Financial Intelligence Units. The process is sensitive, labor-intensive, and subject to strict deadlines. This article explains how non-deterministic Artificial Intelligence (AI) components can be incorporated into a dependable agentic system that reduces the cost of doing business, increases drafting and review speed, and maintains the quality of the final report.
What is a Suspicious Activity Report?
A Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) is a formal document submitted by regulated entities and financial institutions to law enforcement or financial intelligence units (such as the UK's National Crime Agency) to flag known or suspected instances of money laundering, fraud, or terrorist financing.
SARs should give a clear and concise explanation of the reason(s) for the suspicion, identifying:
- Who – the identity of the party, or parties involved
- What – the transaction they are involved in
- Where – a description of the criminal property
- How – a description of the prohibited act(s)
- Why – the criminal activity suspected
- When – any critical deadlines
The Inverted Pyramid Plot Model for SAR narratives organizes information from most to least important, much like a news article.
- The narrative opens with the lead, a short summary of the most noteworthy details and the main story event.
- It answers the five W questions: who, what, when, where, and why.
- Next comes the body, a series of crucial details that build up the main story event, supported by evidence, facts, and patterns.
- The narrative closes with the tail, which gives concluding remarks.
Because the structure moves from the broadest, most critical information down to the narrowest, a reader can grasp the core of the case from the opening lines alone and turn to the later sections only for supporting detail.
Risks and cost of non-compliance
- Regulators penalize institutions for systematic data deficiencies, missing narratives, or failing to report suspicious transactions adequately.
- Public enforcement actions can undermine the confidence of investors, business partners, and customers.
- Considering the sensitivity of data and investigations, typically these cases are investigated and reported by in-house employees in a very secure environment. If suspicious activity volumes increase, the cost of investigation and reporting increases as well. For example, If there are 10% of active customers who are detected, investigated, and reported, and each case takes $50 in human labour cost, there is a significant increase in the cost of doing business, which has to be eventually passed back to the customer.
Typical Deterministic System Architecture
In the following system context diagram, a human agent views the investigation notes prepared by another human agent and then drafts the suspicious activity report. Once the report is reviewed by another peer, it is submitted to a financial intelligence unit.
System Context Diagram of Suspicious Activity Reports in a Financial Institution (Source: authors)
In the following diagram, there are 4 key timelines of any investigation:
- Detection: Any suspicious activity is detected either through manual oversight or with the support of machine learning models.
- Investigation: Once suspicious activity is detected, it goes for thorough investigation and peer review to confirm the suspicion.
- Reporting: Any confirmed suspicious activity has to be reported to the national financial intelligence unit within a tight deadline. The report has to be factually correct, and the suspicion has to be clearly articulated.
- Further investigation by the Financial Intelligence Unit: All of these suspicious reported activities by all financial institutions enable the national intelligence unit to understand the complete web of illicit activities and intervene before they become a threat to national or international security.
High-level diagram of a traditional reporting system (Source: authors)
- The quality of the reports is directly proportional to the quality of investigation & editorial style of the human workforce. There is a lack of consistency.
- If there is an increase in suspicious activities, then the manual system can not keep pace with the increase in demand.
- There is a cost to the business and the customer for every suspicious activity investigation and reporting.
Non-Deterministic Agentic System Architecture
We propose improving the traditional reporting system by using AI to automate selected tasks and generate high-quality SAR drafts, followed by specialized human review and minor edits where necessary. The goal is to increase throughput, reduce cost per case, and decrease reporting failures.
In the following system context diagram, human agent effort is shifted to review/edit the AI-assisted report drafting and review.
System Context Diagram of Suspicious Activity Reports in a Financial Institution (Source: authors)
We changed the earlier design to support background automation of suspicious activity report generation. As soon as the investigation is complete, the case is sent to the queue for processing by the Agentic System. Before the human agent picks the case for drafting the report, the AI Agent has drafted the first version to speed up the report generation.
High-level diagram of an AI-powered reporting system (Source: authors)
The non-deterministic nature of AI, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), creates two central concerns:
- High-quality first-attempt drafts require strong control, evaluation, and monitoring of AI components.
- Low-quality drafts create repeated draft-and-review cycles and additional human editing, increasing the cost per report.
Multi-agent system for report generation
The proposed solution is a multi-agent system, with access to selected LLMs via a gateway, and supported by a tailored knowledge graph built from operational data.
Grounding is the foundation of trustworthy SAR generation. The system should make it easier to state only what the evidence supports, not merely make the prose more fluent.
High-level diagram of the agentic system (Source: authors)
- Preprocessed Event Plot Knowledge Graph: All the data is already tagged and collected by previous processes. There is an Event Plot Knowledge Graph already generated as part of detection and investigation.
- Data Query Planner Agent: fetches the quality data required to generate the report. If the data is not present, then we stop the agentic automation and give feedback to the user that Agents cannot generate the report as the data is not present.
- Data Reranker Agent: takes the data returned by Data Query Planner and re-ranks the data to ensure that data is relevant to the context.
- Drafter Agent: specialized agents produce a narrative from factual data, against a defined SAR schema, and cite supporting source identifiers.
- Judge Agent: deterministic checks and an independent judge assess factuality, completeness, consistency, and style.
- Coordinator Agent: Once the quality of the generated report is of decent standard, then the report is published for human review.
- Since the investigation of the network is already done, there is no need for community detection. Hence, the GraphRAG approach is not considered.
- We also need to ensure that security and privacy concerns of the cases are under consideration; hence, data is carefully labelled and collected.
- All the real-time updates are present in operational databases, which can be fetched by the agents if there are some updates for a particular user profile or transaction.
- Knowledge Graph of main and associate suspects are generated at a regular cadence through data pipeline jobs.
- If a case is investigated and reported, then data needs to be retained as per data retention policies of the jurisdiction.
Sequence diagram of Drafter agent, Judge Agent and Human (Source: authors)
High-quality report generation with Evals
Quality means more than well-written prose. It means a complete, internally consistent, reviewable narrative that meets institutional and jurisdictional requirements.
- Completeness against the required SAR narrative fields.
- Consistency across names, dates, amounts, accounts, locations, and transaction sequences.
- Clear separation of observed facts, analysis, and unresolved uncertainty.
- Appropriate tone and terminology without overstatement or unsupported conclusions.
- Traceable provenance for material statements and reviewer edits.
Unlike traditional software, LLM outputs are non-deterministic, and "quality" is subjective. In the case of report writing, "what does a good report look like?" becomes more subjective. Hence, there is a need to test the "subjective" aspects against "objective" metrics, and here the Eval shines.
Evals are like tests of regular software development practices, and they can be leveraged in the following processes:
- Initial development of the system
- Updates to the system when there is a change in the requirements
- Updates in the models
- Regular run on some percentage of production spans to assess overall drift in quality
- Any new release in any aspect of the AI system has to be gated with the Evals suite
Eval Creation
There are a few broad focus areas where the model output has to be tested on a continuous basis:
- Instruction following capability
- Generation capability
- Narrative-specific correctness
For example, Evals can be written to assess different aspects of the generated narrative like:
- Factual accuracy of the narrative
- Factual completeness of the narrative
- Name identification
- Timeframe of events
- Narrative follows the Inverted Pyramid Plot structure
- Narrative Articulation
- Narrative Coherence
- Narrative tone
- ..etc.
Sample Eval can look like this:
Sample Eval (Source: authors)
Once we have scores from all the evals, either we can use a weighted average or a simple average of all the individual scores to figure out the final grading criteria. This is how the Evals can be leveraged to grade the quality of generated output
Sequence diagram of Evals grading (Source: authors)
Regression Evals with Golden Data Set
Since the model and prompt are bound to change, this adds another dimension of non-determinism to the system. With any production system, we need to have a regression run of all evals against the golden data set before any model upgrade or prompt/config change happens.
The golden data set has to be collected initially with different edge cases with defined input and output. This will help in testing the system during development. The Golden Data Set can be augmented with human feedback in production where they love the output generated by the AI system.
Evals shall answer some of the generated report’s quality metrics like :
- Did the system provide a factually correct answer?
- Was the summary faithful to the source?
- Was the final response actually helpful to the user?
System Behavior observability
Traditional testing is a deterministic process of verification - it asks, "Did we build the product right?" against a fixed specification. This approach fails when a system’s core logic is probabilistic, because non-deterministic output may be more likely to introduce subtle degradations of quality that do not result in explicit crashes and may not be repeatable. Hence, it is important to monitor the decision-making trajectory, from initial intent to final outcome.
- LLM Model: We first check the core reasoning. Is the LLM Model itself the problem? Failures here include hallucinations, nonsensical or off-topic responses.
- RAG Performance: The response depends on the quality of its retrieved information. Failures include irrelevant document retrieval, fetching outdated or incorrect information, or the LLM ignoring the retrieved context entirely and hallucinating an answer anyway.
- System Failures: What happens when the Model is not able to find the right context or data? Does it make things up or throw the error? What happens when the underlying system is unavailable?
The system is gradually improved by generating telemetry, understanding the system, and patching the underlying issues.
Human-in-The-Loop Control
Human review remains a policy decision owned by the BSA/AML function. AI accelerates preparation; it does not replace accountable judgment.
- Risk-tiered routing: low-risk, familiar typologies may use sampling or streamlined review; novel, high-risk, multilingual, or low-confidence cases default to full review.
- Reviewer experience: show evidence beside each material claim, highlight uncertainty, and make changes explainable rather than forcing reviewers to rewrite from scratch.
- Review quality: evaluate human edits as well as AI output so reviewers correct errors without introducing unsupported statements.
- Accountability: the designated BSA/AML officer retains responsibility for filing decisions and approved risk thresholds.
Release Process
Treat models and prompts as regulated production changes. The release plane provides controlled progress rather than "ship and hope."
- Version: register the model, prompts, retrieval logic, data mappings, policies, and eval set with an owner and change rationale.
- Test: run deterministic factuality checks, rubric scoring, security and privacy checks, and jurisdiction-specific regression suites.
- Gate: require approval from engineering, Compliance/AML, Risk, and Legal according to the change type.
- Shadow and canary: compare the candidate with the incumbent before increasing traffic.
- Monitor: track factuality pass rate, judge scores, reviewer edit rate, latency, queue age, and escalation volume.
- Rollback: use configuration-based feature flags to revert to the previous model, stricter review, or full human drafting when thresholds are breached.
Engineering Trust Into AI-Drafted SARs
The bottleneck in drafting a quality Suspicious Activity Report was qualified personnel. LLM-based systems can reduce that dependency, but only if they're engineered for it, with grounding and evals as the substitute for the judgment of a qualified investigator.
The mechanism we've described treats non-determinism as an engineering problem rather than an excuse. Grounding drafts in a case-specific knowledge graph and operational data keeps the Drafter Agent grounded in evidence. A Judge Agent and deterministic fact-checker turn "does this read well?" into measurable checks against factuality, completeness, and the Inverted Pyramid structure the FIU expects. Evals and a golden dataset give these subjective judgments an objective, regression-testable backbone, the same way unit tests do for deterministic code. And a release process that versions models, prompts, and configuration, gated with shadow/canary rollout and feature-flag rollback, treats every change to the system as a production release
None of this shifts accountability away from the humans who own it. The BSA/AML officer still decides what gets filed; the agentic system's job is to make sure that when a human reviews a draft, the evidence is already assembled, the uncertain claims are flagged, and the reviewer's time goes to judgment rather than transcription. Risk-tiered routing means the system earns trust on familiar, low-risk cases before it is ever allowed near the ones that matter most.
SAR narratives can now be drafted at machine speed, by codifying what "good" looks like into evals a machine can check against. When a human reviews the output, they're not taking the narrative on faith; they can trace the reasoning and the evidence lineage behind it, and that traceability is what turns speed into trust.

articles.title: Mario, español viviendo en Australia: “Tardo 4 horas de trabajo en cubrir el alquiler de un mes”
articles.text:
Mario lleva más de un lustro viviendo en Australia trabajando en diferentes campañas agrícolas, pero hay una con la que gana muchísimo dinero: la temporada del algodón. El joven español (conocido en TikTok como @lega.wave) contó que llega a cobrar unos 85 dólares australianos por hora de media, una cantidad que le ayuda a pagar el alquiler mensual con solo cuatro horas de trabajo.
En un vídeo del que se hizo eco Infobae, Mario revela que vive en una zona rural con gastos relativamente bajos: 140 dólares semanales por el alojamiento, 90 por la comida y unos 20 en gasolina. Es decir, cubre sus necesidades básicas con 250 dólares y media jornada de trabajo, algo impensable en países como España.
Trabaja casi toda la semana, pero consigue ahorrar buena parte del sueldo
Y aunque sus gastos estén cubiertos en unas pocas horas, Mario no dedica el resto de la semana a descansar. De hecho, reconoce que durante estas campañas trabaja prácticamente todos los días y que el esfuerzo físico es considerable. «Trabajo como un esclavo», comenta al hablar de unas jornadas que le permiten acumular dinero para sus proyectos y futuros viajes.
La temporada del algodón puede ocupar varios meses del año, y es precisamente en ese periodo cuando el joven intenta aprovechar al máximo sus ingresos. Su idea es sencilla: gastar lo menos posible mientras dura el trabajo y guardar buena parte de lo que cobra. Eso sí, el propio Mario reconoce que detrás de esos ahorros hay jornadas agotadoras, muy alejadas de unas vacaciones en Australia.
Hay una cifra de su relato que, sin embargo, no termina de cuadrar. Si realmente cobra 85 dólares por hora y paga 140 semanales de alquiler, necesitaría unas seis horas y media de trabajo bruto para cubrir cuatro semanas, no cuatro. Además, esas cuentas no descuentan impuestos. En cualquier caso, el joven sostiene que las campañas agrícolas le permiten ahorrar una cantidad considerable a cambio de dedicar prácticamente todo su tiempo al trabajo.

articles.title: New Inception extortion gang launches large-scale vishing campaign
articles.text:
A newly formed data extortion group named ‘Inception’ has been linked to a large-scale campaign that targets single sign-on (SSO) credentials of multiple global brands and firms.
The gang surfaced on November 17, claiming seven victims on its extortion site, including chip maker AMD, PepsiCo, Cigna Healthcare, AutoZone, and Lucid Motors, but none of them have publicly confirmed a data breach.
However, cybersecurity company ReversingLabs has been tracking Inception gang's activity and says that it has been operating since late October.
The security firm has confirmed the existence of 21 domains used for SSO phishing, 41 domains believed to be used in campaign infrastructure, and 4 other domains with suspected use.
The researchers identified an extensive phishing infrastructure impersonating dozens of major corporations, including Dropbox, Duolingo, Western Union, Indeed, Activision Blizzard, Riot Games, Twitch, Reddit, Nestlé, Anthropic, Nintendo, Starbucks, McDonald's, Paramount, and NBCUniversal.
The existence of these domains is not proof that those firms have been breached, or even targeted yet, and none have recently disclosed cyberattacks or other related incidents.
The campaign appears to rely on phone-based social engineering rather than email phishing, strongly resembling the tactics used by the infamous ShinyHunters extortion group.
Inception is using legal-themed websites that imitate corporate authentication services, primarily Okta but also NetIQ/OpenText Access Manager.
ShinyHunters link and denial
One of those authentication providers, Okta, published a report yesterday linking Inception to O-UNC-053, a threat cluster it previously associated with ShinyHunters, which has been active since March.
According to Okta, after law enforcement disrupted the ShinyHunters extortion group following the arrest of suspected members [1, 2], and the shutdown of the leak site, O-UNC-053 continued to register new phishing domains.
In late October, the activity cluster launched its legal-themed campaign, and in mid-November, the Inception leak site went live, announcing victims that matched previous targeting.
“This gap in publishing on any leak site followed by publishing on a new data leak site with a new brand is consistent with prior shifts from Com-affiliated actors,” describes Okta.
“Before and after the change in DLS publication, O-UNC-053 maintained consistent infrastructure and TTPs, leading us to assess that the cluster has very likely changed their brand affiliation.”
Inception was quick to respond and dispute the alleged links to other threat actors in an announcement on their extortion page.
The threat actors claimed to operate independently and with no affiliation to any previous group, arguing that overlapping targets and the use of common domain registration and CDN services did not establish operational links.
They also acknowledged that private tooling is circulating among independent threat actors, and using it does not prove affiliation.
To defend against the latest Inception campaign, ReversingLabs recommends enforcing phishing-resistant authentication, including FIDO2 security keys and passkeys, and strengthening help desk identity verification procedures.
DNS, proxy, and identity provider logs dating back to October 21, 2026, should be carefully reviewed for signs of suspicious activity.

articles.title: El resurgir de Jensen Huang en Nvidia con apoyo de Trump tiene un precio: a China no le van a pasar ni una
articles.text:
Nvidia ha repuesto a Jensen Huang como consejero delegado apenas once días después de su dimisión, y todo tras una intervención directa de Donald Trump que no tardó en atribuirse la decisión (desde el primer día fue muy vocal). Su vuelta ha disparado las acciones de Nvidia, pero no todos parecen estar contentos porque también coincide con el momento en el que Washington estudia limitar aún más la venta de chips de Nvidia a China.
Y no sólo buscan frenar la evolución de la IA china, sino toda su tecnología: la de consumo, la de los coches y la de los robots humanoides.
Vaya viaje, niño. Es complicado no haber seguido el hilo de la historia, pero por si lo necesitas, ayer publicamos una cronología de todo el lío de Jensen Huang y Nvidia. Aunque, para líos, los que ha tenido él no sólo con la supuesta espía china, sino con varias empleadas de Nvidia (y cada día más), hecho que llevó a su dimisión el pasado 12 de noviembre.
Sin embargo, este lunes 23, la junta de Nvidia lo readmitió. La compañía dijo que lo hacía tras recibir aportaciones de altos niveles del Gobierno de Estados Unidos y, como digo, Trump salió a la palestra a decir que había sido gracias a él al no ver en Huang una amenaza para la seguridad nacional. The Washington Post va más allá, afirmando que Trump orquestó personalmente la operación.
Nvidia en China. De la manera que sea, Huang vuelve a ocupar el trono de la compañía que es la columna vertebral de la IA y ahora toca preguntarse... qué va a pasar en China. El motivo es que Huang es una pieza clave para la IA china sin poder ser, oficialmente, una pieza clave para la IA china. Me explico: Nvidia no vende en China sus procesadores más potentes, ya que esos están vetados por la guerra comercial y tecnológica que mantienen ambos países.
Lo que pueden vender es gamas inferiores o recortadas como GPUs para ordenadores de juego, PCs profesionales, chips para robótica y otros como los H20 que pueden usarse tanto para entrenar como para ejecutar modelos de IA. Sin embargo, y más allá del asunto del contrabando y de que los chips más potentes sí han terminado llegando a China, está el hecho de que Huang se tiró meses intentando convencer a Trump de que le dejaran vender los H200.
Estos H200 no son los chips punteros de Nvidia para la IA, ya que esos son exclusivos para los socios estadounidenses, pero sí una plataforma muy capaz que era de las que estaba vetada en China y que, por la insistencia del mandamás de Nvidia, Trump accedió a vender en el gigante asiático. La lógica era impepinable: China va a llegar en algún momento a tener chips similares, así que lo mejor es vendérselos directamente para ganar dinero y, además, hacer que sigan dependiendo de tu tecnología.
Lupa. El problema viene cuando llevamos años de restricciones y, realmente, no se ha vigilado prácticamente nada, o eso consideran algunos en Estados Unidos. En la cúpula del Gobierno se han mantenido dos velocidades estos últimos meses. Por un lado, los que abogaban por seguir vendiendo a China para lo mencionado: que China dependa de tecnología estadounidense a la vez que empresas de EEUU se llevan un buen dinero. Por otro, los que querían cerrar el grifo directamente para no beneficiar a las tecnológicas chinas ni un poco.
Durante los escándalos de Huang, el Departamento de Comercio dio un paso para regular de una mejor forma hacia dónde van los chips. Hasta ahora, parecía que las propias empresas que vendían los chips tenían que cerciorarse de que sus chips llegaban al destino adecuado. Eso abría el agujero de que se podían vender a Singapur o Malasia, pero luego los chips podían terminar llegando a China. Además, las empresas chinas no podían comprar chips directamente, pero sí alquilar computación en la nube a las neoclouds.
Con la nueva regla entre manos se busca que esas restricciones de acceso no puedan eludirse, ya que el propio Gobierno va a estar mucho más encima.
Problemas. De hecho, y como publicó mi compañera Laura hace unas horas, el propio Departamento de Comercio de EEUU ha dado un golpe más a China al endurecer los mecanismos de control sobre circuitos integrados más antiguos que se seguían usando en dispositivos como móviles, coches o electrodomésticos, entre otros. Esos chips maduros son esenciales para la industria tecnológica china, y EEUU acaba de poner un palo en las ruedas de la bici.
Todo esto ya está teniendo consecuencias en la industria china. Como leemos en Reuters, hay clientes que han comenzado a cancelar pedidos de una GPU muy concreta: la RTX Pro 5500. Se trata de una GPU diseñada para ordenadores profesionales, pero puede ejecutar modelos de IA y, aunque no está vetada, hay quien asume que lo estará en algún momento y no quieren que el dinero y los pedidos se queden en el limbo.
Hay un temor, según las fuentes de Reuters, de que ese mayor escrutinio se extienda a las ventas legales de chips de Nvidia. Antes de la salida de Huang, esas empresas chinas pidieron más de seis millones de RTX Pro 5500 por valor de unos 70.000 millones de dólares, siendo ByteDance, Alibaba y Tencent los tres máximos compradores. Con la salida de Huang, esos clientes frenaron o cancelaron los pedidos por si la tarjeta no podía entrar en el país.
Reacciones. Dos días después de que la Cámara de Comercio hiciera públicos sus planes, Tencent comentó que la norma tiene el potencial como para hacer retroceder a todos en China debido a que el proceso de entrenamiento de sus próximos modelos se verán afectados.
Huang ligado a la Casa Blanca. Pero claro, que ahora Huang haya vuelto (y por la puerta grande) no implica que la situación vuelva a ser la que era. Estados Unidos parece que se va a poner las pilas con los controles de exportación tanto a China como a Singapur, Malasia, Tailandia, Indonesia o Brasil y se estima que el Congreso empezará a presionar de forma más activa para que se cierre el grifo tras dos años de supervisión casi nula.
Lo que parece claro es que Nvidia, ese pegamento de la industria de la IA, va a estar algo más controlado porque el apoyo de Trump implica que Huang está mucho más ligado a la Casa Blanca y no se puede dar ni un traspiés más, sobre todo en un clima político en el que el Congreso tendrá mayoría demócrata en enero.
Si Jensen ya era una pieza política antes, ahora lo es aún más. Sólo queda ver cómo evoluciona la industria china y si sus alternativas patrias (Cambricon y Huawei) dan con la tecla para llenar ese posible hueco de Nvidia. Y el problema no es tanto tecnológico como de producción: no dan abasto.

articles.title: Ne plus dépendre de la Chine : la France veut ses propres « stocks stratégiques » de terres rares et de métaux
articles.text:
Ce 23 novembre, Le Figaro révélait un projet d’Emmanuel Macron sur les stocks stratégiques de métaux critiques. Dans la foulée, l’Elysée l’a confirmé à l’AFP, comme l’a rapporté Le Monde : Emmanuel Macron a annoncé ce projet lors d’une table ronde à huis clos avec certains industriels français. En clair, le président de la République souhaite lancer un projet de création de stocks stratégiques de certaines terres et métaux destinés aux industriels français pour réduire leur dépendance, notamment face à la Chine.
Des stocks stratégiques d’une vingtaine de matières premières pour soutenir l’industrie française
Aujourd’hui, la France a des stocks de pétrole pour pallier à des crises pétrolières, par exemple si l’approvisionnement depuis l’étranger n’est plus possible. Face à la hausse de prix du carburant, une partie a d’ailleurs été utilisée pour être injectée dans le marché français ce mois-ci. Emmanuel Macron a lancé hier un projet de stocks similaire, mais pour une vingtaine de matières premières. Elle fait partie de la liste des 34 matières premières critiques de la liste dressée par l’Union européenne. Ces métaux, terres et minéraux sont considérés comme essentiel par l’UE afin d’atteindre ses objectifs « en matière d’énergies renouvelables, de numérique, d’espace et de défense ». Il va de pair avec un autre projet lancé en mai dernier par Bercy, visant à relocaliser la production de métaux rares en France.
Géré par la Caisse des dépôts, ce projet a pour mission d’avoir des réserves opérationnelles dès l’année prochaine. La Caisse va donc consulter les industriels français de différents secteurs stratégiques qui ont besoin de ces matières. En plus de ces stocks, l’Elysée a indiqué qu’il y aurait un mécanisme d’achats mutualisés entre ces industriels ; on imagine que cela faciliterait les signatures de contrat et les livraisons.
La présidence ajoute que des « mécanismes de garanties de prix » sont également prévus afin de « donner de la visibilité aux producteurs et mobiliser davantage [les] outils d’investissement ». Elle en appelle d’ailleurs à la Commission européenne à faire de même. En effet, l’Union européenne est forcée de passer des accords avec la Chine, ce qui ne se passe pas toujours sans encombres.
Dans le même temps, Emmanuel Macron a annoncé renforcer le « conditionnement » des aides publiques sur les secteurs de la défense, de l’aéronautique et de l’automobile. Les entreprises affiliées devront « diversifier leurs sources d’approvisionnement en minerais stratégiques pour continuer à en bénéficier », écrit l’AFP. L’objectif pour le président de la République est de réduire leur dépendance, notamment vis-à-vis de la Chine. Pour continuer à bénéficier de certaines aides, les sociétés concernées devront monter un « plan de désensibilisation » le plus vite possible.
L’élection présidentielle va-t-elle mettre à mal ce projet ?
Il reste des imprécisions par rapport à ce projet de stocks stratégiques. Tout d’abord, le calendrier : il n’a pas été précisé. On sait seulement que l’objectif est d’avoir de premières réserves en 2027. Mais c’est aussi cette année que va se dérouler l’élection présidentielle, dont la campagne a déjà débuté. Le ou la futur(e) président(e) de la République pourrait l’enterrer ou le renforcer, selon ses envies.
L’AFP précise qu’au moins Jean-Luc Mélenchon de La France Insoumise a un projet de tels stocks dans son programme. Qui dit nouveau président de la République dit aussi nouveau budget de l’État : selon les sensibilités des candidats l’élu(e) pourrait bien mettre fin à ce projet dans l’idée de faire des économies. Le projet est lancé, mais son avenir reste incertain en raison du contexte politique.

articles.title: Asus could go back to 8GB of RAM in entry-level and mid-range PCs as memory prices soar
articles.text:
Facepalm: With memory prices continuing to track upward, Asus is reportedly considering reducing the amount of RAM in some of its mid-range laptops from 16GB to 8GB. Explaining the potential move, Asus co-CEO S.Y. Hsu said that the rising prices have reached an inflection point where the company can no longer afford to pass all additional costs on to buyers without potentially losing customers.
Talking to investors at Asus' Q3 2026 earnings call, Hsu said that the company is likely to "adjust the memory configuration" in its entry-level and mid-range PCs to 8GB following the latest Windows 11 update, which Microsoft promises will make the operating system faster and more responsive on devices with just 8GB of RAM.
Hsu claimed that Asus worked closely with Microsoft on memory optimization in Windows 11 and that the changes implemented in the new build work as advertised. He added that 16GB had become the default memory standard on Windows devices to ensure a lag-free user experience, but the "adjustments" in the updated build ensure that even 8GB offers an "acceptable" experience.
Hsu's statement comes just weeks after Microsoft released Windows 11 26H2 with a series of optimizations aimed at improving performance on PCs with just 8GB of memory. Pavan Davuluri, Microsoft's EVP of Windows and Devices, claimed that the changes will make Windows up to 20% more responsive and boost multitasking performance by up to 40% on devices with 8GB of RAM.
Redmond, however, acknowledged that Windows 11 PCs with 16GB or 32GB of RAM will still be better at gaming and multitasking, but added that 8GB PCs will help users "do more" without a noticeable drop in performance. That said, the data shared by Microsoft comes from its own lab tests under controlled conditions, so don't expect as much of a performance boost in real-world use cases.
It is worth noting that in May 2026, Microsoft actually raised the recommended memory configuration for Windows 11 devices from 16GB to 32GB. However, faced with skyrocketing memory prices, the company removed that recommendation shortly afterward and pushed out the latest update designed to improve memory usage in Windows 11 devices.

articles.title: The Role of Edge AI and Robotics in Autonomous Agriculture
articles.text:
Over the past decade, agricultural digitalization has improved how farmers monitor crops, soil conditions, weather, and equipment performance. Satellites, drones, connected machinery, and ground-based sensors now provide increasingly detailed information about farming operations. With advances in AI, embedded computing, and robotics, this information is also being used to control agricultural equipment directly, supporting a move from precision agriculture toward more autonomous farming.
Agricultural sensing moves to finer spatial resolution
Modern agricultural equipment integrates a broader range of sensing technologies. RGB cameras can identify crops, weeds, and obstacles. Thermal imaging can detect variations in temperature and moisture. Multispectral and hyperspectral imaging can assess vegetation health, nutrient status, and certain disease indicators. LiDAR and radar provide additional information on terrain, distance, and surrounding obstacles. As these technologies mature, the spatial scale of agricultural decision-making continues to shrink. Management that was once applied at field level increasingly targets individual crop rows, square meters, and, in some applications, individual plants.
This level of granularity places greater demands on embedded computing and actuator control. Cameras must continuously capture images as machinery moves, while AI models identify plant type, position, and condition within a short processing window and pass the results directly to nozzles, mechanical tools, or other actuators. Precision spraying already demonstrates this approach. Vision systems can identify individual weeds and activate selected nozzles for localized treatment, and commercial systems have already been deployed across millions of acres. As camera counts, image resolution, and the number of recognized classes continue to increase, agricultural sensing is moving toward a tighter sensor-to-compute-to-actuator loop.
Edge AI enables onboard decision-making
The increasing volume of sensor data drives greater adoption of onboard computing. Cloud platforms remain important for farm management, historical analysis, and model training, but many agricultural operations require decisions to be made immediately. Connectivity can also be limited in remote farming areas, making continuous dependence on cloud processing impractical.
Edge AI allows agricultural machinery to process sensor information locally and respond directly to its surroundings. This is particularly important for applications such as obstacle detection, autonomous navigation, precision spraying, and robotic harvesting, in which delays between perception and physical action can affect performance.
The electronic architecture of advanced agricultural machinery increasingly shares characteristics with autonomous vehicles. Both require onboard systems for localization, environmental perception, path planning, and motion control. Agricultural equipment also needs to recognize task-specific information, such as crop type, fruit maturity, and the position of weeds, before controlling implements such as sprayers, cutting tools, or robotic arms.
As these functions become more sophisticated, computing performance, energy efficiency, and thermal management will become increasingly important. Cloud-based services will continue to support software updates, fleet management, and longer-term optimization, while time-sensitive control functions will remain on the machine.
Autonomous agricultural machinery combines navigation and task execution
Autonomous tractors and agricultural robots integrate larger and more diverse sensor suites. Multicamera systems can provide nearly 360° coverage, while LiDAR and radar can supplement vision in orchards, vineyards, and other environments where dense vegetation creates more severe occlusion. RTK GNSS remains an important foundation for agricultural guidance and automated driving, but tree cover, complex terrain, multipath effects, and temporary signal degradation can affect positioning stability. IMUs, inertial navigation systems, wheel odometry, visual odometry, and other localization technologies are therefore used to improve robustness.
Sensors also become increasingly integrated into the agricultural task itself. Some precision weeding systems use dozens of cameras across a wide working width to continuously classify large numbers of plants and directly support spraying, laser-based weeding, or mechanical removal. Agricultural sensor suites therefore serve two closely related functions. One supports the autonomous operation of the machine, including localization, navigation, obstacle detection, and path planning. The other supports the agricultural task, including plant identification, disease detection, maturity assessment, spraying control, and manipulation. Higher levels of autonomy require these two layers to operate within a unified or highly coordinated computing architecture.
Quantum sensing offers longer-term opportunities
Quantum sensing emerges as a longer-term technology direction for agriculture. A growing body of research explores potential applications in soil nutrients, fertilizer management, trace chemical detection, pollutants, microorganisms, and plant physiological monitoring. Relevant technologies include quantum magnetic sensing, quantum imaging and spectroscopy, and other high-sensitivity devices based on atomic systems or solid-state platforms, such as nitrogen-vacancy centers in diamond. These technologies can enable more sensitive measurement of magnetic fields, optical signals, chemical composition, and other weak physical signals undetectable to incumbent sensors.
In agricultural applications, higher-sensitivity detection could support more detailed monitoring of soil nutrients and moisture, as well as improved detection of plant physiological changes, photosynthetic activity, and early stress signals. Quantum sensing could also support food safety and agricultural biological monitoring through the detection of low-concentration contaminants, pathogens, and microbial activity. With most of the work in the field still in R&D, deployment remains at an early stage. The future progress of quantum sensors in agriculture will depend heavily on improvements in cost, size, power consumption, durability, and the ability to operate reliably in outdoor agricultural environments.
Agricultural autonomous systems require a distinct safety architecture
Agricultural autonomy operates within a very different environment from autonomous passenger vehicles on urban roads and highways. Farms, orchards, and other agricultural environments often lack clear road boundaries and can involve substantial terrain variation. Workers, animals, irrigation equipment, utility poles, other machinery, and temporary obstacles can all enter the operating area. Dust, mud, rain, fog, strong sunlight, and vegetation can reduce the performance of cameras and other optical sensors, while complex terrain and tree coverage can also reduce GNSS positioning stability.
Autonomous tractors and agricultural robots therefore require robust redundant perception and clearly defined operational design domains. GNSS provides absolute positioning; vision systems support scene and object recognition; IMUs and inertial navigation provide continuous motion information; and LiDAR and radar contribute range and obstacle data. Systems also need clearly defined geographic areas, terrain conditions, weather limits, task types, and operating speeds. Field boundaries, permitted working areas, and restricted zones need to be identified consistently. Remote supervision is also likely to remain part of the architecture for some time, allowing one operator to oversee a larger fleet and intervene primarily when abnormal conditions occur.
Agricultural automation and resource efficiency
The commercial value of agricultural automation is closely linked to labor productivity, resource efficiency, and equipment utilization. Farmers must consider machinery investment, maintenance, energy consumption, and the potential savings from reducing agricultural inputs.
Precision spraying and automated weeding already illustrate how advanced electronics can improve resource efficiency. By identifying individual weeds and applying treatment only where needed, these systems can reduce unnecessary herbicide application. Similar approaches could support more targeted fertilization, irrigation, and crop care.
Autonomous machinery could also change how agricultural fleets are organized. Smaller robotic platforms may be deployed in groups to perform selected tasks, potentially reducing reliance on large, conventional machines. Lightweight equipment can also help limit soil compaction in applications in which machine weight is an important consideration.
However, the economic benefits will vary across farming operations. Equipment utilization, field size, crop type, seasonal workloads, and the cost of human supervision will all influence return on investment. Autonomous systems that operate reliably over longer periods and perform multiple useful tasks are likely to offer stronger commercial opportunities.
Outlook
IDTechEx continues to track the development of autonomous agricultural technologies, including sensing, embedded computing, robotics, enabling components, supply chain development, and the evolving regulatory environment. Current technology and commercial activity suggest that applications with clear economic value, well-defined operating boundaries, and relatively repetitive tasks will continue to lead deployment.
The next stage of technology development is expected to move toward tasks with higher operational complexity, including more flexible manipulation, autonomous decision-making in less structured environments, coordination between multiple machines, and longer periods of unattended operation. These applications will place greater demands on perception, embedded computing, control, safety validation, and the ability to reuse capabilities across different crops, machines, and environments. As these capabilities mature, agricultural automation will extend further into tasks that have traditionally required a higher degree of human involvement.

articles.title: Rockstar lanzó el primer parche de GTA VI para corregir cierres inesperados y fallas de guardado
articles.text:
Rockstar Games publicó el 23 de noviembre el primer parche de Grand Theft Auto VI desde su estreno, el 19 de noviembre. La actualización, disponible en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S, soluciona siete fallas, entre ellas varios cierres inesperados del juego y un autoguardado que no funcionaba bien.
Las notas figuran en la página de soporte de Rockstar, bajo el título “Launch Updates” (actualizaciones de lanzamiento). La compañía enumera las correcciones sin describir cada error ni explicar cómo se producía.
Según esa lista, el parche corrigió varios problemas que provocaban cierres del juego y un error que impedía que el clima cambiara durante largos períodos. También solucionó fallas en el autoguardado.
Otras tres correcciones afectan al desarrollo de la partida. Rockstar arregló llamadas telefónicas que no se activaban, incluidas las que hacían avanzar la historia o desbloqueaban misiones, y un error que impedía a los jugadores perder el nivel de búsqueda de la policía.
Los últimos dos arreglos son más puntuales: la barra de pesas del gimnasio, que no se podía usar, y los socios que no entregaban las bolsas que el jugador debía vender a los receptadores.
Una versión menor, con detalles sin aclarar
El parche corresponde a la versión 01.002.002 en PS5 y 1.0.2.2 en Xbox, según RockstarINTEL. Digital Foundry lo calificó como una actualización menor y señaló que pesa 602 MB en PS5. RockstarINTEL informó que en Xbox Series X|S ocupa 1,6 GB y que el tamaño total del juego instalado no aumentó.
William Judd, de Digital Foundry, contó que sufrió un cierre del juego en los primeros 15 minutos de partida. También observó semáforos que permanecían en rojo durante varios minutos. Dijo que no sabe si el parche resolvió esos problemas.
Digital Foundry añadió que tampoco está claro si la actualización corrige los errores que permiten obtener dinero de forma indebida ni el viñeteado más pronunciado de lo esperado, que desarrolladores de Rockstar mencionaron en entrevistas cercanas al lanzamiento. RockstarINTEL indicó que el parche no resuelve un fallo que permite jugar a 60 cuadros por segundo en Xbox.
El autoguardado, en el centro de las quejas de la semana
El sitio Notebookcheck informó el 19 de noviembre de que algunos jugadores de PS5 y Xbox perdieron horas de progreso tras cierres del juego, pese al sistema de guardado automático. Según Tech Times, el streamer JasonTheWeen perdió unas 10 horas, aunque no se sabe si su consola falló o se apagó por accidente.
Tech Times señaló que Rockstar no vincula la corrección con esos reportes y que sus notas no permiten saber si el error solucionado es el mismo. Notebookcheck e Insider Gaming recomiendan, mientras tanto, usar los guardados manuales, de los cuales el juego ofrece 15 espacios.
Distribución por tandas y dos parches previos sin notas
Tech Times informó que la actualización llegó por oleadas. Wccftech, que cita un seguimiento publicado en X, mencionó tres etapas: cerca del 33% de los jugadores al inicio, otro tramo a las tres horas y el resto a las seis. Rockstar no confirmó ese cronograma. Quien no vea la descarga puede abrir el juego en PS5, pulsar Options y elegir buscar actualización.
Antes de este parche, Tech Times registra otras dos actualizaciones sin notas públicas: la 01.002.000, del 13 de noviembre, y la 01.002.001, del 16 de noviembre. La página de soporte de Rockstar solo contiene por ahora la entrada del 23 de noviembre.

articles.title: Porsche 718 Boxster prototype drive: This electric roadster is real
articles.text:
It wasn’t until I was stuck in traffic on the way back from a run up and down some canyon roads that I realized just how low Porsche’s upcoming all-electric 718 Boxster truly is. I was idly looking around at the other cars, doing the math on the EV adoption rate in this small sample of Los Angeles gridlock (roughly 50 percent, impressively) when I noticed that I was eye-level with a Tesla Model Y door handle.
That’s not particularly low for a sports car, but it’s practically unheard of for an EV. Nearly all modern electric cars are built atop a skateboard-style battery pack, a stack of cells that elevates the seating position by a good 3 inches. In these SUV-heady days, that’s usually not a problem, possibly even an advantage. But, in a car like this, the closer you can get your keister to the road, the greater the sensation of speed.
So, for the company’s first all-electric sports car, the 718 Boxster that will be fully revealed next year, Porsche engineers put the battery pack behind the driver. That powers a single motor spinning the rear wheels and creates a driving experience that both honors the simple joy of motoring in a mid-engined Boxster while pushing the 718 to new heights of power and performance.
Mid-engined? Mid-batteried.
That EV battery layout, stacked behind the two-seat cabin rather than sandwiched below it, isn’t novel. It’s the same setup that Tesla used on the original Roadster back in 2008. Back then it was done for cost reasons as much as anything, enabling Tesla to repurpose a Lotus chassis meant to hold an internal combustion engine in the middle.
For Porsche’s new Boxster (and the Audi Concept C, which is built on the same platform), that pack enables the low seating position and also delivers a rearward weight bias (40:60 front/rear) that’s in keeping with the last-generation 718 Boxster, the internal combustion model killed by EU cybersecurity regulations last year.

A see-through hub with the ports you need and up to 8TB of storage
