articles.title: KI-Code schneller prüfen und freigeben: Was Entwickler jetzt über Claude Ship wissen müssen
articles.text:
Neue KI-Funktionen für Entwickler: Was du über Claude Ship wissen musst
Anthropic hat Claude Ship vorgestellt. Das Tool für Entwickler:innen prüft Codeänderungen automatisch, behebt Probleme und gibt Änderungen gemäß den Regeln eines Teams frei. Die Neuerung soll ein bestehendes Problem lösen: Zwar erstellen KI-Agenten Code sehr viel schneller als Menschen – wegen der anschließenden Prüfungen und Korrekturen beschleunigte sich der gesamte Prozess bisher aber nur bedingt.
Überprüfung nimmt viel Zeit in Anspruch
KI-Tools können zwar die Produktivität beim Programmieren steigern, die Gewinne schlagen sich aber oft weder im Ergebnis noch im Arbeitsaufwand nieder. Das hat eine Harvard-Studie ergeben. Der Grund: Entwickler:innen müssen mehr Zeit in die manuelle Prüfung von KI-generiertem Code investieren. Die Forscher:innen werteten über 300 Millionen Arbeitsergebnisse der Engineering-Analytics-Plattform Jellyfish aus. Dadurch wollten sie herausfinden, wie sich KI konkret auf die Arbeit von Entwickler:innen auswirkt.
Laut den Studienautor:innen entstanden durch Coding-Tools und KI-Agenten zwar messbar mehr Codezeilen – auf den Output hatte das allerdings kaum einen Einfluss. „Wir sehen Anzeichen für einen Engpass im Überprüfungsprozess des Codes”, heißt es in den Ergebnissen der Harvard-Studie. Durch den Einsatz von KI stieg die durchschnittliche Zeit für die Überprüfung eines Pull-Requests deutlich, ebenso wie der Anteil der Pull-Requests, bei denen Änderungen nötig waren. Die Aufgaben der Entwickler:innen würden sich deshalb zunehmend hin zur Überprüfung verlagern.
Anthropic will Entwickler:innen entlasten
Mit Claude Ship will Anthropic jetzt eine Lösung bieten und erweitert die Entscheidungsbefugnisse der eigenen KI. Entwickler:innen können künftig nicht nur die Prüfung und Korrektur von Codeänderungen, sondern auch deren Freigabe nach individuell definierten Richtlinien an Claude delegieren. Für Claude Ship kombiniert Anthropic das seit Oktober 2026 regulär verfügbare Code Review mit zwei neuen KI-Agenten: PR Steward und Claude Approvals, die zunächst in der Beta-Version verfügbar sind. Gemeinsam übernehmen sie die Bearbeitung von Pull Requests, mit denen Entwickler:innen Änderungen an einer bestehenden Code-Basis vorschlagen. Code Review identifiziert mögliche Fehler, PR Steward nimmt notwendige Korrekturen vor und Claude Approvals entscheidet anhand der hinterlegten Richtlinien, ob die Änderungen freigegeben werden dürfen.
Mithilfe von Code Review ermöglichte Anthropic es Entwickler:innen, Codeänderungen im Kontext der gesamten Code-Basis automatisiert auf Fehler zu prüfen. So müssen sie weniger Zeit in manuelle Prüfungen investieren und können sich stärker auf neue Funktionen konzentrieren. Über die drei Review-Stufen Quick, Standard und Deep lässt sich bestimmen, wie gründlich Claude dabei vorgeht. Welches Potenzial in KI-gestützten Reviews steckt, zeigt Anthropic anhand eigener Erfahrungen mit dem Tool. Im eigenen Coding-Team, das die Funktion als eine von mehreren Prüfinstanzen nutzt, habe sich die Zahl der zusammengeführten Pull Requests zwischen Juni und September mehr als verdoppelt. Zugleich sank der Anteil der rückgängig gemachten Änderungen um über 40 Prozent.
Wer jetzt auf Claude Ship zugreifen kann
Damit die Eingriffe der KI nachvollziehbar bleiben, dokumentiert PR Steward nach jeder Aktualisierung, welche Änderungen er vorgenommen hat und wie sich diese bei Bedarf rückgängig machen lassen. Der Agent darf den Code zwar ändern, diesen aber nicht eigenständig freigeben. An dieser Stelle kommt Claude Approvals ins Spiel. Welche Entscheidungen Entwickler:innen der KI überlassen, legen sie in einer Richtliniendatei im jeweiligen Repository fest. Nutzer:innen mit Team- oder Enterprise-Abonnement, die ihren Code auf GitHub verwalten, können ab sofort auf Claude Ship zugreifen. Berechtigten Enterprise-Kund:innen gewährt Anthropic ein Guthaben von mindestens 10.000 US-Dollar.

articles.title: Turnitin discloses cyberattack affecting customer-facing systems
articles.text:
Educational technology company Turnitin disclosed that it detected unauthorized activity involving certain customer-facing systems and deployed its incident response plan.
In a public statement, CEO Chris Caren says that the incident is being investigated with help from external cybersecurity specialists, and law enforcement and cyber regulators have been notified.
Turnitin is a major education technology firm with a global presence, best known for its AI-generated writing detection, digital grading, academic research integrity checks, and examination proctoring.
According to its website, its software is used in over 16,000 institutions across 185 countries and serves 71 million students.
“We are writing to let you know that we recently identified unauthorized activity involving certain customer-facing Turnitin systems,” reads the letter from the CEO on the platform's website.
“Upon identifying the matter, we implemented our incident response plan, initiated an investigation with external cybersecurity specialists, and notified law enforcement and cyber regulators.”
Turnitin says its systems are fully operational and safe to use, noting that the affected systems do not collect government identification credentials or institutional financial information.
The company said its investigation into the incident remains ongoing and has not disclosed any details about the nature and scope of the unauthorized activity.
If you have any information regarding this incident or other undisclosed attacks, you can contact us confidentially via Signal at 646-961-3731 or at tips@bleepingcomputer.com.
Turnitin continues to monitor its systems for further unauthorized activity, indicating that it is still early to guarantee that the threat has been eliminated completely.
The company has not disclosed whether any user data was accessed or stolen, when the incident occurred, and how many individuals might have been impacted.
Regarding Turnitin service availability, the platform’s status page shows no incidents for November 2026, and the uptime history logs no disruptions. However, it's unclear whether it is safe to continue using the service and uploading sensitive data.
As of writing, no ransomware groups have publicly taken responsibility for the attack at Turnitin.
BleepingComputer has contacted the firm with questions about the incident, but a company representative said they have no additional details to share at this time.

articles.title: QCon San Francisco 2026: Lessons from Building a $100M Product in Six Weeks at OpenAI
articles.text:
At QCon San Francisco 2026, Brian Yang, Member of Technical Staff at OpenAI, described how a small group of engineers used coding agents to build the ChatGPT ads product, reaching $100 million in annualised recurring revenue within six weeks of launch and $1 billion in under 200 days, with zero human-written code.
Yang, previously at Google, Meta and LinkedIn, was a founding member of technical staff on ChatGPT Ads, which was built entirely using Codex. His central claim was that software engineering is alive but reshaped around building the system that builds the product, with the engineer acting more as a manager of agents than a line-by-line contributor. One engineer can now triage an issue, open a pull request, write documentation and unblock CI in parallel, a shift Yang compared to multi-processing.
Every change runs local and unit tests, complex changes get end-to-end user journeys via browser automation, and the most critical changes run inside production-like sandboxes with representative traffic. Sandboxes come in three forms of read-only, write-only with telemetry suppressed, and full-fidelity with telemetry tagged using a shadow tag so it can be filtered out downstream. Yang's team targets around 90% auto-approval of everyday PRs, reviewing the past 300 to 400 PRs weekly and backtesting reviewer thresholds against that rate.
He illustrated the model with a sanitised latency study where candidate PRs targeted time-to-first-ad at P50 and P95 with guardrails for ads returned, timeouts and error rates. Candidates A and B passed; candidate C was rejected because the sandbox returned no ad. Thirty to forty candidates are typically bundled into one PR and run together for a day or two before human review, because changes that pass in isolation can regress when combined.
On failure modes, Yang described codebases filling with "slop" when agent output is unchecked, so maintenance agents sit alongside feature agents to root-cause newly appearing log patterns. Agents over-write tests, so he reviews the 50 slowest tests weekly. He recounted an agent that deleted and re-provisioned slow Kubernetes pods without asking, arguing that teams need big-company controls such as authorised roles for destructive actions and physical confirmation for deployments. Yang encouraged teams to revisit "cached assumptions" such as the belief that four nines of uptime always beats higher revenue, and recommended giving every engineer a monthly AI budget with no leaderboards.
For team adoption, Yang recommended a gradual path from automating one PR, to one feature, to one project, warning that jumping straight to project automation is where systems tend to break. For teams that are resistant to AI, he described rotating an "AI champion" every two weeks. The champion picks the team's most tedious recurring task, such as GPU provisioning at OpenAI which can take hours of babysitting, snapshots and permissions work, teaches an agent to do it end-to-end as a reusable skill, and demos the result at the end of the fortnight. Over a year, that converts 26 pain points into agent-owned workflows and gives sceptical engineers tangible value rather than abstract promises.
Day to day, Yang prefers Codex's bidirectional voice mode over typing for task intake, spending around ten minutes being interviewed by the agent about requirements before agreeing on a spec and handing it to multiple agents. He uses an orchestrator thread that spawns five sub-threads to explore different approaches in parallel and picks the strongest result, rather than copy-pasting the same prompt into several chats. On models, he switches only when a new release makes the workflow feel easier, with fewer clarifying questions and equivalent output quality, rather than chasing benchmark scores. His closing message was that engineers will increasingly do for agents what managers currently do for engineers, requiring an expansion of skills around direction-setting, architecture and verification rather than their replacement.

articles.title: MTN Benin’s $215 million plan is running into a good problem with customers’ demand for more data
articles.text:
A jump in traffic is forcing MTN to spend faster than planned. Getting customers onto 5G will take more than building the network.
MTN Benin has a problem that most telecom operators would welcome: people are using its network more, and keeping up is proving expensive. But that extra usage has not brought a comparable jump in revenue.
The company’s third-quarter service revenue rose to R1.592 billion (~$91m) in 2026, from R1.562 billion (~$89m) a year earlier—an increase of R30 million, or about 1.9%. The longer view was less encouraging: service revenue for the nine months to September fell 6.1% in reported rand terms to R4.42 billion. Stripping out currency movements, the decline was 0.3%.
Those figures point to a business still working to turn growing network usage into sustained revenue growth. They do not establish how much additional revenue came directly from the traffic increase Ofodile described.
In January 2024, MTN Group pledged $215 million for infrastructure in Benin over three years. Now, chief executive Uche Ofodile expects the local operation to exceed that budget by early 2027, as demand forces it to bring spending forward.
The commitment is substantial for one market, though only a fraction of MTN’s wider investment bill. The group spent R38.5 billion (~$2.2bn) on capital expenditure, excluding leases, in 2025, equivalent to about $2.15 billion at its average exchange rate for that year. Benin’s entire three-year pledge is therefore roughly one-tenth of a single year’s group-wide spending.
“We’re probably going to outspend that,” Ofodile said in an interview with TechCabal on the sidelines of the Cyber Africa Forum, held between November 16 and 17, 2026, in Cotonou, the Republic of Benin.
Ofodile linked the spending pressure to a regulatory change in February, after which, she said, traffic grew by 100 per cent. She did not specify the comparison period or disclose how much of the investment pledge MTN has spent.
Her account highlights the difficult economics of cheaper connectivity: customers can consume more data without the operator earning proportionately more revenue, even as the operator needs additional capacity to serve them.
The original investment announcement also included a new office for MTN Benin. But Ofodile said unexpected demand had already pushed the company beyond its 2026 spending plans.
There is more to accommodate than heavier usage. Cotonou is growing, nearby communities are expanding, and MTN wants stronger coverage in the north. The question is where to build next, what customers can afford once the network arrives, and whether their spending can justify the investment.
The phones have to follow
MTN launched commercial 5G in Benin in November 2024, six years after Africa’s first commercial deployment in Lesotho, later followed by South Africa (2019), Seychelles (2020), Togo (2020), Mauritius (2021), and Botswana (2022).
Benin’s market shows why introducing a newer network does not immediately displace older technology. Regulatory figures for September 2026 show that 2G still held a narrow lead, accounting for 44% of mobile subscriptions, compared with 43.6% for 4G. Specifically for internet access, however, 4G accounted for 58% of mobile internet subscriptions in 2025. The September 2026 figures do not separately identify 5G subscriptions.
Ofodile expects MTN’s 5G network to expand beyond Cotonou in early 2027. She is, however, less interested in putting coverage everywhere before enough people have the devices to use it.
“I can have all the desire in the world to expand,” she said. “But if we don’t have enough devices, then… it makes it a bit difficult.”
It is an unglamorous hurdle for a technology usually sold on speed. A faster network does little for someone whose phone cannot connect to it.
Nigeria offers a cautionary example. By September 2026, 5G accounted for 5.05 per cent of mobile subscriptions, up from 2.81 per cent in April 2025, but still a small share of the market. High device costs have been a barrier to adoption. Nigeria’s figures do not describe Benin’s market, but they illustrate why building a network does not automatically bring customers onto it.
Ofodile said MTN Benin allows customers to pay a deposit for a phone and then clear the balance daily or weekly. Benin’s mobile penetration stood at 78.1 per cent at the end of 2025, representing about 10.3 million unique subscribers, although this measure reflects access to mobile services rather than smartphone ownership.
Elsewhere, MTN’s South African MoMo business introduced rent-to-own smartphones in July 2025, with advertised daily payments starting at R10 (¢57). But those terms apply to South Africa, not Benin.
Splitting a bill into smaller payments can help. It does not necessarily make the phone cheaper or the repayments manageable.
Following the customers
For now, businesses and households offer MTN another route to growing its network.
Ofodile said business customers are increasingly interested in fixed wireless access: broadband delivered over a mobile network, without running a physical connection to every building. It is particularly useful where fibre is unavailable.
New homes around Cotonou and Abomey-Calavi also mean potential customers. MTN wants to follow that growth, rather than expand 5G simply to claim more coverage.
Farther afield, the approach changes. Ofodile cited a rural-site partnership with Africa Mobile Networks Group (AMN) as an example of how to find infrastructure suited to the communities being served.
“I’m going to put the best technology for the environment,” she said. “Rural telephony, rural coverage.”
A rural community and an urban business district do not necessarily need the same setup, or generate enough revenue to justify the same costs.
Data prices, meanwhile, have fallen sharply. Government figures drawn from regulatory data put the average price at CFA995 ($1.66) per gigabyte in 2022 and CFA440 ($0.74) per gigabyte in 2024, down by roughly 56%.
For customers, lower prices mean their money can go further. For MTN, more usage means finding ways to carry the extra traffic while keeping costs down. Neither side of that equation disappears when the company switches on 5G.
The challenge, however, is making those investments pay without asking customers to shoulder prices that put connectivity beyond their financial reach.
The 83% question
Ofodile’s benchmark for success is not another generation of mobile technology. It is mobile money, and how thoroughly it has worked its way into everyday life.
According to the GSMA’s 2026 mobile-money report, global services processed over $2.1 trillion in 2025, driven largely by sub-Saharan Africa. Merchant payments grew fastest, jumping 42% to $155 billion as phones became tools for daily commerce rather than just transfers. Importantly, mobile money functions over USSD on basic phones, meaning deeper digital inclusion does not require 5G or smartphones.
“Mobile Money represents 83 per cent of the value of the transactions in the country,” Ofodile said.
Benin’s 2025 annual report from the Autorité de Régulation des Communications Électroniques et de la Poste (Electronic Communications and Postal Regulatory Authority) (ARCEP) gives MTN Mobile Money approximately 83% of mobile financial services revenue, from a total market of CFA82.5 billion.
Provider revenue is not the money customers transfer or spend. The report confirms MTN’s dominance by revenue; it does not independently establish Ofodile’s claim about transaction value.
Her wider point, though, is about what people do with the service. She remembers early mobile-money advertising that centred on a city worker sending money to a parent in a village. Today, its uses extend well beyond that transaction.
She wants connectivity to follow the same path: from something customers subscribe to, to something they rely on to work, trade, and improve their lives. Subscriber totals alone cannot tell her whether that is happening.
“We can count the customers all we want,” Ofodile said. “At the end of the day, if they’re not using digital services to grow the economy, to improve their own lives, then we haven’t done enough.”

articles.title: Placer une pièce de monnaie sur son routeur Wi-Fi : pourquoi et à quoi ça sert
articles.text:
Placer une pièce de monnaie sur son routeur Wi-Fi : pourquoi et à quoi ça sert
L'astuce fait le tour des réseaux sociaux : poser une pièce, ou un bout d'aluminium, sur sa box internet améliorerait la connexion. La réalité physique est tout autre. Non seulement le métal ne renforce pas le signal, mais il peut le dégrader et faire surchauffer l'appareil. Voici ce qui marche vraiment.
C'est une astuce de grand-mère version numérique qui revient régulièrement sur YouTube : poser délicatement une simple pièce de deux euros sur le dessus de sa box internet permettrait d'obtenir enfin un réseau fluide et sans coupures. Entre démonstrations convaincantes et commentaires enthousiastes, la promesse est séduisante. Le geste est si simple et gratuit qu'on serait tenté de l'essayer sur-le-champ. C'est pourtant là que se niche le piège de ces recettes miracles qui circulent en ligne.
Une croyance séduisante mais sans fondement
L'idée paraît presque logique. Le métal réfléchit les ondes, alors une pièce posée sur la box redirigerait le signal Wi-Fi et étendrait sa portée. C'est sur ce raisonnement que repose l'astuce, largement relayée. Sauf qu'aucune preuve technique ne la soutient, et les spécialistes des télécoms sont unanimes pour la réfuter. Poser un objet métallique sur ou contre un routeur n'améliore rien, et peut même aggraver la situation.
Si certains utilisateurs jurent avoir constaté un mieux, il s'agit au mieux d'un effet placebo, au pire d'une coïncidence avec un simple redémarrage de la box au moment de la manipulation. La vérité est que l'amélioration du Wi-Fi ne passe jamais par un gadget posé sur le boîtier, mais par le placement de l'appareil et par ses réglages. La pièce, elle, ne fait qu'ajouter un problème là où il n'y en avait pas.
Pourquoi le métal nuit au signal, et à l'appareil
La physique explique clairement pourquoi cette astuce se retourne contre l'utilisateur. Les antennes d'une box sont des circuits calibrés au millimètre pour émettre sur des fréquences précises. Approcher un objet métallique conducteur perturbe leur environnement immédiat et décale leur fréquence de résonance, un phénomène que les ingénieurs appellent le désaccordage d'antenne. Résultat, une partie de l'énergie n'est plus rayonnée vers la pièce, mais réfléchie vers les circuits internes de la box, avec une perte d'efficacité qui peut dépasser 50 %.
Le métal déforme aussi le diagramme de rayonnement, ce halo en forme d'anneau selon lequel la box diffuse normalement son signal. Au lieu d'une couverture homogène, on crée des zones d'ombre et des réflexions incontrôlées. À cela s'ajoute un risque matériel : un objet posé sur le boîtier bloque les grilles de ventilation. La box chauffe, déclenche une sécurité qui bride ses performances, et souffre à la longue d'une usure prématurée. En cherchant à gagner quelques mégabits, on abîme donc l'appareil.
Les gestes qui améliorent vraiment le Wi-Fi
Bonne nouvelle, les vraies solutions sont tout aussi simples et, elles, réellement efficaces. La première tient au placement. Installez la box en hauteur, à environ 1,5 mètre du sol, et au centre du logement. Posée par terre ou cachée dans un meuble, elle perd jusqu'à 30 % de sa portée et risque la surchauffe. Éloignez-la des masses métalliques, des murs épais, mais aussi des perturbateurs comme le four à micro-ondes, les téléphones sans fil ou même un aquarium, l'eau absorbant fortement les ondes.
Asus ZenWiFi BT8
Côté réglages, quelques ajustements changent tout. Réservez la bande 5 GHz aux usages intensifs proches de la box, streaming ou visio, et gardez la 2,4 GHz, qui traverse mieux les murs, pour les objets connectés éloignés. Une application d'analyse réseau permet de repérer un canal moins encombré par le voisinage. Reliez en câble Ethernet vos appareils fixes, ordinateur de bureau ou console, pour libérer les ondes. Et pensez à redémarrer la box de temps en temps, puis à maintenir son logiciel à jour. Pour les grands logements, un système de répéteurs ou un kit CPL fera le reste. Autant de gestes qui, contrairement à la pièce de monnaie, reposent sur la science plutôt que sur la rumeur.
Cet article a été initialement publié en septembre 2026. Nous le republions aujourd'hui car l'optimisation du réseau Wi-Fi à domicile reste une préoccupation majeure pour nos lecteurs, et il est toujours utile de rappeler pourquoi certaines "astuces" devenues virales sur les réseaux sociaux sont en réalité de très mauvaises idées.

articles.title: IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes
articles.text:
IBM quantum computer solves problem classical computers can’t in just 15 minutes
- Date:
  November 23, 2026
- Source:
  IBM
- Summary:
  IBM and University of Chicago researchers have demonstrated that a quantum computer can complete an extraordinarily complex calculation in just 15 minutes, beyond the practical reach of leading classical computing methods. A novel error-detection technique also allows scientists to establish confidence in the accuracy of the results, overcoming a major hurdle in quantum computing.
- Share:
An IBM quantum computer has completed an extraordinarily complex computational task in just 15 minutes, while leading methods for simulating the calculation on conventional computers would require prohibitively long runtimes. Perhaps even more significantly, researchers were able to establish statistical confidence in the accuracy of the quantum computer's results, addressing one of the biggest obstacles in the field.
The achievement, led by IBM and researchers from the University of Chicago, satisfies the fundamental criteria for quantum advantage. This milestone occurs when a quantum computer performs a computational task beyond the practical capabilities of leading classical computing methods while producing results that can be trusted.
In their new paper, "Sampling hard circuits with verifiably high fidelity," the researchers demonstrated that both objectives could be achieved simultaneously using a novel design for encoded quantum circuits. The experiment represents one of the largest demonstrations of logical quantum computing to date. The researchers have also made their circuits and experimental results publicly available through the Quantum Advantage Tracker.
Solving Quantum Computing's Verification Problem
Unlike conventional computers, which process information using bits that represent either zero or one, quantum computers rely on quantum bits, or qubits. These can exist in combinations of both states and interact through a phenomenon known as quantum entanglement. These properties allow quantum computers to approach certain computational problems in fundamentally different ways.
For years, scientists have tested the capabilities of quantum computers using a benchmark called random circuit sampling (RCS). This technique involves running a series of randomly selected quantum operations and generating samples from a complex probability distribution. As the circuits grow larger and more complicated, reproducing their output with a classical computer becomes increasingly difficult.
However, this approach creates a fundamental dilemma. If a computation is too difficult for a classical computer to reproduce, how can researchers establish that the quantum computer performed it correctly?
As computational complexity increases, independently verifying the results becomes progressively more difficult and eventually impractical without making strong assumptions about how accurately the quantum hardware operates.
To overcome this problem, the IBM and University of Chicago team developed a more structured alternative to random circuit sampling. The researchers mathematically demonstrated that their approach preserves the same computational hardness criteria as conventional RCS while introducing a structure that allows errors to be detected during the computation.
"Verification remains one of the biggest challenges in firmly establishing experimental quantum advantage," said Bill Fefferman, Associate Professor at the University of Chicago. "This experiment develops techniques to better characterize the fidelity of hard quantum states under noise, increasing confidence that the quantum computer is solving a computationally hard problem."
Soumik Ghosh, PhD student in Fefferman's group at the University of Chicago, added, "Beyond strengthening experimental validation, advances in verification have the potential to unlock practical applications for the next generation of quantum computers."
70 Logical Qubits and Tenfold Lower Error Rates
One of the greatest challenges in building powerful quantum computers is their extraordinary sensitivity to errors. Quantum information can be disrupted by environmental disturbances, imperfections in hardware, and inaccuracies in the operations used to manipulate qubits. As computations become longer and more complex, these errors can accumulate and undermine the reliability of the results.
Quantum error correction addresses this weakness by encoding quantum information across multiple physical qubits to create more reliable units known as logical qubits. This approach allows certain errors to be identified and, depending on the technique, corrected or accounted for without destroying the underlying quantum information.
In one of the largest known demonstrations of quantum error correction, the researchers performed computations using 70 protected logical qubits. The experiment involved 2,415 logical two-qubit operations and 468 logical "T gates."
Quantum gates are the fundamental operations that manipulate quantum information, much like logic gates in conventional computers. Two-qubit gates allow qubits to interact, while T gates enable additional types of quantum operations needed for universal quantum computing. Together, these gate counts illustrate the considerable complexity of the experiment.
By encoding the quantum circuits, the researchers achieved effective logical error rates 10 times lower than the underlying physical error rates. This substantial reduction allowed the quantum computer to maintain remarkably high fidelity, a measure of how closely the actual quantum state matches the intended one, despite performing thousands of complex operations.
A New Era of Quantum Advantage
"We are now firmly in the quantum advantage era," said Jay Gambetta, Director of IBM Research and IBM Fellow. "We have demonstrated a quantum computation beyond the practical reach of classical computers that establishes, with statistical confidence, a lower bound on how faithfully it was executed. This milestone gives scientists, developers, and businesses a new foundation for trusting quantum computers as they scale to problems far beyond what we can achieve classically."
The researchers found that many leading classical simulation techniques would require impractically long periods to reproduce the computation. IBM's quantum computer, by comparison, accomplished the task in approximately 15 minutes.
Although the experiment was designed to demonstrate quantum advantage rather than solve an immediate real-world problem, it addresses two essential requirements for making large-scale quantum computing practical: controlling errors and establishing confidence in computational results.
By demonstrating both capabilities in a computation beyond the practical reach of leading classical methods, the researchers have taken a significant step toward a future in which quantum computers could reliably tackle scientific and industrial problems that are currently out of reach.

articles.title: GTA VI hacker who used a Fire Stick to breach Rockstar walks free on the day he's sentenced
articles.text:
TL;DR: Arion Kurtaj broke into Rockstar Games using an Amazon Fire Stick plugged into a hotel television, a Bluetooth keyboard, and a mouse, and took nearly an hour of footage from the unreleased Grand Theft Auto 6. On Tuesday, a London court sentenced the 21-year-old Lapsus$ hacker to seven years in prison and then released him "on licence," the British version of parole, which lets an offender serve the rest of a sentence in the community under conditions and allows a return to prison if those conditions are broken.
The judge decided that Kurtaj had already served enough time between his stay in a secure hospital and his period "on remand," the British term for being held in jail while awaiting trial or sentencing. He was sent off with a warning: "Don't let this happen again."
Kurtaj had no computer when he attacked Rockstar in 2022. Police had seized his equipment, and he was out on bail, staying under police protection at a Travelodge in Bicester. Rival hackers had threatened him over the Bitcoin he had stolen, and the protection was meant to keep him safe from them.
Inside the hotel room, a streaming device and a few wireless peripherals were all he needed to get back online and into one of the games industry's most closely guarded projects.
He took internal company data, including 90 clips totaling nearly 60 minutes of GTA 6 gameplay. Rockstar had kept the game tightly under wraps until its release last week. Kurtaj then got into the studio's internal Slack workspace and posted a demand: "If Rockstar does not contact me on Telegram within 24 hours I will start releasing the source code." Rockstar refused to engage. He then published the clips and the source code on a forum under the name TeaPotUberHacker.
Rockstar said recovering from the breach cost $5 million and thousands of staff hours. The leak also gave away a marketing secret the company had been protecting: one of the game's playable characters is a woman.
 – Crown Prosecution Service (@CPSUK) November 16, 2026
The Rockstar attack was one of several Kurtaj carried out at ages 16 and 17 as a member of Lapsus$. During the same period on bail, he also breached Revolut and Uber. The group's attacks on those firms and on BT/EE did not depend on new exploits. The hackers used social engineering, tricking people into clicking malicious links or handing over sensitive information, and that gave them access to internal systems. In the Uber case, the court heard that Kurtaj posted an image of a penis while trying to pressure the company into paying a ransom.
Damage to the companies is estimated at around £10 million. The gang also used the stolen corporate data to target cryptocurrency investors. Prosecutors said individual victims lost at least $300,000.
Because of the severity of his autism, Kurtaj was first ordered to be held indefinitely in a secure hospital. He was later found fit to stand trial and was moved to an ordinary prison in January. He pleaded guilty last Monday to the Rockstar hack and several others.
He also admitted physically assaulting staff while in custody, including several biting incidents. In prison, he was caught with a mobile phone after sending police a taunting text and posting updates on Snapchat.
His defense argued that the internet was where Kurtaj felt most at ease. They said he first met people who taught him to cheat at games and then "people who were involved in hacking." They said he was "very isolated" during the pandemic and that his "connection to Lapsus$ provided him with a sense of community and self-worth that had been absent in his life previously."
JJustice Turner acknowledged Kurtaj's technical abilities during the hearing. "You are a very talented young man," he told Kurtaj.
His release comes with restrictions on his online activity. A Serious Crime Prevention Order will be in force for five years and will bar him from using Telegram and Discord, among other restrictions. He used Telegram for his ransom demand to Rockstar.
City of London Police said the case "highlights the dangers that young people can end up being drawn to online."

articles.title: OpenAI pagará hasta USD 8.000 al mes a quienes enseñen ChatGPT a pequeños negocios de Estados Unidos
articles.text:
OpenAI lanzó OpenWorks, un programa que contrata a expertos en inteligencia artificial (IA) para que ayuden de forma gratuita a pequeños negocios de Estados Unidos. Los elegidos recibirán un pago mensual de hasta USD 8.000, según la página oficial de la compañía, y el piloto ya funciona en 20 ciudades.
La empresa busca personas y grupos pequeños con conocimientos técnicos, y alienta a las consultoras de software e IA a postularse junto con su trabajo habitual. A cambio del pago, los participantes deben dedicar días de cada mes a trabajar con comercios locales y dar un taller mensual en su comunidad.
El compromiso es de cuatro días completos de trabajo presencial por mes, además del taller. USD 8.000 es el máximo anunciado y no un sueldo fijo para todos.
Qué reciben los comercios y quiénes quedan fuera
Los negocios no pagan por el servicio. Eligen una tarea o un problema, lo resuelven junto con un socio de OpenWorks y reciben tres meses de ChatGPT Business, la versión del chatbot pensada para empresas, sin costo. OpenAI afirma que no hace falta experiencia técnica.
El piloto está abierto a negocios de propiedad independiente en Estados Unidos, como restaurantes, tiendas, empresas de servicios y fábricas. Quedan excluidas las empresas de software, las respaldadas por capital de riesgo y las que pertenecen a fondos de inversión privados.
Las 20 ciudades incluyen Chicago, Nueva York, Los Ángeles, Seattle, Houston, Atlanta, Nashville y Austin, además de localidades más pequeñas como Fargo, en Dakota del Norte, y Jackson, en Misisipi. La compañía no anunció una fecha límite general para postularse.
Los resultados que cuenta la empresa
OpenAI publicó cuatro casos. En Fargo, los dueños de la tienda de miniaturas Tiny Things usaron ChatGPT para armar un panel de control de inventario con más de mil productos. Uno de ellos estimó que encargar una herramienta así costaría unos USD 50.000.
En Charleston, Carolina del Sur, un productor de microvegetales pidió al chatbot que identificara restaurantes y redactara correos para los chefs. Según su propia estimación, la tasa de respuesta subió del 20% al 75% y consiguió 10 clientes nuevos en cuatro meses.
Asimismo, los relatos son de los propios comercios, sin auditoría independiente. La página oficial cita a una empleada de una empresa de carteles que dice ahorrar entre dos y cinco horas semanales, y a dos fundadoras de una firma de papel de regalo que evitaron cobros indebidos de proveedores.
Un paso para ampliar la base de clientes
El programa llega cuando OpenAI intenta convertir el uso masivo de ChatGPT en suscripciones empresariales recurrentes. El medio recordó que en abril la compañía informó que los clientes empresariales aportaban más del 40% de sus ingresos, y que Anthropic superó a OpenAI este año en una medida de adopción de IA en empresas.
OpenAI tampoco aclaró qué ocurre cuando terminan los tres meses gratuitos. OpenWorks estaría relacionada con una iniciativa de octubre de 2026 con los centros de desarrollo de pequeñas empresas de Estados Unidos, destinada a formar asesores y llegar al menos a 1.000 negocios mediante talleres.
El formulario para postularse como socio ya está abierto en la página de OpenWorks, donde también se puede nominar a un comercio o a un posible instructor local.
Quedan pendientes datos que permitirían medir el alcance real del piloto. La compañía no señaló cuántos especialistas espera incorporar, qué criterios usará para seleccionar a los comercios ni cuál es el presupuesto total asignado.
OpenAI tampoco precisó si evaluará resultados con indicadores comunes, más allá de los testimonios publicados. Esas definiciones serán relevantes para determinar si OpenWorks puede extenderse a otras ciudades o mantenerse como una experiencia limitada por ahora.

articles.title: No more heated seat subscriptions for cars in New York from 2027
articles.text:
Car buyers in New York may find the cost of ownership reduces a little next year. Maybe. Governor Kathy Hochul signed a bill yesterday that bans car companies and dealerships from locking up car features behind a subscription, a law that goes into effect on February 27 next year.
“People spending their hard-earned money on a car shouldn’t have to fork over even more money for features that should automatically come with the car. My message to car companies is clear: this kind of deceptive business model isn’t going to fly in New York State. Keep your hands out of New Yorkers’ wallets,” the governor said.
In the old days, the only options you paid to use after you bought a car were mods or upgrades you installed after the fact. That started to change with services like General Motors’ OnStar, which introduced telematics to the vehicle—for a monthly fee.
We end users might not like having to open our wallets each month, but the capital markets sure do, and car companies love making the capital markets happy. Which is why there has been such a push toward connected vehicles. Remote start and predictive maintenance alerts are nice, but your regular payments to the car company—plus any data of yours it can sell—is the goal.
Some automakers have gone even further. Infamously, BMW and its heated seats. Like the McDonald’s coffee lawsuit, it’s a fact half-remembered; BMW North America never tried such a thing, just in countries like South Korea and the UK, and in 2023 BMW’s board said that subscriptions would only be for software-related features from then on.
My 2022 Mustang Mach-e "came with" Ford's Blue Cruise, which is excellent.
NOWHERE on the Monroney sticker or in my contract does it say anything about Blue Cruise being for a limited time, then being subscription afterward.
It didn't say "3 years of Blue Cruise" or anything similar.
I do understand how updating the maps creates an on-going cost, but the system already only works on divided highways and uses built-in hardware, and doesn't really need updated maps to maintain hands-off lane-keeping.
Ford gave all the 2022 owners an extra year for "free", but I still find it pretty frustrating.

articles.title: UK warns AI-driven cyberattacks are exposing years of weak security
articles.text:
The U.K. government’s cybersecurity unit says it has seen a “marked rise” in AI-driven cyberattacks in recent months, as hackers increasingly rely on autonomous hacking tools to identify and exploit simple weaknesses to break into systems and networks.
The U.K. National Cybersecurity Center (NCSC) said it has seen several cyber incidents since September involving autonomous hacking tools, such as penetration testing tools used by defenders to stress-test their cybersecurity defenses. These incidents have caused intrusions at organizations and resulted in downtime, the unit said in a blog post.
The NCSC says that while none of the vulnerabilities being exploited are new, the speed at which these AI tools are able to carry out simple hacks has changed.
The rise in AI-related cyberattacks coincides with the broader release earlier this year of open source autonomous penetration testing tools like Artex and Cairn, among others, which anyone can download and use at no cost. The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation recently warned that malicious hackers are using AI penetration testing tools to carry out cyberattacks at unprecedented speeds.
While cyberattacks and intrusions are on the rise, the message from London is that many of these attacks are preventable with basic cybersecurity defenses and best practices.
“Notably, the issues being exploited currently are not novel memory corruption vulnerabilities (or even known but unpatched vulnerabilities), but unmitigated weaknesses that are often the result of years of technical debt that organisations have accumulated,” the NCSC wrote.
The unit said that agentic hacking tools often look for exposed or internet-facing systems, then quickly run through lists of weak or easy-to-guess passwords or abuse API endpoints often used by developers to access data.
The NCSC said that AI “does not make established cyber security controls obsolete,” but rather that “building strong foundations has never mattered more.”
The unit added that AI has made it easier to find vulnerabilities and faster to exploit them, warning that weaknesses that have gone unnoticed for years can now be found in minutes.

articles.title: Big Final Fantasy XIV concert is coming to Canada
articles.text:
Final Fantasy XIV is going on tour next year.
Gaming giant Square Enix has announced that its popular MMORPG is getting its first-ever international concert, the Eorzean Symphony. The show, which is being put on in partnership with Promax and Soho Live, will feature a full orchestra and choir conducted by Hirofumi Kurita and featuring performances by original FFXIV vocalists Amanda Achen and Jason Charles Miller.
The press release doesn’t mention which music will be featured in the concert. It should be noted that the game’s sixth expansion for the long-running FFXIV, releases on Feb. 23, ahead of the first show in Bangkok on March 27. Therefore, it remains to be seen whether it will include pieces from that expansion as well as the five previous.
So far, 10 cities have been confirmed for the tour, with the sole Canadian stop being Toronto. It remains to be seen whether other Canadian cities may be added.
The Eorzean Symphony will take place in Toronto on July 7 and 8 at Roy Thomson Hall. The Toronto show is being presented by local media company Kashamara Productions, which has helped bring popular concerts for the likes of Final Fantasy VII Rebirth, Dragon Ball and Stardew Valley to Canada, as well as Roy Thomson Hall and 54 Entertainment.
View this post on Instagram
Tickets go on sale on Dec. 2.
It’s worth noting that fellow Square Enix series Nier is also getting its own concert in Toronto in February. Other notable video game concerts coming to Toronto in 2027 include March’s Sonic Live in Concert and October’s The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Concert.
Image credit: Square Enix

articles.title: Rockstar le cierra la puerta a Hollywood con ‘GTA’, pero podría llevar ‘Red Dead Redemption’ al cine
articles.text:
Con GTA 6 en boca de todos gracias a su exitoso lanzamiento, el interés de Hollywood por las propiedades intelectuales de Rockstar Games se ha revitalizado. Según un nuevo reporte de The Ankler, el estudio no está dispuesto a desarrollar una adaptación basada en Grand Theft Auto, pero no vería con malos ojos la posibilidad de una película o serie de Red Dead Redemption.
La citada publicación indica abiertamente que a Rockstar no le interesa expandir GTA al mundo del cine o la TV. Tiene todo el sentido que así sea, considerando que la franquicia ya tiene el hype y la anticipación suficiente por parte del público como para no requerir ningún tipo de adaptación. Los casi 3.800 millones de dólares que generó al cierre de su primer día a disposición son prueba cabal de ello.
En el caso de la saga Red Dead, la historia sería diferente; en especial, con las dos entregas de Red Dead Redemption. Según se menciona, Rockstar Games estaría abierta a escuchar ofertas para convertirla en películas o en una serie de televisión. Esto no necesariamente implica que el estudio termine aceptando alguna propuesta, pero sí que las posibilidades de que la IP dé el salto más allá de los videojuegos no son nulas.
Eso sí, los que quieran poner sus manos sobre Red Dead Redemption tienen que estar dispuestos a desembolsar en grande. El reporte indica que Rockstar quiere un mínimo de 100 millones de dólares para cualquier acuerdo de licencia.
Rockstar estaría dispuesta a adaptar Red Dead Redemption en películas o series
Desde Rockstar saben que tienen entre manos algunas de las propiedades intelectuales más buscadas de Hollywood. No es ilógico pensar que los pesos pesados del cine y la TV no tendrán problemas en desembolsar cuanto se les pida por licenciar Red Dead Redemption. En especial, considerando el empuje que en los últimos años han tenido las adaptaciones basadas en videojuegos.
The Last of Us (HBO) y Fallout (Amazon) son dos de los ejemplos más exitosos de esta movida. A estos hay que sumarle otras apuestas como God of War, Tomb Raider, Far Cry, Metal Gear Solid y Assassin's Creed. The Ankler sostiene que algunos de estos proyectos están destinando entre 15 y 25 millones de dólares por episodio, lo cual deja en claro que hay grandes expectativas detrás de este tipo de títulos.
Si una película o serie de Red Dead Redemption termina viendo la luz, aún es un misterio si podría tratarse de una adaptación fiel de los juegos, o una historia original que se inspire en estos. Sea como sea, todo el ruido por GTA 6 podría ayudar a darle más empuje a la iniciativa, para que Rockstar y Take-Two inflen todavía más sus cuentas bancarias.

articles.title: AI Vs. High-Level Synthesis
articles.text:
AI promises to automate chip design from spec to implementation, but can it match HLS in productivity, verification, and quality of results?
Key Takeaways:
- The main advantage provided by HLS is productivity, but those gains diminish if not accompanied by a robust verification methodology.
- AI agents around current HLS tools will allow more exploration and build on existing trust but full AI potential may want to work outside those bounds.
- Producing RTL is the easy part. HLS has to generate RTL that is implementable, that meets power, performance and area constraints, within a defined context. AI struggles with this today.
High-level synthesis (HLS) initially struggled to find a market, but eventually it became a valuable tool for certain kinds of design. It is now threatened by the promise of AI, which some predict will allow engineers to go from specification to finished silicon while avoiding many EDA tools, including HLS.
Most developers of HLS solutions are not troubled by this today, though they do see many changes on the horizon.
HLS has been most valuable for algorithmic accelerators, although that could change. “When I have something that is too slow or power hungry to run on a CPU, I may want to look at custom silicon,” says Stuart Clubb, technical product management director at Siemens EDA. “I might choose to go the path of IP reuse, and that is the most likely answer for a bus interface or peripheral. HLS got shoved off to the new blocks — things that hadn’t been done before and needed some smart architectural hardware design, and solving problems that hadn’t been tackled before.”
The main advantage of HLS is productivity. “HLS handles complex control logic and data path equally well, with 10 to 20 times less code than RTL,” says Badru Agarwala, CEO and co-founder at Rise Design Automation. “Less code is easier to review, so you can trust what you’re shipping, and easier to edit when the specification changes. That is what lets a design scale from a single block to a large subsystem, whether an engineer or an AI writes it.”
Those productivity gains can be significant (see figure 1, below.) “When we talk about HLS, the goal is not to do everything using HLS, or when we attempt LLM to RTL, the goal is not to do everything on LLM to RTL,” said Diptesh Nandi, senior product marketing manager at Microchip. “There will be a certain portion that requires time to market, or faster processing that will not be optimized. If you use HLS, it’s probably going to consume more power because it’s not going to be optimized (compared to hand-crafted RTL). If you take the LLM-to-RTL route — where you focus on time to market and then apply it on the development time, the training time that you require where you’re creating the whole tools flow, or creating the whole design — then you will spend less time developing the whole solution, less time training the whole solution, thereby saving power.”
Fig. 1: An HLS flow for FPGA designs. Source: Microchip
The real challenge is that chip complexity is growing faster than engineering productivity. “Writing RTL was never the biggest bottleneck,” says Rise DA’s Agarwala. “Amdahl’s law applies here. Making one relatively small part of the development process dramatically faster doesn’t help much if the rest of the process remains unchanged. Most of the schedule is spent on verification and the iterations needed to meet performance, power, and area targets.”
This does play into one aspect of HLS, which is that verification time of C code is orders of magnitude faster than RTL. Given that HLS can synthesize designs quickly, and those can be verified at the abstract level, it enables an AI agent to evaluate a lot of alternatives in a small amount of time. This coupling may be the big winner, but we are not there yet.
“Software is leading the pack,” says Tom De Muer, fellow at Keysight EDA. “Digital design is coming next, followed by mixed analog, and then the full physics. High-level synthesis sits at that digital part. It’s lagging software. In addition, we have the problem in the semiconductor world that you cannot prompt something very vague and expect something to come out that’s production-ready.”
To see widespread adoption, it has to solve a real problem. “For 50 years, EDA progress meant climbing abstraction,” says Mehir Arora, head of engineering at ChipAgents. “We built RTL, then HLS, because the human mind cannot hold the full design space. Abstraction narrows the potential design space for an engineer, making it possible for them to reason about it. But it is a loss of potential QoR. HLS was never about better hardware, but a price of designing for human capacity.”
Still, trust must be gained for any new tool or abstraction. “When we talk about AI doing this, there is some resistance from people like us because we have been burnt by things that we didn’t understand,” says Keysight’s De Muer. “For instance, if you have a design that works, that’s great, but it works under the test conditions that you know that you tested it with. But we all had our tape outs that went into production. We had full 100% regression test, but in the field something failed, and then you need to understand how it works to fix it.”
It took a long time before HLS was trusted. “HLS is now providing significant value for a specific segment of designs,” says Dave Kelf, CEO at Breker Verification Systems. “One of the most significant barriers to entry for the technology, and indeed logic synthesis originally, was the disconnect between the abstract model, especially regarding circuit timing, and the final design output. Engineers had trouble making that connection, making them nervous about trusting the results.”
What is stopping AI from doing the synthesis itself? “The rules for the synthesizable subset of C++, and by extension SystemC, have remained relatively constant for probably the last 10 to 15 years,” says Siemens’ Clubb. “In the C+ world, modeling streaming interfaces needed some level of IP to be able to represent that in an untimed sequential language, versus trying to model the explicit concurrency. We created AC channel and bit-accurate data types. A designer, or AI, needs to write out code that understands these. There’s just not a lot of training material.”
Verification
No new abstraction is going to be successful if you don’t have both a development and a verification methodology that work together. The widespread adoption of RTL required both RTL simulation and static timing verification. ESL required C and SystemC simulation and equivalence checking.
“On the verification side for HLS, people have clamored for sequential equivalent checking,” says Clubb. “It is slowly improving, but as with any formal verification challenge, there are limitations, capacity issues, things associated with latency and throughput. There’s still a lot of RTL verification required.”
Building trust takes time. “We already trust synthesis tools to perform complicated transformations without inspecting every gate,” says Agarwala. “That trust comes from verification, not from how the implementation was generated. Coverage-driven verification is equally important. Requirements can be mapped to assertions and functional coverage points, showing which parts of the specification have been exercised and which still need attention. Formal verification adds another level of confidence by checking RTL properties exhaustively within the assumptions of the formal model. The goal is to make verification faster and more complete, not simply generate RTL faster.”
The need to perform simulation on the output slows down performance and adoption. “The issue that arises, especially with analog and RF, is that you need to verify them against a physical oracle, a high-frequency simulator,” says De Muer. “Those take a long time to simulate. An agent typically needs multiple runs, and if that run takes you two or three hours, it naturally limits how much exploration can be done. Comparing it to software, you can produce a program, compile it, test it, and it stands up. In a fraction of a second, you have a data point to learn from. That’s not the case when you’re doing a 200 or 300 gigahertz design. Many runs are required so that models can improve.”
AI’s potential
In a similar manner, the primary advantage that AI can provide is productivity. By finding better architectures through a process of trial and error, it may eventually get to better designs, but that is not the case today. “The next leap in engineering productivity won’t come from doing the same work faster,” says Agarwala. “It will come from fundamentally changing how work gets done. The biggest productivity gains will come from shortening the time between an idea, an implementation, and a verified result. The teams that succeed will be the ones that can explore, measure, and verify the best architectures fastest.”
But that is not going to happen with agents. “Somebody once said that AI is a really good cover band,” says Clubb. “It’s seen the sheet music. It knows all the lyrics, and it will give you a variation on a theme. But for something completely new, maybe not so much. AI is still a way off, and it’s still very reliant on skill files that somebody else has to put together to guide how to do it. There’s not enough volume of training material. Even with these trillions of parameters and all of this input to these frontier models, they’re still not there yet.”
In addition, agents are built around existing tools, which may not be the best idea. “An LLM is much more acceptive for lower-level abstractions,” says ChipAgents’ Arora. “Give it verification and fast feedback and it can skip abstraction layers. Taking CUDA kernel generation as an example, we’ve seen LLMs write CUDA or even lower-level PTX without traditional compiler optimizations, but generate better output. Similar trends are happening in EDA and the IC flow. While humans are well suited to microarchitecture => HLS => RTL => netlist, we already see that LLMs are better at producing RTL directly when equipped with physics surrogates to predict PPA. Indeed, in the future, we may see LLMs directly generate netlists, eliminating another layer of indirection.”
Many people point to a context issue today. “If I say, ‘Design me an inductor for some IC design,’ my agent will do this, but it probably didn’t care about how well it will perform in situ in a bigger context,” says De Muer. “Does it even select the process I’m allowed to use? All of those things are missing. AI is helping to translate those intents. But you still need to be very specific because where the engineering matters, for the semiconductor pieces, all of these things need to be specified. They are not coming out of thin air.”
This is an opportunity to bring more of the context together for some problem domains. “Engineers can develop and verify the design within a TLM-based system simulation environment, alongside processors, memories, and other components, and then synthesize that same description into RTL,” says Agarwala. “This avoids maintaining separate functional models that can gradually diverge from the hardware implementation. Software development and system-level verification can also begin before RTL is available.”
That context is the ultimate shift left as well. “HLS historically, and most RTL designers, have striven to produce RTL that closes timing because if it doesn’t close timing, it’s useless,” says Clubb. “In HLS we do a lot of algorithmic, arithmetic stuff that has cascading wavefronts. When you get to a gate-level netlist, and in order to close timing, it’s not just a nice bunch of fast adders and AND gates or multipliers. There is a benefit to making sure that you don’t put too many operators between registers, because then your glitch power starts to get unmanageable. Even though your area goes down, if you over-pipeline, you’ve got too many registers. That puts your switching power up and puts your clock tree power up. You can do design exploration to hone in on the local saddle for power, or the local saddle for area, or — and this sounds like a prompt — find me the lowest power that doesn’t exceed the smallest area by 5%.”
One of the concerns is design stability. “With AI-generated RTL, changing the pipeline, resource allocation, or memory architecture often means generating a new implementation and verifying it again,” says Agarwala. “Every rewrite creates another opportunity for subtle bugs. HLS takes a different approach. We can keep the functional description unchanged while using synthesis constraints to control pipelining, parallelism, resource sharing, and memory organization. This allows AI to explore hundreds of implementations without regenerating thousands of lines of RTL. Some architectural changes still require modification of the source, but those changes are generally easier to make and verify at a higher level.”
Reality
The big question is exactly how well can AI do this today? “It does really badly, mainly because the type of code that we are handling in HLS does not usually have an easy one-to-one mapping for RTL,” says Clubb. “Once you start the process of scheduling and laying out a data path, you need to understand the process technology and the frequency that you are aiming for. What interfacing do you want? Is this a single-ported memory as an array? Is it a dual-ported memory that has memory bandwidth limitations? Can I split that up? Can I re-architect that? There are things you can do as microarchitectural constraints in HLS because they’re programmatic, but for the interfacing things like stalling, flushing, bubble compression, AI is not good.”
Still, if you have productivity gains, is it good enough? “If you need a small widget and you don’t care too much about performance, you don’t care too much about power consumption, if all of those things are irrelevant to you, AI can produce something reasonable for digital or even analog design,” says De Muer. “But even if we reduce that time to zero, the end-to-end results or gains are pretty modest. We need to look one step further, but that’s a long journey, and it comes from changing the workflows.”
Some of the gains are consumed by additional verification demands. “There was a recent paper out of Harvard talking about how AI-generated code in general is pushing more effort into verification of that code,” says Clubb. “That means the ROI for many companies is becoming questionable.”
For now, AI appears more likely to augment HLS than replace it. While AI can accelerate RTL generation and architectural exploration, producing silicon-ready designs still requires verification, implementation awareness, and careful optimization for power, performance, and area. Whether AI ultimately replaces existing abstraction layers may depend less on its ability to generate code than on its ability to produce predictable, verifiable results.

articles.title: ChatGPT passe à GPT-6.2 : ce qui change dans vos conversations avec l'IA
articles.text:
Une semaine après avoir présenté GPT-6.2 Astra et Sol, OpenAI déploie une version de sa nouvelle génération de modèles pensée pour les conversations du quotidien. Au programme, une meilleure compréhension des consignes et des images, des recherches web plus pertinentes, mais aussi quelques compromis.
Jusqu'ici réservée à ChatGPT Work, Codex et à l'API d'OpenAI, la nouvelle génération de modèles investit désormais l'interface conversationnelle classique du chatbot. Depuis ce lundi 23 novembre, OpenAI a commencé à déployer une variante de GPT-6.2 Sol, simplement appelée GPT-6.2 dans le sélecteur de modèles de ChatGPT, qui a fait l'objet d'optimisations spécifiques pour mieux répondre aux usages du quotidien, qu'il s'agisse de retravailler un texte, d'analyser une photo ou de chercher des informations sur Internet.
ChatGPT comprend mieux vos demandes et affine ses recherches sur le web
Parmi les améliorations revendiquées par OpenAI figure la capacité de ChatGPT à respecter des consignes complexes. Sur une série de requêtes conçues pour mettre le modèle en difficulté, le taux de réussite est passé de 62,5 % avec GPT-6 à 78,1 % avec GPT-6.2. Les progrès sont encore plus marqués dans la compréhension des images, avec un score de 71,7 %, contre 47,4 % pour la génération précédente.
OpenAI a aussi travaillé sur la capacité de son chatbot à mener des recherches sur Internet et à tenir compte des préférences de ses utilisateurs et utilisatrices. Sur une version interne du benchmark BrowseComp, qui évalue la capacité des modèles à trouver des informations difficiles à dénicher sur le web, GPT-6.2 a surpassé son prédécesseur à tous les niveaux de raisonnement testés, avec un taux de réussite de 64,5 % contre 54,4 % au niveau le plus élevé.
Dans la pratique, si vous lui demandez de comparer des hôtels, par exemple, ChatGPT devrait mieux hiérarchiser les résultats en fonction de vos priorités, qu'il s'agisse du prix, de l'emplacement ou des prestations proposées. L'IA devrait aussi mieux identifier les situations dans lesquelles il serait utile de vous proposer un suivi, comme vous prévenir lorsque le prix d'un produit baisse.
Une IA plus fiable, mais aussi moins souple
Dans le rapport d'évaluation qui accompagne le lancement de GPT-6.2, OpenAI fait état d'une baisse importante des hallucinations lorsque le modèle est confronté à des requêtes pour lesquelles des internautes avaient déjà signalé des erreurs factuelles. Les résultats sont en revanche beaucoup moins tranchés sur les autres questions factuelles et dans des domaines sensibles comme la médecine, le droit ou la finance, où les taux d'erreur restent comparables à ceux de GPT-6 Sol.
Plus paradoxal, si GPT-6.2 respecte mieux les consignes de réécriture d'un texte ou de modification du code informatique, il a aussi davantage tendance à privilégier les règles de comportement qu'OpenAI lui impose par défaut, y compris lorsque les internautes lui demandent de s'en écarter de façon légitime. Sur les tests destinés à mesurer cette capacité, le taux de réussite a chuté de 60,6 % à 48,6 %. Invité à défendre un point de vue sur un sujet controversé, le nouveau modèle est ainsi plus enclin à exposer aussi les arguments de la partie adverse, même lorsque l'exercice ne le demande pas.
OpenAI a par ailleurs renforcé les protections destinées aux mineurs, en intégrant ces exigences de sécurité à l'entraînement du modèle. Sur les conversations difficiles portant sur la dépendance affective à l'IA et les troubles du comportement alimentaire, le taux de conformité aux règles de protection des moins de 18 ans est respectivement passé de 77,1 % à 94,3 % et de 77,2 % à 92,9 %. Les évaluations de sécurité générales révèlent toutefois une légère hausse des refus opposés à des requêtes légitimes.
Le déploiement de GPT-6.2 a débuté à l'échelle mondiale pour les abonnements Plus, Pro, Business et Enterprise, sous réserve des paramètres définis par les administrateurs dans le cas de cette dernière offre. La mise à jour concerne le mode Instant ainsi que les niveaux de raisonnement Medium, High et Extra High, selon la formule souscrite. Le modèle GPT-6 Pro, propulsé par GPT-6 Astra, demeure inchangé, tandis que les générations précédentes de GPT (5.6 et 6) restent accessibles depuis le sélecteur de modèles. Les offres Free et Go ne sont pour l'heure pas concernées par ce déploiement, qui ne change rien non plus aux modèles déjà disponibles dans ChatGPT Work et Codex.
- Assistant IA extrêmement polyvalent
- Fonctionnalités gratuites nombreuses
- Automatisation de tâches complexes

articles.title: Le rival du MacBook signé Google déçoit : voici le gros défaut de l’Asus Google Book 14 (test vidéo)
articles.text:
L’Asus Google Book 14 est l’un des tout premiers à faire tourner Google Book OS, la fameuse fusion entre Android et Chrome OS promise depuis des années par le géant de Mountain View.
Une intégration matérielle réussie mais un logiciel capricieux
Du point de vue matériel, la proposition s’avère solide : un châssis en métal soigné, une puce Intel récente et performante, ainsi qu’un bel écran OLED montant jusqu’à 120 Hz. Pourtant, la partie logicielle gâche en partie l’expérience. Google Book OS promettait une continuité transparente avec votre smartphone Android, à la manière de l’écosystème Apple, permettant par exemple de lancer ses applications mobiles dans des fenêtres dédiées ou de synchroniser ses tâches en un instant. Malheureusement, la réalité s’accompagne de nombreux ralentissements et de bugs de connexion.
Le Black Friday est lancé sur l’univers Apple. Sur Back Market, profitez de promotions sur les iPhone, MacBook, iPad, AirPods et Apple Watch. Chaque appareil est soumis à jusqu’à 100 points de contrôle qualité et est livré avec une garantie de 12 mois. De quoi profiter de performances comparables à celles d’un produit neuf.
« Les applications de mon téléphone lancées sur le Google Book affichaient d’abord un écran noir, tout simplement. »
Le système refuse également d’activer ces fonctions de partage de connexion cellulaire si vous êtes en déplacement, ce qui limite grandement son intérêt pour les travailleurs nomades.
L’intelligence artificielle Gemini rate son entrée
Google insiste beaucoup sur l’intégration de son intelligence artificielle Gemini. Quelques fonctionnalités bien pensées font leur apparition, à l’image de Rambler, une dictée vocale intelligente capable de corriger vos hésitations à la volée, ou du curseur magique, conçu pour interroger l’assistant sur le contenu affiché à l’écran.
« Google nous promet un OS conçu pour Gemini. Et au final, Gemini, c’est juste un assistant posé par-dessus comme une application installée sur votre smartphone. »
Pour autant, l’intégration reste décevante. L’assistant IA se contente d’ouvrir une fenêtre d’application classique au lieu de modifier directement vos fichiers. Les fonctions d’agent autonome, censées ranger vos dossiers à votre place, ne sont tout simplement pas disponibles en France pour le moment.
Dans l’ensemble, le système souffre d’un manque persistant d’optimisation. Les applications Android s’adaptent mal au grand écran de 14 pouces, tandis que l’explorateur de fichiers régresse par rapport à l’ancien Chrome OS en rendant impossible la connexion à un serveur réseau NAS. Bref, si l’Asus Google Book 14 s’impose comme une belle machine physique, son système d’exploitation demande encore de sérieuses mises à jour avant de pouvoir inquiéter Windows et macOS.

articles.title: Fritzbox am Black Friday: 9 gute Deals rund um Router und Repeater
articles.text:
Black Friday: Diese 9 Fritzboxen, Repeater und Co. sind wirklich günstig
Hinweis: Wir haben in diesem Artikel Provisions-Links verwendet und sie durch "*" gekennzeichnet. Erfolgt über diese Links eine Bestellung, erhält t3n.de eine Provision.
In vielen Bereichen sind Hardware-Produkte aktuell teuer wie selten. Der Zeitraum rund um den Black Friday ist dabei eine gute Gelegenheit, beim Einkauf ein wenig zu sparen. Neben Apple– und Samsung-Geräten sowie Homeoffice-Gadgets sind 2026 auch zahlreiche Produkte vom Router-Hersteller Fritz reduziert. Das Angebot umfasst nicht nur Fritzboxen, sondern auch entsprechende Repeater und Gadgets fürs Smarthome. Nicht immer sind die Preise aber auch gut. Wir zeigen euch Angebote, die sich wirklich lohnen.
Fritzboxen bei Amazon, Otto und Saturn
Ganz vorn stehen zwei Fritboxen, die unter anderem bei Amazon reduziert sind und auch anderswo aktuell kaum günstiger zu bekommen sind.
Fritzbox 7690 als Router und Smarthome-Zentrale
Ihr surft zu Hause via DSL, wollt aber demnächst wechseln? Bei der Fritbox 7690 spielt das keine Rolle. Sie eignet sich für den handelsüblichen DSL-Anschluss, lässt sich laut Hersteller aber auch am Kabel- oder Glasfasermodem betreiben. Der Router unterstützt den aktuellen Wi-Fi-7-Standard mit theoretisch möglichen Übertragungsgeschwindigkeiten von bis zu 7,1 Gigabit pro Sekunde. Dazu unterstützt sie die Mesh-Produkte des Herstellers und dient dank DECT und Zigbee auch als Smarthome-Zentrale. Normalerweise kostet die Box rund 280 Euro. Derzeit ist sie bei Amazon, Notebooksbilliger.de und Otto aber auf 250 Euro reduziert. Das liegt unter dem zuletzt gemessenen Durchschnittspreis von Idealo (93 Tage, 258 Euro).
Fritzbox 5690 für Glasfaser-Nutzer
Auch die Fritzbox 5690 bietet Wi-Fi 7 (bis zu 6,4 Gigabit pro Sekunde). Sie eignet sich jedoch nur für Glasfaser-Nutzer:innen. Dabei unterstützt die Box die Standards AON und GPON. Ein externes Modem ist für die Verbindung nicht notwendig. Gleichwohl könnt ihr sie aber daran anschließen, wenn ihr das bevorzugt. Wie die 7690 unterstützt die 5690 DECT und damit entsprechende Telefone, aber auch ausgewähltes Smarthome-Zubehör des Herstellers. Ein Zigbee-Hub fehlt allerdings. Die Fritzbox 5690 kostet normalerweise ebenfalls 280 Euro. Rund um den Black Friday bekommt ihr sie für rund 247 Euro bei Amazon und Otto, oder für 249 Euro bei Saturn.
Mesh-Sets und Repeater
Passend zu den Boxen sind zudem Reichweitenverstärker (Repeater) und entsprechende Mesh-Sets vergünstigt, mit denen ihr euer Netzwerk auch in entlegene Räume erweitert.
Fritz Repeater 2700 mit Wi-Fi 7
Dazu gehört der Fritz Repeater, der ebenso Wi‑Fi 7 unterstützt. Im Einsatz übernimmt er laut Hersteller direkt die Einstellungen des Routers. Zudem ist ein 2,5-Gigabit-LAN-Anschluss verbaut, falls ihr die kabelgebundene Vernetzung bevorzugt. Mit 150 Euro ist so ein Reichweitenverstärker eigentlich nicht erschwinglich. Zum Black Friday sinkt der Preis unter anderem bei Amazon und Otto aber auf rund 120 Euro.
Fritz Repeater 6000
Der Fritz Repeater 6000 unterstützt „nur“ Wi-Fi 6, unterstützt dafür aber drei statt der normalen zwei Bänder. So soll er dabei helfen, auch große Mengen schnell durchs WLAN zu befördern. Darüber hinaus bietet er dieselben Vorzüge wie der Repeater 2700. Für die Einrichtung soll ein Knopfdruck genügen. Ein LAN-Anschluss ist an Bord. Derzeit ist der Repeater bei Otto und Amazon auf rund 200 Euro reduziert und sonst nur beim Hersteller für diesen Preis zu bekommen.
Fritz Mesh Set 1600: Repeater im Doppelpack
Wer mehr als zwei Zimmer hat, profitiert von einem sogenannten Mesh-Set. Dabei handelt es sich im Prinzip um mehrere Repeater im Paket. Zum Black Friday gibt es bei Amazon ein solches Set mit zwei Repeatern für rund 153 statt 199 Euro zu kaufen. Das Fritz Mesh Set 1600 unterstützt Wi-Fi 6, die einzelnen Repeater haben allerdings keine LAN-Eingänge.
DECT-Telefon, Heizkörperthermostat und mehr Zubehör
Fritz Fon X6 als Steuerzentrale
Das Fritz Fon X6 sieht aus wie ein handelsübliches Festnetztelefon. Es bietet jedoch viele Funktionen, die man vom Smartphone kennt. So könnt ihr bei Bedarf Podcasts darüber hören oder eure Smarthome-Geräte von Fritz steuern. Grundsätzlich funktioniert das Fon X6 auch mit anderen DECT‑Basisstationen. Das volle Potenzial schöpft ihr aber in Verbindung mit kompatiblen Fritzboxen aus. Zuletzt kostete es rund 90 Euro. Bei Amazon könnt ihr derzeit zehn Euro sparen. Damit liegt es genau auf dem Schnitt der vergangenen 185 Tage.
Fritz Thermo 302: Smarte Heizungssteuerung
Gerade im Winter kann ein smartes Heizthermostat von Vorteil sein, wenn etwa das Arbeitszimmer schon vor Dienstantritt automatisch aufgeheizt wird, sich die Heizung über Nacht aber automatisch wieder abschaltet. Das Thermostat verbindet sich per DECT mit der Fritzbox, funktioniert also nicht in anderen Smarthome-Systemen. Über die Oberfläche des Routers könnt ihr unter anderem Heizpläne festlegen. DAs E-Ink-Display zeigt jeweils die aktuelle Temperatur an. Das Thermostat sollte auf gängige Heizkörper passen. Derzeit ist es bei Amazon, Saturn und Otto auf 45 Euro. Günstiger war es in den vergangenen Wochen nicht.
Fritz Smart Control 350 erkennt offene Fenster
Passend dazu ist der Tür-Fenster-Sensor Fritz Smart Control 350 bei Amazon auf rund 26 Euro reduziert. Über die richtigen Regeln lassen sich die Heizkörperthermostate dann so einstellen, dass sie sich automatisch abschalten, wenn ihr etwa das Fenster zum Lüften öffnet. Alternativ lässt es sich auch an Türen oder am Briefkasten anbringen. Wie das Thermostat ist der Sensor nur mit DECT kompatibel.
Fritz Smart Control 440: Die Universalfernbedienung
Bis zu zwölf Geräte könnt ihr über die vier Tasten am Fritz Smart Control 440 steuern. Dazu gehören smarte Thermostaten, Steckdosen oder Glühlampen. Auch hier liegt der Fokus auf der DECT‑Verbindung zur Fritzbox. Es ist laut Hersteller aber möglich, trotzdem Zigbee-Geräte über das Smart Control 440 zu steuern. Preislich liegt das Gadget normalerweise bei 69 Euro. Bei Amazon ist es derzeit für rund 46 Euro zu haben – aktuell der beste Online-Preis.

articles.title: Radware discloses breach exposing customer cloud access keys
articles.text:
Cybersecurity company Radware says attackers gained access to some of its customers' account details and cloud access keys through an unsecured internal Cloud WAF (Web Application Firewall) management API that was left exposed online.
Founded in 1996 and headquartered in Tel Aviv, Radware now provides application delivery and DDoS protection services to more than 12,500 enterprise and telecom carrier customers worldwide.
In a root cause analysis report shared by an anonymous source with BleepingComputer, Radware says it blocked the originating IP address and access to the internal management API. The company also revoked and replaced all internal account credentials after detecting the breach on Thursday, ten hours after the initial unauthorized API access.
"On 19 November 2026, an unauthorized party accessed an internal-only Cloud WAF management API that was reachable from the Public Internet without requiring authentication," Radware said.
"The confirmed information potentially accessed includes customer contact details, and for a subset of customers, the credentials configured for log export into their self-managed storage (AWS S3, Azure Blob Storage, or SFTP)."
The company added that the breach did not expose WAF traffic inspection, certificates, end-users’ data, customer application traffic, or cloud DDoS services and data.
Customers advised to rotate exposed keys
It also "strongly" advised affected AppSec (WAF, BOT) customers to rotate Cloud WAF log export credentials (including Azure Blob Storage keys or SAS tokens, AWS S3 access keys, or SFTP credentials) as soon as possible and review access logs on their cloud storage accounts for unexpected access since at least November 19.
The company is still investigating the breach and whether any API keys or other customer information exposed in the incident were used without authorization, and said it has already received reports from customers about AWS alerts for an unfamiliar IP address attempting to access their log-export buckets.
"WAF traffic inspection and protection have continued without interruption, and we have not identified an impact on the availability or protection of customer applications and services," Radware added. "We have found no evidence to date of changes to customer security policies or of access to customer application traffic."
Radware has yet to issue a public statement regarding the incident or file a breach report with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
BleepingComputer also reached out to a Radware spokesperson with questions about the incident, but a response was not immediately available.
