articles.title: Pour son VPN, Firefox rajoute un split tunneling par site
articles.text:
Le VPN gratuit de Firefox peut désormais être activé ou coupé pour des sites précis. Mozilla ajoute donc une forme de split tunneling à son navigateur.
Mozilla vient de publier Firefox 161 sur ses serveurs et le lancement officiel est prévu aujourd'hui. L'équipe s’est focalisée sur les améliorations du VPN intégré en apportant davantage de flexibilité.
Un VPN limité aux sites que vous choisissez
Le split tunneling, ou « tunnel fractionné », consiste à trier le trafic qui passe ou non par le VPN activé sur le système. D’ordinaire, cela permet de couper le VPN sur certaines applications. Certaines recevront donc votre vraie adresse IP tandis que d’autres verront celles du serveur géré par le fournisseur.
Firefox 161 applique ce principe site par site. Selon Mozilla, le VPN ne tourne qu’aux endroits où l’on veut plus de confidentialité ou une autre localisation. Il sera par exemple possible de l’activer en consultant sa messagerie ou pour éviter le ciblage géolocalisé sur les réseaux communautaires ou sites marchands.
- Gratuit et open source
- Protection renforcée contre le pistage
- Nombreuses extensions et personnalisations
Avec des mises à jour désormais passées à un rythme bi-mensuel pour le navigateur, les travaux s’accélèrent sur le VPN. Nous rapportions en mars, lors de son arrivée avec Firefox 149, qu'il s'agissait techniquement d'un proxy, c’est-à-dire un intermédiaire qui relaie les requêtes web. Il ne protège alors que le navigateur, avec un relais unique, un serveur choisi automatiquement et 50 Go par mois. Deux mois plus tard , avec Firefox 151, il devenait possible de choisir le pays de connexion. Ce nouveau réglage apporte donc encore davantage de flexibilité et devrait par ailleurs permettre de mieux gérer le quota de 50 Go mensuels.
Firefox 161 apporte d’autres nouveautés. Un raccourci permet de copier l’adresse de l’onglet actif. Il est possible de le configurer dans les paramètres, sous « Personnaliser les raccourcis clavier ». Une section de thèmes classiques arrive aussi, avec le thème Proton des anciennes versions, un thème OLED et des teintes unies. L’historique importé depuis Chrome garde désormais la fréquence de visite des pages. Les sites habituels remontent donc dans les suggestions de la barre d’adresse. Enfin, Mozilla corrige des onglets qui ne se restauraient pas après un redémarrage, lorsque la session renvoyait vers un groupe d’onglets supprimé.

articles.title: OPINION: Separate the hype from reality in China’s robotics race
articles.text:
Let’s start with the obvious; most of what you’ve seen of Chinese robots is not real. If you’re like me, your Instagram feed is full of humanoids doing backflipS or folding the laundry. The conclusion is either that China has solved robotics and we (Europe) are finished, or that they have adopted everything and we are just behind.
So we went to look. In August, six of us from Extantia visited around fifteen companies across Shanghai, Hangzhou and Beijing, then walked the floor of the World Robot Conference with its 300 exhibitors.
So, what is real?
The gap between the hype and reality
Much of what you see on Instagram is AI-generated while a lot of the rest is sped up. What looks autonomous is often teleoperated, or remote controlled
The reality is this: Chinese companies sold more humanoid robots than anyone last year. Roughly 75% went to research institutes, universities and schools. Another 20% went to entertainment: the robot that greets you at the supermarket, 50 robots dancing at a Chinese New Year show. Only 5% went to real industrial applications, 5% of maybe 13,000 units.
That is 650 robots in the whole of China doing work. At home it is non-existent, and will stay so for a while. A 180 cm, heavy machine in the living room? People have babies at home (I have checked, nobody wants this).
At the same time, the hardware problem has been solved, it is game over. What China did in batteries, cars and drones, it is doing now in humanoids. The supply chain exists and government centres publish the blueprint. It is like building Lego: you buy the parts, you assemble them. And it is only going to get cheaper.
The people building humanoids built the battery and car industries first. Around 85% of what goes into a humanoid, the actuators, magnets, chips and sensors, also goes into an electric car, so the suppliers and know-how were already there. Car companies finance the founders and are often their first customers.
What has not been solved is the software that makes a robot act on its own. We visited what the Chinese call humanoid gyms: halls where 200 people spend the day folding sheets, cleaning toilets and moving boxes while the robots record every movement as training data. Every room is different so the model learns variation. Impressive, but no model yet lets a humanoid finish a job without a person in the loop, which is why so much online is teleoperated. That is an opening for anybody with the right data and engineers, including European teams.
A more basic point the videos hide: for most real jobs, the human shape is the wrong shape. For clean floors, a robot vacuum is better than legs. In a factory you want wheels, because they are cheaper and more stable, and a gripper rather than a hand. A five-fingered hand is one of the most expensive parts of a humanoid and lasts a million open and close cycles, which is not long in industry.
The essence of the work is matching each task to the right amount of automation. The robots we saw actually earning money did precisely that: robot dogs carrying a hose into a fire, machines inspecting grid infrastructure, a robot directing traffic. Not spectacular on camera, but the return exists today.
China has hardware, Europe can win on application
Founders in China also think differently. American founders, and increasingly European ones, optimise for valuation: maximum hype, ambitious technology, all eyes on the next round. Chinese founders optimise for cash. The question is not how to disrupt an industry, but how little innovation gets you to market and paid, so the real work is funded from revenue.
If a supermarket wants a greeter robot, they will sell it one. CATL and BYD, which supply over half of the world’s EV batteries, did not start with lithium iron phosphate or solid state. BYD started with rechargeable cells for toys and phones, CATL’s predecessor with batteries for consumer electronics, and that cash paid for the breakthroughs later. Northvolt took the opposite route, and we all know what happened there.
There is a catch, of course. Europe depends on China for raw materials, batteries and components, and the debate about tariffs and export controls is justified.
But the dependence runs both ways. The Chinese car market is in a severe price war and most companies in it are losing money at home. When we told exhibitors we were European buyers, their eyes lit up. They need our market. Even China’s newly published five-year plan assumes these companies grow through exports, and with the US closed, that means Europe.
So a European company trying to beat China at manufacturing robot hardware is placing a bad bet. Better to benefit from China than compete with it: if my parts come from China, every fall in their costs improves my margins. The opportunity for Europe is not building the best humanoid. It is taking the best hardware available and putting it to work where we have the know-how and the customers: construction, heavy industry, petrochemicals and facility management. The more an industry has declined in Europe, the more automation can change its economics. That is the real case for reshoring.
Three things I tell our founders
First, have a China strategy. Competitor slides I see usually list only American companies, because the information firewall between Europe and China is real. Decide whether you are sourcing from China, partnering there, selling there or competing with it. You cannot build a hardware company without that answer.
Second, go there in person. See the factories, meet the suppliers and sit across from the founders you will compete with or buy from. No report or video replaces a week on the ground.
Third, deliver value now and automate later. Start with teleoperation if you need to. A team that stays in the lab until the autonomy is perfect may build something brilliant in five years for a market that has already been taken.
So, founders: what is your China strategy?

articles.title: GoFundMe confirmó que un atacante accedió a datos personales de donantes de organizaciones sin fines de lucro
articles.text:
GoFundMe confirmó que una persona no autorizada accedió a información personal de donantes y simpatizantes de organizaciones sin fines de lucro a través de GoFundMe Pro, su plataforma para esas entidades.
Según el aviso, el atacante entró a la interfaz de programación de GoFundMe Pro del 10 al 18 de octubre de 2026 y de nuevo el 8 y 9 de noviembre de 2026. Los datos revisados incluyen nombres, direcciones postales y números de teléfono. En algunos casos, también fechas de nacimiento u otra información que las personas habían dado de forma voluntaria en formularios de registro.
La empresa afirmó que, hasta ahora, no se accedió a las credenciales de donantes y simpatizantes. Tampoco a números completos de tarjeta, códigos de seguridad ni datos de cuentas bancarias guardados en GoFundMe Pro. GoFundMe no dijo cuántas personas están afectadas.
En un correo a las organizaciones clientes, que la empresa compartió con la revista Fortune, GoFundMe agregó que la información incluía también direcciones de correo. La compañía dijo que empezó a notificar a los afectados el 19 de noviembre de 2026 y que denunció el caso ante las fuerzas de seguridad.
A quién afectó este ciberataque que sufrió GoFundMe
El incidente se limita a GoFundMe Pro, el servicio que usan las organizaciones para gestionar donaciones y contactos. El aviso no habla de las campañas personales que cualquier usuario crea para reunir dinero, y GoFundMe aclara que las notificaciones no mencionan a ninguna organización por su nombre.
Un punto del ataque tocó a Salesforce, el software de gestión de clientes que algunas organizaciones conectan con GoFundMe Pro. Según el correo a los clientes que citó la publicación Chronicle of Philanthropy, el atacante accedió a credenciales de esa conexión y pudo usarlas para entrar a los registros de esas organizaciones en Salesforce.
Salesforce explicó a The NonProfit Times que desactivó la aplicación conectada de GoFundMe Pro como medida de precaución, tras detectar un uso sospechoso de las claves de acceso del proveedor externo.
La empresa precisó que el problema no surgió de una falla en su plataforma central. La conexión seguía desactivada el 20 de noviembre de 2026, según la página de estado de GoFundMe.
GoFundMe sugirió a los clientes que usan esa conexión cambiar todas las claves y credenciales guardadas en Salesforce y revisar la actividad de las cuentas en busca de movimientos desconocidos.
Qué otras plataformas de donaciones resultó atacada
GoFundMe no fue la única plataforma afectada. DonorPerfect, un software de gestión de donantes con más de 11.000 clientes, desconectó sus sistemas el 10 de noviembre tras detectar actividad no autorizada. Su presidenta, Lauren Sheehan, dijo a Fortune que sospecha del uso de bots de inteligencia artificial, y que el acceso inicial fue su sitio web de marketing.
Un portavoz de GoFundMe Pro dijo que hay “razones sólidas para creer” que otros atacantes intentan entrar a plataformas similares del sector. Sheehan afirmó que DonorPerfect comparte registros y detalles de vigilancia con competidores y socios. DonorPerfect dijo que las donaciones se procesan con normalidad, aunque su conexión con otros servicios, entre ellos GoFundMe, seguía sin funcionar.
Cómo los donantes pueden evitar riesgos
GoFundMe aseguró que los pagos de donaciones no se interrumpieron. Cybernews advirtió que nombres, teléfonos y direcciones pueden servir para estafas de ingeniería social, como mensajes falsos que simulen ser de la plataforma o de un organizador para pedir más dinero o verificar una cuenta.
Una de las organizaciones afectadas pidió a sus donantes cambiar contraseñas con frecuencia y desconfiar de correos, llamadas o mensajes inesperados que soliciten datos personales o bancarios.
La investigación de GoFundMe, con ayuda de especialistas externos en ciberseguridad, sigue en curso. La empresa envió avisos por correo postal a personas de Dakota del Norte y Washington y notificó a los reguladores de esos dos estados.

articles.title: Banks and card networks raid Safaricom, Airtel for talent
articles.text:
African banks and Visa have poached at least six senior executives from telecoms and mobile money companies this year, bringing in leaders from Safaricom, M‑PESA Africa, Airtel Money, and MTN to run businesses spanning retail banking, payments, and technology.
Four of the six hires came from Safaricom or M‑PESA Africa. The appointments show how competition over who handles everyday payments is changing where financial companies hire.
Mobile money operators have built merchant networks and used them to extend wallets into savings, lending, and investments. Banks are now trying to bring more of those activities into their own apps, while Visa is looking for more ways to reach customers and merchants who already use mobile wallets.
Kenya’s banks and telcos have been recruiting from one another for at least a decade. Safaricom hired Ronald Webb from Equity Bank to run its financial services business in 2016. It recruited Michael Mutiga from Citi in 2022 and Esther Masese Waititu from KCB in 2023. Waititu’s move set off another hire. KCB turned to NCBA for John Okulo to replace her as director of corporate banking.
This year, Mutiga returned to banking as Stanbic Kenya’s chief executive, and Waititu went to Visa. Absa’s two hires from M‑PESA Africa show how the competition has widened. The expertise Safaricom once sought from banks is now being recruited out of mobile money businesses to run retail banking and payments operations.
Absa bets on payments
In April, Absa Group, South Africa’s third-largest lender, appointed Sitoyo Lopokoiyit as chief executive for personal and private banking. He previously led M‑PESA Africa, which served more than 56 million active customers across seven markets.
Kenny Fihla, Absa Group CEO, said in February that the leadership changes, including Lopokoiyit’s appointment, reflected Absa’s ambition to bring in “expertise from outside the firm to close the gaps in key capability areas.”
In October, Absa recruited Naima Yusuf, M‑PESA Africa’s executive head of products, to lead Absa Pay. Yusuf had spent 19 years at Safaricom.
Between the two hires, Absa launched Absa Next in Kenya, an app that offers payments, savings, investments, and credit, and is open to people without an existing Absa account. Kenya is the first market in the group’s wider digital expansion. Safaricom’s M‑PESA revenue rose 13.6% to KES 100.1 billion ($769.1 million) in the six months to September, showing the scale at which the incumbent operates.
“Rather than digitising traditional banking, we have reimagined the banking experience around our customers’ goals, behaviours and aspirations,” Yusuf Omari, Absa Bank Kenya managing director, said on the launch of Absa Next.
Kenyan banks already reach mobile money users through partnerships. NCBA underwrites M‑Shwari loans, and KCB underwrites KCB M‑PESA loans, both available through Safaricom’s platform. An app such as Absa Next gives a bank a direct channel to customers.
Visa raids Safaricom and Airtel
Visa appointed Anne Kinuthia‑Otieno, the former managing director of Airtel Money Kenya, as vice-president and head of East Africa in August.
In November, it named Esther Masese Waititu, former Safaricom chief financial services officer, as senior vice-president and group country manager for Southern and Eastern Africa. Kinuthia‑Otieno’s remit covers seven markets, and Waititu’s covers 24.
“Esther brings deep industry expertise, a strong understanding of the region and a proven ability to build businesses and partnerships at scale,” Tareq Muhmood, Visa regional president, said on hiring Waititu.
Visa’s interest in mobile money expertise differs from Absa’s. A bank can use its app to sell loans and savings products directly. Visa grows its payments business by getting more transactions onto its network, which depends in part on where merchants accept it and which payment options banks, fintechs and wallet operators offer.
Hiring executives who have managed large wallets gives Visa experience on the other side of those commercial relationships.
Other appointments show demand for telecoms experience outside payments. Stanbic Bank Kenya hired Mutiga as chief executive after four years at Safaricom, where he led business development and strategy.
Mutiga had previously spent 15 years at Citi. In South Africa, Nedbank appointed Nikos Angelopoulos as group chief information officer in September, drawing on his experience overseeing technology strategy and investment across 16 markets at MTN.

articles.title: NASA may get $2 billion boost as White House seeks to accelerate Artemis
articles.text:
As part of ongoing wrangling over the US budget for the current fiscal year, the White House on Monday night sent a list of budget exceptions to Congress that it seeks in the near term for the federal government (PDF).
The list of so-called “funding anomalies” is dominated largely by appropriations for the Department of Defense, including the Golden Dome missile defense program championed by the Trump administration. However, among the highest non-defense exceptions is $2 billion for NASA’s Artemis program for a “higher rate of operations.”
The funding represents a significant 25 percent boost for NASA’s Artemis program, which received approximately $7.8 billion in fiscal year 2026. Technically, the White House is seeking to increase the annualized funding rate for Artemis to $9.8 billion, rather than immediately providing NASA with an additional $2 billion. It comes at a time when it is increasingly clear that China’s lunar ambitions are as expansive as NASA’s, and there is a good chance the country reaches the Moon with astronauts before NASA can get back there.
Another continuing resolution?
Fiscal year 2027 began on October 1 of this year, but the US Congress and White House have not agreed upon a budget. The government, including NASA, has been operating on a “continuing resolution” since that time. The existing continuing resolution remains in effect until December 11, by which time the parties need to agree to a final budget or another continuing resolution, or else the government will shut down.
Given the broad disagreement in funding priorities, it seems most likely that Congress will settle on another continuing resolution, punting a budget deal into the new year and a new Democratic-led House and Senate. The release of the White House “anomalies” document signals to Congress which priorities the Trump administration wants to see addressed in a new continuing resolution that would be agreed to in the coming weeks, which the president would have to sign.
The budget plus-up for Artemis appears to be a significant win for NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman, who arrived at the space agency 11 months ago, after the White House had already put together its “President’s Budget request” for the fiscal year 2027 process. This is the first time he has had a chance to work with the Trump administration on budget priorities, and in doing so has convinced officials that NASA deserves more funding in its race back to the Moon.

articles.title: Electric truck startup Harbinger gets financing boost from Palmer Luckey's bank
articles.text:
Harbinger has tapped Palmer Luckey’s Erebor Bank as a new source of capital as the electric truck startup looks to diversify how it funds its growth and an expanding portfolio of products spanning autonomous vehicles, energy storage, and defense.
Los Angeles-based Harbinger said Tuesday it secured more than $100 million in financing, including a convertible note from Pinegrove Venture Partners and senior debt from Erebor Bank, which launched in February 2026 and recently surpassed $1 billion in loans, according to the Financial Times.
The new financing comes less than three weeks after Harbinger raised $240 million in a Series D funding round co-led by Tiger Global, Capricorn’s Technology Impact Fund, and Ridgeline. FedEx, which ordered 2,000 trucks from Harbinger, also participated.
Harbinger co-founder and chief executive John Harris explained in a statement that building an industrial technology company at scale requires a “different financing approach,” adding that the capital needed to ramp up production and deliver vehicles to customers shouldn’t have to come entirely from equity. Harris noted that major vehicle and aerospace manufacturers have long relied on debt financing to support their production operations.
Erebor is now Harbinger’s primary banking partner. In a statement, Luckey said traditional lenders have struggled to support the unique capital needs of businesses developing real technology and creating U.S. jobs.
“Harbinger is exactly the kind of business we built Erebor to back: an American manufacturer building world-class technology,” he said.

articles.title: Preview abxylute M6 — hands-on do protótipo
articles.text:
O celular vira um handheld deslizante
O abxylute M6 é um controle magnético que encaixa atrás do celular e desliza para o lado, revelando o conjunto completo de botões — a mesma ideia do Sony Xperia Play, refeita para a era do MagSafe. Fechado, ele parece uma capa grossa. Aberto, vira um gamepad com dois analógicos, D-pad, ABXY, gatilhos lineares e vibração.
A proposta resolve um incômodo conhecido de quem joga no celular: o controle telescópico tradicional é desconfortável de carregar, e o controle full-size obriga a levar dois aparelhos na mochila. O M6 consegue ficar junto do celular o tempo todo.
A abxylute levou quase três anos para chegar a este formato, que sucede o M4 — menor e mais portátil, mas apertado para sessões longas. O M6 é maior, tem analógicos maiores, grips magnéticos destacáveis e vibração, sem deixar de caber no bolso de uma jaqueta.
A unidade testada é uma amostra de engenharia (T2), não a versão final de produção. Tudo o que está descrito aqui vale para esse estágio — e a própria fabricante lista um conjunto de ajustes já previstos para a linha de montagem, detalhados mais abaixo.
Ficha técnica
| Item | Especificação | 
| Conexão | Bluetooth sem fio (5.3) | 
| Modos | NS (Nintendo Switch), XInput (Xbox), PS (PlayStation) e Mapeamento Virtual | 
| Analógicos | Capacitivos, desenvolvidos com a K-Silver; 20° de inclinação; clique L3/R3 | 
| Gatilhos | Lineares Hall Effect, 5,5 mm de curso, com modo de acionamento rápido | 
| Botões frontais | Membrana, de acionamento silencioso | 
| D-pad | 8 direções por padrão, alternável para 4 direções | 
| Vibração | Motor linear no eixo Z, 4 níveis (100%, 70%, 40% e desligado) | 
| Sensores | Giroscópio de 6 eixos | 
| Bateria | 500 mAh, até 10 horas de jogo | 
| Suporte do trilho | Celular com capa de até cerca de 300 g | 
| Extras | Botão Z programável, Turbo (5, 10 ou 20 acionamentos por segundo), grips magnéticos destacáveis, ilha magnética móvel, iluminação ambiente difusa | 
Dados da página oficial da campanha.
Vale separar duas coisas que costumam ser confundidas na divulgação de controles: o Hall Effect do M6 está nos gatilhos, não nos analógicos. Os sticks usam tecnologia capacitiva, outra abordagem sem contato físico. As duas dispensam o potenciômetro que causa o drift clássico, mas não são a mesma coisa.
O trilho é o coração do projeto
O componente mais difícil do M6 não é eletrônico: é o trilho. O M6 precisa sustentar um celular moderno com capa, e a abxylute afirma ter desenvolvido o mecanismo com um fabricante que já produziu trilhos para Nokia e Sony, projetado para aguentar cerca de 300 g.
Na prática, o trilho tem amortecimento dos dois lados e um movimento que trava no início e completa sozinho depois de alguns centímetros.
Três decisões de design merecem destaque:
- Ilha magnética móvel: a área de fixação desliza para os lados, o que acomoda celulares com módulos de câmera grandes e permite até encaixe na vertical.
- Grips destacáveis: combinam força magnética com trava mecânica e só saem num ângulo específico. Com eles, o controle ganha pegada de gamepad full-size; sem eles, volta a caber no bolso.
- Iluminação difusa: a luz reflete na superfície em vez de apontar para os olhos, e muda de cor conforme o modo ativo — roxo no PS, magenta no Switch e azul no XInput.
A própria fabricante desaconselha o uso com celulares dobráveis: são maiores e exigem mais da fixação magnética, e a empresa prefere não prometer compatibilidade.
Analógicos, gatilhos e botões
Analógicos capacitivos, não Hall Effect
Os sticks do M6 são capacitivos, desenvolvidos em parceria com a K-Silver — a mesma linha estreada no abxylute One Pro. A escolha tem um motivo prático: o controle inteiro é magnético, e a fabricante cita justamente a resistência à interferência magnética como um dos critérios do componente. Um stick Hall Effect, que lê posição por campo magnético, conviveria pior com os ímãs de fixação logo atrás.
O ganho prático é o mesmo que se espera de um stick sem contato físico: nada de desgaste de potenciômetro, origem do drift clássico. Vale dizer que um teste de dias não comprova ausência de drift: drift é problema de desgaste, que aparece depois de meses. O que dá para afirmar é que não há deriva nem zona morta perceptível no estado de fábrica.
Apesar do tamanho compacto, o stick atinge 20° de inclinação — perto dos 23° de um analógico full-size — e aceita clique L3/R3. O recorte em degrau ao redor libera espaço para o polegar sem a borda alta atrapalhar.
Os botões de cima são dois pares diferentes
Essa é a distinção que escapa na maioria das análises rápidas. O M6 tem quatro controles na parte superior, em dois pares de natureza distinta:
| Par | Tipo | Comportamento | 
| LB / RB (ombros) | Digital | Liga/desliga, com clique | 
| LT / RT (gatilhos) | Linear Hall Effect, 5,5 mm | Analógico, com leitura de intensidade | 
Os gatilhos ainda aceitam um modo de acionamento rápido, que registra pressão total já no primeiro toque: útil em tiro e ação, desnecessário em corrida.
Botões frontais de membrana
Os ABXY e o D-pad usam membrana, não microswitch mecânico. A abxylute trata isso como recurso: o argumento é jogar na cama ou em quarto compartilhado sem o estalo do microswitch. O trade-off existe e é honesto: quem vem de controle mecânico sente menos retorno tátil no fim do curso.
O layout segue o padrão Xbox (A embaixo, B à direita, X à esquerda, Y em cima) e, no modo PS, as posições mapeiam os equivalentes do DualShock. Nos jogos testados não houve diferença de precisão entre os quatro botões.
O D-pad sai de fábrica em 8 direções e pode ir para 4 direções com M + direcional esquerdo — configuração que fica salva mesmo depois de desligar. Os sticks também alternam entre saída quadrada (padrão) e circular.
Como ele se comporta em jogo
Escolhi dois gêneros que punem controle ruim por motivos opostos: luta, que exige timing exato em sequências de comandos, e corrida, que exige modulação fina de pressão.
Luta: o teste de latência
Em The King of Fighters, a resposta foi rápida mesmo por Bluetooth — e esse era o ponto de dúvida. Jogo de luta é o pior cenário para conexão sem fio: um atraso de poucos quadros entre o comando e a tela já quebra a execução de combos e golpes especiais. Não houve atraso perceptível que atrapalhasse a jogabilidade, nem perda de entrada em sequências encadeadas.
Um ponto de atenção que a própria abxylute documenta nesta amostra: pressão excessiva no D-pad, ou deslizar o dedo lateralmente sobre ele, pode acionar botões vizinhos sem querer. É exatamente o tipo de movimento que um jogo de luta exige o tempo todo, e a empresa afirma que vários componentes serão ajustados na versão de produção.
Quem joga luta deve notar outras duas coisas: o D-pad em 8 direções é o padrão e é o que se quer aqui, e o Turbo — que faz até 20 acionamentos por segundo — é recurso de uso questionável em partidas online competitivas.
Corrida: o teste de modulação
Em GRID, os gatilhos lineares mostraram boa precisão para acelerar e frear, com níveis intermediários reconhecíveis de intensidade: dá para dosar o acelerador em vez de ter só ligado e desligado. Os 5,5 mm de curso ajudam: é bastante coisa para um controle desta espessura.
O detalhe que torna esse resultado mais relevante é que a função de calibração dos gatilhos ainda não está totalmente implementada no firmware desta amostra, o que pode fazer alguns valores aparecerem imprecisos em ferramentas de leitura. Mesmo assim, a modulação em jogo se manteve consistente.
Os analógicos não apresentaram deriva nem zona morta — esperado num aparelho recém-saído da fábrica, e o motivo pelo qual a promessa de durabilidade dos sticks sem contato só se confirma com meses de uso.
Macro, giroscópio e mapeamento virtual
O M6 tem um botão Z dedicado, que sai de fábrica como clique do analógico esquerdo (L3) e pode virar macro. Segurando M + Z por dois segundos, o controle entra em modo de gravação e aceita sequências com sticks, ABXY, ombros, gatilhos, direcional e botões de sistema.
O giroscópio de 6 eixos também simula movimento de stick: M + L3 ou M + R3 por dois segundos transfere a mira para o sensor. A posição em que o controle está no momento da ativação vira a referência inicial, e a configuração se perde ao desligar.
Para jogos sem suporte nativo ao controle, o M6 faz mapeamento virtual pelo próprio firmware, traduzindo botões físicos em toques na tela. Esse recurso é exclusivo do Android — no iPhone, jogos só de toque continuam sem suporte.
O modo certo muda conforme o que você vai jogar, e a troca é manual:
| Cenário | Android | iPhone | 
| Jogos nativos com suporte a controle | XInput | XInput | 
| Jogos nativos só com toque | Mapeamento Virtual | Sem suporte | 
| PS Remote Play | PS | PS | 
| Moonlight e GeForce NOW | XInput | XInput | 
| Xbox Cloud Gaming | XInput | — | 
| Emuladores PPSSPP e RetroArch | PS | PS | 
| Emuladores de GBA | Nintendo Switch | Nintendo Switch (iGBA/Delta) | 
A vibração funciona nos três modos — o que não é regra em controle mobile — e tem quatro níveis ajustáveis pelo próprio controle, com M + direcional para cima ou para baixo.
Há ainda um aplicativo próprio da abxylute, previsto para abrir jogos locais e centralizar remapeamento, ajuste de sticks e gatilhos, macros, iluminação e vibração. Ele não estava disponível durante este teste.
O que ainda é protótipo
A unidade analisada é uma amostra de engenharia da série T2, e a própria abxylute distribuiu aos avaliadores a lista do que será corrigido. Registrar isso é o mínimo para que o leitor saiba o que está julgando.
No hardware:
- Pressão excessiva no D-pad, ou deslizar o dedo sobre ele, pode acionar botões vizinhos. Componentes serão ajustados na produção.
- Os botões M e O podem interferir um no outro e ficar duros em alguns casos.
- A textura gravada a laser nos dois botões de ombro está rasa demais e será mais marcada na versão final; o clique deles também deve ficar mais silencioso.
- A força de sustentação do trilho será aumentada.
- Alguns botões X podem sair levemente desalinhados, por um problema de produção de fornecedor.
- Logos e indicadores de botão ainda não foram aplicados, e as ilhas magnéticas ainda não receberam o tratamento final de superfície, marcando mais a digital.
No firmware:
- A intensidade da vibração está baixa, mesmo no nível máximo, e será reforçada.
- A calibração dos gatilhos ainda não está completa.
- O efeito de respiração do LED não está otimizado e o ajuste de brilho não foi implementado.
- O aplicativo complementar ainda não estava disponível.
Nenhum desses pontos é estrutural — são ajustes de acabamento e de software. Mas dois deles, o D-pad e a vibração fraca, afetam diretamente a experiência de jogo e precisam mesmo ser resolvidos antes da entrega.
Preço e disponibilidade
O M6 foi financiado no Kickstarter, em campanha que terminou em 15 de novembro de 2026 com US$ 264.535 arrecadados junto a 2.713 apoiadores — muito acima da meta de HK$ 10 mil, equivalente a cerca de US$ 1,3 mil. A campanha recebeu o selo Project We Love da plataforma.
Durante a campanha, o M6 ficou em torno de US$ 69 e o M5, a versão mais fina e com conexão USB-C, em cerca de US$ 65. As entregas estão previstas para novembro e dezembro de 2026, e a página do projeto segue aberta para pedidos tardios.
Não há distribuição oficial no Brasil. Quem comprar vai importar, o que acrescenta frete internacional e tributos ao preço de etiqueta.
Veredito
O M6 acerta onde controles mobile costumam errar: ele não pede que você escolha entre levar o controle e ter controles de verdade. O trilho deslizante é a engenharia mais interessante do produto, e os gatilhos lineares de 5,5 mm são um luxo para um aparelho desta espessura — fazem diferença real em corrida e em qualquer jogo que leia pressão.
A resposta por Bluetooth se mostrou suficiente até para jogo de luta, o gênero que menos perdoa latência. Os analógicos capacitivos resolvem a questão do drift por construção, ainda que a durabilidade só se comprove com tempo de uso.
O que separa este protótipo de uma recomendação fechada são dois itens que a própria fabricante reconhece: o D-pad que aciona vizinhos sob pressão lateral — justamente o movimento de quem joga luta — e a vibração fraca demais. Se a versão de produção entregar o que promete nesses dois pontos, o M6 passa a ser uma das opções mais completas da categoria.
Os botões de membrana são uma escolha de perfil, não um defeito: quem quer silêncio ganha, quem quer clique mecânico vai sentir falta.

articles.title: Vancouver considering stricter rules, oversight for AI data centres
articles.text:
Vancouver City Council has unanimously directed City of Vancouver staff to examine stronger oversight of new data centres, including third-party assessments of their effects on the surrounding area, public reporting on their operations, and ways to secure benefits for local residents.
OneCity city councillor Lucy Maloney’s member motion, approved last week after amendments, asks City staff to develop recommendations on how the municipal government should assess and regulate data centres as artificial intelligence (AI) facilities grow.
“This is about ensuring we move forward responsibly and thoughtfully. As we’ve seen in the United States, hyperscale data centres can bring significant challenges. Compared to many other industrial businesses, data centres are often far more resource intensive, placing greater strain on public infrastructure. They can consume vast quantities of water and energy while producing pollution, waste heat, and noise. They also tend to create fewer jobs than other industrial uses of the land,” said Maloney during the City Council meeting.
“Furthermore, the economic benefits to host communities often fall short of the returns realised by investors by a long shot. This is a global issue, not just limited to the U.S. Cities worldwide are sharing best practices to develop effective frameworks and ensure data centres represent the best use of valuable land,” continued Maloney.
The decision comes as local developer Westbank pursues two proposed AI data centres in highly urban and central locations of Vancouver: a brand-new, 10-storey building with 100 per cent AI data centre uses at 150 West Georgia St. in Downtown Vancouver, located immediately adjacent to BC Place Stadium and integrated with Creative Energy’s industrial steam plant on the same site (using the data centre’s excess heat to provide heating for many Downtown Vancouver buildings), and the conversion of the existing M3 office building (previously part of Hootsuite’s headquarters) at 111 East 5th Ave. (near Main Street) at the developer’s Main Alley tech campus in the Mount Pleasant Industrial Area.
Both projects are under Prime Minister Mark Carney’s Enabling Large-Scale Sovereign AI Data Centres initiative. The federal government has determined a need for such
“sovereign” facilities for national security reasons — a strategy to keep AI computing infrastructure and sensitive data in Canada and under Canadian control, reducing the reliance on foreign providers. This is intended to protect Canadian governments, post-secondary institutions, public institutions, researchers, and businesses.
Telus is no longer a partner in those Westbank projects. Earlier this month, as first reported by Daily Hive Urbanized, both companies confirmed the change, with Telus noting it is pursuing other projects elsewhere, while Westbank said it would continue to pursue the two projects under a yet-to-be-announced new partnership. A spokesperson for the projects also told Daily Hive Urbanized they support Maloney’s motion.
The existing zoning for 150 West Georgia St. already permits data centre use, while the M3 proposal is undergoing additional City staff review, after the previous makeup of City Council removed it from the July 2026 agenda and directed City staff to perform more public consultation, which is now scheduled to occur in December 2026.
City staff’s forthcoming broader review based on Maloney’s motion will also look at facilities already operating or being converted, including 175 West Cordova St., located at the southern edge of Gastown.
Under Maloney’s approved motion, City staff will examine requiring AI data centre applicants to commission third-party studies before rezoning or permitting. These would assess water use, greenhouse gas emissions, possible air pollutants, noise, and heat, along with measures to reduce those impacts, including recovering heat for other uses.
The studies would also compare the jobs a proposed AI data centre facility would create with those from other industrial activities that could reasonably use the same land.
Another part of the work will examine a business licence specifically for data centres. The proposed approach would require annual public reporting of water consumption, electricity consumption, and noise levels, while giving the municipal government a way to hold applicants accountable for commitments made during the approval process.
City staff will also explore fees or other contributions that could provide public benefits and help address the demands these data centres place on Vancouver.
The goal is to have new municipal requirements in place before new rezoning applications are considered by City Council or new development permit applications are approved by City staff.
As previously reported by Daily Hive Urbanized, the original version of Maloney’s motion in July 2026 called for a temporary pause on considering major new AI data centre projects. However, during last week’s meeting, Maloney explained that City staff had subsequently told her that the provincial legislation of the Vancouver Charter requires applications to be processed, which makes such a moratorium not possible.
During the meeting, City Council approved an amendment from COPE city councillor Solomon Yi-Kieran directing City staff to develop and report back with a separate definition for AI data centres — effectively distinguishing them from conventional data centres to better account for significant differences in electricity and water use, noise, and emissions.
ABC city councillor Mike Klassen also supported Maloney’s motion, asserting the municipal government should welcome technology investment while taking concerns about its effects on residents and surrounding neighbourhoods seriously.
He pointed to Canadians’ heavy reliance on technology and services based outside the country, citing the recent Microsoft Outlook outage as an example of that dependence. He also called for cooperation with the federal government, which he argued still has considerable work to do on regulating the sector.
When it comes to local considerations, Klassen said concerns about noise, water, and electricity consumption, heat, environmental impacts, and how data centres fit alongside neighbouring properties deserve attention.
“Having clear guidelines and reasonable safeguards benefits residents, businesses and investors alike,” said Klassen.
He added that clearer expectations would give companies greater certainty when proposing new facilities, helping Vancouver accommodate technology investment while addressing its potential impacts.
This AI data centre review was one of 11 wide-ranging member motions from Maloney, Mayor Pete Fry, and COPE city councillor Sean Orr approved by City Council on Nov. 18.

articles.title: PureVPN has launched 5-year plans just in time for Black Friday — $1.49 per month for half a decade of protection
articles.text:
PureVPN has introduced new five-year plans just in time for Black Friday, becoming one of the few VPNs offering Black Friday VPN deals beyond two years.
Its Basic plan now starts at $1.49 per month, while Plus and Max plans, which add features such as password management and dark web monitoring, are $2.19 and $2.49 per month, respectively.
Five years is far more than most VPNs will ever offer - only FastestVPN's lifetime VPN deal lasts longer at the time of writing. Most VPNs offer two years, and VPNs like NordVPN are only $13 less right now for the far shorter duration.
PureVPN's deal is perfect if you're looking to avoid inflated auto-renewal costs for as long as possible. Just turn off auto-renewal once you've signed up, then, in five years, find a new Black Friday VPN deal that takes your fancy instead.
PureVPN: Get five years of VPN protection for Black Friday
Was: $2.15/month for two years
Now: $1.49/month for FIVE YEARS of protection
PureVPN's new five-year plans offer a brilliant way to set up and forget a VPN that protects your whole household. You get 10 simultaneous connections, apps for most platforms, and features like password management and dark web monitoring if you choose a more premium plan. Unsure? Try it with its 30-day money-back guarantee.
That said, I'd recommend considering how you'll use it before signing up.
When we recently tested PureVPN, it was surprisingly slow, clocking just 560 Mbps on WireGuard.
This will be fine for most things: browsing, gaming, and some streaming, but the fastest VPNs offer speeds around 4x quicker right now if you want reliable 4K streaming, low-ping gaming, or high-speed downloads.
It unblocks all global Netflix libraries, most Disney+ libraries, and many local services such as BBC iPlayer or 7Play. But if you want a VPN for YouTube or Prime Video, I'd again look elsewhere, as it struggled to unblock either.
If you can live with this, then no VPN offers better value - even FastestVPN can't meet PureVPN's performance.
But, if you're more focused on performance, look towards some of this year's best VPNs. NordVPN is $2.99 per month for two years, ExpressVPN is $2.79, and Proton is $2.49, all offering a superior experience if you're willing to sacrifice the 3 additional years.

articles.title: Los mejores teléfonos de Samsung, Apple, Nothing, Google… en oferta para este Black Friday
articles.text:
Muchas personas están esperando a esta semana para comprar un teléfono premium a un precio más reducido. Durante el Black Friday de PcComponentes puedes encontrar ofertas en los mejores teléfonos del mercado, de marcas como Samsung, Apple, Google o Nothing, pero también otras más asequibles como Xiaomi Redmi o Motorola.
Lo mejor de todo es que en PcComponentes puedes encontrar cientos y cientos de teléfonos, de todo tipo de configuraciones y por supuesto, precios. Entra en su web porque seguramente encuentres el modelo que busques.
Para que sea más fácil para ti, lo hemos dividido por marcas.
Teléfonos Samsung
En esta sección hemos incluido dos opciones. La primera es el teléfono más importante de la marca, el flagship que incorpora todas las novedades del sector en cuanto a cámara, pantalla, procesador… Es el Samsung Galaxy S26, con 12 GB de RAM y 256GB de almacenamiento. Ten en cuenta que este teléfono tiene un precio que ronda los mil euros, pero con la oferta se queda en tan sólo 799 euros.
El segundo es el gama media por excelencia. Un teléfono al que recurren todas las personas que quieren un teléfono de una marca tradicional como Samsung, pero sin irse al más top. Este Samsung Galaxy A57 cuesta poco más de 400 euros. Un teléfono que te durará muchos años sin que tu bolsillo se vacíe por completo.
Teléfonos Apple
Hay dos tipos de personas: los que quieren un iPhone, y lo tienen, y los que quieren un iPhone, pero se conforman con otro teléfono. Pero sí, el iPhone es en general un objeto de deseo para muchísimas personas. Durante el Black Friday de PcComponentes puedes conseguir el último lanzamiento, el más top, el iPhone 18 Pro con su precio más bajo histórico.
Sin embargo, el último iPhone no incorpora demasiadas novedades con respecto al modelo anterior, por eso recurrir al iPhone 17 es también una buena opción. En este caso puedes conseguir el modelo normal por menos de mil euros, sólo 970 euros.
Google Pixel
Es mi teléfono personal, y la verdad, no tengo ninguna pega. Una muy buena cámara, buen rendimiento con un sistema operativo fluido y puro y un diseño que a mi particularmente me gusta mucho. Los Pixel están ganando mucho terreno precisamente por eso, porque son la marca que mejor está sabiendo plantar cara a los iPhone. Por eso han pasado de ser teléfonos de nicho, a un uso más generalizado, tanto los modelos grandes como el Pro XL como los pequeños, la familia A.
En el caso de este Black Friday, tienes el teléfono más top, el Google Pixel 11 Pro XL por sólo 1.081 euros, su precio más bajo desde su lanzamiento.
Nothing
Y seguimos hablando de teléfonos que pasaron de ser de nichos a tener un uso más generalizado. Cuando Nothing llegó al mercado, lo hizo para revolucionarlo, principalmente con un diseño nunca visto antes. A nivel de especificaciones no destaca en nada pero cumple perfectamente con lo que esperas de un buen teléfono.
En este Black Friday tienes el Nothing 3 por menos de 500 euros, tan sólo 489 euros.
Motorola y Xiaomi Redmi
Los dos candidatos perfectos para el 75% de la población. Dos teléfonos de gama media, con un precio muy ajustado y que puede usar cualquier tipo de persona. En el caso del Xiaomi Redmi Note 17 es uno de los que más se ven por la calle. Este modelo tiene una configuración de 6GB de RAM, 256GB de almacenamiento, una inmensa batería de 8340 mAh, una pantalla AMOLED de 6,83 pulgadas y un sistema de carga rápida de 67W. Muy buen teléfono que ahora solo cuesta 295 euros.
El segundo modelo es uno de Motorola, sí, la mítica Motorola. La que todos recordamos, que se acabó yendo pero que regresó hace unos años más fuerte que nunca y manteniendo todos sus valores de ofrecer buena tecnología y un precio ajustado. El Moto G77 tiene una pantalla AMOLED de 6,8 pulgadas, un procesador Dimensity 6400, una cámara principal de 108 megapíxeles y una capacidad de almacenamiento de 512 GB. Cuesta menos de 250 euros.
Bonus: el teléfono con la mejor cámara del año
Se acaba el año y ya podemos hablar de la mejor cámara en un teléfono móvil. En este caso hay dos que nos han gustado mucho: uno es el Oppo XFind X10 Pro Max y el otro es el vivo X500 Pro Max. Los dos ofrecen la mejor experiencia en fotografía tanto en hardware como en software, respetando a la perfección lo que vemos, sin retocar de manera excesiva nada, con un zoom increíble al que le puedes acoplar un teleconvertidor. Pero es que además son dos teléfonos potentes, con las mejores especificaciones del mercado. La pega es que no son teléfonos baratos pero en el Black Friday de PcComponentes puedes conseguirlos por un precio más bajo del habitual.

articles.title: Smartphones Samsung : ça s'annonce mal pour les prochains Galaxy A
articles.text:
Comme tous les constructeurs, Samsung doit composer avec la montée des prix des composants, comme la mémoire RAM, mais aussi des coûts de fabrication. Selon des informations qui viennent directement de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, les futures Galaxy A38 et Galaxy A58 pourraient souffrir de ces contraintes. Cela se traduirait notamment par une partie photo qui ferait du surplace par rapport à la génération précédente, voire qui ferait un pas en arrière.
Un capteur photo moins bon pour le Galaxy A38 ?
Sur le papier, le futur Galaxy A38 afficherait toujours un bloc caméra principal de 50 mégapixels. Pourtant, certains documents indiquent que Samsung testerait un capteur Sony IMX882 pour ce modèle. Ce serait donc une régression par rapport au Galaxy A37, qui embarque un Sony IMX906 sur de nombreux marchés. Le capteur IMX882 propose une surface de 1/1,95 pouce, nettement plus petite que les 1/1,56 pouce du IMX906. Dans les faits, Samsung réutiliserait un composant déjà présent sur le Galaxy A36, sorti deux générations plus tôt.
Un capteur plus petit, c’est moins de lumière, ce qui vient dégrader les photos en basse luminosité ainsi que le flou d’arrière-plan naturel (bokeh). Ce compromis sur la photo s’ajouterait aux rumeurs évoquant l’intégration d’une dalle OLED plus économique sur le Galaxy A38. Le smartphone compenserait néanmoins avec une batterie de 6 000 mAh, soit une capacité en hausse de 20 % par rapport à la génération précédente. Samsung pourrait donc faire des arbitrages afin de privilégier l’autonomie au détriment de l’affichage et du module caméra.
Le Galaxy A58 ferait le choix du statu quo
Du côté du Galaxy A58, Samsung ne se foulerait pas. Les informations en fuite évoquent la présence du même capteur Sony IMX906 de 50 mégapixels déjà utilisé sur le Galaxy A57. On en viendrait presque à être content que le constructeur ne rétrograde pas un nouveau modèle par rapport au précédent… Drôle d’époque.
Ce maintien des spécifications sur le Galaxy A58 et le recul du Galaxy A38 traduisent surtout la pression financière qui pèse sur l’industrie mobile. La hausse générale des coûts de fabrication pousse les marques à rationaliser la fiche technique de leurs appareils. Il reste possible que Samsung teste simplement ces composants en laboratoire et modifie la fiche technique finale d’ici la sortie officielle, mais rien n’est moins sûr. Dans ce contexte, a-t-on vraiment besoin de nouveaux modèles en 2027 ?

articles.title: Cet accessoire PlayStation vous permet de jouer à GTA 6 sans PS5 et il tombe en promo pour le Black Friday
articles.text:
Le PlayStation Portal est affiché à 249,99 € chez Cdiscount, et passe à 239,99 € avec le code 10DES99 à saisir dans le panier pendant le Black Friday. C’est dix euros de moins que son prix public, fixé depuis la hausse décidée par Sony en avril 2026.
GTA 6 sans PS5 ? Oui mais à deux conditions
Jusqu’ici, le Portal ne lançait GTA 6 qu’en lecture à distance : il affichait, via le Wi-Fi, l’image d’une PS5 allumée ou en veille dans le salon. Depuis ce lundi 23 novembre, le jeu de Rockstar est aussi disponible en streaming cloud. Il tourne alors sur les serveurs de Sony, et la console devient facultative. L’exclusivité dont profitait Xbox Cloud Gaming avec la Xbox One n’aura duré que quatre jours.
Il faut toutefois remplir deux conditions. La première, c’est de posséder le jeu, vendu 79,99 € en édition Standard, puisqu’il ne fait pas partie du catalogue du PlayStation Plus. La version boîte ne contient qu’un code de téléchargement : une fois activée, elle rejoint votre bibliothèque numérique comme un achat sur le PlayStation Store, et devrait donc ouvrir les mêmes droits. La seconde, c’est d’être abonné au PlayStation Plus Premium, la formule la plus chère du service : 18,99 € par mois, 54,99 € pour trois mois ou 151,99 € pour un an. Les sauvegardes sont stockées en ligne, ce qui permet de reprendre sur le Portal une partie commencée sur une PS5.
Reste la connexion, et ça sera sûrement le point le plus incapacitant pour certains. Sony demande au moins 13 Mbit/s pour streamer en 1080p sur le Portal, et 7 Mbit/s en 720p. L’image reste celle d’un flux vidéo, forcément moins nette qu’un jeu installé sur la console, mais le mode 1080p Haute qualité ajouté en mars augmente le débit pour limiter la casse.
Est-ce que ça vaut le coup ?
On ne lui avait mis que 5/10 lors de notre test, en 2023, à une époque où il ne savait rien faire sans PS5. Ce n’est plus tout à fait vrai car le PlayStation Portal s’est bonifié avec le temps au fil des mises à jour. Toutefois, son prix a suivi la même pente que celui des consoles, avec une hausse de 30 € en avril 2026.
Mais face à une PS5 affichée à 649,99 € (599,99 € en édition Digital) et une PS5 Pro à 899,99 €, difficile de ne pas y voir une bonne affaire. Contrairement à Xbox, qui plafonne désormais son cloud gaming à 15 heures par mois avec le Game Pass Ultimate, Sony n’annonce aucune limite de temps de jeu et n’impose pas de publicités pour les abonnements gratuits. Pour 294,98 €, le prix du Portal et de trois mois de PS Plus Premium, vous avez de quoi lancer GTA 6, une fois le jeu acheté.
Si vous avez déjà une PS5, le Portal sert toujours à lancer GTA 6 depuis la chambre pendant que la télé du salon sert à quelqu’un d’autre, en lecture à distance et sans abonnement. Sony a bien présenté un nouveau modèle avec du stockage interne, mais il est pour l’instant réservé au Japon et à la Corée du Sud, sans sortie annoncée en Europe. Le modèle actuel reste donc la seule option chez nous.
Black Friday 2026 : tout ce qu’il faut savoir
Depuis une dizaine d’années, le Black Friday s’est infiltré dans le calendrier commercial des grandes marques et enseignes françaises. Avec l’expérience, on peut vous dire que cet événement fait partie des meilleurs moments pour faire de bonnes affaires.
Les dates du Black Friday
Bien qu’il porte encore le nom du vendredi noir, le Black Friday s’étend désormais sur un mois chez de nombreux revendeurs. Un format moins typique qui lui retire un peu son petit côté FOMO. On dirait presque les soldes, finalement. Mais c’est aussi moins le rush, ce qui est une bonne chose pour ceux qui veulent faire des achats plus raisonnés. Globalement, on peut résumer ce Black Friday en quatre temps forts :
- Début novembre : les avant-premières Black Friday.
- Autour du 20 novembre, selon les enseignes : la Black Week commence généralement plusieurs jours avant le jour J.
- 27 novembre : la date du Black Friday, même si les offres commencent généralement avant et se prolongent le week-end des 28 et 29 novembre.
- 30 novembre : le Cyber Monday.

Que faut-il acheter pendant le Black Friday ?
Globalement, tous les rayons profitent des remises, mais il ne faut pas pour autant se jeter sur les premiers prix bradés. N’oubliez pas que pour les enseignes, ce moment est aussi l’occasion de déstocker de vieux produits, dont les plus remisés frôlent parfois l’obsolescence.

Pour les produits phares comme les AirPods, la PS5, la Switch 2, un iPhone ou un Samsung Galaxy, sachez que nos tests sont là pour vous aider à savoir s’ils méritent votre argent.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
articles.text:
AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
- Date:
  November 21, 2026
- Source:
  University of Plymouth
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer earlier and spare patients unnecessary invasive procedures.
- Share:
Bladder cancer kills approximately 220,000 people worldwide each year, yet recognizing the disease early can be difficult. Its symptoms can resemble those of far less serious conditions, including kidney stones, allowing warning signs to go unnoticed.
Researchers at the University of Plymouth have now developed an artificial intelligence system that could help doctors identify people at risk of bladder cancer years before they receive a diagnosis. In some patients, the technology detected subtle warning signals dating back as far as five years.
The new approach uses AI to examine electronic health records, searching for combinations of symptoms, medical conditions, risk factors, and healthcare activity that might otherwise be overlooked. By recognizing these patterns, researchers hope to make bladder cancer screening more accurate and help doctors find the disease when treatment is most likely to succeed.
AI Finds Hidden Bladder Cancer Clues in Medical Records
Under current medical referral guidelines, one of the main warning signs of bladder cancer is visible blood in the urine (hematuria). However, blood in the urine can also result from noncancerous problems, including kidney stones and prostate conditions. This overlap makes it difficult to determine which patients need further investigation and contributes to missed cases.
Confirming bladder cancer currently requires a procedure called cystoscopy (where a long, thin tube with a small camera inside is moved up the urethra and into the bladder). Although effective, the examination is invasive, highlighting the need for better ways to identify patients who are most likely to have the disease.
To explore a possible solution, a team led by Professor Shang-Ming Zhou at the University of Plymouth's Centre for Health Technology studied electronic medical records from nearly 70,000 patients. The records covered a 25-year period, from 1995 through 2020.
The researchers created an AI model called PRECISE-AGZ and used it to investigate 48,261 possible health indicators (from smoking and exercise habits to medication use). From this enormous collection of information, the system narrowed the list to 38 features that were especially useful for predicting bladder cancer risk.
AI Identifies 85% of Bladder Cancer Cases
The results suggest that AI could substantially improve the way patients are assessed for bladder cancer.
The model correctly identified 85% of patients who had bladder cancer and accurately classified 91% of those who did not have the disease. It also performed better at detecting bladder cancer than existing NHS referral guidelines.
Importantly, the system demonstrated effective detection as early as 12 months before a patient's official diagnosis. Some of the warning signals it recognized could be traced back up to five years, suggesting that valuable clues may exist in medical records long before cancer is discovered.
The AI confirmed the importance of established risk factors, including smoking and blood in the urine. However, it also uncovered unexpected associations that conventional screening approaches would be unlikely to detect.
For example, patients diagnosed with Parkinson's disease or dementia appeared to have a lower risk of bladder cancer. Meanwhile, long-term use of tamoxifen (a breast cancer medication) was associated with a higher risk.
These findings do not establish that Parkinson's disease or dementia protects against bladder cancer, or that tamoxifen causes it. Instead, they raise questions about possible shared biological mechanisms that researchers believe deserve closer examination.
Another surprising finding involved blood in the urine. Although this symptom is often considered a major warning sign, its significance appears to depend partly on a patient's other medical conditions. Among men with benign prostate enlargement, for instance, blood in the urine was associated with a lower bladder cancer risk.
Understanding these relationships more fully could eventually help doctors distinguish patients who need urgent investigation from those who may not require invasive testing.
A New Approach to Early Cancer Screening
Beyond identifying warning signs, the AI system could also divide patients into three groups according to their estimated likelihood of having bladder cancer: low-risk (below 7% probability), uncertain (grey zone: 7-55%), and high-risk (above 55%).
This approach could help healthcare providers decide which patients need immediate attention and which may benefit from additional monitoring.
For example, patients in the uncertain category might be monitored before undergoing procedures such as cystoscopy. If further research confirms the system's reliability, this could reduce unnecessary examinations while allowing doctors to concentrate resources on people at greatest risk.
PhD student Xu Wang, who led the data analysis, said: "Bladder cancer ranks as the ninth most common cancer worldwide, with 614,000 new cases diagnosed in 2022."
"Despite its prevalence, no routine screening program exists for the general population, and - following symptoms - detection relies heavily on invasive cystoscopy procedures. Our system goes far beyond traditional symptoms, and it's great to have uncovered the results that we have. The research shows that the combination of multiple factors - from medication histories to seemingly unrelated conditions - can reveal patterns invisible to conventional screening methods."
Could AI Help Doctors Catch Bladder Cancer Earlier?
The potential benefits extend beyond improving diagnostic accuracy. Detecting bladder cancer earlier could mean more treatment options, better survival outcomes, and fewer patients undergoing invasive procedures unnecessarily.
Dr. Helen Winter, Clinical Director for the Somerset, Wiltshire, Avon and Gloucestershire (SWAG) Cancer Alliance, emphasized the importance of developing better screening methods.
"Bladder cancer has a major unmet need in early detection and the prospect of a screening tool is hugely exciting for patients and their families.
"It could identify those most at risk more accurately, reduce harm from invasive procedures, and catch cancer earlier, when survival outcomes and quality of life can be dramatically improved."
Professor Shang-Ming Zhou believes the findings point toward a more individualized approach to cancer screening, in which AI helps doctors interpret a patient's broader medical history rather than relying primarily on individual symptoms.
"This work represents a paradigm shift towards precision screening for bladder cancer.
"By harnessing the power of interpretable machine learning and comprehensive health records, we're moving closer to detecting this disease at its earliest, most treatable stages."
More Research Needed Before Clinical Use
Despite the promising results, the researchers caution that the technology is not yet ready for widespread clinical use.
All the patient information used in the study came from the SAIL database in Wales. Before the model can be introduced into other healthcare settings, researchers will need to determine whether it performs equally well with different patient populations and medical record systems.
Professor Zhou explained why broader testing is essential.
"It's important to emphasize that further validation across different healthcare systems is essential before anything is rolled out more widely - for example, all of the data analyzed came from the SAIL database in Wales, so we'd want to investigate other datasets too.
"But it's a very exciting early study. Additional studies would also be needed to confirm the causal relationships suggested by the model's predictions."
The findings offer an encouraging glimpse of how artificial intelligence might improve cancer screening by uncovering patterns hidden within years of routine medical information. With further validation, such tools could help doctors recognize bladder cancer sooner, prioritize patients who need testing, and potentially improve outcomes.
The study, "Early Detection of Bladder Cancer Using Advanced Feature Engineering and Swarm Intelligence Optimization on EHRs," was published in IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering.
The research also involved collaborators from North Bristol NHS Trust and University Hospitals Bristol NHS Foundation Trust.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Plymouth. Original written by Mrs. Amy King. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Xu Wang, Andrea Preston, Jonathan Aning, Michael Loizou, Shang-Ming Zhou. Early Detection of Bladder Cancer Using Advanced Feature Engineering and Swarm Intelligence Optimization on EHRs. IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering, 2026; 73 (11): 3680 DOI: 10.1109/TBME.2026.3658230
