articles.title: GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
articles.text:
Game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one big effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old “NotRexed,” has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two.
GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
Modders are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC.
Leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game’s code and rebuild it into native PC code.
Some have managed to get the game to boot on PC, but recompiling the full game won’t be easy — even with help from AI tools like Claude. Take-Two is trying to slow this progress, and its IP enforcement team targeted the main GitHub repository for Leonida and more than 2,900 forks of it, claiming that it “infringes upon Take-Two’s copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI.”
PortWatch VI is tracking the efforts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox build over to PC. At the time of publishing, the VIctory project and forks of it are leading the way. People are also trying to use XCL, a compatibility layer that runs Xbox Series X games on a Windows PC, to get GTA VI running.
At this point, it seems like Take-Two might not be able to avoid the inevitable here. The clock started ticking down to the release of the PC version last week, and if recent reports are true, we might see it in a few months. If GTA VI is close to being officially ready for PC, we could hear about a release before modders manage to get the game running on PC unofficially.

articles.title: Browser auf dem iPhone: Warum Mozilla und 55.000 andere Unternehmen die EU auffordern, gegen Apple vorzugehen
articles.text:
Browser auf dem iPhone: Warum Mozilla und 55.000 andere Unternehmen die EU auffordern, gegen Apple vorzugehen
Ein Bündnis aus Mozilla, dem E-Commerce-Anbieter Shopify und über 50.000 Firmen aus der EU fordert von der Europäischen Kommission ein Verfahren samt Strafen gegen Apple. In einem offenen Brief „für mehr Wettbewerb im Web“ und ein „stärkeres Europa“ sprechen die Unterzeichner Kommissionspräsidentin Ursula von der Leyen direkt an.
Worum es im Streit geht
Im Zentrum steht die sogenannte Browser-Engine – also der technische Unterbau, der Webseiten darstellt. Auf iPhone und iPad schreibt Apple außerhalb der EU und Japans vor, dass alle Browser Apples eigene Engine WebKit nutzen. Selbst Googles Chrome läuft dort deshalb mit Apple-Technik.
In der Europäischen Union ist das anders: Durch den Digital Markets Act (DMA), die EU-Regeln für besonders marktmächtige Plattformen, dürfen Entwickler seit knapp drei Jahren eigene Engines auf iOS und iPadOS anbieten. Apple ist dabei als sogenannter Gatekeeper reguliert. In Japan gilt eine ähnliche Regelung seit Dezember 2025.
Warum bislang niemand mitmacht
Genutzt hat die neuen Möglichkeiten bisher aber kein großer Anbieter. Der Grund: Es ist kompliziert. Mozilla kritisiert, Apples Bedingungen seien „nicht praktikabel“, weil Entwickler eigene App-Pakete allein für die EU bauen und pflegen müssten. Für Mozilla lohne es sich so nicht, einen echten Alternativbrowser umzusetzen. Das Projekt würde für Firefox gerne die hauseigene Gecko-Engine nutzen statt WebKit. Auch Google hat bislang keine Anstalten gemacht, Chrome auf iOS umzustellen, auch wenn der Internet-Konzern die entsprechenden Mittel sicher hätte.
Die Koalition verlangt nun, dass die EU-Kommission „den DMA endlich umsetzt“. Apple habe „technische und rechtliche Hindernisse“ errichtet, die die Ausübung der Rechte der Browser-Anbieter unmöglich machten und dadurch den Markt behinderten. Dadurch fehle Firmen und ihren Kunden die echte Wahlfreiheit bei Browsern und der Wettbewerb bei Web-Apps, den der DMA eigentlich ermöglichen sollte. „Die Zeit drängt“, heißt es im offenen Brief. Apple habe mehr als zweieinhalb Jahre Zeit gehabt, die Anforderungen zu erfüllen, doch die Hindernisse bestünden weiter, während das mobile Internet „an Boden verliert“. Eine Reaktion der EU-Kommission steht bislang aus.

articles.title: Chatr rolls out new, pricier six- and 12-month plans
articles.text:
Rogers’ Chatr brand rolled out new six-month and yearly plans that are more expensive than previous offers.
First up is the new six-month plan. It costs $150 and includes 90GB of 4G data — that works out to about $25 and 15GB of data per month.
The other plan is a 12-month plan. It costs $199 for the year and includes 60GB of data. That’s about $16.58 and 5GB of data per month.
Unfortunately, this plan is more expensive than Chatr’s previous yearly offer. The old $159/year 40GB plan is no longer available.
Both plans include unlimited Canada-wide talk, unlimited Canada, U.S., and international texting, and voicemail. Chatr offers 4G data speeds up to 150Mbps.
On the one hand, I like to see more multi-month plans like this, as they’re often good value for people who don’t need a crazy phone plan. I could see these plans being good for a kid’s first phone, or perhaps for an elderly family member who just needs a cellphone for emergencies. On the other, I don’t like to see Chatr pushing the price up on these plans.
It’s worth noting, however, that there are a few other carriers offering multi-month plans. Freedom Mobile, for example, has several six- and 12-month plans. On the six-month side, Freedom has a $90 talk and text plan, a $150/90GB plan, and a $180/180GB plan. And for the 12-month options, Freedom has a$129/20GB and $159/40GB plans.
Telus’ Koodo also offers a couple of yearly plans, including a $100 plan with 400 minutes and 400 texts, and a $159/40GB plan.
In other words, if you really liked Chatr’s $159/40GB plan, there are some other carriers out there worth considering now that Chatr no longer offers it. But if the new six- and 12-month plans call to you, you can check them out on Chatr’s website.

articles.title: Amsterdam’s Good Heat raises €2 million to replace industrial gas-fired steam boilers with heat batteries
articles.text:
Good Heat, an Amsterdam-based startup that delivers zero-carbon heat as a service to industrial heat users, has raised €2 million to support its growing project pipeline.
The round is led by SET Ventures, Europe’s leading energy VC, with participation from Shell Ventures and existing investor Investible. In October 2025, the company announced €1.83 million ($2 million) in pre-Seed funding backed by Understorey Ventures, Investible, 2100VC, and Foobar VC.
“Industrial heat is an enormous market: a fifth of all the energy the world uses, and almost 90% of it still comes from fossil fuels. The cost of that dependence is obvious at every site we see. We have built a pipeline across two continents, and this financing lets us scale the team to deliver it. Our message to industry: take the heat, leave the project to us,” said Bauke van Gent, Founder and CEO, Good Heat.
Founded in 2025 by Bauke van Gent and Tom Geiser, Good Heat is a developer and platform for clean industrial heat. Batteries that store electricity have helped transform power grids. Good Heat expects heat batteries could play a similarly important role, charging with cheap renewable power and delivering heat when needed.
It argues this could be particularly useful for industries and factories that need significant heat for everything from frying potato chips to producing chemicals. European industry faces crippling gas bills and needs to diversify its energy supply to avoid energy disruptions
The Dutch startup replaces gas-fired steam boilers at industrial sites with heat batteries—advanced thermal energy storage systems powered by electricity. It claims to develop, finance, own, and operate each system, selling steam at a stable price with no upfront investment for the customer.
Since its launch over a year ago, Good Heat reports building a pipeline of more than 100 MWt across the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, and Poland, supported by structured partnerships with leading energy companies that deliver leads each year, alongside Good Heat’s own origination. The same model is already driving multiple site developments.
In Australia, the company is developing Project Arcadia, a 200MWh eTES (electrified thermal energy storage) project for a food company in Victoria. The eTES system will be charged with renewable electricity, converting it to and storing it as high-temperature heat, released on-demand (24/7) as hot steam into the factory. The company says this is the largest electric thermal storage project under development in Australia and expects to reach financial close in 2027. It has an active pipeline of prospective projects totalling more than 75 MWt. It has an office in Sydney.
It also highlighted that the projects are backed by long-term offtake agreements and hedged energy supply agreements, helping provide the predictable, inflation-protected cash flows infrastructure investors seek. A growing portfolio lowers the cost of capital for each new project while supporting technology validation.
It notes that the company is technology-neutral and selects the thermal energy storage technology best suited to each site’s requirements through a competitive procurement process.
“Industrial heat isn’t held back by technology, it’s held back by the complexity of delivering and financing the projects. We’ve seen this play out in wind and solar: once independent developers took over, the market scaled. Our research into industrial process heat pointed to exactly this model, and Bauke and Tom have the track record to build it. Good Heat is our first investment in the sector, and we’re excited to lead this round,” said Anton Arts, Managing Partner at SET Ventures.

articles.title: Hackers invadem CIA e agência de inteligência dos EUA e expõem dados
articles.text:
A Agência Central de Inteligência dos Estados Unidos (CIA, na sigla em inglês) e o Escritório do Diretor de Inteligência Nacional (ODNI, na sigla em inglês) identificaram invasão cibernética que expôs parte de suas informações não classificadas. O incidente atingiu sistema utilizado para analisar dados de fontes abertas e autoridades estadunidenses ainda não esclareceram exatamente quais informações foram comprometidas.
Segundo reportagem do The New York Times, a invasão também pode ter afetado sistemas de outros órgãos do governo. Uma das fontes ouvidas pelo jornal afirmou que o problema já havia sido resolvido em pelo menos uma dessas instituições.
Apesar da gravidade do episódio, informações classificadas não teriam sido comprometidas. O ODNI também informou que não houve interrupções em capacidades consideradas críticas. A CIA não comentou o caso.
O que os hackers conseguiram acessar?
- A invasão atingiu rede utilizada para atividades de inteligência de fontes abertas, conhecidas pela sigla OSINT (Open-Source Intelligence);
- Esse tipo de trabalho consiste em reunir e analisar informações disponíveis publicamente ou comercializadas por fornecedores de dados. Entre os materiais utilizados estão publicações em redes sociais, imagens de satélite, bases de dados comerciais e outros conteúdos encontrados na internet;
- Embora parte dessas informações esteja disponível gratuitamente, conjuntos de dados vendidos por empresas especializadas podem revelar detalhes sensíveis sobre pessoas, organizações e atividades quando são combinados com outras fontes;
- Agências de inteligência utilizam esse material para identificar padrões e produzir avaliações que ajudam a orientar suas análises;
- Ainda não está claro quais informações foram efetivamente acessadas pelos invasores, nem quem foi responsável pela operação. As fontes consultadas pelo jornal afirmaram que um hacker conseguiu obter acesso não autorizado a pelo menos um sistema governamental.
Governo estadunidense enfrenta sequência de incidentes digitais
O episódio acontece em meio a uma série de problemas de segurança e funcionamento de sistemas tecnológicos ligados ao governo dos Estados Unidos.
Na semana anterior, o presidente Donald Trump confirmou publicamente que o Centro Nacional de Informações sobre Crimes (NCIC, na sigla em inglês), banco de dados do FBI utilizado para compartilhar informações sobre suspeitos entre autoridades locais, estaduais e federais, havia sido alvo de ataque hacker.
O FBI investiga o caso. Questionado sobre a invasão durante entrevista por telefone à Fox News, Trump afirmou que não gostou do ocorrido.
Outro incidente envolveu o Departamento de Agricultura dos Estados Unidos (USDA, na sigla em inglês), que identificou problema de cibersegurança que levou à retirada temporária de alguns de seus aplicativos internos.
Além disso, a Agência de Segurança Nacional (NSA, na sigla em inglês) enfrentou interrupção de vários dias em sua rede interna de informações classificadas. Segundo autoridades e empresas citadas pelo jornal, o problema não foi provocado por ataque cibernético.
A sequência de ocorrências aumentou a preocupação entre autoridades atuais e antigas da inteligência estadunidense. Funcionários também apontaram que ferramentas de inteligência artificial (IA) estão ajudando a identificar vulnerabilidades em softwares, que precisam ser corrigidas rapidamente.
Leia mais:
- 123456 é a senha mais usada no Brasil e no mundo em 2026
- Nvidia investiga possível vazamento de dados após ameaça de grupo hacker
- Vazamento expõe 3,5 bilhões de dados em dois bancos na internet
- Hackers usam cada vez mais IA – e acordo bilionário tenta frear isso
Diretor de inteligência tenta tranquilizar população
Jay Clayton, diretor de inteligência nacional e recentemente escolhido por Trump para exercer também a função de diretor interino de cibersegurança, comentou os incidentes em entrevistas a programas de televisão no domingo.
Ao falar sobre a invasão ao banco de dados do FBI, Clayton afirmou que episódios desse tipo fazem parte da realidade digital estadunidense e não deveriam provocar alarme generalizado.
“Investigações cibernéticas e incidentes digitais fazem parte da economia e da vida americana há muito tempo”, declarou durante participação no programa This Week, da ABC. Segundo ele, o FBI está lidando com a ocorrência pelos procedimentos habituais.
Os episódios, porém, mantêm a segurança dos sistemas governamentais sob atenção, especialmente diante da quantidade de informações que essas instituições utilizam e armazenam.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Tidal to ban and remove millions of AI-generated tracks as AI slop inundates music streaming
articles.text:
Music streaming service Tidal said on Tuesday that it will start banning and removing songs generated fully with AI in a bid to stem the flood of submissions to its platform. The company said that over the past 90 days, more than 43% of tracks uploaded to its platform were generated by AI, and that was a major reason driving this decision.
Tidal said it will start removing fully AI-generated music on December 9, and the process will result in more than 29 million songs being deleted from the platform by the end of the year. With the new rules in place, the platform said it will be rejecting roughly 80,000-85,000 tracks per day.
Tidal is also banning distribution services from delivering 100% AI-generated tracks, and will reject submissions if songs’ metadata says they are made fully using AI.
The company said it will still accept songs that were made with AI assistance, but not fully generated.
The move comes as AI-generated music inundates streaming services across the board. Tidal is one of the first major platforms after Bandcamp to ban AI music outright. Deezer, which also provides detection tools to other streaming services, said that it will introduce a toggle to let users filter out AI music. Larger platforms like Spotify and YouTube Music have adopted a milder approach to this issue, choosing to label AI-generated music instead of offering filters or taking stronger measures.
Tidal started de-monetizing songs made using AI in June, but that did not prove enough of a deterrent, Tidal Music’s lead, Robert Anderson, said on X.
The company said that 27 million, or 6.3% of tracks on the platform, are fully AI-generated, but 96% of those have no streams.
“It’s true that not all songs catch on immediately, and artists should have time to build their fanbases. But this situation is different – at this scale, the authentic music and artists that Tidal subscribers are looking to listen to and discover get buried,” the company said in a post.
Meanwhile, music labels are trying to make money by partnering with platforms and AI model makers to sell their catalog for training or remixing features. Goldman Sachs estimates that by 2035, AI-related licensing tools and new monetization opportunities have the potential to improve record labels’ revenue by 10%.

articles.title: El hacker que filtró ‘GTA 6’ queda en libertad tras declararse culpable
articles.text:
La historia del hacker que filtró GTA 6 siendo un adolescente ha dado un giro bastante curioso. Apenas días después de declararse culpable, el pirata informático recuperó su libertad con una advertencia por parte del juez británico a cargo del caso, quien le pidió que no repitiera sus actividades delictivas.
"Que no vuelva a suceder", le manifestó el magistrado a Arion Kurtaj, según publica BBC. El joven de 21 años se declaró culpable de varios delitos vinculados con el hackeo a varias tecnológicas como parte del grupo Lapsus$ en 2022. Entre las firmas impactadas estuvo Rockstar Games, que padeció la divulgación de una gran cantidad de vídeos de GTA 6 cuando su desarrollo todavía estaba lejos de finalizado.
Uno de los puntos más curiosos de aquel incidente fue que Kurtaj hackeó Rockstar desde la habitación de un hotel, usando un Fire TV Stick. El por entonces adolescente intentó extorsionar al estudio para evitar la filtración de los materiales de GTA 6, pero estos acabaron divulgándose en Twitter y servidores de Discord.
Cuando la policía finalmente dio con el paradero de Arion Kurtaj, la justicia decidió mantenerlo internado por tiempo indefinido en una institución psiquiátrica debido a la severidad de su autismo. Asimismo, se determinó que esta era la mejor opción de supervivencia del hacker de GTA 6, debido a que piratas informáticos rivales lo doxxearon y amenazaron su integridad física en múltiples oportunidades.
Arion Kurtaj, el hacker que filtró GTA 6, sale en libertad
A comienzos de este año, la justicia británica determinó que el joven estaba en condiciones de afrontar el juicio por su accionar. La semana pasada, Kurtaj finalmente se declaró culpable de sus delitos en línea, incluyendo la filtración de GTA 6. El pirata informático afrontaba penas de hasta 14 años de cárcel por los intentos de extorsión a las empresas impactadas por su accionar. El tribunal finalmente se inclinó por un castigo de 7 años de cárcel, aunque no serán de prisión efectiva.
El juez a cargo del caso finalmente le otorgó la libertad condicional, de modo que no pasará más tiempo retenido. Eso sí, Kurtaj ha recibido una orden de prevención de delitos graves que tendrá una duración de cinco años. Mientras la misma se encuentre en vigencia, el hacker de GTA 6 verá restringidas sus actividades en línea. Así, por ejemplo, tendrá prohibido el uso de plataformas de comunicación como Discord y Telegram.
La filtración de GTA 6 en 2022 fue un golpe duro para Rockstar Games, tanto económico como emocional. La filtración le costó unos 5 millones de dólares al estudio y requirió de miles de horas de trabajo adicionales para mitigar su impacto. El éxito que tuvo el juego tras su lanzamiento, que embolsó casi 3.800 millones de dólares al cierre del primer día, no borró el mal momento que pasó la empresa.
Aaron Garbut, uno de los líderes de GTA 6, habló recientemente de lo duradero que fue el golpe anímico del hackeo. "Es como si alguien estuviera hurgando en tu ropa sucia. Es como si se metieran dentro de tu cabeza. Ves tus primeros trabajos expuestos ahí fuera y se supone que nadie debería ver eso nunca. Resulta extrañamente invasivo. Por eso es bastante difícil de gestionar a nivel emocional", reconoció.

articles.title: Cómo hacer búsquedas en el Modo IA de Google sin que queden en tu historial
articles.text:
Google activó en todo el mundo los “hilos temporales” del Modo IA, su asistente conversacional dentro del buscador. Quien los use puede hacer consultas que no se guardan en el historial, no se mezclan con sus preferencias y desaparecen al cerrar la conversación.
La compañía presentó la función como una forma de explorar temas sin dejar rastro en las recomendaciones, con un ejemplo cotidiano: buscar ideas para un regalo sorpresa. La opción llega a computadoras y a navegadores de teléfonos, en todos los idiomas que admite el Modo IA.
Para empezar no hace falta tocar la configuración de privacidad. Google indica que basta con abrir el Modo IA en el navegador y hacer clic en el ícono de hilos temporales, ubicado en la esquina superior derecha de la pantalla. Desde ahí, la conversación comienza en blanco.
Cómo usarlo, paso a paso
Primero, entrar al Modo IA desde el navegador. Segundo, seleccionar la opción “Temporary thread” (hilo temporal), arriba a la derecha. Tercero, escribir la pregunta en la barra “Ask anything” (pregunta lo que quieras). El sitio de ayuda de Google resalta que también se pueden subir imágenes y archivos desde el menú, o consultar por voz con el micrófono.
Para salir, se toca el botón de cierre que aparece en la misma esquina. Al abandonar el hilo, el acceso se pierde de inmediato: la conversación no se puede recuperar ni consultar desde el historial del Modo IA.
Qué queda fuera del historial y qué no
Google sostiene que la sesión está desvinculada de la cuenta. Por eso las respuestas no se basan en actividad pasada, y lo que se pregunta en el hilo no sirve para personalizar respuestas futuras ni aparece en el historial de Búsqueda o del Modo IA.
Estos hilos no se guardan en la cuenta de Google y desaparecen al cabo de 24 horas. Tampoco se usan para entrenar los modelos de IA generativa de la empresa, salvo que el usuario envíe comentarios o que sea necesario por razones de seguridad.
La privacidad no es total. Google aclara que sigue recopilando datos no asociados a la cuenta, por ejemplo para que sus servicios funcionen y se mantengan seguros. Además, el navegador puede guardar su propio historial cuando se visita una página web desde un hilo temporal.
Si el usuario sale del hilo siguiendo un enlace a otro sitio, ese sitio y los servicios que usa, como Google Analytics, recopilan datos de la visita igual que en cualquier navegación.
Funciones que no están disponibles
El modo temporal tiene restricciones. En un hilo temporal no se pueden usar las Aplicaciones conectadas ni otros servicios integrados a la cuenta de Google, ni obtener respuestas personalizadas, ni guardar información para personalizar más adelante.
Tampoco se puede compartir el hilo ni una respuesta, y no es posible generar imágenes. Quien necesite enviarle la conversación a otra persona, o retomarla otro día, debe usar un hilo normal.
En su blog, Google publicó la novedad el mismo 17 de noviembre de 2026, con la firma de Robby Stein. Para quien prefiera volver a las búsquedas habituales, la empresa indica que se puede cambiar de modo en cualquier momento, sin ajustes previos.

articles.title: Why Photonic Design Is Becoming a System-Level Challenge
articles.text:
A component can meet its individual design targets and still behave differently as part of a complete optical link.
Photonic engineers make design decisions at many levels.
A laser has its own performance requirements. So does an optical fiber. The interface between them introduces another set of variables. Ultimately, those individual components have to perform together as part of a complete optical link.
If the individual pieces meet their design targets, will the complete system perform as expected?
Not necessarily.
A Keysight EDA-Photonics Design (VPIphotonics) study of short-reach datacenter links provides a useful example. Two multimode VCSEL channels were designed with comparable signal characteristics and evaluated with a wideband multimode fiber. Yet when evaluated as complete transmission links, the two channels produced different results.
Understanding the difference in performance requires looking beyond any single component.
The VPIphotonics study modeled 26.5625 GBaud PAM4 transmission over 150 meters of wideband multimode fiber, using VCSEL channels operating at 850 nm and 910 nm. Each VCSEL was modeled with four transverse modes, and the link considered coupling conditions and receiver models.
25 Gbaud PAM4 with a multimode VCSEL and OM4 fiber.
At first glance, the two channels seemed comparable.
The calculated 3 dB bandwidth was 27.0 GHz at 850 nm and 27.8 GHz at 910 nm.
But that wasn’t the end of the story.
When the complete link was simulated, the outcomes diverged after transmission over 150 meters: the 850 nm channel exhibited better performance compared to the 910 nm channel. By examining the performance of both channels in back-to-back, it is concluded that the difference in performance results from the impairments of the multimode fiber.
System-level simulation of the 850 nm and 910 nm channels after 150 m reveals different transmission performance despite comparable VCSEL modulation bandwidths.
The study found that fiber bandwidth metrics alone did not fully predict system performance. Instead, link quality depended on interactions among:
- VCSEL mode structure
- modal dispersion
- chromatic dispersion
- fiber differential modal delay (DMD)
- wavelength-dependent behavior
That’s an important distinction.
A component-level metric describes an important part of the design, but not necessarily what happens when that component interacts with other components in a link.
For a short-reach optical link, the transmitter, launch conditions, fiber, modal behavior, and receiver all contribute to the final result.
Studying system-level performance reveals the limitations of the system and helps determine the maximum transmission distance, the optimum launch power, and the appropriate driving conditions. Moreover, it enables the prediction of system performance at higher data rates using the same components. These findings may feed back into component design, for example by motivating efforts to extend the bandwidth limitations of the VCSEL. As a result, the design process becomes iterative, progressing from component design to system design and then back to component optimization. This interdependence highlights the need for integrated design tools.
The VCSEL example illustrates a broader challenge in photonic engineering.
At the device level, engineers need an accurate representation of optical and physical behavior.
At the component level, they need to understand how devices work together.
At the system level, the question changes again:
Does the completed design deliver the required performance in its target application?
In the VPIphotonics framework described in the study, an optical link is constructed from parameterized building blocks including lasers, couplers, fibers, photodetectors, filters, receiver blocks, and analysis tools.
That allows the engineer to move beyond “Does this component meet specification?” to “How does this component affect the performance of the complete system?”
Consider the VCSEL-to-fiber interface.
Launch conditions influence which fiber modes are excited. In the VPIphotonics model, coupling between the VCSEL and fiber can account for factors including lateral offset, angular tilt, longitudinal spacing, coupling losses, and the modal fields of the two devices.
The fiber introduces additional considerations, including modal field distributions, effective indices, DMD, chromatic dispersion, attenuation, group delay, and mode coupling.
None of those effects exist independently in the operating link. The engineering value comes from understanding how they combine to influence system-level outcomes.
For the multimode-link application, the VPIphotonics framework includes virtual test benches for measurements such as:
- Differential Modal Delay (DMD)
- Effective Modal Bandwidth Calculated (EMBc)
- Encircled Flux (EF)
The study also evaluates complete-system outputs including eye diagrams and symbol error rate.
This creates a useful connection between simulated component behavior and the measurements engineers use to evaluate the finished link.
For the 850/910 nm example, that system context exposed performance differences that VCSEL bandwidth metrics by themselves did not predict.
At what level do I need to simulate my design to answer the question I am trying to solve?
Detailed device simulation remains important when the problem is the physical behavior of the photonic component.
Component- or circuit-level simulation becomes important when individual devices interact together to perform some function within a single component.
System-level simulation adds the application context needed to investigate how components and circuits affect the performance of the complete optical system.
These are different views of the same engineering problem.
With VPIphotonics now part of Keysight, the broader opportunity is to look at photonic design across multiple levels of abstraction.
The goal is not simply to apply more simulation. It is to use the appropriate level of abstraction for each engineering question and understand how decisions made at one level influence performance at another.
The 850/910 nm example illustrates why that matters. Comparable component metrics did not result in identical link behavior. The difference became clear when interactions among the VCSELs, launch conditions, fiber characteristics, and receiver were evaluated at the system level.
As photonic systems grow more complex, that system context can become increasingly important for making informed design decisions before committing to hardware.
By linking component design directly to system performance, engineers can work from application requirements rather than isolated device metrics. This closes the loop between system architects and component designers, leading to faster development cycles, more efficient trade-offs, and solutions that are optimized for real-world deployment.

articles.title: Accent, ton, débit : Google prépare une fonction pour créer une voix de A à Z sur Gemini
articles.text:
Et s’il était possible de décrire à Gemini la voix que vous souhaitez utiliser ? C’est la nouvelle fonction sur laquelle semble travailler Google.
Le mode vocal de Gemini a fait bien du chemin depuis son lancement, il y a plus de 2 ans. Avec Gemini 3.8 Live, Google a récemment réussi à supprimer les silences gênants durant les échanges. Dans la foulée, le géant de la Tech a ouvert aux développeurs un catalogue de plus de 2000 voix. L’agent Spark devrait, quant à lui, pouvoir aider les utilisateurs à passer aisément d’une conversation à une tâche.
Et nous ne sommes pas au bout de nos surprises puisqu'il sera bientôt possible de concevoir soi-même la voix de l’assistant. Explications.
La création de voix sur mesure est en préparation dans Gemini
En analysant le code de la version 17.78.13 de Gemini, l’équipe d’Android Authority a découvert des lignes de code qui annoncent l’arrivée prochaine d’un bouton « Create a voice » (« Créer une voix » en français). Plutôt que de laisser les utilisateurs choisir la voix de l’assistant dans un catalogue, Google semble vouloir ouvrir la voie à davantage de personnalisation.
L’utilisateur devrait en effet pouvoir décrire à l'IA ce qu’il veut entendre. Il pourrait, par exemple, décider du ton à employer, mais aussi de l’accent, du débit et de bien d’autres caractéristiques. Google explorait déjà cette piste cet été : de nouveaux curseurs en développement devaient permettre de régler la vitesse d’élocution ou le niveau de formalité de la voix.
Autre fonctionnalité plutôt sympathique : les développeurs ont aussi inclus un bouton « Surprise me » (« Surprends-moi ») qui devrait plaire aux indécis.
- Multimodalité texte, voix et fichiers
- Intégration poussée aux services Google
- Applications Web, mobile et bureau
De nombreuses questions en suspens
Sur le plan technique, Google dispose d’ores et déjà de tous les outils pour arriver à ses fins. Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS sait créer des voix à partir d’une description écrite. La firme a aussi promis une fonction de remixage pour ajuster la hauteur, l’accent ou le rythme d'une voix existante.
Les curieux qui veulent en savoir plus seront déçus car beaucoup de questions restent aujourd'hui sans réponse : la fonctionnalité sera-t-elle disponible dans tous les pays ? Sera-t-il possible de créer et de conserver plusieurs voix ? Pourra-t-on aussi accéder à ce niveau de personnalisation sur les enceintes et TV connectées ? Google n’a rien confirmé pour le moment.
Alors que 63 % des utilisateurs de Gemini passent par le mode vocal, cette fonction devrait, on s’en doute, rencontrer beaucoup de succès. Il ne reste plus qu’à espérer qu’elle soit déployée bientôt et qu'elle soit, bien sûr, disponible en langue française.

articles.title: De una isla retiraron 131 gatos, y luego sucedió algo que incluso sorprendió a los científicos
articles.text:
En 2008, las palomas de cabeza roja de Ogasawara (un archipiélago japonés) era crítica, ya que quedaban menos de 80 ejemplares por culpa de los gatos asilvestrados que llegaron a esas islas por la acción humana. Dos años después, empezó una campaña para capturarlos que terminó con 131 gatos retirados de Chichijima, una de las islas del archipiélago, y lo curioso llegó después cuando los científicos comprobaron que las aves se recuperaban a una velocidad por encima de lo esperado.
Tres años después, los registros de palomas adultas pasaron de 111 a 966, e incluso los ejemplares más jóvenes aumentaron de 9 a 189. Se trata de un crecimiento enorme para una subespecie (Columba janthina nitens) que solo vive a unos 1.000 kilómetros del territorio principal de Japón, pero todavía queda una pregunta por resolver que va más allá de de la retirada de gatos: ¿cómo consiguieron recuperarse tan rápido?
Una recuperación que también tenía una explicación genética
Un equipo de la Universidad de Kioto, encabezado por Daichi Tsujimoto, decidió investigar qué estaba pasando. En un estudio publicado en Communications Biology en julio de 2025, analizaron el ADN de estas palomas y lo compararon con el de otras poblaciones emparentadas. Descubrieron que más del 80 % de su genoma presentaba homocigosidad (una señal de reproducción entre individuos emparentados), pero tenían menos mutaciones especialmente perjudiciales de las que cabría esperar.
¿El motivo? Los investigadores creen que siglos de aislamiento y reproducción en poblaciones pequeñas pudieron favorecer la eliminación gradual de algunas mutaciones dañinas. Este proceso se conoce como purga genética y podría explicar por qué las palomas resistieron mejor las consecuencias de la endogamia. Eso sí, los científicos advierten de que no ocurre necesariamente con otras especies y que la escasa diversidad genética sigue siendo un riesgo para su futuro.
La historia también tiene otra particularidad. Los gatos capturados no fueron sacrificados como parte del programa de conservación, sino trasladados a Japón continental para acostumbrarlos al contacto humano y buscarles familias adoptivas. De esta forma, la retirada de los depredadores permitió proteger a las palomas sin acabar con la vida de los felinos.

articles.title: “Accès malveillant” chez Decathlon : 163 000 fiches clients dans la nature, jusqu'aux consignes laissées au livreur
articles.text:
“Accès malveillant” chez Decathlon : 163 000 fiches clients dans la nature, jusqu'aux consignes laissées au livreur
Noms, téléphones, adresses, présence d'un ascenseur, instructions pour le livreur, colis attendus cette semaine même : un pirate a déversé sur un forum cybercriminel les coulisses logistiques de decathlon.fr. L'enseigne confirme l'intrusion. Avec ces données, un escroc peut écrire un faux SMS de livreur d'une crédibilité redoutable.
Dans la nuit du dimanche 22 au lundi 23 novembre, vers 3 heures, un pirate se faisant appeler 4me1 a publié sur PwnForums quatre fichiers attribués à Decathlon. Le site spécialisé Cyberattaque.org s'est procuré l'archive, qui pèse environ 147 Mo une fois décompressée. Il y a dénombré 163 646 fiches, 137 549 adresses e-mail distinctes et 135 586 numéros de téléphone. Le soir même, l'enseigne nordiste a reconnu auprès de FrenchBreaches une intrusion chez l'un de ses prestataires.
🔴 ALERTE - Decathlon de nouveau concerné par une fuite de données, 163 000 clients potentiellement touchés !
Un pirate diffuse des fichiers contenant des noms, adresses, téléphones et détails de livraison, après plusieurs précédents incidents de sécurité liés à l'enseigne.… pic.twitter.com/okJBNntNCT
— Seb (@seblatombe) November 23, 2026
Que contiennent les fichiers volés à Decathlon ?
Le butin contient d'abord les noms, prénoms, adresses de commande et de livraison, ainsi que les références et dates d'achat. Il va beaucoup plus loin : type de logement, présence d'un ascenseur, consignes rédigées pour les livreurs. Un second fichier aligne 255 011 lignes de commandes, de juillet 2021 à novembre 2026. On y trouve aussi des prestations comme la livraison dans la pièce, le montage ou l'enlèvement.
Le détail le plus inquiétant : 611 lignes portent sur des livraisons programmées entre le 23 et le 28 novembre, en pleine semaine du Black Friday.
L'analyse de Cyberattaque.org confirme ce point : les champs structurés des quatre fichiers ne contiennent ni mot de passe, ni numéro de carte complet, ni IBAN. Le nom du prestataire reste inconnu. La CNIL doit être notifiée, et les clients touchés recevront un e-mail. Decathlon allonge ainsi une liste déjà copieuse de fichiers clients français dans la nature, du piratage de SFR au vol de données chez Engie, en passant par la fuite chez Chargemap.
Fuite Decathlon : le faux SMS de livreur, principal danger
Un message qui connaît votre nom, votre commande et votre créneau désarme les plus méfiants. Le scénario de l'arnaque au SMS de livraison est rodé : "colis bloqué", quelques euros de frais de réexpédition, puis un lien vers une page de paiement piégée. Il existe aussi une variante où un prétendu livreur laisse un message vocal. Decathlon invite à vérifier l'adresse de l'expéditeur et détaille sur sa page consacrée à l'hameçonnage es signes qui doivent alerter. Le réflexe le plus sûr : suivre ses colis depuis son compte, sur le site ou l'application, et jamais depuis un lien reçu par SMS.

articles.title: Hackers compromise Check Point Servers in 22 organizations
articles.text:
Threat actors have exploited multiple vulnerabilities to compromise two dozen Check Point Security management servers in an ongoing campaign targeting 22 organizations.
Threat intelligence firm GreyNoise detected the activity, noting that it resembled cyberespionage operations, although the attacker's motivation could not be conclusively determined.
The researchers track the activity as GT13 and confirmed it was ongoing between October 17 and November 2, when their visibility ended. However, given the threat actor's persistent access to Check Point devices, they believe the campaign remains active.
GreyNoise says the 22 victim organizations are spread across 17 countries, and show no clear evidence of specific targeting. They include government entities, financial services providers, and companies in the energy, transportation, mining, and manufacturing sectors.
The attacks were launched from 99 IP addresses that appear to come from compromised Check Point devices and ExpressVPN exit nodes.
A Rejetto HTTP File Server, compromised by exploiting CVE-2026-61500, was used as an operational relay for managing intrusions and collecting stolen data from the compromised environments.
While GreyNoise could not determine when or how the Check Point servers were breached, it observed the exploitation of CVE-2026-16232 during the post-compromise stages.
The vulnerability is an authentication bypass in Check Point SmartConsole that allows attackers to obtain an application login token and authenticate with administrator privileges.
Check Point warned about the flaw in July, marking it as an actively exploited zero-day.
The researchers also observed attempts to exploit CVE-2025-5777 (Citrix NetScaler), CVE-2024-21893 (Ivanti), CVE-2026-41089 (Windows NetLogon), CVE-2026-16232 (Check Point SmartConsole auth bypass to Run Script), and CVE-2026-98432 (Linux IPv4 UAF).
GreyNoise recorded over 1,400 network sessions, 800 command-line artifacts, and 1,200 file-related activities, such as:
- Stealing firewall databases, credentials, configuration data, and internal certificate authority files.
- Generating a new certificate in one victim's environment.
- Unloading security policies, effectively disabling firewall protections.
- Conducting internal network reconnaissance and attempting lateral movement.
- Targeting additional enterprise systems, including Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2023-4966), Ivanti Connect Secure (CVE-2024-21893), VMware vCenter (CVE-2021-21972 and CVE-2023-34048), Microsoft Exchange (CVE-2021-26855/34473), and Microsoft Netlogon (CVE-2020-1472).
On October 26, the attacker performed a bulk certificate management operation across all 24 compromised Check Point servers, which failed, but still helped GreyNoise identify victims.
Τhe researchers assess that GT13 operated an AI-powered offensive tool, based on behavior, observed automation, and custom tooling, but the use of AI in this campaign remains unconfirmed.
Although GreyNoise lost visibility into the campaign operations on November 2, the researchers believe it could still be ongoing and have notified international government partners and CERTs to alert impacted organizations.
The company also shared indicators of compromise (IoCs) that could help identify additional intrusions or block future attempts.
BleepingComputer has contacted Check Point to ask if they have better visibility into those attacks and which flaw was exploited for initial access, and we are waiting for their response.

articles.title: Disney+ Canada discounts six-month subscription for Black Friday 2026
articles.text:
Disney+ has kicked off its latest deal for Black Friday 2026.
Until Nov. 30, new and eligible returning subscribers can get Disney+ Standard with Ads for $3.99/month for six months. For context, this plan normally costs $8.99/month, so you’re saving $72 in total. None of the other Disney+ tiers are discounted for Black Friday.
It’s worth noting that this isn’t quite as good as last year’s Black Friday deal, which Disney said at the time was its best-ever. That offer gave you the Standard with Ads plans for 12 months instead of six.
Still, it’s a decent discount if you’re willing to put up with ads. It comes right after the premiere of Percy Jackson (Season 3) and shortly before the Dec. 8 premiere of Only Murders in the Building (Season 6).

articles.title: Plus forte que la RTX 5090 ? Ce qu'on sait de la carte graphique Moore Threads Lushan équipée de 64 Go de VRAM
articles.text:
Un simple teaser sans le moindre chiffre a suffi à faire rêver tous ceux qui font tourner des modèles d’IA sur leur PC. Le fabricant chinois Moore Threads y promet que sa future carte Lushan embarquera « la plus grande capacité de VRAM de l’histoire des cartes grand public ».
La VRAM, c’est cette mémoire ultra-rapide soudée directement sur la carte graphique, où un modèle d’IA doit tenir en entier pour rester fluide (s’il déborde sur la RAM classique du PC, les performances s’effondrent).
Le record actuel appartient à la RTX 5090 et ses 32 Go, vendue environ 7 000 euros en France.
Publié le 18 novembre sur les réseaux sociaux chinois, le message provient d’un chef de produit de la MTT S80, la carte actuelle de la marque. Les détails officiels tomberont lors de la MDC 2026, sa conférence développeurs organisée les 29 et 30 décembre à Pékin.
Lushan avait déjà été évoquée en décembre 2025 aux côtés de Huagang, la nouvelle architecture maison destinée à remplacer les MTT S80 et S90. Moore Threads promettait alors de quadrupler la mémoire de la MTT S80 (qui compte 16 Go), d’où la rumeur tenace des 64 Go qui circule aujourd’hui sans aucune confirmation officielle.
Ce que l’on attend
Les multiplicateurs avancés par la marque donnent le vertige : 15 fois plus de performances en jeu, 50 fois en ray tracing et 64 fois en IA. Il faut pourtant remettre ces chiffres en perspective, puisqu’ils se comparent à la MTT S80, une carte de 2022 battue à sa sortie par de vieilles GeForce d’entrée de gamme.
    Pour aller plus loin
La Chine affirme avoir son « Nvidia killer », Moore Threads dévoile Huagang avec de premiers chiffres
            
Le bond spectaculaire en IA pourrait surtout provenir de formats comme le FP4, qui code chaque nombre sur 4 bits au lieu de 16 pour calculer plus vite au prix d’une précision moindre. Plus concret pour les joueurs, Lushan devrait enfin prendre en charge DirectX 12 Ultimate (l’interface des jeux modernes avec ray tracing), là où la MTT S80 se contentait de DirectX 9 et 11.
Pour l’IA locale, la quantité de mémoire ne fait de toute façon pas tout. Un LLM (grand modèle de langage) doit relire l’intégralité de ses poids en mémoire pour générer chaque token (un fragment de mot), ce qui rend la bande passante mémoire déterminante.
Un modèle de 70 milliards de paramètres compressé en 4 bits pèse environ 40 Go. Avec les 448 Go/s de la MTT S80, la génération plafonnerait autour de 11 tokens par seconde, contre plus de 40 avec les 1 792 Go/s d’une RTX 5090, et Moore Threads n’a encore communiqué aucun débit pour Lushan.
CUDA, ROCm, MUSA : le vrai test sera logiciel
Une carte pensée pour l’IA ne vaut que par son écosystème logiciel, et la quasi-totalité des outils reposent sur CUDA, la plateforme propriétaire de Nvidia. Zhang Jianzhong, le fondateur de Moore Threads, le sait mieux que quiconque : il a dirigé Nvidia en Chine pendant quinze ans.
Même AMD a mis des années à rendre ROCm (son équivalent de CUDA) réellement exploitable sur ses Radeon grand public, PyTorch n’y étant arrivé sous Windows qu’en préversion en septembre 2025.
Moore Threads a choisi un raccourci pragmatique avec MUSA, qui calque volontairement les interfaces de CUDA pour rendre le portage presque mécanique. Son adaptateur torchada promet ainsi que le code PyTorch existant « fonctionne sur le matériel MUSA » après un simple import, tandis que le moteur llama.cpp (la référence pour faire tourner des LLM en local) a intégré un module MUSA dès juillet 2024.
Ce passage par le code source n’a rien d’un détail juridique. La licence de CUDA interdit en effet de décompiler un programme compilé avec les outils de Nvidia pour l’exécuter sur une puce concurrente.
Ce qu’il faut surveiller à l’annonce
- La mémoire : sa capacité exacte, son type (GDDR6 ou GDDR7) et surtout la largeur du bus, qui dicte la bande passante réelle.
- La consommation : la MTT S80 engloutissait pas moins de 109 W au repos à son lancement.
- Les pilotes : seuls des tests indépendants permettront de vérifier si les jeux DirectX 12 tournent sans accroc.
- Le support logiciel : sous Linux, on compile aujourd’hui llama.cpp avec l’option GGML_MUSA=ON, on installe torch_musa pour PyTorch et vLLM passe par le greffon vllm-musa. Moore Threads devra confirmer que Lushan est pris en charge dès sa sortie.
- La disponibilité : la marque n’a quasiment jamais vendu ses cartes hors de Chine, et figure depuis octobre 2023 sur la liste noire commerciale américaine, ce qui complique son accès aux fondeurs comme TSMC.
Lushan arrive avec le bon argument au bon moment, alors que les GeForce les mieux dotées en mémoire ont vu leurs tarifs s’envoler. Calquer MUSA sur CUDA reste le pari logiciel le plus pragmatique du marché. Bref, rendez-vous le 29 décembre.

articles.title: Frankfurt-based CommerzVentures closes €50 million Fund IV, betting on early-stage FinTech and AI
articles.text:
CommerzVentures, a Frankfurt-based specialist venture capital firm focused on financial services, has closed its fourth fund at €50 million.
The fourth fund — CommerzVentures IV (Fund IV) — is anchored by Commerzbank and is deliberately smaller than its predecessors; the firm managed over €550 million across three prior funds, including €300 million in Fund III.
“Fund IV is deliberately smaller because we want to invest earlier. We aim to combine early conviction with the experience, industry connections and hands-on support founders need to build their businesses,” said Judith Vogel, Partner, CommerzVentures.
Founded in 2014, CommerzVentures is a specialist financial services investor having backed more than 40 companies across its three previous funds. Its notable portfolio companies include eToro, iwoca, Mambu, and Marqeta, several of which have gone on to achieve significant scale or public listings.
The CommerzVentures IV is jointly led by general partners Heiko Schwender and Vogel, supported by venture partners and senior advisers. The pair have backed companies including Deblock, eToro, Marqeta, and Unique, supporting these startups through major growth phases, and in some cases, through to public listing.
With Fund IV, CommerzVentures is making a strategic shift from its past funds to focus on earlier-stage investing. It argues this shift also reflects a maturing FinTech ecosystem, with the strongest companies reaching revenue faster, scaling more quickly, and moving through funding rounds at a pace that rewards investors who come in earliest.
“In financial services, a strong AI product is only the starting point. Founders also need to earn trust, navigate regulation, and connect to complex infrastructure. That is where our experience and network can make a difference,” said Schwender, Partner, CommerzVentures.
The firm says the new fund will back founders building at the intersection of AI and financial services, though it will also selectively back adjacent sectors such as supply chain and cybersecurity, where its financial services expertise and network can add tangible value.
CommerzVentures says its co-founders, Patrick Meisberger and Stefan Tirtey, will continue overseeing CommerzVentures’ existing funds. “We are proud of what CommerzVentures has built together with our founders, our team and Commerzbank as anchor investor. We are delighted to see Heiko and Judith lead Fund IV into its next chapter,” said Meisberger.
The Fund IV will deploy capital at Seed and early Series A stages, primarily across the EU, the UK and Switzerland. CommerzVentures plans to build a portfolio of around 25 companies with Fund IV and ,with its new investment thesis, the firm is positioning itself to catch the next wave of FinTech and AI innovation at its earliest stages.

articles.title: Nigeria plans 500,000-job pipeline in data protection
articles.text:
Nigeria’s data protection regulator wants more mid-career professionals to step into the country’s growing privacy workforce, betting that local talent can fill a global shortage of certified experts.
Speaking at a capacity-building session for media professionals in Abuja on Friday, November 20, the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) National Commissioner Vincent Olatunji outlined the agency’s push to expand the country’s data privacy ecosystem and position Nigeria as an exporter of compliance talent.
Section 32 of the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 requires businesses to employ Data Protection Officers (DPOs), but without enough certified professionals, local companies risk non-compliance, data breaches, and lost foreign investment.
To prevent a talent crunch and preserve local experts, the NDPC said it is using a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model to create 500,000 jobs. According to Olatunji, compliance with the Act has already triggered a sharp rise in certified professionals across the country, though supply still lags behind market demand.
While he did not specify the exact number of DPOs the market requires, the regulator’s 500,000-job target highlights how wide the talent deficit remains.
“When we started, we had less than 1,000 data protection officers in all of this country,” he said. “At the commission, we have over 90% of our staff that are certified. And in Nigeria, we have over 10,000 certified data protection officers.”
Exporting talent
Olatunji noted that the ecosystem has already created more than 27,000 jobs in under three years, driven largely by Data Protection Compliance Organisations (DPCOs) licenced to conduct audits and enforce compliance on behalf of the government.
Beyond local businesses, the regulator said it is pitching Nigeria as a talent hub for international markets grappling with privacy skill shortages.
“We want data privacy within the ecosystem, or if you need the service of a DPO, you look towards Africa, and of course, Nigeria,” Olatunji said, pointing to talent gaps abroad. “Even in the UK, 94.7% of breaches are due to lack of qualified personnel in data privacy and protection. So everywhere, all over the world, they are looking for data privacy and protection experts.”
Several former NDPC staffers have already transitioned into international roles across the United States and the United Kingdom, including executive leadership positions at global financial institutions, he added. To sustain the talent pipeline, the commission said it has begun taking data privacy training directly into Nigerian tertiary institutions to introduce students to the field as a viable career path.
For working professionals, Olatunji framed data protection not as a complete career pivot, but as a flexible, high-demand add-on. Because organisations are legally required to appoint DPOs, certified individuals can consult for multiple firms simultaneously.
“The good thing about this is you can be a DPO and do some other stuff. And you can be a DPO for four, five, three, ten organisations. You can be a freelance DPO. Nobody ties you down to any particular spot,” he said.

articles.title: Auf Tiktok ist alles „Code Rotted“: Was der Gaming-Begriff im echten Leben beschreibt
articles.text:
Auf Tiktok ist alles „Code Rotted“: Was der Gaming-Begriff im echten Leben beschreibt
„Code Rotted“ ist ein neuer Begriff, der es in die Jugendsprache geschafft hat. Ursprünglich stammt er aus der Gaming-Szene und beschreibt plötzlich auftretende Fehler in alten Spielen. So kann beispielsweise eine Figur, mit der man früher interagieren konnte, plötzlich nicht mehr reagieren, oder eine Tür, durch die man in der virtuellen Welt schon tausendmal hindurchgeschritten ist, bleibt dauerhaft verschlossen. Grund dafür sind oft Aktualisierungen der Plattformen, auf denen die alten Spiele laufen und dafür sorgen, dass Teile davon nicht mehr funktionieren. Die Gen Z wendet diesen Begriff allerdings inzwischen auch auf alltägliche Situationen an. So lässt sich inzwischen nahezu jedes Problem auf „verrotteten Code“ zurückführen.
So kam der „Code Rot“-Begriff zustande
Wie Mashable berichtet, gewann der Begriff erstmals auf Roblox an Bedeutung. Auslöser waren einige Gamer:innen, die Spiele aus ihrer Kindheit wiederentdeckten. Insbesondere auf Tiktok sind zahlreiche Videos zu finden, die sich mit diesen Glitches befassen. Im Oktober machte ein Ich, einfach unverbesserlich 4-Filter den „Code Rot“-Witz auch über Roblox hinaus bekannt. Dieser greift allerdings ein tatsächliches Problem auf. So stellte das Pew Research Center in einer Studie aus dem Jahr 2024 fest, dass 38 Prozent der Internetseiten, die es 2013 in seine Stichprobe aufgenommen hatte, zehn Jahre später nicht mehr zugänglich waren.
    Top-Artikel
        
    
    
    
    
Es gibt auch eine visuelle Version dieses Verfalls mit einem ähnlichen Namen. Der Begriff „Pixel Rot” beschreibt den Zerfall von Bildern in sichtbare Blöcke und verschwommene Darstellungen. Ein Beispiel hierfür sind Memes, die so oft gespeichert und geteilt wurden, dass sie kaum noch erkennbar sind. Mit jeder Komprimierung gehen weitere Details verloren, sodass ein Bild weiter im Umlauf bleiben kann, obwohl es längst nicht mehr wie das Original aussieht. Ein anschauliches Beispiel hierfür lieferte Petapixel: Je öfter man ein Bild auf Instagram hochlädt, desto unkenntlicher wird es.
Gen Z nutzt digitale Begriffe für Alltägliches
Für die Generationen Z und Alpha kann inzwischen alles „Code Rot“ sein. Beispiele sind ein fehlgeschlagener Login, eine unverständliche Hausaufgabe – oder auch eine Hauswand, von der die Farbe abblättert. Der Begriff reiht sich in einen wachsenden Wortschatz ein, mit dem junge Menschen ihr Leben beschreiben, als handele es sich um ein Videospiel. Das Wort „NPC” ist ein bekanntes Beispiel. Die Abkürzung steht für „nicht spielbarer Charakter” und beschreibt jemanden, der sich wie eine Nebenfigur in der Geschichte einer anderen Person verhält. Dass junge Generationen Begriffe wie diese in ihren Wortschatz übernehmen, ist nicht überraschend – schließlich sind sie damit aufgewachsen, online zu lernen, zu spielen oder Freundschaften zu knüpfen.
Müsste man Code rot nicht klein schreiben, weil ja das Verb „to rot“, also verrotten gemeint ist. So sieht es immer nach der Farbe Rot aus, Code Red ist aber wieder was ganz anderes.

articles.title: The Download: AI’s gas power boom and a consciousness reality check
articles.text:
The Download: AI’s gas power boom and a consciousness reality check
Plus: Huang's Nvidia return has lifted markets and put Trump under fire.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants
One of the biggest obstacles to building a data center is getting approval to connect to the grid, a wait that could last as long as a decade. Some developers won’t wait and are instead building their own off-grid gas power plants to fuel the AI boom.
As of October 2026, developers had announced plans for more than 100 such gas power plants at data centers in the US. But bypassing the grid brings its own problems, from worsening climate emissions to potentially higher energy bills for everyone else.
Find out how the push for gas power could shape the grid—and the climate—for decades.
—Casey Crownhart
A legendary philosopher isn’t buying Anthropic’s consciousness argument
Before going public last week, Anthropic named the possibility of AI consciousness as a risk factor for investors, warning that it might introduce new rules to protect its models. But that stance came under fire from an inconvenient source: one of the philosophers who helped shape our understanding of consciousness in the first place.
Thomas Nagel, best known for his essay about what it's like to be a bat, was blunt. “Here are some of the smartest people on the planet being completely idiotic,” he said. He argued that producing language isn't enough to establish consciousness. But other philosophers disagree.
Here's why language has become central to the debate over conscious AI.
—James O'Donnell

Quote of the day
“The President is selling out our national security to keep the stock market high and probably for some f**king donation to his ballroom.”
—Senator Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.) says on X that Donald Trump’s avarice is behind Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO.
One more thing
How gamification took over the world
It’s a thought that occurs to every video-game player at some point: what if the weird, hyper-focused state I enter in virtual worlds could somehow be applied to the real one?
For a handful of consultants, startup gurus, and game designers in the late 2000s, this state of “blissful productivity” became the key to unlocking our true human potential. Their vision became the global phenomenon of gamification—but it didn’t live up to the hype.
Instead of liberating us, gamification became a tool for coercion, distraction, and control. Find out why we fell for it—and how we can recover.

articles.title: Ladybird is the first new browser engine in years, and of course some sites are broken
articles.text:
First look: Ladybird, an independent web browser running on a rendering engine its developers wrote from scratch, is now available for alpha testing on macOS and Linux. Developer Andreas Kling announced the release Monday after more than four years of work. It is the first browser in years not to run on Gecko, Blink, or WebKit, the three engines behind today's most popular browsers.
Most browser makers start from an existing engine and build features on top of it. Ladybird's team wrote its own, so every part of the browser, from how pages are laid out to how they are drawn on screen, comes from code the project controls instead of code it inherited.
Ladybird started as part of a C++ project, but its developers later began porting the code to Rust using AI. That means testers are getting a codebase that is partway through a move from one language to another, with AI tools helping with the rewrite.
For engineers, this makes Ladybird a live test of whether AI-assisted porting can work at the scale of a full browser engine.
Kling is candid about the browser's current limitations. In his announcement, he said the browser built around the Ladybird engine "is modest but functional." He also warned that "some websites won't work" during the alpha. A new engine has a lot of ground to cover before it can handle the full range of sites people use every day, and the alpha is meant to show where it still falls short.
For now, only two platforms are supported. The alpha runs on macOS and Linux, and a Windows version is planned for a "later stage" of the project.
A nonprofit organization backs the software. Its stated goal is to create "an independent, fast and secure browser that respects user privacy and fosters an open web." That mission makes Ladybird less a commercial product than an effort to add another independent engine to a web that just three engines now dominate.
That concentration has built up over time. Many engines have come and gone over the decades, and an online catalog documents dozens of them. The three left standing all have deep roots. Gecko, the oldest, first appeared in Netscape 6 in 2000 and now powers Mozilla Firefox.
Apple's WebKit arrived in Safari in 2003 as a fork of KHTML, the engine developed by the KDE project. About a decade later, the Google-backed Chromium project forked WebKit to create Blink, which now runs Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Opera, and several other browsers.
The family tree shows how narrow the field really is. Blink comes from WebKit, and WebKit comes from KHTML, so two of the three leading engines share an ancestor. Any browser built on one of them inherits years of design decisions made by someone else.
That is the gap Ladybird is trying to fill. The alpha gives developers and enthusiasts their first chance to try an engine with no ties to that lineage and see how it handles the modern web. Their testing will show how far a from-scratch project has come in four years and how much work is left before Ladybird can be used as an everyday browser.

articles.title: OnePlus vació su tienda en línea en Estados Unidos y Canadá y solo deja soporte para sus celulares
articles.text:
OnePlus eliminó todos los productos de su sitio web en Estados Unidos y lo convirtió en una página de soporte para quienes ya tienen sus equipos. El cambio se notó el 23 de noviembre y alcanza también a Canadá y a otras regiones, aunque no a todas.
El sitio muestra ahora un mensaje de la empresa: tras el anuncio del 16 de julio, la web se “simplifica” para centrarse en la atención de los dispositivos existentes. Para garantía y reparaciones, remite a su página de servicio. Los accesorios también desaparecieron del catálogo.
En el aviso oficial publicado en su sitio de soporte, fechado el 12 de noviembre, OnePlus precisó dos consecuencias. El historial de pedidos de la cuenta dejó de estar disponible en línea y la aplicación OnePlus Store se discontinuó ese mismo día. Quien necesite ayuda con una compra anterior debe contactar al servicio al cliente. Los términos de venta, incluida la garantía limitada, siguen publicados en el sitio de servicio.
Qué conservan los dueños de un OnePlus
El anuncio del 16 de julio, que la empresa mantiene en su página, indicó que OnePlus concluía los lanzamientos de productos en Europa y Norteamérica. Según ese texto, los equipos existentes seguirán recibiendo actualizaciones de software, parches de seguridad y servicio posventa.
Sus preguntas frecuentes agregan que la garantía vigente se respetará y que las reparaciones seguirán disponibles para los equipos elegibles. La empresa también afirmó que los derechos de los consumidores bajo la ley aplicable no cambian.
Hay una transición de software en marcha. Los usuarios cuyos teléfonos cumplan los requisitos podrán actualizar, si lo desean, a ColorOS, la capa de Oppo, en lugar de OxygenOS. La empresa dijo que quien lo haga podrá volver a OxygenOS, aunque las versiones disponibles para ese regreso se informarán más adelante. Los modelos que no entren quedarán con mantenimiento.
El soporte no dura lo mismo para todos los productos. Según Android Authority, los Buds 4 dejaron de recibir actualizaciones de seguridad en julio, el reloj OnePlus Watch 3 tendrá soporte hasta marzo y la versión de 43 mm hasta julio.
Otros mercados siguen abiertos, con matices
El resto del mapa es desigual. 9to5Google, medio digital especializado en noticias, señaló que los sitios del Reino Unido y de países europeos como Francia siguen operativos, pero ofrecen sobre todo productos de Oppo. El OnePlus 15, por ejemplo, ya no puede comprarse en el Reino Unido. El medio supone que esos sitios también cerrarán, aunque la empresa no lo confirmó.
El sitio de la India no sufrió cambios y sigue vendiendo equipos. Android Authority informó que la marca concentra ahora su actividad en China y la India, donde lanzó en octubre el OnePlus 16, con un precio inicial de 5.999 yuanes, unos USD 898.
El aviso de OnePlus no da una fecha de cierre para los sitios que siguen abiertos. Tampoco precisa hasta cuándo recibirá actualizaciones cada modelo, un dato que depende de cada equipo y que la empresa aún no detalló en su página de soporte.

articles.title: VMware Updates Patch Critical ESX, vCenter Vulnerabilities
articles.text:
Broadcom on Tuesday announced the release of patches for 23 vulnerabilities across multiple VMware products, including critical-severity flaws in ESX and vCenter.
The vCenter patches resolve seven bugs, including a critical authentication bypass issue in the VMware Directory Service tracked as CVE-2026-123903 (CVSS score of 9.8).
Additionally, the fixes target three denial-of-service (DoS) issues in the VMware Directory Service, a local privilege escalation in a vpxd service script, an arbitrary file write while processing certain archives, and a security policy enforcement failure in the vSphere Distributed Switch (vDS).
The ESX updates resolve seven security issues as well, including three critical-severity weaknesses leading to code execution on the host.
CVE-2026-123910 and CVE-2026-123911 (CVSS score of 9.8) are heap out-of-bounds write and use-after-free flaws in the I/O filter service, while CVE-2026-123912 (CVSS score of 9.3) is an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the XHCI USB controller that requires local administrative privileges on a virtual machine.
An attacker “may exploit this issue to execute code as the virtual machine’s VMX process running on the host. On ESX, the exploitation is contained within the VMX sandbox whereas, on Workstation and Fusion, this may lead to code execution on the machine where Workstation or Fusion is installed,” Broadcom explains.
The remaining four include a stack-based buffer overflow in the VMkernel, a DoS vulnerability in guest RPC, a security bypass in the host configuration store, and a signature verification bypass.
Broadcom also patched eight flaws in Avi Load Balancer that could lead to code execution with root privileges, privilege escalation to root, command execution, password hash leaks, access to the routing management interface and other resources, and unintended file access, and one in VMware Tools leading to DoS.
According to Broadcom, some of the issues were resolved with the vCenter updates released last week. vCenter version 8.0 U3m contained the fixes, and customers who applied it do not need to update again. vCenter 9.1.x deployments, however, as well as ESX, VMware Tools, Workstation, Fusion, and Avi Load Balancer instances, need to be updated.
“Patches are cumulative, so the updates listed in this advisory also contain the fixes from VMSA-2026-0009 when they are newer than the fixed versions listed in VMSA-2026-0009. However, this advisory does not mention the SDDC Manager updates from VMSA-2026-0009; please ensure you are handling those,” the company notes.
Broadcom makes no mention of any of these vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild, but it’s not uncommon for the company to not warn about exploitation in its public advisories.
On Tuesday, Broadcom also updated its advisory on Node2Shell to add VMware Cloud Foundation version 9.1.2 to the list of fixed releases.

articles.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
articles.text:
Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
- Date:
  November 17, 2026
- Source:
  University of Jyväskylä - Jyväskylän yliopisto
- Summary:
  A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.
- Share:
An eight-year study of children in Finland has revealed a surprising connection between screen time and brain function. Researchers found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the widespread assumption that screen time is necessarily harmful to developing brains.
The findings suggest that the amount of time children spend in front of screens may be less important than how they use that time. Activities that encourage learning, creativity, and problem-solving could be particularly valuable. Researchers emphasize that the goal should not be to eliminate screen time, but to balance it with physical activity and mentally stimulating experiences.
The discovery comes amid growing concerns about insufficient physical activity among teenagers. A sedentary lifestyle has been linked to poorer academic performance, while regular exercise is known to support brain function, particularly in adults. However, scientists still have much to learn about how physical activity, sitting, and screen use during childhood influence thinking abilities later in adolescence.
These questions are especially important because childhood and adolescence are critical periods of brain development. Changes in attention, memory, and learning during these years can have lasting consequences, potentially influencing educational opportunities and career paths well into adulthood.
To investigate these relationships, Finnish researchers examined how screen time, physical activity, and sedentary behavior from childhood through adolescence were associated with cognitive performance in teenagers. They also explored whether the connections differed between boys and girls and whether the intensity of physical activity made a difference.
More Screen Time Linked to Better Thinking Skills
One of the study's most unexpected findings was that greater screen time throughout childhood was associated with better cognitive processing in adolescence.
Cognitive processing refers to the mental abilities people use to take in information, pay attention, remember details, learn new things, and solve problems. These abilities play an important role in school performance and everyday decision-making.
The findings challenge the idea that all screen time should be viewed as harmful. However, the researchers caution that the relationship may depend on what children are actually doing while using digital devices. Watching videos, playing games that require strategic thinking, and engaging in educational activities may involve very different levels of mental effort.
"The findings suggest that screen time can support children's and adolescents' cognitive processing. Presumably, the essential point here is what kind of things they do in their screen time. Teachers and parents should encourage children to use devices and screens in such ways that promote active thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and learning," states Doctoral Researcher Petri Jalanko from the University of Jyväskylä.
"We should not regard screen time solely as harmful but seek balance between physical activity and screen time that promotes active thinking," Jalanko summarizes.
Exercise Affects Boys' and Girls' Brains Differently
The researchers also uncovered a more complicated picture of how physical activity relates to thinking and memory.
Among girls, spending more time engaged in light-intensity physical activity since childhood was associated with better working memory during adolescence. For boys, greater participation in guided physical activity over the same period was linked to stronger working memory.
Working memory is the brain's ability to temporarily hold and use information. It allows someone to remember instructions while completing a task, keep track of numbers during mental calculations, or follow a conversation while processing new information.
Light-intensity physical activity generally includes relatively gentle movements that do not substantially increase breathing or heart rate. Guided physical activity refers to exercise carried out with some form of instruction or supervision, such as organized sports or structured exercise sessions.
The differences between boys and girls suggest that the relationship between exercise and brain health may depend on more than simply how much a person moves. The type of activity, how it is organized, and the individual's sex could all play a role.
Another Surprising Finding About Physical Activity
The study produced another counterintuitive result. Teenagers who reported spending less time in unsupervised physical activity tended to perform better on measures of cognitive processing.
Yet when researchers used wearable sensors to objectively measure movement and heart rate, they found no association between overall physical activity or sedentary time and cognitive performance.
One possible explanation is that wearable devices measure movement without revealing what a person is actually doing. For example, a sensor may record periods of sitting or physical activity, but it cannot determine whether someone is solving a difficult problem, studying, participating in an organized activity, or simply resting.
This distinction could help explain why questionnaire responses revealed relationships that were not apparent in the sensor measurements.
"Our study indicates that the connections of physical activity and sedentary behavior to cognitive processing are complex and depend on the sex, the type and assessment method of physical activity and sedentary time. Moreover, boys and girls may benefit from different types of physical activity in view of brain health," Jalanko adds.
"However, we need more intervention studies to find out causal relations and sex differences in this respect. Moreover, it is important to examine more specifically the effects of the intensity of physical activity on changes taking place in cognitive processing."
What the Eight-Year Study Revealed
The findings come from an eight-year follow-up conducted as part of the PANIC study, a long-running Finnish research project investigating children's physical activity and nutrition.
The current analysis included 260 participants, consisting of 124 girls and 136 boys. Their average age at the adolescent assessment was 15.8 years.
Researchers collected information about physical activity and sedentary behavior using both questionnaires and wearable devices that combined heart rate monitoring with movement measurements. This approach allowed them to compare participants' reported activities with data collected by sensors.
To evaluate cognitive abilities, the researchers used the CogState test battery, a collection of computerized assessments designed to measure aspects of mental performance. The tests examined learning, attention, and working memory.
Importantly, the findings show associations rather than cause and effect. They do not establish that increasing screen time will improve a child's thinking abilities or that reducing certain types of exercise will produce cognitive benefits. Intervention studies, in which researchers deliberately change participants' activities and measure the results, are needed to determine whether these relationships are causal.
Nevertheless, the results offer an important perspective on the continuing debate over children's screen use. Rather than treating all time spent with digital devices as equally harmful, the researchers suggest paying closer attention to whether those activities encourage active thinking and learning.
The research also highlights the importance of considering different forms of physical activity rather than focusing exclusively on the total amount of exercise children receive.
Together, the findings suggest that supporting healthy brain development may require a more nuanced approach, one that combines physical activity with opportunities for learning, creativity, and mental engagement, including those that take place on screens.
The study was published in the scientific journal Pediatric Exercise Science.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Jyväskylä - Jyväskylän yliopisto. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Petri Jalanko, Marja H. Leppänen, Bert Bond, Jari A. Laukkanen, Timo A. Lakka, Eero A. Haapala. Associations of Physical Activity and Sedentary Time From Childhood to Adolescence With Cognition in Adolescence: The PANIC Study. Pediatric Exercise Science, 2026; 38 (3): 268 DOI: 10.1123/pes.2025-0083
