articles.title: Plus besoin d’un smartphone dernier cri : Free intègre la traduction en direct directement dans son réseau mobile
articles.text:
Jusqu’à présent, briser la barrière de la langue au téléphone relevait du parcours du combattant. Il fallait soit jongler avec des applications tierces peu ergonomiques, soit posséder un smartphone très haut de gamme, comme les derniers Samsung ou les Google Pixel. Free a décidé de rebattre les cartes. Dans un communiqué publié ce mardi 24 novembre, l’opérateur dévoile « Traduction Live », qu’il présente comme « une première en France sur un réseau mobile ».
L’astuce de Free ? Rapatrier toute l’intelligence artificielle directement au cœur de son infrastructure réseau. Résultat : plus besoin de télécharger la moindre application ni de s’équiper d’un appareil spécifique. Le service fonctionne sur les appels entrants comme sortants, vers un fixe ou un mobile, depuis la France ou l’étranger, et peu importe l’opérateur de votre interlocuteur (seuls les numéros d’urgence 112, 15, 17 et 18 sont logiquement exclus). L’unique prérequis technique consiste à disposer d’un smartphone 4G ou 5G compatible avec les appels VoLTE, VoNR ou Wi-Fi (VoWiFi).
Dix langues au menu et une activation en deux temps
Pour son lancement, « Traduction Live » prend en charge dix langues : l’allemand, l’anglais, l’espagnol, le français, l’italien, le portugais (brésilien), le russe, le chinois (mandarin), le coréen et le japonais.
Concrètement, comment ça marche ? Avant de passer votre premier appel polyglotte, il faut activer l’option gratuitement depuis votre Espace Abonné Mobile ou via l’application Free (dans la rubrique « Mes options »). Une fois cette étape validée, la manipulation en plein appel se veut enfantine :
- Lancer l’outil : au cours d’une conversation en 4G, 5G ou Wi-Fi, tapez simplement ## sur le clavier de votre téléphone.
- Choisir la langue : prononcez la commande vocale « Ok Free, traduis-en… » suivie de la langue désirée, puis parlez le plus naturellement du monde.
Clonage vocal et résumé par SMS : les deux bonus bien pensés
Free ne s’est pas contenté d’une simple traduction robotique. L’opérateur ajoute deux options supplémentaires, elles aussi activables depuis l’espace client, pour muscler l’expérience.
La première mise sur le clonage vocal : plutôt que d’infliger une voix de synthèse monotone à votre correspondant, le système reproduit votre propre timbre de voix pour rendre l’échange bien plus naturel. La seconde génère automatiquement un résumé de la conversation par SMS une fois l’appel terminé. Un outil particulièrement pratique pour retrouver d’un coup d’œil l’horaire d’un rendez-vous ou les détails d’une réservation effectuée à l’étranger.
Serveurs en France et consentement : Free joue la carte de la transparence
Forcément, qui dit écoute et traduction en temps réel dit questions légitimes autour de la confidentialité. Free a anticipé les critiques en mettant en avant une approche souveraine. Développé en interne par ses équipes à partir de plusieurs briques d’IA — dont l’opérateur tait toutefois la provenance exacte —, l’outil tourne exclusivement sur des serveurs hébergés en France et gérés par Free. L’entreprise assure qu’aucune conversation n’est enregistrée ni utilisée pour entraîner des modèles d’intelligence artificielle, précisant que les transcriptions servant aux résumés SMS sont supprimées sitôt le message envoyé.
Enfin, impossible de piéger votre interlocuteur à son insu. Dès que vous déclenchez la traduction, un message vocal l’avertit et lui laisse la possibilité de s’y opposer. Même son de cloche si le résumé par SMS est activé : la personne au bout du fil est prévenue dès le début de l’appel et peut bloquer la fonction directement depuis le clavier de son mobile. Une transparence bienvenue, et surtout indispensable pour rester dans les clous de la loi française, qui interdit d’enregistrer une conversation sans l’accord de son correspondant.

articles.title: Amazon says hackers’ AI agents found and exploited 0-day with little human input
articles.text:
Amazon said AI agents recently found and exploited a zero-day vulnerability with no human oversight beyond a simple instruction to get root access on an East Asian university server.
The agents were running on Cairn, an open source AI penetration-testing framework. The hackers, who provided prompts in simplified Chinese and configured the model to the Chinese Standard Time zone, gave the agents a list of IP addresses and the goal: “obtain shell access.” In short order, the agents discovered a zero-day in an open source medical imaging AI application running on one of the target servers. The agents then exploited the vulnerability and gained full control of the system.
“These findings show that agentic offensive operations are already happening, and defenders should prepare for the speed and persistence these tools enable,” Amazon said.
Made for defenders, but attackers like it too
Cairn is an open source AI problem-solving engine whose first validated domain is autonomous penetration testing. Users give it a task or goal and, optionally, hints for achieving it. A server maintains a shared graph containing facts and hints. A dispatcher reads the graph, schedules tasks, manages containers, and writes the protocol. The dispatcher can then assign each project to a dedicated worker container, each of which runs multiple agents concurrently. Cairn is model-agnostic and can be used on worker back ends, including Claude Code, Codex, and Pi. Researchers from security firm Palo Alto Networks have also observed Cairn being used with GLM 5.2, DeepSeek V4 Flash, and DeepSeek V4 Pro.
Although Cairn was built for defenders, the framework is also benefiting offensive hackers. Earlier this month, Palo Alto Networks said hackers used the framework to target organizations in the semiconductor, defense, and civil society sectors. articles.title: ¿A qué hora se estrenan los episodios 3x07 y 3x08 de 'Los Anillos de Poder', el final de la temporada 3?
articles.text:
La temporada 3 de Los Anillos de Poder llega a su final con el estreno de sus episodios 7 y 8, los últimos de esta entrega. En ella, los ejércitos de Sauron han avanzado por todo el continente, conquistando cuanto encuentran a su paso. Solo unos pocos bastiones aislados se interponen entre el Señor Oscuro y la victoria total: Khazad-dûm, donde los enanos permanecen ahora recluidos en las profundidades de sus salones bajo la montaña, y los reinos élficos de Lindon y Rivendel, protegidos por sus Tres Anillos.
Mientras tanto, en las profundidades de Mordor, en su recién erigida torre de Barad-dûr, el Señor Oscuro trabaja sin descanso, obsesionado con forjar un poder capaz de doblegar a los últimos enemigos que aún se le resisten: «Un Anillo para gobernarlos a todos…». Ahora, todos los pueblos libres de la Tierra Media —enanos, elfos, hombres y magos— deberán encontrar la forma de unirse en una carrera contrarreloj para impedir que Sauron alcance su objetivo: someter toda forma de vida bajo su dominio absoluto.
Acerca de dónde podrá verse, a diferencia de otros títulos, aquí no depende para nada del territorio. En Estados Unidos, España, Latinoamérica y en el resto del mundo, el final de Los Anillos de Poder temporada 3 estará disponible en Amazon Prime Video. La plataforma alberga los derechos exclusivos de toda la serie, incluyendo su tercera entrega. Por tanto, evidentemente el desenlace de esta formará parte de su catálogo.
Hora de estreno de Los Anillos de Poder 3x07 y 3x08
En cuanto a la hora de estreno de los episodios 7 y 8 de Los Anillos de Poder, en Estados Unidos se emitirán el martes 24 de noviembre a las 21:00h E.T. En España y Latinoamérica, llegará a Amazon Prime Video en la conversión horaria de cada país:
- España: 3:00 h. del miércoles 25 de noviembre.
- México, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica: 20:00 h.
- Perú, Colombia, Panamá, Ecuador: 21:00 h.
- Venezuela, Bolivia, República Dominicana, Puerto Rico: 22:00 h.
- Chile, Paraguay, Argentina, Brasil, Uruguay: 23:00 h.
Prueba Amazon Prime Video totalmente gratis durante 30 días y disfruta del catálogo completo de la plataforma sin límites. Solo con darte de alta tendrás acceso instantáneo a las mejores películas y series, además de envíos gratis en Amazon y otras ventajas.
Este horario es diferente al habitual para la serie y la plataforma, que ha adelantado el estreno unas horas en parte por la celebración de Acción de Gracias en Estados Unidos. Así las cosas, la temporada 3 de Los Anillos de Poder llegará a su final a la espera de saber si Amazon Prime Video la renueva o no para una cuarta entrega.

articles.title: Ozempic: estudo encontra possível benefício para a fertilidade masculina
articles.text:
Medicamentos conhecidos pelo tratamento do diabetes tipo 2 e pela perda de peso, como o Ozempic, podem também estar associados a melhorias na fertilidade masculina. Um estudo publicado na revista científica Biomedicines identificou mudanças positivas na qualidade dos espermatozoides e nos níveis de testosterona de homens que utilizaram medicamentos da classe dos agonistas do receptor GLP-1.
A pesquisa acompanhou 108 homens com obesidade e/ou diabetes tipo 2 durante 12 meses. Os participantes utilizaram semaglutida, princípio ativo do Ozempic, ou liraglutida, comercializada sob a marca Victoza.
Ao final do acompanhamento, os pesquisadores observaram aumento significativo na concentração de espermatozoides, além de melhorias em indicadores relacionados à forma e à capacidade de movimentação das células reprodutivas.
Os níveis médios de testosterona também aumentaram aproximadamente 30% durante o período. Apesar dos resultados promissores, os cientistas ressaltam que ainda não é possível afirmar que os medicamentos melhoram diretamente as chances de um homem conseguir ter filhos.
Estudo identifica mudanças na qualidade do sêmen
- Um dos resultados observados pelos pesquisadores envolve a morfologia dos espermatozoides, característica relacionada à forma e à estrutura dessas células;
- Antes do tratamento, pouco mais de 3% dos espermatozoides analisados apresentavam formato considerado normal. Depois de um ano, essa proporção chegou a aproximadamente 4,5%;
- Outro indicador foi a motilidade progressiva, que representa a capacidade de os espermatozoides se movimentarem para a frente. Nesse caso, o percentual aumentou de 23% para 38%;
- Essas características são importantes para avaliar a qualidade e a funcionalidade do sêmen. Entretanto, os pesquisadores destacam que espermatozoides não precisam apresentar formato perfeitamente normal para conseguir fertilizar um óvulo.
Leia mais:
- “Mísseis teleguiados” trazem esperança contra o câncer de próstata avançado
- Como um rim de porco mudou a rotina de uma americana de 56 anos
- Brasil prevê iniciar testes de vacina terapêutica contra o câncer em 2027
Testosterona aumentou aproximadamente 30%
Outro resultado chamou a atenção da equipe: os níveis médios de testosterona aumentaram cerca de 30% após o início do tratamento. Ao mesmo tempo, os pesquisadores observaram redução nos níveis de estradiol, hormônio relacionado ao estrogênio.
Uma possível explicação está na perda de peso dos participantes. Pesquisas anteriores apontam que a gordura visceral, acumulada na região abdominal e ao redor dos órgãos, pode ter influência importante na redução da testosterona.
No entanto, os resultados não permitem estabelecer relação direta entre emagrecimento e melhora da concentração de espermatozoides. Mesmo depois de considerar fatores, como idade e presença de diabetes, as mudanças no índice de massa corporal (IMC) não acompanharam necessariamente as alterações na concentração espermática.
Os pesquisadores também consideram a possibilidade de os medicamentos atuarem diretamente nos testículos, órgãos responsáveis pela produção de espermatozoides e testosterona.
Estudos identificaram receptores funcionais de GLP-1 em espermatozoides humanos. Além disso, experimentos com camundongos obesos sugerem que medicamentos dessa classe podem proteger os testículos contra danos.
Uma hipótese é que os tratamentos influenciem processos, como inflamação e estresse oxidativo nos testículos, contribuindo para ambiente mais favorável à produção de células reprodutivas.
Resultados ainda não comprovam aumento da fertilidade
Apesar dos indicadores positivos, o estudo apresenta limitações importantes. Uma delas é a ausência de um grupo de controle, o que dificulta determinar se as mudanças observadas foram provocadas diretamente pelos medicamentos.
Os pesquisadores também não tinham informações sobre o histórico de fertilidade dos participantes. Por isso, não é possível concluir se o tratamento realmente aumentou as chances de concepção.
A pesquisa não é a primeira a investigar essa possível relação. Em 2025, um pequeno ensaio clínico realizado na Eslovênia acompanhou 13 homens com obesidade, diabetes tipo 2 e níveis baixos de testosterona que utilizaram semaglutida.
Nesse grupo, a proporção de espermatozoides com formato considerado normal dobrou, enquanto os níveis de testosterona aumentaram. Entretanto, o experimento também não contou com grupo de controle que recebesse placebo.
Os próprios pesquisadores ressaltam que ainda faltam evidências clínicas suficientes para recomendar medicamentos da classe GLP-1 especificamente como tratamento de primeira linha para problemas de fertilidade masculina.
Ensaios clínicos maiores, controlados e com acompanhamento adequado serão necessários para confirmar os resultados e entender os mecanismos envolvidos.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Uber and Nuro begin driverless testing of Lucid robotaxis ahead of 2027 launch
articles.text:
Uber and Nuro have started testing driverless Lucid Gravity SUVs on public streets in the San Francisco Bay Area more than six months after receiving the permit that allowed the companies to pull the human safety driver from behind the wheel.
The companies will soon begin offering driverless rides to employees in the final lead-up to launching a commercial robotaxi service in the first quarter of 2027.
The milestone comes just 16 months after Uber announced an ambitious plan to launch a premium robotaxi service using Lucid electric vehicles outfitted with autonomous vehicle technology developed by startup Nuro.
That plan came with hefty investments in both companies and much-needed endorsements of their respective products. Uber initially agreed to invest $300 million in Lucid — a figure that has since ballooned to $500 million. Uber also agreed to invest nearly $500 million in Nuro, TechCrunch previously reported, citing sources familiar with the deal.
The agreement provided both Lucid and Nuro with boosts beyond the obvious capital injection. Uber agreed to buy at least 20,000 of Lucid Gravity SUVs over the next six years, giving the struggling EV maker a more predictable source of revenue. Nuro, meanwhile, was less than a year removed from announcing a risky, but necessary pivot away from developing driverless delivery vehicles and toward licensing its autonomous vehicle technology to automakers and mobility companies.
Nuro has spent nearly a year testing the Lucid Gravity robotaxi on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area with a human safety operator behind the wheel. The California Department of Motor Vehicles, the agency that regulates the testing and deployment of autonomous vehicles in the state, granted Nuro a driverless AV permit in May 2026.
Uber and Nuro are also testing autonomous vehicles on public roads in Houston with human safety operators behind the wheel. Nuro is supplementing that on-road testing with closed-course testing and simulation to validate the self-driving system before opening the robotaxis to the public. The companies’ combined engineering fleet of autonomous vehicles, which stood at 100 AVs earlier this year, is expanding as Lucid begins manufacturing the first production versions of the robotaxis at its Arizona factory.
The Lucid Gravity robotaxi, unveiled in January 2026, is outfitted with high-resolution cameras, solid-state lidar sensors, and radars that help the self-driving system perceive the real-world environment and operate in it. Uber, which will own and operate the fleet, has focused its efforts on the in-cabin experience, including how riders will interact with the vehicle.

articles.title: We Get the Infrastructure We Pay For
articles.text:
We Get the Infrastructure We Pay For
This essay originally appeared as part of a round table in The Free Press entitled “Is America’s Infrastructure Under Attack?”
Microsoft, the FAA, banks, United Airlines, the NSA—it’s been a really bad week in cyberspace. But, amazing as it might seem, these are not related. As far as we know, they’re not the result of cyberattacks. They’re not even related to AI. (Well, that’s mostly true. The NSA will probably never tell us what went wrong.) It’s really just a series of unfortunate coincidences.
Our computerized infrastructure is vulnerable and fragile. Much of it is old, and has been incrementally patched and upgraded. A surprising amount of it is maintained by hobbyists, without any recompense. And more and more of it is centralized: the same systems affecting many different aspects of our lives and society. In many cases, it just barely works. And when it fails, it tends to fail badly.
There are a lot of technological reasons why this is true, but they are all downstream of the economic ones. The technologies we rely on are built and maintained within our economic system—and that’s where the core problem lies.
Security, safety, resilience, redundancy, recoverability—these are all essential parts of reliable technology, but they are all costs.
More importantly, they are inefficient: costs that feel wasteful until something bad happens. Modern shareholder capitalism, and private equity in particular, squeeze all inefficiencies out of a company in pursuit of near-term profits. Competition, with multiple companies competing to do the same thing, is another inefficiency. Monopolization removes that in pursuit of near-term profits.
The result is brittle systems, single points of failure. They’re more susceptible to cyberattack—both human and AI-fueled—and more susceptible to random mistakes. The more we allow unregulated capitalism to privatize gains while socializing risks, the more we should expect these sorts of failures.
Fixing this is technical, but it’s political first. It requires changing incentives, and that involves regulation and control. “What to do” is easy; finding the political will to stand up to moneyed interests and do it is hard.
Untitled • November 24, 2026 7:49 AM
Your opening sentence cited Microsoft, the FAA, banks, United Airlines, the NSA. Two of those five (FAA and NSA) are government-funded, not unregulated capitalism.
Politicians have different incentives than private corporations, but the outcome is much the same: maintenance is neglected in favour of eye-catching, glossy new initiatives.

articles.title: Bientôt des BYD « made in France » ? Le géant chinois veut racheter l'usine des 4x4 Ineos
articles.text:
BYD cherche depuis l’été une usine déjà construite en Europe, et la France et l’Espagne étaient restées seules en lice pour l’accueillir. Ce mardi 24 novembre, le constructeur chinois a confirmé être entré en négociations exclusives avec Ineos Automotive pour racheter son usine de Hambach, en Moselle, où le groupe britannique assemble ses 4×4 Grenadier. Le choix étonne, car la direction de Smart avait expliqué à Numerama que le site imposait trop de contraintes pour que la marque puisse un jour y revenir.
Rien n’est signé pour l’instant. Le communiqué de BYD précise que l’opération doit d’abord passer devant les instances représentatives du personnel, qui donnent leur avis avant toute vente. La piste circulait depuis début novembre, quand Le Républicain Lorrain plaçait le site d’Ineos au cœur des spéculations.
Côté vendeur, Ineos a annoncé le même jour avoir présélectionné plusieurs sites aux États-Unis pour y produire ses 4×4 à partir de 2028. Les États-Unis pèsent 70 % des ventes mondiales du Grenadier. En attendant, même si la vente aboutit, le Grenadier et le pick-up Quartermaster resteront assemblés à Hambach « à moyen terme ».
Une usine déjà debout et sous-utilisée
BYD a déjà vu un projet d’usine neuve s’enliser. En Turquie, l’usine de Manisa, dont le contrat a été signé en juillet 2024 et qui devait ouvrir fin 2026, est en pause depuis juin : la construction n’a jamais commencé et BYD ne donne plus de calendrier. Racheter une usine existante permet donc d’être opérationnel plus rapidement.
Si la vente aboutit, BYD serait le premier constructeur chinois à racheter une usine automobile en Europe, selon l’agence Reuters. Ses concurrents chinois ont jusqu’ici préféré louer de la place dans des usines existantes. Tous anticipent les règles « Made in Europe » prévues par l’Union européenne, qui doivent imposer une part de contenu local aux voitures électriques pour qu’elles ouvrent droit aux aides et aux marchés publics.
Le site de Hambach tourne loin de ses capacités. Du temps de Smart, l’usine sortait environ 100 000 voitures par an au milieu des années 2000. Ineos y assemble aujourd’hui moins de 10 000 véhicules par an alors que l’usine est capable d’en produire 35 000.
Ni prix, ni date, ni modèle pour Hambach
La marque continuera de cohabiter avec les 4×4 d’Ineos jusqu’au démarrage de leur production américaine. BYD n’a donné ni montant, ni date de signature, ni nom de modèles assemblés pour son potentiel site mosellan. En Hongrie, l’usine de Szeged devait, elle, commencer à produire des voitures électriques au quatrième trimestre 2026, selon le calendrier donné en juin par Stella Li.

articles.title: Intel Arc G3 Play : la puce graphique la moins chère pour consoles portables fuite avant l’annonce
articles.text:
Intel travaillerait bien au lancement d’une nouvelle puce mobile « Arc G3 Play » consacrée aux consoles de jeu portables. Positionnée sur l’entrée de gamme, cette dernière reprendrait en partie la fiche technique d’un processeur mobile bien connu de la lignée Panther Lake.
Ça se confirme, Intel chercherait effectivement à lancer une nouvelle puce abordable pour étoffer sa famille de SoC « Arc G3 », vouée aux consoles de jeu portables. Après les puces Arc G3 et Arc G3 Extreme, que nous avons déjà croisées sur de nombreuses machines, malheureusement très coûteuses (on pense par exemple à la MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ et ses 1700 euros), le géant américain s’apprêterait donc à lancer une troisième référence.
BenQ iScreenBar : la barre lumineuse qui s’accorde avec l’iMac
Des lignes en harmonie avec celles de l’ordinateur d’Apple, une conception rigoureuse, des matériaux sélectionnés, rien n’a été laissé au hasard, tout comme le service qu’elle rend une fois allumée !
Vers des consoles plus modernes sous les 1000 euros ?
Baptisée « Arc G3 Play », du moins si l’on en croit les dernières informations partagées par le site spécialisé VideoCardz, ce weekend, cette nouvelle puce viendrait compléter l’offre d’Intel par le bas, pour s’installer sur des machines vendues entre 800 et 1000 euros - en les modernisant au passage.
Face à des consoles d’entrée de gamme souvent équipées de puces AMD Ryzen Z2 ou Z2A, désormais datées sur le plan technique (architecture CPU Zen 3+ ou Zen 2 et architecture graphique RDNA 2), Intel déclinerait là encore sa dernière architecture « Panther Lake », introduite en janvier 2026 avec les Core Ultra de série 3.
Des spécifications qui se précisent peu à peu
Comme l’avaient suggéré de précédentes rumeurs, l’Arc G3 Play miserait d’ailleurs sur une configuration proche de celle du Core Ultra 5 325, que l’on trouve sur de nombreux PC portables milieu de gamme. Parmi eux, l'Honor MagicBook 16 2026, que nous testions il y a quelques mois.
Cette nouvelle puce combinerait elle aussi un CPU regroupant 8 cœurs et 8 threads, et une partie graphique comprenant pour sa part 4 cœurs Xe3 seulement. À titre de comparaison, les puces Arc G3 et Arc G3 Extreme intègrent des parties graphiques nettement plus grosses, de 10 et 12 cœurs Xe3, respectivement.
Comme le souligne TechPowerUp, la répartition exacte des différents cœurs CPU de l’Arc G3 Play est encore sujette à caution. Les premières informations dont nous disposions faisaient état d’une configuration « 4+0+4+4 » (pour 4 cœurs hautes performances, aucun cœur haute efficacité, 4 cœurs très basse consommation et 4 cœurs graphiques).
Depuis quelques semaines, une nouvelle fuite du leaker Jaykihn tend plutôt à appuyer la piste d’une répartition 0+8+0+4 (aucun cœur hautes performances, 8 cœurs haute efficacité, aucun cœur très basse consommation et 4 cœurs graphiques) un peu plus modeste sur le plan CPU.
On suppose par ailleurs que la puce profitera d’un TDP compris entre 8 et 25 W, sans plus de détails à ce stade. Espérons que nous pourrons en apprendre plus à son sujet dans les prochaines semaines.
Source : TechPowerUp / VideoCardz

articles.title: Pan de masa madre o pan integral: cuál es más saludable según una dietista
articles.text:
Cuando vas a la panadería y ves hogazas con etiquetas como “masa madre” o “100% integral”, puedes pensar que están compitiendo por ser un tipo de pan más saludable. Pero esas dos etiquetas no describen lo mismo, y conviene saber las diferencias: una habla de cómo se fermenta la masa y la otra de qué parte del cereal se ha utilizado para hacer la harina. Esto también quiere decir que puede haber panes que reunan las dos cosas.
La respuesta corta. Si buscando un pan saludable comparamos el blanco de masa madre y uno 100% integral, la balanza se inclina con bastante claridad hacia el segundo. La dietista Victoria Taylor, de la British Heart Foundation, lo explica en un artículo publicado en 2023: para el consumo habitual recomienda el pan integral antes que el de masa madre hecho con harina blanca, y esto tiene que ver con la mayor cantidad de fibra del grano entero, sin desacreditar la fermentación.
Por lo tanto, si quieres un pan que tenga las dos ventajas puedes buscar uno que sea 100% integral fermentado con masa madre, aunque también debes fijarte en que sus ingredientes y su contenido en sal sean adecuados. Eso no hace que el pan integral hecho con levadura comercial sea malo, o sea que tampoco necesitas pagar más por uno que tenga la “masa madre” si estás buscando uno nutritivo.
Dos etiquetas diferentes. La masa madre es un fermento de harina y agua en el que conviven levaduras y bacterias silvestres que hacen fermentar y subir la masa. Mientras, que un pan sea integral significa que la harina conserva el grano completo, con el salvado, el germen y el endospermo, mientras que la refinada se queda prácticamente con este último. Vamos, que lo que hace integral a un pan son sus harinas, y da igual que suba con masa madre o con levadura de panadero.
Y en España la cuestión no queda al gusto de cada obrador. La norma de calidad del pan reserva las denominaciones “pan integral” y “pan 100% integral” a los elaborados con harina exclusivamente integral, y si se mezcla con harina refinada hay que indicar “elaborado con harina integral X%”, con el porcentaje calculado sobre el total de harina utilizada. En un pan 100% integral, además, la masa madre también tiene que proceder de harina integral, así que un pan de masa madre puede ser tanto blanco como integral, del mismo modo que un integral puede fermentar con masa madre o con levadura.
Por qué el integral parte con ventaja. Al conservar el grano entero, el pan integral suele aportar más fibra, además de vitaminas del grupo B y minerales que se concentran en el salvado y el germen, que son justo las partes que se pierden al refinar la harina según la misma guía de Harvard. La cifra exacta cambia con el cereal y con la receta, pero la diferencia frente a la harina blanca tiene una base nutricional sólida.
Esa fibra ayuda al buen funcionamiento intestinal, según Harvard, y la Organización Mundial de la Salud recomienda que los hidratos de carbono procedan principalmente de cereales integrales, verduras, frutas y legumbres, con al menos 25 gramos diarios de fibra natural a partir de los diez años. Los grandes estudios observacionales, como el metaanálisis de Imperial College London publicado en ‘The BMJ’ en 2016, asocian además un mayor consumo de cereales integrales con menos riesgo cardiovascular y de mortalidad.
Pero esto no convierte al integral en un pan mucho más ligero, ya que su valor energético apenas se aleja del blanco, tal y como recoge la ficha del pan integral del Ministerio de Agricultura. Tampoco equivalente a uno de grano entero cualquier producto enriquecido con salvado, porque añadir fibra no devuelve todo lo que aporta el cereal completo.
Lo que la masa madre hace y lo que no. La fermentación con masa madre tiene efectos reales sobre el pan, porque modifica su acidez y puede reducir determinados compuestos de las harinas, aunque el resultado depende de las cepas microbianas, la harina, el tiempo y las condiciones del proceso. Lo que no hace es provocar siempre un pico de azúcar más bajo: una revisión sistemática publicada en agosto de 2026 en Frontiers in Nutrition que reunió 27 estudios concluye que las pruebas de un efecto beneficioso sobre la glucemia o la insulina frente al pan de levadura no son suficientes ni convincentes en personas sanas.
Algunos ensayos sí observaron una respuesta más favorable tras la comida, unas veces en el conjunto de la curva y otras sólo en momentos concretos, pero con mucha variación entre unos estudios y otros. Vamos, que no se puede garantizar un menor pico de glucosa porque la hogaza lleve masa madre. Con el hierro ocurre algo parecido, y la fermentación puede reducir parte del ácido fítico, una sustancia del cereal que dificulta la absorción de algunos minerales, pero otra revisión de 2026 centrada en ocho estudios de intervención en personas encontró resultados contradictorios: una mayor disponibilidad en las pruebas de absorción no se tradujo en mejores reservas a largo plazo.
La fermentación tradicional también puede disminuir algunos fructanos, unos hidratos fermentables que importan a ciertas personas con síndrome del intestino irritable, aunque según el equipo de la Universidad de Monash especializado en FODMAP un pan de masa madre de trigo o de centeno puede seguir siendo alto en FODMAP, porque depende de la harina y de la elaboración. Tampoco es un alimento probiótico, ya que, como recuerda la British Heart Foundation, el calor del horno acaba con las levaduras y bacterias del fermento.
Qué mirar antes de comprar. Al comprar el pan no te fijes solo en el color o aspecto de su corteza, porque es más importante revisar la denominación de venta. “Pan integral” y “100% integral” tienen un significado legal concreto en España, y si aparece “elaborado con harina integral X%”, ese porcentaje te dice cuánta hay realmente. Un pan no demuestra que sea integral solo por ser más oscuro, y unas semillas tampoco convierten en integral una masa de harina blanca. Con el nombre del cereal pasa igual, porque en un pan de espelta con masa madre toca comprobar si esa espelta es refinada o integral.
En los panes envasados conviene mirar además la sal por cada 100 gramos, porque el pan es una de las principales fuentes de sal de la dieta, y también de fibra cuando aparezca. Y “elaborado con masa madre” tampoco significa “100% integral”: la norma regula esa mención con condiciones de composición y fermentación, pero no obliga a utilizar harina de grano entero.
Las personas celíacas deben tener cuidado. La masa madre hecha con cereales que contienen gluten, como el trigo o el centeno, no hacen que el pan sea apto para celíacos, porque la fermentación no elimina el gluten. La organización estadounidense Beyond Celiac desaconseja el pan de masa madre a quienes tienen celiaquía, salvo que esté etiquetado como sin gluten o se haya hecho con fermento e ingredientes sin gluten.
Al final, un buen pan no tiene por qué convertirse en un alimento milagroso. Si hay que escoger entre un blanco de masa madre y uno 100% integral, el integral suele ser la mejor elección nutricional para el día a día, y si además está bien fermentado con masa madre puede sumar otras cualidades interesantes, aunque lo que de verdad pesa, según la dietista de la British Heart Foundation y la evidencia disponible, son unos buenos ingredientes, suficiente fibra y una cantidad razonable de sal.
Foto | Wesual Click

articles.title: Boulanger divise par deux le prix de la Samsung HW-Q995H pendant le Black Friday
articles.text:
Depuis quelques jours, L’Odyssée de Christopher Nolan est disponible en vidéo à la demande. Parmi les qualités de ce film, il y a le travail apporté à la partie sonore. Pour pouvoir pleinement en profiter chez vous, il vaut mieux passer par une barre de son. Justement, le Black Friday rythme le mois de novembre et la Samsung HW-Q995H est vendue presque à moitié prix chez Boulanger, code promo compris.
Les atouts de la Samsung HW-Q995H :
- L’ensemble de 23 haut-parleurs compatible avec le Dolby Atmos
- La restitution sonore qui s’adapte à votre intérieur
- La Q-Symphony pour les TV Samsung
C’est le moment de foncer sur la Samsung HW-Q995H puisqu’elle est actuellement disponible à 785 euros au lieu de 1 499 euros chez Boulanger grâce au code BLACK15.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant la Samsung HW-Q995H. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Une barre de son qui se plie à votre salon
La Samsung HW-Q995H a la sobriété comme mot d’ordre. Si cet ensemble audio se compose de quatre éléments, dont un caisson de basse, ils sont tous intégralement noirs et n’auront aucun mal à se fondre dans votre salon.
En ce qui concerne la configuration, vous n’aurez rien à faire si ce n’est installer l’application SmartThings. La HW-Q995H se calibre ensuite toute seule grâce à la fonction SpaceFit Sound Pro. Petite subtilité : Samsung réserve cette calibration à ses propres téléviseurs (gamme Q7 et plus de 2021 à 2024, Q8FA et plus en 2025 et 2026, ainsi que les The Frame). Elle analyse la configuration de votre intérieur pour adapter la restitution sonore selon la disposition de vos meubles.
Lorsque vous regardez un film, la barre de son analyse automatiquement les sons ambiants dans la pièce grâce à la technologie Active Voice Amplifier Pro. Ainsi, si elle détecte un bruit parasite comme un aspirateur, elle va ajuster le niveau des voix sans que vous ayez à modifier le volume. La fonction Adaptive Sound reconnaît aussi le type de contenu (film, sport, musique) et ajuste le son pour garder des voix claires, y compris dans les scènes d’action.
23 haut-parleurs et plus si affinités
Samsung n’a pas communiqué officiellement la puissance sonore de sa HW-Q995H. L’ensemble compte 23 haut-parleurs, répartis en 11.1.4 canaux : 11 canaux avant et surround, un caisson de basse et quatre canaux verticaux pour le Dolby Atmos. La barre se place sous la TV et les deux enceintes arrière derrière le canapé, ce qui enveloppe le spectateur à 360 degrés. Seul bémol, le caisson et les enceintes arrière n’ont pas de câble audio, mais il leur faut quand même chacun une prise électrique.
L’expérience sera encore meilleure si vous disposez d’un téléviseur Samsung. Grâce au Q-Symphony (compatible avec les TV Samsung récentes, à partir des gammes 2021), vous pourrez synchroniser les haut-parleurs de la barre de son avec ceux de votre TV pour élargir davantage votre scène sonore.
Pour rester sur la connectivité, la barre propose deux entrées HDMI, qui laissent passer la 4K à 120 Hz d’une console, et une sortie HDMI eARC vers la TV, ainsi qu’une entrée optique. La Samsung HW-Q995H ne se limite pas aux TV puisque vous pouvez connecter votre smartphone en Bluetooth et diffuser votre playlist sur la barre de son. L’appareil est aussi compatible AirPlay 2 et Chromecast, et gère Spotify Connect et Tidal Connect.
On a testé une multitude de barres de son cette année, et les meilleures sont réunies dans notre guide d’achat des barres de son.
Black Friday 2026 : pour ne rien rater des meilleures offres Tech

articles.title: La fusée Ariane 6 livre enfin les 36 satellites d’Amazon : voici les plus belles images du décollage
articles.text:
Amazon avait besoin d’un lancement sans accroc. Le 15 novembre 2026, sa constellation internet Amazon Leo a perdu 40 satellites dans l’échec de la fusée américaine Vulcan, en Floride. Ariane 6 devait emporter 36 nouveaux satellites dès le lundi 23 novembre, mais un problème technique sur les installations au sol a interrompu le compte à rebours.
La fusée européenne est finalement partie de Kourou ce mardi 24 novembre à 8h14, heure locale (12h14 à Paris), et l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) a diffusé les images du décollage sur X.
Les images du décollages de la fusée Ariane 6, pour son 10e tir
Il s’en est fallu de peu : la chronologie a encore été arrêtée quelques minutes avant le tir par une alerte rouge sur l’ensemble de lancement. Ariane 6 a ensuite pu décoller, à la toute fin de sa fenêtre de tir prévue.
4 propulseurs plus puissants, visibles sur la vidéo d’Arianespace
Arianespace a publié ses propres images du tir dans la foulée, puis remis en ligne la vidéo du décollage en mettant en avant ses quatre propulseurs à poudre P160C, utilisés pour la deuxième fois seulement. Vus de l’extérieur, ils ont la même taille que les P120C des premiers vols. Pourtant, leur moteur mesure un mètre de plus et contient 156 tonnes de propergol solide, le carburant qui pousse la fusée.
D’après le communiqué d’Arianespace, ils apportent un gain de 10 % en orbite basse, ce qui porte la capacité de la version la plus puissante d’Ariane 6 à environ 22 tonnes. Les 36 satellites ont été largués vers 460 kilomètres d’altitude, 2 heures et 4 minutes après le décollage.
Arianespace revendique 10 succès en 10 vols, un bilan flatteur : le vol inaugural de juillet 2024 s’était terminé sur une anomalie de l’étage supérieur.
Pendant cette campagne, un représentant de l’ESA a renvoyé la question d’une Ariane 6 capable d’envoyer des astronautes européens d’ici à 2036 à la prochaine réunion ministérielle de l’agence. Côté Amazon, 136 satellites sont désormais en orbite grâce à Ariane 6, sur 24 lancements commandés au total depuis le plus gros contrat de l’histoire d’Arianespace, signé en 2022.

articles.title: BlackBerry revient avec un navigateur sécurisé pour les entreprises
articles.text:
BlackBerry vient de sortir Access Secure Browser, un navigateur pour Windows basé sur Chromium misant sur la sécurité en entreprise.
Basé sur Chromium, le navigateur remplace l’ancien client de bureau BlackBerry Access et rejoint les versions iOS et Android. Il vise les prestataires, les partenaires et les salariés qui utilisent leur propre PC.
Un espace de travail chiffré, sans agent sur le PC
Le BYOD (“bring your own device”) consiste à travailler sur son propre appareil. Sur smartphone, le compromis est relativement facile puisque l’employeur isole les applications pro et l’intrusion reste limitée. Sur un PC que la famille utilise aussi, les utilisateurs refusent en général un agent de gestion permettant potentiellement à l’employeur de piloter la machine. Les organisations hésitent aussi, par crainte de leur responsabilité. BlackBerry change donc d’approche. Le navigateur tourne dans un conteneur chiffré, séparé du reste de Windows. Selon l’éditeur, rien d’autre n’est touché. Pas d’agent, pas d’accès aux photos ni aux fichiers personnels, pas d’effacement à distance du PC.
Pour que ce soit pratique, Outlook, Teams et OneDrive fonctionnent en PWA, et disposent donc de leurs propres fenêtres. Teams peut même envoyer des notifications Windows. Les fichiers téléchargés restent dans un stockage protégé du navigateur, et ne viennent pas se mélanger avec les dossiers personnels de l’utilisateur. Un module LibreOffice permet d'effectuer des modifications hors connexion, dans un train ou dans un hôtel au Wi-Fi capricieux. Pour joindre les applications internes, le navigateur passe par l’infrastructure de BlackBerry, sans client VPN. Le VPN reste toutefois possible en parallèle. Certains clients gardent cette voie en secours, quand leur VPN est saturé ou en panne pendant un incident.
BlackBerry cible aussi les administrations, les régulateurs et les opérateurs d’infrastructures critiques. Leur question est simple. Qui fixe les règles du navigateur ? Depuis où ? Sous quelle juridiction ? Selon l’éditeur, la plupart des navigateurs sécurisés reposent sur une console cloud gérée par leur fournisseur. Ici, quand BlackBerry UEM est installé sur site, les règles, la gestion et les identités restent chez l’organisation. Le système peut même tourner sur un réseau isolé d’Internet. Le RGPD entre aussi en jeu. Pour le Comité européen de la protection des données, un accès à distance depuis l’extérieur de l’Union compte comme un transfert de données. Même quand les données restent en Europe. BlackBerry en déduit qu’un navigateur piloté depuis un cloud hors UE peut être concerné, mais pas une console hébergée par l’organisation.
Mozilla a pris une direction similaire. Nous apprenions le mois dernier que Firefox Enterprise arrivait avec une console que les organisations installent elles-mêmes, en commençant par la France, l’Allemagne, l’Autriche et la Suisse.

articles.title: Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants
articles.text:
Data centers are getting their own natural gas power plants
The numbers behind the off-grid gas power boom.
One of the biggest roadblocks to starting up a data center is getting approval to connect to the electric grid—a wait that could last as long as a decade. Some developers aren’t willing to wait and are instead opting to build their own off-grid, or behind-the-meter, gas power plants to fuel the AI boom.
xAI’s Memphis campus has famously used dozens of natural gas turbines, some of them without permits, as far back as 2024. At the time, that facility was a rarity, and it faced scrutiny from regulators. It remains the subject of ongoing legal battles. But the strategy of going off-grid for power has since become a lot more common.
As of October 2026, data center developers have announced plans for more than 100 behind-the-meter gas power plants at facilities in the US, according to data from Cleanview, a market intelligence company. The facilities have a combined planned capacity of over 115 gigawatts, more than double the peak power demand of California. The vast majority of these announcements have come since the beginning of 2025.
It’s possible that not all these facilities will be built; only a small fraction are under construction or operating today. But there’s a growing trend of large data centers looking to build their own power supply, and this could shape the grid—and its climate impacts—for decades to come.
Building your own power plant is generally more expensive than just hooking up to the grid, but the AI rush has made developers willing to pay a significant premium to get online faster. “The biggest motivator for on-site power right now from data centers is speed,” says Musfika Mishi, an associate at BloombergNEF, an energy consultancy.
When developers want to build a new industrial facility—like a data center—that requires a lot of electricity, they need to request a grid connection from a local utility or regional grid operator. That request kicks off a yearslong process in which grid planners study the existing grid to understand what would need to be built to safely deliver power to the facility without compromising reliability. Upgrades might be required, like building new transmission lines or larger transformers, and the developer might be on the hook to help pay for them.
Rather than waiting for that process to play out, developers can opt to instead build their own power plants. These facilities are referred to as “behind the meter” because they sit on the customer’s side of a utility meter—supplying the building directly, rather than relying on a utility via a grid hookup.
“This shift in the data center developers’ power strategies towards off-grid gas raises some important questions about how data centers will be powered going forward,” says Brendan Pierpont, director of electricity at the think tank Energy Innovation.
Behind-the-meter doesn’t always mean being totally disconnected from the grid, however. Some facilities may build such plants as a temporary measure, eventually connecting to the grid and tapping their own power plants only as backup. “It’s really just a very expensive way to bridge that maybe five-to-seven-year timeline gap until these data centers can get a grid connection,” Pierpont says.
Even if gas plants are pitched as a near-term solution, building new fossil fuel infrastructure could lead to longer-term effects, since an operator might choose to continue running plants once they’ve spent money building them. “Even though data centers say that it’s a grid-bridging solution, the probability that it is going to be in use much longer is a real risk, and that leads to fossil fuel lock-in,” Mishi says.
The on-site gas rush could have major implications for greenhouse-gas emissions. Today, the US grid is still reliant on fossil fuels, but nuclear and renewables together make up about 40% of electricity generation. That means making a grid connection is generally a lower-emissions option than relying entirely on an on-site gas plant. (That’s not the case everywhere—India, for example, is expecting to see a data center boom in the next decade, and its grid is largely served by emissions-intensive coal-fired power plants today.)
Utilities are already planning to build more natural gas power plants on the grid to meet rising electricity demand. Equipment manufacturers are struggling to keep up with the surge, and it’s pushing developers of behind-the-meter plants toward less-efficient alternatives.
Today, large natural gas plants generally use combined-cycle turbines. These capture heat to generate additional electricity, making them more efficient than single-cycle turbines, which are generally cheaper to build. Very few of the planned behind-the-meter facilities, however, will use combined-cycle turbines, Mishi says. That means these off-grid plants will likely produce more greenhouse-gas emissions than even other natural gas resources.
BloombergNEF is also tracking on-site natural gas plants at data centers, finding 181 gigawatts’ worth of announced projects globally, with 90% of that capacity designated for the US. If all planned behind-the-meter gas plants for data centers in the US go ahead, they could emit 345 million metric tons of carbon dioxide equivalent each year by 2035, according to a BloombergNEF report. That’s 152 million metric tons more than if those data centers pulled power from the US grid—a difference greater than the total annual emissions of the Netherlands.
And while it might seem logical that data centers bringing their own power could ease communities’ energy bills, those facilities going off-grid doesn’t protect prices for everyone else, says Matthias Fripp, director of global policy research at Energy Innovation. More demand for natural gas could push its price higher, he explains, which could in turn raise rates for the roughly 60% of American households that use natural gas for heating and cooking. That effect may also trickle into electricity prices.
There’s still a lot of uncertainty about how much of this gas rush will come to fruition, so this future isn’t set in stone. Today, just 4.9 gigawatts of behind-the-meter gas projects tied to data centers are operating, and 15.8 gigawatts are under construction, according to Cleanview’s data.
Creative solutions could also help limit the climate burden of the on-site gas buildout, BloombergNEF’s Mishi says. Building gas alongside on-site renewables or energy storage could help limit how often a gas plant needs to fire up, she says, though the economics of building multiple energy sources can be tricky.
While the grid is struggling to keep up with demand, building more renewables could help, Fripp adds. In a recent study, his team found that building renewables and energy storage to meet rising electricity demand could be reliable and cheaper than relying on fossil fuels.
“These data centers want a lot of power, and they want it fast, and the grid is not well equipped to provide that,” Fripp says. “There are potentially good solutions and bad solutions … Rushing off the grid and putting in your own behind-the-meter gas is probably a bad way, because it’s still going to raise other people’s bills, and it’s not great for the environment.”

articles.title: Ingrid (58) compra una autocaravana por 12.500 euros, que inmediatamente necesita una reparación de 3.000 euros
articles.text:
Ingrid (58 años) y su marido llevaban tiempo con ganas de comprarse una caravana. Cuando encontraron una de segunda mano por 12.500 euros decidieron dar el paso, pero antes de pagar quisieron asegurarse de que todo estaba en orden. Y sí, sobre el papel lo estaba, ya que el vendedor les dijo que no había filtraciones de agua, pero su primera escapa terminó costándoles… 3.000 euros.
La pareja se marchó a Zelanda (una provincia de Países Bajos) para estrenarla y durante el viaje se toparon con una tormenta que empezó a filtrar el agua por las paredes. Los cojines de la zona de estar acabaron empapados, el interior sufrió daños por la humedad y la situación llevó a Ingrid a contar la historia a Metronieuws, un portal en el que habló de cómo una caravana que parecía perfecta se convirtió en un problema serio.
Una reparación de 3.000 euros que no esperaban
Tras descubrir las filtraciones, el matrimonio tuvo que afrontar una reparación de 3.000 euros, que se sumaron a los 12.500 que ya habían pagado. En total, la caravana les salió por 15.500 euros. Y todo después de que el anterior propietario les hubiera asegurado que no tenía problemas de humedad.
Lo complicado de estos desperfectos es que no siempre se ven durante una visita. Por eso, el ADAC, el club automovilístico alemán, recomienda comprobar si una caravana de segunda mano ha sufrido filtraciones y realizar una medición de humedad antes de comprarla. El agua puede terminar dañando la madera, las instalaciones eléctricas o incluso provocar la aparición de moho.
Y hay otro detalle que conviene tener en cuenta: no es lo mismo comprar a un particular que a un concesionario. En Alemania, los vendedores particulares pueden excluir ciertas responsabilidades por defectos, aunque no cuando han ocultado deliberadamente un problema conocido o han garantizado expresamente que no existía. Por eso merece la pena dejar por escrito cualquier garantía sobre el estado de la caravana, especialmente si se refiere a posibles daños por agua.

articles.title: Google Maps cache un mode « Haute visibilité » : voici à quoi il ressemble
articles.text:
Repéré dans la version 26.48.00.1027729593 de Google Maps pour Android, ce mode « Haute visibilité » que l’on retrouve dans les paramètres de l’application n’a pas encore été officialisé par le géant de Mountain View. Actuellement, il est possible de basculer entre le thème clair et le thème sombre, mais Google testerait une option pour améliorer la visibilité pendant la conduite, sans pour autant modifier l’emplacement des boutons ni l’ergonomie générale.
Du violet et du gris pour un affichage plus lisible
En mode clair, cette nouvelle interface de Google Maps abandonne les teintes habituelles pour privilégier des nuances beaucoup plus sobres. Les zones de végétation, d’ordinaire d’un vert éclatant, adoptent un vert plus sombre et plus mat. De leur côté, les zones blanches et beiges de la carte cèdent leur place à différents dégradés de gris. Enfin, le traditionnel repère bleu de positionnement devient violet.
Les changements sont encore plus marqués sur le mode sombre. Au lieu de l’arrière-plan bleuâtre classique, la carte affiche des teintes très foncées, proches du noir. Le tracé du trajet à suivre n’est plus une ligne bleue, mais une ligne violette bordée d’une couleur lavande claire. L’objectif est évidemment d’offrir un contraste important avec le reste du décor.
Le reste de l’interface et la disponibilité du mode « Haute visibilité »
Imaginé pour offrir un meilleur contraste pendant la navigation, ce style graphique garde intactes toutes les commandes d’itinéraire. Les noms de rues, les panneaux de direction et les indicateurs de changement de direction restent parfaitement identifiables. Ces couleurs ne sont pas sans rappeler des teintes similaires aperçues sur Android Auto en septembre dernier.
Découvrez : Comment transformer gratuitement un smartphone ou une tablette Android en écran CarPlay ou Android Auto ?
Les images que vous voyez ci-dessus viennent de l’analyse d’un fichier APK à partir duquel l’option a pu être activée. Cela ne garantit pas pour autant que Google déploiera la fonctionnalité dans un futur proche, même si l’on peut l’espérer. En attendant, n’hésitez pas à nous dire ce que vous pensez de ce nouvel affichage qui, avec son contraste plus important pourrait plaire à certains conducteurs.

articles.title: Apiary Therapeutics raises $7.3 million for engineered stem cell therapies
articles.text:
A biotechnology startup seeking to make more effective stem cell-derived therapies has announced its first round of venture funding.
The news: Apiary Therapeutics, co-founded by two Canadian entrepreneurial academics, announced on Monday that it had secured $7.3 million CAD to advance its stem-cell therapy technology toward pre-clinical trials. The seed round was co-led by Genesys Capital and BDC Capital’s Life Sciences Venture Fund, with participation from InBC and Mission BioCapital.
From the source: “A medicine that the body makes for itself, at the right level, in a durable manner, from one dose would change what treatment looks like for people who today depend on frequent infusions,” Apiary co-founder Yale Michaels, an assistant professor at the University of Manitoba, said in a statement.
The context: Apiary was co-founded by Michaels and University of British Columbia biomedical engineering professor Peter Zandstra, who has previously founded three biotech startups. Its technology turns stem cells, instead of a patient’s blood, into B cells (white blood cells that make antibodies) that can create proteins that fend off diseases, which could have applications across protein deficiencies, autoimmune diseases, and fighting cancers.
The startup is looking to validate its technique in preclinical trials, meaning in model animals like mice, before testing in humans. Apiary also hopes to expand its teams in Vancouver and Toronto.
Final thought: The funding announcement is the second from BDC Capital’s Life Sciences Venture Fund, a new direct investment vehicle that the Crown corporation announced after admitting it had pulled back too early from life sciences investing. The wider industry is seeing a funding crunch, as the medtech industry is on track to see its lowest financing activity in a decade.
Feature image courtesy Unsplash. Photo by Trnava University.

articles.title: Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
articles.text:
Quantum computers are getting too powerful to check. Scientists have a solution
- Date:
  November 16, 2026
- Source:
  University of Innsbruck
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed a new way to determine whether quantum simulations can be trusted, solving a growing problem as quantum computers become too powerful for conventional machines to check. Demonstrated on a 51-qubit system, the technique measures uncertainty and provides verifiable error margins that could help unlock the full potential of quantum computing.
- Share:
As quantum computers grow more powerful, researchers face a troubling question: How can they know whether the results are correct when conventional computers can no longer verify them? Scientists have now developed a promising new method that could help overcome this challenge by measuring the accuracy of quantum simulations and identifying how much uncertainty their predictions contain.
The technique uses experimental measurements to reconstruct how a quantum system behaves, then calculates how uncertainties in that reconstruction affect the results. Researchers successfully demonstrated the approach using a quantum simulator with up to 51 qubits in Innsbruck, Austria.
Quantum systems are expected to become capable of solving increasingly complex problems that traditional computers struggle with or cannot handle at all. However, this progress creates a verification problem. When a simulation is small enough, scientists can compare its results with calculations performed on a conventional computer. As quantum systems grow beyond those limits, that direct comparison becomes impractical, making alternative ways to assess their reliability essential.
A New Way to Measure Quantum Computing Accuracy
The breakthrough comes from an international research team led by Tristan Kraft at the Technical University of Munich and Peter Zoller at the University of Innsbruck and the Institute for Quantum Optics and Quantum Information of the Austrian Academy of Sciences, working alongside Barbara Kraus of the Technical University of Munich. The researchers developed a method for experimentally determining how a quantum simulator operates and translating uncertainties in its behavior into measurable limits on the accuracy of its results.
Quantum simulators are specialized physical systems designed to reproduce the behavior of other quantum systems. They are especially useful for investigating situations involving large numbers of interacting particles, where the calculations required can quickly overwhelm even powerful conventional computers.
But quantum experiments are never entirely free from errors. "But no real experiment is perfect," says Tristan Kraft. "Interactions may turn out differently than expected, the system is influenced by its environment, and measurements are also subject to uncertainties."
Rather than assuming a quantum simulator behaves exactly as intended, the new approach examines experimental data to determine what is actually happening inside the system. This allows researchers to identify important interactions and account for disturbances such as fluctuations and noise.
"From this data, we determine the relevant interactions as well as key influences from fluctuations and noise. We then calculate how the uncertainties in this model affect the simulation results," explains Tristan Kraft. "The quantum simulator thus provides not just a single value, but a result with error margins that quantify its accuracy."
Successfully Tested on a 51 Qubit Quantum Simulator
To evaluate the method, the researchers began with a relatively small quantum system containing ten trapped ions. Because conventional computers can still calculate the behavior of a system of this size, the team could test its reconstructed models and calculated error limits against independent measurements.
After this initial validation, the researchers expanded their experiments to a chain of 51 trapped ions. The larger demonstration, carried out by a team led by Manoj Joshi and Christian Roos using an ion trap quantum simulator, showed that the technique could also work with substantially more complex quantum systems.
This represents an important step toward establishing how trustworthy quantum simulation results are, particularly as quantum devices advance into territory where direct verification with traditional computing methods becomes increasingly difficult.
Extending the Breakthrough to More Complex Quantum Systems
The next challenge is to bring the technique to two-dimensional quantum simulators. These systems can model more complicated interactions among particles, making them valuable for exploring quantum physics. At the same time, their growing complexity makes their results particularly difficult to confirm using conventional calculations.
"This is particularly important because classical calculations for such systems become significantly more difficult as the number of particles increases," explains quantum computing pioneer Peter Zoller. "This also makes independent verification of the results increasingly complex, making the question of experimentally determined error limits all the more important."
The researchers are now adapting their method for the newest generation of two-dimensional quantum simulators, which offer improved precision and can investigate systems containing larger numbers of particles.
Looking further ahead, the approach could help scientists establish a more meaningful way to measure quantum advantage, the ability of quantum systems to outperform conventional computers. Instead of comparing machines based only on their processing speed or the size of the problems they can handle, researchers could also examine how accurately each system produces its answers.
"After all, when a classical computer and a quantum simulator tackle the same problem, it's not just a matter of which one delivers a result faster. What's also crucial is which one can solve the problem with a smaller, verifiable margin of error," says Peter Zoller.
This shift could change how progress in quantum computing is evaluated. Future breakthroughs may be judged not simply by how many particles a simulator can model or how quickly it performs calculations, but by its ability to solve increasingly difficult problems with demonstrably reliable results.
The findings were published in Physical Review X. The research received support from the Austrian Science Fund (FWF), the German Ministry of Research, Technology and Space, the European Union, BMW, and other funding organizations.

articles.title: TikTok was down
articles.text:
Earlier on Tuesday, TikTok experienced some issues, with videos, search results, favorites, and other features not loading as they usually do. Videos sometimes wouldn’t load in the For You feed on my iPhone, and search results occasionally didn’t show up as expected in the app on iOS or Android, or on the web. Even trying to pull up a profile would show a blank page, while links to videos are dead in the water too. However, as of 3:45PM ET or so, things appear to be working normally again.
TikTok was down
TikTok says a ‘brief technical issue’ impacted access to the platform.
Downdetector showed around 25,000 reports of issues at around 2:56PM ET, and many people on social media were saying that TikTok was down for them.
“We experienced a brief technical issue that impacted access to TikTok,” TikTok’s Jessica Casano-Antonellis tells The Verge. “The issue has been resolved. We apologize for the inconvenience and thank you for your patience.”
TikTok being down follows a slew of other outages over the past couple of weeks.
Update, November 24th: Added statement from TikTok.

articles.title: Designing A Microarchitecture From Formal Proof To Full-System
articles.text:
Combining architectural proof, software-driven verification, simulation, emulation, and cloud-based compute infrastructure.
Data center and high-performance computing workloads are pushing CPU designers to deliver higher per-watt throughput and support complex multicore systems. Meeting these goals requires specialized compute cores. This reality is forcing engineers to rethink not only how cores are built, but also which instruction set architecture (ISA) can scale efficiently, support software validation, and still create product differentiation. To meet these challenges, a lean R&D team from a startup company in Austin, Texas, chose the RISC-V ISA as the foundation for its first CPU IP microarchitecture.
Designing the microarchitecture involved balancing software-visible architectural behavior, RTL implementation details, and internal performance and power tradeoffs, which together introduced verification requirements that extended well beyond isolated hardware blocks. When these interactions are not addressed early in development, system-level issues can emerge later, making them more difficult to resolve. These decisions also expanded the scope of verification. The core had to be validated with actual software under full-system scale, including interactions that extend beyond individual hardware blocks.
To manage the complexity, the engineers adopted a formal-first verification strategy. By applying formal analysis during the design cycle, key architectural properties were proven before transitioning to large-scale simulation and system bring-up. Formal verification handled block-level functionality and end-to-end checks of functional intent. Simulation and emulation addressed long-running behavior in the full-core environment. Some failures may not emerge until the design has run for tens of millions of cycles under full operating system (OS) stress.
The design and verification group used a tightly integrated Cadence tool flow spanning architectural proof, software-driven verification, simulation, emulation, and cloud-based compute infrastructure. Figure 1 below illustrates a type of multicore CPU architecture that the Cadence verification methodology is designed to validate.
Fig. 1: A representative multicore CPU subsystem showing the processors, cache hierarchy, and system interfaces that engineers verify as the RTL design evolves. (Source: Cadence)
The Jasper Formal Verification Platform supported the implementation of a formal-first methodology to validate architectural intent early in the design. Formal Property Verification was applied across the fetch, decode, execution, and instruction-flow paths to ensure that key correctness properties were maintained throughout the pipeline. Jasper Superlint identified structural and coding issues early, preventing common RTL problems from propagating into later verification stages. Jasper XPROP addressed X-propagation risks associated with initialization and reset behavior, reducing simulation uncertainty and increasing confidence in system-level results. These results were then used to focus long-running simulation and emulation workloads on architecturally sensitive areas rather than simply increasing regression volume.
While formal verification established early architectural correctness, validating full OS behavior required executing long instruction streams, which challenged the practical limits of traditional simulation. To address this requirement, a snippet-based simulation flow was developed using the Xcelium Logic Simulator. This allowed long-running software execution to be divided into manageable segments while maintaining architectural state and full debug visibility across boundaries.
To exercise the design under realistic system conditions, the team ran Linux as the primary software workload on a QEMU-based virtual platform. The workload advanced in one-million-cycle increments, with the complete architectural state captured at each checkpoint to create a reusable snippet representing a defined window. Each snippet was then loaded into Xcelium with full signal visibility, allowing engineers to debug a specific region without rerunning the entire OS boot sequence.
Across the full verification flow, approximately 120 snippets were generated, enabling analysis of instruction streams spanning more than 35 million cycles. Extended instruction-stream execution also tested interrupt handling and exercised pipeline behavior. This approach reduced the turnaround time for long software workloads from days to hours and enabled detailed root-cause analysis of complex interactions. Xcelium achieved a simulation rate of approximately 100,000 cycles per second while preserving full debug visibility.
Debugging was done using Verisium Debug, which provided traceability across long instruction sequences and preserved context across simulation runs. This capability enabled efficient analysis of failures observed under software stress without sacrificing visibility.
Combining formal proof with logic simulation enabled a consistent way to connect the results and measure progress across verification stages. Within the platform, Verisium Manager provided a central dashboard for test planning and coverage tracking against defined targets. This unified view showed which coverage targets had been met, where gaps remained, and where to focus next. Verisium Debug complemented these capabilities by maintaining traceability across extended runs and linking simulation and emulation results.
The company transitioned to the Cadence Palladium Enterprise Emulation Platform for Linux bring-up and multicore software workloads. The platform provided the speed and hardware/software visibility needed to execute complete operating-system boot sequences. The team booted Linux on a single-core system in 50 minutes and on a dual-core system in 90 minutes. This confirmed system functionality and architectural scalability. Additionally, the engineers verified coherency and interrupt handling while identifying performance hotspots in concurrent workloads.
Cadence OnCloud platform provided the scalable compute capacity needed to maintain that visibility as verification workloads grew more complex. This emulation stage exposed system-level behavior, supported validation of operation and scalability, and made full-system bring-up practical within the engineering schedule.
By leveraging Cadence OnCloud, compute resources could be scaled to match verification demand during peak periods without requiring a fixed infrastructure commitment at the start of the project. At the same time, built-in security aligned with industry standards such as ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 27017 helped ensure that sensitive IP remained protected throughout the process. The project validated both the approach and the platform.
The company uncovered complex interactions between cores and subsystems to achieve first-silicon success. For a small team, the biggest constraint was not methodology or tooling. It was the amount of work that could realistically be pushed through the system at any given time. Using a Cadence verification tool flow removed that barrier by providing additional capacity when verification demand peaked and turnaround time directly affected development momentum. The team could prioritize critical work instead of scaling back verification to fit the available infrastructure.
First-silicon success provided evidence that the cloud environment could meet the verification demands of a complex CPU design. Future processor development can move more system-level validation into the pre-silicon phase. At-speed prototypes provide a way to evaluate multicore operation and hardware-software interactions before silicon. On-demand access to emulation and prototyping capacity can expand with changing design needs, allowing system-level integration work to begin earlier without requiring an in-house lab.

articles.title: Windscribe CEO tells Canadian Senate he will move the VPN abroad unless Bill C-22 changes
articles.text:
Windscribe CEO tells Canadian Senate he will move the VPN abroad unless Bill C-22 changes
Yegor Sak warned that Canada's Lawful Access Act threatens the global privacy trust placed in homegrown VPNs
- Windscribe warns to exit Canada if Bill C-22 passes without major changes
- Police, child-safety groups back the bill, but tech firms warn of security risks
- The Senate committee begins clause-by-clause review on November 24
Windscribe CEO Yegor Sak has told Canadian lawmakers he would move his Toronto-based VPN company out of the country unless they make substantial changes to Bill C-22.
For privacy-conscious readers picking the best VPN, the standoff shows how far Canada's Bill C-22, or Lawful Access Act, reaches. The bill would let Ottawa compel certain tech providers to build police access capabilities and retain customer metadata they currently refuse to store.
Sak testified by videoconference on Monday, November 23, during the final witness panel before the Standing Senate Committee on National Security, Defence and Veterans Affairs. He appeared alongside Apple and Google Canada, one day before senators begin clause-by-clause review on Tuesday, November 24.
Can Ottawa give investigators faster access to digital trails without weakening encryption or driving privacy businesses abroad? Sak warned senators that passing the bill unchanged leaves Windscribe no choice.
Windscribe Pro: 58% off and lifetime price promise
Was: $69
Now: $29 per year for life!
Windscribe's Black Friday deal has returned, more than halving the price of its 12-month plan to $29 (normally $69). It packs in all of Windscribe's features, 112 locations, unlimited device connections, and seriously fast download speeds. Plus, the price doesn't increase on renewal, meaning you get it for $29 for every year you want it.
Windscribe's ultimatum to Canadian lawmakers
In testimony shared in a post on X on the Windscribe official account, Sak tied his company's survival in Canada directly to the country's legal reputation.
"Canada's rule of law and respect for privacy are the primary reasons we incorporated here in 2015. Bill [C]-22 destroys all of that," Sak told the committee.
"People around the world trust a Canadian company with their privacy. Please don't make leaving Canada the price of keeping the trust," he added.
Passing Bill C-22 would not flip a logging switch overnight, since Ottawa would still need to issue a specific regulation or ministerial order targeting a provider.
Even so, Sak has weighed moving out of Canada since May, and Windscribe previously pledged no changes to its no-logs policy, according to earlier TechRadar coverage.
Relocating corporate headquarters has clear limits, however.
Because Bill C-22 defines electronic service providers broadly enough to cover firms serving Canadians or doing business in Canada, moving the Toronto office alone would not automatically shield a VPN if it kept local servers or corporate ties.
NEW: Leave No Trace — A weekly newsletter on digital privacy and online surveillance.
Leave No Trace investigates the companies and governments putting our digital freedom at risk — and the people fighting back.
📩 Subscribe now to get every edition delivered to your inbox every Friday, launching this September.
Why Bill C-22 divides privacy firms and police
Bill C-22 cleared the House of Commons in June, and debate centres on Part 2.
It empowers the public safety minister to issue confidential orders requiring service providers to build access capabilities for police and intelligence agencies, while regulations could mandate storing IP addresses and connection metadata for up to six months.
Supporters say the updates are overdue. Police chiefs and child-protection advocates told senators that investigators lose vital leads when cross-border digital evidence vanishes, calling the bill critical for fighting online child sexual exploitation.
According to CBC News, Public Safety Minister Gary Anandasangaree's office maintains the law does not introduce systemic vulnerabilities or backdoors.
Ottawa has already cut proposed metadata retention from 12 months to six, barred orders that create a "systemic vulnerability," and clarified that firms need not decrypt data unless they hold the keys, as detailed in the CBS report.
Still, Citizen Lab researchers and tech firms say those safeguards remain too vague, while gag rules block providers from alerting users.
Last week, Meta also warned it may have to "consider" pulling encrypted apps like WhatsApp from Canada. Signal has also threatened to exit rather than alter its protocol.
Windscribe also joined 22 other companies and groups, including NordVPN's parent firm, in signing a September open letter at fixc22.ca.
With Australian officials telling senators Monday that no firms left after Australia's 2018 access law, lawmakers must now decide whether the industry warnings are a bluff or an exodus.

With over two decades of experience as a reporter and editor, he specializes in making complex topics like cybersecurity, VPNs, and enterprise software accessible and engaging.
