articles.title: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket’s Marisa Kabas.
Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
It’s also not because of ‘tech bro’ culture.
It’s also not because of ‘tech bro’ culture.
During the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement — an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself — “completely untrue.” He added, “Don’t think for a second politics played a role in the company. We are the most apolitical company,” according to Kabas.
Along with attempting to dismiss Trump’s involvement, Huang reportedly said he also didn’t return because he was a “tech bro” who was “above the law” or “above the code of conduct.” He added that, “no story has been more tortured than this one in human history,” Kabas reports. Instead, Huang said the Nvidia board “evaluated the entire situation,” while receiving assurance from the government that he posed no national security threat, according to the NYT.
Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on November 12th, following reports of affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two employees, including vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell. On Monday, Nvidia announced that it had reinstated Huang as CEO, president, and member of the board — a decision the White House said Trump was “totally involved in.” Trump also confirmed that he worked with Vice President JD Vance and other officials to bring Huang back. A swath of tech leaders, including Tesla CEO Elon Musk, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and former White House AI czar David Sacks, were also in favor of Huang’s return.
In a post on Truth Social, Trump said that the government “has no reason to believe” Huang’s return poses a risk to national security, adding that the US attorney general “does not possess evidence” that he engaged in “unlawful conduct.” Nvidia is still facing an investigation over its accounting practices, according to Reuters. The company is also carrying out its own internal investigation surrounding reports that Huang was the target of a Chinese spy plot. Huang is set to testify before Congress on December 1st to answer questions about national security concerns, and Democrats are already planning to press Huang about his return, as well as Trump’s involvement.
Even after all this, Huang reportedly said he “doesn’t believe in succession planning.” He also acknowledged that he violated Nvidia’s code of conduct, adding that he is attending therapy daily, Bloomberg reports. “I made some terrible mistakes,” Huang said, according to the NYT. “I was unfaithful to Lori, and I hurt my kids and of course, I hurt all of you.”

articles.title: Paso a paso para crear fotos de Las Guerreras K-pop en el universo de GTA 6 en WhatsApp y gratis
articles.text:
Crear una imagen de Las Guerreras K-pop en el universo de GTA 6 desde WhatsApp requiere reunir buenas referencias, abrir una conversación con Meta AI y describir con precisión la escena.
La herramienta puede combinar elementos de distintas imágenes para proponer una versión nueva con estética urbana, vehículos, palmeras y luces de neón.
El proceso puede hacerse desde el celular y sin instalar un editor adicional. La calidad del resultado depende, en buena medida, de las imágenes elegidas y del nivel de detalle del texto que acompaña la solicitud.
Cuál es el primer paso para generar la ilustración
El primer paso consiste en guardar una imagen nítida de las protagonistas. Conviene elegir una fotografía o ilustración en la que aparezcan de frente, con el rostro visible y sin objetos que cubran el cuerpo.
Además, es útil revisar el tamaño del archivo antes de enviarlo. Una imagen borrosa, oscura o comprimida puede dificultar que la inteligencia artificial identifique detalles como el color del cabello, las prendas o los accesorios.
La segunda imagen debe aportar el escenario. Para lograr una composición cercana al universo de Grand Theft Auto VI, se puede elegir una captura promocional con calles costeras, edificios bajos, autos deportivos, murales, palmeras o un atardecer sobre la ciudad.
No hace falta que las protagonistas aparezcan en la imagen del videojuego. La referencia sirve para marcar el tipo de ciudad, la iluminación y la paleta de colores. Una avenida tropical con luces de neón, una playa urbana o un estacionamiento junto a edificios modernos pueden dar mayor coherencia al resultado final.
Cómo subir las referencias a Meta AI en la app de WhatsApp
Con ambas imágenes guardadas en el teléfono, hay que abrir WhatsApp y localizar el acceso a Meta AI, que puede aparecer como un chat propio o mediante el ícono circular de la herramienta. Después, se debe iniciar una conversación y pulsar el botón para adjuntar archivos desde la galería.
Primero se pueden enviar las dos imágenes juntas: una con Las Guerreras K-pop y otra con la ambientación de GTA 6. La aplicación permite añadir texto antes de enviarlas, así que hay que incluir allí el pedido.
Qué prompt se puede usar para pedir la ilustración
El texto debe indicar quiénes aparecen, dónde están, qué ropa llevan, cuál es la composición y qué estilo visual se busca. En lugar de una frase breve, conviene detallar los elementos que se quieren conservar. Puede aclararse que no se agreguen textos, marcas de agua ni personajes adicionales.
Un prompt posible es el siguiente: “Crea una imagen horizontal de tres guerreras K-pop en una ciudad costera inspirada en GTA 6. A la izquierda, una joven de cabello negro recogido, chaqueta de cuero negra y dos dagas. En el centro, una joven con larga trenza violeta, chaqueta amarilla y una espada con brillo azul. A la derecha, una joven de cabello rosado, ropa rosa y una lanza. Están frente a una camioneta con grafitis, palmeras, edificios y luces de neón al atardecer. Estilo de arte digital cinematográfico, colores intensos, alta definición, sin letras ni logotipos”.
Cómo corregir el resultado si la primera versión no convence
La primera respuesta puede incluir cambios no deseados en los rostros, las manos, las armas o el fondo. En ese caso, no es necesario empezar desde cero.
Se puede responder sobre la misma imagen y pedir correcciones puntuales, como “mantén el cabello violeta en una sola trenza”, “cambia el vehículo por un auto clásico” o “elimina a las personas del fondo”.
Otra opción es modificar el encuadre. Si las protagonistas aparecen muy lejos, puede pedirse un retrato de medio cuerpo. Los ajustes breves y específicos suelen dar mejores resultados que un nuevo texto extenso con muchas órdenes a la vez.
De qué forma descargar y compartir la imagen creada
Cuando Meta AI entregue una versión satisfactoria, hay que mantener presionada la imagen o abrir el menú de opciones del mensaje. Allí aparece la alternativa para guardarla en la galería. Antes de descargarla, hay que revisar que esté en buena resolución para publicarla en redes sociales o enviarla a través de un chat.
Asimismo, la imagen final puede compartirse desde WhatsApp, subirla a una historia o incorporarla a una publicación. Si se quiere probar otras variantes, como una versión para colorear, solo hay que conservar las referencias iniciales y cambiar detalles del prompt.

articles.title: Adyen’s co-founder Pieter van der Does to retire as Co-CEO; Ingo Uytdehaage to become sole CEO
articles.text:
Pieter van der Does, co-founder and Co-CEO of Dutch Fintech Adyen, is stepping down from his executive role after 20 years at the helm of one of Europe’s most prominent technology companies.
In an announcement on 23 November 2026, marking Adyen’s 20th anniversary, the company said van der Does will retire on 31 December 2026, and Ingo Uytdehaage, Co-CEO since 2023, will become sole CEO
“After 20 years, this is the right moment for me to step down on a positive note and with a very good feeling. Adyen has been my life’s work, and I’m incredibly proud of what our teams and customers have built together over the past two decades. Ingo and I have worked very closely together as Co-CEOs, and now we have completed the transition,” said van der Does, co-founder and co-CEO of Adyen.
Arnout Schuijff and van der Does launched Adyen in 2006, and the company was formally incorporated on 23 November 2006, when Schuijff visited a notary in Amsterdam to formally establish the company. Van der Does, who was on a sabbatical in Brazil at the time, followed the proceedings remotely over Skype.
Before starting Adyen, the co-founders had previously worked together at payments company Bibit, and their shared ambition became Adyen, which means “doing it again” in Surinamese. In his farewell letter, Van der Does says, “Adyen outgrew our wildest imagination.”
Since its early days in Amsterdam, Adyen has grown into a global FinTech processing more than €1.4 trillion annually. It serves over one billion shoppers per year across more than 29 offices worldwide and counts customers like Meta, Uber, H&M, eBay, and Microsoft.
The company listed on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange in 2018 and has sustained double-digit annual growth since 2007. It has also expanded beyond payments into a broader enterprise financial operating system following the acquisitions of loyal technology firm Talon.One and billing platform Orb.
The leadership transition comes weeks after the company posted robust third-quarter performance results. During Q3 2026, the company reported net revenue of €738.1 million, a 23% year-on-year increase, while processed volume climbed 30% year-on-year to €451.1 billion. The platforms segment stood out during the quarter, with net revenue up 46% year-on-year. Adyen also guided net revenue growth of 21% to 23% on a constant currency basis for the full year.
In a statement, the company confirmed that the CEO transition will not impact its financial objectives and the leadership change had been in the making for over three years through a co-CEO model. “We have been planning this transition for more than three years with the Co-CEO model. It took some time for all the pieces to fall into place, but the moment is now,” Van der Does wrote in his company-wide letter.
As part of the transition, Van der Does will remain available to the company as an advisor, while the Supervisory Board chair Herna Verhagen said the company is ready for its next chapter.
Uytdehaage, who has worked alongside Van der Does for more than 15 years, acknowledged the opportunity to keep building and the responsibility to shape the next stage.
“Pieter built more than a company. He built a culture that shapes how we make decisions, how we treat each other and how we put our merchants first, and it will outlast any one of us,” he added.

articles.title: Google wants to create an AI-generated TV channel starring you, complete with ads
articles.text:
Through the looking glass: Companies that have invested millions or billions into AI aren't being discouraged by the "slop" label. Google, for example, has filed a patent application for an entirely AI-generated TV channel in which the main character is... you. If that doesn't sound off-putting enough, the content will be based on the data Google collects about you, and it will also feature customized ads.
First noticed by Patentlyze, Google's AI-generated channel, imaginatively called "My Channel," is described as an option in a TV app. The content it generates will be based on demographic data, device data, YouTube watch history, and any other information Google holds about the user, who will also be the protagonist in these shows.
Once someone clicks on the channel, they will be given options to watch a personalized show starring themselves. Examples include sci-fi adventures, fun romantic comedies, and an action/thriller experience, all featuring the user's own likeness and voice. These shows can be created with or without specific user requests.
One section describes how, if a person watched a lot of sports videos, such as the best moments of a particular player, the system could create a video of the player's highlights interspersed with footage of the user cheering in the stands. The user could even be shown "interacting" with the player – something that sounds a little concerning.
Not surprisingly, it's also suggested that the channel would be connected to an "advertising server," one that inserts ads into the personalized content. "An advertising stitcher included in the advertising server generates an updated customized media content item by inserting at least one advertisement into the customized media content item," it reads.
An entirely AI-generated TV channel isn't new. In August, Fairground AI Creator TV launched, a free, ad-supported streaming channel that airs AI-generated films and series 24 hours a day. It lists Roku, LG, and Amazon among the platforms to watch the channel.
AI-generated movies and TV shows are still about as popular as the plague. China's first fully AI-generated movie recently flopped at the box office, pulling in just $270,000 over three weeks.
Google might think using your likeness as the star of the personalized shows will make the content more appealing, but most people will probably just find it creepy and a worrying illustration of just how much the company knows about them. There's also the fact that the more AI-generated slop proliferates across social media, the more people are pushing back against it. Instagram took note and recently made it harder for AI-generated personas to pass themselves off as real people.
The majority of patents don't become real products, of course. Let's hope this one never does.

articles.title: Mozilla explica por que não há um Firefox "puro" para iPhone
articles.text:
Mozilla explica por que não há um Firefox “puro” para iPhone
Mozilla afirma que regras impostas pela Apple são complexas e inviabilizam o Firefox de ter seu próprio motor no iOS.
A Mozilla lançou a primeira versão do Firefox para iPhone em 2015. Mas, até hoje, o navegador não conta com uma implementação totalmente “pura” no iOS, com motor próprio. Em tom de desabafo, a organização explicou o motivo. Saiba desde já que, sim, a Mozilla culpa a Apple por isso.
Quando falamos de motor, nos referimos ao componente central do navegador, que interpreta o código de páginas web escrito em padrões como HTML, CSS e JavaScript, e transforma esse conjunto de informações em um conteúdo visual e interativo para o usuário.
Hoje, a maior parte dos navegadores é baseada no projeto Chromium, a exemplo do Microsoft Edge, do Opera, do Brave e, claro, do Google Chrome. No Chromium, o motor utilizado é o Blink.
O Firefox é diferente, pois conta com um motor próprio: o Gecko. Mas, no iOS, o navegador é executado a partir do WebKit, motor mantido pela Apple que, como tal, é a base do Safari.
É aqui que está o ponto de conflito: se dependesse da Mozilla, o Firefox também contaria com o Gecko no iPhone.
A Apple exigia que os navegadores para iOS usassem o WebKit sob o argumento de que essa condição favorecia aspectos como segurança, privacidade e desempenho. Isso mudou em 2024, quando a Digital Markets Act (DMA) passou a vigorar. Trata-se de uma legislação da União Europeia que busca aumentar a concorrência no âmbito digital.
Entre várias outras medidas, a DMA determina que os usuários tenham a opção de escolher o navegador padrão de seus dispositivos. Isso também deu abertura para que outros motores de navegação pudessem ser usados no iOS.
Então, problema resolvido, certo? De acordo com a Mozilla, não. A organização explica que as condições determinadas pela Apple para que um navegador para iPhone conte com um motor diferente do WebKit são tão complexas que, até hoje, nenhum desenvolvedor conseguiu encontrar um caminho viável para isso.
Em um comunicado recente, a Mozilla conta o principal problema relacionado às condições da Apple:
Para usar o Gecko [no iOS], não podemos simplesmente atualizar o Firefox que as pessoas já usam e adoram. Teríamos que criar um aplicativo completamente separado, um segundo Firefox.
Depois, teríamos que pedir a todos os usuários do Firefox que baixassem a nova versão, transferissem seus favoritos, senhas e histórico e fizessem a transição manualmente, passo a passo, de modo confuso.
Onde, exatamente, está o problema? O Firefox é um software de distribuição global. Para se adequar à DMA, a Apple passou a permitir o uso de mecanismos alternativos ao seu, mas com a condição de que eles sejam distribuídos exclusivamente na região autorizada, e não em escala global.
A Mozilla teria então que ter um Firefox para iOS válido globalmente (a versão atual, com WebKit) e outro, com o Gecko, específico para a União Europeia. Pelo menos até o momento, é inviável para a Mozilla trabalhar com essa dualidade.
Na prática, isso significa que os usuários teriam que baixar um novo app e transferir manualmente seus dados para ele. A organização também considera esse aspecto inviável.
Por conta disso, a solução vislumbrada pela Mozilla é a de pressionar a Apple: “continuaremos lutando por condições realmente justas, não por uma brecha que prejudique os navegadores independentes”.

articles.title: Huawei é condenada por roubo de segredos comerciais nos EUA
articles.text:
A Huawei foi considerada culpada de conspiração para roubar segredos comerciais e de fraude bancária em um julgamento realizado nos Estados Unidos. Por outro lado, a gigante chinesa de tecnologia e telecomunicações foi absolvida da acusação mais abrangente de associação criminosa, considerada mais grave no processo. O veredicto foi divulgado nesta terça-feira (24), após dois meses de julgamento.O julgamento durou dois meses, e as acusações contra a companhia foram anunciadas pela primeira vez por promotores federais em 2019.
Durante o processo, os promotores acusaram a empresa de recorrer a mentiras, fraudes e roubo de informações para obter vantagens competitivas no mercado. A defesa da Huawei contestou a abordagem da acusação e afirmou que os investigadores partiram da premissa de que a companhia era uma organização criminosa, construindo o caso a partir dessa interpretação. As informações são da BBC.
Huawei se manifesta após veredicto
Em sua defesa, a empresa argumentou que seu sucesso comercial foi resultado de inovação própria, e não de práticas criminosas. A estratégia dos advogados foi questionar a maneira como o caso foi conduzido pelos promotores norte-americanos.
Após a decisão, a Huawei divulgou um comunicado no qual destacou a absolvição da acusação de associação criminosa. Segundo a companhia, o resultado confirma que as alegações relacionadas a esse ponto não tinham fundamento factual.
A empresa também afirmou que a decisão valida sua posição mantida ao longo dos últimos oito anos. O comunicado foi divulgado depois que o júri decidiu pela condenação em duas acusações e pela absolvição na imputação mais abrangente.
Promotores e defesa apresentam argumentos finais
Durante as alegações finais, realizadas na semana anterior ao veredicto, a promotora assistente dos Estados Unidos Meredith Arfa afirmou que a Huawei passou 20 anos fazendo o que fosse necessário para expandir seus negócios. Entre as acusações apresentadas aos jurados estavam mentiras a bancos sobre as operações comerciais da empresa no Irã e o roubo de segredos tecnológicos de companhias concorrentes para garantir vantagens no mercado.
O advogado de defesa Brian Heberlig apresentou uma versão diferente sobre o crescimento da companhia. Segundo ele, a Huawei expandiu suas operações para 170 países e chegou a mais de 200 mil funcionários por meio de trabalho e inovação.
Empresa é condenada por duas acusações
O resultado do julgamento representa uma decisão dividida para a Huawei. A companhia foi considerada culpada de conspiração para roubar segredos comerciais e de fraude bancária, mas não foi condenada pela acusação mais ampla de associação criminosa.
O processo durou dois meses e envolveu acusações de que a empresa teria utilizado diferentes práticas ilegais para fortalecer sua posição competitiva. A defesa, por sua vez, sustentou que os resultados alcançados pela Huawei decorreram de seu próprio desenvolvimento tecnológico.
A decisão foi divulgada em um julgamento considerado marcante nos Estados Unidos.
Ana Figueiredo é editora de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em Jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).

articles.title: One terminal command gave my forgotten Android device a desk job
articles.text:
My kitchen junk drawer used to hold takeout menus and coupons, but it has since become a storage spot for old tablets or phones. Like me, you probably have a few devices lying around that are perfectly functional but don’t meet your daily driving needs. It’s tucked out of view, living out its life in a drawer until being erased and donated after someone asks why you’re holding onto outdated, unused devices. Thankfully, PhoneBox has a solution. You weren’t hoarding old tech; you were waiting for the proper use.
The PhoneBox home screen displays useful stats and what’s currently playing in your browser.
Credit:
Nick Indge
The PhoneBox home screen displays useful stats and what’s currently playing in your browser.
Credit:
Nick Indge
I had an old AllDoCube iPlay 50 mini Pro 8.4-inch tablet that seemed like the perfect candidate. I bought the tablet second-hand as a possible big-screen gaming and emulation tablet to use with a telescopic control deck, but I quickly found I vastly preferred just using a dedicated device. Since that realization, this decent little unit has lived its life in “the drawer.”
Launch applications on your PC from the connected Android device.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Launch applications on your PC from the connected Android device.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Installation is a doddle
Getting PhoneBox up and running on my tablet and PC couldn’t have been simpler. After making sure that the Android tablet was in developer mode, the process was as easy as plugging the tablet in to my PC via USB and executing a single copied command in my Linux terminal. The script downloaded the PhoneBox 0.9.29 software for my PC, verified the downloaded checksum against the release, and walked me through a few quick Y/N installation questions. The script offers to create a systemd user service, so the desktop agent launches after initial login, and even asks if you’d like it to install the PhoneBox APK to your connected Android device.
Developer options and ADB are required for USB setup.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Developer options and ADB are required for USB setup.
Credit:
Nick Indge
I already had developer mode initialized on the tablet but had to go back and allow ADB over USB in settings. The total installation time from copying the script from the project website to everything running on my PC and tablet was less than a minute. The app is MIT-licensed, works on Android 5.0 or later, and requires sideloading, since it is not available on the Google Play Store.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Credit:
Nick Indge
The installation script also prints its own uninstall script before it finishes. So often these days, getting rid of an unwanted app feels more difficult than installing it, so I appreciate the straightforward approach the developer has implemented.
The script can install the APK directly to your device.
Credit:
Nick Indge
The script can install the APK directly to your device.
Credit:
Nick Indge
What your device becomes
The first time you fire up PhoneBox, you get live performance and diagnostic information from your PC, along with several pages of optional content that can be tweaked for your local setup to display information that’s pertinent to your uses.
Want to check on your system resources in-game?
Credit:
Nick Indge
Want to check on your system resources in-game?
Credit:
Nick Indge
Where PhoneBox really starts to shine is the widget catalog—a collection of free add-ons that can be added as pages to the tablet’s cycling page layouts. There are more general widgets, such as RSS feeds that display news highlights from your chosen sources, or simple displays like timers or world clocks.
No shortage of available add-ons.
Credit:
Nick Indge
No shortage of available add-ons.
Credit:
Nick Indge
I opted for a few different widgets that caught my eye. One let me view my library of installed Steam titles and launch them on my PC with a simple tap of the tablet screen. Another allows me to control smart home entities hosted by my Home Assistant server. I was controlling the lights in my office from my tablet within seconds of adding the widget. It’s brilliant.
Home Assistant connected device controls on PhoneBox.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Home Assistant connected device controls on PhoneBox.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Setting up additional widgets is as simple as adding them to the page layout from the PC’s web interface and hitting save. As soon as I updated things from the PC, the connected tablet immediately began reflecting the changes. I haven’t had the chance to test most of the 131 current options in the widget catalog, but the ones I did try were simple to modify and worked on the first try.
I can launch installed Steam Library titles from the tablet controls.
Credit:
Nick Indge
I can launch installed Steam Library titles from the tablet controls.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Some frictions
While I didn’t have any major issues with PhoneBox, I did notice a couple of early annoyances along the way. Windows users should be aware that the PC companion app on that OS is currently unsigned, and they should expect a SmartScreen notification when attempting to install the software.
All control settings live in the web interface rather than the phone or tablet you’re connecting. When I first started messing with PhoneBox, I noticed it displayed my weather location as Tallinn. Nothing against the capital of Estonia, but that’s not weather information that does me much good here in the US Midwest. When I went into the widget settings to change the report location, there was nothing to be found. It turns out that you have to change those settings from the general user preferences section rather than within the widget itself. Not a deal-breaker by any means, but a slight hiccup for someone who was new to the software.
Connecting the Android tablet with my PC over USB was totally painless, but I never got the wireless route to work in my testing. Users are meant to generate a QR code from the PhoneBox web interface on their PC and connect it to their device by scanning the code with their phone/tablet. Every time I tried to scan the code from my device’s camera app, the tablet refused. There’s no QR scanner built into the PhoneBox app, so if your camera app won’t cooperate, the documented path dead-ends. USB was my intended route anyway and works great, but if you’re planning a wireless-only setup, be prepared for possible friction. The documented flow needs your device camera to open the pairing link, and mine wasn’t in the mood.
I may have to go back and try the wireless mode again.
I may have to go back and try the wireless mode again.
These minor gripes should be smoothed over before the release of 1.0. The project is early, but it seems to be moving quickly. I tested and installed PhoneBox version 0.9.29, which was one of several releases pushed to the project’s GitHub in as many days. One item of history worth noting: On November 20, the project published a high-severity security advisory covering versions 0.9.23 and earlier. The vulnerability potentially allowed another app running on the connected Android device to execute commands or receive stored credentials from the host PC. The flaw no longer existed by the time I tested the package in version 0.9.29, but it’s a good reminder that you’re installing something with deep system access and should exercise appropriate caution.
Is it worth trying?
As long as you’re part of the group that has an old phone or tablet lying around somewhere, and these days I expect that most of us are, then it’s an emphatic yes. Repurposing old devices to find new lives is one of the things that keeps me a tech hobbyist. I love finding genuinely useful and practical applications for devices that have been pushed aside by their manufacturers in favor of the latest and greatest in the lineup.
Monitor all your system processes live.
Credit:
Nick Indge
Monitor all your system processes live.
Credit:
Nick Indge
PhoneBox took a tablet that was forgotten in a junk drawer and destined for donation and gave it a new lease on life. I haven’t spent a single penny, but I now have a useful secondary display on my desk. The tablet is powered via a dedicated USB port on my PC, and only goes to sleep when my main monitor displays do. Go dig through those mystery drawers in your house, because this one is worthwhile.
Nick Indge is a Senior Technology Reporter at Ars Technica covering hardware, embedded systems, and self-hosted infrastructure. A former security investigator turned tech writer, he writes to help readers escape subscription traps and regain ownership of their digital lives. He lives in Chicagoland with his family and a goofball husky.

articles.title: Why a Crusoe investor is betting on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
articles.text:
The problem of supplying power to AI data centers has become one of the central debates of the AI era. In just a few years, the U.S. grid has gone from basically zero growth to adding several gigawatts a year.
“Demand is growing faster than people appreciate,” Brook Porter, partner at G2 Venture Partners (G2VP), told TechCrunch. “It’s atoms, not bits, and the world is in the process of recognizing the realities of those challenges.”
It’s been a bumpy road. Because it takes a while to scale supply chains, companies have been securing power in any form they can. In many cases, that has meant buying, renting, and deploying natural gas power plants, but Porter thinks that hyperscalers and data center developers should look at the bigger picture if they want to move faster.
That picture involves solar paired with energy storage, based on an analysis Porter and his colleagues at G2VP recently conducted on the state of the data center power market.
“Global capacity of natural gas is only about 60 or 70 gigawatts per year, where solar is already at well over a terawatt,” he said. “Probably the most important lesson that we’ve learned over the last 20 years of backing companies is that Wright’s Law is the thing you want to leverage — making the same thing over and over again.”
Both solar and most forms of long-duration energy storage are built on small, modular technologies that can be manufactured at massive scale. “This is about speed and scale and economics, and we can win across all those dimensions,” Porter said.
G2VP had an early window into AI data center development, having led Crusoe’s Series C. “We’ve had a front-row seat at what’s been happening at that company, how they’ve evolved, how the different waves of data centers have evolved,” Porter said.
The venture firm estimates that data center investment will top $4 trillion until the end of the decade. As the next wave takes shape, the firm sees two different paths for data centers: small, on-grid facilities with their own generating capacity, and larger data centers powered by solar and long-duration energy storage.
“The big idea is to go off-grid,” Porter said. “What that would enable you to do is build with renewables in a way that’s independent of the grid. You can determine your own fate, go around some of the constraints of permitting, whether that’s access to the grid or air permits. You can accelerate your time to market dramatically.”
In recent years, energy storage has been synonymous with lithium-ion batteries, which are too expensive to compete with fossil fuels for round-the-clock power. But a new generation of long-duration energy storage products from the likes of Form Energy and G2VP portfolio company Antora Energy have brought the cost per megawatt-hour down significantly.
Even though the technologies might be a few years away from broad acceptance among data center developers, Porter said they should start thinking about them now.
“It’s analogous to surfing the biggest waves off of Mavericks here in Northern California. The wave is so big that you really have to be paddling and moving and be incredibly nimble to catch it. If you’re at a standstill, it’s just gonna blow you by,” he said.

Enchufes y luces inteligentes

Limpieza inteligente
Se trata de una de las categorías más novedosas dentro del catálogo de TP-Link Tapo: su robot aspirador. El mejor ayudante para tener la casa limpia de una manera totalmente autónoma. Sólo hay que programarlo con la aplicación para que salga a aspirar y pasar la mopa unos días determinados y listo, cuando lleguemos a casa estará limpia. Su estación de carga también puede vaciar el depósito de residuos (para que no tengamos que hacerlo nosotros) y limpiar y secar las mopas para dejarlas perfectamente para la siguiente limpieza.
El Tapo RV50 Pro Omni destaca especialmente por su estación de autolimpieza todo en uno, diseñada para que tengas que preocuparte lo mínimo posible por el mantenimiento del robot. Se encarga de automatizar tareas como el vaciado del polvo, el lavado de las mopas y su secado, ofreciendo una experiencia de limpieza mucho más cómoda y reduciendo las tareas de mantenimiento del día a día.

Lo mejor de todo es que su precio es bastante bueno, más incluso teniendo en cuenta el descuento.
Estos han sido sólo algunos de los productos que más nos han llamado la atención, pero hay muchísimos más por lo que si no has encontrado el adecuado, visita la web de TP-Link y su sección exclusiva para el Black Friday y haz que tu casa sea más inteligente, más segura, mejor conectada y más limpia.

articles.title: Tech leaders call for action on scale-up capital, procurement, and government support
articles.text:
In 1714, the British Parliament offered up to 20,000 pounds, a fortune at the time (roughly $3.5 million in today’s Canadian dollars), for a reliable way to determine longitude at sea—a problem that was costing sailors their lives. The answer didn’t come from astronomers of the day; it was John Harrison, a self-taught carpenter and clockmaker, who developed the marine chronometer and made ocean navigation safer.
What could a prize like that help Canadian innovators solve today?
“Canada can’t grow the innovation economy with public money and regulation. It’s stifling, overly restrictive, and full of red tape.”
Fiona Simpson, BioMimir
Robert Kaul, CEO of remote patient monitoring company Cloud DX, would like to find out. In a MaRS pulse-check of 21 high-growth founders and executives looking at what it takes to scale a company in Canada, Kaul proposed putting up $100 million to incentivize startups to solve “the hardest problems the country faces,” from hospital overcrowding and lagging productivity to homelessness and substance addiction.
“The allure of a large monetary prize and ultimate prestige can generate more than 100 times [the investment],” he said.
Toronto-based MaRS Discovery District is marking 25 years as the anchor innovation hub for Canadian startups. Its fall snapshot (captured from October 23 to November 6) heard from founders and executives of 21 high-growth ventures in its portfolio. It captures both ambitious ideas, like Kaul’s, and concerns about whether companies can get the backing they need to succeed globally. With seven of the 21 respondents considering moving their headquarters abroad, the findings also raise the question of whether Canada can provide the support they need to stay at home as they grow.
Finding the money to grow
For startups ready to expand, financing is the most common concern respondents raised. Access to growth capital was a challenge cited in 17 of the 21 responses, with Canadian venture funding particularly limited for companies seeking $25 million or more in a single financing round.
Fiona Simpson, CEO of BioMimir, a Sherbrooke-based medtech company, called for more private investment in young startups.
“Canada can’t grow the innovation economy with public money and regulation,” she noted. “It’s stifling, overly restrictive, and full of red tape.”
She called for capital gains tax incentives to encourage more early-stage and seed funds to form and make more investments. Initial successes could build confidence in complex, high-risk fields such as medtech, deep tech, and AgTech, helping attract additional capital, retain Canadian talent, and recruit international expertise.
The federal government proposed a related measure in Budget 2026: the Canada Growth Incentive, which includes a tax exemption on up to $15 million in capital gains from eligible startup investments, along with more time to reinvest proceeds in qualifying Canadian businesses.
Finding customers at home
Convincing investors to take a chance on startups is easier with a paying customer on board, which presents another hurdle. Twelve of the 21 respondents identified slow procurement and difficulty finding Canadian customers as barriers to growth.
For deep tech and hard tech businesses, those first sales can be especially tricky, explained Vida Gabriel, COO of TerraFixing, an Ottawa-based company that develops cold-climate carbon capture technology.
“Investors want to see customers and market traction, but early-stage deep tech and hard tech companies have a hard time selling first-of-a-kind projects,” she said. If the government can help get tech from demonstration stage to full commercial readiness, “that would help.”
For Sam Mugel, CTO of Multiverse Computing, an AI and quantum software developer with an office in Toronto, Canadian corporations’ reluctance to adopt new technology makes it harder for businesses that sell it to grow at home. He wants the government to give buyers both direction and a financial incentive.
“Canada needs to send a clear message to its industrial sector to say these are the champions which I would like you to support; and I will finance your procurement if you’re procuring from these companies,” he said.
Choose a priority, and stick with it
Albert Tai, CEO of Toronto-based healthtech Hypercare, suggests concentrating that backing in a few industries, including healthcare IT, medical devices, and pharmaceuticals.
“We have world-renowned hospitals, but the majority of the hospital software systems are American,” he said.
Louis Brun, CEO of Montreal’s Sollum Technologies, which develops programmable LED lighting for greenhouses, also favours a focused approach, with a commitment to see it through. He suggests sustained public investment in priorities such as sustainable clean tech, sovereign AgTech, and applied frontier engineering.
“By locking in a multi-decade commitment that transcends election cycles, we [give] researchers, entrepreneurs, and global investors the policy stability required to build world-leading domestic industries from the ground up,” he said.
For Kaul, the value of a major innovation award is personal. Cloud DX, based in Kitchener, was Canada’s entry into Qualcomm Tricorder XPRIZE and in 2017 became the first-ever recipient of the XPRIZE Bold Epic Innovator Award. But he knows prizes alone won’t make Canada a better place to build a business.
“There’s no magic bullet,” he said. “We need the best rules and regulations, the fairest taxes, the best R&D partnerships, the best (and quickest) access to capital, the most trustworthy, low-friction legal environment, and the strongest commitment from government, the media, enterprise, and academia—all pulling together.”
PRESENTED BY
For 25 years, MaRS has helped Canadian ventures grow. Meet the founders, thinkers, scientists, entrepreneurs, and investors behind the ideas and innovations shaping what’s next, from climate solutions to advances in health and medicine.

articles.title: How Can AI Build Faster And Better Silicon For Physical AI?
articles.text:
Shortening the path from design intent to verified implementation could put custom silicon within reach of more teams.
The age of physical AI is here, and with it comes a significant increase in the demand of custom silicon.
By 2025, five million industrial robots were operating worldwide. As these systems become more capable, their demands on silicon become more distinct. Each must balance computation and memory with the realities of power, latency, reliability, and security.
Fig. 1: Annual installations of industrial robots, 5 largest markets, 2025. Source: International Federation of Robotics, World Robotics 2026. Chart redrawn by ChipAgents.
For humanoid robots in particular, application-specific hardware can provide the agility and speed required to perform specialized tasks in real time. As those requirements diverge, specialized ASICs become more attractive, because they can be optimized for the exact workloads, latency targets, power envelopes, and operating environments of a particular system.
The constraint to this innovation is development speed: AI models and software evolve faster than the conventional silicon tape out cycles, creating a need to accelerate the entire path from design intent and exploration to physical implementation and validation.
For agentic AI to deliver that acceleration, it must meet three requirements.
Agents need a shared, persistent representation of the design and the engineering knowledge behind it. A design ontology provides structure: it connects design flows, RTL design, verification, verification tools, error diagnosis and repair, synthesis, timing, and PPA optimization methodologies. Organization-specific methodologies and prior decisions add the rationale for how the design should evolve. To remain useful across tasks, this context must track provenance, design versions, and dependencies, so agents can distinguish current evidence from assumptions or superseded results.
Consider a 3D-IC, where logic, memory, die-to-die interfaces, packaging, power delivery, and thermal behavior are coupled. An RTL change that preserves functional behavior can alter switching activity, placement, or interconnect demand, affecting timing, power integrity, and temperature after implementation. Persistent context helps agents trace those dependencies across die and system boundaries, identify which analyses and verification results may no longer be valid, and invoke the appropriate tools to reassess them. AI then also converts improvement from specific cases into reusable knowledge, helping reduce recurring mistakes and repeated investigation across similar tasks.
Second, agents must carry design objectives through many dependent steps, measuring progress against verified engineering outcomes: functional correctness, physical feasibility, and target power, performance, and area within schedule and compute budgets.
Novel architectures for physical AI introduce more configurations, interfaces, and corner cases. Accelerating individual tasks delivers limited value if downstream verification or physical implementation cannot converge. Every action must therefore serve the overall objective, with explicit acceptance criteria guiding execution and determining when the work is complete.
This requires co-optimizing models, tools, and compute across the workflow. Complex reasoning may benefit from a larger model, repeatable operations from deterministic procedures, and numerical analysis from specialized engineering tools. CPU and GPU allocation, memory capacity, and parallel execution must be selected according to their contribution to the final result. The relevant measure is total time and cost to a validated outcome.
Third, all systems produced must be held to a critical standard of verifiability and security.
Physical AI applications operate in the real world, often in environments where failures can create direct safety risks. Specialized hardware also introduces hardware-specific security requirements and potential vulnerabilities that must be identified and verified before deployment. Agentic AI can help automate portions of that process by checking implementations against security requirements, surfacing potential vulnerabilities, and generating additional verification scenarios. That being said, to achieve an entirely autonomous workflow, you need traceable decisions, reproducible tool runs, explicit verification assumptions, and engineer review and signoff. Trust in this system is dependent on the evidence supporting each engineering decision.
At ChipAgents, we’re building toward a question: what would it take to make chip development 10× faster? Our approach brings organizational design ontology, physics-aware models, and LLM agents together in IC-STAR, the chip neural engine powering our platform. We study how models and multi-agent orchestration can work together to reach verified outcomes faster, with lower inference cost. Our ambition is to shorten the path from design intent to verified implementation, which could put custom silicon within reach of more teams, opening new possibilities for machines that sense, move, and act. We see a future where more engineering ideas make it beyond the drawing board and into the world.

articles.title: 1 600 sorties en une semaine : Steam peine à suivre et les délais de validation explosent
articles.text:
Pour vendre un jeu sur Steam, un studio doit passer par Steamworks, l’espace que Valve réserve aux développeurs. Il y fait vérifier son compte (identité et informations fiscales), puis Valve examine sa page boutique et son jeu.
Jusqu’ici, ces étapes prenaient quelques jours, tout au plus deux semaines. Mais ce mardi 24 novembre, le développeur indépendant derrière Murder Meet Cute a alerté sur Bluesky : d’après d’autres développeurs, ces délais atteignent désormais 45 jours.
Autrement dit, un studio qui ouvre son compte cette semaine ne pourra pas montrer son jeu sur Steam avant janvier, voire fin janvier si ces 45 jours sont des jours ouvrés, comme l’évoquent plusieurs témoignages.
Le Black Friday est lancé sur l’univers Apple. Sur Back Market, profitez de promotions sur les iPhone, MacBook, iPad, AirPods et Apple Watch. Chaque appareil est soumis à jusqu’à 100 points de contrôle qualité et est livré avec une garantie de 12 mois. De quoi profiter de performances comparables à celles d’un produit neuf.
Une avalanche de jeux
Début novembre, ce même développeur parlait déjà de délais passés de 15 à 30 jours pour valider un compte. Il conseillait alors aux autres studios de « planifier en conséquence ». Il accompagnait son analyse du graphe des sorties sur Steam au fil des semaines.
On peut voir une moyenne de 400 jeux par semaine tout au long des années 2024 et 2025, avant une explosion en 2026 jusqu’à 1600 sorties par semaine.
On a aussi le témoignage de la développeuse Bertine van Hövell qui a publié la réponse de Steamworks à son dossier fiscal et d’identité. Quand elle l’a envoyé, on lui annonçait 15 jours maximum. Steamworks parle maintenant de 45 jours. En attendant, elle ne peut pas monter la page de son jeu, et encore moins l’annoncer ou récolter des wishlists (les ajouts en liste de souhaits, qui aident un jeu à se faire remarquer à sa sortie).
Valve n’a reconnu qu’une partie du problème
Dans un billet publié le 3 novembre, l’équipe Steamworks reconnaît bien que le nombre de pages et de jeux à examiner a connu « une hausse importante » ces derniers mois. Elle y explique que l’examen d’une version de jeu peut prendre jusqu’à 12 jours ouvrés, alors qu’il en faut d’habitude trois à cinq.
Valve ne dit pas quels types de jeux sont en cause, mais on pense évidemment au flux très importants de jeux développés avec l’IA. La boutique de jeux indépendants itch.io, qui reçoit 6 000 nouvelles pages de jeux par jour, a fini par supprimer des téraoctets de contenus. Sur Steam, des joueurs ont aussi demandé à Valve un filtre pour repérer ces jeux pendant le Steam Next Fest.
Pour accélérer l’examen, Valve a ajouté de nouvelles étapes à la liste de vérification que les studios remplissent avant de soumettre un jeu. Ils doivent notamment le lancer depuis Steam et y jouer au moins cinq minutes : la firme explique avoir déjà examiné des versions qui n’avaient jamais tourné via son client. Valve promet d’autres améliorations de son processus d’examen.
En revanche, le billet de Valve ne dit rien de la vérification des comptes, l’étape où Bertine van Hövell attend 45 jours.

articles.title: Altersvorsorgedepot: Banken werben schon, der Staat lässt wohl auf sich warten
articles.text:
Altersvorsorgedepot: Banken legen los – doch der Staat verspätet sich
Während sich Banken und Versicherer schon eine Werbeschlacht um das neue Altersvorsorgedepot liefern, werden Verbraucher noch länger auf die staatliche Variante warten müssen. Eigentlich sieht die neue Form der staatlich geförderten privaten Altersvorsorge vor, dass nicht nur Broker und Banken das neue Produkt anbieten. Auch der Staat sollte ein Altersvorsorgedepot auflegen.
Wie das Redaktionsnetzwerk Deutschland (RND) berichtet, wird das staatliche Depot aber zum Start am 1. Januar nicht zur Verfügung stehen. Aus Regierungskreisen heißt es, mit der Einführung sei frühestens im Sommer 2027 zu rechnen. Grund für die Verzögerung ist, dass die Verordnung für das öffentlich organisierte Angebot länger dauert als gedacht.
Die Rechtsverordnung muss auch noch festlegen, welche Institution das Angebot verwalten soll. Im Gespräch sind unter anderem Bundesbank, KfW und Deutsche Rentenversicherung. Das Gesetz zum Altersvorsorgedepot ist seit Ende Mai in Kraft.
Das Altersvorsorgedepot ist der Nachfolger der Riester-Rente und soll es den Deutschen leichter machen, breit gestreut am Kapitalmarkt fürs Alter zu sparen. Dafür gibt es staatliche Zuschüsse von bis zu 540 Euro pro Jahr sowie zusätzlich 300 Euro jährlich je kindergeldberechtigtem Kind. Anlegen können Sparer:innen in ETFs, Aktienfonds und Anleihen.
Das vom Staat bereitgestellte Produkt ist dabei als Benchmark gedacht, um die Kosten im Zaum zu halten. Es soll Sparer:innen jährlich nur 0,2 Prozent der Anlagesumme kosten. Außerdem kann es als Maßstab dienen, um die Konditionen von Banken und Versicherern vergleichen zu können.
Werbeschlacht ums Altersvorsorgedepot
Schon jetzt locken viele Banken, Versicherer und Broker mit Angeboten für den Riester-Nachfolger, die sie frei gestalten können. Für sie alle gilt allerdings: Wer ein Altersvorsorgedepot auflegt, muss auch ein Standarddepot im Angebot haben, dessen Kosten bei einem Prozent Effektivkosten im Jahr gedeckelt sind.
Im Wettbewerb zeichnen sich zum Start allerdings deutlich geringere Kosten ab. Teils bieten Banken und Broker das Standarddepot unter bestimmten Bedingungen fast kostenlos an. Verbraucherschützer sehen den entstehenden Angebotsdschungel und die aggressive Werbung für das Altersvorsorgedepot allerdings kritisch. Denn Anbieter könnten zwar jetzt mit günstigen Konditionen um Kund:innen werben, die Gebühren aber mit der Zeit nach oben schrauben.
Die Verbraucherzentrale Baden-Württemberg kritisierte daher zuletzt den Verordnungsentwurf des Bundesfinanzministeriums, der regelt, welche Kosten und Informationen die Anbieter beim Altersvorsorgedepot offenlegen müssen. Der soll eigentlich dafür sorgen, dass Sparer:innen die Angebote besser durchschauen und vergleichen können.
Laut den Verbraucherschützer:innen werden die Kosten aber weiterhin nicht vollständig ausgewiesen. Auch wie stark Entgelte die Rendite schmälern, sei für Verbraucher:innen undurchsichtig. Damit blieben Probleme bestehen, die schon von der Riester-Rente bekannt sind. Lösen lässt sich das aus Sicht der Verbraucherschützer:innen erst, wenn ein öffentlicher Träger ein Standarddepot ohne Vertriebsinteresse anbietet.
Bis dahin hätten Verbraucher:innen keine echte Alternative, die frei von Verkaufsanreizen, Kostenfallen und irreführenden Werbepraktiken ist. Ein erster Anbieter wurde von der Verbraucherzentrale bereits wegen irreführender Werbung erfolgreich abgemahnt.

articles.title: El gran fraude de la canela: Bruselas dice que dos tercios de la que se comercializa en Europa tiene problemas
articles.text:
La canela fue la quinta especia más importada por la UE en 2023. También ha sufrido un control de laboratorio. Los laboratorios de Europa han puesto a prueba a esta especia. El Centro Común de Investigación (JRC) ha analizado 104 productos de venta. De ellos, un 66,3 % tenían algún problema.
Entre ellos se detectaron problemas de calidad o incumplimientos de seguridad alimentaria. En algunos se sospechaba de fraude y en otros había un posible riesgo asociado a su contenido en cumarina. Sin embargo, esto no quiere decir que dos tercios de la canela que se comercializa en Europa tenga estos problemas.
Los problemas pueden ser muy diversos. Desde los que implican un incumplimiento de los estándares internacionales de calidad hasta posibles sospechas de adulteración o dudas en cuanto a la seguridad alimentaria. Esto último no implica que haya un fraude demostrado o que sean necesariamente peligrosos para el consumidor.
Ya se habían dado casos preocupantes. En el año 2021 se publicó un informe europeo donde se detectaron indicios de adulteración en algunas especias. Así ocurrió con pimienta, comino, cúrcuma, azafrán o pimentón. En el caso de la canela, la Comisión ha hecho públicos los resultados el 24 de septiembre de 2025. Las muestras fueron adquiridas en 10 países de la UE.
Lo que decía la etiqueta y lo que había dentro
Entre los problemas destacan los casos con exceso de plomo. Otro caso es el de muestras con altos niveles de cumarina. Se trata de un componente natural de la canela cassia, algo que puede llegar a ser tóxico para el hígado. En la legislación europea se regula el máximo admisible de cumarina en ciertos productos elaborados, pero no hay un valor concreto para la que viene de forma natural en la canela. El estudio apunta a posibles riesgos asociados al consumo. En especial para niños.
Por otro lado, también se encontraron discrepancias entre las declaraciones de la etiqueta y el propio producto. Alrededor del 9 % de las muestras que se anunciaban como canela de Ceilán tenían cassia (total o parcialmente). Se trata de una variedad más barata y con un sabor más fuerte. Es decir, se puede estar comprando una cosa y en realidad tener otra diferente (sin saberlo).
Para detectar este tipo de sustituciones (y otros problemas) es necesaria más que una sola técnica analítica. El JRC avisa de que es necesario disponer de métodos estandarizados en los laboratorios de control. La Comisión hace un llamamiento a los responsables políticos y fabricantes. Es necesario asegurar que la especia es auténtica (y cumple con la legislación en materia de seguridad alimentaria) y de calidad.

articles.title: Avant de taper votre code de carte bancaire, attention au skimming, une arnaque redoutable qui sévit en France
articles.text:
Plusieurs cas de skimming ont été repérés en France, tout savoir sur cette arnaque redoutable
Si vous utilisez votre carte bancaire dans une station-service ou un distributeur de billets, la prudence est de mise alors que plusieurs cas de skimming ont été relevés en France ces derniers temps.
Si la technologie nous a appris à être spécialement méfiants en ligne, prêts à repérer les tentatives d'arnaques par email, SMS ou même au téléphone, le monde physique n'est pas à l'abri des personnes malintentionnées. Si le phénomène n'est assurément pas nouveau, une vague de skimming semble actuellement toucher la France ces derniers mois. Derrière cet anglicisme se cache une arnaque sophistiquée complexe à repérer et dangereuse, car elle en veut aux données de votre carte bancaire.
Le skimming, une arnaque sophistiquée et difficile à détecter
Surtout focalisée sur les stations-service et les distributeurs de billets, cette arnaque physique permet d'intercepter les données qui se trouvent sur la puce de la carte, mais aussi le code confidentiel de celle-ci. Pour cela, les pirates installent un dispositif caché au niveau du lecteur de carte, ainsi qu'un faux pavé numérique ou une caméra cachée au-dessus de ce dernier.
Ainsi, des personnes délivrent à leur insu toutes les informations nécessaires pour qu'un pirate vide ensuite leurs comptes. C'est ce qui est arrivé il y a quelques jours à des automobilistes dans une station-service en Alsace.
Les bonnes pratiques pour se protéger
Pour éviter de livrer ses données aux pirates à cause du skimming, plusieurs méthodes permettent de limiter les risques. Lors du paiement, contrôler qu'aucun dispositif additionnel (caméra, élément dans le lecteur de carte, pavé numérique suspect...) n'est présent sur le matériel habituel est un bon réflexe. Payer en sans-contact, donc sans renseigner son code, est également préférable.
De plus, bien cacher son code avec sa main au moment de le rentrer peut aider, et s'il est demandé de le renseigner plusieurs fois il s'agit probablement de skimming. En cas de doute après coup, consulter régulièrement son compte en banque en quête d'éventuels achats suspects peut permettre de rapidement limiter la casse.

articles.title: Cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne : des données personnelles ont été volées, des hackers chinois sont suspectés
articles.text:
La cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne s’est bien soldée par une fuite de données. Ce lundi 23 novembre, l’exécutif a reconnu que l’EU Academy, une plateforme en ligne qui propose des formations et des ateliers conçus par les institutions de l’Union, a subi une fuite de données personnelles. Cité par Reuters, Thomas Regnier, porte-parole de la Commission pour les questions numériques, indique que « la plateforme EU Academy a été affectée par la campagne de cyberattaques détectée contre la Commission », qui a abouti à une « fuite de données personnelles des utilisateurs ». Toutes les victimes ont été informées « aujourd’hui via le site de l’EU Academy ».
À lire aussi : Piratage de frigos de supermarchés – une opération secrète a évité une catastrophe au Royaume-Uni
Quelles données ont été compromises ?
Parmi les données compromises, on trouve les noms et les adresses e-mail des utilisateurs. Sans surprise, Bruxelles met en garde toutes les personnes concernées contre d’éventuelles campagnes de phishing. En effet, des pirates pourraient se servir des informations subtilisées pour envoyer des e-mails piégés et crédibles. Dos au mur, la Commission a mis la plateforme hors ligne jusqu’à nouvel ordre.
« L’incident fait toujours l’objet d’une enquête. L’accès public à la plateforme a été désactivé », indique le site de l’EU Academy.
Pour rappel, plusieurs autres applications internes ont été coupées par précaution. Certaines de ces applications internes sont encore et toujours indisponibles. Détectée le 22 octobre, la cyberattaque n’a toujours pas été entièrement maîtrisée un mois plus tard.
« Panda », la piste chinoise
Officiellement, la Commission européenne refuse de pointer du doigt un coupable. « En ce qui concerne l’attribution, il faudrait que l’enquête soit terminée pour savoir qui est derrière tout ça. Donc, pour l’instant, pas d’attribution de notre côté », a expliqué Thomas Regnier. En interne, les soupçons de Bruxelles se portent sur la Chine. D’après deux sources citées par Euronews, la Commission soupçonne fortement un réseau de pirates soutenu par la Chine. Le gang est connu sous le nom de Panda.
Selon les investigations menées par la Commission européenne, la cyberattaque reposait sur ARTEX, un outil qui s’appuie sur l’IA pour repérer les failles exploitables dans du code informatique. Sujet d’une alerte du FBI, cet outil est de plus en plus exploité dans le cadre de cyberattaques autonomes. Microsoft et CrowdStrike ont remarqué que le logiciel, qui peut être branché sur des modèles d’IA, est impliqué dans des campagnes d’espionnage visant des centaines d’organisations dans le monde. Storm-0940 et Panda Vapor font partie des nombreux gangs chinois à se servir d’ARTEX. Selon l’enquête en cours, les pirates ne visaient pas de systèmes ou de personnes bien précis. Les hackers voulaient plutôt voir jusqu’où ils pouvaient pénétrer les réseaux de la Commission. Il s’agissait donc vraisemblablement d’un test.
Une année noire pour la cybersécurité de la Commission
C’est déjà la troisième cyberattaque contre la Commission européenne survenue cette année. En janvier dernier, l’infrastructure mobile de l’institution a déjà été compromise. Deux mois plus tard, c’est l’infrastructure cloud, qui héberge le site Europa.eu, qui a été piratée. En coulisses, les deux attaques sont également attribuées à la Chine, mais à des groupes criminels différents.

articles.title: Jensen Huang regresa a Nvidia entre aplausos, ovaciones y abrazos de los empleados
articles.text:
Jensen Huang volvió a pisar las oficinas de Nvidia, apenas once días después de haber dimitido en medio de un escándalo de espionaje. Los empleados lo recibieron entre aplausos, abrazos y ovaciones en la sede de Santa Clara, California.
A pesar de su retorno a la compañía, la investigación por el posible caso de espionaje sigue en curso. Sin embargo, esta noticia le permitió a la compañía subir el valor de sus acciones en más de un 30%, sumando cerca de un billón de dólares en capitalización.
Cómo el recibimiento de Jensen Huang en Nvidia
El fundador de Nvidia ingresó a la sede central entre el entusiasmo del personal, que lo recibió con aplausos tras su breve ausencia. Ante los empleados, Huang bromeó sobre su regreso con un comentario que resume el tono informal de la jornada: “Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo”.
El directivo agregó, con humor, que no contaba con herramientas de trabajo: “No tengo ordenador, así que el departamento de informática me va a dar uno nuevo”. Más allá de las bromas, Huang dejó una frase que funcionó como balance de la crisis que acababa de atravesar: “Voy a ser un mejor CEO la segunda vez”.
La readmisión se produjo tras la aprobación formal de la junta directiva de Nvidia, que convirtió el regreso en un hecho oficial antes de que Huang volviera a cruzar la puerta de la empresa que fundó.
Once días que sacudieron a Nvidia
La salida de Huang se había producido el 12 de noviembre, cuando renunció a todos sus cargos en la compañía después de que trascendiera que mantenía una relación extramatrimonial con Alice Huang, una empresaria tecnológica china señalada por los servicios de inteligencia de Estados Unidos como una presunta espía de Pekín.
El escándalo no se limitó a ese vínculo. Huang también había mantenido relaciones con dos empleadas de la compañía que lideraba, un dato que agravó la crisis interna y puso en duda su continuidad al frente del mayor fabricante de microprocesadores del mundo.
El episodio generó lo que se describió como un caos bursátil y expuso cuánto depende Nvidia de la figura de su fundador. Tras su dimisión, Colette Kress asumió las funciones ejecutivas de manera interina, un rol que Huang reconoció públicamente al agradecerle por sostener la operación durante su ausencia.
La relación con Alice Huang, en particular, instaló la sospecha de un riesgo de seguridad nacional para Estados Unidos, dado el perfil de la compañía como líder global en inteligencia artificial y la sensibilidad de su tecnología.
Cómo se dio su regreso a Nvidia
La reincorporación se definió tras una serie de reuniones entre Huang y el Consejo de Administración, en las que la empresa aseguró haber quedado satisfecha con su “franqueza y capacidad de liderar”. El organismo votó a favor de su regreso con efecto inmediato.
Harvey Jones, presidente del Consejo, explicó la decisión en un comunicado: “El Consejo de Administración considera que Jensen es la persona idónea para liderar Nvidia y que su reincorporación redunda en beneficio de nuestros accionistas, empleados, socios y clientes”.
Nvidia también precisó haber recibido información de altos funcionarios del gobierno de Estados Unidos, datos en los que basó su confianza de que el retorno de Huang no representa un riesgo para la seguridad nacional del país.
A diferencia del cargo que ocupaba antes de su salida, Huang regresó con un control institucional ampliado: vuelve como director ejecutivo, pero también como presidente y director de la junta de accionistas, una concentración de poder mayor a la que tenía previamente.
El propio Huang respondió a la decisión con un mensaje difundido por la empresa: “Es un honor para mí regresar a Nvidia y liderar una de las compañías tecnológicas más importantes del mundo al comienzo de una nueva revolución industrial”. Afirmó volver con “la mayor humildad y el compromiso renovado” y agradeció tanto a la junta directiva como a Kress por su gestión durante la interinidad.
“Estoy profundamente agradecido a nuestros empleados, accionistas, líderes de la industria y socios de todo el mundo por su extraordinario apoyo”, cerró Huang en el comunicado oficial.

articles.title: F1 racing as a model for digital twin excellence
articles.text:
F1 racing as a model for digital twin excellence
F1-inspired digital twins help organizations do more with limited resources
Formula 1 racing is an adrenaline-fueled contest of drivers, machines and split-second decisions. Behind the spectacle is an equally intense engineering competition built on data simulations, advanced modeling and constant testing.
Since racing teams can’t physically test every possible configuration, they use digital twin representations to explore design choices and performance scenarios.
Federal CTO at Intel.
This well-documented resource discipline helps F1 teams concentrate scarce engineering resources where they matter most; and it’s a discipline that’s also relevant far beyond motorsports.
Enterprises are being asked to extract more performance from aging IT infrastructure, constrained budgets and limited technical staff while managing increasingly complex operations.
Digital twins can be a lifeline for such companies, provided they heed some of the configuration lessons learned from how digital twins operate in the intense, five-nine’s precision environment of F1 racing.
The Hidden Discipline Behind the Spectacle
As with a high-performance racing vehicle, high-performance organizations operate under hard constraints: limited time, finite compute, fixed budgets and little tolerance for failure. These pressures appear on a factory floor, in a logistics network, inside a utility, or across a public-sector fleet.
In such environments, a digital twin becomes valuable because it provides a safer place to test these choices before committing them to the physical world. A manufacturer can model a production increase before rearranging equipment. A transit authority can test capacity changes before changing service patterns, while an aircraft operator can anticipate maintenance needs before an asset becomes unavailable.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The challenge is that digital twins can consume resources as quickly as they create insight. More components, more sensor feeds and more scenarios can drive up compute, engineering time and data-management demands. Organizations therefore need a strategic approach to managing digital twins that applies the same discipline seen in racing: put the deepest modeling where it can materially change performance, risk, cost or availability.
Strategic Priorities for Digital Twin Performance and Efficiency
F1 motorsports is an eye-catching use case for a strong digital-twin strategy that starts early and continues long after a product or system leaves the design environment. During concept development, engineers can evaluate assumptions and compare configurations virtually. During prototyping and testing, real measurements can feed back into the model, revealing where physical performance differs from what synthetic testing predicted.
The same twin should then continue into production as an evolving operational resource that becomes more useful as performance data exposes wear patterns, bottlenecks and unexpected behaviors. After delivery, it can continue supporting the customer in deployment and day-to-day operations to improve maintenance, optimize use and continually refine the model against real-world conditions.
Where and how to allocate compute resources is an operational priority throughout. Large simulations may fit cloud or data-center infrastructure during design, while test environments can benefit from analysis closer to equipment generating large data volumes. In remote plants, ships, field sites or public-safety settings, edge deployments can keep critical analytics available when bandwidth is limited or connectivity is intermittent.
Three Pro Tips to Get More Value From Digital Twins
The most useful digital twins combine detailed models of individual components with a broader view of the complete product, facility or operating environment. These three design principles can help organizations scale that approach without allowing simulation demands to outrun the business value they produce.
Use distributed models to put detail where it matters – A complex system may have separate twins for motors, cooling systems, production cells or other components, all of which feed a higher-level model. That lets teams apply deeper simulation selectively while preserving a system-wide view. Bidirectional feedback matters because a change that improves one component may create cost, energy or performance dependencies elsewhere.
Build business context and KPIs into the model – Cost, throughput, uptime, energy consumption, supportability, compliance and service levels can be just as important as core engineering metrics. Sensitivity analysis helps identify which variables are most likely to change an outcome, allowing scarce modeling resources to focus on assumptions that could alter an investment or operating decision.
Design the twin to live beyond the build – The digital twin model should travel with the asset into operations, where sensor data and operator observations can continuously update assumptions. That enables more accurate maintenance planning and gives operators a stronger basis for local decisions. It also sends real-world evidence back to OEM engineering teams, improving future designs and upgrades.
Together these principles ensure the digital twin remains a dynamic and economical framework for ongoing decision support. Consider a factory preparing for a major jump in orders; rather than simply adding labor or equipment, the operator can simulate higher loads, alter line configurations and identify where queues, cleaning cycles or material flows become constraints. The same logic can help an aircraft fleet run predictive maintenance, or a municipal facility examine water treatment, power delivery or physical access under different operating conditions.
Formula 1 racing provides a vivid illustration of digital twins as a driver of value in conditions where performance thresholds are exacting and the margins for error or competitive advantage are miniscule. The same disciplines honed under those punishing conditions of continuous modeling, targeted compute and constant real-world refinement can help organizations across industries operate more efficiently, anticipate problems earlier and push performance to a higher level.
