articles.title: Cómo cerrar desde el celular las sesiones de WhatsApp Web que quedaron abiertas en computadoras ajenas
articles.text:
Quien usó WhatsApp Web en la computadora de una oficina, un cibercafé o la casa de un familiar y no cerró la sesión puede hacerlo ahora desde su teléfono, sin volver a ese equipo. La opción está en la sección Dispositivos vinculados de la aplicación y no borra ningún chat.
WhatsApp permite vincular hasta cuatro dispositivos a una misma cuenta, además del teléfono principal, según su Centro de ayuda. Entre ellos hay navegadores con WhatsApp Web, las aplicaciones para Windows y Mac, tablets Android y otros teléfonos. Todos aparecen en una sola lista.
El Centro de ayuda recomienda revisar esa lista con regularidad. Cada dispositivo funciona de forma independiente, por lo que una computadora olvidada puede seguir conectada aunque el teléfono esté apagado o sin internet. Por eso conviene mirar la lista y no suponer que un equipo viejo perdió el acceso.
La propia empresa indica que desconecta de forma automática los dispositivos vinculados tras 30 días de inactividad. Hasta que se cumpla ese plazo, una sesión abierta en un equipo ajeno puede seguir activa.
Pasos para cerrar la sesión desde el teléfono
En Android, hay que abrir WhatsApp y tocar los tres puntos de la esquina superior derecha. Después se elige Dispositivos vinculados, se toca el navegador o la computadora que se quiere desconectar y se pulsa Cerrar sesión. Según la ayuda de WhatsApp Business, en algunos casos hay que confirmar.
En el iPhone, la ruta empieza en Ajustes, en la parte inferior de la pantalla, o en la foto de perfil. Allí se entra en Dispositivos vinculados, se toca el equipo y se elige Cerrar sesión, con una segunda confirmación. Los pasos coinciden en la página de WhatsApp Business y en la guía del portal Gadgets Now, del grupo Times of India.
Si hay varios equipos desconocidos, el procedimiento se repite con cada uno. No hace falta cerrar todos: basta con quitar los que no se reconocen o ya no se usan. Cerrar la sesión de un dispositivo vinculado no elimina chats, fotos ni documentos del teléfono principal, según Gadgets Now.
Cómo evitar que el problema se repita
Si el usuario todavía está frente a la computadora, puede salir desde WhatsApp Web o la aplicación de escritorio: se abre Ajustes y se elige Cerrar sesión. Cerrar la pestaña o el navegador no siempre desconecta la cuenta, advirtió Gadgets Now, porque la sesión puede seguir vinculada.
En equipos compartidos o públicos, se recomienda desmarcar la casilla “Mantener sesión iniciada en este navegador” antes de escanear el código QR. La sesión se cierra sola al terminar de usar el navegador. Tampoco conviene guardar contraseñas ni descargas en la máquina.
Las notificaciones del teléfono también colaboran. La ayuda de WhatsApp Business indica que, con ellas activadas, el usuario puede tocar el aviso de un dispositivo que no reconoce para revisarlo y quitarlo. WhatsApp pide, además, vincular equipos solo desde sus canales oficiales y advierte que las versiones no oficiales de la aplicación pueden comprometer la cuenta.
Para vincular un dispositivo nuevo, WhatsApp pide que el usuario inicie sesión en su teléfono principal al menos cada 14 días, según la página oficial sobre cómo vincular un dispositivo. Esa misma página indica que, ante un equipo no reconocido durante la vinculación, la aplicación pide confirmar con la opción de no vincular.

articles.title: A Link Is Not Architecture: Why Multi-Die Systems Need More Than Die-to-Die Connectivity
articles.text:
Maintaining consistent communication behavior, integration, and security across configurations.
The system-on-chip (SoC) transformed semiconductor design by bringing the major functions of an electronic system onto one die, an integration that shaped chip architecture for years. Multi-die design is now changing the model again, distributing system functionality across multiple dies within a single package.
While this approach gives engineers greater flexibility to align semiconductor design with system requirements, bringing these designs to life takes more than a die-to-die link to transport transactions across the package. It requires a system architecture that manages how data moves between dies.
In AI and high-performance computing (HPC) systems, multi-die architectures enable teams to scale compute and select an appropriate process technology for each part of the design. These partitioning choices determine which transactions remain within a die and which must cross die boundaries. Treating each boundary independently increases integration and verification effort, complicates performance management, and reduces the practical value of chiplet reuse.
Still, managing communication across these die boundaries requires a clear separation between the physical interface that transports transactions and the system architecture that manages them. Extending the system’s data-movement architecture across die boundaries allows engineers to repartition or scale designs without rebuilding the entire communication architecture.
The die-to-die controller and PHY provide transport between dies: the controller handles protocol functions, while the PHY provides the electrical interface. The link does not automatically preserve the traffic management, quality of service (QoS), routing, address handling, and observability established by the network-on-chip (NoC). These functions remain part of the system architecture above the physical interface.
Getting transactions across a die boundary is only part of the challenge. Those transactions must also compete for shared bandwidth, often with different performance and latency requirements. QoS manages how bandwidth is allocated across die boundaries, preserving traffic priorities as the system architecture evolves.
In architectures that implement end-to-end QoS, service can be coordinated for each transaction along its route, from initiator to target. Arbitration and packet-level priorities determine which traffic advances when demand changes, while bandwidth controls regulate how much capacity each source can consume. Coordinating these mechanisms across the NoC ensures that each traffic class receives its configured service level, while the physical link is responsible for transport.
A multi-die package can carry coherent shared-memory traffic alongside non-coherent data and control flows. Coherent interconnects support data sharing across dies, while non-coherent interconnects serve paths that do not require shared-memory coherency. These different traffic requirements call for different interconnect capabilities, with Arteris addressing both coherent and non-coherent communication through its multi-die IP portfolio.
FlexGen Multi-Die smart interconnect IP provides non-coherent NoC connectivity for AI and HPC architectures. It extends NoC connectivity and QoS across chiplet boundaries, enabling traffic management across the multi-die system. FlexGen Multi-Die supports bidirectional transactions over a single UCIe PHY, reducing PHY area, power, and I/O requirements by up to 50 percent.
Ncore Multi-Die interconnect IP addresses cache-coherent compute architectures. It extends cache coherency and data sharing across dies, enabling software to see the multi-die assembly as a single piece of silicon.
Magillem integration automation supports IP, chiplet, and hardware-software integration as the number of components and interfaces increases. This reduces the engineering effort and complexity associated with assembling a growing set of reusable components.
As a multi-die system adds interfaces between dies, the number of trust boundaries increases. Security assurance must therefore extend beyond individual dies to cover the interfaces and trust boundaries.
Cycuity hardware security assurance helps teams uncover vulnerabilities, identify weaknesses, and verify security requirements.
Bringing these capabilities together requires coordination across the multi-die system. As chiplet configurations evolve, engineers must manage a changing combination of components and interfaces while maintaining the system’s communication, integration, and security requirements.
These products operate within a broader ecosystem because no single layer defines the complete multi-die stack. Arteris focuses on interconnect, data movement, integration, and assurance while engineering teams select the controller, PHY, package, and surrounding tools for their design. Standards-aligned integration helps preserve those technology choices, while co-optimization balances system performance and power. As controller, PHY, packaging, and tool roadmaps change, engineers must evaluate how those changes affect the complete design.
The next phase of multi-die design will depend on preserving system intent across all physical partitions. As chiplet combinations and interface technologies evolve, engineers must maintain consistent communication behavior, integration, and security across configurations. The goal is to give designers the freedom to partition systems according to their requirements without having to rethink the entire architecture each time the physical implementation changes.

articles.title: Social media platforms could face billions of dollars in fines after Australian Government passes Digital Duty of Care bill
articles.text:
The Australian Federal Government is about to pass Digital Duty of Care legislation that could see social media platforms find billions of dollars if users are found to be harmed online.
Labour, with support from the Greens, this week agreed on the final structure of the bill which will see it get through the Parliament in the last sitting session of the year.
The Liberal-National Coalition has opposed to the bill and raised concerns about freedom of speech.
The bill is designed to protect users if they feel they have been harmed by harrowing and harmful content on online.
Australians will also be able to launch legal actions against these big tech companies if they feel they have been harmed.
Tech companies could be subjected to fines of up to $109 million or five per cent of global revenue if they break the rules.
Last year Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, earned more than $200 billion and if found guilty in a Digital Duty of Care claim could be forced to pay an estimated $10 billion.
The bill has already drawn criticism from the Trump administration which expressed “serious concerns” saying it was a threat to free speech.
“Preserving a free open internet and protecting freedom of expression online are top priorities for the Trump administration,” the US Embassy said.
This move comes almost a year after the under-16 social media ban, which was designed to shield younger users from potentially harmful online content.
The Digital Duty of Care Bill will also provide control for users over their algorithm.
“Big tech has a choice now: work to make your platform safer. Work with parents to be able to make the engagement online with their kids safer,” Greens communication spokeswoman Sarah Hanson-Young told ABC News.
Under the Digital Duty of Care Bill there have been several amendments, including allowing users over 16 to opt out of algorithms.
Bill also gives the eSafety Commissioner unprecedented power to issue removal notices on what it considers to be adult content.
The bill will also establish an independent ombudsman to give users a course of action to help resolve issues with these big tech companies and social media platforms.
As it stands, individuals who want to take on the social media platforms we’ll have to navigate a long and complex path under the existing consumer protection laws.
The Digital Duty of Care Bill will streamline that process with the aim of assisting users who feel they have been harmed.
At the same time it is also being designed to put the big social media companies on notice and to make the necessary changes to their platforms and rethink their approach to the content they are sharing.

articles.title: China se hizo un hueco regalando sus modelos de IA. Para competir con OpenAI y Anthropic, Z.ai lanza GLM-5.4 primero de pago
articles.text:
En cuestión de laboratorios de IA, hay actualmente dos estilos principales: los que acostumbran a liberar los pesos y aquellos que prefieren mantenerlos cerrados y cobrar por usarlos. La tendencia había colocado a los laboratorios chinos del lado abierto y a los estadounidenses en la acera contraria, aunque poco a poco las líneas se juntan. Z.ai es la prueba.
Nuevo modelo insignia: GLM-5.4. Si el anterior ya era bueno en tareas como la programación, la empresa ajusta esas capacidades con un cambio de arquitectura que apunta a la eficiencia. Según Z.ai, GLM-5.4 es su primer modelo insignia con arquitectura Loop Transformer.
Según la empresa, GLM-5.4 rinde como modelos de entre 2 y 3 billones de parámetros, aunque de momento no ha presentado los benchmarks. Ofrece hasta 200 tokens por segundo fuera de las horas punta (entre 70 y 80 cuando hay más carga), admite hasta un millón de tokens de contexto, incluye modo de razonamiento y suma visión a su especialidad, la programación.
Como pegas, la propia Z.ai reconoce que el nuevo modelo tiende a enredarse en razonamientos demasiado largos. Y las primeras pruebas independientes apuntan hacia esa misma dirección: en KingBench 4 tardó 431 minutos frente a los 109 de Gemini 4 Neon. GLM-5.4 gastó unas 15 veces más tokens.
No hay pesos abiertos ni fecha para ellos. El anuncio del nuevo modelo nos deja por escrito las capacidades y la posibilidad de probarlo en las suscripciones que Z.ai ofrece a los usuarios: actualmente está en todos los planes de GLM Coding Plan. La API aún no está disponible. Y no lo estará hasta que finalice la evaluación de seguridad.
Con la presentación de GLM-5.3, Z.ai prometió publicar los pesos dos semanas después, algo que terminó cumpliendo con ciertos matices: dejó atrás la licencia MIT para exigir una revisión de seguridad a los proveedores que facturen más de 10.000 millones de dólares. Con GLM-5.4 la empresa dice que publicará los pesos cuando complete el endurecimiento de seguridad, un paso que investigadores chinos proponen convertir en norma para todos los modelos abiertos. Z.ai no ha marcado fecha alguna.
Para competir hay que restringir. Los laboratorios chinos usaban sus modelos open source para captar la atención, pero seguían cobrando por la inferencia a través de suscripciones y APIs. Con GLM-5.1, Z.ai ya empezó a subir precios. Ahora aprovecha que su GLM ya es de sobra conocido y valorado para ponerle un peaje a lo Anthropic u OpenAI, con la seguridad como argumento oficial. ¿Quieres usarlo? Paga.
Dos velocidades. Z.ai no cierra por completo la puerta: con GLM-5.3-Flash demostró que puede liberar modelos "pequeños" con pesos abiertos desde el primer día. En Estados Unidos, Nvidia, Microsoft y compañía defienden los pesos abiertos como el futuro de la IA, así que las líneas se juntan desde las dos aceras. El problema es para quien eligió GLM precisamente porque podía descargarlo. Como Revolut, que puso a 2.000 ingenieros a programar con GLM-5.3 ejecutándolo en sus propios servidores.
GLM-5.4 no podrá ejecutarse en local, al menos de momento: o pagar por la suscripción de Z.ai o esperar a la liberación del modelo sin que haya fecha para que eso ocurra. Y la compañía ya avisa de que su próxima iteración, “significativamente más grande”, estará lista pronto. La duda es si llegará con pesos o con peaje.

En Xataka | Entre expandir sus modelos de IA por todo el mundo o protegerlos, China tiene muy clara su decisión

articles.title: AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
articles.text:
AI-powered bionic eye breakthrough could help the blind see again
Using AI to make bionic vision smarter and more precise, scientists are bringing the possibility of restoring sight to people with blindness one step closer to reality.
- Date:
  November 12, 2026
- Source:
  University of California - Santa Barbara
- Summary:
  Scientists have developed an AI-powered approach that makes experimental bionic vision technology more precise, helping predict the flashes and shapes of light perceived by a blind man with a brain implant. By learning how an individual's brain responds to electrical stimulation, the technology could bring researchers closer to restoring some degree of sight to people with blindness.
- Share:
Artificial intelligence could help overcome one of the biggest challenges in restoring vision to people who are blind: getting a brain implant to produce reliable visual experiences. Researchers from three institutions, including UC Santa Barbara, have demonstrated that AI can improve how precisely an experimental visual prosthesis stimulates the brain and predicts what a person perceives.
The team used a deep learning system to develop electrical stimulation patterns for electrodes temporarily implanted in the visual cortex, the region at the back of the brain responsible for processing visual information. By analyzing the brain's responses, the technology gave researchers greater control over neural activity and helped them better anticipate the visual sensations produced by the implant.
Published online in the journal Neuron, the proof-of-concept study represents progress toward more advanced visual prostheses, sometimes described as bionic eyes. These devices could eventually become more effective by learning how each person's brain responds to stimulation rather than relying on predetermined settings.
"Building a model in the abstract is one thing," said Michael Beyeler, an associate professor of computer science and psychological and brain sciences at UC Santa Barbara. "Seeing it shape an experiment with a person is something else entirely. That ability to go from theory to something that may one day help people is what drives much of the work in our lab."
How Bionic Vision Could Bypass Damaged Eyes
For decades, scientists have worked to develop technologies capable of restoring some vision to people who are blind, although the results have generally been limited. Some experimental devices stimulate the retina, the layer of tissue at the back of the eye that detects light. Others attempt to activate parts of the visual system farther along the pathway that carries visual information to the brain.
Visual cortical prostheses work differently. Instead of depending on the eyes or optic nerves, they deliver electrical signals directly to the visual cortex. This approach could offer a potential solution for people whose visual pathways have been damaged but whose visual cortex can still respond to stimulation. Possible candidates include individuals who lost their sight because of strokes, neurodegenerative diseases, or traumatic brain injuries.
The ability to regain even limited vision could be especially meaningful for people who remember what it was like to see.
Beyeler highlighted those "who have been able to see for part of their life, but then, because of an inherited eye disease or an accident, have lost their vision," adding, "For those people, the desire may be very strong to get some vision back."
The new findings build on earlier computational research supported by Beyeler's 2022 National Institutes of Health (NIH) Director's New Innovator Award. The five-year, $2 million grant has supported his efforts to make artificial vision systems more accurate, predictable, and effective.
Scientists Test AI With a Brain Implant in a Blind Man
An important opportunity to test the technology came in 2024, when researchers from Beyeler's Bionic Vision Lab traveled to Spain. Their goal was to determine whether their computer models could improve the performance of a brain implant already being used in an experimental study.
At Hospital IMED Elche, the team worked with a 27-year-old man who had become blind following a traumatic brain injury. He had received an implant containing 96 electrodes arranged in an array within his visual cortex. The device was intended to remain in place for six months before being removed.
When researchers activated the electrodes using electrical current, the participant experienced visual sensations known as phosphenes. These can appear as spots, flashes, or shapes of light, sometimes resembling stars or fireworks.
Producing these sensations is possible, but making them consistent and predictable is much more difficult. The same electrical stimulation does not always trigger an identical response, and activating particular electrodes does not guarantee that the person will perceive a specific visual pattern.
To address this problem, the researchers trained a deep neural network, a type of AI designed to recognize complex patterns, to predict how the visual cortex would respond to different electrical stimulation settings. The model also considered the brain's resting activity immediately before stimulation, giving it information about the participant's current neural state.
Using these predictions, the researchers identified combinations of electrical signals that were most likely to produce particular patterns of brain activity.
AI Makes Bionic Vision More Precise
When the scientists tested the stimulation patterns selected by AI, the results were encouraging. The new approach generated the intended patterns of neural activity more accurately than the comparison methods while requiring less electrical current.
Another important discovery emerged when the team examined the relationship between brain activity and the participant's visual experiences. The patterns recorded directly from his brain were better predictors of what he perceived than the stimulation settings themselves.
This distinction matters because activating the brain is not the same as knowing what a person will see. Even when researchers can produce a desired neural response, they still need to understand how the brain transforms that activity into a conscious visual experience.
"Engineers naturally want to treat phosphenes like pixels: stimulate more electrodes, and you should get a more complete image," Beyeler said. "But the brain does not work that way. Electrodes interact, neural responses fluctuate, and what we put into the brain is not necessarily what the person perceives. The challenge is to learn more about that transformation."
The findings suggest that future visual prostheses may need to do more than simply deliver electrical signals. They may also need to monitor how the brain reacts and use that feedback to continually improve stimulation.
Teaching Brain Implants to Adapt to Each Person
A key advantage of the implant used in the experiment was its ability to perform two tasks. It could stimulate the visual cortex with electrical current while simultaneously recording the resulting neural activity.
This allowed researchers to train their AI model using the brain's actual responses rather than relying exclusively on information about which electrodes were activated and how much current they delivered.
The participant also provided feedback about what he experienced. He reported whether he saw a phosphene and, during certain experiments, described its appearance, including its shape, size, brightness, and color.
Comparing these reports with the recorded brain activity revealed that neural responses contained more useful information about the perceived visual sensations than the electrical stimulation parameters alone.
The AI system also used measurements of resting brain activity to account for changes in the participant's neural state before each stimulation. This could be particularly valuable because the brain's response to electrical signals can vary over time, including from one day to the next.
By adapting stimulation to these changing conditions, future prostheses might provide more consistent visual experiences without requiring users to adjust to a rigid set of signals.
"A useful visual prosthesis cannot rely on a fixed recipe," Beyeler said. "It has to learn how an individual brain responds and adapt the stimulation accordingly. Ultimately, the device should adapt to the person, not the other way around."
A Collaborative Step Toward Restoring Sight
The research brought together scientists from UC Santa Barbara, ETH Zurich, and Miguel Hernández University (MHU). Beyeler described the effort as "a true collaboration."
The project was led by co-first authors Pehuén Moure of ETH Zurich, Jacob Granley of UC Santa Barbara, and Fabrizio Grani of MHU. The supervising researchers were Beyeler, Shih-Chii Liu of ETH Zurich, and Eduardo Fernández of MHU. Their work forms part of a larger feasibility trial taking place in Spain.
Although the technology remains experimental and the participant's visual experiences were limited to flashes and shapes of light, the results demonstrate how AI could improve communication between artificial vision devices and the brain.
Rather than treating every brain as if it responds the same way, future bionic vision systems could learn from each individual and adjust their signals accordingly. That personalized approach may prove essential to developing implants that can eventually restore useful vision to people who have lost their sight.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of California - Santa Barbara. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Pehuén Moure, Jacob Granley, Fabrizio Grani, Leili Soo, Antonio Lozano, Rocío López-Peco, Adrián Villamarín-Ortiz, Cristina Soto-Sánchez, Shih-Chii Liu, Michael Beyeler, Eduardo Fernández. Deep learning-based control of electrically evoked activity in human visual cortex. Neuron, 2026; DOI: 10.1016/j.neuron.2026.07.006

articles.title: Anthropic Expands Enterprise Safeguards for Detecting AI Misuse
articles.text:
Anthropic on Monday announced the public beta of Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS), a system designed to help organizations detect malicious use of AI.
Unveiled in September, EFS has been developed with input from over 100 Anthropic customers, with companies such as Stripe and Salesforce evaluating it in private beta. A quarter of Fortune 100 companies helped develop EFS.
According to Anthropic, existing Claude protections can identify potentially harmful requests made individually, but EFS adds a monitoring layer that can detect suspicious patterns across multiple requests that may appear benign when analyzed individually.
The system targets organizations that use Claude under zero data retention agreements and have so far relied only on classifiers that analyze each request in isolation.
EFS is designed to detect both deliberate misuse of AI, such as AI-powered cyberattacks, and incidents where AI agents go beyond what their operator intended, such as the cases where agents exploited vulnerabilities to gain access to real-world systems.
With EFS, organizations store conversation data in their own cloud and protect it with their own encryption keys and access policies.
Neither Anthropic nor its cloud providers retain copies of the conversation data after it’s transferred to the customer’s storage. Anthropic receives monitoring metadata, but not the content of conversations.
Security teams are provided reports on potentially harmful activity, which can be ingested via SIEM solutions. EFS is currently available via the Claude Platform, AWS, and Google Cloud, with Microsoft Foundry integration in the works.
Guide to securing enterprise coding agents
Anthropic on Monday also published a guide to securing enterprise coding agents, with a focus on risks associated with privilege abuse, credential exposure, risky dependencies, prompt injection, and data exfiltration.
Citing previously published testing results, the company said mechanisms designed to detect prompt injection reduced attack success rates from 90% to 28% on Fable 5.2 and from 55% to 11% on Opus 5.5.
Anthropic also highlighted the effectiveness of its auto mode classifier, which evaluates proposed actions against user intent.
In tests conducted this summer, auto mode, which is now enabled by default for interactive Claude Code sessions, blocked 89% of dangerous commands, compared to only 14% in the case of human reviewers.
However, Anthropic recommends requiring human approval for high-risk actions and enforcing additional controls, such as sandboxing and network access restrictions.
Related: Anthropic Rolls Out Mythos 5.2 With Improved Bug Hunting, Fewer Sandbox Escapes

articles.title: Amazon's Decart acquisition is a bet on using software to narrow the silicon gap with Nvidia
articles.text:
Jensen Huang’s comeback as Nvidia’s CEO is understandably making waves, leaving people wondering about the longer-term implications of his quick reinstatement and the U.S. government’s active role in his return. But there was another development yesterday that could also matter for Nvidia down the road: Amazon’s decision to acquire Decart‘s tech and its team for a reported $7.5 billion.
The broader industry seems to agree that Decart’s tech for optimizing AI models to run on non-Nvidia chips is worth several billion dollars. Anthropic reportedly tried to acquire the startup in the same ballpark, and Nvidia, which invested in the startup’s $300 million funding round at a $4 billion valuation, was also rumored as a prospective buyer.
Amazon was ultimately the one to pull the trigger and bring on board Decart’s co-founders Dean Leitersdorf, Orian Leitersdorf, and Moshe Shalev and their team, but the company is not interested in the world models they had been working on. At the heart of the deal is the startup’s tech that helps AI models run better on all kinds of chips.
By incorporating the startup’s Decart Optimization Stack (DOS), Amazon is now hoping to extract more performance out of its Trainium chips, as the company tries to turn AWS into a $1 trillion revenue business.
In its announcement, Amazon said it has worked with Decart since 2025 to optimize the Trainium chips. This deal is ostensibly aimed at accelerating that work, which could eventually result in the company offering its Trainium-based data centers, which Anthropic already uses, to more customers. Amazon has already been working to make Trainium easier to switch to.
One way Nvidia managed to leapfrog its competitors was by spending $6.9 billion to acquire Israeli chipmaker Mellanox, which eventually grew to become a core piece of its international manufacturing strategy. Amazon could well be following a similar path.
Annapurna Labs makes for a more interesting parallel than Mellanox, however, as the latter formed the basis of Amazon’s custom chip-designing unit following its 2015 acquisition. Add Intel into the mix, and this becomes a broader story. “Most of the hardware powering the AI wave was built in Israel. Annapurna; Mellanox; Habana Labs; etc…,” VC Eric Reiner observed on X a few months ago.
In an email to TechCrunch, Eze Vidra, co-founder and managing partner at Remagine Ventures, said the deal is “a strong signal for the Israeli deep-tech ecosystem, showing that specialized local talent continues to attract major global players.”
Amazon still has a ways to go before it can make a dent in Nvidia’s near-monopoly on AI chips, but the deal could help the e-commerce giant speed up its efforts. Dean Meyer, a partner at Sequoia who co-led the firm’s seed investment into Decart, said on X that the deal “will be looked back on as one of the most strategically important acquisitions in many, many years.”

articles.title: ¿A qué hora se estrena ‘Blade Runner 2099’ en Amazon Prime Video?
articles.text:
La nueva serie de Blade Runner 2099 por fin se estrena en todo el mundo para devolver a la mítica saga de ciencia ficción a su máximo esplendor. El filme original de Ridley Scott, que cumple ya casi 45 años, es una de las historias más legendarias del género. Tanto que en 2017 se estrenó una secuela, Blade Runner 2049, dirigida por Denis Villeneuve. Ahora, es turno de una tercera entrega, esta vez en forma de serie. Pero, ¿a qué hora y dónde se estrena Blade Runner 2099?
Cincuenta años después de los sucesos de la segunda película, Los Ángeles ha renacido, aunque no a manos de la humanidad. Cora, una fugitiva que intenta dejar de huir de una vez por todas, adopta una última identidad: la de Blade Runner. Obligada a asociarse con Olwen, una replicante a la que le quedan pocos días de vida, da caza a un fugitivo que oculta una verdad capaz de hacer colapsar su frágil ciudad.
En cuanto a dónde podrá verse, a diferencia de otros títulos, aquí no depende para nada del territorio. En Estados Unidos, España, Latinoamérica y en el resto del mundo, Blade Runner 2099 estará disponible únicamente en Amazon Prime Video. La plataforma de streaming alberga los derechos exclusivos del proyecto, que confían que sea uno de los mejores lanzamientos televisivos del año.
Hora de estreno de Blade Runner 2099
En cuanto a la hora de estreno de Blade Runner 2099, en Estados Unidos se emitirá el martes 24 de noviembre a las 21:00h E.T. En España y Latinoamérica, llegará a Amazon Prime Video en la conversión horaria de cada país:
- España: 3:00 h. del miércoles 25 de noviembre.
- México, Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, Costa Rica: 20:00 h.
- Perú, Colombia, Panamá, Ecuador: 21:00 h.
- Venezuela, Bolivia, República Dominicana, Puerto Rico: 22:00 h.
- Chile, Paraguay, Argentina, Brasil, Uruguay: 23:00 h.
Prueba Amazon Prime Video totalmente gratis durante 30 días y disfruta del catálogo completo de la plataforma sin límites. Solo con darte de alta tendrás acceso instantáneo a las mejores películas y series, además de envíos gratis en Amazon y otras ventajas.
A partir de ese momento, Amazon Prime Video estrenará simultáneamente los 8 episodios de Blade Runner 2099. Es decir, en lugar de optar por un estreno semanal, como con otros títulos, la compañía ha decidido lanzar toda la serie de golpe. Una manera de ofrecer a sus suscriptores la posibilidad de ver toda la historia del tirón y a su ritmo, sin tener que esperar siete largos días para ver cómo continúa.

articles.title: Notée 9/10 dans notre test, l’Apple Watch Series 12 passe à 399€ pour le Black Friday !
articles.text:
À quelques jours du Black Friday, fixé ce vendredi, Amazon retire déjà 50 € à la dernière montre connectée d’Apple, sortie en septembre. L’Apple Watch Series 12 GPS de 42 mm en bronze sombre passe à 399 € au lieu de 449 € : notre test, qui lui attribue 9/10, salue son suivi cardiaque sans décrochage, mais elle reste réservée aux possesseurs d’iPhone.
Présentée en septembre, l’Apple Watch Series 12 garde le boîtier de ses aînées, mais change ce qui se trouve dessous : une puce S11 et un capteur cardiaque entièrement revu. Le modèle GPS de 42 mm, en aluminium bronze sombre, est le plus léger de la gamme, à 31,5 g. Amazon l’affiche à 399 € au lieu de 449 €, son prix conseillé, soit 11 % de moins. Cette version sans connexion cellulaire s’adresse à ceux qui gardent leur iPhone sur eux et veulent un suivi santé et sport plus fiable.
L’Apple Watch Series 12 GPS de 42 mm en bronze sombre, notée 9/10 dans notre test, est proposée à 399 € au lieu de 449 € chez Amazon.
Pourquoi choisir l’Apple Watch Series 12 ?
- Un suivi cardiaque sans trous : Apple annonce un relevé toutes les cinq secondes, et notre test n’a relevé aucun décrochage en deux semaines de séances et de marches.
- Une montre enfin réactive : La puce S11 efface les petites latences de la Series 11 : un mail ou un message WhatsApp s’ouvre instantanément au poignet.
- Près de deux jours loin du chargeur : Annoncée pour 24 heures, elle a tenu près de deux journées dans notre test, deux nuits de sommeil comprises.
Des séances de sport aux nuits de sommeil, ce qu’elle change au poignet
Dans notre test de l’Apple Watch Series 12, le capteur cardiaque revu est la nouveauté qui se remarque le plus : les données se mettent à jour en continu, et le suivi ne lâche plus pendant les séances de fitness. Le nouveau Niveau de préparation, noté de 0 à 10, croise activité, charge d’entraînement, sommeil et variabilité cardiaque pour vous dire quand forcer ou lever le pied. Au quotidien, watchOS 27 remplace la grille d’applications par un menu de six apps choisies selon vos habitudes, que nous avons trouvé pertinent. L’écran toujours allumé descend à 1 nit dans le noir, pour ne pas vous éblouir au réveil.
Elle vise d’abord le possesseur d’iPhone dont l’Apple Watch commence à dater, agacé par les pertes de signal cardiaque pendant ses marches ou ses séances. Le boîtier de 42 mm convient à ceux qui préfèrent une montre discrète, y compris pour dormir avec. Si vous portez déjà une Series 10 ou 11, notre test estime que vous pouvez prendre votre temps : le score de préparation ne justifie pas à lui seul de repasser à la caisse. Sous Android, enfin, elle ne fonctionnera pas : elle demande un iPhone 11 ou plus récent.
Face à la Series 11 et aux montres Android, où elle se situe
Dans notre comparatif des meilleures montres connectées, la Series 12 prend la deuxième place et le titre de meilleure montre pour iPhone, derrière la Samsung Galaxy Watch 8, notre premier choix sous Android. Elle ne bouge ni sur le design ni sur l’écran, limité à 2 000 nits quand la Galaxy Watch 9 et la Huawei Watch GT 7 Pro en annoncent 3 000. Elle se démarque par la régularité de son suivi cardiaque et sa fluidité, tandis que l’Apple Watch SE 3, notre choix rapport qualité/prix, reste l’alternative pour découvrir l’écosystème à moindre coût.
✅ Les points forts
- Suivi cardiaque régulier, sans décrochage pendant notre test
- Puce S11 très réactive au quotidien
- Près de deux jours d’autonomie dans notre usage
- 80 % de batterie en environ 35 minutes mesurées
- Boîtier de 42 mm léger, à 31,5 g
❌ Les limites
- Réservée aux possesseurs d’iPhone
- Siri AI indisponible dans l’Union européenne, Workout Buddy absent en français
- Niveau de préparation encore peu explicatif
- Version GPS sans 5G pour courir sans l’iPhone
Le bronze sombre, nouveau coloris de cette génération, est celui qu’Amazon propose à 399 € en GPS 42 mm : vérifiez la taille et le bracelet avant de valider.
À 399 €, l’Apple Watch Series 12 perd 50 € avant même le Black Friday, sur une montre sortie il y a à peine deux mois. Elle ne bouscule pas la formule, mais corrige ce qui agaçait sur les générations précédentes : un suivi cardiaque qui décroche pendant l’effort et de petites latences au quotidien. Notre test lui attribue 9/10, et notre comparatif en fait la référence des possesseurs d’iPhone.
L’offre parlera surtout à ceux qui veulent remplacer une Apple Watch vieillissante, ou s’en offrir une première avec un iPhone récent. Si votre Series 10 ou 11 vous satisfait, rien ne presse : le nouveau menu de watchOS 27 profite aussi aux anciens modèles compatibles. Et si l’intelligence artificielle compte dans votre choix, sachez qu’une partie de ces fonctions reste indisponible en France.

articles.title: Auchan, Leclerc, Lidl : pourquoi ces pommes de terre sont devenues naturellement toxiques
articles.text:
Quand un légume est rappelé, on soupçonne d’habitude un résidu de pesticide ou une bactérie. Ici, c’est le tubercule lui-même qui pose problème. Comme le rapporte franceinfo, plusieurs fiches de rappel publiées entre le samedi 21 et ce mardi 24 novembre 2026 visent des pommes de terre rouges trop riches en glycoalcaloïdes, vendues chez Auchan, E.Leclerc et Lidl.
Les trois rappels portent sur le même numéro de lot, 26128774. La fiche RappelConso publiée par Leclerc ce lundi 23 novembre prévient que ces substances peuvent provoquer « nausées, maux de ventre, vomissements et diarrhées ».
Pourquoi une pomme de terre devient-elle toxique ?
La pomme de terre fait partie des solanacées, comme la tomate et l’aubergine. D’après Santé Canada, ces plantes produisent des glycoalcaloïdes, surtout l’alpha-solanine et l’alpha-chaconine, sans doute pour se défendre contre les insectes, les champignons et les bactéries. À faible dose, ces molécules donnent même son goût au tubercule. Mais leur taux grimpe quand la pomme de terre verdit à la lumière, germe ou s’abîme.
En 2020, l’Autorité européenne de sécurité des aliments (EFSA) a fixé la plus petite dose aux effets nocifs observés à 1 milligramme par kilo de poids corporel et par jour, soit 70 milligrammes pour un adulte de 70 kilos. Les nourrissons et les jeunes enfants, plus légers, sont donc les plus exposés. L’épluchage aide, car selon l’EFSA, il réduit la teneur de 25 à 75 %.
Quelles pommes de terre rapporter en magasin ?
Vérifiez les pommes de terre rouges achetées ces dernières semaines :
- Chez Auchan, les filets de 2,5 kg vendus du 19 octobre au 21 novembre et ceux de 2 kg vendus du 4 au 21 novembre,
- chez E.Leclerc, les sachets de 2 kg Panier du Primeur vendus du 16 octobre au 23 novembre,
- chez Lidl, la variété Chérie de la marque Côté Marché, en filets de 2,5 kg vendus du 22 octobre au 9 novembre.
Ne les mangez pas, même épluchées, et rapportez-les en magasin pour vous faire rembourser. Si vous avez des nausées ou des vomissements après en avoir mangé, consultez votre médecin et dites-lui ce que vous avez consommé. Pour toutes les autres pommes de terre, gardez-les au frais et dans le noir, et retirez les parties vertes et les germes. Et ne mangez jamais une pomme de terre qui a un goût amer.

articles.title: Un SUV électrique allemand à 25 000 € ? Le coup de poker d’Opel avec un géant chinois
articles.text:
S’il est impossible de contrer l’ennemi, autant se joindre à lui. Beaucoup ne seront certainement pas d’accord avec cette affirmation. C’est pourtant ce qu’a fait Opel en signant un accord de coopération avec Leapmotor valable pour les prochaines années. Les fans du Blitz hurleront à coup sûr au sacrilège. Mais vu la situation actuelle, il serait assez bête de vouloir se renfermer sur soi-même.
Surtout que Leapmotor fait partiellement partie du groupe Stellantis. Bref, les fondations étaient en réalité déjà toutes préparées… Mais pour quels produits ? Toute une portée, visiblement ! Et le premier de la série sera un SUV électrique inédit du segment C qui arrivera en 2028. Il complètera donc la gamme Opel aux côtés du Mokka, du Frontera et du Grandland et ne remplacera pas un modèle existant.
Pas question d’un simple modèle chinois rebadgé
Et pour ceux qui s’attendaient au pire, non, ce futur véhicule ne sera pas bêtement un Leapmotor rebadgé. Opel partira bien de zéro en appliquant un design assurément allemand gage d’un minimum de personnalité. La marque souligne que ce modèle sera adapté aux goûts européens. Ce SUV reprendra donc l’identité stylistique du Blitz avec la calandre Vizor dotée d’un logo rétroéclairé.
Des lignes tendues appliquées sur une carrosserie épurée sont donc attendues. Côté dimensions, Florian Huettl, le PDG d’Opel, cherche à placer ce modèle au milieu de sa gamme de SUV : « nous visons le segment C moyen, qui mesure 4,50 mètres, ce qui placera ainsi [cette future voiture] entre le Frontera et le Grandland. Il s’agit d’un marché très porteur au Royaume-Uni et en Europe qu’Opel n’a pas encore couvert ».
De vrais boutons à bord et un prix d’attaque fixé à 25 000 €
Est-ce la solution miracle pour remettre le constructeur sur les rails ? Oui, aux yeux de Huettl : « nous considérons ce véhicule comme un atout majeur pour renforcer notre présence sur ce marché […]. Opel est solidement implanté dans le nord et l’est de l’Europe. Ce sont nos marchés historiques et leur particularité est qu’ils sont davantage attirés par les SUV du segment C et les véhicules électriques ». Espérons que le châssis sera aussi réglé à l’européenne…
À bord, Opel met un point d’honneur à conserver les commandes physiques, comme le confirme Huettl, « nous étudions comment tirer le meilleur parti de l’expertise de Leapmotor en matière d’architectures électroniques […]. Mais l’important, c’est que nous sommes Opel, et nous utiliserons de vrais boutons ». Niveau tarification, le constructeur vise une entrée de gamme aux alentours des 25 000 €, soit à peine plus haut que le Frontera.

articles.title: McDonald's Japan data breach exposes customer location information
articles.text:
McDonald's Japan, the fast-food giant's Japanese subsidiary, has disclosed a data breach after attackers accessed a database containing sensitive information for users of the company's official smartphone app.
Founded in 1940, McDonald's is now a multinational fast-food chain that operates more than 40,000 restaurants in more than 100 countries and serves tens of millions of customers daily.
In a Friday statement, the company's Japanese subsidiary confirmed that threat actors gained access to its official app's database and said the exposed information includes the users' product purchase history, IP addresses, mobile device location data, and customer management IDs (which cannot be used to identify the customers' email addresses or member IDs).
McDonald's Japan also added that the exposed data doesn't include the affected customers' names, email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, or credit card information.
While it has yet to reveal when it detected the attack or how many individuals had their data stolen, the company said a follow-up investigation found no service disruption or misuse of official apps as a result of the incident.
"We are working to invalidate any credentials used for unauthorized access, investigate the relevant systems, and report to the Personal Information Protection Commission," it said. "In addition, we will strive to strengthen security measures and prevent recurrence."
This isn't the first data breach to affect McDonald's in recent years, with the fast food giant disclosing a breach in June 2021 after attackers breached its systems and stole information belonging to employees and customers from the US, South Korea, and Taiwan.
In 2017, McDonald's also patched a cross-site scripting (XSS) security flaw that affected its official website and exposed customers' plain-text passwords.
Japanese companies under attack
Last month, Burger King Japan also disclosed a major data breach after attackers stole 11.18 million customer records that were later leaked online.
The two incidents affecting the two Japanese fast food chains add to a large wave of cyberattacks impacting high-profile Japanese companies since the start of the year, including Japan Airlines, entertainment system maker Daiichi Kosho, cloud and digital infrastructure firm IDC Frontier, Japanese publishing giant Nikkei, cloud and data center service provider Sakura Internet, taxi operator Nihon Kotsu, telecommunications giant KDDI, and many others.
Macnica researcher Yutaka Sejiyama has logged 288 cybersecurity incidents affecting Japanese organizations involving personal information theft or exposure since the start of the year.
Sejiyama found that attackers are now probing websites and APIs for access-control, configuration, and authentication weaknesses, and exploiting known (n-day) vulnerabilities to find other victims.

articles.title: Cómo sacar a personas que usan tu wifi sin permiso y evitar que vuelvan a conectarse
articles.text:
Sacar a personas que usan tu wifi sin permiso ayuda a recuperar la velocidad de conexión, reducir el consumo de datos y proteger la seguridad digital del hogar. Una contraseña fácil de adivinar o una configuración antigua puede permitir que vecinos, visitas o desconocidos entren en la red sin autorización y usen el servicio contratado.
El problema adquiere mayor relevancia porque teléfonos, ordenadores, televisores, cámaras, consolas y asistentes de voz comparten la misma conexión. Un dispositivo ajeno puede saturar el ancho de banda, afectar videollamadas o transmisiones de video y abrir una puerta a riesgos de privacidad si alguno de los equipos de la casa conserva configuraciones inseguras.
Cómo revisar los dispositivos conectados
El primer paso para saber quién usa una red consiste en revisar la lista de equipos conectados. Muchas compañías de internet incluyen esta herramienta en sus aplicaciones móviles. Desde allí es posible consultar los dispositivos activos, ver su nombre, el tipo de aparato y, en algunos casos, controlar cuánto tiempo pueden permanecer conectados.
Antes de bloquear un equipo, conviene identificar los aparatos propios. Un teléfono puede aparecer con un nombre técnico, mientras que una consola, una impresora o un televisor suelen figurar con la marca del fabricante. Apagar temporalmente los dispositivos del hogar ayuda a comprobar cuáles desaparecen de la lista y cuáles siguen conectados.
Si la aplicación del proveedor no muestra esa información, el control puede hacerse desde el panel de administración del router wifi. Para acceder, hay que escribir en el navegador una dirección como 192.168.1.1, 192.168.0.1 o 10.0.0.1. La dirección correcta suele estar impresa en una etiqueta ubicada en la parte inferior o trasera del equipo.
Después de iniciar sesión, hay que buscar secciones denominadas “dispositivos conectados”, “clientes DHCP”, “red local” o “lista de clientes”. El menú suele mostrar el nombre del equipo, su dirección IP local y la dirección MAC, un identificador asociado a cada dispositivo.
La lentitud de la conexión puede ser una señal de alerta
Una caída de velocidad no prueba por sí sola que haya una persona conectada sin permiso. Las actualizaciones automáticas, las copias de seguridad, los videojuegos en línea y el contenido en alta definición también elevan el uso de la red.
Aun así, hay indicios que justifican una revisión. Entre ellos están un consumo de datos fuera de lo habitual, cortes frecuentes, problemas para conectar nuevos dispositivos o actividad constante en las luces del router cuando nadie usa internet en casa.
Los sistemas de wifi mesh facilitan esta tarea. Los equipos de marcas como Google, Amazon, Eero o TP-Link cuentan con aplicaciones desde las que se pueden identificar dispositivos, pausar su conexión o bloquearlos sin necesidad de entrar en los ajustes avanzados del router.
Cambiar la contraseña expulsa a los equipos no autorizados
La medida más eficaz para retirar a intrusos es cambiar la contraseña de la red. Cuando se reemplaza la clave, los dispositivos que tenían acceso con la anterior pierden la conexión. Después, solo podrán volver a entrar si conocen la nueva contraseña.
La clave debe ser larga, difícil de adivinar y diferente de las que se utilizan en el correo electrónico, las redes sociales o las aplicaciones bancarias. Una combinación de palabras, números y símbolos ofrece más protección que una fecha de nacimiento, un nombre o una secuencia sencilla.
También es recomendable cambiar la contraseña de administración del router si mantiene la configuración de fábrica. Esa clave protege el panel desde el que se modifican los ajustes de seguridad, por lo que no debe coincidir con la contraseña del wifi.
WPA2 o WPA3 y las actualizaciones refuerzan la seguridad
En la configuración del router conviene comprobar que esté activado el cifrado WPA2 o WPA3. Estos protocolos protegen la comunicación entre los dispositivos y la red doméstica. Si el equipo es compatible, WPA3 ofrece una capa de seguridad más reciente. WEP debe evitarse debido a sus vulnerabilidades conocidas.
También es aconsejable desactivar WPS, una función que permite conectar aparatos mediante un botón o un código corto. Aunque puede resultar cómoda, reduce el control sobre quién intenta acceder a la red.
El filtrado por dirección MAC permite autorizar solo dispositivos determinados, pero funciona como una medida complementaria. Una contraseña sólida, el firmware actualizado y revisiones periódicas de los equipos conectados son las acciones más útiles para mantener la red bajo control.

articles.title: EEUU sigue soñando con su tren de alta velocidad: California puso la primera piedra hace casi 12 años, ha gastado más que el AVE Madrid-Barcelona y aún no transporta pasajeros
articles.text:
El tren de alta velocidad de California es un proyecto que tiene una idea muy clara. Para cualquier europeo resultará familiar. Se trata de crear un nuevo tren que conecte dos grandes ciudades. En el caso de esta línea serán San Francisco y Los Ángeles (en menos de tres horas). Para ello se van a construir trenes capaces de circular a más de 350 km/h.
La primera piedra oficial se colocó en Fresno el 6 de enero de 2015. Hasta noviembre de 2026 han pasado casi 12 años. Antes están los años de planificación y contratación. Hay una auditoría estatal que indica que se dio el visto bueno para empezar a trabajar en octubre de 2013.
Hay que diferenciar entre los gastos realizados y las previsiones del plan de negocio de 2026. Hasta febrero se han invertido 15.041 millones de dólares (aproximadamente 12.700 millones de euros). Es más que la construcción del AVE Madrid-Barcelona (8.966,7 millones de euros), pero no es exactamente comparable por el año y alcance de la obra. Además, no hay corrección de inflación. En cuanto a la cantidad total del proyecto californiano, son unos 126.100 millones de dólares.
Una línea que debía abrir en 2020
Los californianos aprobaron en 2008 bonos por unos 10.000 millones de dólares para desarrollar alta velocidad. El plan de ese año estimaba que se invertirían unos 33.000 millones de dólares. La fecha de apertura inicial estaba prevista en 2020, pero esto quedó en el pasado sin ponerlo en marcha.
Lo que se pretendía era unir todo el territorio (norte-sur) con futuras prolongaciones hacia Sacramento y San Diego. Las obras se concentran en el Valle Central (entre Merced y Bakersfield). Se están haciendo viaductos y cruces a distinto nivel, traslados de servicios y, además, se está preparando la plataforma sobre la que irán los trenes.
Aún hay que transformar todas estas obras en un ferrocarril (para pasajeros). En el contrato de vías se ha fijado que debería empezar a tenderse el 30 de noviembre de 2026. Además de la propia vía, se incluyen otros elementos como electrificación, control de trenes y comunicaciones. Se prevé que en 2032-2033 se complete el primer tramo operativo.
Los terrenos y la financiación retrasaron la obra
Algunos de los problemas eran conocidos. En una auditoría estatal de 2018 se concluía que se había contratado la construcción sin contar con todos los terrenos necesarios. También había algunas dificultades pendientes de acuerdos de traslados de redes de servicios. Como consecuencia de estas demoras, se han tenido que incorporar costes adicionales (personal, material y maquinaria).
También ha habido problemas de financiación (los fondos están divididos) y de cambios políticos. Aún hay más, ya que no está garantizado todo el dinero necesario para completar la conexión entre San Francisco y Los Ángeles.
Lo único claro es que California continúa trabajando en su sistema de alta velocidad, aunque han pasado casi 12 años desde que se puso la primera piedra, y no tienen un servicio de pasajeros.

articles.text:
Black Friday – Clavier bureautique ou gamer, deux des meilleurs produits de notre comparatif sont en promotion
Le Logitech MX Keys S Plus et le Razer BlackWidow V4 Pro 75%, qui comptent parmi les claviers les mieux notés de notre comparatif, profitent de réductions de prix à l'occasion du Black Friday 2026.
À chaque passion le clavier qui va avec, et cette dernière semaine de Black Friday permet de s'équiper pour toutes les situations : session de tableur ou de Counter-Strike 2, il faut de tout, et cette petite sélection compte deux des meilleures pioches de chez Razer et Logitech.
Logitech MX Keys S
C'est un peu la recommandation officieuse de toute la rédaction des Nums : le MX Keys S Plus de Logitech est l'un des modèles les plus utilisés au sein de l'open space, et c'est loin d'être un hasard. Fin, autonome et silencieux, ce board résolument tourné vers la bureautique propose une frappe réactive et agréable grâce à ses commutateurs chiclets, similaires à ceux que l'on retrouve sur un ordinateur portable. Seuls deux petits défauts sont à signaler : sa double sérigraphie un peu fouillis et son manque de pieds ajustables. En bref, un classique des dactylos de France et de Navarre, actuellement proposé aux alentours de 70 € chez Amazon et Boulanger.
Dans un tout autre genre, le BlackWidow V4 Pro 75% de Razer saura contenter les joueurs et les joueuses en manque de clavier mécanique. Son format plus compact le fait rentrer dans presque tous les bureaux, et sa fabrication premium – ainsi que son PCB hot-swap, avec donc des switches remplaçables – en font un achat avisé en cette période de promotions. Lancé aux alentours de 250 €, il tombe à 170 € pour l'occasion. Attention toutefois : ce format n'existe qu'en QWERTY. La version AZERTY de la gamme BlackWidow V4 Pro est réservée au modèle « 100 % », lui aussi en réduction à 180 € chez Amazon.

articles.title: WhatsApp testa câmera dupla para gravar selfie e paisagem ao mesmo tempo
articles.text:
O WhatsApp começou a liberar recurso que permite usar as câmeras frontal e traseira do celular ao mesmo tempo. A novidade possibilita registrar uma cena e mostrar a reação de quem está filmando em única foto ou vídeo.
A ferramenta está sendo distribuída gradualmente para alguns usuários da versão beta do aplicativo para Android, segundo informações do WABetaInfo. A funcionalidade foi identificada na atualização 2.26.46.9, disponível pela Google Play Store.
Com o novo modo, o aplicativo combina as imagens capturadas pelas duas câmeras em única composição. Assim, é possível mostrar o ambiente à frente do celular enquanto uma pequena janela exibe a imagem de quem está segurando o aparelho.
Como funciona a câmera dupla do WhatsApp?
- Para ativar a novidade, o usuário precisa abrir a câmera do WhatsApp e tocar em novo botão localizado na parte superior da interface;
- Quando o modo é habilitado, a câmera traseira ocupa a maior parte da tela, enquanto a frontal aparece em janela retangular menor, posicionada inicialmente no canto superior direito;
- O usuário pode arrastar essa janela para qualquer região da tela. Também é possível inverter a disposição das imagens: com um toque no botão de alternância, a câmera frontal passa a ocupar o quadro principal, enquanto a traseira fica na janela menor;
- O recurso funciona tanto para fotografias quanto para gravações de vídeo. No primeiro caso, o WhatsApp combina as duas imagens em única foto. Nos vídeos, as câmeras registram simultaneamente, formando um único clipe.
Leia mais:
- WhatsApp começa a permitir que usuários programem mensagens no app
- WhatsApp corrige três falhas de segurança, uma delas suspeita de uso em golpes
- WhatsApp amplia grupos para até 1.500 pessoas e libera mensagens que desaparecem
- WhatsApp ganha figurinhas com som; veja como funciona o recurso
Onde será possível compartilhar as imagens?
O conteúdo produzido com a câmera dupla poderá ser compartilhado nos mesmos espaços em que o WhatsApp permite enviar outras mídias.
Isso inclui conversas individuais, grupos, canais e atualizações de Status. Depois de capturar a imagem ou gravar o vídeo, o usuário também poderá adicionar uma legenda, fazer edições no editor de desenho do aplicativo ou simplesmente enviar o material.
A proposta é facilitar a produção de conteúdos que mostrem simultaneamente o que está acontecendo e a reação de quem registra o momento. Isso pode ser útil em viagens, eventos, passeios e outras situações em que mostrar apenas a paisagem não é suficiente.
Quando a novidade chega para todos?
Por enquanto, o modo de câmera dupla está disponível apenas para alguns participantes do programa beta do WhatsApp para Android. A distribuição é gradual, portanto, nem todos os testadores receberam a funcionalidade.
O WABetaInfo informa que a novidade deverá alcançar mais contas nas próximas semanas. Entretanto, ainda não existe previsão oficial para a chegada da ferramenta à versão estável do aplicativo.
Também não há confirmação de quando — ou se — o recurso será disponibilizado para usuários de iPhone (iOS).
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Amazon is knocking almost $50 off six months of Apple TV
articles.text:
Streaming deals aren’t as plentiful as they used to be, but they’re still around if you know where to look. One that caught our eye is an offer for Apple TV for those with an Amazon account in the US. Apple’s streaming service usually costs $14.99 per month, but following this page will let you get it for $6.99 for your first six months (totaling $42 versus $90 without the deal). Amazon hasn’t shared how long this offer will be available for, so I’d strike on it sooner than later.
Amazon is knocking almost $50 off six months of Apple TV
Instead of paying $14.99 per month, you can pay just $7 for six months when you subscribe through Amazon.
The subscription includes exclusive access to Formula 1 races and Major League Soccer matches, not to mention a bunch of acclaimed shows like Severance, Silo, The Morning Show, Pachinko, Pluribus, Slow Horses, and many more. articles.title: Stealth Health launches direct-to-consumer clinic with MedExpress acquisition
articles.text:
A Canadian telehealth software provider is now spinning up its own online clinic.
The news: Toronto-based Stealth Health announced on Tuesday that it acquired the Canadian business of MedExpress from HeliosX, a United Kingdom-based digital healthcare company, in an all-cash deal. MedExpress is now operating as Mira Health, Stealth Health’s own online clinic that offers consultations and prescription treatment for weight management and sexual health. The purchase price was not disclosed.
Stealth Health said in a statement that the acquisition gives it an established Canadian patient business and a foundation to expand its own direct-to-consumer services, while HeliosX focuses on growing in the US and Europe.
From the source: Stealth Health co-founder and CEO Matthew Mazzuca said in a statement that his company’s goal is to become “the centre of longevity medicine in Canada and the United States.”
“We now have the technology, the clinical network and the pharmacy capability in one company, and we are going to keep building and acquiring until Stealth is the first place people on both sides of the border turn for their long-term health,” Mazzuca said.
The context: Stealth Health provides a white-label platform and pharmacy infrastructure to more than 200 third-party clinics and health brands in the US and Canada, Mazzuca told BetaKit in an email. The company said that acquiring an established patient business, MedExpress, brings those technology and operational offerings to a greater scale.
Stealth Health said it’s coordinating the handover of MedExpress with HeliosX, and that its patients will be transitioned to, and supported by, Mira Health following the acquisition. No employees are joining Stealth Health as part of the deal, Mazzuca said.
Final thought: Stealth Health is directly entering a market it supports with its own software as more telehealth providers specializing in weight loss and sexual health crop up in the Canadian market. Last year, similar platforms like Felix Health and Phoenix secured significant funding as weight loss drugs like Ozempic ballooned in popularity. After seven years of bootstrapping, Science&Humans, another telehealth platform, secured its first round of funding earlier this year as interest in its services heated up.

articles.title: Jura unveils the A8, its slimmest ever automatic coffee machine — and it still squeezes a full-size grinder and brew unit onto tiny kitchen counters
articles.text:
Big flavor, small footprint: Jura's slimmest ever coffee maker promises premium coffee without taking over your kitchen
The Jura A8 may be slim, but it's no lightweight when it comes to flavor
- The new Jura A8 is just 19cm wide and 44.5cm high
- It has a full-sized brewing unit and grinder
- It's on sale now for £999 (about $1,300 / AU$1,970)
The problem with many of the best coffee machines is that big flavor often requires a really big machine — and that's not ideal if your kitchen is barely big enough to fling a feline around. If you're short of space and want a premium coffee maker that doesn't have a huge footprint, Jura would like to introduce you to its new compact: the Jura A8.
The A8 is Jura's slimmest ever coffee machine, but it doesn't skimp on the specifications. It features a full-size brewing unit and grinder to deliver what Jura promises is all the quality and flavor you'd expect from a premium bean-to-cup machine.
The Jura J8 is an automatic coffee maker with a menu of 18 hot and cold drinks, including espresso, cappuccino, flat white and latte macchiato. We like Jura's coffee machines a lot (the J10 has held a spot in our roundup fo the best espresso machines for over a year) and this looks like a typically smart and stylish way to start your day.
Jura A8: key features and pricing
The Jura A8 is sleek and modern-looking. It currently comes in a single finish, Piano Black, and is just 19cm wide, 37cm deep, and 44.5cm high. Despite those compact dimensions, it houses Jura's Professional Aroma Grinder 3 and a full-size professional brewing unit for coffee doses ranging from 5g to 16g. There's also a powder chute you can use for pre-ground coffee, and an automatic cleaning setup for the milk foaming system.
Inside the A8 is a thermoblock heating system designed to deliver quick start-up, which is handy when you're in a morning rush. And you can adjust the strength of your coffee on a scale of one to ten depending on how much of a morning person you happen to be.
The A8 keeps things simple with just four buttons and a 2.8-inch touchscreen. You can use it with the optional JOE app for features such as Coffee Timer, which enables you to 'order' your coffee up to 16 hours in advance. And while it looks simple there are features for serious coffee people here: in addition to changing the coffee strength you can program the grind size, the brew temperature, the amount of milk foam, and the hot water temperature.
It's not just the coffee machine that Jura has made smaller either; it's shunk the price as well. Where Jura's larger coffee machines start at four figures, the Jura A8 has a list price of £999 (about $1,300 / AU$1,970).

articles.title: CRA, AI Robotics, Motor Control, Digital Energy at electronica 2026
articles.text:
The Singapore-based MCU and security-IC supplier showed 35 applications and solutions in Munich and argued that European buying decisions now turn on three things: evidence a chip can survive a Cyber Resilience Act audit, real-time response in AI robotics, and efficient power conversion for digital energy.
NSING Technologies, the Singapore-based fabless semiconductor arm of NSING Group (300077.SZ; 02701.HK), has concluded its participation in electronica 2026, which closed on 13 November at Messe München, after displaying 35 applications and reference designs on its Hall C2 stand (Booth 741), grouped around the questions European OEMs brought to the show: how to prove a product is cyber-secure before the EU Cyber Resilience Act becomes fully binding in December 2027, how to make a robot joint respond in real time, and how to convert power efficiently in digital-energy systems.
The show’s official themes — artificial intelligence, network resilience and energy efficiency — ran through the booth. What tied them together, according to the company, was a shift in where the difficulty now sits: less in any single chip’s peak specification, more in the compliance file, at the joint and in the power stage.
CRA: reporting obligations are already live; the deadline is next December
A sizeable share of the booth went to the EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847), which is less about features than about evidence. The regulation entered into force on 10 December 2024. Reporting obligations for actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents took effect on 11 September 2026. The main obligations — conformity assessment and CE marking — apply from 11 December 2027.
For procurement teams, that sequence mattered more than the headline date. The reporting duty is already enforceable, and the design changes plus documentation needed to pass assessment have roughly a year to land. “Future compliance” is no longer an accurate description of the situation.
NSING maps its portfolio onto the regulation’s classes. N32S security ICs and TPM devices at CC EAL4+ support third-party assessment for Critical-class products. Cortex-M4 and Cortex-M7 MCUs, including the N32H and N32G4 families, are positioned for Class 2, with chip-level SESIP certification in progress. Cortex-M0 parts such as the N32G0 and N32WB fit the Class 1 self-declaration route.
Beyond the silicon, the company packages what an OEM has to put in the file: an ECR (essential cybersecurity requirements) mapping table, a software bill of materials, a compliance support pack and introductions to notified bodies. These are organised around a five-step route — classification and threat modelling, secure development practice, validation and bill-of-materials control, system documentation with a vulnerability reporting channel, and assessment plus CE archiving.
Post-quantum migration sits on the same axis. NSING’s MCUs integrate ML-KEM (512/768/1024) and ML-DSA (44/65/87), starting with the N32H4xx and N32H7xx and extending across its Cortex-M4-and-above N32 line, covering key establishment, device identity, firmware update and secure boot, and data integrity checks. The implementations coexist with RSA, ECC, SHA, and ship with drivers, a crypto abstraction layer, example code and a porting guide — the building blocks for an assessment, hybrid-verify, migrate and evolve sequence.
Digital energy: power conversion and battery management
On the power-conversion side, the pitch is topology coverage rather than a single headline number. The N32DP474 runs PFC, LLC resonant conversion and multiphase interleaved topologies from one device; NSING characterises peak efficiency at up to 99% under rated load, and says a reference design built on it is already in volume production with server-power customers. For energy storage, the NB1802 analog front end monitors 18 series-connected cells, covering 1500 V container systems and residential packs.
Humanoid robots: a three-tier architecture from joint to machine
The bottleneck in humanoid robots is not the model. It is the joint — torque, speed and position loops that have to close deterministically while the rest of the machine stays synchronised — and the coordination above it.
NSING splits that work across cores. The N32H785EC pairs a Cortex-M7 at 600 MHz, dedicated to field-oriented control across torque, speed and position loops plus dual absolute-encoder decoding, with a Cortex-M4F at 300 MHz handling CAN FD and EtherCAT. A 100 ps high-resolution timer and hardware CORDIC/FMAC units support multi-axis synchronisation on high-load joints. Secondary joints at the wrist, ankle and torso use the N32MD473, which integrates a three-phase gate driver. Dexterous hands move to a distributed arrangement of a main controller plus per-channel drivers, so wiring and heat dissipation stop setting the size of a finger.
Around the joints, the company supplies NB1802 battery management ICs, N32WB BLE SoCs and NS350 TPM rated CC EAL4+. NSING says these designs are shipping in volume as part of complete humanoid, quadruped, collaborative-arm and dexterous-hand platforms.
The same control IP appeared elsewhere on the stand: the VIGX π6 exoskeleton uses the N32H49x for high-precision position control; 3D printers run real-time motion planning and stepper drive on the N32G45x with the N32G003 handling housekeeping; collaborative arms implement multi-axis interpolation on the N32H78x.
Industrial, automotive and motor control: the revenue base underneath
Underneath the headline demonstrations sat the business NSING earns today. The N32H7 family serves servo drives, PLCs, inverters and integrated motion controllers. The N32H785EC includes a Beckhoff-licensed EtherCAT slave controller and holds multi-axis synchronisation jitter to the microsecond range; the N32H47x and N32H48x carry IEC 61508 SIL 2 and SIL 3 functional-safety certification. The stand also showed a servo drive controller built on the N32ZH785EC, an industrial I/O module based on the N32H760, and an industrial gateway that pairs an N32S032 security IC with the main controller.
On the automotive side, the N32A455, N32A052 and N32A003 are AEC-Q100 qualified and specified from −40 °C to 125 °C. NSING says they are in volume production with body-radar designs at major Chinese EV makers, and that applications are moving outward from body control into on-board chargers, T-Boxes and smart-cockpit functions. A body control module, a reversing-radar design on the N32A455 and a headlight design on the N32G435 were on display.
Motor control is where the portfolio’s integration showed most clearly. The company’s matrix spans Cortex-M7, M4 and M0 cores and can drive one, two, four or six motors from a single MCU, cutting bill-of-materials cost for appliance and power-tool designs. Three parts carried the demonstration: the N32M016, which integrates a 150 V three-phase 6N gate driver, LDO and differential PGA in a 5×5 mm package to deliver 800 W at 90,000 rpm for drills and handheld vacuums, with back-EMF sensing and three-level overcurrent protection; the N32M012, with a 3P3N driver covering 6–40 V and sensorless sinusoidal FOC for ceiling and pedestal fans that runs stably from 200 rpm; and the N32G033K8Q7-1, a 64 MHz M0 part with three op-amps and a 25 µs current loop that supports 120,000 rpm hair dryers and adaptive-start refrigerator compressors.
One silicon platform across four kinds of building device
The building-automation demonstration was organized around a single data chain rather than individual products. Smart locks and access control pair the N32WB Bluetooth SoC with a security IC, so identification and unlock authorisation happen on the endpoint. The N32G45x drives elevator-car human-machine interfaces. Occupancy and daylight sensing dimming built on the N32G45x, N32G03x and N32WB connects lighting control to energy monitoring. The N32L43x smart breaker folds circuit-level metering, protection and remote control into the same link. For an OEM, the reusable part is that one silicon platform, one provisioning method and one back-end data format can cover all four device classes in an office building.
Why Europe, and what comes next
During the show the NSING team met global end customers, distributors and trade press, and continued talks on distributor coverage and joint reference designs. The company framed electronica 2026 as a live test of its global strategy: compliance, functional safety, long-term supply and local support — the four things European customers ask about first — are the areas it has been investing in for several years.
NSING said it will keep investing in global product development and ecosystem partnerships, with AI computing infrastructure, embodied intelligence and edge AI as its stated priorities, alongside security, SoC, RF and power management as established strengths.
About NSING Technologies
NSING Technologies, an NSING Group member founded in Singapore in 2018, delivers high-performance semiconductor solutions for the global industry. Its expertise spans general MCU, secure IC (TPM), BLE and BMS, with advanced capabilities in Arm/GPU multi-core architectures, low-power design and secure-zone IP. Its solutions power a wide range of applications, including AI, robotics, industrial automation, consumer electronics, smart home, automotive electronics, IoT devices, medical equipment, energy storage systems and wearable technology, enabling customers to innovate with confidence. NSING was established in 2000, listed on ChiNext in 2010 and on HKEX in 2026 (300077.SZ, 02701.HK). Together, we create a secure, smart and sustainable future.
