articles.title: Neue Studie: Verbirgt sich in unserem Sonnensystem ein neunter Planet?
articles.text:
Neues Modell: Gibt es einen neunten Planeten in unserem Sonnensystem?
Unser Sonnensystem hat acht Planeten: Erde, Merkur, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus und Neptun. Und wenn dem doch nicht so wäre? Laut neuen Computermodellen könnte sich in den äußeren Bereichen des Sonnensystems ein neunter Planet verbergen. Astrophysiker:innen der University of Southern Queensland (Australien) und der japanischen Kindai-Universität ziehen die Existenz eines Planeten in Erwägung, der etwa doppelt so groß wie die Erde sein soll und mehr als 200-mal so weit von der Sonne entfernt sein soll wie unsere Erde. Veröffentlicht wurden die Forschungsergebnisse in den Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.
Ist der potenzielle neue Planet etwa doppelt so groß wie die Erde?
Der Mitautor und Professor an der University of Southern Queensland, Jonti Horner, erklärte, die Schwerkraft dieses hypothetischen Planeten – genannt X2 – könnte die „seltsamen“ Umlaufbahnen eisiger Objekte jenseits des Neptun erklären. „In den letzten 10 bis 15 Jahren haben wir eisige Objekte entdeckt, die sich auf stark geneigten oder sehr weit entfernten Umlaufbahnen bewegen – ein Phänomen, das sich mit unserem derzeitigen Verständnis der acht Planeten sowie deren Entstehung und Entwicklung nicht erklären lässt“, betonte Horner.
Computersimulationen halfen bei der wissenschaftlichen Arbeit
Mithilfe von Computersimulationen, die die 4,5 Milliarden Jahre währende Entwicklung des Sonnensystems abbilden, fanden die Forscher:innen laut ABC, der öffentlich-rechtlichen Rundfunkanstalt Australiens, heraus, dass die Einbeziehung eines „Planet X2“ dabei hilft, die Umlaufbahnen dieser eisigen Objekte zu erklären.
In der Wissenschaftswelt gibt es nicht zum ersten Mal Diskussionen über neue Planeten in unserem Sonnensystem. Anfang des 20. Jahrhunderts vermutete der Astronom Percival Lowell, dass ein hypothetischer „Planet X“ die Unregelmäßigkeiten in den Umlaufbahnen von Uranus und Neptun erklären könnte. Diese Suche führte schließlich zur Entdeckung von Pluto.
16 atemberaubende Bilder der Erde aus dem Weltall
Forscher:innen hoffen auf neue Technologien
Der Hauptautor der Studie, Patryk Sofia Lykawka, erklärte aber auch, dass ein „Planet X2“, sofern er tatsächlich existiert, von der Erde aus extrem schwer zu entdecken sein dürfte, da er auch an seinem sonnennächsten Punkt „zigmal lichtschwächer als Pluto“ wäre.
Professor Horner betonte, dass neue Technologien – etwa das Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Südamerika – der Schlüssel zu einer künftigen Entdeckung sein könnten. Die Einrichtung in Chile führt regelmäßig astronomische Himmelsdurchmusterungen durch, um eine Art Zeitraffer-Aufzeichnung des Universums über einen Zeitraum von zehn Jahren zu erstellen. Horner hofft, dass „wir ihn in Zukunft, wenn uns eine bessere Technologie zur Verfügung steht, auch tatsächlich aufspüren können“.

articles.title: La tele, los libros y las redes sociales de GTA VI son un agujero negro: la gente ya pasa más tiempo en ellos que atracando bancos
articles.text:
En uno de los primeros días tras el estreno de GTA VI, un usuario de Reddit presumió de haber visto la televisión de Leonida dos horas seguidas. Dicho de otro modo: la tele del juego funciona exactamente igual que una tele de verdad. Es solo un ejemplo de las múltiples distracciones que ofrece el mundo de 'GTA VI', escalofriantemente realista cuando el ocio resulta ser tan adictivo como su contrapartidas reales.
Culebrón tropical. Una parte de los más de 39 millones de jugadores únicos en PS5 y de las 683 millones de horas que se invirtieron en el juego según Sony, estuvo viendo el canal de Megamundo, la parodia de Telemundo que emite telenovelas en español. Una de ellas, 'El destino extiende sus alas', remite sin disimulo a 'Pasión de gavilanes', y pronto comenzaron a brotar reacciones de jugadores enganchados a capítulos de unos 20 minutos, en un canal que muchos dicen que es "más adictivo que la historia principal".
Dibujitos. Weazel, otra cadena ficticia de la saga, estrenaba también 'Macca & Friends', una serie animada protagonizada por un caimán rosa que, por cierto, viene como figura en la caja de coleccionista de 400 dólares. La serie cuenta con su propio trailer y no tiene nada que envidiar a las series de animación para adultos que vemos en streaming. El trailer juega también al mundo ficticio de Leonida, y fijaba el estreno para el día del lanzamiento del juego.
Remedy lo hizo antes. Este jugueteo no es nuevo: 'Max Payne 2' ya metía en sus televisores varias series completas, aunque breves, entre ellas unos dibujos animados protagonizados por la mascota oficiosa de la saga. Con 'Macca & Friends', sin embargo, este juego de espejos se ha hecho a lo grande: Rockstar North encargó episodios de 'Macc & Friends' a un estudio de animación externo, lo que da buena cuenta de la ambición y el cuidado por el detalle del estudio.
Solo fisgar. Desde antes del lanzamiento sabíamos que podríamos pasar las horas muertas fisgando redes sociales desde nuestro móvil. Snapmatic, la parodia de Instagram, va evolucionando y recibiendo actualizaciones según avanza el juego. Lo que realmente engancha, como en las redes sociales auténticas, son los comentarios que reciben los posts, tan mezquinos como los de cualquier red real. Jason y Lucia pueden seguir cuentas pero no publicar, un grado extra de sofisticación que tampoco habría sido muy de extrañar.
La vida cañón. Todo esto forma parte de un fenómeno más amplio, y que va más allá de las quejas de la manosfera porque hay que hacer demasiados recados domésticos para mantener viva la relación de Jason con Lucía. El juego te ofrece la posibilidad, aunque no te obliga, de hacer muchas, muchas más tareas intrascendentes. El streamer Stable Ronaldo pasó 40 minutos pintando el dormitorio y, al terminar, volvió a empezar porque temía que el azul le hiciera parecer un crío. Otro se quejaba de llevar seis horas cortándose el pelo, haciendo la compra y eligiendo flores sin haber robado un coche. Y en sus primeras 12 horas con el juego, nuestro compañero Alejandro Alcolea hablaba de cómo había invertido un rato en dar de comer a una serpiente llamada Dolores.
Biblioteca de barrio. Hay 34 revistas, libros y cómics, y hay que localizar y leer 30 de ellos para completar el juego al cien por cien. Entre ellos, libros infantiles o un volumen sobre la unidad militar ORCA. No es lo único con lo que pasar el tiempo sin coger un arma: podrás catalogar 62 especies de aves y, en casa, una consola, la JoySystem, con la que jugar en la tele del salón.
Parodia redonda. Para quienes jugamos a 'GTA VI', pero también disfrutamos del juego como espectadores, nos sentimos casi en el centro de un experimento mental cuando invertimos horas en ver a streamers jugar a un juego en el que a su vez pasan horas sumergidos en una actividad pasiva sin componente lúdico. Un uróboros con forma de laberinto de espejos que hace que nos replanteemos la fórmula de la sátira que poníamos en duda antes de la llegada del juego: con su agujero negro de horas, 'GTA VI' es la mejor parodia jamás vista de un mundo real en el que estamos esclavizados por la economía de la atención.

articles.title: ¡Ya es oficial! ‘Ted Lasso’ tendrá temporada 5 en Apple TV
articles.text:
Tan solo unos pocos meses después del final de su temporada 4, Apple ha renovado oficialmente Ted Lasso para una temporada 5. Su exitosa serie regresará una vez más, curiosamente, después de que llegase a su presunto final en la tercera entrega hace unos años. la compañía y los fans pidieron que el proyecto continuase con nuevas historias y, finalmente, el equipo creativo liderado por Jason Sudeikis encontró la forma.
En la cuarta temporada, Ted regresaba a Ritchmond para entrenar al equipo femenino del club. Ahora, con la temporada 5 de Ted Lasso oficialmente en marcha en Apple TV, se espera que el proyecto continúe. En realida,d esta renovación tiene todo el sentido del mundo. Según la base de datos de Nielsen, el estreno de la cuarta temporada acumuló 296,6 millones de minutos de visionado en sus dos primeros días.
Estas cifras convirtieron a la temporada 4 de Ted Lasso en el estreno más visto de la historia de Apple TV. Por encima de cualquiera de las entregas anteriores y de otras series de éxito como Severance o For All Mankind. Ante un triunfo de esta magnitud, a la compañía no le quedaba otra opción que dar luz verde a una temporada más. Y es probable que próximamente también llegue una renovación para la sexta temporada, pues Sudeikis ya sugirió que le interesaba hacer un nuevo arco de tres entregas.
Qué pasará en la temporada de Ted Lasso
La cuarta temporada de la serie dejó algunos frentes abiertos sobre los que Ted Lasso deberá construir a partir de ahora en su temporada 5. Por ejemplo, Ted le dejaba el puesto de entrenadora del equipo femenino a Alice Chilton. A partir de los siguientes episodios, Ted solo será entrenador asistente junto a Beard.
Por otro lado, Roy Kent dejaba de ser el entrenador del equipo masculino al aceptar la oferta de entrenar al Chelsea. Además, Keeley y él esperan un hijo. Y, por su parte, Rebecca por fin se ha comprometido con Matthijs, así que es bastante probable que veamos la boda en la siguiente temporada.

articles.title: Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
articles.text:
Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string
- Date:
  November 11, 2026
- Source:
  ETH Zurich
- Summary:
  Researchers have created a quantum computer that stores information in microscopic vibrations, potentially making quantum machines smaller, more powerful, and better at preserving information. The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.
- Share:
A quantum computer might seem to have little in common with a guitar, but researchers at ETH Zurich have found a surprising connection. Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.
By harnessing these vibrations, the researchers have created a way for quantum computers to process information efficiently while accessing a flexible working memory. "The interaction between the quantum processor and the quantum memory provides a crucial foundation with a view to establishing quantum computers as a powerful and reliable way to perform computations that are not feasible with conventional computers," says Yiwen Chu.
The breakthrough, described in the journal Science, introduces a different approach to quantum computer design. Instead of closely integrating information processing and storage, as many existing systems do, Chu's team has developed an architecture that gives these functions more distinct roles.
Quantum Memory Inspired by Conventional Computers
The researchers drew inspiration from the basic design of everyday digital computers. In a conventional machine, the central processing unit (CPU) carries out calculations while information is held separately in working memory, commonly called random access memory (RAM). The arrangement of these components plays an important role in determining how efficiently a computer operates.
Chu's quantum system follows a similar principle. A superconducting qubit acts as the processing and control unit, performing a role comparable to that of the central processing unit (CPU). Meanwhile, a separate quantum memory temporarily holds the information needed during calculations, allowing the processor to retrieve and modify it as necessary.
The major difference lies in how that information is stored.
"In our quantum working memory, however, information is not stored electromagnetically -- as is usually the case today -- but rather in the form of mechanical vibrations," explains Chu.
Quantum computers take advantage of unusual properties of quantum physics, including superposition, which allows quantum systems to exist in combinations of different states, and entanglement, which creates powerful connections between quantum states. These effects could eventually enable quantum machines to tackle certain extremely complicated calculations much faster than conventional computers, including some problems that are currently beyond their practical capabilities.
Why Vibrating Quantum Memory Could Be Better
One of the greatest challenges in quantum computing is maintaining precise control over quantum information. The states used for calculations are delicate, and even small disturbances can cause information to be lost. To perform calculations reliably, the processor and memory must interact closely enough to transfer and manipulate quantum states with high precision.
In the new system, microscopic structures called mechanical resonators hold information in particular patterns of vibration. When the superconducting qubit needs that information, it accesses the stored vibrational state, performs the required operation, and returns the modified information to memory.
Many existing quantum computers instead use electromagnetic memory alongside superconducting qubits. Researchers understand these technologies well, and they can be combined to provide extremely accurate control over quantum states, including reading, changing, and manipulating stored information.
However, electromagnetic memory systems have a significant disadvantage. They can occupy considerable space, making it difficult to expand experimental quantum devices into the larger, more capable computers that researchers and industries ultimately need.
Mechanical resonators offer several potential advantages. They are substantially smaller, allowing more compact designs. They can also support numerous different patterns of vibration, providing opportunities to store more information simultaneously than conventional electromagnetic memory.
Another important benefit is that mechanical vibrations can preserve quantum states for longer periods before the stored information begins to fade. Longer storage times could make it easier to carry out complicated calculations that require information to remain available throughout multiple processing steps.
New Quantum Computer Passes Major Tests
The research published in Science provides the first experimental demonstration that mechanical resonators can work together with superconducting qubits to carry out quantum computations. The results establish that vibration-based memory is a feasible alternative to electromagnetic storage.
The achievement goes beyond simply storing information. Chu's team demonstrated that its architecture can handle both relatively straightforward calculations and more demanding quantum operations.
To evaluate the system, the researchers tested two important computational techniques: the quantum Fourier transform and period finding. Both are fundamental tools in quantum computing and require a computer to coordinate multiple quantum states with considerable precision.
"The Quantum Fourier Transform is a fundamental computational procedure required for many quantum algorithms. The period-finding algorithm we implemented served as a demonstration of how this procedure can be used," explains Igor Kladaric, doctoral student in Chu's team and co-author of the publication.
Successfully completing these tasks requires the system to store, control, and maintain coherent relationships among multiple quantum states at the same time. The experiments showed that the new architecture can meet these requirements, providing strong evidence that it can support genuine quantum computation rather than simply function as a memory device.
A Promising Step Toward Powerful Quantum Computers
One of the most significant findings is that the new system can, in principle, carry out all the fundamental operations needed for arbitrary quantum computations. This means the architecture has the essential capabilities required for a programmable, general-purpose quantum computer.
However, demonstrating those capabilities in an experimental chip is only the beginning. The next major challenge is scaling the technology to larger systems with greater processing power while preserving the precision and reliability demonstrated in the laboratory.
Chu and her colleagues are continuing to investigate how their approach can be developed further. Its long-term success will depend on whether mechanical quantum memory can remain effective as more components and increasingly complex computations are added.
Practical quantum computers powerful enough for widespread scientific and industrial applications are still some distance away. Nevertheless, by showing that tiny mechanical vibrations can serve as compact, capable quantum memory, the ETH Zurich team has demonstrated a promising new route toward making those machines a reality.

articles.title: OpenAI, Cisco Unveil Open Source Tool to Shield Unpatched Linux Systems
articles.text:
OpenAI and Cisco on Monday unveiled Shirudo, an open source security platform that uses AI agents to prevent the exploitation of vulnerabilities in Linux systems and applications.
The project is an AI-focused rewrite of Cisco-owned Isovalent’s Tetragon runtime security platform. Tetragon was open-sourced in 2022, and it also powers Cisco’s Live Protect vulnerability mitigation technology.
Shirudo is designed to help defenders address the challenges introduced by AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery and exploitation, which is increasing pressure on organizations to deploy patches quickly.
The tool leverages eBPF technology to modify Linux kernel behavior without restarting the OS.
According to Cisco and OpenAI, agents can analyze vulnerability information, generate so-called ‘shields’ to prevent exploitation, and test their effectiveness without disrupting important services. Security teams still retain control over which shields are deployed.
Protections are digitally signed and verified before deployment, with mechanisms designed to prevent even attackers with root privileges from disabling kernel-level enforcement.
In a controlled test targeting the recent Java4Shell vulnerability, a shield generated using OpenAI’s Codex blocked an exploitation attempt targeting an Elasticsearch instance without requiring a restart.
Shirudo is currently in pre-release development and not ready for production use. The tool requires specific Linux kernel capabilities, additional kernel patches, and TPM 2.0.
OpenAI and Cisco hope that down the line Shirudo shields can be distributed alongside vulnerability disclosures to give organizations temporary protection until they can install permanent patches.
Amiram Shachar, CEO and co-founder of cloud security firm Upwind, commented, “Writing the most sensitive kernel code on the fly and deploying it straight to runtime is a very risky concept. I love the idea, but doing it with open source is very risky.”
“There are countless Linux versions and distributions this has to work across. It needs to be tested, packaged and automated before anyone should trust it in production,” Shachar added.

articles.title: Huang reportedly admitted to more than two affairs to Nvidia's board
articles.text:
In a complete U-turn, Nvidia’s board on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as the CEO and president of the chipmaker, just a fortnight after he resigned.
During a meeting before his reinstatement, however, Huang admitted to more affairs beyond the two that have been reported in the news, according to The Wall Street Journal.
Early in November, Huang admitted to an extramarital affair in a letter to employees. At the time, he was ostensibly talking about his relationship with Megaspeed executive and alleged Chinese spy, Alice Huang (not related to Jensen). Later, it was reported that he’d also had a relationship with Nvidia’s VP of health, Kimberly Powell.
Afterwards, Reuters reported that he also had an affair with another employee.
It’s not clear which affairs Huang admitted to during this recent conversation with Nvidia’s board of directors.
Huang’s return was spurred by a personal intervention from the U.S. government, Nvidia’s board said in a statement on Monday, and President Donald Trump apparently called the board to bat for Huang’s reinstatement.
The Wall Street Journal reports that over the weekend, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche told Trump and Vice President JD Vance that the Justice Department wasn’t investigating Huang and there was no evidence that he was a national security risk, after which both contacted the company’s board.
Huang received a “hero’s welcome” at Nvidia’s HQ, with several employees applauding his return.

articles.title: Now Firefox can select which sites use its VPN, and clear your browsing history with one click
articles.text:
Mozilla released Firefox 161 on Tuesday with a new setting you can use to choose which pages automatically open with the browser’s VPN active. Using the “Manage VPN rules” option in Firefox’s VPN panel, you can set it to “always on” or “always off” for specific sites, so you don’t have to toggle it manually every time you visit certain pages.
Now Firefox can select which sites use its VPN, and clear your browsing history with one click
The new ‘Fire’ button can wipe history, cookies, and other data right from your toolbar.
Starting Tuesday, Mozilla is also rolling out a “Fire” button in standard Firefox windows that lets you quickly clear your browsing data directly from the toolbar. You can choose which data it deletes, including browsing history, downloads history, cookie data, site data, temporary files, saved form info, and website permissions and preferences. If you set the button to delete all of that data, clicking it will sign you out of everything and open a fresh Firefox window.
Tuesday’s Firefox update also adds an option for creating a keyboard shortcut for copying your current tab’s URL, and brings its “read aloud” option in Reader Mode to the Android version of Firefox. Alongside the update, Mozilla says Firefox is also now available directly through the Play Store on cars with Google built-in.

articles.title: AI’s hunger for compute could break uranium’s boom-bust cycle
articles.text:
Saskatchewan is home to some of the world’s largest, richest uranium deposits. Developing those deposits has turned Canada into the world’s second-largest producer of the radioactive metal. The industry has been beset by gruelling boom-and-bust cycles, but those cycles may soon end as demand for nuclear power—and the uranium to fuel it—continues to ramp up.
“AI needs reliable, carbon-free power, and nuclear [power] needs uranium. It’s a hand-in-hand solution.”
Eduardo Buriticà
Located near the Northwest Territories, Saskatchewan’s Athabasca Basin contains so much uranium that just a small stretch of its more than 100,000-square-kilometre territory has the potential to power more than 40 million homes for around 25 years. Following a particularly lucrative market boom in 2024, the World Nuclear Association predicted that Canada would overtake Kazakhstan as the world’s leading uranium supplier.
That hasn’t happened yet. Commodities market prices have actually fallen somewhat since 2024, but Canada’s uranium sector is still very much experiencing a boom. Between 2019 and 2024, the price of uranium climbed 233 percent, according to reporting by Bloomberg. Gold, another valuable commodity, grew in comparison by just 75 percent.
“The World Nuclear Association projects that reactor requirements will grow 28 percent by 2030 and will more than double by 2040,” said Eduardo Buriticà, the director of external affairs for Canadian Uranium Corporation. Canadian Uranium owns a nearly 16,000-hectare uranium mining project known as Rook II in the Athabasca Basin.
Growth in the industry has experienced peaks and valleys over the past half-decade, but overall trendlines show an increase. That growth is driven, at least in part, by a global renaissance in nuclear development. According to nuclear data platform Yellowcake Analytics, there are more than 400 nuclear reactors operating worldwide; another 80 or so are under construction, and hundreds more are in the planning and development stages.
That resurgence has been spurred on by renewed interest in nuclear’s potential for clean energy after years of declining investment following Japan’s Fukushima disaster. It accelerated again after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.
Increasingly, though, industry insiders see another source of demand emerging: AI.
“Demand is rising due to countries building and restarting nuclear reactors, but the data electricity demand from data centres and AI is only adding to it,” Buriticà said. “Demand for energy is not going to go down anytime soon, especially with the focus on data centres. We’re only seeing that trend go up.”
“AI needs reliable, carbon-free power, and nuclear [power] needs uranium. It’s a hand-in-hand solution,” he added.
Reza Mohammed is Canadian Uranium’s site exploration manager. Mohammed coordinates teams of geologists and contractors, handles site permitting, and helps come up with potential geographic targets for uranium exploration. A geologist with more than 30 years of experience in the Canadian uranium industry, Mohammed sees much the same opportunity as Buriticà does in AI’s scale of demand. Nuclear power, he argues, has distinct advantages for servicing that particular kind of need.
“[AI and data centres] need power, and they need modular power,” Mohammed said. “[Nuclear] is a scalable power source; you can have mobile reactors or massive reactors.”
“Demand for energy is not going to go down anytime soon, especially with the focus on data centres. We’re only seeing that trend go up.”
Eduardo Buriticà
Mohammed’s not speculating. Small, modular nuclear reactors, also called SMRs, have caught the attention of tech giants like Amazon, Meta, and Google, all of which have invested in the technology. SMRs are compact nuclear reactors that can be assembled where needed, allowing them to operate in remote or isolated areas, or in conjunction with other forms of power. They’re also grid-independent, meaning they can prevent transmission loss and reduce dependency on traditional or shared electric grids.
That influx of interest from governments and private businesses has not gone unnoticed by Saskatchewan or Canada. Both governments have moved to prioritize nuclear and uranium development, with the feds aiming to double production by 2035 and Regina looking to further cement nuclear energy as a key economic driver for the province.
Demand is slated to grow: the World Nuclear Association forecasts that by 2040, the world could face a shortfall in uranium supplies by as much as 40,000 tonnes, with that forecast coming prior to any accounting for the additional demands of AI. That presents an opportunity for Saskatchewan and Canada to fill a gap. With the basin’s vast resources, supply is no issue. But whether an industry accustomed to such volatile cycles can handle this kind of sustained demand is an open question.

Used with a verification plan derived from the exact UCIe revision and the design’s supported options, these capabilities help teams build a connected view of both normal operation and failure response.

articles.title: Bouygues Telecom a vendu 5 000 forfaits avec Deezer ou Amazon Prime en une semaine
articles.text:
Bouygues Telecom a écoulé 5 000 forfaits B&YOU Pack Deezer et Pack Amazon Prime en une seule semaine de Black Friday. Un démarrage qui conforte l'opérateur dans son idée de réunir forfait mobile et services de divertissement sur la même facture.
Sept semaines après leur lancement, les forfaits B&YOU Les Packs commencent à « faire leur trou » auprès du grand public. Pas moins de 5 000 Packs Deezer et Amazon Prime ont trouvé preneur en une semaine, à la faveur du Black Friday, selon des chiffres dont Clubic a pris connaissance en exclusivité. Ces forfaits mobiles sans engagement intègrent directement un service numérique, sur une facture unique. Les ventes se sont toutefois faites à prix remisé, sur une offre affichée en quantité limitée. Mais le pari est gagné pour l'opérateur.
Les Packs B&YOU ont passé leur premier test grandeur nature
Les 5 000 ventes ne concernent que les deux derniers-nés de la gamme, lancés le 5 octobre, à savoir le B&YOU Pack Amazon Prime et le B&YOU Pack Deezer. La formule comprend un forfait sans engagement de 170 Go en 5G, dont 60 Go utilisables en Europe et dans les DOM, avec des appels et SMS illimités. L'un des packs fournit Prime Video, avec la livraison Premium gratuite et un accès anticipé aux Ventes Flash. De l'autre, c'est Deezer Premium qui est livré, pour écouter sa musique en illimité et en meilleure qualité. Notons que nous parlons de packs réservés à l'ouverture d'une nouvelle ligne, sur le site de Bouygues Telecom.
Pour l'occasion, l'opérateur a accordé une remise de 3 euros par mois sur les deux packs. Le Pack Prime s'affiche ainsi à 14,99 euros, contre 17,99 euros lors de son lancement, et le Pack Deezer profite de la même ristourne sur un prix de départ de 19,99 euros. Pour Bouygues Telecom, cette semaine de promotions Black Friday a servi de banc d'essai, et le résultat dépasserait ses attentes internes.
Du coup, chez l'opérateur, forcément, on savoure. « Ces résultats confirment que nous avons vu juste : nos clients attendaient une offre qui simplifie réellement leur quotidien numérique et font le choix d'un forfait qui embarque directement leurs services préférés », se félicite Marc Laurier, directeur marketing grand public de l'opérateur. Bouygues Telecom en est convaincu, les Français ne veulent plus jongler entre leur forfait d'un côté et leurs abonnements de divertissement de l'autre. L'argument d'une seule facture, et d'un service accessible depuis le téléphone comme sur les autres écrans semble avoir fonctionné.
Une recette forfait et streaming appelée à s'enrichir
Ce démarrage réussi prolonge celui du B&YOU Pack beIN SPORTS, l'aîné de la famille, lancé en juin pour les 15 ans de la marque, juste avant la Coupe du monde. Affiché à 24,99 euros par mois au lancement des nouveaux packs, il donne accès aux chaînes beIN SPORTS via l'application b.tv, sur deux écrans en simultané. Du sport à la musique, en passant par les séries et les colis, Bouygues Telecom revendique ainsi le titre de premier opérateur à avoir intégré nativement un service numérique au cœur d'un forfait mobile.
Pour étayer son pari, l'opérateur s'appuie sur l'étude Usages et Attitudes réalisée il y a deux ans par Ipsos, pour son compte. Chez les clients qu'il range dans la catégorie des « digitaux autonomes », 86 % ont un abonnement SVOD de type Netflix ou Prime Video, et 31 % sont abonnés à un service de streaming musical comme Spotify ou Deezer. Au quotidien, 52 % passent par leur mobile pour regarder des vidéos ou la télévision, ou pour écouter de la musique. Hier encore, s'affichait sur le site de Bouygues Telecom une « Limite des 5 000 bientôt atteinte », en ajoutant que le Pack Prime y est présenté comme une « série spéciale ». Peut-être que ce succès donnera des idées à l'opérateur.
Il sera intéressant de voir comment ces packs se comporteront une fois les étiquettes Black Friday décrochées. D'autant que forfait et abonnement sont indissociables, puisque résilier l'un, c'est résilier l'autre. Les abonnés Prime ou Deezer tentés par l'aventure doivent aussi d'abord résilier leur abonnement en direct, puis se reconnecter avec leurs identifiants habituels pour garder leur historique. Bouygues Telecom, lui, regarde déjà plus loin. « C'est la preuve que cette nouvelle catégorie de forfaits répond à un vrai besoin, et nous avons bien l'intention de continuer à l'enrichir », promet Marc Laurier. articles.title: ASUS Turbo Radeon AI PRO R9700 Review
articles.text:
While much of the attention in the market for AI inference has been focused on servers and datacenter-scale deployments, the heart and soul of the modern AI revolution started with video cards. And that is where it still beats on today, overshadowed by servers but still an important market segment overall.
Within the AMD ecosystem, the company has taken a very visible pivot in how it markets and categorizes its professional video cards. The Radeon Pro lineup, once the backbone of AMD’s workstation graphics efforts, has become the Radeon AI Pro lineup, and the backbone of AMD’s add-in video card/AI accelerator efforts. The flagship for this line, in turn, is the Radeon AI Pro R9700, a 32GB VRAM card that AMD and its partners are positioning as a more budget-friendly alternative to NVIDIA’s RTX PRO Blackwell lineup of workstation cards.
Today we are taking a look at one of those R9700 cards in the form of ASUS’s Turbo Radeon AI Pro R9700. The sub-$2000 card have been heavily optimized for workstation use, balancing graphics needs and display outputs with the ability to fit up to four cards into a single system for larger AI workloads.
ASUS Turbo Radeon AI PRO R9700 Hardware Overview
As AMD is not selling their own reference design workstation cards for this generation, it falls to AMD’s partners to sell the cards instead. Which is a production strategy that they are well-accustomed to on the consumer side of matters, but is a bit more unusual for a workstation card.
Notably, AMD has been keeping their Radeon Pro partners on a rather short leash with card designs. AMD is curating a very specific image for a very specific market here, not the least of which is the ability to install multiple cards in a single workstation. As a result, though AMD is not selling their reference card their partner cards are all quite similar in their high-level design as dual slot blowers, a form factor you will not readily find outside of workstation video cards these days.
That brings us to ASUS’s Turbo Radeon AI PRO R9700. ASUS has long been a heavyweight in the world of video cards, so it is no surprise to see them jump on board producing a Radeon Pro card.
ASUS’s R9700 card is, in all practical application, exactly what you would expect from a workstation card given the form factor and the AMD’s constraints. This is a dual slot video card that follows the PCIe specifications to a T in terms of width and height, in order to ensure that it (and perhaps a few of its friends) can fit into a workstation chassis.
| ASUS Turbo Radeon AI R9700 Specifications |  |  |  | 
| CUs | 64 |  |  | 
| AI Accelerators | 128 |  |  | 
| GPU Boost Clockspeed | 2.92GHz |  |  | 
| Peak Matrix Throughput (FP8) | 382.7 TFLOPS |  |  | 
| Peak Vector Throughput (FP32) | 47.8 TFLOPS |  |  | 
| Memory | 32GB GDDR6 |  |  | 
| Memory Bandwidth | 640GB/sec (20Gbps x 256-bits) |  |  | 
| ECC | Yes (Linux Only) |  |  | 
| Infinity Cache | 64MB |  |  | 
| I/O | PCIe Gen5 x16 |  |  | 
| TBP | 300W |  |  | 
| Form Factor | PCIe CEM (Air Cooled) |  |  | 
| Dimensions | 267 x 111 x 40 mm (10.5 x 4.4 x 1.6 in) |  |  | 
| Architecture | RDNA 4 |  |  | 
| GPU | Navi 48 |  |  | 
Under the hood, the card is powered by AMD’s Navi 48 GPU, which is the most powerful RDNA 4 GPU offered in this generation. The GPU offers 64 of AMD’s CUs, which in turn is comprised of a total of 4096 shading units for vector math and 128 AI accelerator cores for matrix operations.
With a peak clock speed of 2.92GHz, this gives the R9700 a peak matrix math throughput of 382.7 TFLOPS with dense FP8 math, or double that with sparsity. One of the key improvements in this generation of RDNA architecture is the addition of FP8 support, which not only further improves the compute throughput of the card, but it better aligns AMD’s hardware with the general trends in the industry towards lower precision weights, and fitting a large number of weights within a given amount of memory.
On that note, as is traditional for a workstation card, AMD and ASUS have packed the R9700 with as much memory as the card can handle. With Navi 48 sporting a 256-bit bus, the card has been equipped with 32GB of GDDR6 memory organized as 16 2Gbit chips in clamshell mode. Above all else, memory support is a key differentiator between AMD’s consumer and professional cards, so 32GB is something you will only find on the Radeon AI Pro cards.
The GDDR6 memory itself is clocked at 20Gbps, allowing for a total of 640GB/second of memory bandwidth for the card. Soft ECC is also available, though only under Linux (and even then, it has to be manually enabled). This allows for an extra degree of reliability for systems and racks based around the card.
Navi 48 itself is somewhere between a mid to high-end GPU as far as die size (357mm2) and transistor counts (53.9B) go, which makes it a bit of an oddity within AMD’s lineup as far as card progression is concerned. AMD did not produce a true high-end GPU this generation, and as a result the R9700 actually has less VRAM than the previous-generation 48GB Radeon Pro W7900. This means that it is a step back in terms of overall memory capacity, but AMD is looking to make up the difference with compute throughput, thanks in large part to the newer chip architecture.
One advantage of being a smaller chip, however, is that it keeps TDPs in check. AMD (and ASUS’s) Total Board Power figure for the card is just 300 Watts, which makes it relatively easy to keep a blower-style card cooled without a blowout on noise. This also means that even 4 cards in a system is not going to result in excessive power requirements, though it will certainly be pushing the limits of a single power supply.
ASUS Turbo Radeon AI PRO R9700 Build and Design
As far as video card designs go, ASUS’s Turbo Radeon AI Pro R9700 is a very typical dual slot blower design. With a need to ensure that the card can be installed in multiples together, ASUS has kept things tightly tuned to PCIe specifications, with a dual slot card measuring 10.5 inches long and 4.4 inches high.
Interestingly, the blower design here is open-backed, that is, the back side of the card has open vents so that the card can pull in air from both sides of the card.
The fan itself is a pretty typical blower design. According to ASUS they are using dual ball bearings here.
Taking a look at the rear of the card, we can better see the venting cut into the card’s PCB and its shroud. For that matter, we can also see that the card even has a shroud on its back side. As noted earlier, the 32GB of GDDR6 is organized in a clamshell configuration on the R9700, meaning that 8 chips are on the rear of the card and need to be protected and cooled, just as with all of the chips on the front side of the card.
Being that this is a workstation card, ASUS has also put some thought into their power connector placement. The Turbo R9700 uses an ATX 12V-2×6 connector, which has been placed on the rear of the card instead of the top, another workstation-centric design element that makes it easier to install multiple cards in a system. The 12V-2×6 connector is rated for up to 600W, so the 300W TBP R9700 is well within the cable’s limits.
Meanwhile, at the front of the card we find a not too subtle reminder that this is a video card, with 4 display outputs – the maximum number of displays the Navi 48 GPU can drive. ASUS has given their card a triple DisplayPort plus single HDMI port configuration. The DisplayPorts are all DisplayPort 2.1a, while the HDMI port supports HDMI 2.1b. Coupled with DSC, and the card can drive displays at up to 12K in resolution.
Otherwise, besides the display outputs, the rest of the front of the card is almost entirely vent cut-outs. 300W is still a lot of heat to expel from a blower card, so ASUS does not hold back here, and you can clearly see the fins from the heatsink running within the card.
With our hardware tour complete, let us take a look at the performance of the Turbo R9700

articles.title: Black Friday : la cafetière avec broyeur Delonghi Magnifica S s'affiche à 258,00 €
articles.text:
Black Friday : La machine à café à grain Delonghi Magnifica S à 258,00 €
La Delonghi Magnifica S passe à 258,00 € chez Electro Depot. Simple à entretenir et rapide pour préparer les boissons au quotidien, cette cafetière automatique affiche une note actuelle de 3,5/5 dans nos tests.
La cafetière Delonghi Magnifica S ouvre la gamme avec broyeur du fabricant italien en misant sur l'efficacité au quotidien. Elle permet de préparer des boissons à partir de café en grains tout en conservant des réglages manuels pratiques pour ajuster sa tasse. Ce modèle d'entrée de gamme s'est distingué lors de son passage dans notre labo par son fonctionnement rapide et discret.
L'appareil descend à 258,00 € chez Electro Depot
Une utilisation quotidienne simple et des réglages complets
Cette machine automatique s'adresse aux personnes qui cherchent un premier équipement à grains facile à vivre. Son bac à grains accueille 250 g de café et son réservoir d'eau propose un volume de 1,8 L, ce qui évite les remplissages constants entre deux préparations. Comme souligné dans notre test complet, la cafetière sait se montrer rapide à l'allumage et discrète lors du broyage.
Le panneau de commande autorise plusieurs ajustements utiles au quotidien. Il est possible de modifier la finesse de la mouture grâce au broyeur en acier, mais aussi de personnaliser la température de l'eau et l'intensité en tasse. Deux cafés peuvent également couler simultanément si nécessaire.
Delonghi Magnifica S
Points forts
- Facile à utiliser et simple à entretenir.
- Format relativement compact.
- Silencieuse et rapide.
- Options bienvenues (réglages des températures, dureté de l'eau, finesse de la mouture).
- Accès facile à l'extracteur.
- Afficheur LCD.
Points faibles
- Pas d'informations textuelles sur l'écran.
- Pas de passage au lave-vaisselle.
Un entretien manuel obligatoire et quelques limites d'affichage
Pour conserver un tarif serré, l'appareil impose deux concessions pratiques à connaître avant l'achat. L'écran de la machine n'affiche pas d'informations textuelles détaillées pour guider les réglages, ce qui demande de se référer aux voyants lumineux pour comprendre les alertes.
Le nettoyage des différents bacs demande également un soin particulier : les éléments amovibles ne sont pas compatibles avec le lave-vaisselle et doivent être lavés à la main. L'accès direct à l'extracteur facilite toutefois cette routine pour les utilisateurs prêts à réaliser ce nettoyage manuel.
Cuisinart EM550E : l'autre option face au Delonghi Magnifica S
La Cuisinart EM550E propose une autre approche pour s'équiper avec un budget plus réduit. Elle intègre également un broyeur et ajoute une fonction Cold Brew dédiée aux extractions à froid, tout en occupant un espace plus restreint sur le plan de travail. Elle demande en revanche davantage de concessions sur la personnalisation des recettes et sur l'automatisation de son entretien par rapport au modèle italien.
La Cuisinart EM550E est vendue à un tarif inférieur de 53,02 € par rapport à la Delonghi Magnifica S, mais la Magnifica S conserve une note actuelle de 3,5/5 contre 3/5 pour sa rivale grâce à ses réglages de mouture et de température plus complets.
Cuisinart EM550E
Points forts
- Record de compacité.
- Très bon dosage de café.
- Fonction Cold Brew.
- Machine silencieuse.
- Chambre d'extraction accessible.
Points faibles
- Aucune personnalisation de l'arôme ou de la température.
- Maintenance manuelle pour le détartrage.

articles.title: New Shirudo tool uses AI to shield unpatched Linux systems from exploits
articles.text:
OpenAI and Cisco launched an open-source Linux security tool named Shirudo that deploys temporary runtime protections to block vulnerability exploitation while administrators prepare and roll out patches, without restarting services.
Shirudo leverages the eBPF (extended Berkeley Packet Filter) mechanism in Linux to monitor for suspicious activity and deploy targeted protections called "shields."
eBPF is a Linux technology that lets programs run in a controlled environment within the operating system's kernel without modifying its source code or requiring a restart.
It enables real-time monitoring of system and network activity, performance analysis, and enforcement of targeted security protections, making it an ideal operational basis for Shirudo.
Shirudo’s shields aim to block malicious behavior in a targeted way, leaving legitimate application operations undisturbed. OpenAI highlights four core capabilities for the tool:
- Live protection: Blocks vulnerable code paths without restarting systems, letting operators assess shield impact before enforcing them.
- AI-assisted defense: Enables agents to investigate vulnerabilities, develop shields, and validate their effectiveness, with deployment remaining under human control.
- Trusted deployment: Uses cryptographic signatures, Linux's eBPF verifier, and kernel security controls to prevent unauthorized modifications.
- Hardware-backed verification: Uses Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) to provide verifiable records of shields being loaded or removed.
OpenAI and Cisco researchers tested custom-generated shields and demonstrated that they could successfully block a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without interrupting its operation.
Marcus Hutchins, principal threat researcher at managed detection and response company Expel, says that while there is "genuinely so much runtime exploit mitigation potential with eBPF," it may not be a good idea to let AI agents write rules that could impact the kernel.
He also noted that the tool's "capabilities are limited to Linux because Mac/Windows haven't implement the components needed to be effective."
Researchers at Isovalent, a cloud networking and security company acquired by Cisco in 2024, explain that "Shirudo is a rewrite of Tetragon," an open-source eBPF-based runtime security platform the company introduced in 2022, which also serves as the foundation for Cisco's existing Live Protect technology.
Shirudo is designed for agentic control plane, and a configurable degree of autonomy when it comes to deploying mitigations. Isovalent says the tool isn’t limited to eBPF and can also modify application or userspace runtime bytecode to extend protection where needed.
When a shield is deployed, they also provide operators with hit counts, giving them insight into attempted exploits and where defenses need strengthening.
The two companies plan to provide “ready-to-use” mitigations in the form of tested shields, along with vulnerability disclosures, until patching is possible. Shields will be distributed as cryptographically signed ‘.bee’ packages through an OCI registry.
Isovalent says that Shirudo can be activated through a command-line interface and doesn’t require a daemon to run permanently on the machine.
"The Shirudo project is only the beginning, but it already shows the true potential of combining agents as a workforce with machine interfaces to let agents output what they are best at: code," the researchers say.
They expect the tool to evolve and other projects to emerge around it, to the point of building self-defending that can run applications and agents side by side.
Shirudo is open-source (BSD + GPL) and comes with a quick-start guide as well as "getting started" documentation from Isovalent.
In a deep-dive webinar on December 15, OpenAI will provide a technical rundown of how the tool works and how it combines eBPF and artificial intelligence to detect and counter new attacks.

articles.title: Une arnaque vise les stations-service et les distributeurs de billets en France : comment éviter de se faire piéger ?
articles.text:
Nous avons ici affaire à une arnaque sophistiquée qui cible plus particulièrement les stations-service et les distributeurs de billets. Plusieurs victimes ont été recensées en France ces derniers jours, avec des montants dérobés allant de 500 à plus de 1 000 euros. Il faut dire que cette arnaque est difficilement repérable. Une victime peut effectuer un paiement ou retirer de l’argent en saisissant son code PIN, sans rien remarquer. Cependant, un point précis peut alerter sur la situation.
Une minuscule caméra et un lecteur de carte piégé pour vider vos comptes bancaires
Une nouvelle arnaque, particulièrement élaborée, a été repérée à plusieurs reprises ces derniers jours en France. Cette arnaque vise plus particulièrement les stations-service et les distributeurs de billets. En d’autres termes, tous les dispositifs qui demandent d’insérer une carte bancaire et de saisir un code PIN. Le mode de fonctionnement de cette arnaque est, il faut le dire, sophistiqué. Comme l’explique BFMTV, les arnaqueurs parviennent à intégrer un dispositif dans le lecteur de carte d’un système de paiement. Ce dispositif est ensuite capable d’intercepter les données échangées avec la puce de la carte bancaire. Il est ici plus précisément question de skimming, une technique qui consiste à insérer un boîtier très fin dans le lecteur afin de récupérer les données de la carte.
En parallèle, les arnaqueurs placent une minuscule caméra juste au-dessus du pavé numérique destiné à saisir le code bancaire. Ainsi, les escrocs disposent finalement des données de la carte bancaire, mais aussi du code confidentiel de leur victime. Selon les témoignages publiés en ligne par certaines victimes, les montants dérobés vont de 500 à plus de 1 000 euros.
Comment ne pas tomber dans le piège de cette arnaque
Autant dire que ce type d’arnaque bancaire n’est pas facilement repérable. Cependant, un point précis peut alerter sur la situation. En effet, le dispositif utilisé par les arnaqueurs demande à la victime de recomposer son code PIN. Par conséquent, si un système de paiement vous demande de composer une seconde fois votre code bancaire, il est vivement conseillé de changer de borne ou de faire preuve de la plus grande prudence, en mettant un terme à la transaction et en appelant par exemple un membre du personnel.
Veillez également à masquer le pavé numérique avec votre autre main lorsque vous saisissez votre code PIN. Pour rappel, les escrocs peuvent dissimuler une minuscule caméra juste au-dessus de celui-ci afin de filmer la saisie de votre code confidentiel. Faites également attention au terminal de paiement. Les arnaqueurs ayant placé d’autres appareils pour enregistrer les données bancaires des victimes, des anomalies peuvent être présentes (éléments inhabituels ou mal fixés).
Enfin, privilégiez le paiement sans contact et surveillez de près vos comptes bancaires. En cas de transaction anormale, contactez votre banque sans attendre.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.text:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
  November 7, 2026
- Source:
  University of Regensburg
- Summary:
  Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.
The discovery comes from an international collaboration involving research groups at the Regensburg Center for Ultrafast Nanoscopy (RUN), led by Profs. Jascha Repp, Rupert Huber, Franz Giessibl, and Klaus Richter, along with a team at the Max Planck Institute in Hamburg led by Angel Rubio.
Watching Electrons Move at Incredible Speeds
Understanding how matter behaves at the smallest scales is essential for developing the next generation of technology. Advances in clean energy, quantum computing, and powerful electronics for artificial intelligence all depend on knowing how chemical reactions unfold, how light interacts with materials, and how electrons travel through electronic devices.
However, even the sharpest microscopic photographs cannot reveal the full picture. Scientists also need to observe how these processes change over time, effectively creating slow-motion movies of events occurring at the atomic scale.
At RUN, researchers are developing ultrafast microscopes capable of recording the movements of electrons, atoms, and molecules with extraordinary precision in both space and time. About ten years ago, scientists in Regensburg used ultrafast scanning tunneling microscopy to resolve the movement of a single molecule across space and time for the first time.
Tracking individual electrons presents an even greater challenge. At these microscopic distances, electrons can move roughly a thousand times faster than atoms and molecules, with important changes taking place over just attoseconds.
To appreciate how extreme these scales are, consider that an atom is approximately ten million times smaller than a millimeter. An attosecond is one-billionth of a billionth of a second. The difference between an attosecond and a second is comparable to the difference between one second and the entire age of the universe.
Making these measurements is especially difficult because electrons do not behave like ordinary objects. Their motion follows the unusual laws of quantum mechanics rather than the familiar rules of classical physics.
Ultrafast Lasers Reveal Quantum Tunneling
To observe electron behavior at these extraordinary speeds, the researchers built a new laser system that provides much finer time resolution than earlier experiments. The system allows them to control and study the quantum motion of individual electrons directly.
In the experiments, carefully timed laser pulses drive electrons from an extremely sharp metal tip toward a silver surface. The distance they travel is only a few atomic diameters.
The researchers detect this movement by measuring the resulting electrical current. To determine exactly when the electrons move, they use two pulses of light separated by a precisely controlled interval.
Simon Maier, the lead author of the paper, explains: "By varying the time interval between the two laser pulses, we can directly observe how the electrons respond."
This approach revealed clear evidence of electron motion occurring on attosecond timescales. It showed that the laser pulses could transfer electrons within these incredibly brief intervals while allowing scientists to observe the process as it happened.
What makes the result particularly remarkable is how the electrons travel. Instead of moving like conventional particles, they behave as quantum waves. This allows them to pass through an energy barrier separating the metal tip from the silver surface, even though classical physics predicts they should not have enough energy to cross it.
This phenomenon, known as quantum tunneling, is somewhat like an object passing through a solid wall without breaking or damaging it.
"Our measurement can be understood as a high-speed camera for the electron wave packets, since you can see at what point in time the tunneling process takes place," explains Katharina Glöckl, a doctoral student and co-author of the publication.
A Surprising 500-Attosecond Delay
To understand the measurements more deeply, researchers working with Prof. Angel Rubio performed sophisticated quantum simulations of the electrons' behavior near the "space-time limit."
Their calculations closely reproduced the experimental findings and uncovered another remarkable detail. The electrons did not respond to the light field instantaneously. Instead, their motion lagged behind it by approximately 500 attoseconds.
At such extreme scales, several fundamental features of quantum physics become important simultaneously.
For example, the researchers found that the laser pulses could not be described entirely by treating light as a wave or entirely by treating it as individual particles called photons. Their effects displayed characteristics of both descriptions. This combination was essential for exploring electron behavior so close to the "space-time limit."
The team also discovered that controlling electron motion over extremely short intervals changes how the electrons are distributed in space. Quantum mechanics describes these electrons using wave packets, which represent how their wave properties extend across different locations.
The relationship between the timing of electron motion and the spatial extent of these wave packets revealed the central limitation behind the discovery.
A Hidden Tradeoff Between Space and Time
Raffael Spachtholz, another co-author of the study, explains: "The more precisely we want to pin down the electron's position in time, the more energy we need to provide. And as a result, the electron wave packet spreads out more spatially."
In other words, improving the precision of an electron's timing comes with a cost. The more tightly researchers define when its motion occurs, the more broadly its quantum wave packet spreads through space.
To examine this relationship experimentally, the team placed a single atom on the surface to confine the electron wave packets to an extremely small region immediately before the laser pulses arrived.
This setup allowed the scientists to directly measure the connection between the electrons' spatial distribution and the timing of their motion.
Importantly, even when the electrons received substantial energy from the laser pulses, their wave packets remained sufficiently localized for microscopy with atomic spatial resolution and attosecond time resolution.
The findings provide experimental insight into a fundamental space-time constraint that scientists had previously only suspected. They also make it possible to systematically investigate how changes in electron motion over time affect the spatial structure of quantum wave functions.
Could Quantum Electronics Become Hundreds of Thousands of Times Faster?
Beyond revealing a new aspect of quantum behavior, the discovery could open the door to technologies that operate on timescales far beyond the capabilities of today's electronics.
One especially promising possibility involves using precisely controlled electron wave packets to influence chemical reactions.
Transferring a single electron to a molecule represents the smallest possible transfer of electric charge. But when that electron is concentrated within an exceptionally small region of space and time, the resulting local peak current density can reach as much as 1 trillion amperes per square centimeter.
Such extreme conditions could give scientists new ways to control chemical bonds and observe how molecules change during reactions.
"In the future, we want to use such wave packets to specifically trigger chemical reactions and observe, on the relevant length and time scales, how chemical bonds can be broken or altered," explains Prof. Jascha Repp enthusiastically.
The implications could extend well beyond chemistry. Greater control over electron motion may eventually help engineers develop electronic devices and quantum information systems that operate at speeds approaching the fundamental limits of electron dynamics.
"In the long term, the insights gained could also contribute to operating electronics and quantum information processing at the intrinsic speed limit of electron motion itself -- hundreds of thousands of times faster than the currently dominant CMOS technology," adds Prof. Rupert Huber.
That possibility remains a long term technological goal rather than an achievement demonstrated in the current experiments. Nevertheless, the findings provide a new foundation for exploring how electrons can be manipulated at the smallest distances and shortest timescales.
For Repp and Huber, the results suggest that the range of potential applications is extraordinarily broad. They believe that future advances in controlling electrons at the space-time limit may ultimately depend more on human creativity than on the constraints imposed by nature.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Regensburg. Original written by Karoline Stürmer. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- S. Maier, R. Spachtholz, K. Glöckl, C. M. Bustamante, S. Lingl, M. Maczejka, J. Schön, A. Riedel, K. Richter, F. J. Giessibl, F. P. Bonafé, M. A. Huber, A. Rubio, J. Repp, R. Huber. Tracking electrons at the space-time limit. Nature Photonics, 2026; 20 (8): 961 DOI: 10.1038/s41566-026-01932-0

articles.title: Google pidió una patente para un canal de TV con IA que convierte al espectador en protagonista
articles.text:
Google solicitó una patente para un canal de televisión con videos generados por inteligencia artificial en los que el espectador es el protagonista, con su propio avatar y su voz. La oficina de patentes de Estados Unidos publicó la solicitud el 19 de noviembre. El sistema también prevé insertar anuncios en esos videos.
La solicitud, titulada “Creación de un canal de experiencias de video adaptadas a un usuario”, fue presentada el 13 de mayo de 2025, según el registro de Patsnap Eureka y la ficha del sitio Patentlyze, que sigue las patentes de las empresas tecnológicas. Figuran como inventores Aravind Reddy Ayuluri y Prameela Kavya Thummuru.
El medio 404 Media dio a conocer el documento el 23 de noviembre, después de que Patentlyze se lo compartiera. El periodista Jason Koebler lo describió como una señal de hacia dónde van las empresas de IA: contenido hecho a medida a partir de los datos que acumulan sobre cada persona.
Cómo funcionaría “My Channel”
El texto describe una opción llamada “My Channel” dentro de una aplicación de televisión. En lugar de solo recomendar títulos existentes, el sistema pediría a un modelo de lenguaje (la tecnología detrás de los chatbots) que cree videos nuevos y los muestre como miniaturas en un canal con el nombre del usuario, por ejemplo “John’s Channel”.
La primera reivindicación, que define lo que Google busca proteger, describe un servidor que reúne tres tipos de datos: las preferencias del usuario, información de contexto de su dispositivo y datos demográficos. Con eso redacta una instrucción para el modelo, que genera un video guardado en un repositorio y enviado luego al aparato:
- El contexto incluye la dirección IP, el idioma y las coordenadas GPS del dispositivo.
- El historial de visionado abarcaría programas, películas y videos cortos.
Una de las reivindicaciones señala que la instrucción puede generarse sin intervención del usuario, y otra, que un evento, como un temporizador, puede activar el proceso.
El sistema agruparía los géneros que el usuario ve, por ejemplo crimen, suspenso y acción, para mezclarlos en una misma historia. Los ejemplos del documento incluyen una comedia criminal, una comedia romántica y una aventura de ciencia ficción protagonizadas por un espectador llamado John.
Avatar, voz y publicidad
El documento agrega que el sistema puede crear un avatar a partir de fotos del usuario y sintetizar su voz para los diálogos del personaje principal. Los datos visuales se obtendrían del teléfono del usuario o de repositorios de datos de la empresa.
La cuarta reivindicación incorpora la publicidad: el video generado se enviaría a un servidor de anuncios, que insertaría al menos un aviso antes de que llegue al televisor. Según 404 Media, el sistema ofrecería así programas a medida con anuncios a medida.
Otro ejemplo de la patente describe a alguien que vio resúmenes de un partido de críquet y recibe un video con elementos del Mundial de la disciplina, en el que el usuario aparece alentando desde las tribunas. Patentlyze indica que la instrucción podría tomar noticias y resultados deportivos actuales.
Una idea, no un producto
Google no anunció ningún producto con este nombre. Patentlyze subraya que se trata de una solicitud y que el documento no nombra ningún servicio concreto. 404 Media recuerda que las tecnológicas presentan patentes que luego no llegan a productos reales.
Patentlyze informa además que el examinador emitió un rechazo final de la solicitud, aunque Google todavía puede modificar las reivindicaciones o apelar. India Today también recogió ese dato. No se pudo consultar el expediente del examinador en la oficina de patentes.
La ficha de Patentlyze señala que el propio documento reconoce que quienes comparten menos datos recibirían resultados más genéricos, y que los usuarios podrían controlar qué información se recopila. Por ahora, no hay fecha de lanzamiento ni plan público de Google para el canal.

articles.title: 1.5 Million Impacted by Data Breach at South Korean Electric Company KEPCO
articles.text:
South Korean state-owned electric company Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO, KRX: 015760, NYSE: KEP) has disclosed a data breach impacting approximately 1.5 million people.
The incident, the company says, involved KEPCO ON, its integrated customer service portal, and the supplier relationship management (SRM) platform, which handles procurement and service contracts.
KEPCO attributed the incident to an external attacker and noted the growing sophistication of AI-driven cyberattacks. It did not disclose how the attacker gained access or confirm that AI was used in this breach.
According to KEPCO, it suspended the affected services immediately after discovering the incident, blocked external access, conducted a thorough review of the relevant systems, and took remediation actions.
On November 20, the company confirmed that data was exfiltrated from its systems, including electricity customer and SRM user information.
From KEPCO ON, the hackers stole the personal information of 650,487 people, including names, addresses, phone numbers, unique ID numbers, customer numbers, card numbers and details, bank names, bank account numbers, account-holder names, card issuers, cardholder names, and billing/payment details.
Additionally, the information of 869,761 individuals was stolen from the SRM systems: the names, unique ID numbers, email addresses, and company addresses of 426,827; and the names, affiliation, employee IDs, email addresses, phone numbers, and company phone numbers of 442,934 (including KEPCO staff and partners’ employees).
The company has notified the affected individuals directly and reported the incident to the relevant authorities. It is also strengthening its security against AI-assisted attacks, and will share details on the exposure of financial information with government and financial institutions.
KEPCO’s disclosure followed a November 19 post on a dark web forum by a user operating under the handle Noiem, who reportedly claimed to have stolen KEPCO user and supplier data, as well as bidding and contract documents.
South Korea’s Personal Information Protection Commission (PIPC) has launched an investigation into the incident, noting that KEPCO received an email from the hacker, verified sample data received from the sender, and confirmed a dark web posting. PIPC has not attributed the data breach to Noiem.
Related: AI Inference Providers Failed to Detect Hacking and Prompt Theft, Says Dragos
