articles.title: Ils ont plié l’iPhone Duo 634 000 fois en un mois, voici son état
articles.text:
Tout le monde n’a pas tiré le bon iPhone Duo à sa sortie, le 23 octobre 2026. En quelques jours, des photos d’écrans internes fendus au niveau du pli ont envahi les réseaux sociaux. Apple a fini par reconnaître un problème touchant « un petit nombre d’iPhone Duo », et c’est la charnière qui est pointée du doigt. Ce « crackgate » a semé le doute sur la pièce la plus délicate du pliable, mais on ne sait toujours pas combien de pliages cette charnière peut encaisser. Apple ne le dit pas.
Alors, le média américain CNET a construit une machine qui ouvre et referme un iPhone Duo 900 fois par heure pendant un mois. Il y a eu quelques pauses, mais le compteur affiche déjà plus de 634 000 pliages en 21 jours.
Pour se faire une idée, 634 000 pliages correspondent à plus de 17 ans d’utilisation à raison de 100 ouvertures quotidiennes. C’est évidemment une conversion théorique, puisqu’aucune machine ne reproduit la vraie vie d’un smartphone.
Dans quel état est l’iPhone Duo après plus de 634 000 pliages ?
Un pliage complet prend environ 4 secondes. La machine met une seconde à ouvrir le téléphone, le laisse une seconde déplié, met une seconde à le refermer, puis le laisse une seconde fermé avant de recommencer.
Après 634 540 cycles au moment où nous écrivons ces lignes, le 24 novembre en début d’après-midi, le smartphone fonctionne, mais il n’est plus tout à fait comme neuf comme l’on pouvait s’en douter.
Pendant les premières semaines, rien n’a bougé. L’iPhone Duo a franchi les 160 000 pliages le 31 octobre, puis les 281 000 le 5 novembre, sans que la charnière ni le pli de l’écran ne changent.
Les premiers signes d’usure sont apparus autour de 390 000 cycles. En repassant les données des capteurs et les vidéos, l’équipe de CNET constate que l’ouverture demande moins de force et que le claquement net du mécanisme s’est adouci.
Dans la nuit du 12 au 13 novembre, vers 440 300 pliages, la charnière lâche un peu plus. L’écran n’a plus le temps de s’ouvrir complètement avant que la machine ne le referme, et s’arrête 5 à 10 degrés avant la position à plat.
Malgré cela, l’iPhone Duo continue de fonctionner et d’afficher l’interface sur son écran, ce qui prolonge le test encore plus loin. Le média s’est fixé trois critères d’arrêt : une perte d’alimentation, des capteurs qui ne détectent plus la position de l’écran, ou un écran qui reste noir. Aucun n’a été atteint, et la machine continue de tourner.
Si le cœur vous en dit, vous pouvez suivre les pliages un par un sur YouTube ou sur le compte X de CNET. Le média diffuse quelques heures de direct chaque jour de semaine, en général de 19h à 23h, heure de Paris.
Le Galaxy Z Fold 7 avait connu des ratés bien plus tôt
À l’été 2025, un youtubeur coréen s’était lancé dans une expérience proche, que Numerama avait suivie au fil des jours. Pendant 5 jours, l’équipe de la chaîne Techit avait plié un Galaxy Z Fold 7 à la main, en direct, jusqu’à 200 000 plis. Le pliable de Samsung était arrivé au bout, mais pas sans accrocs : une erreur au redémarrage avant 10 000 pliages, une charnière qui grince dès 46 000, un liquide qui suinte de la charnière passé les 75 000, puis un haut-parleur hors service à 175 000.
Les deux tests ne sont pas tout à fait comparables : plié à la main, un téléphone ne subit pas des mouvements aussi réguliers qu’avec une machine.
- L'écran nano texturé est incroyable
- Le pli le moins visible du marché
- Le format passeport dans la poche
- Meilleure interface logicielle pour un pliant
- Autonomie très satisfaisante
- Une réinvention réussie de l'iPhone
- Un peu trop lourd
- Trop d'applications inadaptées
- Touch ID est un retour en arrière
- Il manque un zoom optique
- 2 339 euros, c'est trop cher

articles.title: Precio de ethereum, bitcoin y otras principales criptomonedas para este martes 24 de noviembre
articles.text:
Las criptomonedas son un activo digital innovador que han experimentado un crecimiento monumental en los últimos tiempos debido a varios elementos que contribuyen a ello, entre ellos que algunos gobiernos hayan decidido darles una oportunidad como moneda de curso legal; no obstante, también han sufrido descalabros que han puesto en duda su viabilidad, como el más reciente episodio conocido como el "criptoinvierno".
Pese a este panorama, cada vez más personas han empezado a adquirir criptomonedas para poder invertir en algo "seguro" y "fiable" tanto a corto como a largo plazo, a pesar de los niveles extremos de inestabilidad que sufre constantemente.
Sin embargo, invertir o comprar en criptodivisas es más fácil de lo que parece. Hay que recordar que se trata de monedas virtuales, por lo que serán controladas en carteras o monederos que comparten esa particularidad, pues a diferencia del dinero corriente, no tienen un soporte físico.
El precio de las criptomonedas hoy
Esta es la cotización de las criptodivisas más destacadas en este momento.
El Bitcoin, cotiza a 60.225,35 dólares, lo que implicó un cambio de -1,61% en las últimas horas.
La segunda criptomoneda más popular del mercado, Ethereum, ha mostrado un movimiento de -0,811% en las últimas 24 horas, por lo que su valor se ubica en 1.695 dólares.
En el caso de TetherUs, su precio es de 1 dólares, por lo que en el último día tuvo un movimiento de 0,05%.
Por su parte, BNB, tiene un valor de 550,2 dólares, con un cambio de -1,49%, en cambio el Litecoin cotizó a 41.493 dólares, tras una variación de 3.3867764.
Finalmente, el Dogecoin, una de las monedas virtuales que fue impulsada por Elon Musk, tiene un valor de 0,06 dólares tras presentar un cambio de 1,6% en las últimas 24 horas.
Qué pasa con las criptodivisas
Luego de que en las primeras semanas de mayo del 2022 se viviera el "criptocrash" o "criptoinvierno" que dejaron al descubierto la enorme volatilidad de estas monedas digitales, ha llegado un nuevo periodo de relativa estabilidad.
Bitcoin, ethereum y BNB han mostrado variaciones "controladas", puesto que no se han disparado los precios como en semanas previas. Por ejemplo, a inicios de agosto, las mencionadas anteriormente tuvieron un cambio menor del 2%.
Por otra parte, algo que esta llamando la atención en el mundo de las criptomonedas es que China está ablandando sus restricciones y podría comenzar a permitir su uso. Específicamente sería Hong Kong en donde este cambio se haría presente.
Sumado a ello, la plataforma de transacciones digitales PayPal anunció su propia stablecoin llamada PayPal USD (PYUSD), que cuenta por el respaldo de depósitos en dólares, bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos a corto plazo y activos equivalentes.
La compañía ha afirmado en su declaración que permitirá la transferencia de fondos a monederos digitales de terceros y proporcionará detalles sobre cómo integrar su servicio en exchanges centralizados y descentralizados, con el objetivo de ser utilizado en Finanzas Descentralizadas (DeFi, por sus siglas en inglés). Por lo tanto, es muy probable que se utilice ampliamente en la industria Web3.
Criptomonedas en Latinoamérica
Criptomonedas en México: el Banco de México (Banxico) ha determinado que ninguna de las instituciones que participan en el sistema financiero nacional podrá hacer uso o deberá permitir operaciones de ninguna clase a través de este medio de pago.
En territorio mexicano el empresario Ricardo Salinas Pliego, uno de los más ricos del país, ha mostrado interés en las criptomonedas y ha asegurado que varios de sus negocios aceptarán bitcoin en el futuro, incluido su banco; hasta el momento una de sus tiendas más populares ya lo hace.
Criptomonedas en Perú: el Banco Central de Reserva del Perú (BCR) ha dejado en claro que su misión no es ser el primero ni el segundo banco central que regule el uso de las criptomonedas, ello debido a la inestabilidad que las caracteriza. Sin embargo, hace días el presidente del (BCR) aseguró que el BCR trabajaba en un proyecto de moneda digital propia.
Criptomonedas en Colombia: en la nación sudamericana hay más de 500 sitios donde es permitido pagar con criptodivisas. Colombia ocupa el puesto 14 entre 26 países de adopción de criptomonedas, según el informe de Finder.
Criptomonedas en Centroamérica: en el gobierno de El Salvador, el bitcoin, que en septiembre de 2021 se convirtió en moneda de curso legal, ha perdido oficialmente este estatus en este enero del 2025 tras una reforma aprobada por la Asamblea Legislativa del país. Según informó la prensa local, la modificación de la Ley Bitcoin fue impulsada por el gobierno del presidente Nayib Bukele y respaldada por la mayoría oficialista en el órgano legislativo. Este cambio marca el fin de una política que había colocado al país centroamericano en el centro del debate global sobre las criptomonedas.
¿Cómo crear una criptomoneda?
Al momento de crear una criptomoneda es importante primero determinar qué se desea tener: una moneda o un token. La primera usa su propia blockchain, mientras que la segunda se basa en una red preexistente.
De acuerdo con el sitio de Binance, para crear una criptomoneda se necesita de un gran equipo de desarrolladores y expertos; mientras que para el token sí se requieren conocimientos técnicos pero es posible crearlo en minutos a través del uso de otras blockchains como Ethereum o BNB, que son las más populares.
Los costos de creación, el tiempo requerido y el uso de fuerza de trabajo dependerá de si se opta por hacer una moneda virtual o un token. En éste último caso también se puede usar un código establecido para crear tokens o pagar para usar un servicio de creación de monedas.
Es importante saber que antes de crear una criptomoneda se debe considerar su utilidad y estado legal.
En el caso de elegir crear una criptomoneda, entonces se debe elegir una blockchain, posteriormente se debe hacer un plan acorde al funcionamiento y la funcionalidad de la blockchain para diseñar los nodos y la interfaz.

articles.title: Traduction Live : Free Mobile fait sauter la barrière de la langue avec une fonction inédite en France
articles.text:
Traduction Live : Free Mobile fait sauter la barrière de la langue avec une fonction inédite en France
Free vient de dévoiler une nouveauté que ses concurrents pourraient bien lui envier. Dopée à l’intelligence artificielle, cette fonctionnalité promet de simplifier considérablement le quotidien de certains abonnés.
Commander un taxi à Séoul ou joindre un hôtel à Rome sans bafouiller trois mots appris à la dernière minute ? C’est désormais possible avec Traduction Live, le service inauguré ce 24 novembre 2026 par Free Mobile. Une première chez les opérateurs français qui pourrait rendre bien des services aux voyageurs.
Free transforme votre smartphone en interprète personnel
Contrairement aux solutions made in Apple ou Android, Free ne mise pas sur les performances de votre terminal. L’intelligence artificielle, développée par ses équipes, intervient directement sur son réseau. Inutile donc d’investir dans un appareil dernier cri ou de télécharger une app dédiée.
Pour en profiter, il vous suffit de l'activer dans votre espace abonné ou l’app Free. Lors d’un appel entrant ou sortant, appuyez deux fois sur la touche dièse (#), puis dites "Ok Free, traduis en…" en précisant la langue désirée.
Chacun peut alors s’exprimer dans sa langue, l’IA traduisant oralement les échanges dans les deux sens. Dix langues sont proposées : français, anglais, espagnol, italien, allemand, portugais brésilien, russe, japonais, coréen et mandarin.
Un smartphone compatible avec les appels en 4G, 5G ou wifi suffit. Votre correspondant peut même décrocher depuis un téléphone fixe, indépendamment de son opérateur. Le dispositif fonctionne également à l’étranger.
Une IA qui imite votre voix, mais pas que
Deux options facultatives complètent le dispositif : le clonage vocal, pour conserver votre timbre plutôt qu’une voix artificielle standard, et l’envoi d’un compte rendu par SMS après l’appel. Pratique pour retrouver une adresse ou un horaire.
Prévenu par une annonce sonore, votre interlocuteur peut refuser la traduction ou le résumé via la touche 0. Free assure traiter les échanges sur ses serveurs français, sans conserver les conversations ni alimenter ses modèles d’IA. La transcription est quant à elle effacée après l’expédition du SMS.
Mieux vaut néanmoins discuter au calme, patienter entre chaque traduction et rester vigilant face aux contresens, notamment médicaux, juridiques ou financiers. Les numéros d’urgence sont d’ailleurs exclus.
Seul bémol : cette nouveauté est réservée aux forfaits Free Max (29 €/mois, ou 19 € mensuels avec une Freebox) et Free Pro Max. Aucun supplément n’est demandé, hors éventuels frais habituels des communications internationales.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.text:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
  November 4, 2026
- Source:
  Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
  Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or significantly disturbing the information it contains.
The research, supported by FAPESP, was published in Physical Review B Letters. It was led by José Carlos Egues, a full professor at the São Carlos Institute of Physics at the University of São Paulo (IFSC-USP) in Brazil, and Yugui Yao of the School of Physics at the Beijing Institute of Technology in China. If experimentally confirmed, their method could simplify quantum computing by removing the need for extra qubits used in certain measurement techniques.
Why Measuring Quantum Information Is So Difficult
Conventional computers store information in bits that have one of two values, 0 or 1. These values can be checked repeatedly without changing the information. Quantum computers work differently because their qubits can exist in superpositions, meaning they can combine the states 0 and 1 in ways that are not possible with conventional bits.
This unusual ability is central to the potential power of quantum computing. However, it also creates a major vulnerability. Quantum states can be disrupted by interactions with their surroundings, including the instruments scientists use to examine them.
"In the conventional formulation of quantum mechanics, a projective measurement causes the system to assume one of the states associated with the measured quantity. Thus, if a qubit has been prepared in a certain superposition of 0 and 1, its direct measurement tends to destroy that superposition and, consequently, the information it contained," says Egues.
To minimize this problem, physicists developed techniques known as "quantum nondemolition measurements," or QND. Many of these approaches use an additional quantum system called an ancilla. Rather than measuring the original qubit directly, researchers transfer information to the ancilla and measure that auxiliary system instead.
The term "ancilla" comes from a Latin word meaning "slave" or "servant." In modern scientific usage, it describes something that performs a supporting function. Here, the ancilla acts as an intermediary, allowing researchers to obtain information while preserving the original qubit as much as possible.
Although effective, these procedures come with practical disadvantages. Scientists must prepare the auxiliary qubits, connect them to the qubits being studied, transfer information between them, and perform repeated measurements. These additional steps require time and equipment, and the complexity becomes increasingly significant as the number of qubits grows.
"Our strategy is different. Instead of transferring the information to an auxiliary qubit, we seek to obtain it from a signal produced by the qubit under study itself," says the researcher.
A Special Quantum Bit That Produces Its Own Signal
The proposed technique relies on the unusual properties of an Andreev qubit. Its name honors Soviet physicist Alexander Andreev (1939-2023), who identified a distinctive quantum process in 1964 that occurs where normal materials meet superconductors.
Superconductors are materials that can conduct electricity without electrical resistance under appropriate conditions. At the boundaries involving these materials, special quantum states known as "Andreev states" can form. In the system studied by the researchers, these states are confined to an extremely small region between two superconducting materials.
These quantum states can represent the basic values 0 and 1, along with superpositions of those values, making them suitable for storing quantum information.
"In the system under consideration, this region is a quantum dot - that is, a nanoscale structure in which electrons are spatially confined - formed in an indium arsenide [InAs] nanowire connected to superconducting materials on both sides. It's in this environment that the states characterizing the Andreev qubit are formed," Egues explains.
The key to the new approach is an electrical phenomenon called a "supercurrent." Unlike the current flowing through ordinary electrical conductors, a supercurrent moves without resistance.
The researchers found that when the Andreev qubit exists in a superposition, the supercurrent develops a component that oscillates over time. These fluctuations arise from quantum interference between the different states making up the superposition.
Crucially, the oscillations are not random. Their behavior contains information about the qubit's underlying quantum state, potentially allowing scientists to determine what that state is without directly measuring the qubit.
"It's precisely that property that we use to read the qubit. It's that supercurrent that lies at the heart of our proposal," the researcher points out.
How a Tiny Electrical Current Reveals Quantum Information
To understand how the technique works, it helps to consider how physicists describe a qubit's state mathematically.
One common representation is the "Bloch sphere," a geometric model in which every possible pure state of a single qubit corresponds to a point on the surface of a sphere. Two angles determine the location of that point.
The first angle describes how much each of the two basic states contributes to the superposition. The second describes their relative phase, which specifies how the quantum components are aligned with one another. Together, these two measurements provide the information needed to identify the qubit's state.
According to the new research, both pieces of information can be extracted from the supercurrent. Its steady component and the size of its oscillations reveal the relative contributions of the two basic states. Meanwhile, the timing of the oscillations provides information about their phase relationship.
"Our study showed that this information is encoded in the supercurrent itself. The supercurrent has a constant component and a fluctuating component. The value of the constant component and the amplitude of the oscillation reveal the proportion of each state (0 and 1) in the superposition, and the moment when that oscillation begins reveals the phase relationship between them. Thus, by measuring how the current varies over time, it's possible to reconstruct the initial state of the qubit," Egues explains.
This means the electrical current effectively carries a signature of the quantum information stored in the system. By observing how that signature changes over time, researchers could reconstruct the qubit's original state.
A Supercurrent That Oscillates Without Voltage
Another surprising feature of the proposed system is that the electrical current can oscillate without an externally applied voltage.
Ordinarily, producing an oscillating supercurrent in this type of superconducting system requires a voltage. This familiar phenomenon is called the "AC Josephson effect."
The researchers predict something different in their Andreev qubit. Here, the current's oscillations arise naturally from the qubit's own quantum evolution. No outside voltage is required to generate them.
"Our system generates a supercurrent that varies over time like an alternating current but without voltage. It's the very evolution of the qubit's state that produces that oscillation," says Egues.
This behavior is important because it transforms quantum activity occurring on an extraordinarily small scale into a detectable electrical signal. The current provides a connection between the microscopic world of quantum states and the larger physical systems scientists can measure.
That connection is what makes the proposed reading technique possible.
Detecting Quantum States With an Extremely Sensitive Sensor
The researchers envision placing the Andreev qubit inside a closed superconducting circuit, allowing its supercurrent to circulate continuously.
Next to the circuit would sit a SQUID (superconducting quantum interference device), a highly sensitive instrument capable of detecting extremely weak magnetic fields.
Whenever an electric current flows, it produces a magnetic field. Because the supercurrent in this system oscillates, the magnetic field it generates also changes over time.
The nearby SQUID could detect these tiny magnetic variations and use them to determine the behavior of the circulating current. Since the current contains information about the qubit's quantum state, the researchers could then reconstruct that state without measuring the qubit directly.
Egues compares the arrangement to two compasses that interact through a magnetic field.
"We can think of the qubit as one compass and the SQUID as another compass. The current in the circuit produces a magnetic field, and the SQUID 'senses' that field. Since the coupling between the two is very weak, the effect of the measuring instrument on the qubit tends to be very small."
The weak interaction between the sensor and the qubit is especially important. It offers a way to gather information while minimizing the disturbance that normally accompanies quantum measurements.
Reading Quantum Information With Almost No Disturbance
In quantum physics, observing a system is not necessarily a harmless process. A measuring instrument interacts with whatever it is attempting to measure, and that interaction can change the system's behavior.
This fundamental difficulty puzzled the earliest researchers studying quantum mechanics. It remains an unavoidable feature of quantum measurements today.
The proposed technique does not eliminate this effect entirely. The SQUID still interacts with the circuit, creating a small amount of feedback that can influence the qubit. However, the team's simulations suggest that this disturbance can be reduced to a level so small that it becomes effectively negligible.
"Our method doesn't eliminate the fundamental problem of quantum measurement. But it can approach the limit of a non-destructive readout and, at the same time, avoid the use of auxiliary qubits - the ancillas - employed in other non-destructive quantum measurement protocols," Egues notes.
The approach could also remove another complication found in some existing techniques. Because researchers would not need to restore the qubit to its original state after every measurement, they could make repeated observations as the state changes.
This would allow scientists to follow the qubit's quantum evolution over time, rather than obtaining information only through separate measurement and reset cycles.
Simulations Achieve Up to 99.85% Accuracy
To investigate whether the method could work outside ideal theoretical conditions, the researchers performed computer simulations designed to account for imperfections that would arise in real experiments.
These calculations included measurement noise, as well as the small amount of feedback introduced by the detection coil. The goal was to determine whether the qubit's state could still be reconstructed accurately despite these disturbances.
The results were encouraging. Depending on the number of measurements used, the simulations produced accuracies of 99.52%, 99.81%, and 99.85%.
According to the researchers, these values fall within the standard thresholds used in quantum error correction schemes, which are designed to manage errors in quantum information processing.
The findings suggest that the method could provide highly accurate quantum state reconstruction without the additional complexity of auxiliary qubits.
However, the technique has not yet been demonstrated experimentally. The results come entirely from theoretical analysis and computer simulations, so researchers still need to establish whether a physical device can achieve comparable performance.
Could This Make Quantum Computers Simpler?
Despite the lack of experimental confirmation, the researchers emphasize that their proposal does not depend on technologies that have yet to be invented.
The calculations use realistic properties drawn from existing quantum systems, and SQUID sensors are already established tools for detecting exceptionally weak magnetic fields and electric currents.
What remains to be built is the specific arrangement of components required to implement the proposed measurement technique.
"All the numbers we used are realistic. In principle, this can be achieved. In fact, we used parameters from existing systems in our calculations. What doesn't yet exist is that geometry, that setup that we proposed," he argues.
This makes the approach different from theoretical concepts that cannot be realized until scientists develop entirely new materials or manufacturing techniques. In principle, the necessary components already exist, although assembling them into the proposed configuration and demonstrating the predicted behavior remain important challenges.
The research offers two potentially significant advances.
From the standpoint of fundamental physics, it predicts that a qubit can produce an oscillating supercurrent resembling the AC Josephson effect, but without requiring an external voltage. Instead, the oscillations emerge from the qubit's own coherent quantum evolution.
From a technological perspective, the study shows how those oscillations could serve as a measurable signature of the qubit's internal state. By analyzing the electrical current, researchers could recover quantum information while causing very little disturbance to the system.
If future experiments confirm these predictions, the method could make reading Andreev qubits substantially simpler. Eliminating auxiliary qubits and repeated resets could reduce the equipment and procedures needed to retrieve quantum information.
More fundamentally, the work points toward an intriguing possibility: information hidden in the microscopic quantum world may be accessible through an electrical current produced by the quantum system itself, offering a promising new way to observe delicate quantum states without destroying them.

articles.title: Elecbrakes Bluetooth Vulnerabilities Expose Trailers to Forced Braking
articles.text:
Vulnerabilities discovered in Bluetooth-enabled brake controllers made by Australian firm Elecbrakes could allow hackers to manipulate trailer brakes, potentially causing accidents, researchers warned.
The affected products include the EB2, VM1 and ELBC 2000 brake controllers from Elecbrakes. According to the cybersecurity agency CISA, which last week published an advisory on the vulnerabilities, the affected brake controllers are mainly used in Australia and New Zealand.
The controllers regulate the braking force applied to trailers, with the EB2 unit mounted on the trailer and the VM1 unit on the towing vehicle. The devices can be controlled remotely via a special remote or a smartphone app.
Researchers from Australian IT and cybersecurity consultancy Element Digital — with help from AI — discovered three vulnerabilities in the braking controllers, including two critical missing authentication and insufficient replay-attack protection issues.
They demonstrated that an unauthenticated attacker who is within Bluetooth range of the targeted vehicle (up to 100 meters or 328 feet) can use a laptop or phone to engage or release a trailer’s brakes or adjust the braking force, without any interaction required from the victim.
“Your trailer’s brakes slamming to maximum while your tow vehicle keeps going is the exact recipe for a jackknife – one of the more reliably fatal things a vehicle combination can do,” the researchers warned.
The third vulnerability is a medium-severity issue related to the firmware update mechanism. Unauthorized firmware changes could enable persistent compromise of the controller, allowing an attacker to interfere with braking, brake lights, and other safety functions. However, the researchers noted that this risk is theoretical, as they did not demonstrate the full impact or attempt to install malicious firmware during their tests.
Elecbrakes was notified about the findings in mid-May and released firmware updates with patches in early July for its EB2 and VM1 products. Element Digital disclosed technical details last week.
Once the firmware patches are installed, an attacker can no longer access the brake controllers remotely without an initial pairing that requires physical access to the device and cannot be performed over Bluetooth.
The vendor is still working on a remediation plan for the older ELBC 2000 product. In a customer advisory published on Monday, Elecbrakes advised owners of the older ELBC controllers to maintain an active connection between the controller and their smartphone or wireless remote whenever the device is in use.
Elecbrakes told iTnews that nearly 40,000 app users had initially been alerted to the availability of the update, and that it had been installed on 60-70% of controllers used to connect to the system daily.
There is no evidence of malicious exploitation of these vulnerabilities.
While the researchers praised Elecbrakes for quickly developing patches, they criticized the company over the lengthy disclosure process and its failure to initially identify the older ELBC 2000 as being affected.

articles.title: El Niño e aquecimento global levam temperatura da Terra a novo recorde
articles.text:
A Terra registrou o dia com a maior anomalia de temperatura já medida: na sexta-feira (20), a temperatura média global ficou 2,12 °C acima dos níveis pré-industriais. Os dados preliminares são do Serviço de Mudanças Climáticas Copernicus (C3S), da Europa, e representam novo alerta sobre a intensidade do aquecimento do planeta.
O recorde é resultado da combinação entre as mudanças climáticas provocadas pela atividade humana e um episódio excepcionalmente forte do fenômeno El Niño. O evento atual pode ser o mais intenso dos últimos mil anos.
O fenômeno ainda está ganhando força e deve atingir seu ápice aproximadamente no próximo mês. Por isso, cientistas esperam que novos dias com temperaturas pelo menos 2 °C acima da média pré-industrial sejam registrados nos próximos meses.
El Niño pode provocar novos recordes de temperatura
- A influência do El Niño sobre a temperatura global não acontece de maneira instantânea. O calor liberado no Oceano Pacífico leva algum tempo para afetar as médias de temperatura do planeta, o que significa que os efeitos mais intensos do fenômeno ainda podem estar por vir;
- Zachary Labe, cientista da organização de pesquisa climática Climate Central, acredita que novas marcas podem aparecer em breve.
- “Provavelmente veremos mais dias ultrapassando 2 °C nos próximos dois meses, possivelmente até março de 2027”, afirmou o pesquisador à Scientific American. Ele ressalvou, porém, que esses registros ainda devem ser relativamente raros quando comparados ao conjunto de dias do período;
- O cenário também coloca 2026 e 2027 na disputa pelo posto de anos mais quentes já registrados. O ano atual pode superar 2024, embora exista a possibilidade de empate. Já 2027 deverá receber o impacto mais intenso do El Niño e tem grandes chances de estabelecer novo recorde;
- Os dois anos também devem apresentar temperaturas médias superiores a 1,5 °C acima dos níveis pré-industriais. Até agora, apenas 2024 havia ultrapassado essa marca.
Leia mais:
- El Niño pode ser o mais forte registrado desde 1950, diz NOAA
- El Niño pode desencadear crise mundial muito além do clima
- Por que Roraima enfrenta seca extrema mesmo após cheias em junho
O que significa ultrapassar 1,5 °C ou 2 °C?
Os números chamam a atenção porque estão relacionados às metas estabelecidas pelo Acordo de Paris, firmado em 2015 durante a COP21.
O compromisso internacional prevê limitar o aquecimento global a bem menos de 2 °C acima dos níveis pré-industriais, com esforços para mantê-lo abaixo de 1,5 °C.
Entretanto, ultrapassar 2 °C em um único dia — ou mesmo durante um ano — não significa que o limite do acordo tenha sido definitivamente rompido. Isso porque a avaliação considera a temperatura média ao longo de vários anos, e não oscilações pontuais.
Segundo a Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU), o planeta já aqueceu quase 1,4 °C em relação ao período pré-industrial. A entidade também alertou recentemente que ultrapassar a marca de 1,5 °C se tornou inevitável, com a temperatura global podendo chegar a 1,8 °C acima dos níveis históricos.
Recorde acontece em meio a impasse climático internacional
O novo marco de temperatura foi registrado em momento de dificuldades nas negociações internacionais sobre mudanças climáticas.
A COP31 terminou sem acordo para um documento final. Os textos produzidos nessas conferências funcionam como orientações para que os países reduzam suas emissões de gases de efeito estufa e se adaptem às transformações do clima. Os Estados Unidos não enviaram uma delegação oficial ao encontro.
O secretário-geral da ONU, António Guterres, manifestou frustração com o resultado da conferência. O dirigente, que defende a eliminação gradual dos combustíveis fósseis, afirmou que os recordes de temperatura continuam sendo quebrados, enquanto as emissões permanecem muito elevadas.
“Cada atraso torna nossa tarefa mais difícil e mais custosa”, declarou Guterres. Ele também alertou que a janela de oportunidade para manter o eventual ultrapassamento da meta de 1,5 °C o mais curto e limitado possível está diminuindo rapidamente.
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Dreame and Eufy are offering nearly 60 percent off robovacs for Black Friday
articles.text:
Between putting up decorations, entertaining guests, and meal prep, the holidays are busy enough without worrying about vacuuming. Thankfully, a proper robot vacuum can do the dirty work while you focus on more enjoyable things. And thanks to Black Friday, you can pick up some of the best we’ve tested for up to 60 percent off.
Dreame and Eufy are offering nearly 60 percent off robovacs for Black Friday
We’ve rounded up the best discounts on our favorite robot vacuums, including models that can mop on your behalf.
We’re seeing some excellent deals on a wide range of robot vacuums, including some of our favorite models from Roborock, Dreame, and Eufy. There are also rare discounts already available on premium models like the Matic and Matic Serene, which impressed us with their almost humanlike navigation, while midrange options such as the Eufy Omni C28 have dropped into budget territory. Whether you want a high-end model that cleans itself or something budget-friendly but still powerful, we’ve rounded up the best deals we’ve found so far.
Roborock Q10 S5 Plus
Despite lacking a multifunction dock, the budget-friendly robot vacuum and mop offers an impressive set of features for the price, including AI-powered obstacle avoidance, sonic mopping, automatic mop lifting, and a self-emptying dock.
Roborock Qrevo Curv 2 Flow
Roborock’s first roller-mop robot vacuum, the Curv 2 Flow, features flagship specs at a midrange price, including excellent mopping, a retractable mop cover, 20,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a compact design.
Matic robot vacuum
The Matic robot vacuum and mop is ideal for cluttered homes with pets, multiple floors, and a mixture of carpets and hardwood. It offers almost humanlike navigation, tackling high-pile rugs and mopping up wet spills. The quiet bot also requires less maintenance than many rivals thanks to its onboard water tank and dust bag. Read our review.
Eufy Omni C28
The Eufy Omni C28 combines excellent mopping performance with a small self-cleaning dock that’s well suited for apartments and other smaller spaces. It navigates around furniture and into tight areas with ease, while its roller mop does a great job cleaning hard floors.
Dreame X60 Ultra
The Dreame X60 Ultra is a powerful robot vacuum and mop that does a great job of cleaning carpets thanks to its dual roller brushes and 35,000Pa of suction. It can climb over tall thresholds, squeeze under low furniture, and automatically detach its mop pads when vacuuming carpets.
Narwal Flow 2
If you have all hardwood floors, the Narwal Flow 2 is an excellent option. A superb mop with a wide flat roller pad and an excellent vacuum, the Flow 2 also has top-notch navigation and obstacle detection. Its sleek base station is also less of an eyesore than most.
Roborock Saros 20
Roborock’s Saros 20 stands out for its ability to climb tall thresholds, avoid obstacles with impressive accuracy, and clean under low furniture thanks to its slim design. It also combines powerful 36,000Pa suction with great spinning mop pads, which is why we recommend it for homes with multiple floor types and tricky transitions between rooms.
Ecovacs Deebot X12 OmniCyclone
Ecovacs’ robot vacuum and mop can pretreat stains, keep carpets dry with a smart mop cover, and deliver powerful 22,000Pa suction. It also includes an all-in-one dock that automatically empties the dustbin, refills the water tanks, and washes the mop with heated, pressurized water.
Switchbot K11 Plus
The Matter-compatible SwitchBot K11 Plus is ideal for small apartments, bedrooms, and home offices. It can easily navigate around chair and desk legs and into tight spaces that most other bots miss. It also features a commendable 6,000Pa of suction power — which is great for this price point — and works well on both hardwood and carpet.
Dreame X50 Ultra
With high suction power, an improved brush system, and the ability to scale thresholds up to 6cm, the X50 Ultra stands out as a great robot vacuum-mop hybrid. While its 20,000Pa suction isn’t quite as powerful as the X60 Ultra’s and it can’t tackle especially high thresholds as well, it’s still an excellent option. Its edge cleaning also isn’t quite as effective as the X60 Ultra’s, but you’re otherwise getting many of the same features for a lot less.
Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2
The Dreame L40 Ultra Gen 2 delivers powerful 25,000Pa suction, AI-powered obstacle avoidance, and a self-cleaning dock that empties the dustbin, washes the mop, and refills its water tanks. Unlike the X50 Ultra, however, it lacks the ability to climb high thresholds or stairs.

articles.title: Der KI-Masterplan ist veraltet, bevor er beschlossen wird – was Unternehmen stattdessen tun sollten
articles.text:
Der KI-Masterplan ist veraltet, bevor er beschlossen wird – was Unternehmen stattdessen tun sollten
Mitte September hat der Bitkom neue Zahlen veröffentlicht. 57 Prozent der Unternehmen in Deutschland setzen inzwischen KI ein, ein Jahr zuvor waren es 36 Prozent. Mich haben zwei andere Zahlen aus derselben Befragung mehr beschäftigt. 66 Prozent aller befragten Unternehmen schätzen die KI-Kompetenz ihrer Beschäftigten als gering ein. Und nur elf Prozent schulen alle Beschäftigten im Umgang mit KI.
Die Lizenzen sind also schnell gekauft. Was danach kommen soll, ist in vielen Organisationen offen. Wie führt man ein Unternehmen dahin, KI sinnvoll zu verankern, wenn niemand weiß, wie das Ziel genau aussieht?
Der Plan ist auch eine Absicherung
Die naheliegende Antwort ist ein Masterplan. Drei Jahre, klare Meilensteine, ein Budget, das hält. Im ersten Schritt ist das nachvollziehbar. Aufsichtsrat und Banken wollen wissen, wofür Geld ausgegeben wird, und Mitarbeitende wollen wissen, woran sie sind. Ein Plan schützt außerdem den, der ihn geschrieben hat. Geht etwas schief, hat man sich zumindest an den Plan gehalten.
Bei KI ändert sich die Grundlage jeder Planung allerdings in Monaten. Modelle werden leistungsfähiger, Preise und Nutzungsbedingungen verschieben sich, neue Werkzeuge sind da, bevor die alten eingeführt sind. Viele etablierte Geschäftsmodelle stehen unter Druck und neue Geschäftsmodelle implodieren genauso schnell, wie sie entstanden sind. Und manchmal ist ein Werkzeug über Nacht weg, wie beim Ausfall von Fable 5. Ein Dreijahresplan ist veraltet, bevor er alle Gremien durchlaufen hat. Wer auf ihn wartet, verliert die Zeit, in der andere lernen.
Was ist die Alternative? Auf Sicht führen. Kurze Schritte. Schnelle Rückmeldungen. Korrekturen ohne Gesichtsverlust. Das ist in meinen Augen kein Kontrollverlust, sondern Realismus. Auf Sicht zu steuern heißt aber nicht, ohne Regeln zu fahren.
Vier Spielregeln für alle
Dass Verbote genau die unkontrollierte Nutzung erzeugen, die sie verhindern sollen, sehe ich weiterhin so. Was Mitarbeitende brauchen, sind verständliche Spielregeln. Bei uns sind es vier. Erstens ist die Nutzung von KI ausdrücklich erwünscht, und zwar über gesicherte interne Plattformen. Zweitens gilt der Datenschutz auch für KI: Vertrauliche und personenbezogene Daten, auch die unserer Kunden, gehören nicht unreflektiert in externe Werkzeuge. Drittens setzen wir KI verantwortungsvoll ein. Im Personalbereich fließt KI nicht in die Beurteilung ein. Wir nutzen sie erst im Nachgang, um mögliche Verzerrungen in unseren Bewertungen zu erkennen. Und viertens zeichnet, wer ein KI-Ergebnis nutzt, mit dem eigenen Namen dafür.
Der erste Punkt wird oft unterschätzt. Solange niemand laut sagt, dass KI erwünscht ist, nutzen viele sie heimlich oder gar nicht. Beides kostet. Der vierte Punkt beantwortet die Frage, die bei jedem KI-Ergebnis mitschwingt: Wer steht dafür gerade? Bei uns der Mensch, der es weitergibt.
Dazu kommt eine klare Aufgabenteilung. Ein zentrales Plattform-Team stellt die Infrastruktur bereit und prüft Datenschutz, Kosten und die Anforderungen des EU-AI-Acts. Welche Anwendungsfälle sich lohnen, finden die Fachbereiche und Projektteams selbst heraus, denn nur sie können beurteilen, ob ein Ergebnis fachlich taugt. Salopp gesagt: zentrale Plattform, dezentrale Ideen.
Lernen braucht feste Orte
Zurück zu den Bitkom-Zahlen. Eine Schulung ist schnell gebucht. Ob danach jemand KI im Alltag nutzt, entscheidet sich woanders: im Austausch mit Kolleg:innen, beim Ausprobieren, beim Nachlesen. Bei uns heißt das ganz praktisch: Im KI-Webfrühstück zeigen sich Kolleg:innen regelmäßig eine halbe Stunde lang remote, was funktioniert, mit Demos und Fragen. Im Code Retreat, unserem KI-Hackathon, arbeiten Teams einen halben Tag vor Ort an konkreten Aufgaben und zeigen am Ende ihre Ergebnisse. In einer internen Blogreihe lässt sich nachlesen, was andere gelernt haben. In unserer AI Community of Practice auf Slack kommen jeden Tag ganz praktische Tipps, Ideen und Fragen auf den Tisch, die sehr schnell beantwortet werden. Niedrigschwellig, intensiv, dokumentiert. Die Formate verlangen unterschiedlich viel Zeit, weil Menschen unterschiedlich lernen.
Mindestens so wichtig ist der Einstieg, und das nicht nur für Berufseinsteiger:innen in der Softwareentwicklung. Wer anfängt, braucht Aufgaben mit geringem Risiko und die Erlaubnis, dass etwas schiefgeht. Scheitern ist auf dem Weg vom Spieltrieb zur handwerklichen Professionalität ein notwendiger Zwischenschritt. Wer Fehler bestraft, bekommt Menschen, die KI verstecken. Das Risiko, die Aufgaben an die Entwicklung der Skills zu koppeln, ist auch hier eine unternehmerische Selbstverständlichkeit.
Befähigung schlägt Lizenz
Wenn jemand mich fragen würde, was die eine Sache ist, die ich für morgen mitgeben soll, dann diese: Investieren Sie in Befähigung. Den Vorsprung hat am Ende die Organisation, die am schnellsten gemeinsam lernt, nicht die mit der teuersten Lizenz.
Das Lernen bezieht sich dabei auf alle Beteiligten im Unternehmen, von den (Top-)Führungskräften bis zu den Mitarbeitenden und von der reinen Skillvermittlung bis hin zur Akzeptanz, dass es auf viele Fragen aktuell noch keine Antwort gibt. Nur eines ist ganz klar: dass die KI gekommen ist, um zu bleiben.
Handlungsfähig bleibt nicht, wer den perfekten Plan hat, sondern wer Rahmen schafft, in denen Menschen eigenverantwortlich lernen und entscheiden können. Die nächste Bitkom-Umfrage wird wieder zählen, wie viele Unternehmen KI einsetzen. Mich würde eine andere Zahl mehr interessieren: wie viele ihren Leuten das Lernen ermöglichen.

articles.title: Google teme que los agentes de IA se descontrolen y planea restringirlos en Chrome
articles.text:
Google quiere limitar el poder de los agentes de IA dentro de Chrome. La compañía propone un sistema de permisos a nivel de navegador para controlar qué webs pueden visitar y qué acciones pueden realizar. La iniciativa surge tras la oleada de incidentes en donde los agentes se han saltado las barreras de seguridad y terminan hackeando páginas o accediendo a contenido para el que no estaban autorizados.
De acuerdo con Neowin, Google ha planeado un sistema que limitaría el alcance de los agentes autónomos. Ingenieros de la empresa propusieron cambios en WebDriver BiDi, el protocolo utilizado para automatización y pruebas en navegadores. En una publicación en el grupo de Chromium, los empleados anunciaron una intención para prototipar la idea y regresarle el control a los usuarios.
En la versión actual del protocolo, WebDriver BiDi asume una relación de confianza total entre el cliente y el navegador, lo que permite un control prácticamente ilimitado. Si bien esto funciona para pruebas automatizadas, resulta peligroso para agentes de IA que navegan en la web. Muchos agentes usan protocolos de bajo nivel o configuraciones que les dan acceso sin restricciones y sin supervisión del usuario.
La idea de Google es añadir extensiones para WebDriver BiDi que se aplicarán a la IA. En los casos donde un agente autónomo navegue, el sistema añadirá un nuevo tipo de sesión restringida. En esta, la IA comienza sin permisos más allá de los valores predeterminados, por lo que debe solicitar explícitamente el acceso a los recursos y capacidades.
La propuesta utiliza un sistema de permisos basado en ACL (lista de control de acceso), que define las webs que puede visitar el agente, los comandos permitidos y los eventos a recibir. Estos permisos se pueden aplicar de forma global a ciertas pestañas o navegaciones específicas.
Google Chrome limitará a los agentes de IA a través de permisos
Google señala que el uso de extensiones permite conservar el control en todo momento. Cuando se aplican, el usuario puede pausar al agente, revocar permisos o detener la sesión. Chrome puede mostrar una interfaz especial cuando el agente realice acciones activas como hacer clic, navegar, escribir texto o ejecutar scripts, de modo que el usuario sepa cuáles son las pestañas controladas por la IA en caso de que se necesite limitarlas o apagarlas.
Bajo la propuesta de Google, los usuarios de Chrome también podrían otorgar permisos muy concretos. Si necesitas que el agente acceda a una tienda en línea, pero no revise páginas de pagos externas, puedes bloquearlo.
Hasta ahora todo suena muy bien, pero existen algunas limitaciones. Por ejemplo, si le autorizas a un agente a hacer clic en botones, Chrome no puede distinguir entre un botón seguro y otro que elimine información importante. Por ello, los ingenieros tienen que seguir experimentando hasta llegar a un nivel confiable que pueda adoptarse por otros navegadores.
Por el momento, esta propuesta se encuentra en una etapa muy preliminar de desarrollo y no se sabe cuándo se implementará en Chrome.

articles.title: ¿Qué pasa en una casa inteligente cuando se cae internet?
articles.text:
¿Qué pasa en una casa inteligente cuando se cae internet?
Una avería en la fibra no tiene por qué dejar fuera de juego toda la domótica, pero sí puede impedir controlar luces, cámaras o electrodomésticos
Televisores, altavoces inteligentes, termostatos, cámaras de vigilancia, electrodomésticos… Cada vez utilizamos más dispositivos conectados y pocas veces nos paramos a pensar qué pasaría en caso de producirse un fallo con la conexión a internet. ¿Seguirían funcionando como si nada? ¿Podríamos controlarlos de alguna manera? Lo cierto es que no hay una respuesta universal, y al final todo depende del producto concreto y del tipo de conexión que se use para configurarlos en la red doméstica.
Lo primero que hay que tener en cuenta es que, aunque a menudo hablamos de internet (o la conexión) y del Wi-Fi como sinónimos, la realidad es que no son lo mismo: internet es la red global que permite acceder a páginas web, plataformas y servidores externos, mientras Wi-Fi es la tecnología que conecta nuestros dispositivos con la red local del hogar sin cables. ¿Por qué es importante esta diferencia? Porque una avería en la conexión de fibra óptica puede dejarnos sin acceso a internet, pero si el router sigue encendido y funcionando, la red doméstica puede seguir comunicando los dispositivos entre sí, siempre que estos dispongan de una vía de comunicación local. En cambio, si el router deja de funcionar, los dispositivos que dependen de él para comunicarse pueden perder esa conexión, aunque algunos sistemas con un concentrador o una red propia podrían seguir funcionando.
Luces, enchufes y termostatos
La iluminación inteligente es uno de los ejemplos más claros: cuando usamos bombillas conectadas a una plataforma que necesita comunicarse con sus servidores para ejecutar órdenes, la caída de internet impedirá que las controlemos desde la aplicación o mediante asistentes de voz. Sin embargo, será posible hacerlo desde los interruptores físicos o los mandos compatibles.
Algo parecido sucede con los enchufes inteligentes, que permiten encender y apagar los aparatos conectados a ellos —o programar su funcionamiento— desde el móvil. Si la aplicación depende de la nube, puede dejar de enviar órdenes cuando no hay internet, pero un enchufe que tenga programaciones almacenadas localmente podría mantenerlas.
Por otro lado, los termostatos inteligentes plantean una situación interesante: aunque perdamos el control desde el móvil, es fácil encontrar modelos que permiten seguir controlando la temperatura desde el propio dispositivo y mantienen su funcionamiento básico. Otra cosa es que se mantengan las automatizaciones, los ajustes inteligentes o las funciones que necesitan consultar servicios externos.
¿Qué ocurre con las cámaras, alarmas y asistentes de voz?
Cuando hablamos de seguridad doméstica, perder la conexión puede tener consecuencias más importantes que van más allá de la imposibilidad de encender una bombilla desde el móvil: las cámaras conectadas suelen depender de servidores externos, así que sin internet no se podrán consultar imágenes en directo, recibir alertas o acceder a grabaciones desde una aplicación. En función del modelo, incluso se interrumpiría la grabación en la nube. Esto no ocurre con las que incorporan una tarjeta de memoria para guardar los vídeos; en este caso, aunque no fuera posible acceder para ver el vídeo en directo, la cámara seguiría encendida y grabando localmente.
Con las alarmas sucede algo similar y, si no hay conexión, se puede dar el caso de que detecte una intrusión y se active la sirena, pero el aviso nunca llegue al móvil del propietario. Para evitarlo, algunos modelos incorporan una conexión alternativa, como la red móvil, que permite transmitir avisos si falla internet.
Los altavoces inteligentes también pueden perder parte de su utilidad en caso de fallo de internet. Si las órdenes de voz necesitan llegar a un servicio en la nube para ser interpretadas —algo habitual—, funciones como consultar el tiempo, pedir información o controlar dispositivos con comandos de voz dejarán de estar disponibles, del mismo modo que no será posible reproducir contenidos en streaming.
La clave está en la nube y en el control local
Con todos estos ejemplos, queda una cosa clara: no hay una respuesta general para todos los dispositivos conectados del hogar, porque depende mucho de cómo se comuniquen y de dónde se procesen las órdenes. En los sistemas basados en la nube, la orden pasa por un servidor externo antes de llegar al dispositivo o de activar la función solicitada. Por eso, si se interrumpe la conexión a internet, ese intercambio deja de ser posible. En cambio, en los casos en los que todo se procesa de manera local, las funciones compatibles se seguirán ejecutando dentro de casa, siempre que los dispositivos, el controlador y la red necesaria continúen funcionando.
Dicho esto, ¿podemos hacer algo para preparar la casa para una caída de internet? Lo esencial sería identificar qué dispositivos utilizamos a diario y qué ocurriría si perdiéramos la conexión. Por eso, al elegir un producto inteligente, no basta con comprobar si es compatible con Alexa, Google Home o Apple Home; es recomendable saber qué funciones mantiene sin conexión, si necesita un concentrador (un dispositivo que coordina la comunicación entre los equipos) y si las automatizaciones se ejecutan localmente o en servidores externos. También conviene comprobar si dispone de controles físicos o de alguna alternativa para seguir utilizando sus funciones esenciales cuando falla la conexión.

articles.title: Firefox 161 updates that can help save time over the holidays
articles.text:
Lighten the holiday load with these four Firefox 161 updates
The holiday season, the festive season, the “how is the year almost over?” season. Whatever you call it, there’s a lot to get done. Gifts to buy, meals to plan, travel details to sort out, all while your regular responsibilities refuse to take time off.
In Firefox 161, we’re introducing a few new updates that can help you save time during the busiest months of the year, plus a new place to browse when you have a few minutes to cross something off your list. So you can cut down on the time spent prepping for the holidays, and get back to the people you’re doing it all for.
Set VPN rules for individual sites
Searching for the perfect gift? You might want to use a VPN to compare how prices differ by region. Sites like your bank or favorite streaming service, however, might work better without it.
Firefox’s free built-in VPN on desktop now lets you choose which sites automatically open with VPN on, and which open with it off. This way, your preferences are applied automatically, and you can save time skipping the constant toggling on/off every time you visit a different site.
Open the VPN panel from your toolbar and select Manage VPN rules, or go to Settings → Privacy & Security → VPN → Manage VPN rules. Add a website and choose Always on or Always off. Once a rule is set, that site will automatically open with your VPN preferences on future visits.
Bonus: VPN data is unlimited through January 31, 2027, so now’s the perfect time to experiment with rules and find the setup that works best for you. Check VPN availability in your region and sign in with a Mozilla account to get started.
Listen to pages when your hands are full
Already available on desktop, the ability to read pages aloud in Reader View is now rolling out on Firefox for Android. So when holiday prep keeps your hands busy, you can catch up on that article you’ve been saving while you untangle the tree lights, or hear the next step in your cookie recipe without getting flour on your phone.
On Android, tap the Reader View icon in the address bar, then tap the headphones icon in the pop-out menu. You can play, pause, rewind, fast-forward, adjust the playback speed, or choose a voice. You can even keep listening with your screen off. For added privacy, Firefox uses only voices that work directly on your device, so the page text and audio stay there.
Meet the Fire button in Classic Window: A faster way to start fresh
Anyone who shares a computer with family knows the risk: one stray autofill suggestion or search history entry, and the gift you spent weeks planning and searching for is no longer a surprise. Before you hand the computer over to the next person, press the 🔥 button in your desktop toolbar in Classic Window to help keep your gifts a secret until the big day.
If you’ve used the 🔥 button in Private Window, you’ll recognize the icon. There, it lets you quickly reset your private browsing session. It’s now gradually rolling out to Classic Window on desktop, where it does something different: it gives you easily accessible control over the data Firefox saves as you browse.
It’s always in reach, so you can clear your browsing and downloads history, cookies and site data, temporary files, saved form info, and website permissions and preferences directly from your toolbar. If you choose to delete everything, you’ll be signed out of sites and your current window will close, and Firefox will open a new one for you to start fresh. Because you’ve got enough to do without hunting through settings to clear it all.
If you don’t want to delete everything or close your open window, you can choose which browsing data to delete and your current window will remain open.
Browse Firefox from your car dashboard
You can now download the Firefox app directly from Google Play in cars with Google built-in. Whether you are waiting for your kid at school pick-up, charging your EV between long drives, or taking a breather in the parking lot before braving the holiday shopping frenzy, you can use Firefox right from your parked car’s dashboard. Less squinting at a mobile screen; more getting stuff done.
The best part? Our commitment to privacy comes along for the ride. Firefox is built on the principle that not even Mozilla should know which websites you visit or what you do there, and your browsing history will never be shared with the car manufacturer.
A little time back this holiday season
When your day is already full, even a few small shortcuts can help. We hope the new improvements in Firefox 161 make it easier to get things done online – not only during the holiday rush, but also long after the decorations come down.
To learn about the other new features released in Firefox 161, check out our newest release notes. And once you’ve given them a go, let us know what you think on Mozilla Connect.

articles.title: Peninsula Energy Halts Trading After Cyber Incident Hits US Uranium Mine
articles.text:
Australian uranium company Peninsula Energy (ASX: PEN; OTCQB: PENMF) has requested a trading halt after a cybersecurity incident hit its uranium mine in the United States.
The incident, the company told the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX), occurred on Friday night and impacted the Lance Project in Wyoming, US.
“The company is undertaking a preliminary investigation of the incident and an assessment of the timing and impact, which will temporarily affect its operations,” Peninsula Energy said in a Monday filing.
According to the filing, the incident resulted in a breach of its “operating system”, while administrative systems in the US and Australia were not affected. It did not specify which technical systems were compromised or whether uranium production had been interrupted.
“Peninsula wishes the trading halt to remain in place until the earlier of the commencement of normal trading on 25 November 2026 or when the company releases the announcement regarding the cybersecurity incident,” the company said.
The wholly owned Lance Project, located in Crook County, relies on in situ recovery to extract uranium, which is then processed into yellowcake, which can be turned into nuclear fuel.
In 2025, the US added uranium to the federal list of critical minerals, and the Lance Project, which is expected to become a key supplier, has likely become an attractive target for hacking groups.
In fact, threat actors have also used influence campaigns against rare-earth mining companies in the US and Australia, although those campaigns involved disinformation rather than confirmed intrusions into mining systems.
SecurityWeek has emailed Peninsula for additional information on the incident and will update this article if the company responds.
The attack on Peninsula was disclosed roughly three weeks after global mining company AngloGold Ashanti disclosed in an SEC filing that it detected unauthorized activity on certain systems on October 16, but said the incident was contained and its mining operations were not affected.
Between July and September 2026, cybersecurity firm Dragos observed 19 ransomware attacks targeting mining organizations. Overall, industrial ransomware activity went up during the timeframe, with North America and Europe being the most affected regions, the company says.

articles.title: GTA VI na Twitch: Brasil entra no top 5 de audiência e Alanzoka é o 2º maior streamer do jogo no mundo
articles.text:
Mais de mil anos de conteúdo de Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) na Twitch foram assistidos por espectadores brasileiros durante o fim de semana de lançamento do jogo, até a manhã de segunda-feira (GMT). Segundo a Twitch, o número coloca o Brasil entre os cinco países com maior audiência de GTA VI na plataforma.
O destaque individual ficou com um nome conhecido da comunidade. De acordo com a Twitch, Alanzoka foi o segundo maior streamer de GTA VI do mundo no período.
Os números reforçam a relevância do Brasil no cenário global de games e o protagonismo dos criadores nacionais na mobilização de grandes comunidades em torno dos lançamentos da indústria.
A programação da Twitch para o lançamento de GTA VI
Para celebrar a chegada do jogo e ampliar a participação dos espectadores, a Twitch preparou uma programação especial entre 18 e 30 de novembro. As iniciativas incluem coleções de distintivos e emotes exclusivos, Hype Trains temáticos, incentivo à publicação de retrospectivas das transmissões e distribuição diária de códigos de GTA VI Ultimate Edition.
Entre as recompensas, está a insígnia especial Iguana Dourada, que poderá ser desbloqueada por quem completar as duas coleções de itens temáticos. As ações buscam transformar o lançamento em uma experiência coletiva, incentivando a interação entre criadores e espectadores e reconhecendo a participação das comunidades.
Quem transmite também entra na campanha
A programação também valoriza os criadores de conteúdo. Streamers que publicarem retrospectivas de suas transmissões durante o período da campanha poderão receber inscrições de presente (Gift Subs), e conteúdos selecionados serão destacados na página inicial da plataforma.
As ações reforçam a estratégia da Twitch de aproveitar grandes momentos da indústria de games para estimular a criação de conteúdo, fortalecer comunidades e ampliar as possibilidades de engajamento. A campanha não tem afiliação nem parceria com a Rockstar Games.
É técnica em audiovisual e community manager com 7 anos de experiência no universo gamer.
Amazon Prime também é feito para jogadores!
Todo mês, obtenha itens exclusivos, jogos grátis, uma assinatura gratuita na Twitch.tv e muito mais com sua assinatura Prime. Clique aqui para um teste gratuito de 30 dias.

articles.title: SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 : ce SSD NVMe PCIe 5.0 de 1 To s'allège de 100 € à l'approche du Black Friday
articles.text:
Le SSD NVMe SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100, qui n’est autre que l’ancien WD Black SN8100, trouve sa place aussi bien dans un PC gamer doté d’une configuration pointue que dans une station de travail dédiée au montage vidéo ou à la création 3D. Ce SSD interne dispose d’une interface PCIe 5.0 et affiche des débits de lecture et d’écriture très élevés. La bonne nouvelle, c’est qu’en pleine crise du stockage et de la mémoire, le prix du modèle de 1 To diminue à l’approche du Black Friday, qui tombe ce vendredi 27 novembre.
Les points forts du SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100
- Une interface PCIe 5.0
- Une vitesse de lecture allant jusqu’à 14 900 Mo/s
- Un espace de 1 To
Auparavant affiché à 309,99 euros, le SSD SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 de 1 To est aujourd’hui disponible en promotion à 204,99 euros sur Amazon.
Des débits particulièrement élevés
Le SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 présenté ici exploite l’interface PCIe 5.0, qui offre une bande passante deux fois plus élevée que celle du PCIe 4.0. Il peut ainsi atteindre des débits particulièrement élevés. Mais il faut évidemment disposer d’une carte mère équipée d’un emplacement M.2 compatible PCIe 5.0 pour en profiter pleinement. Sur un port PCIe 4.0, le SSD fonctionnera, mais les performances seront limitées : les vitesses plafonneront autour de 7 000 Mo/s.
Dans le détail, ce SSD SanDisk affiche des débits séquentiels environ deux fois plus élevés que ceux d’un bon SSD PCIe 4.0, avec jusqu’à 14 900 Mo/s en lecture et 11 000 Mo/s en écriture. Il se montre aussi très véloce lors des opérations aléatoires, avec jusqu’à 1,6 million d’IOPS en lecture et 2,4 millions d’IOPS en écriture, selon la marque. Il embarque en prime la technologie nCache 4.0, qui lui permet d’accélérer les écritures lors des transferts de fichiers volumineux.
Notons aussi la présence d’un dissipateur thermique fabriqué en aluminium anodisé et conçu pour évacuer efficacement la chaleur. Le fabricant le présente comme un dissipateur passif très fin, qui se passe de ventilateur et d’alimentation supplémentaire, pour garder le SSD au frais lors des longues sessions de travail ou de jeu.
Un disque pensé pour les utilisateurs exigeants
Avec une telle fiche technique, le SSD s’adresse aux utilisateurs exigeants à la recherche d’un stockage très rapide, par exemple pour compléter une configuration PC récente et puissante. Les débits très élevés accélèrent surtout le transfert de grosses bibliothèques de titres AAA. En jeu, le gain sur les temps de chargement par rapport à un bon SSD PCIe 4.0 reste souvent modeste. Mais les joueurs ne sont pas les seules cibles de SanDisk : les monteurs travaillant sur de lourds fichiers vidéo 4K voire 8K ou sur des projets 3D y trouveront aussi leur compte, de même que les professionnels de l’IA.
Vous l’aurez compris, ce SSD interne NVMe n’est pas vraiment destiné à la PS5, dont l’emplacement M.2 exploite uniquement l’interface PCIe 4.0. Les débits du SanDisk Optimus GX Pro 8100 seraient donc limités sur cette console. Mieux vaut alors se diriger vers un bon SSD PCIe 4.0, largement suffisant pour étendre le stockage tout en profitant de temps de chargement réduits. Enfin, l’endurance de l’Optimus GX Pro 8100 de 1 To atteint 600 TBW. Ainsi, jusqu’à 600 To de données peuvent être écrites sur le SSD. SanDisk accorde en plus une garantie de 5 ans, qui prend toutefois fin plus tôt si les 600 To écrits sont atteints entre-temps.
